ideas.name: BlueLatticeNoise
ideas.one_liner: Value-style lattice noise built on the discrete Laplacian of white lattice values (or on parity-alternated values), giving a coherent noise with zero DC and power ~k^4 at low frequency: fine, even, blob-free texture whose thresholds give evenly spread specks.
ideas.algorithm:
Lattice values v_c = rnd11(Hash(seed, c)).
Laplacian mode: L_c = 2d * v_c - sum_a (v_{c+e_a} + v_{c-e_a})   (integer-weight discrete Laplacian; Order 2 applies it twice over the 2-neighbourhood).
Field: f(x) = tensor-quintic interpolation of L over the 2^d corners of the cell containing x (exactly Value noise with L in place of v). Needed hashes: the corners' axis neighbours = the 4^d block minus its corner cubes (2D: 12, 3D: 32, 4D: ~80).
Normalise: var(L) = (4d^2 + 2d)/3 for uniform v, interpolation attenuates further; scale by a measured constant per dimension and order.
Parity mode: L_c = (-1)^(sum_a c_a) * (0.5 + 0.5 rnd01(h_c)); same interpolation (a jittered-amplitude checkerboard, power concentrated at the lattice Nyquist). Optional: run the result through a cheap DomainWarp inside the node to break the checker regularity.
Spectrum: the Laplacian transfer function is |sum_a (2 - 2cos k_a)| ~ |k|^2, so power ~ k^4 near k = 0; the quintic interpolation rolls off above Nyquist: a band-pass ring peaking around 0.3-0.5 cycles per cell with no low-frequency content.
ideas.look: A uniform, grainy 'felt' or pebble-bed with no blobs, no drifts, no light or dark regions larger than a couple of cells; at any coverage the threshold set is small evenly spread specks of near-uniform size (stipple), and inverting the threshold gives evenly spread holes. Hillshade: fine even bumps like sandpaper or orange peel. Parity mode: a warped checkerboard with random contrast, quilt or cobble like. Clearly different from every red/pink noise on the sheet.
ideas.why_new: Every existing coherent noise is low-frequency dominated (blobs, continents). A blue coherent noise is the missing detail layer: added to terrain it adds texture without moving coastlines (zero local mean), as a dither it breaks Terrace banding without clumps, and thresholded it is a scatter mask with even density. Not expressible: there is no blur/convolution node, Perlin's k^2 rolloff still looks blobby, and FBm with gain > 1 remains pink at the top octave.
ideas.simd_plan: Value.inl with a bigger hash block: 12 / 32 / ~80 hashes (int ops only) + 2^d-corner interpolation; ~1-1.5x Perlin in 2D, ~1.5x in 3D, ~2x in 4D. Order 2 roughly doubles the hash count. Dimension agnostic with GenT; tiles through 4D.
ideas.continuity: C2 (quintic interpolation of per-corner constants), same as Value noise.
ideas.params: Mode enum (Laplacian, Parity); Order (int 1..2); Feature Scale; Seed Offset; Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks: Still a grid lattice: the Laplacian stencil is axis aligned, so the FFT ring will show four lobes (axis statistic > 1); a simplex-lattice variant (Laplacian over the 6 hex neighbours in 2D) is more isotropic but a bigger port. Parity mode is regular unless warped. Low-frequency suppression means the field cannot be used alone for terrain, only as a detail/dither/scatter layer.
ideas.cost_note: Value.inl with a bigger hash block: 12 / 32 / ~80 hashes (int ops only) + 2^d-corner interpolation; ~1-1.5x Perlin in 2D, ~1.5x in 3D, ~2x in 4D.

ideas.name: BranchworkCaves
ideas.one_liner: 3D SDF of karst conduits: directed river networks on bedding planes, tube radius from exact catchment area, vertical shafts at sources, sinkholes where shafts meet the surface. Builds on the CatchmentRivers lattice.
ideas.algorithm: Layer n=floor(z/Tz). In each of the two nearest bedding layers, run the 2D CatchmentRivers lattice in plan, with flow along dip direction and layer-specific seed. Tube SDF: elliptical cross-section: d=sqrt(dist2D^2+(k*(z-z_n))^2)-rho(area), with rho~c*area^0.4 and k>1 for flattened phreatic tubes. Shafts: sites with area=1 and hash
ideas.look: True branchwork caves: small inlets merging into a large trunk passage, stacked levels linked by pits, unlike the wormy blobs of thresholded noise. A 2D slice shows a plan map of passages.
ideas.why_new: Thresholded noise caves have no flow hierarchy, and passage size has no relation to connectivity. Here passages grow downstream by construction, using exact area.
ideas.simd_plan: 2 layers x CatchmentRivers lattice search + walkers at K=16, plus 3D shaft checks. Estimate 60-100 ns in 3D. 2D is one layer with z=0. 4D would be crossfaded time; no tiling.
ideas.continuity: C0 for the SDF given smooth-min, with area lerped along segments as in CatchmentRivers; layer seam hidden because tubes fade from z distance before layer switching if Tz exceeds the tube's vertical radius.
ideas.params: Layer Thickness, Lateral Scale, K (int), Radius Coefficient, Flattening k, Shaft Chance, Dip Angle (float), Surface Source (optional hybrid).
ideas.risks: Not tested. Depends on the CatchmentRivers look being solved. Shaft alignment with both layers is the fiddly part; missed alignment gives dangling passages. Fairly niche compared to its cost. In 3D the axis bias is less visible, an advantage.
ideas.cost_note: Estimate 60-100 ns in 3D.

ideas.name: CatchmentRivers
ideas.one_liner: Exact upstream drainage area per point at O(K) cost, using a Scheidegger river lattice whose catchment boundaries are two backward walkers. The network model is known hydrology (from memory); the pointwise area trick and the node are not something I recognise.
ideas.algorithm:
Lattice: rows r along the flow axis, sites e across it, at position X(e,r)=e-0.5*r plus hash jitter (world scale RX across, RY along). One hash bit d(e,r) in {0,1}. Each site flows to (e+d, r+1). The map is monotone, so channels can merge but never cross, and the upstream set of any site at any earlier row is a single interval.
Area: L=e-1; R=e; area=R-L; for m=1..K { L-=d(L,r-m); R-=d(R,r-m); area+=R-L }. The two walkers are the dual tree, meaning the catchment divides. R-L can never go negative and they coalesce at the source, so no masks are needed.
Surface: for each candidate segment (rows r-2..r+2, sites e0-2..e0+2 in the test; try 3x4 in the port), project to get t and dist. Lerp log(area) along the segment so a tributary and its trunk share the same value at the junction node. z=Zc*area^-theta + Tilt*(rows to outlet). height=min over candidates of z + S*dist. This lower envelope has no local pits, unlike FBm.
Outputs: Elevation, Channel mask with width ~ sqrt(area), log Area, Distance to divide (the same search on dual segments).
Pinnate mode: fold the row coordinate with a triangle wave of period T and add a trunk valley at the fold.
ideas.look: Eroded badland or mountain-flank drainage: tributaries merge into progressively wider channels, and the area output reads as real river bodies. Good for valley carving, river masks, wetness and sediment masks, and tree or biome placement. Fractal detail across scales comes from the network itself (Hack scaling), so one fine lattice covers many stream orders without octaves.
ideas.why_new: Flow accumulation normally needs a whole-grid simulation. Here it is a pure function of position, and it is exact whenever K reaches the divide. Nothing on the contact sheet or in a graph can report how much terrain drains through a point.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch free: masks for nearest-segment tracking, then fixed K-loop walkers on the winning segment's endpoints, 2 hashes per walker row. Adjacent sites share dual walkers, so a row of n sites needs n+1 walkers if areas are needed for all candidates. Estimate, not measured: nearest search about 2x CellularDistance 2D, K=32 about 128 hashes, total 40-70 ns, about 40-60x Perlin and 10-15x CellularDistance. 3D has no interval property with a 2D lateral: use crossfaded 2D laminae over z (2x cost). 4D does not tile, because the fold and flow axis are not periodic on the torus; native tiling needs hash modulo per axis.
ideas.continuity: Lower envelope of continuous functions is C0 if the candidate window is large enough. The test still showed outlier per-pixel jumps (max 6.8 vs p99.9 2.6, cause not identified; suspect window truncation or clamped rows).
ideas.params: Flow Angle (float), Aspect RX/RY (float), K Upstream Rows (int), Area Exponent theta (hybrid), Hillslope S (hybrid), Tilt (hybrid), Channel Width (hybrid), Output (enum). A deliberate lateral drift bias on d can also be hybrid.
ideas.risks: TESTED in numpy on baked arrays, not as a hash-based pointwise node. Walker identity matched brute-force accumulation at all 172 sites checked (0 mismatches). The look is NOT yet solved: at Aspect 1 the result is long parallel vertical gullies with visible zigzag and seams at the fold. At Aspect 3 plus domain warp the area map looks like rivers, but the height output looks closer to warped marble than dendritic terrain. Strong axis bias needs warp or a local flow frame. Tune or switch to channel-mask output before judging. Area is truncated when K is below the distance to the divide.
ideas.cost_note: Estimate, not measured: nearest search about 2x CellularDistance 2D, K=32 about 128 hashes, total 40-70 ns, about 40-60x Perlin and 10-15x CellularDistance.

queue.name: CatchmentRivers
queue.reason: Wild card. Exact drainage area from two backward walkers on a Scheidegger lattice (J3 top pick). 40-70 ns, global flow axis, and the look is unsolved; the prototype exists to find out whether the look lands.

ideas.name: CausticNoise
ideas.one_liner: Geometric-optics caustic intensity 1/|det(I + D*Hessian(h))| of a built-in random-wave height h, computed analytically pointwise: bright filament networks of pool-floor caustics with no simulation.
ideas.algorithm:
Height h(x) = sum_i a_i sin(theta_i), theta_i = k_i*dot(d_i, x') + phi_i, with the same rotated direction table and hashing as WaveNoise (M ~ 8-16, Ring or narrow-band spectrum so filaments have one dominant scale).
Refraction/lens map: T(x) = x + D * grad h(x)   (D = Depth*(n-1), hybrid).
Jacobian J = I + D*H,  H = Hess h = - sum_i a_i k_i^2 sin(theta_i) d_i d_i^T.
Gen(seed,x):
  H = 0 (2D: Hxx,Hxy,Hyy; 3D: 6 terms; 4D: 10 terms)
  for i in 0..M-1: s = Sin(theta_i); c = a_i*k_i^2*s; H += c * outer(d_i,d_i)   (outer products of table vectors are constants: precompute d_i d_i^T table)
  det = det(I + D*H)   (2D: (1+D Hxx)(1+D Hyy) - D^2 Hxy^2 ; 3D: 3x3 cofactor; 4D: 4x4 by 2x2 blocks)
  Mode Intensity:    v = Min(1, Gain / (|det| + Eps)) * 2 - 1
  Mode LogIntensity: v = clamp(-Log(|det| + Eps) * Gain, 0, 1)*2-1
  Mode Fold:         v = sign(det)        (regions beyond the fold line, i.e. inside the caustic 'cells')
  Mode Height:       v = h normalised (the lens surface itself, for matching normal maps)
Animation: feed 4D w or Seed; Depth as hybrid gives caustics sharpening with water depth across the image.
ideas.look: Thin bright filament network enclosing rounded dark cells, filaments brightest where they cross (cusps): classic underwater caustics / light through wavy glass / foil wrinkles; large D gives doubled, folded filaments; Fold mode gives a crisp organic cell mask with cusped corners.
ideas.why_new: Caustic networks require second derivatives of a smooth surface; no graph of existing nodes can produce the fold-line singularities (users currently fake it with Abs/Ridged which lacks the cusps and brightness law). Analytic Hessian from plane waves makes it as cheap as a noise and dimension agnostic.
ideas.simd_plan: Fixed M loop, per wave 1 Sin plus d(d+1)/2 FMAs into H; one small determinant; no lattice. Est. AVX2 M=12: 2D ~2.5x Perlin, 3D ~1.5x Perlin3D, 4D ~1x Perlin4D. 1/|det| guarded by Eps and Min; Log guarded. GenT with per-dimension det helper.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity away from fold lines; across fold lines 1/|det| diverges and is clamped by Min, giving a C0 plateau (filament core). Fold mode is a step function.
ideas.params: Waves M (int), Feature Scale, Depth D (hybrid), Gain, Eps, Bandwidth (0 = ring), Mode enum {Intensity, LogIntensity, Fold, Height}, Seed.
ideas.risks: Single-sheet approximation: intensity is evaluated at the surface point, not accumulated over the multiple surface points that land on one floor point, so beyond the first fold the picture is a stylised caustic (still looks right). Clamping makes filament width depend on Eps/Gain rather than physics.
ideas.cost_note: AVX2 M=12: 2D ~2.5x Perlin, 3D ~1.5x Perlin3D, 4D ~1x Perlin4D.

queue.reason: Analytic Hessian of a wave sum, flat cost across dimensions (J1 top pick). Judges split on whether single-sheet det=0 reads as pool-floor caustics, so settle it side by side with caustic-web and fold-caustic.

ideas.name: ChaosMapNoise
ideas.one_liner: Iterate an area-preserving chaotic map (Chirikov standard map; Froeschle 4D map) from the sample's fractional position with its kick strength read from noise, outputting orbit stretch: KAM islands, island chains and chaotic seas.
ideas.algorithm:
theta = 2*pi*frac(x*Period), I = 2*pi*frac(y*Period); K = K0 + K1*n(p) (n smooth noise so chaoticity varies across space).
  (jt, ji) tangent vector = (1, 0) and (0, 1) tracked as 2x2 M = I
  for k in 0..N-1:                           // N = 16..40
      s = sin(theta), c = cos(theta)
      I = I + K*s ; theta = theta + I        // mod 2*pi via theta - 2*pi*Floor(theta/(2*pi)) on theta only
      M = [[1 + K*c, 1],[K*c, 1]] * M        // tangent map
      acc += cos(theta)                      // orbit average (optional output)
  FTLE = log(||M||_F / sqrt(2)) / N          // or sigma_max closed form
  Output enum: Lyapunov (FTLE remapped), OrbitMean (acc/N), Mix.
3D/4D: Froeschle map on (theta1, I1, theta2, I2) with coupling b, 4D node uses all four coordinates; 3D node sets I2 (or theta2) from noise(p). Smooth DomainWarp upstream breaks the visible 2*pi lattice.
ideas.look: The phase portrait of a Hamiltonian system: large smooth 'eyes' (islands) with nested resonance chains of smaller eyes along their rims, embedded in a grainy chaotic sea whose extent is controlled locally by the noise-driven K. Spatially it reads as whirlpools, nested cat's-eyes, chained beads: nothing remotely like it on the sheet. Use for ornamental/alien textures, fluid-like eyes, bead chains, as a mask for 'order vs chaos' regions.
ideas.why_new: A fixed iteration count of a symplectic map gives genuine Hamiltonian phase-space structure (KAM tori, resonances) with no counterpart in noise literature; letting noise drive the control parameter lets the ordered/chaotic character vary smoothly across space, so the pattern reads as a texture rather than a math plot.
ideas.simd_plan: One noise eval + N iterations each ~ Sin/Cos (shared polynomial), Floor, ~12 flops and a 2x2 (or 4x4) matrix product; N=32 ~ 600 flops: 2D ~15-20 ns (~15x Perlin), 3D/4D similar plus the 4x4 tangent product (~2x). Tiles on the 2*pi lattice by construction; GenTileable2D works via the noise term only. Everything branch-free.
ideas.continuity: Continuous inside regular (island) regions; effectively discontinuous in chaotic regions because of sensitive dependence (the grainy sea is the look). FTLE is bounded by log of the matrix norm so no NaNs; OrbitMean bounded in [-1,1].
ideas.params: Period float, K0 float, K1 hybrid (noise-driven kick), Iterations int, Coupling float (4D/3D), Output enum, Seeded (noise n), VariableRange.
ideas.risks: Visible 2*pi periodicity (needs upstream warp or K variation to hide); 'math plot' flavour; chaotic regions alias badly at any resolution; 3D story is weaker (noise-driven extra coordinate rather than a true 3D map).
ideas.cost_note: One noise eval + N iterations each ~ Sin/Cos (shared polynomial), Floor, ~12 flops and a 2x2 (or 4x4) matrix product; N=32 ~ 600 flops: 2D ~15-20 ns (~15x Perlin), 3D/4D similar plus the 4x4 tangent product (~2x).

ideas.name: CyclicNoise
ideas.one_liner: Lattice-free fractal of sin(dot(cos(p), sin(p.zxy))) terms with a per-octave orthonormal rotation, lacunarity and sine domain warp (nimitz/Wrighter/0b5vr 'cyclic noise'): fibrous, marbled, flowing structure in 2D/3D at pure-ALU cost.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Octaves N (int, 4-8), Gain (0.6), Lacunarity (1.5), Warp (hybrid, 0.3), WarpFreq (1.2), WarpGrowth (1.5), SeedDirection (from seed: hashed unit vector).
Setup: rot = orthoBasis(seedDir) (3x3 rotation whose z axis = seedDir; 2D: a 2x2 rotation by a hashed angle plus a third coordinate = seed constant; 4D: a hashed 4x4 rotation = product of two plane rotations).
Gen(p): p3 = (x,y,z) (2D: z = seed-derived constant); amp=1; wf=WarpFreq; sum=0; norm=0; for i<N: p3 += sin(p3.zxy * wf - 2*wf) * Warp; sum += sin(dot(cos(p3), sin(p3.zxy))) * amp; norm += amp; p3 = (rot * p3) * Lacunarity; wf *= WarpGrowth; amp *= Gain. Output sum/norm (measured: multiply by ~1.3 for [-1,1] coverage); Turbulent mode: 1 - 2*|sum|/norm.
0b5vr variant (vector-valued, fits DomainWarp): accumulate cross(cos(p3), sin(p3.zxy)) as a warp vector.
Seed sensitivity: the seed enters through the rotation basis and the constant offset; per-octave re-rotation by hashed bases (seed, i) gives more variety.

[GyroidFractal, shader-community] Precompute per octave k (when params set): rotation matrix R_k = GoldenRotation^k (2D: rotate by 137.5 deg; 3D: rotation of 137.5 deg about axis (1, phi, phi^2) normalised; 4D: product of two plane rotations by 137.5 deg and 137.5*phi deg), scale s_k = Lacunarity^k, amplitude a_k = Gain^k.
q = p * Frequency; acc = 0; norm = 0
for k in 0..Octaves-1:
  q = R_k * q * (k==0 ? 1 : Lacunarity)
  if Warp > 0: q += Warp * sin(q.yzx)              // nimitz cyclic noise: the domain is bent by its own sines; 2D: q += Warp*sin(q.yx)
  v = sum over axes i of cos(q_i) * sin(Phi * q_{(i+1) mod dim})   // 2D: cos x sin(phi y) + cos y sin(phi x); Phi = golden ratio keeps it non-periodic
  Profile enum: Sine as above; Triangle: replace cos/sin by tri(x)=4*|fract(x/2pi)-0.5|-1 (nimitz triNoise: cheaper, C0 creased); Ridged: v = 1 - |v|/dim
  acc += a_k * v ; norm += a_k * dim
out = acc / norm (then measured scale: the dim-term sum rarely reaches +-dim, multiply by ~1.6)
Seed: add a seed-derived phase offset per axis (q += seedPhase) so seeds give different fields (no hash anywhere).
ideas.look:
Organic, fibrous, flowing filaments and marble-like veins with no lattice at all; at low octaves large smooth 'plasma', at higher octaves tangled fibre networks; turbulent mode gives cellular-ish rope structure. Visually unlike Perlin/Simplex (which have isotropic blobs) and unlike Cellular.
[GyroidFractal, shader-community] Soft billowy/foamy structure with faint wave-like anisotropy, cloudy when summed; cyclic (Warp>0) version swirls like protean clouds; triangle profile gives crumpled paper. Reads as fbm from a distance but with a wavier, more organic micro-structure. Not on the sheet (SineWave is a single axis-aligned wave).
ideas.why_new: No lattice, no hash per sample, native 3D with trivial 2D/4D, and a signature look prized in the demoscene; also cheap (N octaves of 3 sin + 3 cos + a dot). Could not be built from existing nodes except by an unwieldy chain of SineWave + DomainRotate + warps.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch-free, fixed octave loop, no memory. Per octave: dim matrix mults (dim^2 FMA) + dim SinCos (~25 ops each) -> 2D ~ 60 ops/octave (~0.7x Perlin 2D), 3D ~ 100 ops (~0.5x Perlin 3D), 4D ~ 140 ops (~0.4x Perlin 4D). Triangle profile ~3x cheaper. Dimension-agnostic GenT with precomputed matrices.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity (compositions of sines and rotations).
ideas.params: Octaves (int), Gain, Lacunarity, Warp (hybrid), WarpFreq, WarpGrowth, Mode enum {Smooth, Turbulent}, Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks:
Looks bad at high frequencies / few octaves (periodic sin structure shows, as SquidSquad's docs note); normalisation is empirical; seeds give limited structural variety unless per-octave bases are hashed.
[GyroidFractal, shader-community] Visible large-scale banding in huge flat views (Xor notes 'patterns in large flat scenes'); anisotropy at octave 1 (needs >=3 octaves to look isotropic). Range normalisation must be measured. Seeds only shift phases, so different seeds are translations of the same field unless rotation angles are also seed-perturbed (do that: angle += small seed-derived irrational offset).
ideas.variant_notes: Xor's gyroid dot noise is the same family: hash-free octaves of products of sines under irrational rotation, plus self-warp.
ideas.cost_note: Per octave: dim matrix mults (dim^2 FMA) + dim SinCos (~25 ops each) -> 2D ~ 60 ops/octave (~0.7x Perlin 2D), 3D ~ 100 ops (~0.5x Perlin 3D), 4D ~ 140 ops (~0.4x Perlin 4D).

ideas.name: DefectStripes
ideas.one_liner: Constant-contrast stripes with k-armed dislocations at phase vortices, with fractal roughness added in a way that cannot create branch cuts.
ideas.algorithm: Complex lattice field: per lattice corner c of the 2^D cell, Z=sum over corners of fade weight w_c(p)*exp(i*(2pi*Wave*dot(g_c,p-c)+phase_c)), with g_c and phase_c from hash. Unit phasor U=Z/sqrt(|Z|^2+eps^2). Base=U^k by repeated complex multiply (k integer, no atan2). Fractal roughness: for finer octaves j with a_j<1: R=1+a_j*Z_j(p*Lac^j); multiply Base by R/|R|. |R| never reaches 0 when a_j*|Z_j|<1, so this has no winding and no branch cut, and non-integer effect is safe. Output Re(Base)+Phase rotation from a hybrid if desired. Multiplying unit phasors of different octaves directly fails: it gives white noise.
ideas.look: Fingerprints, zebra, labyrinth or coral with uniform contrast and k-arm forks. Rough version looks like brain coral or tiger stripes with crinkled edges. Strongly unlike Perlin's varied contrast.
ideas.why_new: Phasor-style noises get constant-contrast stripes, usually via larger kernel windows; from memory Phacelle noise is the nearest relative. The k-fold defect control and the winding-free fractal phase perturbation are the additions. FastNoise has no stripe-field generator at all.
ideas.simd_plan: 2^D corners, each one Sin+Cos pair (can share a polynomial), plus 3 mul-adds. 2D about 4-5x Perlin, 3D 8 corners and 4D 16 corners scale like Perlin's cost ratio. Each rough octave adds another full evaluation. A Base+3 rough octaves in 2D costs about 20 ns.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity with eps>0: at vortices, amplitude fades smoothly. Measured c0ratio 5.74 (k=3) and 6.37 (rough). The k power does not create cuts because k is integer.
ideas.params: Frequency, Wave (cycles per cell), Arms k (int), Epsilon, Rough Octaves, Rough Amount (must stay below 1), Gain, Lacunarity, Phase (hybrid).
ideas.risks: Lattice imprint: per-cell plane waves may show at low Wave; not checked on an FFT sheet. Eps too small gives pinholes. Phase rotation hybrid may be subtle. Fractal mode cost is high against plain graph warps. Check whether a warp-based result is close enough.
ideas.cost_note: 2D about 4-5x Perlin, 3D 8 corners and 4D 16 corners scale like Perlin's cost ratio. A Base+3 rough octaves in 2D costs about 20 ns.

disp.how: Arms int only; Rough octaves stay out at 2.83x

ideas.name: DislocationStripes
ideas.one_liner: Stripes with real topological defects: a phase field carrying closed dislocation loops, so stripes fork and terminate, which isolines of a scalar can never do.
ideas.algorithm: phase = Tau*Frequency*Phase(x), where Phase is a source, default a warped plane. Lattice: 3x3 / 3x3x3 / 2^4 round-based window. For each point with hash01 < Density: centre c (jitter), orthonormal pair n,m from a gradient table, sign s = +-1. v = x-c; un = v.n; um = v.m; us2 = |v|^2 - un^2 - um^2 (the component orthogonal to the n,m plane; 0 in 2D). dl = D0*sqrt(max(0, 1 - us2/S^2)). psi = atan2(2*dl*um, un^2 + um^2 - dl^2). This is the angle subtended by the pair at +-dl*n. It jumps exactly 2pi across the cut segment, which cos() cannot see, and it goes to 0 away from the pair. taper = 1 - smoothstep(1.3*max(D0,S), R1, |v|), so taper = 1 on the whole cut. Sum over window: Psi += s*psi*taper. Core guard: amp = min(amp, sat(core_dist/eps)), core_dist = sqrt((|un|-dl)^2 + um^2). Output amp*cos(phase + Psi). No per-point sign bookkeeping: every point is a neutral +1/-1 pair (2D) or a closed elliptical loop (3D, 4D closed surface), so nothing long-range leaks.
ideas.look: Fingerprints, zebra, sand ripples, wood-ish lamellae, seafloor ridges with transform-like forks. Prototyped: clearly fingerprint-like with Y-forks and stripe endings; FFT shows the two side lobes of a stripe pattern, with defects filling the spectrum. Thresholded, it gives zebra and labyrinth masks.
ideas.why_new: PingPong or Terrace of FBm gives isolines, and isolines of a smooth scalar only merge at saddles in X form. They cannot produce a stripe that simply ends. Phasor noise gets singularities only as uncontrolled by-products; here defect density, size and stripe direction are independent controls.
ideas.simd_plan: One polynomial atan2 per feature (no atan2 in FS, so add it). Estimates with 2^D corners: 4 ns in 2D (3.5x Perlin, about 1x CellularDistance), 8 ns in 3D, 16 ns in 4D. With 3^D jittered: 8, 25, 75 ns. GenT generic with dot products only.
ideas.continuity: C0 except at isolated core points or curves, where phase is undefined and cos stays bounded (a small pinwheel). Random-pair ratio about 10 in 2D, 3D and 4D, meaning continuous; dense scanline in 2D: 0 jumps. Requires w=1 across the whole cut disc, which margin ensures.
ideas.params: Frequency (hybrid), Density (hybrid via smooth gate), Core Separation D0, Loop Size S, Influence R1, Phase source or Direction plus Warp Amount.
ideas.risks:
The 3D XZ slice showed some sharp-looking edges near loops; verify they are cores and not cut leakage if the taper start is mis-set. Polynomial atan2 accuracy matters: the jump must be 2pi to well under 1e-3 relative or the cut becomes visible. Phase gets large with Frequency at far coords.
[DislocationStripes, nature-phenomena] A 2D slice of a 3D ring or 4D sphere shows fewer defects: the 3D slice shows some and the 4D slice nearly none at R=0.3, so 4D tiling needs larger R or density (not tested). Frequency near 1 cycle per cell gives crowded defects. I could read only the abstract and citing summaries of the Larkin and Fletcher paper, since its PDF was unreadable through the fetch tool.
ideas.variant_notes: DislocationLoops is the same toroidal-angle formula offered as a domain modifier; it adds a Lift output that feeds the phase into any source as S(x, A cos ph, A sin ph).
ideas.cost_note: Estimates with 2^D corners: 4 ns in 2D (3.5x Perlin, about 1x CellularDistance), 8 ns in 3D, 16 ns in 4D.

disp.how: the look is the plain vortex forks, so nothing extra to build

ideas.name: EscapeNoise
ideas.one_liner: Escape-time of z^2 + c where c (or z0) is read from two seeded noises: fractal coastlines and dendrites from a single octave at ~4x Perlin.
ideas.algorithm:
a = n_1(p), b = n_2(p) in [-1,1] (two seeded Simplex/Perlin, any dimension).
Mode Mandelbrot: c = Centre + Radius*(a, b), z = 0.   Mode Julia: c = JuliaC (param), z = Centre + Radius*(a, b).
  n = 0; (zx, zy) as float32v
  for k in 0..N-1:                                        // N = 16..48 fixed
      r2 = zx*zx + zy*zy
      inside = r2 <= R2                                   // mask, R = 2..4 (escape radius)
      nx = zx*zx - zy*zy + cx ; ny = 2*zx*zy + cy
      zx = Select(inside, nx, zx); zy = Select(inside, ny, zy)   // freeze after escape
      n  = n + Select(inside, 1, 0)
  nu = n + 1 - log2( log(sqrt(r2_final)) / log(R) )     // smooth iteration count, clamp to [0,N] (not-escaped lanes: nu = N)
  Output enum: Count = nu/N ; Banded = sin(nu*freq) ; Trap = min_k |z_k - T| accumulated in-loop (orbit trap, textures the interior) ; Mix = Count with Trap inside.
ideas.look: Mandelbrot mode: smooth noise-like low regions, plateaus where c(p) falls inside the set, and between them fractal coastlines with fjords and islands at every scale that follow the contours of the underlying noise: 'plateau islands with infinitely crenellated shores'. Julia mode with c near the set boundary (e.g. c = i): dendritic lightning/fern/river-delta structures threaded through the noise. Orbit traps give nested 'eye' and 'spiral' ornaments inside. Entirely absent from the sheet; terrain mesas with fractal shorelines, lightning masks, ornamental textures.
ideas.why_new: Pulls back a fractal boundary through a smooth map, so a constant tiny iteration count yields unbounded boundary detail without octaves. Cost is dominated by just two noise evaluations, so it is one of the cheapest 'look' nodes and works identically in 2D/3D/4D.
ideas.simd_plan: 2 noise evals + N iterations of ~8 flops + 2 Selects + 1 compare; N=32 is ~300 flops. 2D ~5 ns (~4-5x Perlin); 3D ~7 ns; 4D ~12 ns, i.e. almost dimension-independent extra cost. One Log and one Log2 at the end. Tiles in 4D trivially.
ideas.continuity: Continuous (smooth iteration count is continuous across escape bands; interior plateau is constant) but with unbounded gradient at the fractal set boundary; Trap output continuous.
ideas.params: Mode enum (Mandelbrot/Julia), Centre X/Y floats, Radius hybrid, JuliaC X/Y floats, Iterations int, EscapeRadius float, Output enum, Trap X/Y floats, Band Frequency float, Seeded, ScalableGenerator.
ideas.risks: Recognisably 'Mandelbrot-ish' if parameters are left at defaults; aliasing when rendered at low resolution; interior is flat unless Trap/Mix is used; R and the log smoothing need care at nu near N.
ideas.cost_note: 2D ~5 ns (~4-5x Perlin); 3D ~7 ns; 4D ~12 ns, i.e. almost dimension-independent extra cost.

ideas.name: ExactGaussianNoise
ideas.one_liner: Value-lattice noise whose marginal is exactly N(0,1) at every point (L2-normalised weights over Gaussian corner values), with an erf output mode that is exactly uniform and a hybrid Coverage mask whose area fraction is exactly what you asked for.
ideas.algorithm:
Lattice: integer grid, 2^d corners c_i of the cell containing x (same as Value noise).
Per corner: h = Hash(seed, c_i); u1 = ((h & 0xFFFF) + 0.5) / 65536; u2 = ((h >> 16) + 0.5) / 65536;
  g_i = sqrt(-2 ln u1) * cos(2*pi*u2)            // Box-Muller, exactly N(0,1); |g| <= 4.7 because u1 >= 2^-17
  (cheaper option: g_i = PhiInv(u) via odd polynomial on (2u-1) with clamped tails; loses exactness in the last 0.5% of mass)
Weights: t_a = quintic(frac(x_a)); w_i = prod_a (corner bit a ? t_a : 1 - t_a)   // standard tensor weights, sum = 1
f = sum_i w_i g_i / sqrt( sum_i w_i^2 )            // key step: for fixed x this is a unit-L2 combination of iid N(0,1) => exactly N(0,1)
   (sum w_i^2 >= 1/2^d > 0 always, so no 0/0; the 1/sqrt is a smooth positive factor)
Mode Gaussian: out = f * (1/3), VariableRange around +-1 (tails beyond 3 sigma clipped by Output Min/Max)
Mode Uniform:  u = 0.5 * (1 + erf(f / sqrt2))  with A&S 7.1.26 (t = 1/(1+0.3275911|z|), 5-term poly * exp(-z^2), restore sign); out = 2u - 1   // exactly uniform
Mode Coverage: c = Coverage(x) (hybrid); out = smoothstep((c - u) / Softness) mapped to [-1,1]  // fraction of plane with out>0 is exactly c, even when c varies in space
Optional Lattice enum: Grid (above) | Simplex (OpenSimplex-style kernels (0.5-r^2)^4 as the w_i, same L2 normalisation; max vertex distance 0.577 < 0.707 so the norm never vanishes).
ideas.look: Like Value noise but without the lattice-period amplitude modulation (ordinary value noise has only half the std at 2D cell centres; the L2 normalisation removes that beat), so blobs look more even and the grid is less visible. Uniform mode is a flat-histogram field: equal area at every grey level. Coverage mode with a spatially varying hybrid gives leopard spots (c~0.2) morphing into zebra labyrinth (c~0.5) into holes (c~0.8) with constant feature size: animal coats, lichen, lakes-vs-land ratio maps. Good for terrain masks where sea level must mean an exact land fraction.
ideas.why_new: No existing node has a known marginal. Thresholds on Perlin/Simplex/Value give coverage that drifts with octaves, gain and position in the lattice. Here coverage c is exact by construction, pointwise, with a hybrid: 'water covers 30 percent' is one parameter, not a trial-and-error threshold. Percolation becomes a knob: in 2D the c=0.5 set is critical (neither phase connects), c>0.5 makes that phase percolate; in 3D a Gaussian excursion set percolates above about 16 percent volume, so c in [0.16,0.84] gives a bi-continuous sponge, outside it isolated blobs. It is also the Gaussianiser stage that StatBlend and CdfRemap need to be exact.
ideas.simd_plan: Pure lattice code like Value.inl: 2^d hashes, 2^d x (Log, Sqrt, Cos) for Box-Muller, tensor weights, one Reciprocal-sqrt (InvSqrt) for the norm; erf = 1 Exp + poly. No window search, branch-free. 2D ~2-3x Perlin, 3D ~3x Perlin (8 corners), 4D 16 corners ~3-4x Perlin; GenT<P...> parameter-pack implementation works since it is dimension agnostic. Tiles correctly through the 4D torus.
ideas.continuity: C2 with quintic weights (sum w_i^2 is a smooth positive function, erf and smoothstep are smooth); Coverage mode is C1 where Coverage is C1.
ideas.params: Mode enum (Gaussian, Uniform, Coverage); Coverage (hybrid, 0..1); Softness (float, width of the mask edge in probability units); Lattice enum (Grid, Simplex); Feature Scale; Seed Offset; Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks: Box-Muller costs three transcendentals per corner; the polynomial PhiInv alternative is cheaper but clips tails. Grid lattice still shows some axis alignment (less than Value noise but more than Simplex). Exactness is per point; neighbouring points are strongly correlated, so coverage over a small window fluctuates like any noise. Gradient-noise version does not work (dividing by the Gaussian variance sqrt(sum w_i^2 |d_i|^2) is 0/0 at lattice points and the limit is direction dependent).
ideas.cost_note: 2D ~2-3x Perlin, 3D ~3x Perlin (8 corners), 4D 16 corners ~3-4x Perlin; GenT<P...> parameter-pack implementation works since it is dimension agnostic.

ideas.name: FernFold
ideas.one_liner: Dendritic river, frost, lightning and vein networks from recursive coordinate folding: one hash per level, no lattice window, and a fade rule that keeps every seam continuous.
ideas.algorithm: Trunks: c=round(y/S); v=y-c*S; u=x+11.3*c; id=hash(c); edge=|y-c*S|/(S/2); mask=smoothstep(0.98,0.8,edge); v+=meander*noise1D(u,c); line=bump(|v|/w)*mask. For each level k in a fixed loop: side=(v>=0); vv=|v|; a=vv/sin(theta) (distance along the branch); ub=u+vv*cot(theta) (constant along a branch heading upstream); ci=round(ub/s); cellb=ub/s-ci (the seam is exactly at +-0.5); h=hash(ci, id+side+13k, seed+100k); gate=r0<keep; L=s*(lenMin+lenVar*r3); u0=(ci+0.55*(r1-0.5))*s; b=(ub-u0)*sin(theta)+bend*(r4-0.5)/s*a*a; al=min(a,L); dl=hypot(b,a-al[,cross axes]); parent=mask*smoothstep(0.5,0.36,|cellb|)*gate; line=max(line,bump(dl/(w*wr*(1-0.65*al/L)))*parent); mask=parent*smoothstep(L,0.75*L,a); then u=-a; v=b; id=h; w*=wr; s*=ratio. In 3D/4D the unused axes are cross axes: include them in dl and swap (v,cross)=(cross,b) each level so branch planes alternate. Valley output: sum over levels of depth_k*bump(dl/(carve*w_k))^2*parent, for subtracting from a terrain.
ideas.look: Branching trees with real width hierarchy: a meandering stem with tapered side branches at every level. It reads as a river network from the air, a frost fern, lightning, roots or leaf veins. Subtracted from fBm it gives gully-dissected terrain.
ideas.why_new: No existing node makes a tree: Ridged and F2-F1 give closed nets with no hierarchy. Branch order comes directly from the level index, so width needs no upstream-area pass. Dendry reports about 10 s for 512x512 on a quad core (about 38 us per sample wall clock), against an estimated 10 ns here.
ideas.simd_plan: Fixed loop over Levels with masks and Select only; the side bit goes into the hash as an int. No window, so cost barely depends on dimension. Estimates from handbook per-feature costs, not measured: 5 levels at 6-10 ns in 2D (6-9x Perlin, 2x CellularDistance), 7-11 ns in 3D (under 1x CellularDistance), 8-12 ns in 4D (0.25x CellularDistance). Generic GenT code works because extra axes are only cross distance.
ideas.continuity: C0 by construction. Every seam fades to zero on the cell coordinate before jitter and bend. Where the side flips (v=0), the parent line is at least as strong as any child, so max() hides the change. Dense scanlines: 0 jumps over 6 lines of 200k steps. Computing the fade on the bent b gave 14 real jumps, so that ordering matters.
ideas.params: Levels (int), Trunk Spacing, Branch Spacing, Spacing Ratio, Width, Width Ratio, Branch Length, Keep Probability, Output {Line, Valley}, Trunk Layout {Parallel, Provinces}. Hybrid-safe: Branch Angle, Width, Bend, Meander. Branch Spacing must stay constant because it sets cell indices.
ideas.risks: Parallel trunks read as bands. A Voronoi province layout (per-cell heading, fade by F2-F1) looked better in the prototype but adds a 3^D window. A line network is 1D, so 3D and 4D slices show only scattered dots (confirmed in a 3D slice), and a 4D torus tile will not resemble the 2D look. An elevation-consistent terrain output was tried and looked like herringbone, so only carving is proposed; carved valleys do not form hydrologically consistent drainage against the base height. The prototype used arbitrary tuning.
ideas.cost_note: Estimates from handbook per-feature costs, not measured: 5 levels at 6-10 ns in 2D (6-9x Perlin, 2x CellularDistance), 7-11 ns in 3D (under 1x CellularDistance), 8-12 ns in 4D (0.25x CellularDistance).

queue.reason: Windowless branching from coordinate folding at ~100 ops per level, rare for dendrites. Fix trunk banding at wide view. 3D slices are dots, so judge it as a 2D tool.

ideas.name: FiberNoise
ideas.one_liner: Sparse convolution with capsule kernels: thin tapered segments in a window, giving scratches, straw, hair and rain, bending seamlessly along a hybrid angle.
ideas.algorithm:
Per cell c in 3^d window, K segments: h=hash(c,k); site uniform in cell; a=Angle(x)+Spread*(rnd-.5)*pi; u=(cos a,sin a); d=x-site; t=dot(u,d); n=dot(perp u,d)-Bend*rnd11*t^2 (parabola keeps it local); LL=L*(.5+.5*rnd); tt=clamp(t,-LL,LL); dist2=(t-tt)^2+n^2; WW=W*(.5+rnd)*(1-.7*(tt/LL)^2); q=1-dist2/WW^2; v=q>0?q^2*(.4+.6*rnd):0.
Output Max (or saturated Sum)*2-1.
Angle is sampled at x, not at the site, so all fibres bend in the field with no seams.
3D/4D: u from unit-vector table biased by an axis; n replaced by the perpendicular component of d, dist2=|d|^2-t^2+(t-tt)^2.
Constraint: LL+WW must be <= window reach (1 for 3^d; 2 for 5^d in 2D only).
ideas.look:
Prototype cl_fiber: Spread 1 is straw or pine needles on a dark ground; Spread .15 is rain, brushed metal, grass tufts; a field Angle turns them into curled hooks and flowing fur strokes. Very sparse, high-kurtosis, totally unlike any contact-sheet field. Use for grass or hair density masks, scratches, leaf litter, wood fibre.
[FlowFibers, texture-materials] Look-tested (m=5). A striking result: flowing hair and combed fibre whirls with thamp=3.14, wood-pore streaks with thamp=0.8. Unlike anything on the sheet. Drive Angle from noise for hair, from a constant for brushed metal, from Gradient-like fields for grain. Coverage mask from another source for tufts.
ideas.why_new: The survey shows Lewis's hair kernel as the demo of sparse convolution, but no FastNoise node has line-like features. CellularDistance with Max metric or anisotropic scale cannot make thin isolated segments with free ends.
ideas.simd_plan: Per capsule: hash, 2 dots, Min/Max, 2 Selects, ~.6 ns. K=1: 9/27/81 capsules = ~5/18/65 ns; K=2 in 2D ~11 ns (10x Perlin; scalar prototype 7.5x). 4D needs 2^4 window with short segments, ~10 ns. Generic GenT possible with direction table.
ideas.continuity: C0 when amplitude tapers with t. The proto did not taper amplitude and measured c0ratio 1.49 from full-height needle tips; the formula above fixes that. Kinks at strand centre lines by design, a smooth profile makes it C1 inside each strand.
ideas.params: Int: K per cell. Float: L, W. Hybrid: Angle, Spread, Bend, Density. Enum: Blend, Window.
ideas.risks:
Very high frequency content, thin lines alias at low resolution; output mean is near -1. Long fibres need 5^d. High field variation makes strokes hook unnaturally (seen). 3D slices show dots and short dashes unless an axis bias keeps fibres in plane.
[FlowFibers, texture-materials] Strands are only approximately streamlines: rapid angle change (field frequency near 1/L) makes them kinked or broken. Thin lines alias at low sample rates. Cost scales with Per Cell, and dense felt needs 4-6.
[StrokeField, lattice-kernels] Reach is L + jitter + Cap so long strokes force a wider window (cost). Bending is not real path integration, and strong orientation gradients produce claws rather than parallel hairs (a look, but not fully controllable).
ideas.variant_notes: The bend comes for free: orientation is read once at the sample, so strokes curve along level sets of the field at one source eval. Taper amplitude as well as width, or tips jump (measured c0ratio 1.49 without).
ideas.cost_note: K=1: 9/27/81 capsules = ~5/18/65 ns; K=2 in 2D ~11 ns (10x Perlin; scalar prototype 7.5x).

queue.name: FiberNoise
queue.reason: Capsule sparse convolution for straw, scratches and hair, absent from the sheet. Long fibres want 5^d, so try the stretched layers from streak-scatter as the cheap path.

ideas.name: FiskMeanders
ideas.one_liner: An analytic floodplain of tangent-continuous circular-arc rivers with real omega loops, oxbow lakes and concentric scroll bars, drawn in generations like the famous Mississippi meander maps.
ideas.algorithm: Strips j=floor(v/S), each with one river along axis u. Breakpoints P_i=(i+jitter(i,j))*Lc on the strip axis (small lateral jitter). Per-strip half-sweep a=hash in [60,130] degrees, constant along a strip so tangents match; sign alternates by parity of i. Arc i: chord c=P_(i+1)-P_i, R=|c|/(2 sin a), centre=midpoint+sign*n*R*cos a. Distance: inside the sector (dot-product tests, no atan2) d=||q-centre|-R|, else min distance to endpoints. Oxbow: if hash(i,j)<pOx the live channel takes the straight chord and the arc becomes a plugged lake whose depth fades to 0 near its ends. Scroll bars: on the concave interior of the arc, add A*sin(2pi(R-|q-centre|)/lambda)*sectorFade*radialFade. Generations: for g=0..G-1 (oldest to youngest) use a different seed; h=lerp(h, -Depth*gamma^g*U(d/W), mask(d)), so younger channels cut older deposits.
ideas.look: Sinuous constant-width rivers with goosenecks, crescent lakes and fingerprint-like point-bar ridges, overprinted by faint abandoned belts. Nothing on the contact sheet resembles this. Good for floodplains, river masks, and map-like textures.
ideas.why_new: Domain warp cannot make omega loops of constant width, because it stretches channels and would need multi-valued curves. Oxbows and scroll bars are explicit topology of this construction.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch free over a fixed window: 3 strips x 5 along-axis arcs (needed for a>90 deg) = 15 arc SDFs per generation, sqrt each. Estimate 8-10 ns per generation, 3 generations about 25-30 ns, about 25x Perlin and 7x CellularDistance. 3D: z is stratigraphic time with crossfaded seed layers (2x cost), which gives channel-belt deposits in vertical slices. 4D: same scheme; no torus tiling without periodic hashing along the strip.
ideas.continuity: C0 for depth via fade masks, with G1 river centrelines because all arcs in a strip share a. Overlapping neighbouring loops simply intersect, reading as cutoffs.
ideas.params: Strip Spacing, Bend Length, Sweep Min/Max (float), Width (hybrid), Oxbow Chance, Scroll Amp and Wavelength, Generations (int), Generation Gain, River Angle (float).
ideas.risks: Not tested. Parallel strips can look regular at wide view, so a warp upstream is needed, which then slightly varies width. Sweep constant per river limits variety; a biarc form would permit per-node tangents at about 2x cost. Oxbow plugging needs care at endpoints. It is a mainstem belt, not a network.
ideas.cost_note: Estimate 8-10 ns per generation, 3 generations about 25-30 ns, about 25x Perlin and 7x CellularDistance.

queue.name: FiskMeanders
queue.reason: Wild card. Omega loops and oxbows that no warp can make, top distinct score. Untested, 25-30 ns, and the parallel strips need a warp.

ideas.name: FlowNoise
ideas.one_liner: Flow noise: a hybrid phase on Perlin, Simplex and Cellular that rotates gradients or orbits features, giving seamless looping animation with no extra dimension. Looping 3D volumes become possible at all.
ideas.algorithm:
Gradient nodes: at each corner g(alpha)=u*cos(alpha)+v*sin(alpha), u,v orthonormal from hash (2D: v=Ju, so v.d=dot(u,(d.y,-d.x)); 3D per Gustavson: per-corner axis, or a 12 gradient table with a perpendicular table).
cos(alpha), sin(alpha) are computed once per lane; alpha=Phase(x).
Equivalently N(x,alpha)=N_u(x)*cos(alpha)+N_v(x)*sin(alpha).
Cellular: site_c(alpha)=c+.5+j1(h)*cos(alpha)+j2(h)*sin(alpha), j1,j2 two jitter vectors in one hash; elliptical orbit with no per-cell trig; orbit bound must fit the window.
A hybrid alpha varying in space is also seamless because alpha is sampled at x.

[PhaseSpinPerlin, volumetric-3d4d] Standard Perlin lattice (4/8 corners). Per corner hash h: gradient g = Grad[h & 15], axis a = Axis[(h>>4) & 15] (table of 16 unit vectors), phase phi = ((h>>8) & 15) * 2pi/16 -> cphi, sphi from a 16-entry table.
 theta = Omega * (w + Phase(p))  (Phase is a hybrid; in 2D/3D w = 0)
 S = Sin(theta), C = Cos(theta) once per lane
 per corner: s_i = S*cphi + C*sphi, c_i = C*cphi - S*sphi   // sin/cos(theta + phi_i)
 3D Rodrigues: g_i(theta) = g*c_i + (a x g)*s_i + a*(a.g)*(1 - c_i)   (precompute a x g and a(a.g) per table pair -> 256 x 3 vectors, or 6 muls on the fly)
 2D: g_i(theta) = (gx c_i - gy s_i, gx s_i + gy c_i)
 n = quintic-interpolated dot products as Perlin; same normalisation (rotated gradients stay unit length).
Period in w is exactly 2pi/Omega.
ideas.look:
A still frame looks like the base node. In motion: Perlin swirls in place with features neither translating nor fading, and Cellular cells jostle and return. Band-pass stays intact, unlike slicing 3D noise (Cook & DeRose, Gustavson). Boiling water, fire, looping clouds, breathing cells.
[FlowNoise, dcc-tools] A still frame looks like Perlin. In time it churns and swirls rather than crossfading or sliding. With pseudo-advection the fractal gains veiny, fluid lines (dcc_lens mode=3 adv=0.35). Good for fire, clouds, water surface, looping VFX.
ideas.why_new: Looping a 2D image needs 4D (torus in t) and looping a 3D volume needs 5D, which does not exist here; the phase gives both with no extra dimension. Looping 2D Cellular would otherwise cost 41 ns (4D). The graph form cos*NoiseA+sin*NoiseB covers gradient noise statistics but not Cellular, needs a per-frame user sin/cos, and has twice the hashing.
ideas.simd_plan:
Gradient: 2 gradient dots per corner, 1 sincos per lane: ~1.6x base. 2D ~1.8 ns; 3D ~3.5 ns; 4D ~7 ns. Cellular: +1 jitter pair: ~1.15x: 4.5/14/47 ns. So 2D loop at 4.5 ns vs 41 ns in 4D, a 9x saving.
[FlowNoise, dcc-tools] 2D estimated 1.7 ns (1.5x Perlin), 3D about 3.5 ns, 4D about 7 ns, with one sincos per lane plus Select per corner instead of per-corner trig. Time can be hybrid since the sincos is per lane. Same GenT layout as Perlin. Scalar proto 2.2x perlin2 with per-corner trig.
ideas.continuity: Same as base node in x (C2 Perlin, C0 Cellular F1). Smooth and 2pi periodic in alpha. Not prototyped; formulas are straightforward from the sources.
ideas.params: Hybrid: Phase (radians or turns). Added member on existing nodes, or new FlowPerlin, FlowSimplex, OrbitCellular. Orbit Radius for cellular.
ideas.risks:
Static look adds nothing, so it needs a video-capable eval. Fixed period of 2pi means all features share the same cycle, which reads as pulsing unless octaves use different speeds (a Fractal phase-speed member is needed). Cellular orbit plus jitter must fit the seam bound. 3D gradient pair table quality untested.
[PhaseSpinPerlin, volumetric-3d4d] Perlin's zeros at lattice corners are pinned, so under animation a faint stationary grid of zero-crossings can show (standard Perlin has it too, but motion makes it visible); mitigations: use inside FBm, or add a small per-corner oscillating value offset. High Omega reads as flicker rather than flow.
[SpinGradient, volumetric-3d4d] Untested. Perlin zero at lattice points remains, so iso-surfaces in animation stay pinned to the lattice corners, a visible artifact; mitigate through Simplex base or per-octave offset. Same 4.5 ns cost as 4D Perlin, so only worthwhile if looping or motion quality win. Well known concept (flow noise) with an exact loop as the new part. Tiling via 4D mapping feeds w as an ordinary coordinate, which does tile but is meaningless as time.
sources: from memory, not consulted: Perlin & Neyret 2001 'Flow Noise' (rotating gradients + pseudo-advection)
ideas.variant_notes: Rotating gradients with integer speeds give an exact loop. Included: orbiting Cellular sites (LoopPhase), per-corner phase to remove pulsing (PhaseSpinPerlin), Gustavson 3D axes. Value shows only in animation, so a video-capable eval is needed to judge it.
ideas.cost_note: Gradient form about 1.6x base: 1.8 / 3.5 / 7 ns. Orbiting Cellular about 1.15x: 4.5 / 14 / 47 ns, so a looping 2D Cellular is 9x cheaper than going through 4D.

queue.reason: Perlin-Neyret rotating gradients for looping animation at 1.6x base, static look same as Perlin. Belongs as a Phase member; only a loop check is needed.

ideas.name: GrowthAge
ideas.one_liner: A 3D growth-time field for wood: trunk radius smooth-min'ed with knot cones hashed along the axis, so rings wrap around knots and slicing gives cathedral grain.
ideas.algorithm: Grain along x. Trunk wobble: y'=y+W*n1(x), z'=z+W*n2(x) from low-frequency 1D noise. r=sqrt(y'^2+z'^2). age=r. For the 3 nearest knot cells along x (cell=floor(x/Spacing)): knot origin at (kx(h),0,0), azimuth from h, axis a tilted Tilt toward +x. q=p-origin, t=clamp(dot(q,a),0,KnotLength), db=|q-t*a|, kage=db/Grow+0.9*t+rnd*Offset. Polynomial smin: k=sat(.5+.5*(age-kage)/Sharp), age=lerp(age,kage,k)-Sharp*k*(1-k). Output: ScaleOutput(age,0,MaxAge). 2D slice: z=Board (hybrid), so Board Offset chooses plain-sawn versus quarter-sawn. 4D: w added to the ring offset so it stays a real 4D function. Feed into StrataBands.
ideas.look: Look-tested through StrataBands (m=3, rings=30). Excellent cathedral arches and grain flowing around knots, with closed ring islands where a branch crosses the board. The most recognisable real wood I have seen from a pointwise formula. Output alone is a smooth field, also usable as a growth mask for horn, bone or shell with different kernels.
ideas.why_new: Plain wood recipes (rings of distance plus noise) produce no knots, and noise warps cannot make grain deflect around a specific feature. This field is the hard part of wood. Researchers have published a very similar time-field approach (from memory: Larsson et al., procedural wood with knots, 2022), but I do not know of a noise library node for it.
ideas.simd_plan: 2D: 2 trunk 1D noises, 3 knots each with 1 sqrt and 5-6 ops, about 1.5-2x Perlin 2D. Same in 3D as the formula is 3D already, so 3D is the natural form and costs only slightly more than Perlin 3D. Knot window: 3 cells along x with one hash each, no 2D lattice at all.
ideas.continuity: C1 inside, except at the axis where r has a cone tip (C0) and where the capped t bends. Measured c0ratio 3.91 through a steep StrataBands, not through this node itself.
ideas.params: Knot Spacing, Knot Growth, Sharpness, Tilt, Knot Length, Trunk Wobble, Board Offset (hybrid), Max Age. Hybrid: Board Offset, Trunk Wobble.
ideas.risks: Non-stationary by nature, a single trunk around the axis, so it is meant to be used inside TileSplit Interior or with DomainOffset. Knot influence widens with radius, so uncapped cones leave the 3 cell window and seam; KnotLength must cap it (proto had no cap and looked clean at board offsets below 0.6, but this is not proven at large radius). Age is unbounded without the cap on distance from axis.
ideas.cost_note: 2D: 2 trunk 1D noises, 3 knots each with 1 sqrt and 5-6 ops, about 1.5-2x Perlin 2D.

queue.name: GrowthAge
queue.reason: Knot-aware wood growth field, the hard part of wood and not graphable. Single non-stationary trunk, so test instancing through tile-domain or stamp-scatter.

ideas.name: IsolatedExtremaNoise
ideas.one_liner: Disjoint-support bump noise: one compact kernel per active jittered cell, radius constrained so bumps never overlap or cross cell borders, giving exactly one maximum per active cell, superlevel components that are always single convex discs, exact feature counts, and a hybrid density control, from a 1-cell window.
ideas.algorithm:
Cell c = floor(x), h = Hash(seed, c). Point p_c = c + 0.5 + Jitter * rnd11(h) * 0.5 per axis (Jitter in [0,1]).
Radius r = RadiusFraction * 0.5 * (1 - Jitter) in cells (RadiusFraction <= 1 guarantees the bump stays inside its own cell: |p_c - cell centre| <= Jitter/2 and r <= (1 - Jitter)/2, so support never reaches the cell boundary and never overlaps a neighbour; the window is the single cell).
Active weight: a_c = smoothstep( (Density(x) - rnd01(h')) / DensitySoft ) with Density a hybrid in [0,1] (continuous fade-in instead of a hard gate, so spatially varying density stays continuous).
Amplitude A_c = lerp(Height Min, Height Max, rnd01(h'')) ; Bipolar flag flips the sign for half the cells (pits).
Kernel K(t) = (1 - t^2)^3 for t < 1 else 0 (C2 at the edge), t = |x - p_c| / r.
Out = Base(x) * BaseAmp + a_c * A_c * K(t)   (Base is a hybrid, default 0).
Guarantees (Base = 0): every active cell contributes exactly one strict local maximum at p_c; for any threshold t > 0 each connected component of {out > t} is one convex disc centred on p_c; the number of components above t in an area is Binomial(cells, P(A_c a_c > t)), i.e. exact expected density per cell. With a weak base (|grad Base| * BaseAmp small compared to A_min * 2.6 / r) the maxima shift slightly but remain one per bump.
Overlap flag: r up to 1 cell with a 3^d window, loses the guarantee, gives standard sparse-convolution 'pebbles'.
ideas.look: A field of separate domes (or craters when Bipolar) on a flat floor, each sitting in its own cell, sizes and heights random, never fused: like raindrops on glass, lunar craters that never cut each other, tree crowns in a plantation, pores in foam. Thresholded at any level: scattered discs with controlled count that never merge. With a Base noise: terrain with islands that never join, or guaranteed isolated hills.
ideas.why_new: CellularDistance F1 discs merge whenever two points come close, and per-cell heights via CellularValue multiply are discontinuous at Voronoi borders. This node gives exact Morse control (one maximum per active cell, nothing else), topology control (all superlevel components are genus-0 discs), exact density via a hybrid, and it costs half a Perlin because the window is one cell. Good as a placement/feature field where every maximum should be an object.
ideas.simd_plan: One hash per lane (three bit fields), one kernel polynomial, one Sqrt-free t^2 compare (kernel in t^2: (1 - t^2)^3 needs no sqrt), Select for t^2 >= 1, plus the hybrid Density/Base evaluations. ~0.5x Perlin in all dimensions (dimension agnostic GenT). Overlap mode = 3^d window like Cellular.
ideas.continuity: C2 (kernel is C2 at its edge, zero before the cell boundary; the density fade is C1), so C1 overall when Density varies.
ideas.params: Jitter; Radius Fraction (0..1); Height Min / Height Max; Density (hybrid 0..1); Density Soft; Bipolar (bool); Base (hybrid), Base Amp; Overlap (bool, 3^d window); Feature Scale; Seed Offset.
ideas.risks: Looks sparse by nature: the flat floor dominates (that is the feature, but it is not a general-purpose noise). Jitter and radius trade off (jitter 0.5 gives radius <= 0.25 cell). The underlying grid is visible at low jitter; Overlap mode exists for a more organic look at the price of the guarantee.
ideas.cost_note: ~0.5x Perlin in all dimensions (dimension agnostic GenT).

ideas.name: KnotFlow
ideas.one_liner: Layers that bend smoothly around scattered obstacles using windowed potential-flow doublets, for wood grain around knots, strata around concretions and wakes behind rocks.
ideas.algorithm: s=n.x+warp*source(x). For each feature in the 3^D window: dy=s-(n.p_i); r=|x-p_i| measured with the warped coordinate along n (x' = x with s replacing the n component); outside=(n.p_i)+dy*(1-(R/r)^D); inside=(n.p_i)+A*(R-r), giving concentric rings; target=Select(r>R,outside,inside); w=smoothstep(1,R,r); psi+=gate*w*(target-s). Output a stripe profile of psi*freq, such as an asymmetric sawtooth min(fr/0.8,(1-fr)/0.2) for early and late wood. On the circle r=R, psi is constant, so stripes hug the knot. The exponent D makes it dimension-agnostic: 2D is the cylinder stream function, while 3D and 4D use the analogous sheet deflection.
ideas.look: Plank-like parallel lines that flow around round knots with rings inside, and streamlines closing behind them; it reads as sawn timber at once. Could also read as draped sediment around concretions, or raked gravel around stones.
ideas.why_new: A domain warp cannot wrap stripes around a disc without pinching or crossing them; this formula keeps lines non-crossing because it is a stream function. The published wood work (Larsson et al.) merges a trunk and knot distance field with a smooth minimum, whereas this is a much cheaper stripe-only approach and needs no trunk model.
ideas.simd_plan: Per feature: hash, one sqrt, integer power of (R/r). Estimated 5.5 ns in 2D (5x Perlin, 1.4x CellularDistance), 16 ns in 3D, 50 ns in 4D. Try 2^D corners with jitter (not tested for this idea). Window fade guarantees no seams.
ideas.continuity: C0 outside core; at r=R both branches equal n.p_i, so psi is C0 with a slope change. Dense scanlines: 0 jumps. A sawtooth profile adds a creased peak by design, not a jump, as the prototype's form is triangular.
ideas.params: Frequency (hybrid), Direction, Knot Density (hybrid), Knot Radius Min/Max, Ring Spacing A, Profile Skew, Warp Source (hybrid).
ideas.risks: Overlapping knots add perturbations and can pinch lines or make stripes cross, since superposition is not exact with windowing. Only 2D was rendered; 3D sheet deflection is a formula-level claim. This is a look, not a tree model, so whole-trunk ring curvature needs a separate radial source.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated 5.5 ns in 2D (5x Perlin, 1.4x CellularDistance), 16 ns in 3D, 50 ns in 4D.

ideas.name: LatticePhasor
ideas.one_liner: Phasor-style constant-contrast stripes on a Perlin corner lattice with no atan2: labyrinths, tiger stripes and fingerprints from one orientation input.
ideas.algorithm:
Cell=q*wavelength, with q about 1.5. For each of the 2^D corners c: h=hash(c); ang=Orientation(p)+(rnd(h)-0.5)*Spread when Orientation is connected, else ang from the hash; dir=(cos,sin)(ang); ph=k*dot(dir,p-c)+rnd2(h)*2pi. Weight w=product of quintic fades, as in Value noise.
re=sum(w*Cos(ph)); im=sum(w*Sin(ph)).
Out=re*InvSqrt(re*re+im*im+eps*eps), which equals cos(arg z).
Wave shapes: run the unit (re,im)/|z| through a charge loop for harmonics; a tri or saw needs a polynomial atan.

[OrientedStripes, nature-phenomena] Dir=Hybrid direction, normalised (source is angle, or two sources in 3D). Lattice form: for each of 2^D corners: phi=2*pi*(r1+freq*(dir.(f-corner))); weight=product of quintic fade; (C,S)+=weight*(cos phi,sin phi). Phase=atan2(S,C) (or normalised C with floor max(|(C,S)|,0.2)). Ripple profile: ph=Phase/(2*pi)+0.5; out=ph/asym for ph<asym, else (1-ph)/(1-asym), where asym is the windward fraction. The published Phacelle form uses a 4x4 window, jitter*0.5, weight max(exp(-2 d^2)-0.01111,0), and shared orientation; Phasor noise uses per-kernel orientations and far more kernels.
ideas.look: Tested. With an orientation field and cell=1.5 wavelengths, the result is tiger or fingerprint-like constant-width stripes with natural forks and chevrons, and this was the cleanest fingerprint look of everything tried. Larger cells (3.75 wavelengths) break into chopped stripe domains with seams. Random orientation per corner gives zebra camouflage patches. Orientation from the gradient of a potential makes stripes follow contours, with starbursts at critical points.
ideas.why_new: Phase-only output at a fixed wavelength has no equivalent on the sheet. Compared with published phasor noise, it replaces sparse Gabor impulses with a dense corner lattice and replaces atan2 with Re/|z|, making it Perlin-shaped in cost and structure. Orientation is sampled at the current position, so any noise steers it.
ideas.simd_plan:
Branch free. Window is 2^D corners, 4 / 8 / 16. Each corner: hash, one Sin+Cos of orientation (shared when Spread=0), one Sin+Cos of phase. Estimated 2-4x Perlin in 2D and similar in 3D and 4D; not measured. 3D needs two orientation angles or a director from 3 sources, and normalised gives lamellae.
[OrientedStripes, nature-phenomena] Lattice form: 4 sincos in 2D, about 3.5 ns plus source (3x Perlin); 8 in 3D, about 7 ns; 16 in 4D, about 14 ns. Published 4x4 form: 16 sincos, about 16 ns in 2D, and 64 in 3D, so it is unattractive above 2D. Add FS atan2 for the profile, or use the two components directly.
ideas.continuity: C0 with eps>0, verified numerically (ratio 8.3). With eps=0 there are point discontinuities at phasor zeros (forks). Sampling Orientation at p means the local phase gradient includes a term proportional to |p-c|*grad(theta), bounded by the cell size.
ideas.params: Hybrid: Orientation, Spread, Wavelength (Frequency), eps. Float: Cell/Wavelength ratio. Source is optional.
ideas.risks:
Wavelength fluctuates near fork chains and where Orientation changes quickly. Some square-lattice imprint in orientation domains could appear with random orientation; FFT not inspected. Stripes on the 4D torus for GenTileable project random 4D directions into a 2D tangent, so the observed wavelength varies per corner. Overlaps with a phasor noise node if another lens proposes it: keep whichever is cheaper.
[OrientedStripes, nature-phenomena] Lattice form has defect positions tied to the integer lattice and no frequency guarantees. An FFT comparison with the 4x4 form was not run. Hybrid frequency changes phase coherence and may stretch stripes. Direction fields with singularities give abrupt changes.
sources: Tricard et al. 2019, Procedural Phasor Noise (from memory, not consulted)
ideas.variant_notes: OrientedStripes is the same 2^D corner lattice and contributes the asymmetric ripple profile.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated 2-4x Perlin in 2D and similar in 3D and 4D; not measured.

queue.reason: 2^D-corner phasor with no atan2, ~3x Perlin in every dimension (J4 top pick). Run beside phasor-noise and read the FFT for square-lattice imprint, since this is the likely shipped kernel.

ideas.name: MagicNoise
ideas.one_liner: Blender's Magic trig-feedback made seedable and non-repeating with incommensurate plane waves, at a cost that does not grow with dimension.
ideas.algorithm: Blender form: a,b,c are sin/cos of diagonal combinations, then depth steps a=Cos(a-b-c)*d, etc., periodic on a diagonal lattice. Proposed form: phases p1,p2,p3 from seed bits; three unit-ish direction vectors at incommensurate angles and frequencies per dimension, e.g. 2D (.809,.588), (-.393,1.210), (-1.570,-.392). a=Sin(dot(u1,x)+p1); b=Sin(dot(u2,x)+p2); c=Sin(dot(u3,x)+p3). for i in 0..Depth-1 (constant): na=Sin(D*(b-c)+p1+1.1*i); nb=Cos(D*(c+a)+p2); nc=Sin(D*(a-b)+p3-0.7*i); a,b,c=na,nb,nc. out=(a+b+c)/3*1.5.
ideas.look: Agate eyes, oil-film rings, glassy interference blobs, psychedelic contours. Depth 3: rings in soft cells. Depth 5: intricate filigree. Blender's lattice form: diagonal repeating tiles (visible in my test). Prototype: dcc_lens modes 4 (Blender) and 5 (quasi-periodic).
ideas.why_new: No lattice, no hash per point, and a look absent from the sheet: closed concentric contours with no cell structure. Same cost in 4D as in 2D, so it is the only family here where 4D (and GenTileable) is cheap. Not a graph: no Sin of a value, and feedback needs per-iteration phases.
ideas.simd_plan: 3+Depth*3 Sin/Cos, no hashing, constant loop. Depth 3: 12 trig calls, est 6-10 ns in every dimension; about 7x Perlin in 2D, 2x in 4D and 0.2x CellularDistance 4D. Far coords: wrap each dot with Modulus by 2*pi before trig; phases at incommensurate frequencies then wrap cleanly. Seed needs only 3 Convert-from-int lanes.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity (compositions of sin), measured c0ratio 7.98. Steepens as D and Depth rise (max slope 36 at Depth 3 D 1.5).
ideas.params: Depth (int), Distortion D (hybrid), Scale via Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks: Statistics are non-stationary-looking and seeds feel like the same family. Direction vectors are hand picked: need testing for visible beat periods at large scale. Quasi-periodic not random, so long-range structure may repeat approximately. Range uneven (mean drifts with seed, measured 0.12).
ideas.cost_note: Depth 3: 12 trig calls, est 6-10 ns in every dimension; about 7x Perlin in 2D, 2x in 4D and 0.2x CellularDistance 4D.

ideas.name: MultigridNoise
ideas.one_liner: N families of parallel 1D lattices (de Bruijn multigrid) instead of a point lattice: aperiodic Penrose-like polygon mosaics, exact edge distance with no window search, and quasi-crystal smooth interference, all in O(N) per sample in any dimension.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Families N (default 5), Mode {Mosaic, EdgeDistance, Smooth}, LineJitter J in [0,0.5], Rotation.
Setup (when params change): direction table d_i, i<N. 2D: d_i = (cos(Rotation + i*pi/N), sin(...)). 3D: the 6 icosahedral 5-fold axes normalize(0, +-1, +-phi) perms (N fixed 6) or N Fibonacci-sphere directions. 4D: N directions from a fixed seeded low-discrepancy set on S3. Also per-family offsets gamma_i = rnd01(hash(seed, i)).
Gen(p):
  for i in 0..N-1 (fixed count, unrolled):
    t = dot(p, d_i) + gamma_i
    k = floor(t); f = t - k
    if J > 0: line positions L(k) = k + J*rnd11(hash(seed, i, k)); a = L(k); b = L(k+1); c = L(k-1);
       below = t < a;  lo = Select(below, c, a); hi = Select(below, a, b); k = k - (below?1:0); f = (t-lo)/(hi-lo)
    keep k_i, f_i
  Mosaic:  value = rnd11( hash(seed ^ Sum_i k_i * Prime_i) )            // Prime_i: X,Y,Z,W + 4 more odd constants
  EdgeDistance: e = min_i min(f_i, 1-f_i) * cellWidth_i; value = ScaleOutput(e, 0, 0.5)   // = Euclidean distance to nearest line = distance to region boundary
  Smooth: value = Sum_i hermite1D(k_i, f_i) where hermite1D = quintic lerp of g0*f and g1*(f-1), g0,g1 = rnd11(hash(seed,i,k)), rnd11(hash(seed,i,k+1)); normalize by sqrt(N)*c.
Graph combos (Mosaic * smoothstep(EdgeDistance)) give leaded glass / cracked glaze.

[QuasiCrystalCell, math-physics] Setup: unit normals zeta_j, j=0..N-1 (2D: angle 2 pi j/N for odd N, pi j/N for even N; 3D: 6 icosahedral normals (0,+-1,+-phi)/norm; 4D: 8 normals from the 4D cross-polytope rotated by an irrational matrix). Offsets gamma_j = rnd01(seed,j) - mean (sum 0 gives Penrose, sum 1/2 anti-Penrose).
Gen(seed, x): x' = x/FeatureScale
  for j: t_j = dot(zeta_j, x') + gamma_j ; K_j = Ceil(t_j) ; lam_j = K_j - t_j  (in [0,1))
  Mode RegionValue:  v = hash(seed, K_0..K_{N-1}) -> [-1,1]      (multigrid polygons; quasiperiodic, each region is dual to one tiling vertex)
  Mode GridDistance: v = min_j |lam_j - 0.5| * 2                    (distance to nearest hyperplane of the N-grid: a 5-fold 'star web')
  Mode VertexDistance: z = sum_j K_j zeta_j (dual Penrose vertex, piecewise constant); p' = (N/2) x' + eta, eta = sum_j gamma_j zeta_j ; v = 1 - |p' - z| / rmax   (quasiperiodic bump field with N-fold rosettes)
  Mode PenroseTile (2D only, exact rhomb containing the tiling-space point p=x'):
    y = (p - eta) * (2/N)                       // back-map, since M = sum zeta zeta^T = (N/2) I
    for each pair (r,s) of the N(N-1)/2 families (fixed loop):
      a = dot(zeta_r,y)+gamma_r ; b = dot(zeta_s,y)+gamma_s
      for (kr,ks) in {Floor a, Ceil a} x {Floor b, Ceil b}:            // 4 candidate grid intersections
        xi = solve zeta_r.xi = kr-gamma_r, zeta_s.xi = ks-gamma_s     // 2x2 inverse precomputed per pair
        z0 = sum_j (j==r?kr : j==s?ks : Ceil(dot(zeta_j,xi)+gamma_j)) * zeta_j
        q = p - z0 ; cr = cross(zeta_r,zeta_s)
        u = cross(q,zeta_s)/cr ; v = cross(zeta_r,q)/cr
        inside = (u>=0)&(u<1)&(v>=0)&(v<1)                              // exactly one hit over all candidates
        Select-accumulate: tileType = pair index (thin/thick by |cr|), corner z0, local (u,v)
    Outputs: TileValue = hash(z0 as integer 5-vector) ; TileEdge = min(u,1-u,v,1-v)*|cr| (distance to rhomb edge) ; TileType = thin/thick
3D: RegionValue/GridDistance/VertexDistance with the 6-grid (icosahedral quasicrystal); exact rhombohedra deferred (20 triples x 8 candidates).
ideas.look:
Mosaic: an aperiodic arrangement of rhombs, pentagons and stars with local 5-/10-fold symmetry (girih / Penrose feel) at N=5; kagome triangles+hexagons at N=3; squares+octagons at N=4; irregular organic polygons with LineJitter. EdgeDistance: crisp crack/mortar networks of straight segments with no cell-size blow-up, inverted = beveled tiles. Smooth: quasi-crystalline rosettes and moire-like interference ridges. Uses: tiled floors, stained glass, basalt/mud cracks that are not Voronoi, alien hull plating, fabric weave (N=2 with jitter), quasi-crystal scientific textures.
[PentagridCells, lattice-kernels] Stained-glass rose windows, 5-fold and 7-fold stars, quasicrystal electron-diffraction feel, pavements, gem facets. Prototyped N=5 and 7: strongly distinct stars and polygons, never exactly repeating, X-junctions everywhere.
ideas.why_new: Nothing on the sheet is aperiodic-yet-ordered; Cellular always gives convex Voronoi cells and its edge distance (F2-F1) is approximate and window-bound. Here the region boundary distance is exact, costs O(N) with no window, polygons can be non-convex stars, and the cost does not grow as 3^dim: 4D is as cheap as 2D (per-direction dot is the only dim-dependent op).
ideas.simd_plan: N x (dot, floor, min, int mul, xor). 2D N=5 about 1 ns AVX2 (proto: 1.57x perlin2 scalar with sincos in the loop, which become constants). 3D N=6: about 1.5 ns. 4D N=9: about 3 ns. Direction tables are constants; gamma_j come from seed hash per lane.
ideas.continuity: Mosaic: discontinuous (piecewise constant). EdgeDistance: C0 (creases on medial lines, like F1). Smooth: C2 (quintic 1D Hermite).
ideas.params: Families (int 2..8), Mode enum, LineJitter (float), Rotation (float; hybrid optional so the quasi-lattice can twist across space), Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks:
Smooth mode has a star-shaped spectrum (N lines) so it is visibly structured, which is the point but not isotropic. LineJitter with J near 0.5 can make neighbouring lines nearly touch, producing sliver polygons. Mosaic hash tuples with N>4 need extra prime constants; verify no visible correlations.
[PentagridCells, lattice-kernels] Lines are infinite, so a long straight line is visible at wide zoom; combine with a warp when unwanted. N=3 and N=4 degenerate to periodic look unless gamma is irrational-offset. On 4D torus tiling the lines become curves, fine but different look.
[QuasiCrystalCell, math-physics] PenroseTile cost and the 3D exact tiling is heavy; VertexDistance normalisation rmax needs measuring (bounded by (N-2)/2); degenerate gamma giving triple intersections must be avoided by tiny irrational offsets.
sources: N. G. de Bruijn, 'Algebraic theory of Penrose's non-periodic tilings of the plane', 1981 (cited from memory, not fetched)
ideas.variant_notes: Hash of the N-tuple of line indices. Exact edge distance needs no window. 3D and 4D are cheaper than Perlin, which suits tiling.
ideas.cost_note: 2D N=5 about 1 ns AVX2 (proto: 1.57x perlin2 scalar with sincos in the loop, which become constants).

queue.reason: de Bruijn multigrid at ~1 ns with exact edge distance and no window (J4 top pick). Mosaic mode is the keeper; test jitter against the long-straight-lines complaint.

ideas.name: MultipoleNoise
ideas.one_liner: Gradient-noise generalised to higher angular order: each lattice point carries an order-m harmonic kernel (monopole=value, dipole=Perlin, quadrupole=saddle, octupole=trefoil), implemented in any dimension with a random 2-plane.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Order {0,1,2,3,Mixed}, Radius R, Jitter (0 = lattice-corner look), Falloff exponent.
Per point (3^dim jittered window, or Jitter 0): h = hash; q = c+o+0.5+Jitter*(rndvec(h)-0.5); r = p-q; s2 = |r|^2
  a = hashed unit vector (dim-D), b = unit vector orthogonal to a (2D: b = perp(a); nD: Gram-Schmidt one step + InvSqrt)
  u = dot(a,r), v = dot(b,r)
  m = Order or (h>>30)&3 for Mixed
  harm_m: m=0: 1; m=1: u; m=2: u^2 - v^2; m=3: u^3 - 3 u v^2      (Re (u+iv)^m)
  Mixed: compute all four, pick with two Selects on the m bits
  acc += harm_m * max(0, 1 - s2/R^2)^Falloff
 value = acc * norm_m (peak of rho^m (1-rho^2)^F at rho^2 = m/(m+2F); divide, then an overlap factor measured once per Order).
Optional 'Hashed phase' is implicit in a,b orientation. For Jitter 0 the window can shrink to 2^dim corners if R <= 1 (document the seam-free condition R <= 1).
ideas.look: Order 2: a carpet of saddles / four-leaf clovers, every lattice point a mountain pass; thresholded it becomes interlocking plus-shaped and bow-tie blobs; terrain reads as knotted ridges with far more cols than Perlin. Order 3: three-pointed stars tiling into a triangular feel. Mixed: a richer, less uniform Perlin-like noise where bumps, dipoles and saddles coexist, nice as an FBm base that avoids the Perlin 'blob' look.
ideas.why_new: Perlin is exactly m=1 with a separable window; Simplex likewise. Higher orders change the topology of the zero set (ratio of saddles to extrema) which is what makes terrain look knotted versus blobby, and no modifier on an m=1 noise can add angular order. Also provides a Jitter-free 'surflet' variant of Perlin with isotropic radial windows as a side effect.
ideas.simd_plan: 3^dim window (or 2^dim at Jitter 0): per point ~20 ops: hash, 2 dots, few mults, window poly. 2D ~1.2x CellularDistance (4.7 ns), Jitter 0 variant ~1.5x Perlin. 3D ~1.2x Cellular 3D; 4D 81 points (or 16 corners at Jitter 0). Dimension agnostic via (a,b) plane trick; Mixed is two Selects, no branches.
ideas.continuity: C(Falloff-1) at the support edge (Falloff 4 gives C3), analytic inside.
ideas.params: Order, Radius, Jitter, Falloff, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks: m>=2 kernels vanish at the lattice point and at the rim, so the energy is in a ring; too small Radius leaves a visible lattice ring structure at Jitter 0. Amplitude normalisation differs per order (table). Visual difference from Perlin at Mixed may be subtler than hoped; the Order 2 and 3 pure modes are the distinctive ones.
sources: K. Perlin, 'Improving Noise', SIGGRAPH 2002 (surflet view of gradient noise; from memory, not fetched)
ideas.cost_note: 2D ~1.2x CellularDistance (4.7 ns), Jitter 0 variant ~1.5x Perlin. 3D ~1.2x Cellular 3D; 4D 81 points (or 16 corners at Jitter 0).
