queue.reason: Disputed: J3 top pick for changing zero-set topology, while the others expect near-Perlin. A kernel swap in a Perlin proto settles it quickly.

ideas.name: NewtonBasins
ideas.one_liner: Damped Newton on a pair (or D-tuple) of noises, coloured by the root reached: smooth patches meeting along genuinely fractal fern-like and scalloped borders with zero octaves.
ideas.algorithm:
F(q)=(n1(q),n2(q)). Repeat N (6..8): evaluate n1,n2 and gradients; det=ax*by-ay*bx with sign-preserving floor |det|>=1e-3; s=(by*n1-ay*n2, -bx*n1+ax*n2)/det; scale s to |s|<=MaxStep (about 0.35); q-=s. Output a value noise or ColorSource sampled at q. In 3D use 3 noises with a 3x3 Cramer solve; 4D uses 4 noises with a cofactor solve. Prototype: dyn_lens mode=5,N=8,maxstep=0.35; zoom with sheet --window 3.

[NewtonBasin, dynamics-iteration] F(p) = (f_1(p), ..., f_d(p)) d internal gradient noises; roots are isolated points (about one per few cells). J = [d f_i / d x_j].
  q = p; count = 0
  for k in 0..N-1:
      f = F(q); J = Jac(q)
      step = (J^T J + lambda I)^-1 J^T f          // Levenberg-Marquardt; lambda=0 is pure Newton (J^-1 f). 2x2/3x3 closed form, 4x4 cofactors
      step *= min(1, maxStep / (|step| + 1e-9))   // clamp jump length, branch-free
      q = q - step
      count += smoothstep(eps2, eps1, |F(q)|)     // fractional 'already converged' count
  Output enum:
    RootId   : rnd11(hash(floor(q*CellScale)))  or Source B(q)
    Residual : |F(q)| remapped
    SoftCount: count / N
    RootDist : |q - p| / maxReach
ideas.look:
Verified at zoom. Large flat patches, with parts of the borders in Julia-style lobes, scallops and fern fronds, and occasional chaotic wedges of tiny detail near curves where det J=0. Boundary detail is self-similar with no octaves. Good for alien terrain masks, stained-glass or lichen, mineral inclusions, fantasy map provinces with ornate coasts.
[NewtonBasin, dynamics-iteration] A mosaic of basins, each a smooth region around one root, separated by boundaries that near every basin triple point fragment into ever-finer interleaved tongues (Wada-like Newton fractal lace) when Damping is small; Residual draws those boundaries as bright circuit-like filaments on a black field; SoftCount shades each basin with concentric convergence bands. Raising Damping continuously morphs it into a soft organic cell map similar to FlowWatershed's catchments. Textures: cracked lacquer, circuit traces, lichen, frost ferns; masks for 'where things break'.
ideas.why_new: Fractal detail here comes from dynamics, not added frequency, so it only appears at borders, while interiors stay perfectly flat. Thresholded FBm and warped Cellular cannot have flat interiors with lobed fractal coasts.
ideas.simd_plan: 2N gradients in 2D (about 14 gradients, about 20 ns with analytic Perlin). 3D 3N gradients (about 60 ns). 4D 4N gradients (about 190 ns) plus a 4x4 solve, so offer 4D as expensive. Clamp with Min and Select only.
ideas.continuity: Discontinuous at basin borders (sign-preserving det floor, measured c0ratio 1.1). Interior C-infinity except where the step clamp is active.
ideas.params: Iterations, MaxStep (hybrid; lower gives less fractal more cell-like), Source pair frequency, Output enum (RootValue, RootDistance |q-p|), hybrid Value source.
ideas.risks:
Heavy high-frequency content in the wedges will alias at low sample rate; no analytic range on Distance output. 3D slices look less ornate than 2D. Two octaves become noisier, so keep the input simple.
[NewtonBasin, dynamics-iteration] Pure Newton can wander far (hence the clamp); fractal detail is unbounded so mipmapping/aliasing issues for rendering; needs the internal gradient-noise utility.
ideas.variant_notes: Damping morphs from fractal lace to smooth cells. High-frequency wedges alias.
ideas.cost_note: 2N gradients in 2D (about 14 gradients, about 20 ns with analytic Perlin). 3D 3N gradients (about 60 ns).

queue.name: NewtonBasins
queue.reason: Wild card. Flat interiors with fractal basin borders at zero octaves. 14+ gradient evals, heavy aliasing and weak 3D, but only a look is at stake.

ideas.name: PercolationLattice
ideas.one_liner: A field whose zero level is literally bond percolation: one parameter flips which phase is connected while coverage barely moves.
ideas.algorithm: Corners: value = (-1)^(i+j) * lerp(HMin, 1, rnd(hash)), so even corners are strict maxima and odd corners strict minima under quintic interpolation. Along each edge the sign changes exactly once, so each cell has four zero crossings and two possible pairings. Cell term: s = smoothstep(-0.02, 0.02, P - rnd(cellHash))*2 - 1; add s*A*b(u)*b(v) with b(t) = 16 t^2 (1-t)^2, which vanishes with zero slope on cell borders. With A larger than the bilinear centre (A = 0.4, HMin = 0.5), s alone decides whether + corners or - corners link through the cell. That is bond percolation on the even sublattice with its exactly known p_c = 1/2. 3D: 8 corners plus 6 face terms s_f*A*b(u)*b(v)*c(w), c = quintic falloff to zero on the opposite face, plus body term. Follow with a built-in low-frequency warp to hide the lattice.
ideas.look: P=0: bright dots on connected dark. P=0.5: critical labyrinth with long winding, power-law clusters. P=1: dark dots on connected bright. Hybrid P gives regions of sea-connected islands turning into land-connected lakes under one threshold. Useful for caves, wetlands, circuit patterns and cracked-to-solid transitions. Measured over window 128, threshold 0: P=0.45 coverage 0.486, largest cluster share +0.039 / -0.883; P=0.5 coverage 0.499, +0.345 / -0.458; P=0.55 coverage 0.512, +0.875 / -0.043. Full range P=0 to 1 moves coverage 0.369 to 0.630.
ideas.why_new: Connectivity is an independent, directly addressable control. Thresholding Perlin ties connectivity to coverage: T=+-0.1 is needed to reach coverage 0.38 to 0.62 for a comparable flip, and connectivity cannot be set per region without changing how much land there is. A related Truchet node gives fixed-width loops but no continuous height field, and no P.
ideas.simd_plan: 2D: 4 corner hashes + 1 cell hash, quintic lerp, 2 bumps: about 1.5x Value. Measured 2.9x perlin2 scalar including two warp Perlin evals. 3D: 8 + 7 hashes. 4D: 16 corners + 24 two-face terms is the expensive version. Branch-free; sign from (i+j+...) & 1 via int ops. Hybrid P per lane is safe because s is a smooth function of (P - r).
ideas.continuity: C1 for value (quintic plus bumps with zero border slope). Measured c0ratio 8, max slope 5.5. The smoothstep on s keeps hybrid P continuous.
ideas.params: P Connectivity (hybrid), HMin (float), Bridge Amp (float), Warp (float), Output Min/Max. A Compensate option could subtract a P-dependent offset to null the coverage drift, untested.
ideas.risks: Lattice structure is visible in the gray image even with warp 0.35, since it is a warped egg-crate at P=0 or 1. Strong warp hides it but breaks nothing, because a homeomorphic warp keeps the topology. 3D range reached +-1.66 and needs normalising. In 3D both phases can percolate together and the threshold is not 1/2; the 3D transition has not been measured. Only 2D statistics were measured. Not a replacement for general noise: it is narrowband and centred on the lattice frequency.
ideas.cost_note: 2D: 4 corner hashes + 1 cell hash, quintic lerp, 2 bumps: about 1.5x Value. Measured 2.9x perlin2 scalar including two warp Perlin evals.

ideas.name: PeriodicFBm
ideas.one_liner: Lattice noises that wrap by integer period per axis, giving tileable 2D at a quarter of the cost and tileable 3D, which FastNoise cannot do today.
ideas.algorithm: Hash uses wrapped lattice indices: ix' = ix - P*floor(ix/P) (AND mask when P is a power of two), per axis, P=0 disables. The offset vector still uses unwrapped ix so gradients and distances are correct. Built-in octave loop: P doubles with lacunarity 2, seed changes per octave. Kernel enum: Perlin, Value, Cellular F1, Cellular inverted, PerlinWorley (Perlin remapped by inverted Worley FBm, the cloud base shape). Cellular wraps neighbour cell indices in the 3^d window the same way. Output tiles exactly at world size P*Feature Scale.
ideas.look: Normal Perlin or Worley, but periodic. PerlinWorley gives billowy cauliflower cloud masses, new on the sheet. For bakes: tiling terrain textures, 3D cloud volumes, tile materials.
ideas.why_new: On Auburn's list: #2 says '3D periodic noise using modulus grid coordinates, probably only valid for value, perlin and cellular noise'. #12 asks for tiled 3D volumes especially cellular; Auburn replied it would need 6D via the hypertorus. FastNoiseLite issues #4, #20, #33, #53, #74, #86, #87 all ask for tiling; #53 links a fork doing 2^N periods and #86 asks for tileability again. Can't be a domain op since fractal parents don't pass period information to sources.
ideas.simd_plan: Same as Perlin or Cellular plus a mask or float floor per axis per lattice lookup, about +10%. Estimated AVX2 per octave: Perlin 1.2 / 2.4 / 4.8 ns, vs 4.3 ns for tiling via 4D, so about 3.5x cheaper in 2D with no hypertorus stretch. Cellular costs the same as CellularDistance.
ideas.continuity: Same as the kernel (Perlin C2 interpolant). Seam fully continuous since hash values match. Non-integer Feature Scale relative to the tile size breaks the tile, so period is the defining parameter.
ideas.params: Kernel enum, Period X/Y/Z/W (int), Octaves, Gain, Lacunarity (int), Jitter, Feature Scale derived or checked.
ideas.risks: Simplex family cannot use it because of the skewed lattice (Auburn notes this). Period and Feature Scale need clear UI. Duplicates some kernels unless Perlin/Value/Cellular kernels are shared. Warps above it break the tile; see DomainTile for those.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated AVX2 per octave: Perlin 1.2 / 2.4 / 4.8 ns, vs 4.3 ns for tiling via 4D, so about 3.5x cheaper in 2D with no hypertorus stretch.

queue.name: PeriodicFBm
queue.reason: No new look: wrapped lattice indices give true tileable 3D and ~3.5x cheaper 2D tiling (J4 top pick). Should land as a Period member on lattice nodes. Only tiling needs checking.

ideas.name: PhacelleNoise
ideas.one_liner: Cell-blended stripes that follow an input direction field with constant width: leaf veins and drainage patterns, and the base of the runevision erosion filter.
ideas.algorithm: Input direction dir at p: Angle (hybrid), or gradient of a Field source by forward difference, normalised. side = perp(dir)*Frequency*TAU. For each cell in the 3^dim window: h=hash(cell); c=cell+0.25+0.5*rnd(h) per axis; v=p-c; wgt=Max(0,1-dot(v,v)/1.5625)^3; ph=dot(v,side); C+=wgt*Cos(ph); S+=wgt*Sin(ph); W+=wgt. Then C/=W; S/=W; m=Max(1-Norm, Sqrt(C*C+S*S)); out=S/m. Original uses 4x4 with exp(-2 r2) minus a constant; my look test shows tight-jitter 3x3 with this polynomial is visually equal.
ideas.look: With a field from low-frequency noise: leaf venation, river deltas, feather barbs, radiating streaks with forks. Constant direction: zebra lines with soft defects. Prototype: dcc_lens mode=15.
ideas.why_new: Stripes aligned to an arbitrary field at constant width and without looping artifacts; warping a sine does neither. Cost is a fraction of Phasor per the author's count (16 loops vs 144-400). Erosion filter ports already exist for Blender and Houdini, so demand is real.
ideas.simd_plan: 9/27/81 sites with Sin+Cos each, about 13 / 40 / 120 ns (12x/18x/28x Perlin) plus (dim+1) Field evals. 4x4 window is 16/64/256 and not worth it. Constant direction collapses to one sincos, which is CarrierStripes territory. Bounded phase allows polynomial sincos.
ideas.continuity: Constant direction with Norm<1: C0, measured c0ratio 8.0 at Norm 0.25-0.75; Norm=1 gives jumps (1.81). Direction from a gradient field: jumps at the field's critical points (measured 1.53), because a unit direction is undefined there. Fix by fading stripe amplitude toward 0 as |grad| goes to 0, as the erosion post does.
ideas.params: Frequency (hybrid), Angle (hybrid) or Field (GeneratorSource), Offset (hybrid, shifts phase), Norm (hybrid), Grid Jitter (float, capped).
ideas.risks:
Singular points in the direction field need the fade. MPL-2.0 applies to the author's code; a clean implementation from this description should be checked against that. 3D direction needs a chosen perpendicular, since a side vector is underdetermined; author's post covers 2D only.
[PhacelleStripes, repo-demand] Too few cells per stripe gives grain, too many turns all ridge (author). Reimplement from the blog since shader code is MPL-2.0. Output depends on Direction being normalised. No prototype run by me.
ideas.variant_notes: Kept apart from PhasorNoise because one direction is shared by all kernels per lane, which is the source of its cost saving. PhasorCellNoise is credited here for its Spread=0 'in unison' mode.
ideas.cost_note: 9/27/81 sites with Sin+Cos each, about 13 / 40 / 120 ns (12x/18x/28x Perlin) plus (dim+1) Field evals.

disp.how: internal stripe kernel only; the critic says no public Stripes output

ideas.name: PhaseVortex
ideas.one_liner: Argument of a rotation-invariant complex lattice field: output histogram is exactly uniform by symmetry, with true topological defects (pinwheels, spirals, forked stripes).
ideas.algorithm: Lattice XY model: per-corner unit phasor e^(i*phi), phi from hash. z(p) = interpolate phasors with quintic weights in the complex plane, summed over two lattices rotated about 40 degrees relative to each other to hide axes. Because all phi are iid uniform, z and e^(i*theta)*z have the same law for any weights, so arg z is exactly uniform at every point and independent of |z|. phase = k*arg(z)/tau + c*|z|^gamma + dot(Carrier, p) + Detail(p). Output tri(phase)*2 - 1 with integer k. Any term added to a uniform circle variable independent of it leaves it uniform, so spiral, carrier and independent-source detail terms all keep the histogram flat. Threshold T then covers exactly (1-T)/2 with no calibration.
ideas.look: k=1: soft pinwheel fields with folded sheets. k=3: star junctions. c about 3: agate curls and spirals. Carrier: parallel stripes with genuine fork dislocations, as in fingerprints, zebra and wood grain. Good for marble, agate, fingerprints, bark and exact-coverage masks. Zeros are closed vortex loops in 3D. Measured coverage on the corner-phase variant: T=-0.8/-0.5/0/0.5/0.8 gives 0.9008/0.7507/0.4995/0.2511/0.1033 against targets 0.90/0.75/0.50/0.25/0.10, with the same accuracy under c=4 and carrier. XY variant: std 0.578 against 0.577 for uniform.
ideas.why_new: Exact histogram with no table and no measurement, and defects are a structural property with integer charge, not a threshold artefact. Phasor and Gabor nodes need sparse convolution and do not give exact uniformity with this cheap a kernel. The graph has no atan2, so it cannot be built from existing nodes. Windowed explicit dislocation dipoles were also prototyped (25 atan2 calls, branch-cut handling); this formula replaces them with a single atan2 and no window.
ideas.simd_plan: Each lattice is value-noise shaped: corners 4 / 8 / 16 in 2D / 3D / 4D, two lattices. Unit phasors from a hash-indexed table or Sin/Cos. One polynomial atan2 per sample. Estimated 2-3x Perlin SIMD; scalar with std::atan2 and cos/sin measured 5x perlin2. Same code for all dimensions via GenT, 4D works so tiling works.
ideas.continuity: Continuous except on the zero set of z (isolated points in 2D, curves in 3D, surfaces in 4D), where all levels meet. Requires integer k. Measured c0ratio about 2.6 to 3 from those singular points.
ideas.params: Winding k (int), Spiral c (hybrid), Gamma (float), Carrier X/Y/Z/W (float), Detail (hybrid source), Spread (float, 1 = exact uniform; below 0.5 no vortices can form because all phases fit in a half circle, so it controls defect density but breaks exactness).
ideas.risks: Corners must use interpolated unit phasors. An earlier version with Perlin gradient times a phase had rank-1 zeros at lattice corners and produced visible slip faults, fixed by this form. A single lattice leaves axis bias. Defects are sharp singular points, which hillshade exposes. Without warp the carrier stays straight, so pair it with DomainWarp upstream. The 3D/4D forms are untested in the prototype.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated 2-3x Perlin SIMD; scalar with std::atan2 and cos/sin measured 5x perlin2.

ideas.name: PhasonWaves
ideas.one_liner: A latticeless sum of N equal-wavelength plane waves where noise moves perpendicular-space phase: quasi-crystals that rearrange without stretching, down to Turing-like labyrinths.
ideas.algorithm:
Table at param-set time: d_j=(cos(j*pi/N),sin(j*pi/N)) and perpendicular star e_j=(cos(j*m*pi/N),sin(j*m*pi/N)), m=2 for N=5 and m coprime with N otherwise. psi_j from hash(seed,j); global rotation from seed.
u=(U(seed,p),U(seed+1,p)).
Out=Sqrt(2/N)*sum_j Cos(k*dot(d_j,p)+k*dot(e_j,u)*Amount+psi_j).
A phonon warp (d_j·u) is plain domain warp and stretches; the phason term (e_j·u) cannot be produced by any warp because it applies a different displacement to each wave.
3D: 6 icosahedral axes for d_j; e_j is the Galois conjugate (swap tau with -1/tau). Threshold bias turns output into spots or labyrinth.
ideas.look: Tested. Amount=0, N=5 gives clean five-fold quasi-crystal rosettes. A phonon warp keeps rosettes but bends them. A phason gives a locally ordered pattern whose motifs dissolve and reform while the wavelength stays fixed. N=13 with phason, thresholded, gives a convincing Turing or leopard-maze pattern with uniform feature size, and no lattice to hide. Uses: alien crystals, tiled ornament that never repeats, reaction-diffusion stand-in, narrow-band bases for threshold masks.
ideas.why_new: Narrow spectrum (one wavelength everywhere) is something Perlin, Simplex and fractals do not offer, and it is what makes thresholded labyrinths look like Turing patterns. The phason parameter is a domain deformation with no equivalent in the warp family, because features keep their size.
ideas.simd_plan: No lattice, no hash at Gen time apart from the seed. N Sin+Cos (only Cos needed), N=5..13, plus U source evals (2 / 3 / 3 or 4 for 2D / 3D / 4D). Estimated N=5 about 2-3x Perlin, N=13 about 6x; not measured. Loop count N is constant, so it is allowed. 4D: generic N-direction table such as a 4D 16-cell star.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity when U is smooth. Not formally checked, but it is a finite sum of Cos of smooth arguments.
ideas.params: Hybrid: Amount, Frequency, plus phase offset. Int: N, Star Multiplier m. U is an optional source.
ideas.risks: Direction table and hash per seed: per-lane seeds force recomputation or a global rotation only, so use the node seed or accept the cost. Large phason Amount at N=5 goes mushy, blurring rosettes (visible in the prototype); keep Amount small or use N>=7. Without U the pattern is deterministic and recurs approximately. Sin precision at far coords degrades as with SineWave.
sources: Gardner 1984 and Perlin 1985 sums of sines, Berry 1977 random waves, cut-and-project phason strain from crystallography (all from memory, not consulted)
ideas.cost_note: Estimated N=5 about 2-3x Perlin, N=13 about 6x; not measured.

ideas.name: PhasorNoise
ideas.one_liner: Complex Gabor splat sum whose phase is kept and whose amplitude is thrown away: constant-contrast labyrinths, zebra stripes and fingerprints, with orientation and frequency drivable per lane. Gabor Real is an Output mode of the same node.
ideas.algorithm: p *= 1/FeatureScale. Window = 3^D cells around floor(p) (see simd_plan for 2^D and simplex variants). Per cell c: h = hash(seed,c); q = c + 0.5 + Jitter*(rnd01(h)-0.5) per axis; r2 = |p-q|^2; w = max(0, 1 - r2/R^2)^3 (R = 1.5, compact C2 window, no exp). Direction d_c by DirectionMode enum: Random (2D angle = 2pi*bits(h); 3D rndDir3(h); 4D rndDir4(h)); Fixed (param angles); Quantised (angle = 2pi*floor(N*u)/N, lerped with the random angle by Snap in [0,1] -> 3-fold snap = circuit traces / 2-fold = brick); Source (direction from HybridSource angle(s) sampled ONCE at p, not at q: 1 eval, kernels in one lane share a direction, phase stays continuous because d(p) is continuous); HalfAngle (fingerprint: two sources n1,n2 sampled at p, u=(n1,n2)/|n|, d = normalize((1+u.x, u.y)) with Select to (0,1) when |1+u.x|<eps; this is a LINE field whose zeros are +1/2 cores and -1/2 deltas, exactly fingerprint minutiae). Kernel phase psi = 2pi*F*dot(d_c, p-q) + PhaseJitter*2pi*rnd01(h') where F is Hybrid 'Frequency' in cycles per cell (>= ~1.5). Accumulate C += w*cos(psi), S += w*sin(psi). Output enum: Real = C/norm (Gabor look), Amplitude = sqrt(C^2+S^2)/norm, Phase = atan2approx(S,C)/pi (sawtooth), SinPhase = S/sqrt(C^2+S^2+eps^2) (the phasor: constant-contrast stripes), CosPhase = C/sqrt(..) (use this for line-field modes: even in d so flipping d->-d is invisible; PhaseJitter must be 0 there), Triangle = 1-2|Phase| (ridge cross-section, constant width = exact furrows/dunes), Pulse = smoothstep(Duty-Soft, Duty+Soft, frac(Phase)) with Hybrid Duty (PWM stripes).
ideas.look: Prototype cl_phasor: PhaseSine gives constant-amplitude worm labyrinths that threshold into Turing or reaction-diffusion mazes; Spread .15 gives zebra or fingerprint flows; a slow Angle field gives flowing wood or hair grain. GaborReal has a clean ring FFT and a flat-topped histogram. Good for reaction-diffusion masks without simulation, coral, zebra, dunes, microstructure, 3D gyroid-like volumes. Simplex window gives shorter, kinkier bars.
ideas.why_new: Nothing on the contact sheet has a narrow ring spectrum or constant-contrast stripes. Perlin, Simplex and FBm are broad band blobs, SineWave is periodic. It cannot be graphed because the splat sum must stay complex until the end, and hybrids stay stable because the phase is per splat.
ideas.simd_plan:
Fully branch-free: masks only in Select for half-angle and octant atan. Window options as an enum: 3^D jittered (quality, 9/27/81 cells); 2^D half-jitter (q within cell centre +-0.25, window cells = floor(p-0.5)+{0,1}, R=0.75, seamless proof: excluded cells are >=0.75 away; 4/8/16 cells, coverage ~1.8 kernels/pt); Simplex corners (D+1 kernels at the skewed simplex corners, falloff (0.5-r2)^4 as Simplex: 3/4/5 kernels, cheapest, lattice-aligned dislocations). Per cell ~45 ops (hash, jitter, dot, window, sincos poly). Est. 3^D: 2D ~4x Perlin (4.5 ns), 3D ~2x CellularDistance 3D (25 ns), 4D ~2.5x CellularDistance 4D. 2^D: 2D ~2x Perlin, 3D ~2x Perlin3D, 4D ~2.5x Perlin4D. Simplex variant ~1.5x Simplex at every dimension. 4D works generically so GenTileable2D tiles.
[PhasorNoise, lit-classic] Fixed loop, masks only for w>=0. One hash: 2x10 bit jitter, 6 bit phase, 6 bit angle. Cost per splat about Cellular cell (.45 ns) plus sincos, window and accumulate (.6 ns) = ~1 ns. Window Cell3: 9/27/81 splats = ~9/28/85 ns (2D is ~8x Perlin, ~2.4x CellularDistance). Window Simplex: 3/4/5 splats = ~3/4/5 ns (~3x/2x/1.2x Perlin), the default for 3D/4D and the tiling path. Scalar prototype ratios to perlin2: 3.0 Simplex, 6.4 3x3, 7.4 4x4. Generic GenT<P...> works with a dimension-specific direction table.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity at eps>0 away from window edges; w reaches zero with C2 so no seams. c0ratio 7.0 for PhaseSine and 6.7 for the Simplex window. Sharp but continuous near Z=0 dislocations. Saw mode is discontinuous by design at wrap and at Z=0. 3D slice verified visually.
ideas.params: Feature Scale; Frequency (hybrid, cycles/cell); Jitter; PhaseJitter; DirectionMode enum; Angle (float) / Angle Source(s) (hybrid) / N snaps + Snap; Fingerprint Re/Im GeneratorSources; Output enum; Duty (hybrid), Softness; Window enum; Seed Offset.
ideas.risks:
Simplex window exposes triangular lattice kinks and faint lines in the FFT. Too high Frequency against a small kernel aliases into checker blobs in 3D slices. 4D Cell3 at 81 splats is impractical, so tiling relies on the Simplex window. Rapid Angle fields compress stripes; Rune Johansen reports abrupt changes in 'Simple Phacelle' where input direction changes quickly.
[PhasorNoise, signal-phase] Frequency below ~1.5 cycles/cell starves the complex sum (grey dropouts). Contrast normalisation amplifies noise where |z| small (needs eps). Source-direction mode distorts stripes slightly vs sampling at kernel centres (sampling at 9 q's would cost 9 evals). Fingerprint 3D is only an extrusion of the 2D line field. 3^D window in 4D is expensive; the 2^D window is the shipping default for 4D.
sources: Tricard, Efremov, Zanni, Neyret, Martinez, Lefebvre, 'Procedural Phasor Noise', SIGGRAPH 2019 (recalled, not fetched)
Lagae et al., 'Procedural Noise using Sparse Gabor Convolution', SIGGRAPH 2009 (recalled, not fetched)
ideas.variant_notes: Folds in the Blender-style GaborNoise proposal, whose look test found 1 impulse per cell already has the right character (Value has dead zones at 1, Phasor is clean at 2), and PhasorCellNoise, whose analytic derivative is what ErosionFilter needs. Two kernel layouts stay selectable: 3^d jittered cells, or the 3/4/5 corner simplex window for 3D, 4D and tiling.
ideas.cost_note: 3^D: 2D ~4x Perlin (4.5 ns), 3D ~2x CellularDistance 3D (25 ns), 4D ~2.5x CellularDistance 4D.

ideas.name: QuadraticCarpet
ideas.one_liner: Value-noise interpolation of a Zadoff-Chu quadratic-phase lattice instead of hash values: zone-plate rosettes and moire carpets from integer overflow.
ideas.algorithm:
Corner value g(i,j)=Cos(2pi*frac((a*i*i + b*i*j + c*j*j)/P)). In SIMD use P=2^32: phase=int32 wraparound of a*i*i+b*i*j+c*j*j, then top bits scaled to float, then Cos or a polynomial. (a,b,c) chosen from seed, tested with a/P near 1/101, 3/251, 1/1009 (ratios to P). Interpolate with quintic fade like Value noise.
3D: add e*k*k, f*i*k, h*j*k; 4D similarly.
ideas.look: Tested. Concentric zone plates with secondary rosettes (Talbot copies) where the chirp aliases against the lattice, checker patches between, and exact global periodicity for rational a/P. Looks like crafted op-art carpet or engine-turned metal, deterministic rather than random. Different seeds give different carpet families, not random textures. Uses: guilloche patterns, sci-fi interference plates, deliberately moire masks, exact tile with period P.
ideas.why_new: A completely different source of coherence: aliasing of a chirp against the lattice rather than randomness. Nothing on the sheet has structured moire. Cheapest possible implementation, because no hash multiply-xorshift is needed.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch free. 2^D corners, integer multiplies only, then Cos per corner (or a 4-term polynomial). About 1-1.5x Value noise in all dimensions. Trivially 4D.
ideas.continuity: C2-ish like Value noise with quintic fade: continuous in interpolation since lattice values are single valued; not numerically checked.
ideas.params: Float or int: Chirp a, Cross b, Chirp c. Seeded selects offsets. ScalableGenerator mixin. Integer lattice offset moves the rosette centre.
ideas.risks: Not noise-like: strong order, centred on origin unless offset, and frequency content varies with distance from the centre in a chirp way. Far from origin at P=2^32 the wrap gives a different look than near it. Highly sensitive to (a,b,c), so a preset list may be needed. Wild and niche; low priority.
sources: Zadoff-Chu sequences and Schroeder quadratic residue diffusers, quantum carpet Talbot effect (from memory, not consulted)
ideas.cost_note: About 1-1.5x Value noise in all dimensions.

ideas.name: RadialPhasor
ideas.one_liner: Interference of windowed circular/spherical waves emitted from jittered lattice points, summed as a complex field: ripple rings, soap-film amplitude nets, zone plates and fringe vortices.
ideas.algorithm:
Same lattice, window and accumulator as PhasorNoise but each kernel is a radial wave: r = sqrt(|p-q_c|^2 + tiny); psi = 2pi*F*r + Chirp*r^2 + PhaseJitter*2pi*rnd01(h) (Chirp != 0 makes each source a Fresnel zone plate, rings tightening outward). Per-cell presence mask m_c = (rnd01(h2) < Density) folded into w (sparser emitters = fewer, cleaner ripple families). Accumulate C += w*m*cos(psi), S += w*m*sin(psi). Outputs: Real (classic overlapping ripples), Amplitude = sqrt(C^2+S^2) (destructive-interference lines form a net between emitters: soap-film / caustic web), Caustic = Amplitude^k (hybrid k), Phase (fringes with vortices), CosPhase (constant-contrast ripples), Triangle (sharp concentric ridges = dartboard terrain).

[SpiralPhasor, lit-classic] As PhasorNoise but the kernel is a spiral. For each splat: r=sqrt(|d|^2+tiny); u=(dx+i*dy)/r; sign s=+-1 from hash.
c=exp(i*(2pi*F*r+phi)) * (s>0?u:conj(u))^W, power by W complex multiplies (W is a constant int member).
Z+=w*min(1,r/r0)*c, with r0 about .1, so the singular centre has zero weight and the field stays continuous there.
Output Zi/sqrt(|Z|^2+(eps*W)^2).
3D: pick hash axis a, two orthonormal vectors e1,e2 from a table; u=(dot(d,e1)+i*dot(d,e2))/rho, rho=length of that pair; r=rho gives extruded scroll waves, r=|d| gives shell spirals. 4D: same with a hash-chosen plane.
ideas.look:
Prototype: overlapping concentric targets and spirals joined by dislocations, resembling Belousov-Zhabotinsky waves, zebra, fingerprints, topographic maps, or sand ripples; with eps large, rain on a pond. Much more ordered than anything on the sheet, with stripe width nearly constant.
[WhorlPhasor, signal-phase] Tested. Each point sits in a bullseye of rings, and neighbouring ring systems meet along lines of forks and deltas, like the topology of fingerprint whorls, peacock eyes or agate. Compared with sin(k*F1) the seams become interference chains, not sharp V kinks. Stripe width is uniform. Uses: agate, eyes, ring-spot animal patterns, sci-fi panels, decorative ripples.
ideas.why_new: Concentric structure from many centres with interference is not reachable by the current nodes: Oscillator(CellularDistance F1) gives rings but with hard Voronoi seams and no superposition; summing two cellular passes does not interfere coherently. The complex accumulation gives phase/amplitude/caustic views for free.
ideas.simd_plan:
Per cell: hash, sqrt, polynomial window, sin+cos (or a parabolic wave pair). 25 cells in 2D ~25-35 ns, or 9 cells at R<=1 ~10-14 ns with smaller patches. 3D 27 cells ~40 ns. 4D 81 cells ~120 ns, for tiling only. Scalar proto was 835 ns against Worley 113 at 5x5, about 7x, so treat 3x3 as the default. Exp not needed; one final InvSqrt.
[RipplePhasor, signal-phase] Identical branch-free structure to PhasorNoise plus one sqrt per cell; window options the same (2^D half-jitter is a good default because overlap of ~2 emitters already interferes). Cost ~1.1x PhasorNoise per dimension. 4D generic (hyperspherical waves) so tiling works.
ideas.continuity: Dislocation points where Z=0 are the only steep spots: c0ratio 1.37 at eps 0.02 (near-point jumps, by design) and 4.67 at norm=0.85 (eps about 0.17). With larger eps it is smooth. Lipschitz constant is about f/eps near zeros.
ideas.params: Feature Scale; Frequency (hybrid); Chirp; Density; PhaseJitter; Jitter; Output enum; Caustic Power (hybrid); Window enum; Seed Offset.
ideas.risks:
At high Frequency the rings alias unless the sampling grid is dense (document a Nyquist note like SineWave). The Amplitude net looks cellular but is softer; make sure it reads as different in a side-by-side.
[RippleField, stamp-scatter] Small eps gives pinprick discontinuities at dislocations, and hybrid frequency sampled per lane bends rings but can create phase runaway at far distances if not applied per-feature, so sample per-feature only. Overlap with a generic PhasorNoise candidate from another lens (share kernels in one node). 3x3 window may reduce targets to tiny patches at low frequency.
[WhorlPhasor, signal-phase] With legal R the grid regularity becomes visible at J=0.6: rings sit in a semi-regular array. Higher jitter forces smaller R and more dead spots where z is near 0 (output goes to 0 there, which is not a seam). The cost is well above the 5x Perlin target, so it is a look node, not a building block. 3D not rendered.
ideas.variant_notes: Complex sum of radial waves with phase normalisation. Charge 0 is RipplePhasor/WhorlPhasor (targets, fork chains), non-zero charge is SpiralPhasor/RippleField (BZ-style spirals).
ideas.cost_note: 25 cells in 2D ~25-35 ns, or 9 cells at R<=1 ~10-14 ns with smaller patches. 3D 27 cells ~40 ns.

ideas.name: RippleNoise
ideas.one_liner: Each lattice site emits a windowed radial wave; the sum gives ring interference, rain on a puddle, or caustic webs, with a built-in seamless time loop.
ideas.algorithm: For each cell in the 3^dim window: h=hash(cell); c=cell+jitter(h); q=(p-c)/R; r2=dot(q,q); r=Sqrt(r2); e=Max(0,1-r2)^2. Interference mode: ph=rnd(h,1)+Time*n where n is an integer speed from hash bits; w=0.6+0.8*rnd(h,2); s += e*Cos(TAU*(Frequency*w*r - ph)). Rain mode: life=Fract(Time+rnd(h,1)); u=(r-life)*Frequency; env=Exp(-0.6*u*u)*(1-life)^2*Min(1,life/0.05); s += e*env*Cos(PI*u). Density keeps a subset by hash. Output enum: Sum, or Caustic = 2*Max(0,1-|s|)^6-1.
ideas.look:
Concentric ring interference like LightWave Ripples and Underwater; expanding rain rings for puddle normal maps; Caustic gives thin bright pool-floor webs. Spherical shells in 3D, useful as a banded solid. Prototype: dcc_lens mode=2.
[TuringShell, nature-phenomena] Worm-like, near-uniform-width bands; higher threshold gives rounded spots with some small rings. Looks closer to brain coral and animal coats than a Simplex threshold does, as Simplex has no preferred width. At K=2 rings around seeds are visible; K=3 reads as a better labyrinth.
ideas.why_new: No ring structures anywhere on the sheet. Modo and LightWave ship Ripples, Rain, Drip Drop and Caustic as distinct textures; none of these are reachable with cell distance plus a graph because each site needs its own phase and the waves must sum over the window. Integer speeds give a seamless loop with no 4D torus.
ideas.simd_plan: 3^dim loop with Sqrt and one Cos per site (rain adds one Exp; replace with a polynomial bump for speed). Time is hybrid, so it can vary per lane. Estimated 8 / 25 / 85 ns, 2x CellularDistance, 7x Perlin in 2D; justified by the look, and Density reduces visual load but not cost.
ideas.continuity: C1 spatially (e has zero slope at r=1); C0 at r=0 (cone point of the wave). Caustic is C0 with creases. Rain is continuous in time thanks to the fade-in factor. Measured c0ratio 7.97-7.98.
ideas.params: Frequency (hybrid), Time (hybrid), Radius (float <=1), Density (hybrid), Mode enum, Grid Jitter (hybrid), Output enum.
ideas.risks:
Near-regular ring lattice shows if jitter is low. Measured Sum range about +-2.5 at gain 0.8, so needs a soft normaliser. High Frequency aliases at normal feature scales.
[RippleNoise, math-physics] Sum of few impulses has visible 'cell density' at Radius<0.7; normalisation must be measured; rings above ~6 per cell alias at the window boundary; 4D cost.
[TuringShell, nature-phenomena] Not true stripes: rings and blobs remain, and DislocationStripes gives a cleaner stripe look. Value range and sigma vary with K and f, so normalisation is empirical. The 3D K=1 density is an assumption, not tested. The DoG and activator-inhibitor link (Young 1984) is from memory and was not checked.
ideas.variant_notes: Real-valued sum of radial kernels. TuringShell is this kernel plus a saturating threshold, which spans spots to labyrinth; RippleNoise (math-physics) adds the amplitude Decay term.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated 8 / 25 / 85 ns, 2x CellularDistance, 7x Perlin in 2D; justified by the look, and Density reduces visual load but not cost.

queue.name: RippleNoise
queue.reason: Rain-on-puddle rings with an exact time loop, an immediate water asset. Needs a soft normaliser. Merge in the Amplitude net from radial-phasor.

ideas.name: SimplexFacet
ideas.one_liner: Value noise on the simplex lattice with exact barycentric (piecewise-planar) interpolation: low-poly faceted terrain and crystals directly from a noise node, with optional per-facet offsets.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: FaceOffset (hybrid, 0 = continuous), Smoothness (0..1 blend toward a smooth variant), Jitter (0..0.5 vertex jitter in skewed space, keeps triangles valid).
2D: s = (x+y)*F2; i = floor(x+s), j = floor(y+s); u = x+s-i, v = y+s-j (skewed cell coords in [0,1)).
  tri = u > v; vertices: V0=(i,j), V1 = tri ? (i+1,j) : (i,j+1), V2=(i+1,j+1)
  lambda = tri ? (1-u, u-v, v) : (1-v, v-u, u)      // barycentric in skewed space; skew is linear so the patch is a plane in world space
  h_k = rnd11(hash(seed, V_k)); value = Sum lambda_k h_k
  FaceOffset: value += FaceOffset * rnd11(hash(seed, i, j, tri))
3D: skew s = (x+y+z)*F3; u,v,w fractional; sort: hi = max(u,v,w), lo = min, mid = u+v+w-hi-lo; lambda = (1-hi, hi-mid, mid-lo, lo); the 4 vertices are V0, V0 + e_argmax, V0 + e_argmax + e_argmid, V0 + (1,1,1); argmax/argmid via compare masks exactly as Simplex3D's traversal does.
4D: same with 5 vertices and the rank trick already in Simplex 4D.
Smoothness: replace lambda by normalised lambda^2(3-2lambda) (C1 inside the simplex, still C0 across edges) or just lerp with SuperSimplex via graph.
Jitter: vertex world position offset by Jitter*rndvec(hash(V)) and lambda recomputed from the jittered triangle via one 2x2 (3x3) solve: optional, costs more; the unjittered version is the core.
ideas.look: Flat triangular facets with crisp fold lines, like a decimated mesh, a cut gemstone or paper origami terrain; FaceOffset adds cliffs between facets (crystal cluster, broken ice floes, shattered glass). The hillshade is flat-shaded triangles, a look that currently needs a mesh pipeline, not a noise.
ideas.why_new: Value noise with linear interpolation on a square lattice gives bilinear saddle patches (curved) with axis-aligned creases; Terrace quantises height not slope. Exact planar facets on an isotropic triangular/tetrahedral lattice are not expressible by any graph of existing nodes.
ideas.simd_plan: Reuses Simplex skew and vertex traversal; no gradients, 3/4/5 hashes and a weighted sum: cheaper than Simplex (2D ~0.7x Perlin, 3D ~0.8x Simplex 3D, 4D ~Simplex 4D). Branch-free via the existing compare-mask traversal. GenTileable2D works through the 4D form.
ideas.continuity: C0 (creases along every simplex edge) by design; discontinuous with FaceOffset > 0; Smoothness only smooths inside facets.
ideas.params: FaceOffset (hybrid), Smoothness, Jitter, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks: The lattice is visible by design (regular triangles); vertex Jitter breaks regularity but needs a per-sample 2x2/3x3 barycentric solve and the window argument becomes delicate (jittered vertex must stay inside its skewed cell, Jitter <= 0.5 guarantees valid triangles). Some may consider this just 'linear simplex value noise'; the facet-offset and jitter are the added value.
ideas.cost_note: Reuses Simplex skew and vertex traversal; no gradients, 3/4/5 hashes and a weighted sum: cheaper than Simplex (2D ~0.7x Perlin, 3D ~0.8x Simplex 3D, 4D ~Simplex 4D).

queue.reason: Barycentric value noise on the simplex lattice, cheaper than Simplex: instant low-poly (J4 top pick). Skip vertex jitter. Triangles show unless warped.

ideas.name: SineFold
ideas.one_liner: Gardner-style sum of sines with cross-axis phase coupling, made into a rotated cascade: latticeless liquid marble and woven folds, same cost pattern in 4D.
ideas.look: Prototype cl_misc node 3: Couple=0 is a lumpy periodic lattice; Couple=.5-1 gives woven, basket-like liquid marble with long sheared folds; Couple=2 gives finely combed swirls, like oil on water, with very strong streaks in hillshade. No hash or lattice artifacts; no isotropic stats. Water caustic bases, stylised marble, fabrics, sci-fi fluid.
ideas.why_new: All existing noises are lattice based except SineWave, which is trivially periodic. Domain warp on SineWave gets part of this but not the per-iteration feedback, and needs one node per iteration.
ideas.simd_plan: K x d x FS::Sin plus phases from seed hash (one per axis per iteration, or a static per-seed table when lanes share a seed). 2D K=7: 14 sin ~3.5 ns (3x Perlin; scalar 4.4x). 3D ~5 ns, 4D ~7 ns (1.6x Perlin 4D). No hash lattice, no masks at all; fully branch free GenT.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity everywhere, c0ratio 7.88; slopes grow with K and Couple. Tiling works through the 4D torus since the function is smooth.
ideas.params: Int: K. Float: F0, Lacunarity, Gain. Hybrid: Couple. Seeded for phases. Mixins standard.
ideas.risks: Large-scale weave periodicity is visible, since low frequencies dominate and only K sines exist. Not isotropic: rotation matrix imprints a directional bias. Seed only changes phases, so seeds look related. Float sin accuracy at far coordinates worsens (FS::Sin reduction): far coord test passed at 4e4 but check 1e6.
ideas.cost_note: 2D K=7: 14 sin ~3.5 ns (3x Perlin; scalar 4.4x). 3D ~5 ns, 4D ~7 ns (1.6x Perlin 4D).

ideas.name: SparseGate
ideas.one_liner: Make most lattice points silent: a hybrid Density parameter on Perlin/Simplex/Value (or a dedicated SparseGradient node) that soft-gates each lattice contribution, giving isolated dipole features on an exactly flat zero background, optionally with blue-noise (local-max) spacing.
ideas.algorithm:
Add to the lattice loop of Perlin (2^dim corners) / Simplex (dim+1 vertices) / Value:
  thr = rnd01(hash(corner))              // per-lattice-point fixed threshold
  g = smoothstep(thr - Softness, thr + Softness, Density(p))   // Density hybrid sampled per lane; soft so a smooth density field fades features in continuously
  contribution *= g
Output unchanged otherwise (still in [-1,1]).
Spacing option 'LocalMax' (2D, 3D optional): a corner is alive only if its hash is the maximum among its 3^dim lattice neighbours: alive = AND over neighbours n of (hash(corner) > hash(n)); this yields a Poisson-disk-like set (no two alive points adjacent) with a density fixed by geometry (1/9 in 2D); Density then scales the soft gate on top. Cost: 5^dim hashes per sample (25 in 2D, 125 in 3D, so 3D defaults to Bernoulli).
Dedicated node variant SparseGradient: jittered 3^dim window + radial window kernel (1-s2)^4 * dot(grad, r), same gate, so features are not stuck on a grid.
ideas.look: Perlin with Density 0.08: a flat plain with scattered crescent dipoles of random heading, each a crest beside a trough: barchan dune fields, isolated hills and holes, meteor splash marks (Abs gives isolated bumps, Ridged isolated sharp ridges). With Density driven by a large Perlin: dunes that thin out and vanish across a region continuously. Per-octave in FBm: rare large features, common small ones: a 'sparse fractal' that reads as island archipelagos.
ideas.why_new: Thresholding/Remap of a dense noise clips shapes and never gives a mathematically flat background with intact feature shapes; placing isolated oriented dipoles with controlled density (and non-adjacent spacing) is what sparse convolution offers but FastNoise lacks. It is nearly free on the existing generators.
ideas.simd_plan: Per lattice point: one extra rnd extract, one smoothstep, one multiply: Perlin cost +10%. Density hybrid sampled once per lane. LocalMax: 25 hashes in 2D (~+60% over Perlin), too costly in 3D/4D (use Bernoulli there); hashes of a 5x5 block can share the row/column prime products. Fully branch-free. Works in 2D/3D/4D since it touches only the existing lattice loops.
ideas.continuity: Same as the host noise (C2 for Perlin quintic, C2 Simplex) provided Softness > 0 and Density is continuous; Softness 0 with a varying density field introduces discontinuities (features pop).
ideas.params: Density (hybrid, key), Softness, Spacing {Bernoulli, LocalMax}; as a dedicated node also Jitter, Radius.
ideas.risks: Hard to make visually impressive in the thumbnail (mostly flat); shines in composition. LocalMax 3D cost prohibitive; document. For Simplex the dipole shape per alive vertex is a hexagonal surflet, fine. Range stays [-1,1] but is rarely reached, so Output Min/Max scaling expectations change.
sources: J. P. Lewis, 'Algorithms for Solid Noise Synthesis', SIGGRAPH 1989 (sparse convolution; from memory, not fetched)
ideas.cost_note: Per lattice point: one extra rnd extract, one smoothstep, one multiply: Perlin cost +10%.

ideas.name: SpiralCells
ideas.one_liner: Each lattice point is a spiral or pinwheel wave source, blended by a partition of unity: curl commas and BZ-reaction spirals without atan or seams.
ideas.algorithm:
For window points: v = x-c, r = |v|; phase-rotated kernel without angles: s = Re[(vx+i vy)^m * exp(i(hand*F*r + phi))] / max(r^m, eps). For m=1: (g.v*cos(Fr+phi) + h.v*sin(Fr+phi)) / r. 3D and 4D use orthonormal pair g,h from a table: s = (g.v*cos(Fr+phi) + h.v*sin(Fr+phi))/r, valid at every dimension. Weight w = max(0, 1 - r^2/R^2)^(2*Sharp). Output = sum(w*s)/sum(w). Damp core with sat(r/eps). F=0 gives pinwheels (spokes), large F gives tight spirals.

[PinwheelNoise, lattice-kernels] Params: Order m (1..4), Twist (hybrid, radians per kernel radius), TwistJitter, Chirality {CW, CCW, Mixed}, Radius R, Jitter.
Gen(p): c = floor(p); acc = 0
 for o in {-1,0,1}^dim:
   h = hash(seed,c+o); q = c+o+0.5+Jitter*(rndvec(h)-0.5); r = p - q; s2 = |r|^2
   2D: u = r.x, v = r.y. 3D/4D: a = hashed unit vector, b = orthonormal to a (b = normalize(w - dot(w,a)a) with w another hashed vector), u = dot(a,r), v = dot(b,r)
   rho = sqrt(u^2+v^2)
   kappa = Twist*(1 + TwistJitter*rnd11(h>>8)) * chiralitySign(h)
   phase = kappa*rho - 2*pi*rnd01(h>>16)        // bounded: |phase| <= Twist*R + 2pi, so one unreduced minimax sin/cos pair
   (cs, sn) = cos/sin(phase)
   zm = (u + i v)^m by repeated complex multiply: m=1 (u,v); m=2 (u^2-v^2, 2uv); m=3 ...  (no normalisation: the rho^m factor acts as the inner falloff)
   kern = (Re zm * cs + Im zm * sn)          // = rho^m cos(m*theta - phase)
   win = max(0, 1 - s2/R^2)^4
   acc += kern * win
 value = acc * norm(m, R) (analytic peak of rho^m (1-rho^2/R^2)^4 times 1/sqrt(overlap)).
ideas.look: Curl commas, Van Gogh sky, whirl patterns, flower spokes, BZ reaction fronts, hair whorls. Prototyped: repeated comma-shaped curls in a labyrinth with strong chirality; F=0 gives clear pinwheels. Terrain-wise reads as scroll ornament.
ideas.why_new: All coherent noises here have no local handedness. Warping into swirls smears, and gets random shear, not consistent per-centre arm counts. Sum (not partition) version looks like plain interference; the normalised blend is what keeps the spirals readable.
ideas.simd_plan: m=1 is cheap: dots, sqrt, Sin, Cos per point. Only hash bits select F sign and g,h. m=2,3 via a complex square. 2D 9 points: 8-12 ns (proto 6.6x perlin2 with 19 points and atan2). 3D 2^3 corners or 27: 15-40 ns. 4D 2^4: 30 ns. Above building-block cost, justified as a look node.
ideas.continuity: C1 away from cores, measured c0ratio 7.99. Core is C0 through sat(r/eps) damp. R must fit reach or there are seams.
ideas.params: Arm Count (int m, or per-point random), Twist F (hybrid), Handedness Bias, Sharpness (hybrid), Grid Jitter.
ideas.risks:
Normalisation denominator must stay positive: eps, and R big enough that every sample has a weight. Sin+Cos per point dominates; a precomputed sincos for two shared radii is not possible with per-point r. Large F aliases near grid scale.
[PinwheelNoise, lattice-kernels] Large Twist aliases inside a kernel (arms thinner than a pixel at the rim); cap Twist*R around 4*pi. Overlap of several spirals muddles the centres; a Jitter below 1 keeps centres apart. Normalisation is empirical for Mixed chirality.
ideas.variant_notes: Real-valued spiral kernels: SpiralCells blends by partition of unity (keeps spirals readable), PinwheelNoise sums and keeps rho^m.
ideas.cost_note: 2D 9 points: 8-12 ns (proto 6.6x perlin2 with 19 points and atan2). 3D 2^3 corners or 27: 15-40 ns.

ideas.name: SteerablePerlin
ideas.one_liner: Perlin noise whose grain follows a per-sample direction field, giving feathery flow-aligned texture with no lattice artifacts.
ideas.algorithm: Per lane, once per call: read direction d from hybrids (Angle in 2D or Dir X/Y/Z/W), a = |d|^2/(|d|^2+eps) fades anisotropy out where d is near zero, d = normalize(d). Metric M = e0*d*d^T + e1*(I - d*d^T), e0 = k (0.51, slow along d), e1 = (Sum-k)/(dim-1) (fast across d); this closed form replaces the shader's eigenvector code. Octave loop built into the node, same M for every octave: p = pos*freq; ip = floor(p); f = p-ip; b = 1 - S5(f) per axis, S5(t)=6t^5-15t^4+10t^3. For each of 2^d corners o: v = o-f; Mv = M*v; n = dot(g(hash(ip+o)), Mv); w = product_axis(|o_axis - b_axis|) * (1 - S5(min(|dot(v,Mv)|,1))); out += n*w. Sum octaves with Gain, then ScaleOutput. Trap: the fade weight must be |o - (1-S5(f))|. My first prototype used |o - S5(f)|, which isolates every cell into a blob with a hard visible grid.
ideas.look: Combed, feathery streamlines: fur, feathers, wind-blown snow and sand, wood grain, muscle fibre, flowing hair, strata following a slope. With Direction taken from a height field's contours the grain wraps around hills. Prototype 5 octaves over a smooth angle field: Gaussian histogram, no grid in the wide view, clean FFT.
ideas.why_new: Direct request: FastNoise2 discussion #159 asks for exactly this (Ideas category, links the SIGGRAPH 2025 talk). godot-proposals #1493 also names anisotropic noise in its title. FastNoise has only global stretch (DomainAxisScale) and warps. A warp shears features and pinches them; it cannot set local orientation with constant feature width. Nothing on the contact sheet looks like this.
ideas.simd_plan: Same 2^d corner loop as Perlin plus M*v (3 mults in 2D, 6 to 9 in 3D) and one S5 polynomial per corner; abs/min only, no branches, no atan. M computed once per lane per call. Dimension agnostic: 4 / 8 / 16 corners. Measured scalar prototype, 1 octave, including the angle field and sin/cos: 4.3x perlin2. Estimated AVX2 per octave: 2.5 / 6 / 15 ns (about 2.5x to 3x Perlin), plus direction hybrids.
ideas.continuity: C1 when the direction field is C1: fade weights and the metric weight both have zero first and second derivative at their ends. Measured c0ratio 8.0 at 1 octave, 7.5 at 5 octaves. A discontinuous direction input gives a C0 break in the metric, so it shows as a crease.
ideas.params: Feature Scale; Angle or Dir X/Y/Z/W (hybrid); Anisotropy Sum (hybrid, default 4); k (0.51); Octaves, Gain (0.67), Lacunarity built in; Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks: Octaves must be internal: a FractalFBm parent would sample the Direction hybrid at scaled positions, so each octave would get an unrelated field. That breaks the look, and it is why this node differs from other generators. The repo reports no licence, so implement from the paper rather than its code (I could only read the shader, the PDF could not be extracted here). Range measured about +-0.75 per octave over 8 seeds, so a measured normalising constant is needed. 4D costs 16 corners with a 4x4 metric.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated AVX2 per octave: 2.5 / 6 / 15 ns (about 2.5x to 3x Perlin), plus direction hybrids.

ideas.name: SteeredBandNoise
ideas.one_liner: Oriented stripe noise that follows any direction field for about 2-3x Perlin: Goldberg-style steering between fixed oriented bands, using LRP-style carrier factorisation so sin/cos is per lane, not per kernel.
ideas.algorithm:
theta=Angle(x). t=theta/pi*K; k=floor(t) mod K; f=frac(t). Use only bands k and k+1, weights cos(f*pi/2), sin(f*pi/2).
For band b: a=pi*b/K (table), w_b=(cos a,sin a). Carrier C_b=exp(i*2pi*F*dot(w_b,x)), one sincos per band per lane.
Modulator L_b(x): rotate x into the band frame q=Rot(a)*x plus a band offset, lattice cell in q, 2^d corners, quintic multilinear weights, complex coefficient from hash(seed+b*prime, corner) as two 16 bit fields mapped to [-1,1].
Z=sum_b weight_b*C_b*L_b. Output PhaseSine = Re Z/sqrt(|Z|^2+eps^2), or Gaussian = Re Z*scale.
Key point: bands are fixed fields, so varying theta only crossfades them, there is no phase shear and no swirl however fast theta varies.
3D: Axis enum (steer around X/Y/Z); or Isotropic mode with 6 icosahedral directions all evaluated. 4D: Isotropic mode with K fixed directions.
ideas.look: Prototype cl_carrier steer=1,K=8,lrot=1. F=3: fine fingerprint or zebra stripes that follow the field with few dislocations, nearly the look of PhasorNoise with a field at a fraction of the kernels. Wood grain, hair, dune ripple, sediment layers that bend along a guide node.
ideas.why_new: Driving orientation of stripes from a node is the classic open problem named in the survey (spatial variation of all noise parameters). Warp distorts spacing, and x*f(x) shears. A graph cannot do per-lane band selection with shared carriers. Cheaper than per-splat Gabor because trig is factored out of the kernel loop.
ideas.simd_plan: Per lane: 1 hybrid sample, k via Floor plus table permute, 2 band rotations (4 mul each), 2 sincos (~1 ns), 2x2^d hashed corners with bit field complex (~.15 ns each). Estimate 2D ~3.5 ns (3x Perlin), 3D Axis mode ~5.5 ns (2.5x), 4D ~9 ns (2x), 3D Isotropic with 6 bands ~11 ns (5x). Scalar prototype 5.2x perlin2, but it does cos/sin per corner, which the port removes.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity in Z (quintic lattice, continuous weights including the k wrap). Normalised output has c0ratio 3.85 with slope ~450 from sharp phase dislocations at eps=.05, which is a slope effect, not a jump; raise eps to soften. 3D form not prototyped.
ideas.params: Hybrid: Angle, Softness. Float: Frequency F (cycles per modulator cell; use >=2.5). Int: K (8 default). Enum: Output, Axis or Isotropic.
ideas.risks: Below F~2.5 boxy dislocation loops follow the rotated lattice (seen in prototype K=1 and F=1.5). Unsteered K=2 shows a grid. Isotropic use (K>=4 all active) is blobby and worse than PhasorNoise, so this node is only good steered. Ghost double stripes in crossfade zones. The theta wrap needs care when Angle is a range outside [0,pi).
ideas.cost_note: Estimate 2D ~3.5 ns (3x Perlin), 3D Axis mode ~5.5 ns (2.5x), 4D ~9 ns (2x), 3D Isotropic with 6 bands ~11 ns (5x).

ideas.name: SteeredStripes
ideas.one_liner: Very cheap steered plane waves: quantise orientation into slots and crossfade only two global waves per lane; the honest output is flowing herringbone and twill, not clean fingerprints.
ideas.algorithm:
L=Theta(p)/pi*N (N even, Theta axial). ra=2*Round(L/2), rb=2*Round((L-1)/2)+1, wa=1-|L-ra| sharpened by smoothstep, wb=1-wa.
A=k*dot(dir(ra),p)+psi(ra); B=k*dot(dir(rb),p)+psi(rb), both from a small table indexed by slot mod N.
y=wa*Cos(A)+wb*Cos(B); E2=wa^2+wb^2+2*wa*wb*Cos(A-s*B), s=sign(dot(dir a,dir b)) so the axial wrap has no seam.
Out=y*InvSqrt(E2+eps^2).
ideas.look: Tested at N=8 to N=64 and multiple sharpness levels. Slots yield a chopped herringbone, twill or op-art moire following the orientation field, with checker beat zones where slots crossfade. With fast-changing Theta it gives swirly op-art eddies. Does not give clean fingerprints; use LatticePhasor for those. Uses: fabric twill, stylised water, Bridget Riley-style graphics.
ideas.why_new: Stripes that follow an orientation field with no lattice and no per-corner work, at under Perlin cost, and N controls the look. The naive cos(k*R(theta(p))*p) shears wildly away from the origin, whereas this stays at constant wavelength everywhere.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch free. Table lookup via integer permute or Cos/Sin of slot angle; 2 Sin+Cos + 1 Cos + InvSqrt. Estimated about 1x Perlin in 2D plus Theta cost. 3D: azimuth x elevation slots, 4 waves bilinear. 4D: 8 waves. Polynomial atan needed only if Theta comes from a gradient.
ideas.continuity: C0 for continuous Theta with eps>0, not numerically checked in the last form. Zebra-like phase breaks at beat zeros are soft, not jumps.
ideas.params: Hybrid: Theta, Frequency. Int: Slots N. Float: Sharpness, eps.
ideas.risks: Fundamentally herringbone: slot width across the image scales as (pi/N)/|grad theta|, and global-phase mismatch between slots cannot be eliminated pointwise. Higher N narrows slots and worsens chopping, lower N widens checker zones, no setting is clean. Same orientation anywhere yields phase-coherent stripes globally (subtle). Include only if the twill look is wanted.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated about 1x Perlin in 2D plus Theta cost.

ideas.name: TPMSNoise
ideas.one_liner: Triply periodic minimal surface family (Gyroid, Schwarz P/D, Neovius, IWP, Lidinoid, Fischer-Koch) as a generator with per-axis hybrid phase, sheet mode and a w-driven phase orbit; the only field whose iso-surfaces are guaranteed bicontinuous labyrinths.
ideas.algorithm:
p *= 2*pi/FeatureScale (ScalableGenerator). Add hybrid phases: x += PhaseX(p), y += PhaseY(p), z += PhaseZ(p) (hybrids, default 0; feeding FBm Simplex here is the 'gyroid noise' sponge). 4D: additionally x += (pi/2)*sin(w), y += (pi/2)*sin(w+2.094), z += (pi/2)*sin(w+4.189) so the surface flows along its own screw axes and loops with period 2*pi in w. Compute sx,cx,sy,cy,sz,cz = Sin/Cos of x,y,z (6 trig). Family enum:
  Gyroid    g = sx*cy + sy*cz + sz*cx                  (|g|<=1.5)
  SchwarzP  g = cx + cy + cz                          (3)
  SchwarzD  g = sx*sy*sz + sx*cy*cz + cx*sy*cz + cx*cy*sz (1)
  Neovius   g = 3(cx+cy+cz) + 4 cx*cy*cz              (13)
  IWP       g = 2(cx*cy + cy*cz + cz*cx) - (c2x+c2y+c2z), c2x = 1-2sx*sx (6)
  Lidinoid  g = 0.5(s2x*cy*sz + s2y*cz*sx + s2z*cx*sy) - 0.5(c2x*c2y + c2y*c2z + c2z*c2x) + 0.15, s2x = 2 sx cx
  FischerKochS g = c2x*sy*cz + c2y*sz*cx + c2z*sx*cy
Output enum: Signed = g/gmax; Sheet = 1 - |g|/gmax (double-walled thin shell; threshold = wall thickness); Channel = Abs flipped. 2D: z = PhaseZ hybrid (default 0), i.e. a slice. Normalise by the per-family analytic max (table).

[TPMSMorph, volumetric-3d4d] Scaled coords X=f*x etc, with six sin/cos. G = sX cY + sY cZ + sZ cX; D = cX cY cZ - sX sY sZ; P = (cX+cY+cZ)/1.5. F = cos(th)*D + sin(th)*G, with th(p) a hybrid (Bonnet-style association by nodal approximations), with an optional second lerp toward P. Output enum: Solid F-Offset, Sheet |F-Offset|-Wall. Offset and Wall hybrids give density grading. Divide by a local gradient estimate is unnecessary since |grad F| is bounded by about sqrt(3) f and is analytic, giving a Lipschitz field ideal for sphere tracing. 4D: G4 = sX cY + sY cZ + sZ cW + sW cX with an analogous D4, a real 4D periodic field whose slices morph and loop over w period 2 pi and support GenTileable. For cheaper loops, th = base + omega*w gives D to G to -D to -G. 2D form is the z=0 slice.
ideas.look:
3D iso-surface at 0: the classic gyroid/Schwarz labyrinths, two interpenetrating connected tunnel systems with saddle-shaped walls; squash with DomainAxisScale for flattened cavern layers that stay connected; warp with FBm via the phase hybrids for organic sponge, trabecular bone, coral skeleton, foam sheets. Sheet mode iso-surfaces are uniform-thickness curved walls (membranes). 2D slice: a maze of wavy stripes and hooks (gyroid) or a dot/ring lattice (SchwarzP); with phase noise it looks like lamellar bone or brain coral.
[TPMSMorph, volumetric-3d4d] Prototyped with th varied by Perlin at mf 0.5. 3D isosurface: a gyroid-like lattice that distorts from one motif to another across space, staying a connected sponge with no pinches. 2D slice: warped wave and diamond motifs. Good for sci-fi lattices, coral, bone scaffold, alien architecture, grown metal. With warp source upstream it becomes organic gyroid noise.
ideas.why_new: Not expressible: SineWave is sin(x)sin(y)sin(z) only, no mixed sin*cos sums. Delivers caves/sponge with guaranteed connectivity of both phases (gyroid level sets for |t| < ~1.41 of 1.5 keep both labyrinths connected), zero-mean-curvature look, tileable by construction, C-infinity, and w-phase looping animation at 3D cost. Phase hybrids give in-node per-axis domain warp.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch-free, no lattice/window: 6 Sin/Cos (+3 Sin in 4D) plus ~15 FMAs; family switch is a node-level enum compiled per Gen (or Select over all families, still cheap). GenT over the pack: 2D drops z to a hybrid. Cost ~0.7x Perlin 3D, ~1x Perlin 4D. Hybrid phases cost whatever is plugged in.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity (sums of products of sines). Sheet mode has a C0 crease at g=0 (intended).
ideas.params: Family enum; Output enum (Signed/Sheet); Phase X/Y/Z hybrid (default 0); Feature Scale; Phase Speed W (float, 4D only); Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks:
Pure TPMS is visibly periodic; it needs a warp or the phase hybrids to look natural (document a default recipe). Normalisation maxima for Lidinoid/Neovius are tabulated constants, not exact. Both-phases-connected guarantee weakens under strong warps.
[TPMSMorph, volumetric-3d4d] Regular without inputs; seeds only shift phases. Interpolated nodal forms are approximations of true Bonnet associates, so intermediate surfaces are not minimal. The w=0 slice of G4 is not exactly a gyroid. Far coordinates: Sin accuracy at large arguments needs checking.
ideas.variant_notes: Family enum plus hybrid phase warp, with TPMSMorph's hybrid Bonnet-angle blend so topology family flows across space. Interpolated forms are nodal approximations, not true minimal surfaces.
ideas.cost_note: Cost ~0.7x Perlin 3D, ~1x Perlin 4D.

queue.reason: Gyroid family: bicontinuous labyrinth volumes for 6 trig ops, ~1.5 ns, no window (J1, J4 top pick). Show that hybrid phases plus a warp recipe break the visible periodicity.

ideas.name: TransverseDunes
ideas.one_liner: Dune field from a phasor-style stripe phase field: an asymmetric stoss/slip-face waveform applied to the phase, amplitude dips at phase defects taper the dune ends, and small ripples ride on the stoss face only.
ideas.algorithm: Wind angle W (hybrid, so direction can vary across the map), Frequency f, Defect strength. Lattice 3x3: for each cell j with point c_j and hash h_j: orientation a_j = W + Defect*0.35*rnd11(h_j); wave vector k_j = 2*pi*f*(cos a_j, sin a_j); gaussian g_j = exp(-2.5*|p-c_j|^2); phase phi_j = dot(k_j, p-c_j) + Defect*2*pi*rnd01(h_j). re = sum g_j cos phi_j, im = sum g_j sin phi_j; amp = sqrt(re^2+im^2); phase theta = atan2(im,re)/(2*pi) in [0,1) (polynomial atan2 in the port, 1e-3 accuracy is plenty since the profile is piecewise linear). Dune profile: prof = theta < Stoss ? theta/Stoss : (1-theta)/(1-Stoss) (Stoss ~0.8 gives a 4:1 gentle windward face to steep slip face); crest rounded by a smoothstep window if Crest Round > 0. Height = prof * sat(amp/0.8) (defects: amplitude falls to zero, dune pinches out instead of tearing). Ripples: sin(2*pi*7f*dot(w, p) + 2*noise) * Ripple * smoothstep(0,0.08,theta) * (1 - smoothstep(Stoss-0.08, Stoss, theta)) * sat(amp): ripples only on the stoss, fading at the brink. Output 2*(height+ripples)-1. 3D: use the same kernels in a 3x3x3 window with k_j in the xy-plane only (dunes extruded along z is meaningless; for 3D density terrains output the 2D value after dropping the axis closest to the wind normal). Star dunes: see PolarCells with Spokes = 3..5.
ideas.look: Long sinuous transverse ridges perpendicular to the wind with Y-junction defects, a broad gently lit windward face and a narrow dark slip face, dune tips tapering at defects, fine ripples only on the windward side. Prototyped: Dunes (c0 7.9, scalar 8.7x Perlin). Different from any stripe pattern the library can make: SineWave + warp gives symmetric profiles and no defects.
ideas.why_new: Dunes are defined by asymmetry and by defect topology, neither of which a graph can get from SineWave, Perlin or warps. The asymmetric waveform requires a phase, and a phase requires the complex (re, im) sum, which is internal to the node.
ideas.simd_plan: 9 kernels (27 in 3D) each: one Exp, one Sin+Cos (or a single sincos poly), FMAs; then Sqrt and a polynomial atan2 (~12 ops), the piecewise profile via Select, one more Sin for ripples. Estimated 2D ~4-6x Perlin, 3D ~15x. 4D: 81 kernels, possible but slow; acceptable since dunes are rarely tiled in 4D.
ideas.continuity: C0: the phase wraps at theta=1 where prof is 0 on both sides; amplitude multiplies out the singular point where re=im=0; ripple gates are smoothsteps. Measured c0ratio 7.91. Not C1 at the crest unless Crest Round > 0.
ideas.params: Wind Angle (hybrid), Frequency, Defect, Stoss Fraction, Crest Round, Ripple Amplitude, Ripple Frequency Ratio, Kernel Width.
ideas.risks: Gaussian kernels truncated at the 3x3 window: with Kernel Width too large a faint seam appears at cell borders (keep exp(-2.5 r^2) or tighter). Frequency must be at least ~1.5 cycles per cell or the stripes break into blobs. Dune height does not depend on dune spacing (real fields do); expose Height as hybrid.
sources: Tricard et al. 2019, Procedural Phasor Noise (phase/amplitude decomposition that this reuses; the dune profile, defect taper and stoss-gated ripples are the new part)
ideas.cost_note: Estimated 2D ~4-6x Perlin, 3D ~15x.

ideas.name: TuringStencil
ideas.one_liner: Two synchronous steps of a center-surround (activator-inhibitor) update with sigmoid saturation, evaluated pointwise through the stencil tree: resolution-free labyrinth stripes and spots of uniform width.
ideas.algorithm:
Ring R of radius r: 2D 8 points on the circle, 3D 14 (6 axis + 8 cube diagonals normalised), 4D 24 (8 axis + 16 diagonals). Source u_0 (any smooth noise, scaled so its features are ~r).
  step(u)(p) = tanh( G * ( u(p) - w * mean_{t in R} u(p + t) ) + Bias )
  u_D = step^D (u_0), D in {1,2} via nested fixed loops: |R|+1 evals per level -> (|R|+1)^D source evaluations.
  out = u_D.
The linear part is a difference-of-scales band-pass peaking at wavelength ~2-3 r (the Turing instability's fixed point); tanh saturates; the second application equalises stripe width and removes wiggles (curvature-flow-like).
ideas.look: Zebra/brain-coral labyrinths with constant stripe width and sharp but smooth walls; Bias moves it to isolated spots (leopard) or holes; Gain softens or hardens walls. Unlike Perlin (broad-band, no preferred width) or Cellular (polygonal), the pattern has one dominant wavelength and sinuous, non-branching walls: the reaction-diffusion signature. Coral, brain, fingerprints, sand ripples, giraffe/zebra, lichen.
ideas.why_new: Reaction-diffusion textures are always baked on grids; this is a grid-free, seedable, tileable approximation using the only pointwise trick available: a bounded-depth synchronous update tree. Nothing on the sheet has a single preferred stripe width with sharp walls.
ideas.simd_plan: Nested fixed loops over a precomputed ring offset table; tanh via FS::Exp or rational polynomial; no masks. Cost 2D: depth 1 = 9 Perlin (~10 ns), depth 2 = 81 Perlin (~90 ns); 3D depth 1 = 15 Perlin3D (~33 ns), depth 2 = 225 (~500 ns, flag as heavy); 4D depth 1 = 25 Perlin4D (~108 ns), depth 2 disallowed. Tiles in 4D.
ideas.continuity: Continuous (tanh of continuous averages); as Gain grows it approaches a step, still C0.
ideas.params: Source (default internal Perlin at scale r), Radius hybrid, Weight w float (~1.2), Gain G hybrid, Bias hybrid (spots/stripes/holes), Depth int (1..2), Ring enum (Axis/Full).
ideas.risks: Depth 2 in 3D is very expensive; depth 1 is 'only' a sigmoid band-pass (close to a phasor/Gabor look) and the fixed-point benefit is visible mainly at depth 2; ring sampling at one radius gives slight angular ringing in FFT (use 12-point ring in 2D if visible).
ideas.cost_note: Cost 2D: depth 1 = 9 Perlin (~10 ns), depth 2 = 81 Perlin (~90 ns); 3D depth 1 = 15 Perlin3D (~33 ns), depth 2 = 225 (~500 ns, flag as heavy); 4D depth 1 = 25 Perlin4D (~108 ns), depth 2 disallowed.

ideas.name: VectorSimplexLength
ideas.one_liner: Multi-channel simplex from one lattice pass with vector outputs reduced to a scalar: |v| gives worm tunnels (Minecraft spaghetti/noodle caves, ore veins) in 3D and lattice-free pebble basins in 2D; MaxAbs reproduces Minecraft's exact cave formula at half the cost.
ideas.algorithm: Single OpenSimplex2 traversal; at each contributing vertex take the 32-bit hash and derive C (2..4) independent gradient indices by multiplying the hash with distinct odd constants and taking top bits (or bit slices); the falloff (a^4) is computed once, each channel adds falloff*(g_c . d). Channels n_1..n_C, each normalised like Simplex. Output enum: Length sqrt(sum n_c^2) (2D C=2: zero set = isolated points -> smooth round basins; 3D C=2: zero set = curves -> tubes; 3D C=3: zero set = points -> pockets); MaxAbs max_c |n_c| (Minecraft: max(|S1|,|S2|) with thresholds -0.0765 - 0.0115*thickness); MinAbs; Channel i (cheap decorrelated noise for graphs sharing a lattice); Tube: 1 - Length/Thickness (hybrid Thickness; Minecraft's thickness modulator) clamped to [-1,1]. Rarity (Minecraft interval_select on scale) is achieved by wrapping in DomainScale, or expose a hybrid Scale Multiplier evaluated per lane (per-lane frequency: continuous if the controlling field is smooth).
ideas.look: 3D: continuous winding tunnels of controllable diameter that branch and merge where channels cross zero together (spaghetti caves), finer 'noodle' version at higher frequency, or spherical pockets (cheese holes) with C=3. 2D: a cellular-like field of round basins with Gaussian spacing and no lattice regularity, smoother than Worley F1.
ideas.why_new: The graph equivalent (two Simplex nodes, Abs, Max) costs two full noise evaluations; the shared lattice version costs ~1.2x one. Length (Euclidean cross-section) gives round tubes that Max(|a|,|b|) cannot. Minecraft 1.18's cave system is the most copied recent world-gen design and FastNoise is routinely used to clone it.
ideas.simd_plan: Simplex cost + (C-1) dot products and accumulations per vertex (3 vertices 2D, 4 in 3D, 5 in 4D) + one Sqrt: ~1.15x (C=2) to 1.4x (C=4) Simplex in all dimensions. Gradient index derivation from one hash: 2 integer multiplies per extra channel. GenT friendly (reuse Simplex.inl with a channel loop).
ideas.continuity: Channels are C2; Length is C0 at the zero set only (|v| cusp, which is the tunnel centre line, harmless after thresholding); MaxAbs C0 at channel crossings; Tube C0 where clamped.
ideas.params: Channels (int 2..4), Output enum {Length, MaxAbs, MinAbs, Channel, Tube}, Channel Index, Thickness (hybrid), Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks: Channels from one hash are correlated if bit extraction is sloppy (test with FFT and cross-correlation); tubes pinch to zero diameter where only one channel is zero and the other is small (same as Minecraft, acceptable).
ideas.cost_note: Simplex cost + (C-1) dot products and accumulations per vertex (3 vertices 2D, 4 in 3D, 5 in 4D) + one Sqrt: ~1.15x (C=2) to 1.4x (C=4) Simplex in all dimensions.

ideas.name: VortexPhase
ideas.one_liner: Treat two sources as a complex field and use its winding: forked zebra stripes, spiral waves, or liquid-crystal brushes, all without atan2.
ideas.algorithm:
Inputs: A, B (one Source at seed and seed+1, or two sources), Carrier (hybrid phase), Charge (int q), Radial Frequency f, Softening eps.
a=A(p); b=B(p); r2=a*a+b*b; inv=InvSqrt(r2+eps*eps); c=a*inv; s=b*inv.
Repeat q-1 times (constant loop): (c,s)=(C*c-S*s, C*s+S*c), where (C,S) is the unit value from the first step. This gives cos(q*theta), sin(q*theta) with no atan2.
r=Sqrt(r2); phi=Carrier(p)+f*r.
Out = Cos(phi)*c - Sin(phi)*s, which equals cos(phi+q*theta).
Presets: Carrier=k*dot(dir,p), f=0 gives parallel stripes with forks at each zero of z. Carrier=0, f=25-45 gives spiral waves. Carrier=0, f=0, q=2, out=c*c gives schlieren brushes. Not normalised, a*cos(phi)-b*sin(phi) gives wave packets (single-sideband mix). Clock mode: quantise the angle into 4 or 8 sectors from sign(a), sign(b) and |a|>|b|, which needs no atan.

[ComplexPhase, signal-phase] re = A(p), im = B(p) (B may default to A with Seed Offset +1). r = sqrt(re^2+im^2+eps^2). theta = atan2approx(im, re): a = min(|re|,|im|)/max(|re|,|im|), poly r(a) = a*(0.99997 + a^2*(-0.3258 + 0.0808 a^2)) (or the 5-term version), then Select(|im|>|re|, pi/2 - r, r), Select(re<0, pi - r, r), Select(im<0, -r, r). Mode enum: Phase = theta/pi; Harmonic = cos(m*theta) (int m); UnitRe = re/r, UnitIm = im/r (phase-only noise: constant-amplitude, pinched at zeros); HalfCos/HalfSin = normalize((1+re/r, im/r)) components (line field for fingerprints); LogMag = log(r) remapped (poles at joint zeros); Winding mask = smoothstep on r (marks vortex cores as dots).
ideas.look:
Tested in 2D. Carrier mode reads as real zebra hide: parallel, constant-width stripes with isolated forks, and fork density set by the frequency of A and B. Spiral mode resembles Belousov-Zhabotinsky chemical waves or marbling with small spiral cores. Schlieren mode gives black and white brushes meeting at point defects, like nematic liquid-crystal micrographs, and is unlike anything on the contact sheet. Uses: animal hides, wood, sci-fi textures, masks. In 3D the zeros of z are lines, so spirals become scroll waves around filaments (not rendered).
[PhaseCharge, volumetric-3d4d] Prototyped. m=3, k=0 in 2D: black and white star pinwheels at vortices with cusp lines between opposite charges, clearly unlike anything on the sheet. m=3, k=14 in 3D isosurface: tight rolled and folded sheets like pastry, ammonite or cortical folds, very unusual. m=1 with large k looks like marble bands, close to a warped PingPong, so charge is what gives the distinctive look. Use for alien organics, fungus gills, spiral chemical waves, plasma, animated textures.
[CarrierStripes, dcc-tools] Zebra, fingerprints, sand ripples, tiger stripes, corduroy with defects, wood figure, combed hair. Defect Scale sets fork density: 0.3 gives few forks, 1.2 gives broken dashes. Warp 2.5-5 gives fingerprint whorls. Good as a mask or displacement. Prototype: dcc_lens mode=25.
ideas.why_new: Stripes with point defects cannot be built from existing nodes: there is no phase carrier, and no way to add topological charge without atan2. It is the first node where the zero set of a complex field is the design control. The fork count follows from the source frequency instead of being a side effect.
ideas.simd_plan: Fully branch free and dimension agnostic because everything flows through sources, so 2D, 3D and 4D use the same code. Cost: 2 source evals, plus one InvSqrt, one Sqrt, one Sin+Cos, and 2 multiplies per extra charge. No lattice window of its own. Estimated (not measured) 2.5-3.5x Perlin when A and B are Perlin, far below CellularDistance in 3D and 4D.
ideas.continuity: C0 everywhere when eps>0 (numerically verified in the spiral preset: step ratio 8.0). At eps=0 there are isolated point discontinuities at the vortex cores. The clock mode is discontinuous by design.
ideas.params: Hybrid: Carrier, Radial Frequency, Softening. Members: A, B (GeneratorSource), Charge (int). Mode enum: Phase, Schlieren, Clock, Quadrature.
ideas.risks:
Spirals have non-constant width because |grad r| varies, so they look like sine-of-noise away from the cores; combining with IsoBands distance could tighten this. Charge 1 and 2 look nearly the same at spiral preset scale. In GenTileable a linear carrier wraps on the 4D torus and stripes curve and chirp. 3D was not look-tested.
[CarrierStripes, dcc-tools] Single global orientation unless warped, and warps change local spacing. GenTileable puts a plane wave on the 4D torus, so tiled stripes curve (seamless, but direction is lost). Seed only changes S,T, not stripe direction.
[PhaseCharge, volumetric-3d4d] Band frequency depends on |grad r|, so wavelength is not constant. r range depends on the sources, so k needs normalisation. Thin cusp lines at m>=3 alias at low resolution; raise e to soften. A bit stylised for terrain.
ideas.variant_notes: One formula: cos(phi + q*arg(a+ib)) from two sources. CarrierStripes is the plane-carrier q=1 preset (fingerprint and zebra forks), PhaseCharge the charge and radial-winding preset (3D scroll-wave sheets), ComplexPhase adds raw phase, log-magnitude and half-angle outputs.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated (not measured) 2.5-3.5x Perlin when A and B are Perlin, far below CellularDistance in 3D and 4D.
