ideas.name: WaveLattice
ideas.one_liner: Sum, product or max of N phase-modulated plane gratings at symmetric angles: hexagonal/octagonal lattices, 5- and 7-fold quasicrystals, 2-coloured line arrangements, with noise-driven phase to melt them organically.
ideas.algorithm:
N wave vectors k_j (N = 2..12). 2D: angle_j = pi*j/N + Rotation (N=2 square, 3 hexagonal, 4 octagonal, 5/7 quasicrystal). 3D: tables: N=3 cubic axes, N=4 tetrahedral body diagonals, N=6 icosahedral fivefold axes (0,+-1,+-phi) cyclic, normalised. 4D: per-seed hashed directions or the 24-cell axes (12). psi_j = 2pi*F*dot(k_j,p) + 2pi*rnd01(hash(seed,j))*PhaseJitter + Beta*m_j(p) where m is a HybridSource 'Phase Modulation' evaluated once at p (shared, 1 eval) or per-grating via seed offset j (N evals; enum). Combine enum: Sum = (1/N) sum cos psi_j (quasiperiodic bumps); Product = prod cos psi_j (sign flips across every grating line: a 2-colouring of a line arrangement, polygon mosaics, soft-pinched near lines); Max = max_j cos psi_j (ridged tile lattice); MinAbs = 1-min_j|sin psi_j|-ish via smooth min (line network / wire mesh: distance-like to the arrangement); Phase = atan2approx(sum sin, sum cos)/pi.

[PlanarWaveNoise, shader-community] Setup when params change: for i in 0..N-1 draw from Seed: unit direction d_i (2D: angle = Orientation + Spread*rnd11; 3D: Fibonacci-sphere point jittered; 4D: normalised 4-vector of 4 gaussians via Box-Muller from hashes), frequency f_i = Frequency*(1 + Bandwidth*rnd11), phase ph_i = rnd01*2pi, amplitude a_i = 1 (or 1/f_i^H for a 1/f spectrum).
Eval: t_i = f_i * dot(p, d_i) + ph_i (one FMA chain per direction)
  Profile enum: Sine cos(t_i); Triangle 4|fract(t/2pi)-0.5|-1; Square sign(cos t); Sawtooth; (precomputed 256-entry periodic table with linear interp = arbitrary profile, e.g. a Gaussian-blurred sawtooth)
  Combine enum: Sum: out = sum a_i prof(t_i) / sqrt(N) (Gaussian-ish, Gabor-like spectrum); Max: out = max_i prof(t_i) (planar fronts intersect into convex cells: the 'cellular wave noise' flavour); SoftMax via exp smin with k; Product of (1+prof)/2.
Anisotropy: Spread small -> all waves near one orientation (stripes with interference); Spread=pi -> isotropic.
N is an int member, loop count fixed across lanes.
ideas.look: N=5 Sum: the classic fivefold quasicrystal lace; N=3 Sum: honeycomb bumps; Product with Beta>0: wobbly polygon mosaic with straight-ish wiggling edges (looks like cracked glaze with ruler-drawn cracks); Max: tiled pyramids; MinAbs: chain-link / woven mesh. In 3D with icosahedral axes: 3D quasicrystal density (slices show aperiodic Penrose-like motifs). Uses: decorative tiles, crystals, lattice masks, honeycomb, energy shields, moire-free background structures.
ideas.why_new: SineWave is the N=D axis-aligned product only. Quasicrystals and line-arrangement colourings are visually unlike every lattice noise and cannot be approximated by warps of SineWave. Phase modulation by a source is what turns a mathematical pattern into a usable noise.
ideas.simd_plan: N x (dot + cos poly) + N hashes for the phase jitter: N=5 in 2D ~0.5x Perlin plus the modulation source; cost is flat in dimension (no window), so 4D is cheap and tiling works. Branch-free; Max/MinAbs via FS::Max/Min chains; tables are per-node constants.
ideas.continuity: Sum/Product/Phase-free outputs C-infinity (modulated by the source's continuity); Max C0; MinAbs C0 (C1 with smooth-min). Phase wraps by design.
ideas.params: Feature Scale; N (int); Rotation; Frequency (hybrid); Phase Modulation (hybrid) + Beta + PerGrating enum; PhaseJitter; Combine enum; Seed Offset.
ideas.risks:
Globally quasiperiodic: no spatial variation without modulation/warp (document). Product output amplitude collapses near lines (normalise by (1/N) power or output sign*|prod|^(1/N)). Aliasing at high F.
[PlanarWaveNoise, shader-community] Low N shows obvious repetition along each wave direction; sums of few sines are quasi-periodic and look 'mathematical' unless N >= 12 or combined with warp. Range normalisation by sqrt(N) is approximate for non-sine profiles.
sources: Quasicrystal plane-wave sum shaders (shader community folklore, e.g. Shadertoy; recalled, not fetched)
ideas.variant_notes: Separated from WaveNoise because Product, Max and MinAbs combines give polygon mosaics and line nets, not a Gaussian field. PlanarWaveNoise contributes the random-direction Max combine (convex crystal cells).
ideas.cost_note: N x (dot + cos poly) + N hashes for the phase jitter: N=5 in 2D ~0.5x Perlin plus the modulation source; cost is flat in dimension (no window), so 4D is cheap and tiling works.

ideas.name: WaveNoise
ideas.one_liner: Sum of M random-direction plane waves with controlled spectrum (Berry monochromatic ring, Kolmogorov/Weierstrass power law, or N-fold quasicrystal), with Real, Speckle and Phase outputs.
ideas.algorithm:
Setup (constant tables, no per-lane state): a low-discrepancy direction table D[0..M-1] (2D: angles pi*i/M + golden jitter; 3D: Fibonacci sphere; 4D: Fibonacci on S^3), and a stratified table t_i = (i+0.5)/M.
Gen(seed, x):
  // decorrelate seeds with ONE random rotation of the sample point instead of M rotations of the directions
  R = rotation from hash(seed): 2D one angle (1 sincos); 3D random quaternion from 3 hash floats (Shoemake, 2 sincos + 2 sqrt); 4D two angles in two planes.
  x' = R * x * k0                  (k0 from Feature Scale)
  re = 0; im = 0; norm = 0
  for i in 0..M-1 (fixed count):
    phi_i = 2pi * hash01(seed, i)                       // integer hash, cheap
    Spectrum == Ring:      k_i = 1,  a_i = 1
    Spectrum == PowerLaw:  k_i = 2^(Bandwidth * frac(t_i + hash01(seed,i+M)*0.5)) ; a_i = k_i^(-Beta/2)
    Spectrum == Symmetric: direction = fixed (cos(pi i/M), sin(pi i/M)), no rotation, phi_i = 0 or random
    theta = k_i * dot(D[i], x') + phi_i
    s = Sin(theta); c = Cos(theta) (c only needed for Speckle/Phase)
    re += a_i * c; im += a_i * s; norm += a_i*a_i
  g = 1/Sqrt(norm/2)                                     // unit variance
  Output == Real:    v = im * g * 0.33 ; if Sharpness>0: v = tanh(Sharpness*v)/tanh(Sharpness) (tanh via Exp)
  Output == Speckle: I = (re*re + im*im)/norm ; v = 1 - 2*Exp(-I)          // |psi|^2 is exponential-distributed -> uniform in [-1,1]
  Output == PhaseSin: v = (re*cosPsi + im*sinPsi) * InvSqrt(re*re+im*im+eps)  // cos(phase - Psi): unit-contrast fringes, no atan2 needed
  Output == Phase:   v = atan2poly(im, re)/pi                                // sawtooth, discontinuous
Turing/Swift-Hohenberg look: Ring + Sharpness ~3 gives labyrinth stripes of exact wavelength 2pi/k0; add a Bias before tanh to switch stripes->spots; Symmetric M=3 gives hexagonal spot lattice.
Weierstrass-Mandelbrot: PowerLaw with k_i on a geometric ladder gamma^n and a_i = gamma^((D-3)n) is exactly the Ausloos-Berman 2D W-M function.
ideas.look:
Ring: band-limited isotropic 'monochromatic' blobs and stripes whose zero set is Berry nodal domains (percolation-like labyrinth), unlike Perlin's mixed scales. PowerLaw: isotropic 1/f^beta noise without any lattice signature in the FFT. Speckle: laser-speckle granules with sharp dark zeros (phase vortices) and bright hot spots. PhaseSin: equal-contrast interference fringes with dislocations. Symmetric 5/7/12: quasicrystal rosettes. Good for Turing patterns (animal coats, coral, sand ripples), clouds with set spectral slope, speckle/dust masks, interference art, optical textures.
[WaveShell, volumetric-3d4d] Prototyped. 3D isosurface, 6 waves: aperiodic sponge with visibly ordered rows and local five-fold motifs that never repeat. 24 waves: amorphous bicontinuous spinodal sponge with one characteristic pore size, like aerogel, polymer blends or Nuclepore. Both phases percolate at threshold 0. 2D grey slice is soft and blobby and on its own not distinctive, so the value is in 3D, FFT ring and isotropy. Good for sponges, porous rock, sci-fi lattices, labyrinth masks.
ideas.why_new: Nothing on the contact sheet is band-limited or has a controllable spectrum: FBm only reaches octave-spaced power laws and always inherits lattice artefacts. WaveNoise has no lattice window at all (so no seams, no 4D blow-up: cost is nearly flat across 2D/3D/4D), gives exact ring spectra (the Turing/Chladni/Berry family), speckle statistics, and subsumes the Weierstrass-Mandelbrot terrain function and quasicrystal interference as parameter settings.
ideas.simd_plan: Fully branch-free: fixed M loop, all per-wave constants from tables + integer hash. Per wave: 1 dot (d FMAs), 1 hash, 1 Sin (+1 Cos for complex outputs). No lattice window. Per-lane seed handled by rotating x once per lane. Est. AVX2 cost M=16: 2D ~2.5-3x Perlin, 3D ~1.3x Perlin3D, 4D ~0.8x Perlin4D (dimension only adds one FMA per wave). Far-coordinate precision: reduce theta mod 2pi before Sin (Round(theta*inv2pi) FMA) since |x|*k0 grows. GenT<P...> parameter pack works directly; tiling via GenTileable2D works since the function is defined for any 4D point.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity for Real, Speckle, PhaseSin (except isolated zeros of psi where PhaseSin is undefined; masked to 0). Phase (sawtooth) is discontinuous across the branch cut by design.
ideas.params: Waves M (int 4-64), Spectrum enum {Ring, PowerLaw, Symmetric}, Feature Scale (k0), Bandwidth octaves (float, PowerLaw), Beta spectral slope (float, 5/3 Kolmogorov in 1D-energy convention; document the power-vs-amplitude factor 2), Output enum {Real, Speckle, PhaseSin, Phase}, Sharpness (hybrid: tanh gain; spatially varying sharpness turns smooth noise into Turing stripes locally), Bias (hybrid: stripes vs spots), Phase offset Psi (hybrid, animates fringes), Seed.
ideas.risks:
Small M (<8) shows visible beating and long-range interference; Ring covariance J0(kr) has oscillating long tails (that is the physics, but users may read it as repetition). Statistical stationarity only: one seed is one global realisation, locally it still looks uniform. Normalisation of Real by 0.33*sigma clips Gaussian tails ~0.3% of samples. 4D Fibonacci-on-S^3 table needs care to be uniform.
[WaveField, lattice-kernels] Low K shows periodic beat and repetition at large scale; K>=16 needed. Phase precision degrades at huge coordinates because f*dot grows; wrap needed. Homogeneous everywhere, so it is a texture rather than a terrain basis. Hybrid frequency impossible in plane-wave form.
[FourierNoise, terrain-tools-engines] Not local: with N < 12 individual plane waves are visible as banding; statistics are stationary but the pattern is quasi-periodic at very large scales (recurrences when few incommensurate frequencies); seed changes phases/rotation only, so different seeds share a 'family' spectrum (acceptable since the spectrum is the parameter).
sources: M. V. Berry, 'Regular and irregular semiclassical wavefunctions', J. Phys. A 1977 (random wave model; recalled, not fetched)
ideas.variant_notes: Global sum of N plane waves with a designed spectrum. Features folded in: exact tiling by snapping wave vectors to integer periods (FourierNoise); a Crystallinity hybrid sliding from icosahedral quasicrystal to amorphous spinodal in 3D (WaveShell); threshold-to-labyrinth use (RingSpectrumNoise); J0 ring kernels as the fallback when wavelength must vary in space (WaveField).
ideas.cost_note: AVX2 cost M=16: 2D ~2.5-3x Perlin, 3D ~1.3x Perlin3D, 4D ~0.8x Perlin4D (dimension only adds one FMA per wave).

ideas.name: WaveNoiseSliced
ideas.one_liner: Sum of N randomly oriented hyperplanar waves with random phases, each wave a precomputed/analytic 1D band-limited profile; gives exact spectral control, isotropy or anisotropy, Gaussian or phasor/ridged outputs, in any dimension at near-Perlin cost (Guehl et al. SIGGRAPH 2025; LRP noise Gilet 2014).
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Directions N (int, 8-32), FreqMin, FreqMax (floats, band), Harmonics M (int 2-6), AnisoAngle (hybrid), AnisoWidth (hybrid, pi = isotropic), SliceSize S (float), Output enum {Real, Phase, Magnitude, Ridged=1-|Real|}.
Setup when params change (small per-node tables are allowed): for i<N: direction d_i stratified over the circle (2D) / sphere via Fibonacci spiral (3D) / 4-sphere (4D), centred on AnisoAngle with spread AnisoWidth; for m<M: frequency f_m log-spaced in [FreqMin,FreqMax], amplitude A_m from the desired spectrum (e.g. 1/f^beta), phase phi_im = rnd(seed,i,m)*2pi.
Gen(p): Re=Im=0; for i<N: t = dot(p, d_i); // alignment-artefact reduction from the paper: slice the axis into cells of width S, jitter per slice: k = floor(t/S + jitter_i), u = frac; use a per-slice phase offset dphi = rnd(hash(seed,i,k))*2pi and blend with the neighbouring slice: w = smoothstep(u) ; for m<M: a = 2pi f_m t; Re += A_m*( (1-w)*cos(a+phi_im+dphi_k) + w*cos(a+phi_im+dphi_{k+1}) ); Im same with sin. Output Real = Re/sqrt(N*sum A_m^2/2) (analytic Gaussian normalisation), Phase = atan2(Im,Re)/pi (phasor-like stripes), Magnitude, Ridged.
Without slicing (S=inf) it is a pure sum of plane waves, exactly LRP-style spectral noise, cheaper but with visible long-range wave alignment; S ~ 2-4 wavelengths removes it.
ideas.look: Smooth band-limited isotropic noise with no lattice artefacts (clean ring spectrum), or with narrow AnisoWidth: fibres, brushed/streaked materials, marble veins; Phase output gives phasor-like stripes; narrow band + Ridged gives 'wired/crystal' nets (paper). Visually cleaner and more controllable than FBm Simplex, and different from everything on the sheet in the FFT (ring instead of blob).
ideas.why_new: FastNoise has no node with explicit spectral control (band-pass, slope, anisotropy); fractal sums only approximate 1/f. Wave noise gives exact band-pass and anisotropy in 2/3/4D at the cost of N*M sincos, and the same node also produces phasor-style and ridged non-Gaussian outputs. It also animates well via a phase/time hybrid.
ideas.simd_plan: Fully branch-free: N x M fixed loop of FMAs + Sin/Cos (FS::Sin/Cos are polynomial, ~10 ops each). N=16, M=3: 48 sincos ~ 4-6x Perlin in 2D, and the cost is dimension-independent (only the dot product grows) which makes 3D/4D cheaper than Simplex3D/4D relative to quality. Directions/amplitudes live in a per-node table (<1 KB).
ideas.continuity: C-infinity (sums of sinusoids with smooth slice blending). Phase output has isolated singularities like PhasorNoise.
ideas.params: Directions N (int), Harmonics M (int), FreqMin/FreqMax (float), SpectralSlope (float), AnisoAngle (hybrid), AnisoWidth (hybrid), SliceSize (float), Phase/Time (hybrid), Output (enum), Feature Scale.
ideas.risks: Too few directions shows plane-wave alignment (paper: 30-60 for perfect isotropy, 8-16 is fine at fractal scale). Normalisation of non-Gaussian outputs is empirical. Per-lane hybrid AnisoAngle requires rotating the direction table per lane (2D: one sincos per direction, acceptable).
ideas.cost_note: N=16, M=3: 48 sincos ~ 4-6x Perlin in 2D, and the cost is dimension-independent (only the dot product grows) which makes 3D/4D cheaper than Simplex3D/4D relative to quality.

queue.name: WaveNoiseSliced
queue.reason: Exact band-pass and anisotropy control at dimension-flat cost (J3 top pick). Cost claims disagree (4-6x versus 13x Perlin), so measure. Merge with wave-noise.

ideas.name: AdaptiveCellular
ideas.one_liner: Density-controlled cellular noise on a hashed quadtree/octree: a hybrid Density field decides, level by level, whether a cell subdivides, so cell size varies smoothly with a control map (Jonchier, Salvati, Derouet-Jourdan 2019, 'Procedural Non-Uniform Cellular Noise').
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Density (hybrid 0..1), MaxDepth D (int 1-5), Jitter (float), Output enum {F1, F2-F1, CellValue, Depth}, Distance enum.
Leaf test for a cell c at level l (size 2^-l): leaf(c,l) = (l == D) | (rnd01(hash(seed,l,c)) >= Density(centre(c,l)) ) with the ancestor chain consistent: a cell exists only if all its ancestors were subdivided; define subdiv(c,l) = rnd01(hash(seed,l,c)) < Density(centre(c,l)).
Gen(p): bestD = inf; for l in 0..D (fixed loop): cl = floor(p*2^l); for each of the 3^dim neighbours n of cl at level l (fixed loop): alive = AND over ancestors a of n (levels 0..l-1, fixed loop of l steps, or carried incrementally from the previous level's 3x3 alive flags) of subdiv(a); isLeaf = alive & (l==D | !subdiv(n,l)); feature point f = (n + 0.5 + Jitter*(rnd-0.5))*2^-l; d = dist(p,f); bestD = Select(isLeaf, min(bestD,d), bestD); track second best for F2 and the hash for CellValue.
Incremental trick: the alive flags of level l+1 neighbours are the subdiv flags of their parents, which are among the 3^dim level-l neighbours already visited, so the whole thing is D x 3^dim hashes + D Density evaluations at cell centres (Density evaluated at the 3^dim centres per level = 9D source evals in 2D, or sample Density once at p and treat it as locally constant for a cheap approximation).
F1 normalised by the leaf size (so cells look uniform in local terms) or absolute (for true multi-scale distances).
ideas.look: Voronoi-like cells whose size follows a map: large plains cells grading into fine mountain cells, dense crowds of small cells near 'attractors', hierarchical cracked-crust looks (Depth output). Smooth transitions in cell density, not just warped Worley.
ideas.why_new: DomainScale with a hybrid scale warps the lattice (stretching cells, discontinuities when scale varies), it cannot change cell density smoothly. Fractal Cellular sums all levels; this picks one leaf per region. Feature-count control from a node is a frequently requested terrain/texture capability.
ideas.simd_plan: Fixed D x 3^dim loop of hashes and distances with Select; 2D D=4: 36 hashes + 36 distances ~ 2.5x CellularDistance2D; 3D D=3: 81 cells ~ 3x CellularDistance3D. Density sampled per level at p only (approximation) keeps Source cost at D evals.
ideas.continuity: F1 is C0 as long as the nearest leaf point lies in the searched window at its level (guaranteed because each level's 3^dim window is searched and points stay in their cells with Jitter<=1). Cell topology flips where Density crosses a hash threshold, but the threshold is evaluated per cell centre, so no spatial discontinuity inside a cell; at borders between leaves of different levels F1 stays continuous.
ideas.params: Density (hybrid), MaxDepth (int), Jitter (float), Output (enum), DistanceFunction (enum), Normalise enum {PerLeaf, Absolute}.
ideas.risks: Cost grows linearly with D times the window; Density evaluated at neighbour centres is expensive if it is a complex graph (use GeneratorCache or the per-point approximation). The original chapter is paywalled; the above is a from-scratch pointwise design of the stated idea.
ideas.cost_note: Fixed D x 3^dim loop of hashes and distances with Select; 2D D=4: 36 hashes + 36 distances ~ 2.5x CellularDistance2D; 3D D=3: 81 cells ~ 3x CellularDistance3D.

ideas.name: AlligatorNoise
ideas.one_liner: Houdini's alligator: weighted compact domes per site, output is the gap between the two strongest, giving raised scales of varied height with flat creased gaps.
ideas.algorithm: Per the SideFX HDK reference. cell=floor(p); m1=m2=0. For each cell in the 3^dim window: h=hash(cell); c=cell+jitter(h); w=rnd01(mix(h)); d=Sqrt(dot(p-c,p-c)); t=Max(0,1-d/R); f=w*t*t*(3-2t); mask=f>m1; m2=Select(mask,m1,Max(m2,f)); m1=Max(m1,f). Return ScaleOutput(m1-m2, 0, 1). The HDK uses R=1 and a 3x3x3 search. Fractal use in other tools: lacunarity 2.2-2.5 with high persistence.
ideas.look: Scaly hide, blistered paint, cobbled skin. Domes of different heights separated by creases, with black dead zones where two weak sites meet. Fractal version reads as cauliflower or lichen. Prototype: dcc_lens mode=0, fractal mode=16 which=1.
ideas.why_new: Not reachable from CellularDistance: F2-F1 has no per-site weight and no compact falloff, and top-2 selection on weighted values cannot be expressed by a graph. SideFX docs say it cannot be simulated with their Worley functions. Height varies per cell, unlike F2-F1 where every cell peaks at a similar level.
ideas.simd_plan: Same 3^dim loop as CellularDistance, plus one hash mix, Sqrt and a cubic. No Sqrt avoidance possible because the falloff needs d. Estimated 5.5 / 17 / 58 ns, 1.4x CellularDistance. Scalar proto 113 ns vs 50 for perlin2 and 109 for the harness worley2.
ideas.continuity: C0 everywhere: R=1 means any site outside the window is at distance >=1 and contributes 0, at any jitter <=1 inside the cell. C1 except on the creases where m1 and m2 swap. Measured c0ratio 8.0 at jitter 1 and 0.7.
ideas.params: Grid Jitter (hybrid), Weight Jitter (hybrid; 0 reduces to a smoothstep F2-F1), Radius (float, <=1), Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks: Mean is low (about -0.34 after 2x-1), so a measured remap may be nicer than the [0,1] bound. 4D is costly like all cell nodes.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated 5.5 / 17 / 58 ns, 1.4x CellularDistance. Scalar proto 113 ns vs 50 for perlin2 and 109 for the harness worley2.

queue.name: AlligatorNoise
queue.reason: Houdini alligator: top-2 weighted domes in the Cellular loop at 1.4x. Proven look; just needs a measured remap.

ideas.name: BarchanField
ideas.one_liner: Analytic crescent dunes with a true constant-angle slip face, combined by Max so rising sand supply merges isolated barchans into barchanoid and transverse ridges.
ideas.algorithm:
Lattice with jitter and staggered rows. For each cell in the 3x3 window, take (u,v)=rotate(p-c, wind(p)), a local rotation about the dune's own centre, so spatially varying wind causes no far-field shear. Size H from hash*SandSupply(p); R=k1*H; toe length Lt=k2*H.
Across-wind: if |v|<R, H_v=H*(1-(v/R)^2). Brink: ub(v)=kappa*v^2 (horns trail downwind). Toe: ut(v)=-Lt*sqrt(1-(v/R)^2).
Height: for u<ub, s=(u-ut)/(ub-ut), z=H_v*s^1.5 (stoss). For u>=ub, z=max(0,H_v-Slip*(u-ub)) (lee), and Slip is a world-space slope constant. out=SmoothMax over candidates.
Second scale: add ripples only on stoss, perpendicular to the wind, weighted by s*(1-s), and none on the slip face, giving non-additive fractal detail. SandSupply controls both size and existence.

[BarchanField, nature-phenomena] H=small base. For each cell in the 3^D window: v=x-p_i; R=Rmin+Rrange*r3; u=(v.w)/R (along wind); t=|v-(v.w)w|/R (across wind: |perp| in 2D, radial distance in the plane perpendicular to w in 3D); sc=u-curve*t^2 (crest is a parabola); env=saturate(1-t^2)^0.75; up=saturate(1+sc/Lw)^1.5 (windward, Lw=1.3); dn=saturate(1-sc/Ls) (slip face, Ls=0.28); pr=Select(sc<0,up,dn)*env*R; H=max(H,pr). Add time by offsetting positions along wind with a speed that scales inversely with R, to make small dunes migrate faster.
ideas.look:
Hillshade reads immediately as barchan dunes seen from above, all aligned with the wind and with shaded crescents. Varying curvature gives parabolic or transverse shapes. In 3D, the same kernel gives scalloped shell shapes.
[PolarKernelField (Barchan), lattice-kernels] Barchan dune fields, wind-driven snow sastrugi, shark scales, directional crag and tail. Prototyped: distinct crescent horns with sharp lee side on a flat ground at density 0.7; density 1 merges into fields of sails. The hillshade is immediately sand-like.
ideas.why_new: Sawtooth or warped-ridge approaches give neither crescents nor a slip angle independent of scale, and no existing node has a mechanism that moves between isolated and connected dune topologies under a single hybrid.
ideas.simd_plan:
9 kernels with Select masks, one sqrt per kernel; about CellularDistance 2D, 4-8 ns, about 5x Perlin. 3D: treat z as time, moving c by wind*z*V/H within a per-cell lifetime fade (larger dunes slower), or 3D cells at 27 kernels. 4D: 81 is expensive; use (x,y) cells plus crossfade or accept no tiling.
[BarchanField, nature-phenomena] Cell loop with max and Select; no atan. Estimated 6 ns in 2D (5x Perlin, 1.5x CellularDistance), 20 ns in 3D, 60-80 ns in 4D. Wind direction is a member or hybrid. Use x^1.5 as x*sqrt(x), or an integer power in the port.
ideas.continuity: C0: H_v=0 at |v|=R, s=0 at toe and lee reaches 0 by clamp. Slip face is a sharp but continuous crease, as in nature. Dune extent must stay within the window, so R and the downwind reach are clamped to 1 cell.
ideas.params: Wind Angle (hybrid), Sand Supply (hybrid), Size Jitter, Horn Curvature kappa, Stoss Length, Slip Slope (float), Ripple Amount and Wavelength.
ideas.risks:
Not tested. Max composition does not produce real collisions. Fully transverse ridges require R at window limit, so high supply may still look like a chain of crescents. Elevation slope depends on Feature Scale, so Slip must be defined in output-per-world units and may need rescaling.
[BarchanField, nature-phenomena] Kernel reach must fit within the window at maximum R, or seams appear at cell edges. Slip-face steepness aliases at low sampling rates. Physical accuracy is stylised, not simulated. Only the 2D form was prototyped; the 3D use is speculative.
ideas.variant_notes: Option: per-dune wind sampled at the lane gives no far-field shear because rotation is about each dune's own centre. Slip slope must be defined in world units.
ideas.cost_note: 9 kernels with Select masks, one sqrt per kernel; about CellularDistance 2D, 4-8 ns, about 5x Perlin.

ideas.name: BarrancoCones
ideas.one_liner: Volcano and basin cones carrying radial gullies that branch by analytic period doubling in log-polar coordinates, so gully spacing stays constant at all radii for O(1) per cone.
ideas.algorithm: For each cone in the 3x3 window: r=|p-c|/R, th=atan2 approx/(2pi)+warp/r_clamped+seed. t=log2(max(r,r0)/r0); k=floor(t); u=t-k. Period P=1/(n0*2^k). q=th/P; s=q-floor(q)-0.5. Branch-specific split time u0=0.15+0.6*hash(floor(q),k). ramp=smoothstep((u-u0)/(1-u0)). Distance in period units: |abs(s)-0.25*ramp|; at u=1 both branches land exactly on the next level's centres, so branches are continuous across levels. World distance=dist*P*2pi*r. g=smooth(1-dist/w). Carve=Depth(r)*Gain^t*g with continuous t, avoiding ring seams. Height=(exp(-a*r)-exp(-a))*fade(r)-Carve. Combine by Max. Variants: Basin sign flip gives centripetal drainage; Caldera replaces the profile centre by a rim and flat floor, optionally with nested collapse circles.
ideas.look: Stratovolcanoes or lone peaks with deep radial barrancos forking as they descend, and a central crater. Inverted: drainage funnels. Good as hero landforms or as a coarse layer under other details.
ideas.why_new: CellularDistance gives smooth cones only, and radial sine stripes have spacing that grows with r. Spacing here stays constant because branch count doubles with radius, with no segment search needed.
ideas.simd_plan: Per cone: polynomial atan2, log2, one hash, Selects. 9 cones with Max; estimate 10-18 ns in 2D, about 12x Perlin. Can reduce to 4 cones with a tighter size cap. 3D: 27 cells with azimuth about a chosen axis plus true 3D radius, gullies as meridians. 4D: 81 is too costly; use a planar lattice, so no torus tiling.
ideas.continuity: C0 if the carve width w stays under 0.25 of the local branch spacing (P*2pi*r, whose minimum is 2pi*r0/n0), since then the carve is 0 at branch interval edges. The test used w above this limit, a known defect to fix. Atan seam is hidden by periodic q when n0 is an integer and warp is added after.
ideas.params: Cone Density, Radius R, Radius Jitter, Base Branches n0 (int), Inner Radius r0, Gully Width w, Gully Depth, Depth Gain, Profile (enum Peak, Basin, Caldera), Warp Source (hybrid).
ideas.risks: TESTED in numpy (radial2), not ported. Near the summit it reads as convincing radial gullies with forks. Outer flanks degrade into wandering squiggles, because angular warp scales up with radius; the warp must scale as 1/r, as written above but not yet retested. First test with heavy warp and stepped depth looked like fingerprints with ring seams.
ideas.cost_note: 9 cones with Max; estimate 10-18 ns in 2D, about 12x Perlin.

ideas.name: BasinTree
ideas.one_liner: Dendritic valley/ridge/canyon networks carved into a base relief from a steepest-descent graph on a jittered lattice: every cell drains to its lowest neighbour, the surface is base minus the max of finite-width valley profiles around the nearby stream segments.
ideas.algorithm: Lattice: jittered integer grid (CellularDistance style), one feature point c_i per cell (jitter ~0.45). Base: a cheap smooth field B evaluated at cell points (prototype used 2-octave Perlin at scale 0.15; a node should use bilinear value noise of a 4x coarser lattice = 4 hashes per cell so no source evals are needed). Downstream of cell i: d(i) = argmin over its 8 (26 in 3D) neighbours j of B(c_j), kept as i itself if none is lower (sink = lake/sea). Segments s_i = [c_i, c_d(i)] form a forest of trees that terminate at the minima of B, so there are no cycles by construction (B strictly decreases along every chain). Pointwise eval at p: for every cell i in the (2R+1)^dim window (R=2 so that any segment with an endpoint within 1 cell of p is included): t = clamp(dot(p-c_i, v)/|v|^2), d = |p - c_i - t v|, hseg = lerp(B(c_i), B(c_d), t); size = sat((h0 - hseg)*k) (lower base = larger stream, the stream-order proxy); width w = W0*(0.25+size), depth D = D0*(0.3+size); profile v = D*(1-smoothstep(0,w,d)) [V], or floor f = 0.5*w*size, e = sat((d-f)/w), v = D*(1-e^2) [U, glacial trough], or v = D*(1-smoothstep(f, f+wall, d)) [Box, slot canyon]. carve = max_i v_i. out = B(p)*relief - carve (+ optional fine fbm). ridge mode: out = -(out). Longitudinal profile is concave-up automatically because hseg follows B along the chain; per-segment hashed knickpoints (step in hseg) give waterfalls. Multi-scale: run a second, 4x finer instance whose B is this node's own output at the fine cell points (fixed extra evals) so tributaries join the trunk valleys; 2D only at sane cost.
ideas.look:
Fern/antler-like branching valley systems converging into basins, with valley width and depth growing downstream; U mode gives flat-floored troughs with parabolic walls (glacial valleys), Box mode gives a slot-canyon network seen from above, Ridge mode gives dendritic mountain spines with spurs. Domain-warping the input position upstream (ordinary DomainWarp node) turns the straight segments into meandering ones and the result reads as real drainage. Prototyped: BasinV/U/Canyon/RidgeTree, BasinWarped, CanyonWarped. Good for river valleys, badlands, canyon lands, glacial troughs, cave networks in 3D.
[CellularDrainage, cell-relations] Dendritic branching: many short tributaries merging into thicker trunks that end in small lakes, like river basins, lightning, leaf veins or root systems (3D tubes). With a large-scale source as elevation, the trees follow the real downhill direction of that terrain, so rivers are consistent with an FBm heightmap. No existing node makes tree-like (acyclic, branching) structures.
ideas.why_new: Nothing in the library produces tree topology: cellular gives closed cells, ridged fractals give isotropic crinkles. A graph of existing nodes cannot express 'drain to the lowest neighbour' or 'distance to a segment'. Differs from the sibling FlowNetwork (Scheidegger lattice, one global flow direction) and QuadDendrite (quadtree parents): here streams follow a smooth base so they converge radially into basins/lakes and the stream size, valley width and floor height all derive from that base, which is what makes it read as terrain.
ideas.simd_plan: Window: compute B for the (2R+3)^dim block once per lane batch (7x7=49 cells in 2D, each 4 hashes + lerp; store in registers/stack arrays indexed by constant loops), then loop the 5x5 inner cells: pick downstream by 8 compare+Select, segment distance (FMA, one Sqrt or compare on squared distance with w^2), profile via smoothstep, running Max. All loops have constant trip counts; no per-lane branching. 3D: 7^3=343 base cells and 125 segments (27-neighbour argmin) = roughly 8-10x CellularDistance 3D; acceptable for a landform node, and it yields branching cave tunnels. 4D: 7^4 is prohibitive; implement with R=1 (5^4 bases, 81 segments) and document that tiling should go through GenTileable2D's 4D path only at low resolution, or decline 4D. Estimated 2D cost ~25-40x Perlin (scalar proto 310x because it re-evaluated fbm 9 times per cell; the block-caching plan removes that).
ideas.continuity: C0: the surface is a max of continuous profile functions over a fixed set of segments, and the base is continuous. Verified c0ratio 7.99-8.01 in all modes. Seams are impossible as long as every segment whose influence reaches p is in the window, which holds because profile width w < 1 cell and segments are at most 1 cell long (sqrt(2)+2*jitter with jitter); keep max width + jitter below 1 cell or raise R.
ideas.params: Feature Scale (mixin), Jitter, Base Scale (coarse lattice ratio), Relief (base amplitude kept), Depth, Width (hybrid: lets a mask thin valleys regionally), Profile enum {V, U, Box}, Wall Width (box), Size Gain (how fast width grows downstream), Ridge bool, Knickpoint Chance, Fine Detail amplitude.
ideas.risks:
Straight 1-cell segments look artificial without an upstream warp (cheap to add, but a user must know). Many parallel chains run into the same sink when the base is very smooth; the base lattice ratio and jitter control this. Junctions are a plain max, so tributary mouths are abrupt (a smooth max fixes it). Cost in 3D/4D. Needs a measured output normalisation (ScaleOutput) since carve depth depends on params.
[CellularDrainage, cell-relations] With hash elevations the descent runs are short (a few cells), so trees look like short dendrites, not long rivers; long rivers need a smooth Elevation source, which multiplies source cost by the 5^D hash window. Width-by-elevation is only a proxy for flow accumulation (a true Strahler order is global). Only one outgoing edge per point: no braided channels.
ideas.variant_notes: Single-level steepest descent to the lowest neighbour. CellularDrainage contributes tapered widths, lightning bias and 3D tubes.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated 2D cost ~25-40x Perlin (scalar proto 310x because it re-evaluated fbm 9 times per cell; the block-caching plan removes that).

queue.reason: Steepest-descent forest with real tree topology (J3 top pick), but J2 read earlier sheets as starfish spokes and the 7x7 block costs ~40 ns. See it warped beside flow-network and fern-fold.

ideas.name: BentWalls
ideas.one_liner: Voronoi where each individual wall gets its own wobble (wavelength and phase hashed from the pair), with an envelope from F3 that makes ownership consistent at junctions.
ideas.algorithm: Track top 3 by squared distance with hash and position (F1=a, F2=b, F3=c). Order (a,b) canonically by comparing hashes to get (lo,hi); pair hash q=mix(h_a^h_b). Fixed-denominator signed wall: s0=(d_lo^2-d_hi^2)/2, positive on hi's side. Envelope e=smoothstep(0,E,d_c^2-d_b^2), which reaches 0 exactly where the identity of F2 changes. Bent wall: s=s0+A*e*sin(dot(k_q, x-m)+phi_q), where m is the pair midpoint and k_q, phi_q come from q. Owner = hi if s>0 else lo. Outputs: owner value, wall line profile(|s|/w), distance |s| clamped, or owner value times line. s is antisymmetric through the canonical order, so both sides agree on the wall.
ideas.look: Amoeba or jigsaw-like cells with hand-drawn walls, each wall bending differently: giraffe hide, mud plates, leaded glass, stone walling, biological tissue. Cell interiors and feature points are not distorted. Prototyped: rel_jigsaw shape=0.
ideas.why_new: Warped Cellular (see contact sheet) bends everything with one shared field, stretching cells and producing long coherent swirls. Per-wall bending keeps cell size and shape statistics and varies wall by wall, and it cannot be built with a domain warp because the displacement depends on the pair of cells.
ideas.simd_plan: Three-rank insertion via Select over (d2, hash, position) per window cell, one masked swap for canonical order, one Sin. 3^D window. No second pass. Estimate 2x CellularDistance (2D 8 ns, 3D 25 ns, 4D 80 ns). Scalar proto measured 5.5x worley2, but it used 5x5 and a naive insertion sort. Using dot(k_q, x-m) instead of an along-wall coordinate makes it dimension agnostic, though the proto used the 2D along-wall coordinate.
ideas.continuity: Line profile output is C0: c0ratio went from 1.03 with true-distance denominators to 7.99 with the fixed denominator, because the fixed form agrees where F2 changes. Owner mosaic is intentionally discontinuous, with an edge that matches the line.
ideas.params: Bend Amplitude (hybrid), Bend Frequency (hybrid), Junction Fade E (float), Line Width (hybrid), Grid Jitter (hybrid), Output enum.
ideas.risks: Fixed denominator makes wall width vary with feature spacing (mild). The nD wave-vector form is untested. A disc-shaped jigsaw tab variant was tried and looks like bubbles stuck on walls, not interlocking tabs, so it was dropped; a sine is the version worth keeping.
ideas.cost_note: Estimate 2x CellularDistance (2D 8 ns, 3D 25 ns, 4D 80 ns). Scalar proto measured 5.5x worley2, but it used 5x5 and a naive insertion sort.

ideas.name: BondGraph
ideas.one_liner: Random bonds between neighbouring jittered lattice points give a distance field to a real network with dead ends, gaps and per-edge width, height and beads.
ideas.algorithm:
Lattice: integer grid, one point per cell, P_c = c + 0.5 + 0.5*J*dir(hash_c) with J in [0,1) a CONSTANT (not hybrid). Margin m = 0.5*(1-J) is the distance every point keeps from its cell faces.

KEY LEMMA (makes it pointwise with a 3^D window): for adjacent cells c,c' (|c-c'|inf<=1) the segment P_c P_c' lies inside the union of cells within 1 of BOTH c and c' and is >= m away from every other cell. So a stroke of half-width w <= m around that segment can only touch samples whose window contains both endpoints. Output is clamped at Dmax = m, which makes the clamped min exact and seamless for any J.

Edge set per sample S in cell s (2D): for each of the 9 window cells c and each offset d in {+x, +y, +x+y, +x-y} with c+d also in the window: 6 horizontal + 6 vertical + 4 diagonal = 16 edges. Diagonal rule: each quad gets exactly one diagonal (bit of hash(c), or the shorter diagonal, or the Delaunay in-circle choice from idea CellularFacetMesh) so the graph is a planar triangulation. 3D: 13 half-offsets -> 54 axis + 36 face-diagonal + 8 body-diagonal edges; axis-only variant 54. 4D: axis-only 108 edges over 81 points.

Per edge e=(c,c'): he = Hash(min(c,c'), max(c,c')) (symmetric) -> present = (he & 0xff) < Density*255, widthMul = 0.5+rnd01(he>>8), bulge = Bulge*rnd11(he>>16).

out = Dmax
for each edge e:
  a = P_c - S, b = P_c' - S, ab = b - a
  t = clamp(-dot(a,ab)/dot(ab,ab), 0, 1)        // reciprocal, no branch
  d = |a + t*ab| - Width*widthMul                  // capsule
  Arc mode (sagitta sg = bulge*|ab|, need Width + |sg| <= m): chord mid M, unit normal n, R = (L^2/(8 sg) + sg/2), C = M - n*(R - sg); inSector = (cross(A-C,S-C) >= 0) & (cross(S-C,B-C) >= 0) (signs flipped by sign(sg)); d = Select(inSector, abs(|S-C| - R), min(|S-A|,|S-B|)) - Width*widthMul
  d = Select(present, d, Dmax)
  out = min(out, d)
Nodes: for each window point out = min(out, |P_c - S| - NodeRadius)  (covers junctions and stroke ends; NodeRadius <= m).
return ScaleOutput(out, -Width, Dmax)   (or profile: 1 - smoothstep(0, Dmax, out) for a 'line mask').

Correct 3D tubes: same code with 3-vectors; caves = threshold.

[BondNoise, lattice-kernels] Params: Width w (< 0.5), Density (hybrid, fraction of live edges), Kernel {Smooth, Hard}, Accumulate {Sum signed, Max}, Lattice {Square, Triangular(2D only)/Square(3D)}, Truchet (bool, 2D).
Gen(p): c = floor(p), f = p - c; acc = 0 (or -1)
 for axis k in 0..dim-1:
  for vk in {-1,0,1}: for each corner choice of the other dim-1 coords in {0,1}: (dim*3*2^(dim-1) edges: 12 / 36 / 96)
    v = c + offset; h = hash(seed, v) ^ (k * AxisPrime), remix
    d2 = Sum_{j!=k} (f_j - v_j)^2 + (clamp(f_k, v_k, v_k+1) - f_k)^2     // axis-aligned segment distance, no dots
    live = (h>>24) < Density*256; a = Sum ? rnd11(h>>8) : 1
    kern = Smooth ? max(0, 1 - d2/w^2)^2 : (d2 < w^2)
    acc = Sum ? acc + Select(live, a*kern, 0) : max(acc, Select(live, kern, 0))
 Truchet (2D): per cell, bit b = hash(c)&1 picks pairing; kern = max over the two quarter-circle arcs: arc centre = b ? (0,0),(1,1) : (1,0),(0,1), radius 0.5, d = | |f - centre| - 0.5 |; combine with Max.
 Triangular lattice: skew p (simplex skew), edges along e1, e2 and e1-e2 of the skewed grid; distance computed in world space via precomputed edge direction vectors (dot needed).
ideas.look:
Road maps, cracks with width, circuit traces, neurons, spider web fragments, mountain-range skeletons with peaks at nodes, strings of pearls. In 3D: connected worm tunnels and chambers when thresholded, the classic hard case of chunk-independent cave worms without a random walk. At Keep near 0.5 it behaves like a bond percolation pattern. Prototyped: rel_edges 2D only.
[BondNoise, lattice-kernels] Density 1 Sum: a smooth noise whose ridges run along straight lattice bonds (woven basket, textile). Density 0.3 Max Hard: mazes, PCB traces, rebar, irrigation ditches, broken drystone wall mortar; Smooth Max gives rounded wires with proper junctions. After DomainWarp the networks become root systems and vein networks that branch and END, unlike F2-F1 which always closes cells. 3D: volumetric scaffold / jungle-gym, sliced into dashes and dots.
[CellularMeshEdges, cell-relations] A wiry planar graph: straight (or gently curved) segments joining jittered points, 6-8 edges per vertex when all diagonals are on, becoming a 'street map' / circuit board / maze with dead ends when Density < 1. Arc mode gives hand-drawn rivers and roads with bends. In 3D: a tunnel system (caves) with guaranteed connectivity along lattice adjacency. Thresholded it is a crisp line drawing; as a distance field it drives width, bevels and erosion masks.
ideas.why_new: F2-F1 gives walls of cells: always closed, no dead ends, no per-edge attributes. This is the dual graph, connecting points rather than separating them, with a density control and open topology.
ideas.simd_plan: Same lattice loop as Cellular.inl (3x3 / 3x3x3 / 3x3x3x3 HashPrimesHB, jitter from hash bits), storing the 9/27/81 relative positions in std::array<float32v,N>. Then a fixed unrolled edge list (16 / 98 or 54 / 108) of capsule distances: ~14 ops each (sub, dot, rcp, clamp, fmadd, sqrt). Presence/width via Select from the symmetric pair hash (hash of the smaller primed cell coords XOR'd with the larger). Arc mode adds ~20 ops per edge. Cost estimate AVX2: 2D ~9 ns (2.5x CellularDistance, 8x Perlin); 3D axis-only ~35 ns (3x Cellular3D), full diagonals ~60 ns; 4D axis-only ~120 ns (3x Cellular4D). Generic GenT works for axis edges; diagonals need per-dimension offset tables.
ideas.continuity: C0: a min over a fixed set (fixed per S's window, and the lemma guarantees agreement between windows) of capsule / arc distances, each C0 in S; creases (not C1) on the medial axis between strokes.
ideas.params: Jitter (constant, 0..0.9), Width (hybrid, clamped to m), Density (hybrid, 0..1 = fraction of edges present), Diagonals enum {None, Hash, Shorter, Delaunay}, Bulge (hybrid, arc sagitta fraction), Node Radius, Width Jitter, Output enum {Distance, LineMask}, Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks:
Edges are 1D objects: any 2D slice of the 3D form or the 4D tileable form shows blobs, not lines, so GenTileable will not look like the 2D node. 3D caves are not prototyped. Straight segments look mechanical unless warped, but a domain warp upstream handles that without a dedicated feature.
[CellularMeshEdges, cell-relations] Jitter must stay < ~0.9 or m becomes tiny and Width is forced thin; the lattice shows through at low jitter (rows/columns of edges). Full-diagonal 3D is expensive. Arc mode: sagitta must obey Width+|sagitta| <= m or seams appear at window boundaries. Needs its own jitter semantics (cannot reuse the ring jitter 0.437 of Cellular at GridJitter=1, margin there is only 0.063).
ideas.variant_notes: Distance to hashed edges of the jittered lattice graph. Unjittered axis edges (BondNoise) need no dot products and let Density act as a bond percolation knob. Thin 3D lines slice to dots. LatticeGraph's BondNet rule is credited here.
ideas.cost_note: Cost estimate AVX2: 2D ~9 ns (2.5x CellularDistance, 8x Perlin); 3D axis-only ~35 ns (3x Cellular3D), full diagonals ~60 ns; 4D axis-only ~120 ns (3x Cellular4D).

ideas.name: BubblePack
ideas.one_liner: Non-overlapping multi-scale sphere packing evaluated pointwise, with no window at all, for foam, droplets, pumice vesicles and pebble mosaics.
ideas.algorithm: For level k in a fixed loop: P=Rot_k*x*f_k; C=floor(P); h=hash(C); r=rmin+(rmax-rmin)*r3 (rmax<=0.48); m=C+r+(1-2r)*(r1,r2), which keeps the disc inside its own cell. World centre cw=Rot_k^-1*(m/f_k); rw=r/f_k. For each ancestor a<k: Q=Rot_a*cw*f_a; ha=hash(floor(Q)); recover that cell's disc (ma,ra,on) with the same formula; if on, rw=min(rw,(|Q-ma|-ra)/f_a). Then rw=max(rw,0); d=|P-m|/f_k; cap=sqrt(max(rw^2-d^2,0)); H=max(H,cap*on_k). Because each disc is confined to its cell, only the sample's own cell can contain it, so no 3^D search is needed. Clearance is tested at the child's centre, so each bubble stays a true circle or sphere.
ideas.look: Clean domes at several scales: large bubbles with progressively smaller ones filling the gaps, with almost no overlap. The field reads as bubble raft, foam or droplets. A 3D threshold should give pumice or basalt vesicles and Swiss-cheese caves, though only the 2D form was prototyped.
ideas.why_new: Random non-overlapping packing normally needs dart throwing or a global pass, which FastNoise forbids. Size-jittered cellular cells overlap or collide, and Simplex blobs are not round. A graph of existing nodes cannot give the clearance test.
ideas.simd_plan: Loops are fixed and ancestor lookups are lane-wise since cw differs per lane. L levels need L(L+1)/2 hashes, independent of dimension: 15 hashes for 5 levels, estimated at 8-10 ns in any dimension (about 8x Perlin in 2D, 2.5x CellularDistance in 2D, under 1x in 3D, 0.25x in 4D). Use fixed per-level rotation matrices; output is analytic in [0, rmax/f0].
ideas.continuity: C0: cap reaches 0 at the rim, with infinite slope there because of the sqrt (an output mode using 1-d^2/rw^2 avoids that). Dense scanlines: 0 jumps. Own-cell and full 3x3 evaluation differ by mean 4e-7, max 0.006.
ideas.params: Levels (int), Level Scale, Radius Min/Max, Fill (hybrid), Output {Dome, Wall, Bubble Value}.
ideas.risks: Confinement to rotated square cells can leave a faint lattice in the largest level. Output is zero outside bubbles, so gaps stay flat unless more levels are added. A child can slightly overlap an ancestor from a neighbouring cell. Ancestor lookup makes high level counts grow quadratically.
ideas.cost_note: L levels need L(L+1)/2 hashes, independent of dimension: 15 hashes for 5 levels, estimated at 8-10 ns in any dimension (about 8x Perlin in 2D, 2.5x CellularDistance in 2D, under 1x in 3D, 0.25x in 4D).

queue.name: BubblePack
queue.reason: Non-overlapping multi-scale discs with no window at L(L+1)/2 hashes, ~8 ns in any dimension (J3, J4 top pick). Check the faint top-level lattice and overlap across cells.

disp.how: Shape Bubble; same own-cell kernel per the lobes critic

ideas.name: CellularCirclePacking
ideas.one_liner: Non-overlapping circle packing of widely varying radii: incircles of the jittered triangulation plus Apollonian-style corner circles filled in closed form, output as an SDF or per-circle id.
ideas.algorithm:
Reuse the 8 candidate triangles of CellularFacetMesh (all circles below lie strictly inside their triangle, so the stroke/clamp lemma holds with Dmax = m: circles in non-candidate triangles are >= m away from the sample's cell).
For each triangle (p0,p1,p2), edge lengths a=|p1-p2|, b=|p2-p0|, c=|p0-p1| (3 sqrt), s2 = a+b+c, twiceArea = |cross(p1-p0,p2-p0)|:
  r = twiceArea / s2 ; I = (a*p0 + b*p1 + c*p2)/s2       // incircle
  out = min(out, |S-I| - r)
  Depth >= 1, for each corner k with unit edge directions u,v from the corner:
     cosA = dot(u,v); sh = sqrt((1-cosA)*0.5)   // sin(alpha/2)
     q = (1-sh)/(1+sh); bis = normalize(u+v)
     rk = r*q ; Ik = p_k + bis*(rk/sh)             // circle tangent to both sides and the incircle
     out = min(out, |S-Ik| - rk)
     Depth 2: rk2 = rk*q ; Ik2 = p_k + bis*(rk2/sh) ; ... (geometric series toward the corner, fixed count)
Shrink: every radius times Gap (0..1) to leave mortar between circles.
Output enum: SDF (clamped at Dmax), Mask (step), Id (hash(T, k, level) of the circle whose SDF is the min; constant per circle).
3D: inspheres of the 48 tets (centre = sum A_i q_i / sum A_i, r = 3V / sum A_i) plus corner spheres (same formula with the solid-angle version is messy; stop at insphere + Gap in 3D).
ideas.look: Pebbles / bubble-wrap / fish-roe: circles of three or four size classes, each large circle hugged by smaller ones in the corners, never overlapping, with triangular gaps that shrink with depth. Completely unlike the Voronoi-based cell looks on the sheet; close to an Apollonian gasket texture or river pebbles.
ideas.why_new: Existing nodes can only give overlapping discs (F1 threshold) or polygons; a guaranteed non-overlapping multi-scale packing is otherwise a global algorithm (circle packing / Lloyd), here it is closed-form per triangle.
ideas.simd_plan: FacetMesh geometry (no barycentric needed, ~250 ops) + per triangle 3 sqrt, 1 rcp, incircle ~25 ops; per corner 1 sqrt, 1 rcp, ~25 ops per level. Depth 1: 8*(25 + 3*25) ~ 800 ops + sqrt's -> ~20 ns 2D (5x Cellular2D). Depth 2 ~ 30 ns. 3D insphere-only ~90 ns (dominated by tet enumeration). All fixed loops; min accumulation with Select for the Id output.
ideas.continuity: C0 (min of circle SDFs over a fixed set); Mask and Id discontinuous by design.
ideas.params: Jitter, Depth (int 0..3), Gap (hybrid), Output enum {SDF, Mask, Id}, Diagonal enum, Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks: Cost ~5x Cellular; 3D version loses the corner spheres; thin triangles give tiny incircles (use Delaunay diagonal choice and moderate jitter).
ideas.cost_note: Depth 1: 8*(25 + 3*25) ~ 800 ops + sqrt's -> ~20 ns 2D (5x Cellular2D). Depth 2 ~ 30 ns.

ideas.name: CellularCluster
ideas.one_liner: Neyman-Scott point process: each lattice parent spawns 0..M children within radius R that inherit the parent's value; Voronoi/F1/value over the clustered point set gives colonies of small cells inside large empty cells.
ideas.algorithm:
Window loop as Cellular.inl (coarse lattice, scale 1). Per parent c: hash -> parent position P_c (ring jitter), active child count n_c in 0..M (hash bits), child k (k = 0..M-1, M constant <= 4): offset = R * rnd01(hash(c,k))^Spread * dir(hash(c,k)); C_{c,k} = P_c + offset; active_k = k < n_c.
Point list per cell: parent (always, keeps every cell non-empty) + M children; distance d = |S - X| with inactive children forced to +inf by Select.
Run the standard F1..F4 / value chain over 9*(M+1) points.
Values: child value = parent value + Variation * rnd11(hash(c,k)); parent value = rnd11(hash(c)).
Outputs: all CellularDistance return types and CellularValue (Nth closest), plus 'ClusterId' (parent hash of the nearest point: colonies with jagged borders).
Consistency: children lie within R of the parent; clamp F1 at Dmax = 1 - R and the min over the window is exact. For walls/values, the in-window nearest point must be closer than 1 - R; with the parent always present and GridJitter <= 0.7 this holds except at extreme corners (same class of caveat as Cellular at full jitter).
3D: 27*(M+1) points; 4D: 81*(M+1).
ideas.look: Foam with mixed scales: clumps of 3-5 small cells (colonies) surrounded by big cells, F2-F1 walls dense inside clumps and sparse between, value output coloured per colony with small variations. Looks like lichen, cell cultures, bubbles that gathered, cobbles with gravel. Uniform-density Voronoi on the sheet cannot show density contrast.
ideas.why_new: Cell density is constant in every existing cellular node; jitter only moves points inside their cell. Clustering changes the point process, which is a different texture class (and gives parent-inherited values for free).
ideas.simd_plan: Same 3^D loop with an inner constant loop of M+1 points per cell: 9*(M+1) distance+Select chains. 2D M=2: 27 points ~ 3x Cellular2D (~12 ns); M=4: 45 points ~ 5x (~20 ns). 3D M=2: 81 points ~ 3x Cellular3D (~36 ns). 4D M=2: 243 points ~ 120 ns. Child hashes derived from the parent hash by a cheap xorshift/multiply per k (no extra lattice hashing).
ideas.continuity: Same as the chosen Cellular output (F1 C0, F2-F1 C0, values discontinuous).
ideas.params: Children M (int 0..4), Child Probability / Count Jitter, Radius R (hybrid, <= 0.5), Spread (radial distribution exponent), Variation (hybrid), Output enum (Cellular return types + ClusterId), Grid Jitter, Distance Function, Feature Scale.
ideas.risks: Cost multiplies by M+1; R near 0.5 makes Dmax small. Overlaps CellularHierarchy's ParentValue look (but with density variation instead of nesting).
ideas.cost_note: 2D M=2: 27 points ~ 3x Cellular2D (~12 ns); M=4: 45 points ~ 5x (~20 ns). 3D M=2: 81 points ~ 3x Cellular3D (~36 ns).

ideas.name: CellularCrease
ideas.one_liner: Worley cells whose crease (wall) depth is driven by the difference of a Region source sampled at the two cells' sites, giving hierarchical crack networks with real T-junctions (leather, dry mud, elephant skin, cobbles in flagstone groups, tectonic terraces) from a single Worley pass.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Region (HybridSource; constant => uniform crease), Base, Gain, Width W (hybrid, cell units <=0.5), Profile power P (hybrid), WallJitter, Lift, Mode {Crease, PlateauMinusCrease, RegionOfNearest}, ExactJunctions bool, jitter, distance function.

Window 3^d around the sample like CellularDistance. Pass 1: for each cell j compute site c_j, d_j = dist(p, c_j); keep d1 = min, nearest index n, c_n. Evaluate R_n = Region(c_n). Pass 2 (recompute sites and distances; cheaper than spilling 27 registers in 3D): for each j != n: R_j = Region(c_j) (3^d Source evals at the site positions, so they are per-point constants and never pop); D_jn = clamp(Base + Gain*|R_j - R_n| + WallJitter*rnd01(hash(min(h_j,h_n), max(h_j,h_n))), 0, 1) (symmetric by construction); t = (d_j - d1)/W; g = max(0, 1 - t)^P; h = max(h, D_jn * g).
Output: Crease: 1 - 2h. PlateauMinusCrease: Lift*R_n - 2h (stepped plateaus whose risers are cracks: terraces where the Region field is terraced). RegionOfNearest: R_n (flat per-cell value of the region field, for masks).

Why difference-of-region: with Region = Terrace(low-frequency noise) you get discrete parents, child walls lying on parent boundaries are deep, interior walls shallow, and the child walls meet the parent walls in T-junctions because the parent walls ARE child walls. With Region = smooth noise the depth is proportional to the local gradient across the wall (graded creases). With Region = Gradient along a direction the creases perpendicular to that direction open wider: anisotropic shrinkage cracks, bark fissures, stretched paint. With Region = coarse CellularValue you get true nested Voronoi (fibre bundles, flagstone groups).

ExactJunctions option: h = max over pairs (j,k) in the window of D_jk * g(|d_j - d_k|/W) * g2((min(d_j,d_k) - d1)/W). Every factor is continuous in p, so the output is strictly C0 at triple junctions where three different regions meet (the cheaper nearest-referenced form can jump by at most D_ab there). 36 pairs in 2D (cheap, no sqrt), 351 in 3D (offer only in 2D/extruded).
ideas.look: Polygonal cells separated by V or U creases whose depth varies in a structured way: wide deep cracks outline groups of cells, fine shallow creases subdivide them, ends meet in T-junctions, exactly like dried mud, old leather, elephant skin, crackle glaze or flagstone paving with sand joints. PlateauMinusCrease gives stepped mesas with fissures along the steps. Distinct from F2-F1 (uniform width, no hierarchy) and from STIT cuts (straight, no polygon cells).
ideas.why_new: CellularDistance gives one uniform crease; CellularValue gives flat cells. No graph can make a wall's depth depend on a property of the two cells it separates, and no existing node yields nested Voronoi with consistent T-junctions in one pass. The Region source makes one node cover leather, mud, bark, flagstone and terraced terrain.
ideas.simd_plan: Two passes over the standard 3^d window with masks, same structure as Cellular.inl; the second pass does 3^d Region evaluations at site positions (int32v seed unchanged, positions are the jittered sites). 2D/3D/4D generic over the pack. Cost: 2D about Worley 3.9 + 9x(Region) + 1 ns (Perlin Region: ~15 ns; constant Region: ~5 ns); 3D 12 + 27x(Region); 4D 41 + 81x(Region), expensive but it works and tiles. Keep W <= 0.5 so the 3x3 window is as exact as F2.
ideas.continuity: C0 in Crease mode away from triple junctions where three distinct regions meet (nearest-referenced form: bounded jump <= D_ab there, usually invisible); strictly C0 with ExactJunctions. PlateauMinusCrease is discontinuous at walls only by the amount Lift*(R_a - R_b), which is exactly the step you asked for; RegionOfNearest is piecewise constant.
ideas.params: Region (hybrid source, the heart of it), Base, Gain, Width (hybrid), Profile power (hybrid), WallJitter, Lift, Mode enum, ExactJunctions, Jitter, DistanceFunction (reuse CalcDistance).
ideas.risks: Window exactness identical to F2 (jitter <= 0.437, W <= 0.5). 3D with a noisy Region is 27 Source evals; recommend Region = cheap Value/Perlin or a constant. The proto must measure the junction jump of the cheap form before deciding whether ExactJunctions is needed in 2D by default.
ideas.cost_note: Cost: 2D about Worley 3.9 + 9x(Region) + 1 ns (Perlin Region: ~15 ns; constant Region: ~5 ns); 3D 12 + 27x(Region); 4D 41 + 81x(Region), expensive but it works and tiles.

ideas.name: CellularDensity
ideas.one_liner: Worley whose feature points survive with a probability given by a Density source sampled at the point's own position (not at the lane), with optional radius coupled to the same density, so clustered pits, rust pitting, barnacles, pebbles that gather in hollows and size-graded packings fall out of F1/F2/coverage with no popping.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Density (HybridSource, 0..1), SizeFromDensity, BaseRadius, WindowRadius int {1,2}, MaxDistance (plateau), Mode {F1, F2MinusF1, Coverage, NearestValue}, Jitter, DistanceFunction.
Window (2 WindowRadius+1)^d. For each cell j: site c_j, hash h_j, keep_j = rnd01(h_j) < Density(c_j) (Density evaluated at the site, 3^d or 5^d evals; constant hybrid makes it a plain Worley), radius r_j = BaseRadius*(1 + SizeFromDensity*(Density(c_j) - 0.5)); d_j = dist(p, c_j)/r_j; d_j = Select(keep_j, d_j, Large). F1 = min d_j, F2 second min (same insertion as Cellular.inl).
Outputs: F1: min(F1, MaxDistance) scaled (the plateau where no point survives is flat and continuous); F2MinusF1 (cells only among survivors, large empty cells); Coverage = 1 - smoothstep(1-Edge, 1, F1) (dots/pebbles mask); NearestValue = rnd11(h_nearest) with the plateau mapped to a background value.
Recursion: feeding Coverage of a coarse CellularDensity as the Density of a finer one (through 1 - value) gives size-sorted packing: small stones only where there is no large stone; feeding the Coverage of coarse sparse points as Density gives Matern cluster processes (clumps).
ideas.look: Patchy point fields: dense clusters of pits fading into clean metal (rust pitting), barnacles crowding one side of a rock, pebbles collecting in hollows of a terrain used as Density, galaxies of clustered specks, and when recursed, cobbles with gravel filling only the gaps. CellularDistance can only jitter a uniform field; the sheet has no clustered or graded point fields.
ideas.why_new: Density-dependent presence cannot be built with a graph (masking the output of CellularDistance by a density field cuts cells in half and keeps the empty-region F1 structure); it needs the decision made per point at the point's position. This also corrects the earlier mat_inv ThinSpots sketch, which thresholds against a density sampled at the lane and therefore lets spots appear and vanish as the sample moves.
ideas.simd_plan: Cellular.inl window loop plus one Source eval per cell at the site position and one Select; 2D cost Worley 3.9 + 9x(Density); 3D 12 + 27x; 4D 41 + 81x (works, tiles, expensive). WindowRadius 2 (25/125 cells) for sparse fields where the plateau would otherwise clip inside visible cells.
ideas.continuity: C0: presence and radius are per-point constants, F1 is a min of continuous functions, the plateau is a min with a constant. F2MinusF1 is C0 as in CellularDistance. NearestValue is piecewise constant by design.
ideas.params: Density (hybrid source), SizeFromDensity, BaseRadius, WindowRadius int, MaxDistance, Edge, Mode enum, Jitter, DistanceFunction.
ideas.risks: Low density plus WindowRadius 1 produces large flat plateaus (intended, but users need the warning); with SizeFromDensity large, points near the window edge can reach the sample (bound r <= 1 cell). Overlaps in concept with StampField(sum/max) fed by a density; the difference is the F1/F2 metric outputs and the fractal-friendly plateau.
ideas.cost_note: CellularDistance plus one Density eval per cell at the site: 3.9 + 9x Density ns in 2D, 12 + 27x in 3D, 41 + 81x in 4D.

ideas.name: CellularDualMesh
ideas.one_liner: Explicit polygon tiling (centroid dual of the jittered triangulation) where every wall is a real segment with its own hash: per-wall thickness, removal (mazes), and flat per-polygon fill, all C0.
ideas.algorithm:
Reuse CellularFacetMesh: the 8 candidate triangles T around S (corners within the 3x3 window). For each T compute centroid G_T and the 3 edge midpoints M_ab. The dual cell of a vertex v is the union over its incident triangles of the kite (v, M_va, G_T, M_vb); its walls are the half-segments G_T - M_ab. Every half-segment lies inside its triangle, so the stroke lemma of CellularMeshEdges applies: strokes of half-width w <= m only touch samples whose window holds the triangle; clamp the output at Dmax = m.

Per primal edge ab (unordered pair of lattice cells): he = Hash(min,max) -> present (Density), thickness mul, optional 'height'.
out = Dmax
for each of 8 triangles T, for each of its 3 edges ab:
   d = dist(S, segment(G_T, M_ab)) - Width*thick_ab
   out = min(out, Select(present_ab, d, Dmax))
return ScaleOutput(out, -Width, Dmax)   // or LineMask profile

RegionValue output: inside the containing triangle, owner = argmax lambda_i (that is exactly the centroid-dual partition); value = rnd11(hash(owner cell)) -> flat fill per polygon. Merged regions for maze-like use: when a wall is absent the two polygons are different colours but no stroke separates them (use the stroke output for walls).
Cheap wall output without strokes (used in 3D): W = lambda_max - lambda_second, C0 across triangles since all lambdas are continuous; per-wall width is NOT applied there (see risks).

3D: tets from CellularFacetMesh; walls become polygons around primal edges; use the lambda formulation (W = lambda_max - lambda_second, uniform width) and RegionValue; stroke-based per-wall attributes only in 2D.
ideas.look: An irregular polygon tiling resembling Voronoi but with walls kinked at edge midpoints, like hand-cut crazy paving or stone walls. Varying mortar thickness per joint, missing joints that merge stones, and uniform-width walls that F2-F1 cannot give. Density ~0.5 yields organic mazes and 'cracked plate where cracks stop' patterns.
ideas.why_new: The Voronoi dual in FastNoise has no addressable walls: a wall is only the locus F1=F2 and its width varies with angle, and removing walls is discontinuous (shown in notes). Here each wall is a segment with a hash, so width, presence and style are per-wall and continuous.
ideas.simd_plan: FacetMesh point location (~300 ops) plus 24 capsule distances (~14 ops each) and 16 symmetric pair hashes: ~700 ops total -> ~15 ns 2D (4x Cellular2D). 3D: tet location (~3000 ops) + lambda wall: ~85 ns. Everything is Select-driven; the half-segment list is a compile-time table.
ideas.continuity: 2D stroke outputs C0 (min of fixed capsule set). BaryWall C0. RegionValue discontinuous (flat fill).
ideas.params: Jitter, Width (hybrid, <= m), Density (hybrid), Width Jitter, Output enum {WallDistance, LineMask, RegionValue, BaryWall}, Diagonal enum, Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks: Not a true Voronoi (walls are centroid-to-midpoint), which some users may not want; 3D loses per-wall attributes; cost is ~4x Cellular in 2D.
ideas.cost_note: FacetMesh point location (~300 ops) plus 24 capsule distances (~14 ops each) and 16 symmetric pair hashes: ~700 ops total -> ~15 ns 2D (4x Cellular2D).

ideas.name: CellularEdgeDistance
ideas.one_liner: Exact distance to the nearest Voronoi cell border (iq's two-pass method) plus bevel/plateau outputs; replaces the incorrect F2-F1 crackle.
ideas.algorithm:
Pass 1 (3^d window, identical to CellularDistance F1): find nearest point: mr = r_nearest (vector sample->point), mg = its cell.
Pass 2 (window centred on mg, 5^d exact, or 3^d approx): for each cell g in window:
  r = (g + jitter(hash(mg+g)) - frac(p))      // vector to that cell's point
  diff = r - mr ; same = dot(diff,diff) < 1e-8 (mask)
  dEdge_candidate = dot(0.5*(mr + r), diff * InvSqrt(dot(diff,diff)))   // distance from p to the perpendicular bisector of mr and r
  dEdge = min(dEdge, Select(same, BIG, dEdge_candidate))
Output enum:
  EdgeDistance : dEdge (0 on borders, grows into the cell; C0 with creases on the medial axis)
  Bevel        : min(dEdge, BevelWidth)/BevelWidth (flat plateau cells with chamfered rims -> paving stones, dried mud plates)
  EdgeMask     : smoothstep(EdgeWidth, 0, dEdge) (crack lines of uniform width, unlike F2-F1 whose width varies with cell spacing)
  InscribedRadius: half the distance from the nearest point to its nearest neighbour (Blender's n-sphere radius) = min over pass 2 of 0.5*|diff|.
Distance metric for the bisector is Euclidean; a Manhattan/Chebyshev option is not exact, omit.
ideas.look:
Prototype cl_cell mode 1 and 8: same polygon layout as F2-F1, but isolines are exact insets, so thresholds give even grout widths, and hillshade shows flat planar facets meeting at a straight skeleton like cut gems or hip roofs. Clean cracks, tiles, cobblestones, low-poly massifs.
[CellularEdge, dcc-tools] EdgeDistance: pyramids with truly constant-width dark borders, unlike F2-F1 on the sheet whose lines vary. Cobble: flagstone or stained glass with height per stone and rounded bevel. PackedDome: non-overlapping tangent bubbles and pebbles. Prototype: dcc_lens mode=12.
ideas.why_new: F2-F1 is 'pretty close' but wrong near cell corners and its line width depends on neighbour spacing; the exact border distance cannot be built from existing F-values because F2 changes discontinuously inside a cell. Needed for tiles, mud cracks, cracked ice, cobbles, Voronoi plateaus.
ideas.simd_plan: Two full 3^dim passes = 18/54/162 hashes, est 8 / 24 / 82 ns (2x CellularDistance). Euclidean only since bisectors are planar only then. Audit in 2D vs 7x7 brute force, 640k samples: FastNoise-style ring jitter, 3x3 second pass: radius 0.30 and below 0 wrong; 0.35 0.02% wrong (max err 0.05); 0.437 (kJitter2D) 0.96% wrong (max err 0.19). 5x5 second pass: 0 wrong even at full-cell jitter. So: 2D use 5x5 second pass (34 hashes, about 14 ns) or cap ring at 0.30; 3D/4D cap jitter.
ideas.continuity: EdgeDistance C0 with slope 1 (Lipschitz) when the window is sufficient; measured c0ratio 8.0 with square jitter <=0.7, and 1.1-1.8 at larger jitter due to missed neighbours. 3D at kJitter3D 0.396 ring with 3x3x3: 8.0 on one z slice, 6.48 on another, so nearly exact but not proven. CellRadius is cell-wise constant, discontinuous at borders. PackedDome is C0 because the disc fits inside the cell.
ideas.params: Feature Scale, Jitter Modifier, Second Pass Window enum {3 (fast), 5 (exact)}, Output enum {EdgeDistance, Bevel, EdgeMask, InscribedRadius}, Bevel Width / Edge Width (hybrid), Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks:
Jitter cap makes cells more regular than default CellularDistance, or 2D costs 3.5x. Size Jitter and non-Euclidean metrics cannot be supported. Sibling lens has related edge work; this entry adds the window audit numbers.
[CellularEdgeDistance, shader-community] 5^d second pass cost in 3D/4D; 3^d second pass gives rare wrong borders at high jitter. Size-jitter (grid jitter per cell) of the existing node is incompatible with exact bisectors; keep plain point jitter only.
sources: Inigo Quilez, 'Voronoi - distances' (2012), https://iquilezles.org/articles/voronoilines/ (cited from memory, not fetched in this task)
ideas.variant_notes: Could ship as new CellularDistance return types instead of a node. 3x3 second-pass audit numbers are in simd_plan: exact up to ring jitter 0.30, about 1% wrong at the default 0.437; 5x5 is exact at any jitter in 2D.
ideas.cost_note: Two full 3^dim passes = 18/54/162 hashes, est 8 / 24 / 82 ns (2x CellularDistance). So: 2D use 5x5 second pass (34 hashes, about 14 ns) or cap ring at 0.30; 3D/4D cap jitter.

ideas.name: CellularFacetMesh
ideas.one_liner: Locate the sample in a jittered-grid triangulation (locally Delaunay diagonals) and output barycentric interpolation, flat facets, random planes or a tent per triangle: a low-poly / faceted surface evaluated pointwise.
ideas.algorithm:
Lattice and jitter as in CellularMeshEdges (J < 1, margin m). Quads Q(c) with corners A=P_c, B=P_{c+x}, C=P_{c+y}, D=P_{c+x+y}. Because the jittered grid graph stays planar for J<1, the quads tile the plane, and for S in cell s the containing quad has c in {s-1,s}^2 (proof: Q(c) is inside [c+m, c+2-m]^2), so only 4 quads = 8 triangles, all 9 corners in the 3x3 window.

Diagonal per quad (depends only on the 4 corners, so every sample agrees):
  adValid = cross(D-A,B-A)*cross(D-A,C-A) < 0 ;  bcValid = cross(C-B,A-B)*cross(C-B,D-B) < 0   (non-convex quad: only the diagonal through the reflex corner is valid)
  both valid: useAD = inCircle(A,B,C; D) <= 0 (3x3 determinant of relative coords, Delaunay) or a hash bit (Mode=Random)
  tris = useAD ? {ABD, ADC} : {ABC, BCD} (via Select on the corner positions, no branch)

Point location for each of the 8 triangles (p0,p1,p2) CCW:
  e0 = cross(p1-p0, S-p0); e1 = cross(p2-p1, S-p1); e2 = cross(p0-p2, S-p2)
  inside = (e0>=0)&(e1>=0)&(e2>=0); area = e0+e1+e2; lambda = (e1, e2, e0)/area
  result = Select(inside, value(T), result)   (exactly one triangle hits; on a shared edge both give the same value)

value(T) by Output enum:
  Lerp:   l0*v0 + l1*v1 + l2*v2, v_i = rnd11(hash of corner cell)  (C0 piecewise-linear 'jittered linear value noise')
  LerpSource: v_i = Source(P_i): mask-select the 3 corner positions first, then 3 source evaluations total
  Flat:   rnd11(hash(c, triIndex))  -> low-poly flat facets
  Plane:  h_T + Slope*dot(g_T, S - centroid_T), g_T random dir from table -> tilted facets (hillshade shows crystal planes)
  Tent:   3*min(l0,l1,l2) -> pyramid on every triangle, C0
  Packing: see CellularCirclePacking

3D: hexahedra H(c), c in {s-1,s}^3 (8 of them), Kuhn/Freudenthal 6-tet split along the main diagonal (consistent across shared faces because every hex uses the same global pattern). Per tet (q0..q3): 4 signed volumes via triple products give lambda and inside. 48 tet tests. Jitter clamped to <= 0.3 so no tet inverts (to verify in the prototype).
4D: 16 hypercubes x 24 simplices is too costly; propose 4D at jitter 0 located by coordinate sorting (like 4D simplex) so GenTileable2D still tiles, with a warning that 4D facets are lattice-regular.
ideas.look:
True low-poly terrain with straight creases (stylised game terrain), triangle mosaics, triangular crack webs, faceted hills. Lookup mode turns any FBm graph into a low-poly world. Prototyped: rel_tri modes 0-4, using an 18-triangle search rather than the fan.
[CellularFacetMesh, cell-relations] Low-poly terrain: flat triangular facets with straight creases (Lerp), shattered flat shards (Flat/Plane) or a field of irregular pyramids (Tent). Hillshaded it looks like folded paper or crystal faces, nothing on the sheet has straight creases. LerpSource turns any node into its piecewise-linear 'mesh-decimated' version.
ideas.why_new: CellularLookup evaluates its source per window cell and gives flat Voronoi tiles, so nothing yields C0 linear interpolation over irregular triangles. Evaluating the source only at the lane-specific n+1 vertices makes it much cheaper than a CellularLookup window.
ideas.simd_plan:
2D: 7 hashes, 6 barycentric solves sharing P_n, Select chain: about 2-3x Perlin. 3D: 15 vertices and 24 tetra around a vertex with Cramer solves: about 2x CellularDistance. 4D: the fan has 120 simplices, which is too costly, so use unjittered Kuhn simplex (sort coordinates like Simplex, 5 values) and accept regular creases in tiled output. Lookup adds n+1 source calls.
[CellularFacetMesh, cell-relations] Window loop as Cellular.inl for 9 / 27 points. Diagonal tests: 4 quads x ~25 ops (crosses + in-circle determinant). Triangles: 8 x (3 crosses, 3 compares, 1 rcp, Select accumulation) ~ 20 ops. Total ~300 ops: ~7 ns 2D (2x Cellular2D, 6x Perlin). 3D: 48 tets x ~60 ops ~ 3000 ops: ~80 ns (6-7x Cellular3D). An alternating 5-tet split (40 tets, all faces share the same diagonal choice via parity) trims ~20%. 4D as stated (regular Kuhn, ~2x 4D simplex cost).
ideas.continuity: C0 by construction (shared edges interpolate shared vertices). check: c0ratio 8.00 with max slope 4.35. The flat-id mode is discontinuous. Mode min/max also C0.
ideas.params: Jitter (constant; 2D <0.9, 3D <=0.3), Diagonal enum {Delaunay, Shorter, Random}, Output enum {Lerp, LerpSource, Flat, Plane, Tent, Packing}, Slope (hybrid, Plane mode), Source (GeneratorSource for LerpSource), Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks:
3D is expensive and the no-inversion jitter bound must be measured; 4D story is weak (regular lattice). Quad diagonals at low jitter show the grid. Thin triangles at high jitter give long sliver facets (Delaunay diagonal choice limits this).
[TriFacet, cell-relations] The 0.23 jitter bound keeps a faint triangular lattice bias, and the proto used a larger 0.28 with search, so the look at 0.23 needs confirming. Only the 2D form has been prototyped; 3D fan code is nontrivial. The 4D fallback has a different look when tiling. Hash ties with a square lattice plus in-circle diagonal choice are an alternative that gives more Delaunay-like triangles.
ideas.variant_notes: Two point locations: nearest vertex fan with bounded jitter 0.23 (TriFacet), or 2x2 quads with Delaunay diagonals (FacetMesh, up to 0.9). LerpSource gives low-poly of any node at n+1 evals.
ideas.cost_note: 2D: 7 hashes, 6 barycentric solves sharing P_n, Select chain: about 2-3x Perlin. 3D: 15 vertices and 24 tetra around a vertex with Cramer solves: about 2x CellularDistance.

ideas.name: CellularFracture
ideas.one_liner: Exact distance to Voronoi walls (uniform width) combined with per-cell radial cracks that stop at the walls, per-wall width from a symmetric pair hash, plus 'order-2 / order-3 Voronoi' region ids (each cell shattered into convex sectors by which neighbour is second closest).
ideas.algorithm:
Pass 1 (Cellular loop): F1 point P1 with v1 = S - P1, F2, F3 hashes and distances.
Pass 2 over the same window (positions kept in an array):
  for each j != F1: n = P_j - P1; wall_j = (dot(v1, n) - 0.5*dot(n,n)) * InvSqrt(dot(n,n))   // signed distance from S to the bisector, true distance to that wall
  t_j = WidthMul(Hash(min(h1,hj), max(h1,hj)))  // symmetric pair hash, 0.5..1.5
  W = min_j wall_j / t_j
  (continuity argument: at the wall between a and b the term for the other cell is 0 on both sides, so min is 0 from both sides; inside a cell all terms are continuous)
Radial cracks: K unit directions u_{c,k} from a table indexed by hash bits of the F1 cell, k = 0..K-1 (K constant):
  tk = max(0, dot(v1, u_k)); ray_k = |v1 - tk*u_k| ; ray_k = Select(tk > RayLen, |v1| - ..., ray_k) (optional finite length)
  C = min(W, min_k ray_k / RayWidthMul)  (C0: at a wall W = 0 dominates on both sides)
Outputs: WallDistance = W (clamped at Dmax), Cracks = C, Order2Value = rnd11(SymHash(h1,h2)), Order3Value = rnd11(SymHash3(h1,h2,h3)), SectorValue = rnd11(hash(h1, sector)) with sector = bitmask of sign(cross(u_k, v1)) over K directions.
3D: identical formulas with 3-vectors; radial cracks become rays (use 'crack planes' through P1 with random normal: |dot(v1, n_k)| for planar fracture faces).
ideas.look: Shattered glass / cracked ice: uniform-width Voronoi walls (F2-F1 walls thin out where walls meet at acute angles; these do not) with extra straight cracks radiating from each cell centre and terminating exactly at the walls. Order-2 value shows every cell split into kite-shaped pie pieces facing each neighbour, a 'mosaic within mosaic' that no existing value mode produces.
ideas.why_new: Exact wall distance is a known shader trick (IQ) missing from FastNoise; the radial cracks are continuous only because of the min-with-wall argument; order-k region ids cost nothing beyond the hashes already computed yet give a genuinely new partition.
ideas.simd_plan: Two passes over the 3x3 / 3x3x3 window: first the normal Cellular F1..F3 search (store relative positions and hashes in arrays), second pass computing wall_j (dot, fnmadd, rsqrt, mul: ~8 ops) and pair hash (~6 ops) per point; rays K x ~8 ops. 2D ~8 ns (2x Cellular2D), 3D ~25 ns, 4D ~80 ns. Fully branch-free; the min/Select chain replaces per-lane early-out.
ideas.continuity: WallDistance and Cracks: C0 (proof in algorithm). Order/Sector values: discontinuous flat fills.
ideas.params: Output enum {WallDistance, Cracks, Order2Value, Order3Value, SectorValue}, Crack Count K (int 0..6), Ray Width (hybrid), Wall Width Jitter, Crack Length, Grid Jitter (hybrid), Distance Function (for F ordering only), Feature Scale.
ideas.risks: Per-wall width must be symmetric and finite; removing walls entirely is discontinuous in this dual formulation (use CellularDualMesh for mazes). Radial crack directions are per cell, so cracks on opposite sides of a wall do not line up (looks fine for glass, wrong for continuous fractures).
ideas.cost_note: 2D ~8 ns (2x Cellular2D), 3D ~25 ns, 4D ~80 ns.

ideas.name: CellularGeodesic
ideas.one_liner: Cellular distance where each candidate's distance is its straight-line length weighted by a cost source integrated along the segment: territories whose borders bend around mountains.
ideas.algorithm:
Same 3^d window, jittered feature points q_j and hash as CellularDistance. Cost C(x) = 1 + CostScale*max(0, S(x)) (or 1 + CostScale*(S+1)/2), S a GeneratorSource.
  for each candidate j (fixed 3^d loop):
      v = q_j - p ; L = |v|
      c = 0 ; for m in 1..M: c += C(p + ((m-0.5)/M)*v)     // M = 2..4 midpoints, fixed
      D_j = L * c / M
      maintain F1, F2 and the winning cell's hash via masked min (as Cellular.inl does)
  Output enum: F1, F2, F2-F1, CellValue (hash of winner), CellIndex, Ratio.
ideas.look: Voronoi cells that shrink in high-cost regions and swell in low-cost ones; borders are curved, asymmetric and bow away from ridges, so a CellValue map reads as political/biome territories that respect the terrain or follow rivers (cost = ridged noise). F2-F1 cracks become denser in costly regions. Distinct from warped cellular, which bends but never redistributes territory.
