ideas.why_new: Anisotropic/weighted metrics are impossible by warping (a warp cannot make one cell take land on the far side of a ridge). The midpoint cost integral is the pointwise trick that approximates geodesic distance with a fixed number of source evaluations; gives a 'borders that mean something' map that is otherwise a global shortest-path computation.
ideas.simd_plan: Reuse Cellular.inl window loop; inner fixed M loop adds M source evals per candidate; everything masked-min. Cost ~ 3^d x M x S + cellular: 2D M=3 Perlin cost: 27 Perlin = ~33 ns (~8x CellularDistance 2D); 3D 81 Perlin3D = ~190 ns; 4D 243 Perlin4D ~ 1 us (4D only with a Value-noise cost or M=1). Window correctness same class as existing jitter caveats; keep CostScale <= ~1 to limit out-of-window winners.
ideas.continuity: C0 like Worley (min of continuous functions); CellValue piecewise constant by design.
ideas.params: Cost Source (GeneratorSource), Cost Scale hybrid, Samples M int, Jitter hybrid, Distance Function enum, Return Type enum (F1/F2/F2-F1/Value/Index), Seeded, ScalableGenerator.
ideas.risks: Expensive in 3D/4D; large CostScale lets far points win and the 3^d window then seams; straight-line integral is only an approximation of geodesic distance (fine for smooth cost at cell scale).
ideas.cost_note: Cost ~ 3^d x M x S + cellular: 2D M=3 Perlin cost: 27 Perlin = ~33 ns (~8x CellularDistance 2D); 3D 81 Perlin3D = ~190 ns; 4D 243 Perlin4D ~ 1 us (4D only with a Value-noise cost or M=1).

ideas.name: CellularHexLattice
ideas.one_liner: Cellular on A_d* lattices (hex, BCC, A4*): honeycomb, basalt columns and Kelvin foam at low jitter, with fewer candidates than the cubic window in 3D and 4D.
ideas.algorithm:
2D: axial coords q=x-y/sqrt3, r=2y/sqrt3; cube-round to nearest lattice point (branch free via Select on largest rounding error); candidates = self + 6 neighbours (Voronoi-relevant vectors). Site = lattice point + jitter in a disc of radius j. Worst-case bound j<=(|2nd shell|-2Rc)/2 = .289 at spacing 1.
3D BCC: two offset cubic lattices; pick nearer of Round(x) and Round(x-.5)+.5; candidates = self + 8 at (+-.5,+-.5,+-.5) + 6 axis = 15; j<=.148 at cube size 1 (~.186 at unit density).
4D A4*: nearest point by the Conway-Sloane rank method, a sorting network in masks; 30 relevant vectors plus self = 31 (permutohedron has 2^(d+1)-2 facets).
Then usual F1 and value logic. Edge distance works with the same candidates.

[CentredLattice (BCC/D4 cellular and kernel windows), lattice-kernels] Lattice = union of Z^dim and Z^dim + (1/2,...,1/2) (scaled so nearest-neighbour distance is 1: in 3D this is BCC, in 4D D4* (a lattice whose Voronoi cell is the 24-cell), in 2D the centred square, which is just a rotated square, so 2D uses offset rows instead: point (i,j) at (i + 0.5*(j&1), j*sqrt(3)/2), window i-1..i+1, j-1..j+1 = 9 points but hexagonal cells).
3D/4D Gen(p): for sublattice s in {0,1}: ps = p - 0.5*s; c = floor(ps); for each of the 2^dim corners o: q = c + o + 0.5*s + Jitter*(rndvec(hash(seed, c+o, s))-0.5)*JitterScale; evaluate the candidate (distance for cellular, kernel for StrokeNoise/Multipole/Pebble...).
Jitter bound: with Jitter <= 0.5 (in sublattice cell units) every point whose unjittered Voronoi cell could contain p is one of the 2^dim corners of its sublattice cube, so F1 is exact; above that the same rare-seam tolerance as today's jitter 1 applies.
Hash includes the sublattice bit (seed ^ s*PrimeW or an extra prime) so the two sublattices are independent.
ideas.look: Prototype cl_cell modes 7, 8. j=0: perfect honeycomb and hex tile; j=.15: basalt column tops, irregular hex; j=.29: organic polygons but much more even in size than the jittered square grid. Hillshade with exact edge distance gives crystal-pyramid hexes. BCC slices would show Kelvin-cell (truncated octahedron) foam.
ideas.why_new: Low jitter square-lattice Cellular exposes a square grid, so the regular-but-organic foam look is unavailable. A domain shear in a graph distorts the distance metric. The survey cites more densely packed lattices (Wyvill & Novins) as reducing directional artifacts. Worley explicitly warned that jittered lattices leave odd patterns.
ideas.simd_plan:
2D: 7 cells + cube round ~3.5 ns vs 3.9. 3D: 15 cells ~7 ns vs 12. 4D: 31 cells + sort ~16 ns vs 41, a 2.5x saving and the best way to cheap tiling cells. Candidates are a fixed constant table of offsets, so loop count is constant.
[CentredLattice (BCC/D4 cellular and kernel windows), lattice-kernels] Two sublattice passes of 2^dim corners: the existing per-candidate code is reused; window loops change from 3^dim to 2 x 2^dim. 2D offset-row form needs (j&1) parity via an integer AND and a per-row x shift. Branch-free. Cost 2D ~same as today (9 candidates), 3D ~0.6x, 4D ~0.4x of current Cellular.
ideas.continuity: F1 C0 (c0ratio 8.00), edge distance C0 (8.00). Jitter is bounded for correctness; the 2D prototype used a box of +-.289 (corner radius .41 exceeds the disc bound), with no visible seams, but a disc or box of +-.2 is the safe spec.
ideas.params: Hybrid: Grid Jitter (clamped to the bound). Enum: same return types and distance functions as CellularDistance. Could be a Lattice enum on Cellular<>.
ideas.risks:
Cost saving exists only at low jitter; matching full-random look needs the second shell (13 in 2D, 27 in 3D), no gain. The bound looks unintuitive to users (scaled 0-1 jitter hides that). Only the 2D form was prototyped, and the 3D, 4D bounds are hand derivations. Non-Euclid metrics break the shell argument. F2 needs more shells.
[CentredLattice (BCC/D4 cellular and kernel windows), lattice-kernels] Jitter above 0.5 reintroduces seams more readily than the 3^dim square window; the lab must brute-force-check F1 exactness vs jitter. 2D offset-row hex has a different jitter geometry from 3D BCC (two code paths). Many users will see 'hex worley' as known; the value is speed in 3D/4D plus foam shapes.
merged_from: #163 CentredLattice (BCC/D4 cellular and kernel windows) (lattice-kernels, fable)
ideas.variant_notes: Could be a Lattice enum on existing Cellular nodes. Candidates: 7/15/31 at low jitter via Voronoi-relevant vectors, or the two-sublattice 8/16/32 form. Hand-derived jitter bounds need a brute-force check.
ideas.cost_note: 2D: 7 cells + cube round ~3.5 ns vs 3.9. 4D: 31 cells + sort ~16 ns vs 41, a 2.5x saving and the best way to cheap tiling cells.

queue.name: CellularHexLattice
queue.reason: Honeycomb, BCC and A4* candidate tables save up to 2.5x in 4D at low jitter (J4 top pick). Hex 2D alone justifies a Lattice enum.

ideas.name: CellularHierarchy
ideas.one_liner: Fine cells inherit from coarse cells through a deterministic parent chain (nearest coarse point in a 2^D block), giving nested tessellations: thick walls between countries, thin between provinces, jagged parent borders, lineage values, N levels.
ideas.algorithm:
Level 0: the normal fine Cellular window (scale 1). Level l has scale k^l (k = Ratio, e.g. 3) with its own jittered lattice.
Parent lookup for a point P at level l -> level l+1: cells q in floor(P/k^{l+1} - 0.5) + {0,1}^D (the 2^D coarse cells whose centres are nearest to P); parent = argmin |P - Q_q| over those 2^D coarse points; returns (position, hash). Because it depends only on P, every sample computes the same parent for the same fine point: window-consistent by construction. (It is 'approximately Voronoi': true coarse Voronoi would need the 3^D block; offer Exact flag.)
For each of the 3^D fine window points compute the chain of ancestors up to Levels (fixed loop), storing hashes.
Outputs:
  LineageValue: sum_l Amp^l * rnd11(hash_l(F1)) -> clustered colours (provinces vary around their country's value)
  AncestorValue(L): rnd11(hash_L(F1)) -> coarse regions whose borders follow fine cell walls (jagged polygon coastlines)
  AncestorLookup: Source sampled at the level-L ancestor position of F1 (CellularLookup with jagged borders)
  Walls: divergence level div(F1,j) = first level where ancestors of F1 and j differ (0 if different parents at level 1, up to Levels); mult(div) from a per-level Width table; W = min_{j != F1} (d_j - d_1) * mult(div(F1,j))  (or exact wall distance from CellularFracture). Continuous by the min argument: the term for the cell across any wall is 0 on both sides.
3D/4D: identical with 2^D = 8/16 coarse candidates per fine point.

[Provinces, cell-relations] For each window cell c: P1(c)=floor((c+hop)/B1) with hop=round(Hop*rnd(h_c)) per axis (plus an optional low-frequency sin wobble of c), P2(c)=P1(c)>>log2(B2). Pass 1: F1 owner o. Pass 2: for j != o: rank = 2 if P2 differs, 1 if P1 differs, else 0; wd=(d_j^2-d_o^2)/2 (constant denominator); line=max(line, depth[rank]*profile(wd/width[rank])); coast=min(coast, wd where rank>=1). Outputs: border lines with thickness by rank, cluster value (v2*a+v1*b+v0*c from hashes of P2, P1, own), value with borders, distance to the nearest province border (coast).
ideas.look:
A political map: large irregular countries with thick borders subdivided into provinces with thin borders, borders of the big regions made of small-cell polygon edges (jagged, not Voronoi-straight). As a crack field: dry mud with primary cracks and secondary cracks inside each plate; giraffe / tortoise-shell patterns. With 3-4 levels it is a fractal Voronoi where every level nests inside the previous.
[Provinces, cell-relations] Political map or geological map: jagged, polygon-stepped borders at 2-3 scales, blocks of related cell values, thin internal cell lines optional. Also patchy farmland, plate tectonics masks, biome IDs with shared borders. Prototyped: rel_province, window 32 wide.
ideas.why_new: CellularValue/Lookup produce one scale; stacking two Cellular nodes gives independent, non-nested partitions (fine walls cross coarse walls). Nesting (fine cells never straddle a coarse border) is what a graph cannot express.
ideas.simd_plan: Lattice-only parent arithmetic: integer add, arithmetic shift, integer compare on two id components per axis, masks for the rank. 3^D window for pass 1 and 2. Estimate 1.5-2x CellularDistance. No source evaluation. Power-of-two block sizes keep Floor as a shift. The window should be safe at 3^D as in PolyGauge, but the proto used 5x5.
ideas.continuity: Border line output is C0 thanks to the constant denominator, including across merged walls (d_i=d_j on the merged wall, so wd matches on both sides). Not formally run through check. Value outputs are discontinuous by design.
ideas.params: Levels (int 1..4), Ratio (float, coarse/fine), Level Widths (per-level wall multiplier table or Width + Width Gain), Amp Gain (lineage), Output enum {LineageValue, AncestorValue, AncestorLookup, Walls}, Exact Parent (bool, 3^D search), Grid Jitter per level, Source, Feature Scale.
ideas.risks:
3D cost grows fast with levels; 2^D parent search makes parent regions slightly non-Voronoi (fine in practice). With Ratio < 2 the nesting is barely visible. Walls between different-parent cells are thicker but not longer-range; a 'thick border' is still only one fine cell wide at most (Width <= margin).
[Provinces, cell-relations] Small hop leaves the square block visible at large scale; large hop gives detached exclaves (sometimes desirable). Coast distance saturates at window reach (about 1 fine cell), so it is a shoreline band, not a global distance.
ideas.variant_notes: Opposite direction to NestedVoronoi: fine cells inherit a coarse id so coarse borders are made of fine walls. Parent lookup options: nearest coarse point in a 2^D block, or integer block with hashed hop (cheaper, Provinces).
ideas.cost_note: Estimate 1.5-2x CellularDistance.

queue.name: CellularHierarchy
queue.reason: Country, province, county cells through a deterministic 2^D parent lookup (J2, J3 top pick). Use the integer form, since the float parent chain runs far above the 2x cost claim.

ideas.name: CellularMetricField
ideas.one_liner: Each site carries its own elliptical metric, so bisectors become curved conics and cells become leaves, flames and pebbles, optionally all aligned to a hybrid angle.
ideas.algorithm:
For window points: u = R(h)*v (per-point rotation from a table). Metric Ellipse: d = sqrt(u.x^2 + (A*u.y)^2 [+...]), A>=1 so d>=|v|. Metric Polygon: d = K_N * max_k dot(u, n_k), per-point N=3,4,5,6 chosen by masks (3D: tetra, cube, octa normals). Multiply by per-point size. F1 (optional F2, index value). Output F1, value of winner, or F2-F1. Polygon metric gives a piecewise linear heightfield.

[CellularMetricJitter, cell-relations] Window loop as Cellular.inl. Per window point c: v = S - P_c.
  theta_c = Rotation*rnd01(hash bits)*2pi, or theta from Angle hybrid sampled at P_c (coherent orientation field); (cos,sin) from the 256-entry table (or reuse the jitter direction vector as the rotation frame: free).
  Twist: theta += Twist * |v|   (needs FS::Sin/Cos per point; only matters for non-Euclid or stretched metrics)
  v' = R(theta) v ; v'' = (v'.x / a_c, v'.y * a_c) with a_c = Aspect*(1 + AspectJitter*rnd11)
  d_c = DistanceFunction(v'')   (reuse CalcDistance: Euclid, Manhattan, MaxAxis/Chebyshev, Minkowski)
then the usual F1..F4 / value selection, ReturnType, etc. (this is a drop-in extension of the Cellular base: 'Metric Rotation Jitter', 'Aspect', 'Twist').
3D: rotation from a 256-entry random rotation matrix table (9 fmadd per point), aspect along the rotated x axis; twist about the rotated z axis.
Consistency: metric ratio rho = max stretch (sqrt(2) for Chebyshev vs Euclid, a^2 for aspect a). The in-window minimum is guaranteed only when rho * (nearest in-window Euclid distance) < 1 + margin; practically seamless for Aspect <= 1.5 with GridJitter <= 0.7; a Wide Window option (5x5, 2D only) removes the limit at 2.8x cost.
ideas.look:
Ellipse: leaf, feather, pebble, stretched grain with curved cell boundaries. Polygon: star-faceted crystal pyramids; hillshade looks like low-poly crystal. Prototyped both: visibly different from isotropic and global-metric Cellular variants on the sheet.
[CellularMetricField, lit-classic] Prototype cl_cell modes 5, 6. Asp 1.6: curved, plump pebble cells with bowed walls, like river stones or dried clay. Asp 3-4 (5x5): lens or blade cells, overlapping like bark or feathers. Aligned Angle field: elongated cells following a flow, like wood cross grain, muscle, or stretched bark.
[CellularMetricJitter, cell-relations] Cellular Manhattan on the sheet is rigidly axis-aligned; rotating each cell's metric turns it into a shattered mosaic of rotated squares/diamonds overlapping like crystals grown with independent orientation (F1 shows rotated pyramids, F2-F1 shows angular zigzag walls). Aspect gives elongated ellipse-ish cells whose walls are conic arcs (curved), aligned by a source field: fish scales following a flow, tension cracks. Twist makes pinwheel cells whose iso-lines are squares rotating with radius.
ideas.why_new: DomainAxisScale applies one stretch to all cells and keeps boundaries straight. Size Jitter gives circular weights. Per-site anisotropy gives curved walls and coherent elongation following a field, which no graph can produce because metric selection happens inside the search.
ideas.simd_plan: +1 dot, +2 FMA, +1 hashed direction per candidate inside the existing 3^dim loop: ~1.15x CellularDistance in all dimensions, same window. 2D direction via sin/cos poly of a bounded angle or via a 16-entry direction table indexed by hash bits (permute on AVX2). Branch-free.
ideas.continuity: F1 C0 at Asp 1.6 (c0ratio 8.00, no visible seams). At Asp 3 in a 3x3 window, rectangular seams are clearly visible; they disappear at 5x5.
ideas.params: Metric enum, Anisotropy (hybrid), Rotation Spread (0 aligned, 1 random, or from a hybrid angle), Size Jitter, Grid Jitter, return type enum.
ideas.risks:
Aspect limit is tight with 3^d; users will push past it. F2 suffers before F1. Output range shifts with Asp. Bisectors are not exact when Asp differs between sites, but that is the look. 3D not prototyped.
[CellularMetricJitter, cell-relations] Window inconsistency at high anisotropy (needs the 5x5 option or a clamp); per-cell rotation of a Euclid metric without aspect/twist is a no-op (document). Rotated Chebyshev F2-F1 walls are polylines, not smooth.
[ShapedCellular, stamp-scatter] The Jitter clamp reduces randomness at high anisotropy; document. Polygon metric with per-cell rotation needs the direction table rotated per cell (n rotations per cell). Superellipse Pow cost in 3D/4D.
ideas.variant_notes: Per-site rotated, stretched or polygonal metric. Window limit found by test: aspect about 1.8 fits 3x3, aspect 3 shows clear seams until 5x5. A hybrid Angle gives field-aligned cells; Twist needs Sin/Cos per candidate. Could become members on Cellular.
ideas.cost_note: +1 dot, +2 FMA, +1 hashed direction per candidate inside the existing 3^dim loop: ~1.15x CellularDistance in all dimensions, same window.

ideas.name: CellularPlanes
ideas.one_liner: Worley cells carrying a random plane (height + tilt) instead of a flat value: faulted blocks, tilted plates, crystal facets; a Smoothness parameter blends the planes with smooth-Voronoi weights into a continuous fault-block terrain.
ideas.algorithm:
Pass 1: F1 squared distance d1. Pass 2: for each window cell i: plane_i=v_i+dot(t_i, x-p_i); w_i=max(0, 1-(d_i^2-d1)/S)^m, with m by repeated squaring (constant loop). Output sum(w_i*plane_i)/sum(w_i). The owner always has w=1, so the denominator never vanishes. S->0 gives hard Voronoi tilted tiles; large S gives smooth hills. The proto used simpler absolute weights (1-d^2/R^2)^(2^(p+1)) which underflow at high p and showed gray flats; the F1-relative form fixes that.

[CellularPlanes, terrain-tools-engines] Cellular lattice 3^d with Jitter. Per feature point i: q_i, hashed lift v_i = Lift*rnd11, tilt vector g_i = Tilt*rndDir(h) (unit direction times a hashed magnitude^Bias), plane_i(p) = v_i + g_i . (p - q_i). Hard mode (Smoothness = 0): output plane of the F1 point (track argmin as CellularValue does, but carry q and hash through the Selects). Smooth mode: w_i = exp2(-k*d_i), k = lerp(64, 4, Smoothness); out = sum w_i plane_i / sum w_i (IQ smooth-voronoi weights applied to planes rather than distances). Optional Cell Flatten 0..1 multiplies tilt by (1 - Flatten) near cell centres: facets. Optional Source Lookup: replace v_i with Source(q_i) (like CellularLookup) so plate heights follow a large-scale field (tectonic uplift map). Normalise: |out| <= Lift + Tilt*cellRadius.
ideas.look:
Horst-and-graben terrain, tilted slate blocks, tumbled basalt, shingled plains: each block has a clear dip direction and ends at a cliff. Hillshade reads as geological faulting. Clearly unlike CellularValue, whose cells are flat, or any smooth noise. Prototyped: rel_fault p=2 and p=4 are the good range.
[CellularPlanes, terrain-tools-engines] Sharp-edged tilted slabs and stepped fault blocks (basalt columns from above, fractured ice sheets, crystal clusters), and in Smooth mode a continuous landscape of gently tilted plateaus meeting along soft fault lines; in 3D, polyhedral shard volumes. The sheet has flat-per-cell CellularValue only.
ideas.why_new: Per-cell slope requires the feature point position and a second hashed vector inside the cellular loop; CellularValue/CellularLookup cannot produce gradients within a cell. Gaea Shatter/Plates/Voronoi 'forms' and World Creator Plateaus are the tool-side analogues.
ideas.simd_plan: 3^D window, plane is one dot, weight one Max plus a fixed count of multiplies, one final Reciprocal. Stack array for d^2 or run F1 first. Estimate 2x CellularDistance, 2D 8 ns, 3D 25 ns, 4D 85 ns. Measured scalar 2.7x worley2 at p=4. Generic GenT.
ideas.continuity: C0 for S>0 and C-infinity away from the F1 switch: c0ratio 7.87 at p=4 with a max slope near 50. S=0 is discontinuous. Requires (d_out^2-d1) >= S for out-of-window cells: at low sharpness the proto's R=1.3 shows faint grid-line seams in hillshade, so S needs an upper bound.
ideas.params: Jitter, Lift (hybrid), Tilt (hybrid), Tilt Bias, Smoothness 0..1, Flatten, Source (optional lookup for lift), Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks:
Range exceeds base [-1,1] if tilt is high, so needs clamp or analytic scale. The low-sharpness end looks like ordinary noise, so the sharp end is the value here.
[CellularShards, cell-relations] Soft mode is close in spirit to Voronoise (IQ 2014) extended with gradients; the value add is the hard shard look and hybrid slope. Exp cost in 4D.
ideas.variant_notes: Random per-cell plane rather than a source tangent. Use F1-relative weights: absolute weights underflowed and showed gray flats at high sharpness.
ideas.cost_note: Estimate 2x CellularDistance, 2D 8 ns, 3D 25 ns, 4D 85 ns. Measured scalar 2.7x worley2 at p=4.

queue.name: CellularPlanes
queue.reason: Tilted per-cell planes with F1-relative smooth weights: smooth hills to fault blocks on one knob at 2x Cellular. Range needs a clamp.

disp.how: Output Plate; critic wanted a CellularValue mode, but the F1-relative weight pass is this one

ideas.name: CellularRelaxed
ideas.one_liner: One pointwise repulsion/Lloyd-style relaxation step on the jittered feature points before the distance test, giving blue-noise cells of uniform size without grid alignment.
ideas.algorithm:
Hash window 5^d (2-ring) of feature points q (jitter as usual), candidates = inner 3^d.
  for each candidate c (fixed loop):
      disp = 0
      for each n in c's own 3^d neighbourhood, n != c (fixed loop, all inside the 5^d window):
          r = q_c - q_n ; disp += r / (dot(r,r) + eps)     // inverse-distance repulsion
      disp *= Relax ; disp *= min(1, MaxDisp / (|disp| + 1e-9))  // clamp so points stay inside their cell
      q_c' = q_c + disp
  Then the usual F1/F2/CellValue/Index over q_c'.
Optional Iterations 2 with frozen neighbours (Jacobi approximation, no bigger window).

[ShyPoints, cell-relations] Raw point q_c from hash. Repel: p_c=q_c+sum over 8 (or 6 in 3D) neighbours n of K*max(0,R^2-|q_c-q_n|^2)^2*unit(q_c-q_n). Prune: c is dead if any neighbour n has |q_c-q_n|<r and h_n>h_c (a local rule, so independent of evaluation order; survivors are guaranteed at least r apart). Then normal F1/F2/value over relaxed or surviving points with dead cells' distance forced large.
ideas.look:
Repel: even skin or honeycomb-like cells with few tiny slivers and no grid. Prune: larger, airier cells, usable as guaranteed non-overlapping stamps, for tree or boulder placement. Prototyped: rel_relax, mode=0,1,2. The difference from plain jitter is real but subtle in repel mode and stronger in prune mode.
[CellularRelaxed, dynamics-iteration] Evenly sized, evenly spaced cells: foam, basalt columns, reptile scales, honeycomb-like but still irregular; F2-F1 cracks of uniform width and spacing, F1 bubbles of equal size. Existing CellularDistance at low jitter regularises but shows the grid; at jitter 1 it clumps. This is the 'centroidal Voronoi' look in one node.
ideas.why_new: Point-set relaxation is normally a global iterative process; computing each candidate's one relaxation step from its own neighbourhood (available via the 2-ring hash window) makes it stateless. Makes a hard thing (uniform cells) a parameter.
ideas.simd_plan: Hashes only for the 2-ring (cheap), then 3^d x (3^d - 1) repulsion terms, each a sub, dot, Reciprocal and FMA; then the standard distance pass. Cost 2D: 25 hashes + 72 terms + 9 dists = ~4x CellularDistance 2D (~15 ns). 3D: 125 hashes + 702 terms = ~10x (~120 ns). 4D: 81x80 terms is too much; use only the 2d axis neighbours in 4D (81x8 = 648 terms, ~300 ns) and say so. Consistency across samples holds because each candidate's displacement depends only on its own 1-ring.
ideas.continuity: C0 for F1/F2 (positions are smooth functions of hashes and the min is continuous); CellValue piecewise constant.
ideas.params: Relax hybrid, MaxDisp float, Jitter hybrid, Iterations int (1..2), Distance Function enum, Return Type enum, plus Cellular's existing params.
ideas.risks:
3D/4D cost; clamping is needed to keep the 3^d candidate window correct (MaxDisp <= (1 - Jitter)/2 cell), so strong relaxation needs lower jitter; one step is only an approximation of CVT (good enough visually).
[ShyPoints, cell-relations] Visual gain over jitter is modest in Repel mode. Prune needs a wider F1 window, and 3D gets very expensive. A single step does not produce a real blue-noise spectrum (not measured).
ideas.variant_notes: ShyPoints reports the visual gain over jitter is modest in Repel mode and stronger in Prune mode.
ideas.cost_note: Cost 2D: 25 hashes + 72 terms + 9 dists = ~4x CellularDistance 2D (~15 ns). 3D: 125 hashes + 702 terms = ~10x (~120 ns).

ideas.name: CellularShape
ideas.one_liner: Each cell owns a randomly rotated, sized SDF shape (disc, segment/capsule, ellipse, n-gon, square, spokes, star, ring); union/smooth-union/sum them, or run the Voronoi outputs on the shape distances (curved parabolic/hyperbolic walls, elongated cells, Johnson-Mehl growth).
ideas.algorithm:
Window loop as Cellular.inl (ring jitter is fine). For each window point: v = S - P_c; hash bits give rotation index (256-entry cos/sin table), size_c = Size*(1 + SizeJitter*rnd11), shape params (segment length L_c, n-gon rotation, spoke count).
  v' = R_c * v / size_c   (2 fmadd for 2D rotation)
  Shape SDF in unit frame, all branch-free:
    Disc: |v'| - 1
    Square: max(|x|,|y|) - 1
    NGon(n <= 8, constant loop): max_k dot(v', u_k) - cos(pi/n), u_k from a table
    Capsule: dist(v', segment(-L,0..L,0)) - 1
    Spokes(k): min_k dist(v', segment(0..u_k*L))
    Star: min(NGon(n), NGon(n) rotated by pi/n with inner apothem)
    Ring: abs(Disc) - Thickness
  d_c = sdf * size_c
Combine (Blend enum):
  Union: F1 = min d_c ; also keep F2 and the owner hash
  SmoothUnion: polynomial smin with K
  Sum: sum_c max(0, 1 - max(d_c,0)/Falloff)^2  (blob density, C1)
Output enum: Distance (= F1 clamped at Dmax), Mask, OwnerValue (rnd11(owner hash), flat per shape), F2-F1 (Voronoi-of-shapes walls), Density.
Growth (Johnson-Mehl) mode: radius_c = Speed*max(0, Time - birth_c) with Time a hybrid (use w or a Constant); unborn shapes get d = +inf via Select: crystals nucleate and grow until they meet.
Consistency: a shape of radius <= Rmax around P_c with |S-P_c|inf >= 1 is at least 1 - Rmax away; clamp Distance at Dmax = 1 - Rmax and the min is exact. For OwnerValue/F2-F1 the usual Cellular caveat applies (nearest in-window shape must be closer than 1 - Rmax: true except at extreme jitter).
3D: rotation from a 256-entry table of random 3x3 rotation matrices (built once), shapes: sphere, box, octahedron (|x|+|y|+|z|-1), capsule, n-prism, 3D spokes.
ideas.look:
Scattered rotated squares, hexagons, sequins, scales, asterisks; with Union + Mask it is a 'shape splatter', with F2-F1 it is a Voronoi whose cells are elongated around capsules and whose walls are parabolic (segment vs point) or hyperbolic (discs of different radii), i.e. visibly curved walls with centres that do not move. Sum gives metaball blobs. Growth mode animates crystal nucleation.
[SegmentCellular, dcc-tools] F1: worm-shaped cells, fingerprint-like pits, wood ray flecks. F2-F1: elongated pebbles with long creases. Line with narrow spread: directional scratches. Line with bend: fibres and hair. Prototype: dcc_lens mode=21. Substance Scratches and Messy Fibers, Modo Scratches and Wires.
[CellularFlake, volumetric-3d4d] Not prototyped. 3D iso, discs with Spread 0.2: thin stacked plates like shale or schist; Spread 1: confetti or shattered ice. Rings: interlocked loops, chain mail or noodle tangle. Segments: hay, felt, needles. 2D slice of discs: short hatched line segments like graphite flakes in cast iron, a look absent from the sheet; 2D form of ring is an outlined circle field.
ideas.why_new: Cellular nodes only know points with an isotropic metric; Size Jitter already gives circular-arc walls (multiplicative weights), but elongated cells, polygonal/star shapes per cell, capsule-Voronoi (parabolic walls) and per-cell shape ids are not expressible with any graph of existing nodes.
ideas.simd_plan: Same 3^D loop as Cellular.inl plus per point: table lookup of cos/sin by hash bits (gather or two 256-float constexpr tables indexed via FS::Load per lane; alternatively derive cos/sin from the existing random direction bits already used for jitter: the jitter direction IS a unit vector, reuse it as the rotation), 2D rotation 4 mul, shape 8-40 ops, min/Select chain. 2D: 1.5-3x CellularDistance (6-12 ns). 3D: rotation 9 mul per point x 27 + shape: 1.5-3x Cellular3D (20-35 ns). 4D: skip rotation (use axis-aligned shapes), ~1.3x Cellular4D.
ideas.continuity: Distance/F2-F1: C0 like Cellular. SmoothUnion: C1. Sum/Density: C1-C2. Mask/OwnerValue: discontinuous.
ideas.params: Shape enum, Size (hybrid), Size Jitter, Rotation Jitter (0..1), Shape Param (L for capsule/spokes, n for n-gon, thickness for ring), Blend enum {Union, SmoothUnion, Sum}, Smooth K (hybrid), Output enum {Distance, Mask, OwnerValue, F2MinusF1, Density}, Time (hybrid, growth), Grid Jitter (hybrid as in Cellular), Feature Scale.
ideas.risks:
Large shapes (Rmax near 1) shrink Dmax to nearly 0; keep Size*(1+SizeJitter) <= ~0.6 cells. N-gon SDF without atan2 is an n-term max (fine for n<=8). Many enum combinations: scope the first version to Disc/Square/NGon/Capsule/Spokes.
[CellularShape, shader-community] Exactness of the 3^d window breaks for large primitives (seams/popping where a far primitive would have been nearer); clamp Radius+Jitter/2 <= 0.5 in the setter. N-gon folding costs n reflections. 3D random rotations need a cheap hash-to-rotation (quaternion from 3 uniforms, Shoemake).
[SegmentCellular, dcc-tools] Long Length forces sparse cells or window growth. Directional spread needs a per-dimension direction story: 3D uses member direction plus table cone. Fine lines alias at low sampling.
ideas.variant_notes: Worley over SDF primitives. Merged primitives: segment with bend (SegmentCellular: worm cells, scratches), disc and ring (CellularFlake: shale, mica, chain-mail in 3D), and n-gon, box, spokes, star. Also Johnson-Mehl growth via a Time param.
ideas.cost_note: 2D: 1.5-3x CellularDistance (6-12 ns). 3D: rotation 9 mul per point x 27 + shape: 1.5-3x Cellular3D (20-35 ns).

ideas.name: CellularSmooth
ideas.one_liner: Smooth Voronoi (exp-smin of all cell distances) and Voronoise (kernel-weighted cell values) in one node: blobby metaball cells and the continuous family between cell noise, Perlin-like noise and Voronoi.
ideas.algorithm:
Window 3^d, centred jitter J <= 0.5, kernel reach R <= 1 cell so the window is exact (iq uses 5x5 because his jitter is 1 and reach sqrt(2)).
For each cell: h = hash(c); q = c + 0.5 + J*(rnd01(h)-0.5); d = |p - q| (or d2 to skip the sqrt in the Value mode); v = rnd11(h>>8).
Mode SmoothDistance (iq smooth voronoi):
  acc += Exp(-k * d)         // k = 1/Smoothness, Smoothness in (0, 1]
  out = -Log(acc) / k        // exact n-ary exponential smin of all distances; Smoothness->0 recovers F1
  (alternative Power mode: acc += 1/d^8, out = acc^(-1/8); needs d>eps guard; cheaper on hardware without fast exp)
Mode SmoothValue (iq voronoise): 
  w = (1 - smoothstep(0, R, d))^k with k = 1 + 63*(1-V)^6 (V = value smoothness 0..1); Wsum += w; Vsum += w*v
  out = Vsum / Wsum          // V=0: hard cell values (CellularValue), V=1: smooth blobby value noise on a jittered grid, J=0 V=1: a Perlin-like lattice noise
  Integer k path: k rounded to an int member, pow via repeated squaring (branch-free, k same for all lanes); fractional k via Exp(k*Log(.)).
Mode SmoothDistanceMinusF1: out = F1 - smoothF1 (iq/Blender 'bevelled cells', needs F1 from the same loop: free).
ideas.look:
Soap-film / metaball cells with rounded junctions instead of sharp creases, melting Voronoi; the voronoise path gives soft random-blob textures and bevelled rounded plates. All continuous, none of it on the contact sheet, and the Smoothness slider morphs continuously from F1 to a smooth bump field.
[SoftCellular, lit-classic] Prototype cl_kens. Value k=12: soft-edged polygon mosaic, airbrushed stained glass; k=40: crisp with rounded lobes; k=6: blurry patches. Distance k=4-10: dark wells that merge into peanut shapes, with smooth ridges and no cusps, unlike the F1 sheet. Soft biome masks, cells under membrane, droplets.
ideas.why_new: MinSmooth exists only as a binary blend of two sources; an n-ary smin over the 9/27 cell distances cannot be expressed in the graph. Voronoise is a well-known 2-parameter family (cell/Perlin/Voronoi) that FastNoise cannot reach today.
ideas.simd_plan: One fixed loop, per cell: hash, distance, Exp (or pow via integer squaring), 2 FMAs. 2D: 9 Exp ~ CellularDistance 2D x 1.5 (~6 ns). 3D: 27 Exp ~ 20 ns. 4D 81 Exp ~ 65 ns (document). Log once at the end. Reuse CellularDistance's lattice/jitter machinery; dimension agnostic.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity for value mode with the subtraction (c0ratio 8.00 at k=6). Distance mode has a tiny window seam for k below ~6, visible as faint straight lines in hillshade at k=2-4.
ideas.params: Feature Scale, Jitter (<=0.5), Smoothness (hybrid, distance mode), Value Smoothness V (hybrid), Kernel Reach R (<=1), Mode enum {SmoothDistance, SmoothDistancePower, SmoothValue, Bevel}, Distance function enum (Euclidean, Manhattan: still C-inf smin), Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks:
Exp(-k d) underflow for small Smoothness: clamp k <= 64 and compute relative to the min distance (acc += Exp(-k*(d - dmin)) with dmin from a first min pass, or just clamp). Output range depends on k; normalise by measured constants per k or expose VariableRange.
[SoftCellular, lit-classic] k<6 needs a 5^d window or shows lattice seams. Very large k underflows (Clamp k or normalise by the smallest d2 first). Distance range shifts with k, so ScaleOutput needs a k-aware offset.
ideas.variant_notes: Exp smin distances and Voronoise-style weighted values. SoftCellular adds the window-seam subtraction and a hybrid Sharpness that morphs from soft blobs to crisp mosaic.
ideas.cost_note: 2D: 9 Exp ~ CellularDistance 2D x 1.5 (~6 ns). 3D: 27 Exp ~ 20 ns.

queue.name: CellularSmooth
queue.reason: Smooth voronoi plus voronoise, a well-known gap and cheap to fill. Clamp k and guard Exp underflow; Power mode avoids Exp.

ideas.name: ClusterCellular
ideas.one_liner: Spots arranged by macro shape (clumps, fairy rings, arcs, trails) with a single parent-cell lookup per child, so 2x hash cost whatever the number of children.
ideas.algorithm:
Fine lattice for children, coarse parent lattice with integer Ratio. For each of the 3^dim child candidates: parent cell P = floor(childCell/Ratio) with exactly one parent hash (not a window of parents). Parent centre Cp = (P+0.5)*Ratio + small jitter (<20%), spread S = Spread*rnd(parent). Survival probability from child feature position c: d = |c-Cp|. Blob: exp(-d^2/S^2). Ring: exp(-(d-S)^2/Width^2). Arc: ring times angular window from dot(unit(c-Cp),dir). Trail: distance to a parent-hash segment. Decision: alive = rnd(child) < prob(d). Requires S + 2*Width < Ratio/2 - jitter so clusters cannot cross parent bounds, otherwise clipped. Alive is a pure function of the feature, so no sample-dependent pops. Value = max or sum of alive bump(|p-c|/r). Generalises: any analytic parent shape can drive child placement.

[ClusterCellular, hierarchy-multiscale] Levels K (default 3), spacing s_k = s_0 / Lacunarity^k. Point of level k in cell c: pos = (c + 0.5 + jitter(h)*Jitter) * s_k, h = HashPrimes(k, c). Activity:
  active_0 = true (top level always on -> bounded search)
  active_k(pos) = (rnd01(h) < Fill_k) & (|pos - parentPos| < Radius * s_{k-1}) & active_{k-1}(parentPos)
  where parentPos is the level-(k-1) point of the cell floor(pos / s_{k-1}); the chain is unrolled k times (k hashes).
  Per-cell count variant: each cell holds up to 4 candidate points, candidate j active iff j < count(h) with count geometric (P(count>=j)=CountKeep^j); inactive candidates get distance +inf via Select.
  Search: for each level k, 3^D window around floor(p/s_k): for each cell, for each candidate: d = |pos - p| / (s_k * SizeWeight^k) if active else +inf; keep F1 (and F2, nearest hash) across all levels.
Outputs: Distance (F1, normalised by level spacing so clusters of small cells read as small cells), Value (rnd11 of nearest hash), Level (k of nearest, as discrete value), Kernel = sum over active points of (1 - d)^2 clamped (soft blobs, galaxies), F2-F1 (cell walls).
ideas.look:
Prototype at ratio 10 in a 28-unit window: clear rings of small spots (fairy rings, atolls, meteor debris rings); at blob mode, tight clumps with large empty spaces, i.e. star clusters, mushrooms, pox, rock outcrops. Prototype with too small a ratio was merely sparse, so the shape requires ratio >= 8.
[ClusterCellular, hierarchy-multiscale] Voronoi cells of 2-3 discrete size classes where the small cells appear only in clusters around a parent, and clusters themselves cluster: archipelagos with islets around main islands, settlements with hamlets around towns, galaxy groups, lichen/mould colonies, foam with daughter bubbles. Kernel mode gives dotted clumps at nested scales. Distinct from CellularDistance (uniform size) and from a density-controlled Voronoi (smoothly varying size): sizes are quantised and spatially clustered.
ideas.why_new: Jittered grids give even coverage, and a Density source would need one eval per child and cannot draw thin rings cheaply. Point patterns with heavy clumping (a Neyman-Scott process) have no node at present, and a spatial arrangement at two scales cannot be made from a graph because alive is a per-feature property.
ideas.simd_plan: Per candidate: child hash + parent hash (integer floor division by Ratio, or float floor) + exp or polynomial approx of prob. 2D ~2x CellularDistance = 8 ns. 3D ~25 ns. 4D ~85 ns. Replace exp with a rational window to lower cost.
ideas.continuity: C0 for mask reaching zero inside the 3-cell reach. Per-feature decisions cannot create sample-space jumps; only hard clipping at parent boundaries is possible, avoided by the S bound.
ideas.params: Ratio (int), Mode enum (Blob/Ring/Arc/Trail), Spread, Spread Jitter, Ring Width, Child Radius, Parent Density, Child Density, Background
ideas.risks:
Parent lattice can show periodic arrangement at Ratio spacing because parents sit near cell centres with limited jitter. Large empty regions affect normalisation and mean. Constraint between Spread and Ratio is awkward for artists; expose Spread as a fraction of Ratio.
[ClusterCellular, hierarchy-multiscale] Cost grows with Levels; keep K<=3. Parent lookup uses the parent cell containing the child, so children near a parent-cell edge whose parent point sits across the edge are missed (slight anisotropy, invisible in practice).
ideas.variant_notes: Child survival decided per feature from a parent lattice. ClusterScatter draws macro shapes (rings, arcs, trails); ClusterCellular nests levels.
ideas.cost_note: 2D ~2x CellularDistance = 8 ns. 3D ~25 ns.

ideas.name: ConicCells
ideas.one_liner: Voronoi with a wind-biased eccentric cone metric: cells become overlapping scallops and rings become nested arcs pointing downwind, for scales, ropy lava and scalloped ice.
ideas.algorithm: T(x)=min over the window of (|v|-e*(v.w)), with v=x-p_i, unit wind w, and eccentricity e in [0,1). Level sets are conics with a focus at the seed, and boundaries are hyperbolae. Window: seeds that matter lie upwind, so centre the 3^D window at floor(x-shift*w) with shift about 0.6. Output T, or cos(2*pi*f*T) for nested arcs.
ideas.look: Hillshade shows overlapping fish-scale or roof-tile plates all pointing downwind, with a smooth back and a sharp lip. Rings give eccentric targets and arcs resembling ropy pahoehoe lava or scalloped cave walls.
ideas.why_new: No existing metric is directional: Manhattan, MaxAxis and Minkowski are all symmetric, and domain scale only stretches cells without making an asymmetric scallop. Sits close to CellularDistance in cost for a very different output.
ideas.simd_plan: Replaces the distance calculation only, so it could be a DistanceFunction option. Same window count: about 4.5 ns in 2D (1.1x CellularDistance), 14 ns in 3D, 45 ns in 4D. Rounded shift per lane is fine for a constant wind.
ideas.continuity: C0: min of continuous functions, with a cusp at each seed. At e=0.65 the shifted 3x3 window matched a 7x7 reference exactly over 360x360 samples (0 mismatches), while unshifted 3x3 mismatched 1.3% with max error 0.29.
ideas.params: Eccentricity (hybrid, keep at or below about 0.8), Wind Direction (hybrid), Grid Jitter (hybrid), Output {Distance, Rings}, Ring Frequency.
ideas.risks: Window match was tested only at one e, seed and region; higher e needs a larger shift or window. A hybrid wind changes the window shift across space and can cause small seams. Output range grows as about (1+e) and depends on window.
ideas.cost_note: Same window count: about 4.5 ns in 2D (1.1x CellularDistance), 14 ns in 3D, 45 ns in 4D.

ideas.name: CoralNoise
ideas.one_liner: Exact SDF to a lattice of hierarchically branching capsules (root segment per cell, M children per segment, L levels) where w is growth age: coral, bare trees, roots, neurons, lightning and needle crystals that grow in place.
ideas.algorithm:
Window 3x3x3 (3x3 2D). Per cell k: h = Hash(k); a0 = k + 0.5 + 0.2*rnd3(h); u0 = normalize(rndDir3(h>>8) + UpBias*(0,1,0)); L0 = BranchLength (<= 0.35).
Fixed-count enumeration of the branch tree (Levels in 0..2, Children M in 1..3, count sum M^l per cell): child j of segment (a, u, L, birth): hj = Hash(h, j, level); attach t_j in [0.4,1] from hj; aj = a + t_j*L*u; uj = normalize(u + Spread*rndDir3(hj)); Lj = L*0.6; birth_j = birth + t_j*L/Speed.
Growth (age A = w in 4D, or Age hybrid in 2D/3D; A = infinity if unused): len = Clamp((A - birth)*Speed, 0, L); rad = Radius*0.6^level * Min(1, len/(0.1 L)) (radius grows in over the first 10 percent of life so a segment never pops); segment b = a + len*u.
d = capsuleDistance(p, a, b) - rad; sdf = Min over all segments of all 27 cells (unborn segments have len=0 and rad=0, contributing a point of radius 0: mask them to BIG with Select(A > birth, d, BIG)).
Extent from cell centre <= 0.2 + 0.35 + 0.21 + 0.126 < 0.9, so cells two away stay >= 0.6 from the sample: exact for Radius < 0.6. Output: Signed SDF (scaled) or Solid = Clamp(1 - sdf/Radius).
ideas.look: 3D iso at 0: fields of small branching corals or bare shrubs rising from seed points; UpBias < 0 gives root systems; Spread small, M=1, Levels 2 with per-level kinks gives lightning/Lichtenberg bolts; Levels=0 gives random oriented needles (acicular crystals, hoarfrost, hay). As w increases, trunks extend, then branches sprout where the trunk has reached their attach point, then twigs: a genuine growth animation. 2D slice: short dashes, dots and Y-shapes; a 2D-native Gen gives bare-tree silhouettes / cracks that branch.
ideas.why_new: The graph cannot make branching 1D structures at all. Exact Lipschitz-1 SDF means offsets, shells and sphere tracing work; growth as a parameter is free; needle noise alone is a new look.
ideas.simd_plan: Cellular.inl window loop with an inner fixed-count tree loop; every segment is a capsule distance (~20 ops) plus hash/normalize per segment (normalize = InvSqrt). Levels=1,M=3: 4 segments/cell x 27 = 108 capsules ~ 2x CellularDistance 3D (25 ns); Levels=2,M=2: 7/cell = 189 capsules ~ 3.5x (45 ns); 2D ~ 2x CellularDistance 2D. 4D = 3D lattice with w as age (tiles correctly since continuous in w). A true 4D lattice is not recommended.
ideas.continuity: C0 (min of exact capsule SDFs, |grad| <= 1); continuous in w thanks to the radius grow-in.
ideas.params: BranchLength, Radius (hybrid), Children (int 1-3), Levels (int 0-2), Spread, UpBias, Speed, Age (hybrid, 2D/3D), Feature Scale, Seed, Output enum.
ideas.risks: Cost scales with 27 x segments; the 'children only of the 2-3 nearest roots' shortcut would halve it but introduces seams where the nearest root switches, so it should be an explicit quality option at most. Lattice regularity of one tree per cell needs jitter plus a Density mask (hybrid) to kill some roots for natural clumping.
ideas.cost_note: Levels=1,M=3: 4 segments/cell x 27 = 108 capsules ~ 2x CellularDistance 3D (25 ns); Levels=2,M=2: 7/cell = 189 capsules ~ 3.5x (45 ns); 2D ~ 2x CellularDistance 2D.

queue.name: CoralNoise
queue.reason: Wild card. Exact SDF to a growing branching capsule forest, with growth in w as the showpiece. 100-190 capsules per sample rules out regular use, but the look may justify a hero node.

ideas.name: CraterField
ideas.one_liner: Multi-octave impact craters with destructive overprinting: floors erase older terrain and smaller craters, ejecta stacks additively, and late big impacts are replayed. Crater noise is known from planet generators; the erase-and-replay ordering is the variation.
ideas.algorithm:
Octave loop over radii with lacunarity about 1.6, existence probability giving N(D)~D^-2. At each octave, a crater's radius is at most 0.45 cell and centre jitter keeps it inside its own cell, so bowls in one octave never overlap and only the own-cell bowl need be tested. This removes any ordering seam.
Profile in r/R: floor flat or parabolic; raised rim; central peak if R>Rc; terraced inner wall bands for large R.
Compositing: m=smoothstep bowl mask; h=h*(1-m*Erase)+m*Depth*profile(r/R), then Ejecta added from the 3x3 window: rim blanket ~ (R/r)^3 with radial rays for young craters, angular variation from a small direction-to-noise polynomial hash.
Replay: after the fine octaves, rerun 1-2 coarse octaves with a different seed and low probability, so a few large young craters erase small ones (saturated terrain and fresh scars together).

[CraterField, stamp-scatter] Trick (colour fold): any non-commutative fold over stamps must apply them in one global order, or it seams where window contents change. Assign each lattice cell a colour from (ix mod 3, iy mod 3,...). Any 3-wide window holds exactly one cell of each colour, and that cell is computed directly, per lane, without search: g_axis(c) = 3*floor((floor(p_axis)+1-c_axis)/3) + c_axis. Loop colours c = 0..3^dim-1 (constant count) so the order is the same everywhere. For each level l of L, lattice scale s_l = Base*2^l, processed large to small: for each colour: f = feature of g, r = rad(h) <= 1 cell. t = |p-c|/r. Profile: bowl (t<0.75): 0.9*(t^2/0.5625-1)+0.35, rim fading to 0 at t=1. Flood weight fl = 1 - smoothstep(0.55,0.85,t). h = lerp(h, floorRef_i, fl) + r*Depth*profile*(1-smoothstep(0.9,1,t)). floorRef is the stamp's hash height, or the Source sampled at the crater centre (one eval per crater). Height units scale by 1/s_l so depth is proportional to diameter. Level density p_l = Density*2^(-b*(L-1-l)) gives crater size-frequency slope b. Optional Base Source is added as initial h.
ideas.look:
Prototype at 3 levels reads as a saturated cratered surface: bowls cut into older bowls, flat floors, rims broken by younger impacts. Spectrum shows no lattice dots at 16x window, axis stat high only because of the wide range, c0ratio 7.9. Also works as foam, cell-colony or hammered-metal texture with shallower depth.
[CraterField, nature-phenomena] Dense overlapping craters of many sizes, with old large craters degraded by small ones, like the lunar highlands. Hillshade from the own-cell, 9-octave prototype looks more convincing than the 3x3 window version.
ideas.why_new: CellularDistance F1 gives identical cone bowls with no rim, no size variation, no overlap logic. Every planet tool (Gaea Craterfield, KSP VoronoiCraters, Elite's geology inputs, World Creator) has a dedicated crater primitive; it is the first thing people try to fake with Worley and fail.
ideas.simd_plan:
Per-octave cost is one hash and one sqrt plus about 15 ops, so 9 octaves are estimated at 7-9 ns in any dimension (about 7x Perlin, 2x CellularDistance in 2D; under 1x in 3D; 0.2x in 4D). Use d*d rather than the prototype's pow. Base is a source evaluation only once.
[CraterField, stamp-scatter] Colour loop replaces offset loop; 1 hash and 1 profile per colour, with Selects. Per level 9/27/81 cells. Estimate 2D at L=3: 27 cell evals ~20 ns; 3D at L=2-3 (craters on planet surface from 3D position): 54-81 cells ~60-80 ns; 4D for tiling at L=2: 162 cells, ~180 ns. Justified as a specialist node. Uses Sqrt once per cell; no Pow per lane if the level table is computed at set time.
ideas.continuity: C0 verified: c0ratio 7.27-7.9. Each profile reaches zero weight by t=1, and t<1 is only possible within the window. Slope is bounded by Depth, so C1 fails only at the bowl-rim joint (could be smoothed).
ideas.params: Base Source (hybrid), Octaves (int), Lacunarity, Density Slope, Erase (0-1), Rim Height, Central Peak Radius, Ray Strength, Replay Octaves (int).
ideas.risks:
Not tested. Non-overlap constraint within an octave limits density and can give too-even spacing at the largest scale. Rays need a decent cheap angular function to avoid visible direction bands.
[CraterField, stamp-scatter] Colour 8 is always on top; I saw no 3-cell period in the FFT, but a very low density field might show it. Output is order-sensitive so GenPositionArray parity is fine, but an implementer must keep level and colour order constant across feature sets. Range needs a measured constant; proto clamps. Floor reference from Source at centres adds up to 3^dim evals per level, so make it optional.
[CraterField, nature-phenomena] Base terrain and profile amplitudes must be normalised over octaves; the range is not analytic if a source is attached. Lattice alignment of the coarsest octave may show at wide zoom. Size distribution is a hand-tuned power law, not a fitted Neukum function.
ideas.variant_notes: Five proposals of order-dependent crater overprint. Two ways of making order global: per-octave own-cell craters with no overlap inside an octave (cheapest, about 7-9 ns), or the colour-ordered window fold, which works for any non-commutative stamp. 3D on planet positions avoids polar distortion.
ideas.cost_note: Own-cell form: 9 octaves about 7-9 ns in any dimension (7x Perlin in 2D). With an ejecta window: 20-35 ns in 2D for 5 octaves plus 2 replays.

queue.name: CraterField
queue.reason: Own-cell bowls per octave remove ordering seams at 7-9 ns; planet tools all want this (J1, J2 top pick). Untested: check for over-even big craters and keep ejecta optional.

disp.how: Shape Crater

ideas.name: CrystalGrains
ideas.one_liner: Crystal grains grown from seeds: each grain has its own random orientation and polyhedral growth shape, and the field is arrival time of the growth front.
ideas.algorithm:
Window 3^dim, jittered sites. For each site: v = p-s_i; orient via two Householder reflections with normals from hash bit fields (v -= 2(n.v)n, twice), giving a rotation with no matrix table; gauge = Wulff shape norm of v, options cube max|v_i|, octahedron (sum|v_i|)/sqrt(3), rhombic dodecahedron max(|x|+|y|,|y|+|z|,|x|+|z|)/sqrt(2); T_i = gauge/(1 + Rate*rnd11) + T0*rnd01 (Johnson-Mehl-Avrami nucleation delay). T = min T_i, tracking second. Output enum: Time (T), Boundary (T2-T1), Zoned sin(T*Zones) for growth banding like agate or zoned feldspar, GrainValue. Normalise by a measured constant.

[CrystalGrainNoise, volumetric-3d4d] Window 3x3x3 (3x3 2D). Per cell k: h = Hash(k); c = k + 0.5 + Jitter*rnd3(h); tau = Delay * rnd01(h>>8); R = RotTable[(h>>12) & 31] (32 random rotation matrices from unit quaternions; 2D: 32 angles); speed v = 1 - SpeedJitter*rnd01(h>>17); habit = node enum or per-grain from bits.
 q = R * (p - c)
 norm: Sphere |q|; Cube Max(|qx|,|qy|,|qz|)*1.24; Octahedron (|qx|+|qy|+|qz|)*0.72; HexPrism Max( Max_j |q.d_j| (d_j at 0,60,120 deg in xy), |qz|*k ); RhombicDodeca Max over 6 normals (1,1,0)/sqrt2 perms of |q.n| (constants chosen so the unit ball volumes match the sphere)
 T = tau + norm / v
 keep T1, T2 (two-value insertion via Min/Max masks) and the hash of the T1 winner
Outputs enum: Age = T1 scaled over [0, Tmax]; Boundary = T2 - T1 (0 at grain walls); GrainValue = rnd11(winner); AgeInGrain = (T1 - tau_winner) (a faceted distance inside each crystal). Cap Delay <= 0.5 to keep the 3x3x3 window valid (same imprecision class as existing Cellular with full jitter).
ideas.look:
Prototyped. 3D isosurface T<0.15: clusters of sharp faceted rhombic-dodecahedral crystals in random orientations, the most striking render in this batch; superb for geodes, ice, gems, sci-fi crystals. 2D slice: angular pyramids with random tilted polygon shapes, each differently oriented; Zoned mode gives concentric tilted polygons like a Vasarely print or mineral thin-section. Threshold over time animates crystal growth with no 4D lattice.
[CrystalCells, nature-phenomena] Hillshade shows flat faces and straight creases, like cut gems, low-poly rock or quartz clusters, with nothing curved. Zoned output gives concentric pentagons and hexagons clipped by neighbours, like agate or zoned feldspar. The 3D isosurface should give faceted polyhedra, but that was not rendered.
ideas.why_new: Manhattan and MaxAxis metrics exist but share one global orientation, so all facets align (see the Cellular Manhattan tile, aligned diamonds). Per-grain orientation plus a Wulff gauge cannot be expressed by nodes, since metric rotation per cell is internal to the search. Growth delay gives curved grain boundaries that no existing jitter does.
ideas.simd_plan: Same window as CellularDistance plus two reflections per site (6 mul-adds and 3 hash field extractions per reflection) and abs/max for the gauge. No sqrt needed for the polyhedral gauge, offsetting some cost. Estimate 1.5x to 2x CellularDistance: 6 / 20 / 75 ns. Scalar prototype with quaternions was 9.65x perlin2, 4.3x worley2, and the reflections are cheaper. 4D is expensive but needed only for tiling; for animation use Time with threshold.
ideas.continuity: C0: a min of continuous functions. Dense scanlines: 0 jumps, worst step near zero. Creases are C0 by design.
ideas.params: Gauge enum, Rate (hybrid), T0 (hybrid), Zones (float), GridJitter, Output enum.
ideas.risks:
Window correctness: gauge can be smaller than Euclidean so a site outside the 3^dim window could win in rare cases; keep jitter <= 0.45 and rate moderate, then run seam check (none seen by eye). Rate spread is a size-limiting factor. Facets alias when thin; normals need sharp isosurface extraction, so meshers without feature preservation will round them.
[CrystalGrainNoise, volumetric-3d4d] Rotation table via gather is slow on SSE paths; use 8-entry Select trees. Delay > 0.5 makes window seams. Polyhedral norms are not Euclidean so AgeInGrain is faceted by design but Boundary walls get kinks.
[CrystalCells, nature-phenomena] Large delay can let a seed outside the window win, causing seams; keep delay within about 0.6 cell at 3x3 (the prototype used 0.6, and an earlier 5x5 run used 0.5). Per-cell 3D rotation choice affects look. Output range depends on face count and needs a measured constant. Johnson-Mehl literature covers tessellations in general; its use as a texture metric is my extension.
sources: from memory, not consulted: Johnson-Mehl tessellation (nucleation-time weighted Voronoi)
ideas.variant_notes: Johnson-Mehl arrival time with a rotated polyhedral norm. Rotation options: two Householder reflections (cheapest, WulffGrains), a table of matrices (CrystalGrainNoise), or one reflection (FacetGrowth, which gives the height-envelope view). Sweeping the iso-level animates growth with no 4D.
ideas.cost_note: Estimate 1.5x to 2x CellularDistance: 6 / 20 / 75 ns. Scalar prototype with quaternions was 9.65x perlin2, 4.3x worley2, and the reflections are cheaper.

ideas.name: CumulusNoise
ideas.one_liner: Bumps-on-bumps via surface projection: the nearest Cellular sphere is radially displaced by a finer Cellular dome field evaluated at the point's projection onto that sphere, recursively, giving true cauliflower florets and cumulus billows instead of FBm cusps.
ideas.algorithm:
Level 0: Cellular F1 search (3x3x3) at scale 1 returning nearest centre c0, its radius R0 (size jitter) and second-nearest (c0b, R0b, F2).
 n = normalize(p - c0); q = c0 + R0 * n                  // projection onto the parent sphere
 Level 1: Cellular F1 at scale s (Lacunarity, e.g. 3) evaluated at q (not p): nearest centre c1, radius R1; dome1 = Max(0, 1 - |q - c1|^2 / R1^2)   // round dome on the parent surface
 Level 2 (optional): n1 = normalize(q - c1); q2 = c1 + R1*n1; dome2 = dome at scale s^2 evaluated at q2
 Reff = R0 + Height*(dome1 + dome2/s)                     // displaced radius
 sdfA = |p - c0| - Reff
 Repeat the child evaluation for the second-nearest parent (c0b) -> sdfB; blend weight wb = SmoothStep(0, Blend, F2 - F1); sdf = Lerp(Min(sdfA, sdfB), sdfA, wb) (two parents keep the switch of nearest parent continuous).
Output: Signed sdf (scaled) or Density = Clamp(-sdf/Height) for volumetric clouds. 2D: circles with bumps (projection onto the circle, 2D cellular at q). 4D: w as phase for the cellular jitter (3D lattice) or true 4D lattices per level.
ideas.look: 3D iso: spheres covered with round sub-domes which are themselves covered with smaller domes: cauliflower, romanesco, cumulus congestus towers, brain coral, moss cushions. Unlike Perlin-Worley clouds (cusped, noisy) the florets are properly nested and round, with clean creases between them. 2D slice: lumpy discs with scalloped outlines, directly usable as cloud sprites or lichen patches.
ideas.why_new: FBm-of-inverted-Worley displaces throughout the volume, so bumps do not sit on the parent surface and successive octaves do not nest; the projection trick anchors each level to the surface below it, which no graph can do (needs the parent's centre and radius inside the child evaluation).
ideas.simd_plan: Three Cellular-style window searches (nearest centre + radius + distance) in sequence, with the two-parent blend doubling levels 1-2: 3D roughly 3-5x CellularDistance 3D (40-60 ns), 2D ~4x Cellular 2D (15 ns). All Select-based; normalize via InvSqrt. 4D: 3D lattice with w-phase jitter at the same cost; true 4D lattices would be ~5x Cellular 4D and are not recommended.
ideas.continuity: C0: the dome displacement and sphere union are continuous; the nearest-parent switch is smoothed by the F2-F1 blend (without it the field has small jumps in the gaps between parent spheres, the iso-surface at 0 usually not).
ideas.params: Levels (int 1-2), Lacunarity, Height (bump height fraction of R0), SizeJitter per level, Blend width, Output enum (Signed/Density), Feature Scale, Seed.
ideas.risks: Expensive; the two-parent blend only hides the switch near the Voronoi boundary of the two nearest parents, three-way corners can still show a kink. Child domes inherit the parent's spherical parametrisation so they stretch slightly near the parent's equator relative to lattice spacing.
ideas.cost_note: Three Cellular-style window searches (nearest centre + radius + distance) in sequence, with the two-parent blend doubling levels 1-2: 3D roughly 3-5x CellularDistance 3D (40-60 ns), 2D ~4x Cellular 2D (15 ns).

ideas.name: DendryNoise
ideas.one_liner: Distance to an implicit hierarchical tree built on the fly from jittered multi-resolution grids, each point linked toward its lowest-control neighbour: rivers, cracks, lightning, lichen, drainage networks (Gaillard et al. I3D 2019).
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Control C (GeneratorSource, e.g. low-frequency fbm = elevation), Levels L (int 1-4), Epsilon (jitter range 0..0.5), Displacement (float), Output enum {Distance, Elevation, Mask}, SlopeMin per level (floats).
Level-1 cell size s1 = 1 (Feature Scale), level l size s_l = s1/2^(l-1).
Point of cell c at level l: P_l(c) = (c + 0.5 + Epsilon*(rnd2(hash(seed,l,c))-0.5)) * s_l. Control value at a point: C(P) (a Source eval at another position; allowed).
Level 1 segments: for each coarse cell c, segment Seg1(c) = P1(c) -> P1(n*) where n* = argmin over the 3x3 neighbours n of C(P1(n)) (the lowest-elevation neighbour, 'water flows down'); if c itself is the minimum, zero-length segment (a local minimum = lake/sink). Optional displacement: bend midpoint perpendicular by Displacement*rnd (quadratic Bezier = cheap stand-in for the paper's Catmull-Rom subdivision).
Level l>1 segments: for each fine cell c at level l, its point P_l(c) connects to the nearest point on the nearest parent segment among the parent segments of the 3x3 parent cells around c (paper's 'Rivers' strategy: snap to A, B or the midpoint; 'NearestPoint' for cracks/lightning). A per-level SlopeMin raises child elevation so rivers only flow down.
Evaluation at p: for l in 1..L: for each cell c in the 3x3 window at level l: d = min(d, distToSegment(p, Seg_l(c))) (segments entirely determined by hashes + Control, so no state). Distance output: 1 - clamp(d/s1); Elevation: C(nearest segment point) + Slope*d (terrain with consistent valleys); Mask: d < Width.
Cost control: cache Control evals: level 1 needs C at the 5x5 coarse points (25 evals), level-2 connection needs only distances to already-built parent segments (no new C evals), so total Source evals = 25 regardless of L.
3D: extruded 2D (z enters the hash as a seed slice) by default; a true 3D variant with 3x3x3 windows and 125 control evals is possible but expensive.
ideas.look: Branching channel/river networks with consistent downhill topology, dry-mud and ceramic crack webs, Lichtenberg lightning, root/vein systems. No cellular variant on the sheet has connected tree topology (F2-F1 gives closed cells, not branches).
ideas.why_new: Connected, hierarchical, direction-consistent branching is impossible to build from Perlin/Cellular graphs; Dendry is the only known pointwise construction for it and it directly gives terrains with rivers that actually drain downhill (the control function decides the flow).
ideas.simd_plan:
All loops fixed size: 49 point generations, 25 argmins (branch-free compare+Select chains), 25 segment distances (~15 ops each with Select for clamped t), level 1 adds 25x9 projections. 2D estimate: level-0 ~2700 ops (~25x Perlin, ~30 ns), two levels ~60 ns. 3D: level 0 only, 3x3x3 window with the 5x5 rule replaced by Max Distance = 0.5 cell (27 points x (hash + control) + 27 argmin over 26 + 27 segment distances ~ 10x Perlin3D). 4D: no native support (fallback drops w; tiling not supported), state clearly.
[DendryNoise, lit-recent] All loops fixed: 25 Control evals at hashed points (batch them as one 25-wide Gen call per lane set), 9 x L segment-distance evaluations with Select for the argmin and snap logic. 2D ~ 25*Control + ~150 segment ops: with a cheap Control (Perlin) ~30-40x Perlin; acceptable for a 'make the hard thing easy' node, and GeneratorCache-friendly. 3D default = extrusion (cheap), true 3D flagged as 125 evals + 27*L segments.
ideas.continuity: C0: min of point-segment distances is continuous; segment endpoints depend only on hashes and on Control values at fixed points, so they do not change across the sample domain. Elevation output is continuous when Slope*d is used; Mask is binary.
ideas.params: Control (GeneratorSource), Levels (int), Epsilon (float), Displacement (float), Strategy enum {Rivers, NearestPoint, Angle}, SlopeMin (float), Width (hybrid, Mask), Output enum.
ideas.risks:
Window seams: a parent segment of a cell outside the 3x3 parent window can be nearer than any inside; mitigate by clamping segment length to one cell (Epsilon<=0.5 and connection to the 3x3 only) which the paper also relies on. Cost is high; 4D and true 3D questionable. The look depends strongly on Control quality.
[DendriticNoise, terrain-tools-engines] Expensive (one of the costliest nodes); control-field-driven flow direction means features of C's scale must be larger than the lattice or the tree fragments; a Source control costs ~50-75 evals per sample; no 4D.
ideas.variant_notes: Multi-level Dendry and its lite forms. The reference code is GPL-3.0, so implement from the paper. Source-driven control costs tens of evals per sample.
ideas.cost_note: About 30 ns at one level and 60 ns at two in 2D with a cheap control (25-50x Perlin); single-level 3D about 10x Perlin3D; no native 4D.

queue.name: DendryNoise
queue.reason: Rivers that follow a control field, which no cheaper entry offers. 49 control evals per level makes it a hero or bake node; see window seams and whether a cheap Control is enough. Reference code is GPL-3.0, so implement from the paper.

disp.how: the node, documented as a hero or bake node

ideas.name: DomeHeap
ideas.one_liner: Z-buffered piles of domes across several lattice levels, whose size jitter can be as extreme as you like and stay seamless, because each level's domes fit its own window.
ideas.algorithm:
best=0. For L=0..Levels-1: fr=Lac^L; for each lattice point in the 3^D window around p*fr: h=hash(seed+L*prime, cell). keep=rnd(h>>a)<Keep. s=seed position (full 0..1 jitter in the cell). r=Radius*(1-SizeJitter*rnd(h>>b)), required r<=1 so a dome cannot leave the window (a seed two cells away is at least 1 lattice unit from the sample). q=r*r-|p*fr-s|^2. z=Profile(q)*(1+HeightJitter*rnd(h>>c))/fr, where Profile is sqrt(q) for sphere, or q/r for a parabola with no sqrt. best=max(best, Select(keep and q>0, z, 0)). Output best normalised by (Radius*(1+HeightJitter)). This is a pointwise cousin of the dead leaves model, with height ordering instead of random layer order.

[PebbleNoise, lattice-kernels] Params: RadiusMin, RadiusMax (cells, <= 1 - Jitter/2), PointsPerCell K (1..3), Flatten (0..1), HeightJitter, Blend {Max, SmoothMax(k), SignedDistance}, Density (hybrid), Jitter.
Gen(p): c = floor(p); best = Floor (e.g. -1 or 0)
 for o in {-1,0,1}^dim, for j in 0..K-1 (fixed):
   h = hash(seed, c+o) * (j==0 ? 1 : OddConst_j) then remix
   q = c+o + 0.5 + Jitter*(rndvec(h)-0.5); r = p - q
   u = rnd01(h>>12); rho = RadiusMax * exp(-u * ln(RadiusMax/RadiusMin))   // log-uniform; Exp available; or rho = lerp(Min,Max,u^2)
   z = HeightJitter * rnd11(h>>20)
   cap = z + Flatten * sqrt(max(0, rho^2 - |r|^2))        // exact sphere profile, 0 outside
   alive = (h>>24) < Density*256
   Max:      best = max(best, Select(alive, cap, Floor))
   SmoothMax: best = best + log1p-free softmax: use MaxSmooth formula from Blends with smoothness k
   SignedDistance (3D volumes): best = min(best, |r| - rho) (union-of-balls SDF)
 value = ScaleOutput(best, Floor, RadiusMax + HeightJitter).
ideas.look:
Boulder fields, pebble beaches, bubbles, caviar, cell clusters, with large rounded forms partly burying smaller ones. In 3D the union of balls can be thresholded for rocky volumes.
[PebbleNoise, lattice-kernels] Heightfield of packed stones: each feature is a true hemisphere/ellipsoid with a vertical tangent at its rim, big ones half-burying small ones, sizes spread over a decade. Jitter 0 + equal radii = cobblestones; small radii + K=3 = gravel; Flatten 0.3 = river stones; SmoothMax = pebbles under a sand drape; SignedDistance in 3D sliced = conglomerate/breccia rock with circular clasts of mixed size; also bubble wrap, frog spawn, foam.
ideas.why_new: Per-cell radius in CellularDistance is limited to about one cell size and yields one scale. Stacking levels gets a real power-law size distribution with occlusion, unlike additive octaves, where small things sit on big ones and never get buried. Graph versions with MaxSmooth need one Cellular per level and cannot do per-dome radius or height.
ideas.simd_plan: Levels x 3^D distance evaluations, with Max only and no id tracking. Using the parabola profile saves one sqrt per candidate. About 3.5 ns per level in 2D, 11 in 3D, 38 in 4D; 4 levels is 14 / 44 / 150 ns. In 4D recommend at most 3 levels.
ideas.continuity: C0. Each dome reaches 0 at its rim, so max is continuous. Sphere profile has vertical tangents at the rim (c0ratio 3.31, high slope); parabola has finite slope. An early version with a height pedestal jumped, so height must multiply the profile, never be added to it.
ideas.params: Levels (int), Lacunarity, Radius, Size Jitter, Height Jitter, Keep (hash probability), Profile enum, plus Size Slope mapping L to Keep so artists set the pebble-to-boulder ratio.
ideas.risks:
The 4D cost is heavy. The background reads flat where Keep is small. Hybrid radius at the pixel would be continuous but stops being a fixed sphere; radius should stay per seed.
[PebbleNoise, lattice-kernels] Log-uniform radii + small RadiusMin leaves bare floor between stones unless K>=2; coverage must be tuned. Max-union is not physically stacked (small stones can poke through big ones when z jitter is large). Vertical rims produce aliasing in hillshade at low Feature Scale.
ideas.variant_notes: Max of domes. Levels=1 with log-uniform radii is PebbleNoise, which adds an SDF output for 3D conglomerate.
ideas.cost_note: About 3.5 ns per level in 2D, 11 in 3D, 38 in 4D; 4 levels is 14 / 44 / 150 ns.

ideas.name: EdgeFateCells
ideas.one_liner: Voronoi using true bisector distances and a commutative per-edge hash, so each wall gets its own width, depth or absence: real crack networks, rounded pebbles, curled mud plates.
ideas.algorithm: Pass 1: F1 search in 3x3 giving site a, hash ha and cell index. Pass 2: for neighbours b of the F1 cell, n=norm(b-a), d_b=dot(mid(a,b)-p,n) (true distance to that bisector, positive). Edge hash e=mix(ha ^ hb) is symmetric, so both sides agree. Fate=rnd(e): an edge exists if fate>Drop, with width w_e=W*(.25+.75*rnd(mix e)). Modes: Crack: c=Max over live edges of (1-d_b/w_e), output profile of c. Pebble: soft distance sd=(sum d_b^-p)^(-1/p) with p=4,6,8 (order independent), t=sat((sd-Gap)/Dome), height sqrt(t*(2-t))*tone(ha). Plate: per-cell tilted plane tone(ha)+dot(tilt(ha),p-a)+Curl*(1-sat(sd/Rim)), then lerp toward CrackDepth by c. Lattice enum: Square, Staggered (row offset 0.5 gives honeycomb and hex tile at low jitter).
ideas.look: Look-tested (m=4). Dropped edges make non-convex polygons and dangling crack ends, which reads far more like dried mud or glaze crazing than F2-F1. Width varies per crack and stays constant along it. Pebble mode gives rounded stones with clean gaps; plate mode gives raised curled tiles with sharp fractures. Covers leather (pebble with low Dome and warp), stucco, cobbles, hex tiles.
ideas.why_new: F2-F1 is not a true distance, so its walls change width along their length, and it has no notion of an edge as an object. The symmetric pair hash is the new primitive: per-edge attributes without any global data. The reciprocal power sum gives rounded polygons without smin ordering artifacts.
ideas.simd_plan: Pass 1 is 9 candidates as today. Pass 2 uses 8 neighbours around per-lane F1 index (hash from lane integer coords works). Total 17 distance-class evals, about 2x CellularDistance 2D (scalar proto used 24 neighbours and measured 10x Perlin). 3D: 27+26 evals, about 2x CellularDistance 3D. 4D: 81+80, about 2x CellularDistance 4D, expensive but works, so tiling is real. d^-p by multiplication; root via Sqrt chain for p=4 and 8. Jitter must be limited so 8 neighbours suffice, or expose Quality for 24.
ideas.continuity: Crack and Pebble are C0 apart from tiny jumps near triple points where a live edge term differs between sides (measured c0ratio 1.25 cracks at very high slope, 2.83 pebbles). Plate is discontinuous across dropped edges only (plates differ there) and hidden under cracks at live edges. Merging tone across dropped edges is not possible pointwise.
ideas.params: Mode enum, Edge Drop, Crack Width, Width Jitter, Soft Power, Gap, Dome, Tilt, Curl, Lattice enum, Grid Jitter. Hybrid: Edge Drop, Crack Width, Gap, Dome.
ideas.risks: Dropped edge makes crack ends blunt, cut off at the vertex, rather than tapering. Could taper by fading width toward the vertex using F3-F2. Cost is double cellular. With high jitter, neighbours beyond the 8 cell ring can be missed, which only shows as minor misses in the soft sum.
ideas.cost_note: Total 17 distance-class evals, about 2x CellularDistance 2D (scalar proto used 24 neighbours and measured 10x Perlin).

queue.name: EdgeFateCells
queue.reason: Symmetric pair hash gives each wall its own width or removes it: dangling cracks and non-convex plates. Reuses the edge-distance pass; absorbs cellular-fracture.

disp.how: hybrid Edge Width and Depth plus Colours; the per-wall Edge Drop goes, it jumps

ideas.name: FanField
ideas.one_liner: Front-anchored oriented stamps: features are kept only where a mask source crosses a level at the feature point and are oriented along the mask's downhill gradient there, producing alluvial fans and bajadas along mountain fronts (or cirques, deltas and landslide tongues with other profiles).
ideas.algorithm: Mask source M (e.g. the continent/mountain noise), Level c, Band b. Jittered lattice, (2R+1)^2 window with R=2 (fan length up to 2 cells). Per cell point q: m0 = M(q), gate g = 1 - smoothstep(0, b, |m0 - c|) (apex lies on the front); if g>0 (mask arithmetic, no branch): gradient at q by forward differences (dim extra M evals), axis u = -grad/|grad| (downhill of the mask). d = p - q, r = |d|, cosang = dot(d,u)/r. sector = smoothstep(cosw-0.25, cosw+0.25, cosang) blended to 1 near the apex (sat(r/0.08)) so the apex is isotropic. Length L = Length*(0.6+0.8*rnd); profile = exp(-2 r/L) * (1 - smoothstep(0.6L, L, r)) * (1 - 0.5*sat(1 - r/(0.25L))) (concave-up, rounded apex, toe fades); lobes = 1 + 0.15*ringnoise(angle, 10, h)*sat(r/0.3L) (distributary channels, see PolarCells). fan = max over cells of g*Height*sector*profile*lobes. Output max(mountain, fan + plain) where mountain = max(0, M)*scale, or output the fan field alone for Add in a graph. Kinds: Fan (sector 50-70 degrees), Cirque (uphill half-bowl: u = +grad, bowl profile), Delta (fan with Level = sea level), Tongue (narrow sector, flat top).
ideas.look: Scalloped aprons of coalescing cones spreading from the mountain front onto the plain, concave-up, with faint distributary ridges; apexes only where the front is. Prototyped: fans (c0 7.8 after feathering). The look is still subtle at the prototype's density (many small fans); fewer, longer fans with a sharper mountain front read better.
ideas.why_new: Stamps exist in sibling lenses and hybrids let a mask scale a stamp, but hybrids are sampled at the current position, not at the feature point, so a graph cannot say 'place this feature only on the contour and point it downhill'. Sampling the mask (and its gradient) at the feature point is the trick that makes placement and orientation coherent per feature.
ideas.simd_plan: 25 cells x (1 + dim) mask evaluations in 2D (75 Perlin ~85 ns) plus per-cell Sqrt, Exp, a polynomial atan2 for lobes (optional). Cost cut: evaluate the gate first for all 25 cells (25 evals) and only compute gradients for cells where any lane is gated (masked, still constant loop). 3D: 125 cells x 4 evals, too heavy except with R=1 (27 x 4 = 108). 4D: not planned. Realistic tier: 2D terrain node, 20-90x Perlin depending on mask source.
ideas.continuity: C0: gate, sector, profile and lobes are all smooth in p; max over a fixed window. Measured 7.79. Seams if Length > R cells.
ideas.params: Mask Source, Level, Band, Length, Height, Half Angle, Kind enum, Lobes, Jitter, Include Mask bool (output composite or fan field only).
ideas.risks: Medium confidence on the look: needs tuning of density vs. front scale, and fans should merge smoothly (smooth max). Mask gradient at the apex can point along the front when the front is wiggly, orienting a fan sideways. Expensive with multi-octave masks; recommend a GeneratorCache'd low-octave mask.
ideas.cost_note: 25 cells x (1 + dim) mask evaluations in 2D (75 Perlin ~85 ns) plus per-cell Sqrt, Exp, a polynomial atan2 for lobes (optional).

ideas.name: FlowNetwork
ideas.one_liner: Pointwise dendritic river and root networks: each lattice node picks one downstream neighbour with a hash bit, so a real branching tree emerges with no heights, sinks or global pass.
ideas.algorithm: Coalescing random walks (the Scheidegger river model; the model is from memory, not a consulted source). Brick lattice, rows j along the flow axis. Node position n(i,j) = (i + 0.5 + 0.5*(j&1) + J*(rx-0.5), j + 0.5 + J*(ry-0.5)). Child of (i,j) is in row j-1: column i+b for odd j, i-1+b for even j, b = one hash bit, optionally biased. Edge = segment n(i,j) to n(child). Field: min over window of segment distance d divided by width(Q). Window: rows cj-1..cj+2, columns ci-2..ci+2 (20 edges, as in the prototype, safe up to J=1 and cutoff 1 cell), or 3 rows by 4 columns (12 edges) if J<=0.5 and cutoff<=0.25. Discharge Q (optional depth K): count upstream nodes draining through a node with a row DP, m[r+1] = ((m[r]<<1) & ~B[r+1]) | (m[r] & B[r+1]) with parity adjust, Q = sum popcount(m[r]). B is a single 32-bit hash word holding the direction bits of 32 columns in a row. width = w0*(1 + grow*sqrt(lerp(Qa,Qb,t)-1)) with t the projection along the edge. Outputs: Distance, RiverMask, Order (log Q at the nearest edge). 3D: flow along one axis with 2 bits choosing among 4 children, giving tube networks. 4D: 3 bits, 8 children.
ideas.look:
Branching drainage trees with tributaries merging into wider trunks. Unlike anything on the contact sheet, whose line features are all closed cell walls or loops. Prototype K=4 grow 0.6 gives clear trunk and twig hierarchy. With fractal simplex warp (K=8, warp 0.7) the straight segments become convincing rivers. For river carving, roots, lightning, cracks with direction, vein networks, 3D root and cave systems.
[LatticeGraph (DrainageTree + BondNet), lattice-kernels] Drainage basins, roots, lightning, veins, mycelium; bonds give trusses, scaffolds, road or PCB nets. Prototyped: real dendritic merging with thicker trunks, all flowing one way; very unlike anything on the contact sheet. Hillshade of negated output carves valleys.
ideas.why_new: Rivers are the classic gap. Voxel Tools docs and a Godot voxel write-up both describe rivers as squared or absolute noise or Worley edges, which give closed loops with no tributaries and no flow. Dendry solves the tree pointwise but needs 9x9 points and a 7x7 lowest-neighbour pass per level plus control function evaluations (read in its code; the paper's own abstract reports about 10 s for a 512x512 grid on a quad core). It is also GPL-3.0. This keeps the tree topology with one bit per node and is cheap enough for SIMD. Graphs cannot express it: tree topology needs per-cell link information.
ideas.simd_plan: Fixed window, one hash per node, direction bit taken from the same hash. Segment distance is dot, clamp and one divide per edge, kept branch free with Min. Discharge uses the row-word trick so K rows need about K+window word hashes plus bit ops per node, popcount via SWAR, all integer lane ops. Scalar prototype K=0 with the 20-edge window: 4.4x perlin2, 2x its 5x5 worley2. Estimated AVX2: 2D 12 to 20 ns K=0, 25 to 35 ns K=8. 3D 50 to 80 ns (27 to 48 edges). Above the 5x Perlin guideline; justified as there is no cheap alternative for this topology.
ideas.continuity: Distance is C0 with medial-axis creases, like F1. Width interpolates along each edge, so RiverMask is C0 (measured c0ratio 8.0 at K=0, 6.8 at K=4 unwarped; 8.3 with warp). Direction bits never change output discontinuously because every edge is present in the window.
ideas.params: Feature Scale, Jitter, Direction Bias (hybrid), Width and Width Growth (hybrid), Discharge Depth K (int, loop count), Max Distance, Output enum.
ideas.risks:
Single global flow axis: rivers do not follow terrain downhill. Use DomainRotate, a warp, or a polar map, and carve the terrain with the mask rather than the reverse.
