Independent octaves cross each other (seen in the oct=2 prototype, a cross-hatch), so hierarchical tributaries need a parity-refined lattice, which is unsolved here. A 2D slice of the 3D or 4D form shows dashes and dots, and hypertorus tiling is not meaningful; tile by wrapping the lattice instead. Discharge width steps visibly if K is small. The 5x Perlin budget is exceeded.
[LatticeGraph (DrainageTree + BondNet), lattice-kernels] Lattice angles show at low jitter: segments look zig-zag (prototype visible). Fix with Jitter about 0.45 or a small warp. True flow accumulation is not available pointwise, so very long trunks do not keep thickening; octave stacking at 2x scale helps. No consistent downhill height in the output.
ideas.variant_notes: Scheidegger coalescing walks: one hash bit per node with discharge by row word DP. Triangular-lattice form from LatticeGraph. Single global flow axis.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated AVX2: 2D 12 to 20 ns K=0, 25 to 35 ns K=8. 3D 50 to 80 ns (27 to 48 edges).

queue.name: FlowNetwork
queue.reason: Cheapest true river tree at ~10 ns, and the earlier proto shows real dendrites from hashes alone (J2 top pick). Hide the global flow axis with a warp or polar map.

ideas.name: FlowShingle
ideas.one_liner: Overlapping oriented stamps where stacking order is the projection of each stamp centre onto the local flow, and only the winning stamp evaluates a source in its own frame: scales, feathers, roof tiles, trowel strokes.
ideas.algorithm: Lane dir d=(cos th,sin th) from hybrid Angle. For each candidate cell: centre c (stagger plus jitter), r=p-c, v=dot(r,d), u=dot(r,perp d), both divided by per-stamp size. Optional curvature v+=Bend*rnd*u^2 and chevron v+=Chevron*|u|. Inside test by Shape: Scale (u^2/a^2 + (v/(v>0?b:.55b))^2 <1), Stroke (max(|v|/b,|u|/w)<1), Disc. Priority = -dot(c,d) + PJ*rnd. Keep the highest-priority covering stamp: mask = inside AND prio>best, then Select best, u, v, hash. After the loop, one evaluation of optional Interior source at (u*Su+off_u(h), v*Sv+off_v(h)). Output = tilt profile (0.5-0.5*v/b for Scale; flat with raised rim for Stroke) + Detail*Interior + tone(h). Lanes with no stamp return Base.
ideas.look:
Look-tested (m=8). Fish or dragon scales with fine barbs that flow around a field and always overlap the right way, plus palette-knife stucco strokes with shape=1 and bend. Hard occluding edges give a hillshade no blend can produce. Chevron plus stretched Interior gives feathers; Stroke with low detail gives plaster; Disc with Min composite gives hammered dents.
[ShingleStack, cell-relations] Roof shingles, fish or dragon scales, pine cone, leaf litter, overlapping river pebbles, stacked plates. Hillshade has occlusion edges and T-junction overlaps that Voronoi cannot produce. Prototyped: rel_shingle flow=0 and flow=2.5.
ideas.why_new: Texture bombing has a fixed order or per-cell priority, so a flow-following shingle needs per-region ordering. Here the order comes from a float comparison computed per lane, so overlap direction follows the field automatically and any orientation works. The single post-selection eval keeps source cost at 1 regardless of window, which makes rich stamp interiors affordable, where CellularLookup only gives a constant per cell.
ideas.simd_plan: Masked loop, no per-candidate source. 2D: 4x4 window centred on the nearest lattice vertex (16 candidates, reach at least 1.5, stamps up to about 1.2 fit); 9 candidates only if stamp reach is below 1-jitter/2. About 1.5x CellularDistance plus 1 Interior: scalar 7x Perlin including the interior simplex. 3D: 27 candidates, ellipsoid stamps with reach below 0.8 and axis from Angle plus Tilt, about 1.5x CellularDistance 3D. 4D: 81 candidates, 4x CellularDistance 3D, Scale shape only.
ideas.continuity: Discontinuous by design at stamp edges (occlusion steps). Inside a stamp, continuous except where a fast-changing Angle reorders priorities. The look depends on hard edges, and a Softness option can fade the step over the last 10% of the stamp if C0 is needed.
ideas.params: Angle, Tilt, Size, Size Jitter, Bend, Chevron, Priority Jitter, Shape enum, Interior (generator), Interior Scale U/V, Detail, Base. Hybrid: Angle, Tilt, Size, Detail.
ideas.risks:
The proto used a 3x3 window with reach above 1, so small seams are possible; the port needs the 4x4 window. Coverage holes appear if Size is too small (visible black gaps in stroke mode). Rapidly curling fields can produce popping priority flips. Feature size is capped by the window.
[ShingleStack, cell-relations] Rare uncovered gaps appear as specks at r below coverage limit (seen in proto). The directional look in 3D needs a 3D direction, and in 4D tiling the direction has no clean meaning. Hillshade of discontinuous output is harsh as raw terrain.
ideas.variant_notes: Same priority-plane idea in both. FlowShingle adds a post-selection Interior source at one eval, plus bend and chevron shapes.
ideas.cost_note: About 1.5x CellularDistance plus 1 Interior: scalar 7x Perlin including the interior simplex.

ideas.name: GiniFoam
ideas.one_liner: Foam field from how evenly a point is shared between nearby sites: smooth, no sorting, with Plateau-border thickening at junctions and curved pressure walls.
ideas.algorithm: Lattice: jittered sites as CellularDistance, window 3^dim. For each site i: d2 = |p-s_i|^2; r_i = 1 + Pressure*rnd11(hash bits), rr = r_i^2; a_i = max(rr/(d2+1e-3) - rr/Rc^2, 0) (Franke-Little form, compact at Rc); w_i = a_i^k with integer k by repeated squaring (k=4). Rc must not exceed the distance to the nearest site outside the window: Rc = 1.1 for jitter radius 0.4 (GridJitter 0.8). S1 = sum w_i, S2 = sum w_i^2. g = (S1^2 - S2)/(S1^2 + eps). g is 0 inside a cell, 1/2 on a two-cell wall, 2/3 on a three-cell edge, 3/4 at a four-cell vertex, because it is the Gini-Simpson participation index of the Shepard membership p_i = w_i/S1. Output ScaleOutput(g, 0, 0.75). Pressure gives multiplicative weights, so walls become spherical Apollonius caps and small bubbles bulge into large ones, as Young-Laplace predicts. A threshold on g gives a wall thickness that grows at junctions by itself.
ideas.look: Prototyped. 2D: bubble raft, thin soft bright walls that flare at triple junctions, small round bubbles sitting on large ones (press 0.5 to 0.9). 3D slice: round bubble cross-sections with soft membranes. 3D isosurface: g<0.2 gives pebble-like polygonal bubble cells with narrow gaps; g>0.2 gives open-cell foam or metal-foam struts. Use for foam, sea foam, bone, soap films, cell tissue, cloud cell masks. w animates sites and pressures.
ideas.why_new: F2-F1 has creases, flat walls and no junction thickening, and needs sorting. A soft wall needs F1..F4 together, which CellularDistance cannot combine. The Gini field has 3 and 4 cell information with no sort, so it is a single smooth value with no crease inside walls. Clearly unlike the CellularDistance tiles on the contact sheet.
ideas.simd_plan: Plain window loop, no masks for sorting, one div per site plus k squarings, just S1 and S2 accumulators. Fully dimension agnostic. Scalar 2D prototype 1.57x perlin2, 0.71x worley2. Estimate AVX2 about 0.8x to 1.2x CellularDistance: 3 / 10 / 35 ns for 2D / 3D / 4D.
ideas.continuity: C0 with bounded slope, smooth almost everywhere: all weights fall to 0 at Rc and the ratio is smooth. Check at jitter 0.7 gave c0ratio 7.98, max slope 67 per unit, no NaN.
ideas.params: Pressure (hybrid), Sharpness k (int), GridJitter (hybrid only if Rc is derived from the maximum), Output: Gini or Entropy. Feature Scale, Seed, Output Min/Max mixins.
ideas.risks: When only a few sites lie inside Rc the ratio can form small fan-shaped wedges: seen with the first (1-d2/R2)^3 taper at jitter 0.8, much less with Franke-Little at jitter 0.7, and absent with a 5^dim window. High pressure (0.9) gives sharp thin lines. Range is slightly above nominal (about 1.08 after scaling) when using 0.75 max with a free gain; choose a measured constant.
ideas.cost_note: Scalar 2D prototype 1.57x perlin2, 0.71x worley2. Estimate AVX2 about 0.8x to 1.2x CellularDistance: 3 / 10 / 35 ns for 2D / 3D / 4D.

ideas.name: GradedVoronoi
ideas.one_liner: Voronoi whose cell size follows a source node continuously across any size range, with no shear or seams, for the price of two cellular searches.
ideas.algorithm: Inputs: hybrid Level l(p) in [0, Levels-1). L=floor(l). For j in {0,1}: fr=Base*Ratio^(L+j) (per lane); search the 3^D window at p*fr with seed+(L+j)*prime, giving F1_j, F2_j in that level's own lattice units and hash h_j. Penalty pen_j=k*|L+j-l|. Candidates are F1_j+pen_j and F2_j+pen_j. b1 and b2 are the smallest and second smallest candidates, id is the hash of b1. Output: CellValue=rnd(id), Crack=sat((b2-b1)*gain), Pillow=rnd(id)*smoothstep(0,w,b2-b1). Why two searches are enough: when l crosses an integer the search set changes from {L,L+1} to {L+1,L+2}. At that moment the outgoing and incoming levels both carry penalty k, so k above the largest F2 (about 1.6) means neither can win. Proto mode 7 searches all levels and mode 13 searches two. Both give c0ratio 8.00 at k about 1.5-1.6 and look the same.
ideas.look: Cells grade smoothly from huge to tiny, with fine cells budding along the boundary of large ones. Reads like graded sediment, cracked mud that tightens near a river, or foam. Good for biome-driven rock size, paving, skin scales and masks.
ideas.why_new: Today, a per-pixel scale on a lattice shears, and Size Jitter is limited by the window. Fade across fixed scales needs one Cellular per scale and cross-dissolves the patterns instead of making real cell boundaries. Here the boundaries are real across scales and the cost does not depend on the level range.
ideas.simd_plan: No lane branching. The lattice frequency is just a per-lane float, so lanes can sit on different levels. Each search is a normal CellularDistance F1/F2 pass; the merge is Min/Select on floats and ids. Cost is 2x CellularDistance plus one Level eval: about 8 / 24 / 82 ns for 2D/3D/4D, or about 7x Perlin in 2D. Dimension agnostic.
ideas.continuity: C0 (c0ratio 8.00 with the 5x5 proto window) for Crack and Pillow, because b1 and b2 are order statistics of continuous values. CellValue is deliberately discontinuous at cell borders only.
ideas.params: Level (hybrid), Levels range, Base Scale, Ratio (default 2), Blend k (lower lets levels mix but then needs more searches), Jitter, Output enum, Distance function.
ideas.risks: The proto used a 5x5 window, so 3x3 F2 errors at jitter 1 may show as small jumps at level changes; test at Jitter 0.8-1. Below the k limit, seams appear on integer crossings of Level. A steep Level gradient compresses the transition band.
ideas.cost_note: Cost is 2x CellularDistance plus one Level eval: about 8 / 24 / 82 ns for 2D/3D/4D, or about 7x Perlin in 2D.

ideas.name: GradientMetricCellular
ideas.one_liner: Cellular distance using a per-lane metric stretched by a sampled gradient, so cells flow along any field's contours with no displacement.
ideas.algorithm: g from guide stencil at p. Standard CellularDistance window search, with distance d^2 = |dp|^2 + B (dp.g)^2/(|g|^2+e), where dp = site - p, B = k-1 >= 0. No frame needed in any dimension. Use F1, F2-F1, etc. as usual. e fades the anisotropy where the guide is flat, which removes the direction singularity. Enum for the slope-aligned version: |dp|^2 + B(|dp|^2 - (dp.g)^2/(|g|^2+e)).
ideas.look: F2-F1 gives long fibrous cells bundled along the guide's contours, closing in loops around its extrema: bark, muscle, stretched scales, drawn-out mud cracks. F1 gives flowing wood-like streaks. Contrast with Warped Cellular on the contact sheet: cells there are bent but keep rounded proportions, while these are consistently elongated in a controlled direction.
ideas.why_new: Directional stretch whose amount and direction you can dial and paint, independent of position, with sites unmoved. Lets cell patterns align to terrain contours. A warp cannot produce a controlled uniform aspect ratio. Because the metric is evaluated at the sample and dp is bounded by the window, there is no far-origin shear.
ideas.simd_plan: Same window as CellularDistance plus (D+1) taps once per lane, one extra dot and mul per candidate. 2D 3.3+3.9 = about 7 ns, 3D 8.8+12 = about 21 ns, 4D 21.5+41 = about 62 ns on a Perlin guide. Metric computed once before the window loop.
ideas.continuity: Same class as CellularDistance. Measured c0ratio 6.73 at k=5 with a 3x3 window, and the 5x5 window gave the same mean and ratio, so window truncation was not visible at that k. Discontinuity would appear at extreme k, where a far site should beat every window site.
ideas.params: Stretch k (hybrid, >=1; shrink is disallowed since it would need a larger window), Alignment enum, Guide source, Sample Distance h, usual Cellular members.
ideas.risks: Seams at k well above about 8 from window truncation, needing a clamp or documented limit. This is not a true anisotropic Voronoi with a metric at the site, so cell shapes vary slightly with the sample point, but this was not noticeable.
ideas.cost_note: 2D 3.3+3.9 = about 7 ns, 3D 8.8+12 = about 21 ns, 4D 21.5+41 = about 62 ns on a Perlin guide.

ideas.name: HardCoreCellular
ideas.one_liner: Rank each cell's hash among its 3^d neighbours: exactly uniform per-cell ranks, and the top-rank cells form a hard-core (Matern-like) point set with guaranteed minimum spacing, giving spots that never touch at exact density and a blue-noise scatter with a hard guarantee.
ideas.algorithm:
h_c = Hash(seed, c) for integer cells.
rank_c = sum over the 3^d - 1 neighbours n of c of [h_n < h_c]  in {0 .. 3^d - 1};  u_c = rank_c / (3^d - 1).
Facts: P(rank_c = r) = 1/3^d exactly for every r (ties negligible with 32-bit hashes); two cells with rank = 3^d - 1 (local maxima of the hash) can never be adjacent (each would have to beat the other), so top cells have Chebyshev spacing >= 2 and density exactly 1/3^d per cell; more generally no 3^d block holds more than (3^d - R) cells of rank >= R.
Modes:
  Rank: out = 2 u_{floor(x)} - 1 (cellular steps, like CellularValue but with anti-correlated neighbours).
  Smooth: quintic tensor interpolation of u over the 2^d cell centres around x (needs a 4^d block of hashes).
  HardCoreDistance: feature point p_c = c + 0.5 + Jitter*rnd11*0.5 for cells with rank_c >= RankMin (others masked to +inf); out = F1 distance to the nearest selected point over the 3^d window (ranks of those cells need the 5^d hash block). With RankMin = 3^d - 1 and Jitter j the selected points are at least 2 - j cells apart, so thresholding F1 at radius r < 1 - j/2 gives discs that never overlap, at exactly 1/3^d points per cell.
ideas.look: Rank mode: a cellular mosaic where bright cells are always surrounded by darker ones (a checker-like, 'dappled' anti-clustered mosaic unlike CellularValue's random clumps). Smooth: an even, bumpy field whose peaks are spaced >= 2 cells apart, with no large bright or dark regions. HardCoreDistance thresholded: evenly spread, non-touching discs (lichen patches, craters that do not overlap, tree crowns, bubbles, rivets); hillshade: a bed of separate domes at even spacing. Versus CellularDistance F1 the discs never merge and the count per area is exact.
ideas.why_new: CellularDistance/CellularValue points are Poisson-like per cell: discs merge, densities fluctuate, and thinning them (CellularValue < p) breaks the spacing. Blue-noise point sets with a minimum distance are exactly what scattering needs, and FastNoise cannot produce one; this does it from hashes alone, pointwise, with a provable spacing and exact density, and the Smooth mode is a coherent noise whose maxima are guaranteed separated (one extremum per 3^d block at most).
ideas.simd_plan: Hash-only inner loops: Rank 2D = 9 hashes, Smooth 2D = 4x4 block = 16 hashes with the 9 compares per centre done on the block (3D 64, 4D 256 hashes); HardCoreDistance = 5^d hashes (25 / 125 / 625) + 3^d distance tests. Each hash ~6 int ops, so 2D Smooth ~1x Perlin, 3D Smooth ~1.5x Perlin 3D, 2D Distance ~1.3x CellularDistance, 3D ~1.6x, 4D ~2x (heavy, like all 4D cellular). Compares are int masks summed with Masked adds; all branch-free.
ideas.continuity: Rank: discontinuous (cell steps, by design); Smooth: C2; HardCoreDistance: C0 (F1-type kinks), continuous across cells because masked points simply drop out of the min.
ideas.params: Mode enum (Rank, Smooth, HardCoreDistance); Rank Min (int 0..3^d-1, controls density: top rank = 1/3^d); Jitter; Feature Scale; Seed Offset; Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks: Hash-count explosion in 4D distance mode. Spacing guarantee is in cells, so with Jitter near 1 the Euclidean guarantee weakens (2 - j). Top-rank density 1/9 (2D) is fixed; lower RankMin trades density for a weaker clustering bound. The 'uniform rank' property holds per cell, not for the Smooth field.
ideas.cost_note: Each hash ~6 int ops, so 2D Smooth ~1x Perlin, 3D Smooth ~1.5x Perlin 3D, 2D Distance ~1.3x CellularDistance, 3D ~1.6x, 4D ~2x (heavy, like all 4D cellular).

ideas.name: LavaColumns
ideas.one_liner: Metaballs that actually move: columns scroll at different integer speeds so blobs rise, pass, merge and split, with exact time loop at 3D cost.
ideas.algorithm: Vertical axis y, Time = w in 4D or hybrid Time param in 3D. For each column in 3x3 (x,z): hc = hash(col); v = table {+1,+2,+3,-1}[hc bits]; ys = y - v*Time*P/(2*pi); iy = floor(ys). For dy in {-1,0,1}: h = hash(col, (iy+dy) mod P); site s = (col_x + jx, iy+dy + jy, col_z + jz) + Sway*(sin(Time+ph), 0, cos(Time+ph)) with sway sine pre-computed once per lane and rotated by table ph; r = r0*(0.5+rnd01); d2 relative to (x, ys, z); k = max(1 - d2/(r*r), 0); S += k^3. Output 1-exp(-S*g) or S/(S+1), scaled. Because hash uses iy mod P and v is an integer, Time=2 pi shifts each column by exact multiple of P, so loop is exact. Mixed-sign v gives rising and sinking blobs. Keep r <= 1.0 plus sway so kernels fit the 3x3 columns.
ideas.look: Not prototyped. Expected in 3D iso: smooth round blobs with soft necks that stretch and pinch while rising. 2D (x,y) slice: oil-droplet discs and bridges with teardrops in motion. Static frame looks like metaballs, animation is the point: real topology change caused by motion rather than 4D boiling. For lava lamps, magma, oil, cell motion, slime.
ideas.why_new: Moving w through 4D Cellular or Simplex makes features fade in place, not travel. Translating the whole domain moves everything rigidly. Independent column speeds give relative motion, which is what makes blobs merge and split, at 3D window cost instead of a 4D window, and a built-in exact loop. Can't be done in a graph since per-column offsets occur inside the window.
ideas.simd_plan: Loop 9 columns x 3 y cells = 27 kernels in 3D, no sqrt: estimate 7 to 10 ns; can trim to 2 y cells by half-offset to reach 18 kernels. 4D same cost as 3D (vs 41 ns for 4D CellularDistance). 2D: 3 columns x 3 = 9 kernels, under 3 ns with Time. Mod P via AND with power-of-two P. Single sin and cos per lane, phase offsets from a small table.
ideas.continuity: C2 from compact (1-d2/r2)^3 kernel with the window containing all contributions; output map smooth. Continuous in time as well.
ideas.params: Time (hybrid, or w), Radius (hybrid), Density gain, Sway, Period P (int, power of two), Axis enum (optional).
ideas.risks: Untested. Vertical period P cells is visible if small, so P>=8. Vertical axis is privileged: columns may read as streams if speeds are too uniform. GenTileable: 4D mapping is continuous, but w on the torus does not mean time. Hybrid Radius varying per lane breaks kernel fit if above limit, so clamp.
ideas.cost_note: Loop 9 columns x 3 y cells = 27 kernels in 3D, no sqrt: estimate 7 to 10 ns; can trim to 2 y cells by half-offset to reach 18 kernels.

ideas.name: LevelDendrite
ideas.one_liner: A multi-level parent tree computed in O(1) per lattice cell gives connected branching networks and a monotone downhill valley terrain with no search.
ideas.algorithm: Level l has cell size s=fine*2^l and a jittered node per cell. Parent of cell c at level l: node at level l+1 in cell floor((c+hop)/2) with hop in {-1,0,1} from hash. Since the parent is itself a level l+1 child, all segments connect into trees. For each level, window +-2 cells: segment child->parent, width growing along t. Network output: max over levels of profile(d/w_l)*weight_l. Terrain output: node heights in strictly falling per-level bands; h_seg(t)+k_l*d with k_l chosen so distance reaches the cap of +1 by reach s_l; take the min over all segments and levels. The cap makes out-of-window segments irrelevant, so no seams.
ideas.look: Lightning, roots, cracks with hierarchy; terrain has V valleys that join downstream and drop monotonically. Prototyped: rel_dendrite, hop=1 for the non-grid form. Star-shaped convergence at parents is visible and more spidery than a real river.
ideas.why_new: Real hierarchical dendritic structure and monotone drainage, which are normally simulation results, with no pass over a grid. Ridged noise makes ridges with no tree topology.
ideas.simd_plan: Level loop is constant. Per level 25 cells in 2D with 2 hashes each and a segment distance. Scalar measured 12x worley2 with 4 levels. Estimate SIMD 2D 50-80 ns, well outside the 5x Perlin target, so justify it as a hero node. 3D with 125 cells per level is impractical without R=1 and small widths. 4D not practical, so tiling would need a dedicated fallback.
ideas.continuity: C0: network c0ratio 7.81, terrain c0ratio 8.00 with max slope 2.3. Terrain range measured -1 to about 0.67.
ideas.params: Levels (int), Hop (int enum), Width, Width Growth, Slope (float), Jitter, Output enum.
ideas.risks: Pure quadtree parents without hop guarantee no crossings but leave clear empty corridors along the top grid; hop fixes that and allows crossings. Nearest-of-4-parents would be better but it is essentially the published Dendry approach (Gaillard 2019, from memory, not checked) and costs 4x more. Poor 3D/4D story is a serious issue with the handbook's dimension rule.
ideas.cost_note: Estimate SIMD 2D 50-80 ns, well outside the 5x Perlin target, so justify it as a hero node.

ideas.name: LightConeCA
ideas.one_liner: Runs an exact cellular automaton (cave rule, maze rule, Life) for k generations on a hash-seeded infinite grid per sample by computing only the (2k+3)^2 light cone with bit-sliced logic, optionally as a multi-resolution pyramid.
ideas.algorithm: State at (cell,t) depends only on cells within radius t at t=0, so it is exact, stateless and seamless. For sample cell c, W=2(k+1)+1: build W rows as int32v bit-rows, each bit = hash(seed,c+offset) < Fill. For each generation run a bit-sliced neighbour count (full adders over the 8 shifted row copies, 4-bit count across all columns simultaneously), apply a birth/survive rule table as boolean logic. Take the final 4x4 cells around the sample, weight by radial tent (1-d^2/3.2)^2, output Clamp((sum/ws-0.5)*Sharp). Pyramid mode: L levels, each level's cell = parent bit XOR (hash<Flip), then 2 generations; patch radius stays constant across levels. Prototypes: dyn_lens mode=31,gens=4 (4-5 rule); mode=31,gens=5,birth=8,survive=62 (maze); mode=35,L=5,flip=0.25,cs=1.5 (pyramid).
ideas.look: Verified in prototype. 4-5 rule: rounded cave blobs with concave bays and no specks, more compact than thresholded noise and no axis feel after tent smoothing. Maze rule: rectilinear circuit-like corridors. Pyramid: chunky fractal coast with islands and crisp edges, not the tendrils of thresholded FBm. Good for roguelike caves, dungeon masks, microbial colonies, circuit patterns.
ideas.why_new: Cave CA is the canonical thing that everyone thinks needs a grid pass. Here it is the same exact automaton as a pure function of position, with GenPositionArray support and identical output at any scale. Rule choice opens a pattern family that no noise covers (maze corridors).
ideas.simd_plan: Bitboards per lane: rows of int32v with shifts and boolean ops; full adder neighbour count about 30 vector ops per row per generation. 2D gens=3, W=9: 81 cell hashes plus about 800 ops, estimate about 25 ns. Pyramid L=4 with k=2 and radius 7, about 60 ns. 3D gens=2, W=7: 49 rows of 7 bits, 26-neighbour adders, estimate about 150 ns. 4D gens=1 only (W=5, 625 bits), about 300 ns, or offer 4D as expensive. Per-node boolean rule tables.
ideas.continuity: Discontinuous at Sharp high; Lipschitz at Sharp low because the tent over 4x4 cells moves smoothly with fx, fy, but cell changes at lattice lines are covered by tent going to 0 at the 4x4 border only approximately, so check with fnlab. Treat as C0 with small seams to tune the kernel.
ideas.params: Generations int, Rule enum (Cave45, Maze, Coral, Custom B/S masks), Fill float (hybrid would alter pattern locally, cheap and useful), Sharpness, Levels and Flip for pyramid.
ideas.risks: Short generations are not enough to converge slow rules (maze at 5 gens is partial). Axis alignment returns with crisp sharpness or maze rules, so usually pair with a warp. High dimensions are costly. Patch is per-lane stack data, which is new territory for FastNoise but legal (no heap).
ideas.cost_note: 2D gens=3, W=9: 81 cell hashes plus about 800 ops, estimate about 25 ns. 3D gens=2, W=7: 49 rows of 7 bits, 26-neighbour adders, estimate about 150 ns.

ideas.name: LocalFrameDrainage
ideas.one_liner: Isotropic hierarchical river tree at cost linear in levels: each finer level drains toward only the single nearest coarser segment, treated as a local frame. Dendry (Gaillard et al., from memory) is the known hierarchical relative, but it evaluates and caches parent structure.
ideas.algorithm:
Level 0: jittered points on a coarse lattice, hash heights, each flows to its lowest of 8 neighbours (steepest descent, acyclic because heights are strictly ordered). Use a 5x5 lattice to resolve outlets for the 3x3 candidates. Keep nearest segment S0, distance d0, second-nearest d0b.
Level k+1, cell size / 2 or 3: for each of the 25 points q, define height H(q)=dist(q,S_k)-alpha*dot(q-A,dir(S_k))+jitter*hash(q), an analytic function needing only the one parent segment, not a recursive evaluation. Steepest descent over 8 neighbours. If a point's H is below a threshold, its outlet is its projection on S_k, making a Y-junction.
The tilt alpha makes tributaries join at acute angles pointing downstream.
Fade f_k=smoothstep(0,w,d_kb-d_k) goes to zero at the medial axis of level k, where the parent frame switches. That is exactly a drainage divide, so finer rivers vanish there and the switch is invisible.
Height: h=sum_k Depth_k*profile(d_(k+1)/W_k)*f_k, plus a base of d0-based hillslope.
ideas.look: Rivers and tributaries with a dendritic hierarchy in all directions, no global flow axis, and divides between them. Ridges appear as the medial axis of the parent network. Good for continental river masks and carved valleys.
ideas.why_new: The naive approach is exponential because each child needs the parent field at every child point. Fixing a local frame per sample removes the recursion, using the fact that parent influence only changes at divides, which is where the fade hides it. CatchmentRivers offers exact area but has an axis; this has no axis but width by level only.
ideas.simd_plan: Per level: 25 hashes and heights, 9x8 neighbour comparisons by Select, 9 segment distances. Estimate 20-25 ns per level, 3 levels about 70 ns, about 60x Perlin and 18x CellularDistance. Cheaper variant: 4-way outlet. 3D: 125 points and 27x26 comparisons per level are too much; use 2D plane with z crossfade, or a 7-point 3D stencil, for root-like filaments. 4D no; no tiling.
ideas.continuity: C0 through f_k fade provided the window holds all segments that can be nearest and the top-2 distance tracking is correct. Outlet search can flip with parent choice only inside the faded zone.
ideas.params: Levels (int), Subdivision (2 or 3), Depth Gain, Width Gain, Tilt alpha, Jitter, Height Source for level 0 (optional; 25 evals).
ideas.risks: Not tested. Sinks exist at local minima of level 0 unless a tilt or height source is supplied, producing disconnected basins. Child streams can run parallel to the parent if alpha is too high. Stream elevations are not guaranteed monotonic. Y-junctions at a parent's endpoint need clamped projection. Highest implementation risk here apart from caves.
ideas.cost_note: Estimate 20-25 ns per level, 3 levels about 70 ns, about 60x Perlin and 18x CellularDistance.

ideas.name: ModalCells
ideas.one_liner: Each lattice cell vibrates as a Chladni drumhead with hash-chosen mode numbers, and C0 across cells is automatic because all modes vanish on cell edges, so no neighbours are needed.
ideas.algorithm:
Cell i=Floor(p), u=p-i. h=hash(i); n=1+(h&255)%M; m=1+((h>>8)&255)%M; if m==n set m=1+m%M (Select; the degenerate case with minus sign is otherwise identically zero); sg=+-1 from bit 16.
Out=0.5*(Sin(n*pi*u)*Sin(m*pi*v)+sg*Sin(m*pi*u)*Sin(n*pi*v)).
3D: cyclic sum of three products, 4D: four. Optional bubble multiply by Sin(pi*u)*Sin(pi*v) for zero-slope seams (C1 at cost of a dark grid). Hybrid M lets a source select local complexity.

[ChladniCell, math-physics] Cells of side 1 (Feature Scale). No neighbour window: because sin(n pi u) is 0 at u=0 and u=1, each cell is independent and the field is C0 across edges.
Gen(seed, x):
  c = Floor(x); u = x - c (in [0,1)^d); h = hash(seed, c)
  f = 0
  for m in 0..Modes-1 (fixed):
    hm = rehash(h,m)
    n = MinMode + (hm bits) % (MaxMode-MinMode+1); k = same from other bits; if n==k: k = k+1 (Select)
    sigma = +-1 from a bit; amp = 1/(m+1) or rnd
    2D:  f += amp * ( Sin(n pi u) Sin(k pi v) + sigma * Sin(k pi u) Sin(n pi v) )
    3D:  cyclic antisymmetrised cube modes: f += amp*( S(n,u)S(k,v)S(l,w) + sigma*S(k,u)S(l,v)S(n,w) + sigma2*S(l,u)S(n,v)S(k,w) )
    4D:  same with 4 indices, 2 permutations
  Output Field:        v = f * normConst
  Output NodalLines:   grad f analytic (Cos terms, computed in the same loop) ; dist = |f| * InvSqrt(|grad f|^2 + eps) ; v = 1 - 2*Min(1, dist/LineWidth)   // constant-width Chladni sand lines
  Output EdgeFade (optional): multiply f by (4u(1-u))^q... to hide the plate border lines if undesired.
ideas.look:
Tested. A mosaic of ornamental tiles: dots, checks, rosettes, each cell a different mode, all with exact nodal grid lines. Warped, it reads as bubbled ornamental glass or sci-fi panels. Very distinct from the sheet. Uses: panel greebles, tiles, decorative masks, and zero crossings exactly on a known lattice (useful for connected paths and grids).
[ChladniCell, math-physics] A grid of ornamental tiles, each with its own symmetric curvilinear nodal pattern (cymatics sand figures, Islamic/Art-Deco tiles, engraved plates); NodalLines mode gives crisp uniform lines; 3D: nodal surfaces in cubes giving chambered mineral/ bismuth-like structures in slices. Low modes: soft lobed bumps; high modes: fine woven lattices.
ideas.why_new: The only coherent cell node that needs no window at all (cheaper than Perlin in hash count), with an exact guarantee on where zeros lie: the zero set always contains the lattice, and internal crossing count is (n-1)(m-1)-like and hash-controlled. Fits the zero-crossing control brief directly.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch free. 1 hash, 4 Sin in 2D (6 and 8 in 3D and 4D by reuse), integer mod, Select. Window 1^D. Estimated about 1-1.5x Perlin in 2D and below Perlin in 3D and 4D.
ideas.continuity: C0 (verified numerically, ratio 8.0), kinks across cell edges due to different slopes. C1 with the bubble option.
ideas.params: Hybrid: Max Mode M. Enum: Bubble on/off. Seeded, ScalableGenerator.
ideas.risks:
The grid is always visible by design, and offset-lattice sums blur the identity (tested, it looked muddy). It is a pattern node, not a general purpose noise. Output contrast varies by mode. High M in a small cell aliases at small feature scales.
[ChladniCell, math-physics] The cell grid is visible in the zero set (plate edges) which is a style, not a bug, but limits use as terrain; sign and normalisation constants need measuring; high modes alias at low sampling.
ideas.variant_notes: Chladni modes per cell, needing no window. ChladniCell contributes the NodalLines output with constant line width by analytic gradient.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated about 1-1.5x Perlin in 2D and below Perlin in 3D and 4D.

ideas.name: NestedVoronoi
ideas.one_liner: Each Voronoi cell owns a private child Voronoi with its own seed, density, orientation and stretch, and may stay unbroken, giving terrazzo and polycrystal looks.
ideas.algorithm:
id=0 start: level 0 search gives F1,F2,h. crack=0.5*(F2-F1), id=h. For L=1..Levels-1: h'=mix(id,L). alive=rnd(h'>>a)>=Gap; once a lane dies it stays frozen. fr=Lac^L*(1+FreqJitter*rnd(h'>>b)). q=p reflected through the Householder plane from hash n (q-=2n(n.q)), then stretched along hash axis m (q+=(Aniso-1)m(m.q)), times fr. Search q with seed=h'. crack=min(crack, Age*L+0.5*(F2-F1)/fr); id=hash of the child's F1. Output: rnd(id)*smoothstep(0,w,crack), rnd(id), or crack. The key trick is that a child lattice seeded from the parent's id can differ arbitrarily across a parent border, because the crack term reaches 0 exactly there.

[HierarchicalCracks, nature-phenomena] pid=0. For each level l: seed_l=seed+1000*l+pid (a per-lane int32v). Pass 1: search the 3^D window for the nearest point, keeping its vector vn and hash. Pass 2: over the same stored points, e=min((0.5*(vi+vn)).(vi-vn)/|vi-vn|), skipping the nearest point itself; this is the exact bisector distance. Convert to world units e/f_l; out=min(out, saturate(e/(f_l*width_l)))) with e already in world units after that conversion; pid=pid*31+nearest hash. Options: Corner Rounding replaces min in pass 2 with smin(k), giving rounded plates (giraffe, cobbles). Anisotropy scales one axis before the distance. Plate Tilt adds (cos a, sin a).vn/f on the last level with angle a from the hash. Output is sqrt(out)*(1+plate).
ideas.look:
Large polished stones sitting in fields of rubble, terrazzo, conglomerate rock, or metal grains with differently oriented sub-cells. The Gap parameter is what makes the size distribution so bimodal.
[HierarchicalCracks, nature-phenomena] Mud-crack mosaics where newer cracks end against older, wider ones. Tilt gives curled, shard-like plates, anisotropy gives furrowed bark, and one level with rounding gives striking giraffe or pebble patches.
ideas.why_new: Voronoi fracturing is usually done with two independent layers, where children cross parent borders. Here children are clipped by parents, and density, orientation and survival change per parent, which no graph of existing nodes can do (no node passes a cell id to a child's seed or domain).
ideas.simd_plan: Seed is already int32v per lane in Gen, so per-lane re-seeding fits directly. Positions from pass 1 go in a fixed stack array of float32v. Estimates per level: 8 ns in 2D, 24 ns in 3D, 75 ns in 4D, so 3 levels are about 24 ns in 2D (6x CellularDistance-level cost per 3 levels) and 72 ns in 3D. An F2-F1 mode costs one CellularDistance per level (4/12/41 ns). 4D is expensive.
ideas.continuity: C0 for crack and for rnd(id)*fade, measured at c0ratio 8.00 with max slope 6. Use F2-F1, not the exact bisector formula (see notes). Raw id output jumps by design.
ideas.params: Levels (int), Lacunarity, Gap (hybrid at parent is not possible at pixel level; use hash, or sample a source at the parent seed), Frequency Jitter, Aniso, Age, Crack Width, Output enum.
ideas.risks:
Age must rise with level or C0 breaks. Fine levels alias if Lacunarity is high. 4D cost is heavy; offer 2 levels for tileable use. The 3D form was not rendered; proto Eval3 is only a sheared 2D slice.
[HierarchicalCracks, nature-phenomena] Real cracks meet at near 90 degrees; here child cracks meet parents at arbitrary angles. Pass 2 in a 3^D window is an approximation: the reference two-pass code uses 5x5, while the Blender change reduced it to 3x3. Hybrid per-level seed cost is linear in levels but 4D is heavy.
ideas.variant_notes: Child lattice reseeded per lane by the parent's hash. HierarchicalCracks adds exact bisector option, plate tilt and corner rounding. Crack age must rise with level for C0.
ideas.cost_note: Estimates per level: 8 ns in 2D, 24 ns in 3D, 75 ns in 4D, so 3 levels are about 24 ns in 2D (6x CellularDistance-level cost per 3 levels) and 72 ns in 3D.

ideas.name: OcclusionStack
ideas.one_liner: Opaque cut-out sheets with a global depth order plus built-in contact shadow: leaf litter, slate, feathers, torn paper.
ideas.algorithm:
Window 3^dim. Each cell has a stamp with rotation, size and priority pr = rnd(h) (a pure function of the feature, so any window sees the same order, no seams). Rotate into local (u,v). Shape SDF by enum, e.g. Leaf: t = 1-(u/L)^2, sd = (|v|/W - t)*W, sd = max(sd, |u|-L); also Superellipse, Ngon, Shard. Mask m = 1 - smoothstep(-Edge, 0, sd). Shadow s = 1 - smoothstep(0, ShadowWidth, sd). Interior value val = per-stamp hash value + vein term exp(-|v|*k) + slope*u, optionally + Source at local coords. Sort candidates by pr with a fixed sorting network (9 inputs = 25 comparators with Selects in 2D), or keep top K by pr among m>0 for 3D. Composite front to back: col += vis*m*(val*shade + (shade-1)*ShadowDark); shade *= 1 - ShadowStrength*s*(1-m); vis *= 1-m. Final col += vis*Background. Shingle mode: pr is replaced by the lexicographic row, so rows overlap like roof tiles or fish scales with no sort at all.

[ScatterPainter, stamp-scatter] Same per-cell instancing as Scatter, but each cell yields a triple (key, value, alpha): key = rnd01(h1) (Age mode), or -s (Smaller-on-top), or value itself (Height mode, which degenerates to Max); alpha = coverage envelope of the stamp (0 outside, 1 inside, smooth over EdgeWidth) times presence.
Sort the N = 2^d triples per lane with a fixed compare-exchange network: 4 elements -> 5 CEs, 8 -> 19 CEs, 16 -> 60 CEs. One CE = mask = keyA > keyB; swap keys/values/alphas with Select (3 Selects + 1 compare per CE).
Composite back to front (lowest key first): out = Background; for i in sorted order: out = lerp(out, value_i, alpha_i).
Because the loop count and the network are constants, this is fully data parallel. Octaves: composite octave results with the same rule, treating the whole coarse octave as 'older' (key offset per octave), so small features always overwrite big ones, matching how a crater field evolves.
Optional Crater mode: the stamp value is a *replacement height* inside the bowl and an *additive* rim outside it: out = lerp(out, value_i, alpha_i) + rim_i*(1 - alpha_i). This gives rims that sit on older terrain while bowls cut through it.
ideas.look:
Prototype reads immediately as a pile of autumn leaves with real occlusion; hillshade looks like a modelled layer. Other shapes give slate, flagstones, feathers, dragon scales, camouflage, paper collage. Output is piecewise smooth with steep contours, which is unlike anything on the contact sheet.
[OcclusionStack (DeadLeaves), lattice-kernels] Pebble piles, leaf litter, bubbles, roof shingles, overlapping coins, bokeh. Prototyped: coherent layered discs, with hillshade immediately reading as stacked stones. T-junction topology is unavailable in anything on the sheet.
ideas.why_new: Overlap order and occlusion cannot be built from Max or MaxSmooth over any graph, because a graph has no per-instance identity. Compared with plain dead-leaves noise, the node adds shape, inner structure and shadows from upper sheets on lower ones, which give the depth cue that makes it read as an object pile.
ideas.simd_plan:
Analytic only: 9 cells with rotation and SDF, plus sorting network. Estimate 2D 10-14 ns (3x CellularDistance). 3D with top-K=3 selection: 27 cells ~30-40 ns. 4D top-K=3: 81 cells ~110 ns, usable only for tiling. Source input: evaluate only at the K top slots. Rotation via table or rational form, no atan2.
[ScatterPainter, stamp-scatter] Scatter cost plus the network: 2D 5 CEs (~25 ops), 3D 19 CEs (~95 ops), 4D 60 CEs (~300 ops, roughly +8 ns on top of the 4D Scatter cost); Wide 3x3 window needs a 9-element network (25 CEs) which is still fine in 2D; 27 and 81 element networks are not worth it, so Wide is 2D only or falls back to SoftOver. Registers: N triples live simultaneously (16x3 float32v in 4D) so 4D may spill on SSE; acceptable. Lattice window and 2D/3D/4D as Scatter.
ideas.continuity: C0 with Edge > 0, verified: c0ratio 8.16 in 2D with the full sort. Near-discontinuous contours by design as Edge approaches 0. Top-K truncation introduces very small pops only where more than K soft edges coincide.
ideas.params: Shape enum, Size, Aspect (hybrid), Edge softness, Shadow Width, Shadow Strength, Vein Strength, Order enum (Random/Rows), Rotation Spread (hybrid, so scales can align), Density, optional Source, Background, K in 3D+
ideas.risks:
Reach is capped at 1 cell, so sheets need size <= 1 and coverage depends on density; some background shows through at low size. Sorting network code per dimension is awkward: use insertion-based partial selection in 3D/4D. In 3D the sheets become ellipsoids or lenses and the look is less obvious, so 3D's value is unproven (the proto's 3D slice is a sheared 2D fake).
[OcclusionStack (DeadLeaves), lattice-kernels] Coverage gaps at low density need a background. Discontinuities alias, so offer an optional output that returns edge distance to antialias. Windows limit radius, so size distribution is bounded: no truly scale-free leaves in one node, only through stacking two.
ideas.variant_notes: Dead leaves with a global priority. Options: plain top-wins Select (OcclusionStack, cheapest), sorting-network painter's over (ScatterPainter), and contact shadows from upper sheets (CollageStack, which is what makes it read as a pile).
ideas.cost_note: Estimate 2D 10-14 ns (3x CellularDistance). 3D with top-K=3 selection: 27 cells ~30-40 ns.

ideas.name: OrbitBlobs
ideas.one_liner: Sum of compact Wyvill kernels on jittered lattice points that travel closed Lissajous orbits parameterised by w: metaball necks, lava-lamp rise-and-sink, exact-period looping at 3D cost.
ideas.algorithm:
Window 3x3x3 (3x3 in 2D). Per cell k, for j in 0..PointsPerCell-1 (fixed int):
  h = Hash(k, j); c = k + 0.5 + Jitter*rnd3(h)
  per-point phase phi (table by bits), orbit frame u,v (table of random orthonormal pairs by bits)
  S,Cw = Sin/Cos(Omega*(w + Phase(p))) once per lane; s = S*cphi + Cw*sphi, cc = Cw*cphi - S*sphi
  c(w) = c + OrbitAmp * (u*cc + v*s)          // per-axis amplitude vector OrbitAmp, default (0.1, 0.4, 0.1) = lava lamp
  R = Radius * (1 + RadiusJitter*rnd11(h>>16))
  r2 = |p - c(w)|^2 / R^2; k = Max(1 - r2, 0); field += k*k*k    // Wyvill, C2, compact
out = field - Threshold, ScaleOutput over [-Threshold, Kmax - Threshold] (Kmax measured constant per PointsPerCell). Window validity: Radius <= 1.5 - Jitter - |OrbitAmp|max, so blobs may be larger than cells and overlap. 4D = 3D lattice + w phase (so tiling via GenTileable2D still holds).
ideas.look: 3D iso-surface: smooth merging droplets with proper necks (metaballs); low threshold gives a fused foam/sponge of rounded cavities, high threshold separate pearls. Animated in w: blobs rise, sink, pass each other, merge and split, exactly the lava lamp, looping with period 2pi/Omega. 2D slice: soft discs that fuse like mercury; animated: drifting, merging ink drops.
ideas.why_new: CellularDistance F1 gives a union of hard spheres with creases where they meet and cannot add overlapping influences; CellularLookup cannot either. This gives smooth union/necks, per-blob size, and an exact animation loop without a 4D lattice (41 ns Cellular 4D avoided).
ideas.simd_plan: Cellular.inl window loop, no sorting; per point ~20 ops (orbit 6 FMA, distance 8, kernel 5). 3D with 1 point/cell: ~27 points ~ 1x CellularDistance 3D (12 ns); 2D ~4 ns; 4D same as 3D plus one Sin/Cos per lane.
ideas.continuity: C2 in space and C-infinity in w (Wyvill kernel is C2 at its support edge); gradient bounded by PointsPerCell*27*max kernel slope/Radius.
ideas.params: Radius (hybrid), RadiusJitter, Jitter, PointsPerCell (int 1-2), OrbitAmp X/Y/Z, Omega, Phase (hybrid), Threshold, Feature Scale, Seed.
ideas.risks: Lattice-regular density (one point per cell) shows as even spacing at low Jitter; large OrbitAmp forces a small Radius to keep the window valid. Kmax normalisation is a measured constant.
sources: from memory, not consulted: Lewis 1989 sparse convolution noise; Wyvill soft objects
ideas.cost_note: 3D with 1 point/cell: ~27 points ~ 1x CellularDistance 3D (12 ns); 2D ~4 ns; 4D same as 3D plus one Sin/Cos per lane.

ideas.name: PebblePack
ideas.one_liner: Non-overlapping discs with pairwise weighted radii, provably disjoint, so any-node stamps need just one Source eval, in any dimension.
ideas.algorithm: Per feature i: weight w_i (hash)^Pow. Radius r_i = min over neighbour cells j of d_ij * w_i/(w_i+w_j), clamped to 1. Pairwise proof: for any pair r_i <= d_ij*w_i/(w_i+w_j) and r_j <= d_ij*w_j/(w_i+w_j), so r_i + r_j <= d_ij, hence disjoint. The neighbour set must be symmetric. Radius is a pure function of lattice coordinates, not of the sample. Implementation: hash and store features for the 5^2 block; for each of 9 candidates compare with its 8 neighbours (72 distances) or 4 edge neighbours + 4 corners subset that is symmetric. At most one disc contains p, so select it with Select: dome height, or local coordinates (p-c)/r plus seed h for exactly 1 Source.Gen. Optional Survivor mode (Matern II): feature dies if a higher-priority neighbour is within Exclusion radius, also a pure function, giving a blue-noise spot set.
ideas.look: Prototype: separated domes of many sizes with no touching, or Perlin-textured discs. Reads as pebbles, bubbles, bacteria, polka-dot skin; used as a mask gives exactly non-colliding spot placement. Coverage is lower than expected at about 25-35%, so it looks like sparse pebbles rather than a full cobble floor unless layered.
ideas.why_new: Size Jitter in CellularDistance produces weighted cells, not disjoint round objects with gaps. Circles cut by Max of cellular get flat clipped boundaries. The disjointness guarantee turns any-node stamping into a K=1 problem with no fade and no overlap ordering, which is what makes 3D and 4D affordable.
ideas.simd_plan: 2D: 25 hashes + 72 distances (store in arrays of float32v on stack, allowed as small tables) ~20-30 ns + 1 Source. 3D: 125 hashes and 27x6 face neighbours, ~80-100 ns + 1 Source. 4D: 625 hashes is too much; use 4D with 8 axial neighbours and 81 candidates, stored hash count 3^4 + 8 faces... expensive, about 300 ns; justify only for tiling or fall back to fixed radii from a fixed jitter bound (r=(1-Jitter)/2) which is free. Fixed-radius mode is a cheap 3x3 scan, which is the recommended cost-saving mode for 3D and 4D.
ideas.continuity: C0 with profile (1-t^2)^0.75 or lower power: c0ratio 4.67 at jit 0.5 (steep domes near the edge; sqrt profile has infinite slope at edge). Any profile reaching 0 at t=1 is seamless because radii are global.
ideas.params: Jitter, Pow (size contrast), Fill (<=1), Profile enum, Source (optional stamp), Exclusion Radius, Value Mode (dome, id, size)
ideas.risks: Only moderate coverage; a second-pass inflation would need a 7^dim window. Reduced jitter reintroduces a visible grid. Cost is quite high for what is a sparse pattern; the K=1 Source advantage is the justification. Two layers via Max would lose disjointness, though only at the combine level.
ideas.cost_note: 2D: 25 hashes + 72 distances (store in arrays of float32v on stack, allowed as small tables) ~20-30 ns + 1 Source.

ideas.name: PebblePile
ideas.one_liner: A pointwise dead-leaves model: stacked layers of confined rounded stones where the first covering layer wins, giving real occlusion for gravel, rock piles and conglomerate.
ideas.algorithm: covered=false; out=0. For layer L (top first) in a fixed loop: P=Rot_L*x/(s0*g^L)+offset_L; C=floor(P); h=hash(C); R=0.3+0.2*r4; v=P-(C+R+(1-2R)*(r1,r2)); rotate v by an angle from the hash; asp=0.65+0.35*r5; q=(u/R)^4+(w/(R*asp))^4; inside=on & q<1; val=sqrt(max(1-q,0))*R*asp*s_L+0.15*r6*s_L+(Layers-L)*bias; out=Select(covered,out,Select(inside,val,out)); covered|=inside. The prototype used exponent 2.6; integer powers should be used in the port. Optional last layer: full F1 cell value, to guarantee coverage.
ideas.look: Hillshade reads clearly as a pile of rounded stones, gravel or cobbles, with visible occlusion contours and T-shaped overlaps. Output mode with per-stone values gives clast mosaics like conglomerate.
ideas.why_new: No existing node has occlusion: all cellular nodes partition space, and blends average or take min/max across a whole layer. Layer order gives stones sitting on stones, a look which needs painter's ordering in a graph.
ideas.simd_plan: One hash per layer, no window: 9 layers estimated at 9-12 ns in any dimension (about 10x Perlin and 3x CellularDistance in 2D; under 1x in 3D; 0.3x in 4D). A 3x3 per layer version also looked good but costs about 6x more in 2D and far more in 3D, so own-cell is preferred. Hit tracking with masks only.
ideas.continuity: Discontinuous by intent at occlusion edges (28 jumps over 6 scanlines), because a stone edge is a real height step. A C0 mode can use max of dome heights without the layer bias, at the loss of occlusion.
ideas.params: Layers (int), Base Size (Feature Scale), Layer Growth, Fill (hybrid), Roundness, Aspect Jitter, Output {Height, Stone Value}.
ideas.risks: Discontinuities can alias, and small holes remain unless a backstop layer is added. Stones appear smaller and more uniform in the own-cell version, needing tuning. Dead-leaves background is from memory and was not checked. 3D stones were not prototyped.
ideas.cost_note: One hash per layer, no window: 9 layers about 9-12 ns in any dimension (10x Perlin in 2D, 3x CellularDistance; under 1x in 3D).

queue.name: PebblePile
queue.reason: Dead-leaves gravel with real occlusion and no window, ~10 ns at any dimension. Discontinuous and needs a backstop layer. occlusion-stack is the richer sibling.

ideas.name: Phyllotaxis
ideas.one_liner: Exact nearest point on a Fermat spiral found in O(1) with four candidates in the local Fibonacci basis, with a fixed-point golden angle: sunflowers, pinecones, succulents, spiral scales.
ideas.algorithm:
c=spacing. n=(x^2+y^2)/c^2. n0=round(n). th=atan_poly(y,x)/2pi. Choose Fibonacci pair F0,F1 from k=floor(log_phi(2.2*sqrt(n))), table lookup via a permute. Golden angle in fixed point: alpha(m)=m*0x61C88647 as uint32, which is exact for all m and needs no float. a0,a1=signed fraction of F0*G, F1*G. dth=signed fraction of th32-n0*G. Solve [F0 F1; a0 a1](i,j)=(n-n0,dth). Candidates m=n0+(floor(i)+e0)*F0+(floor(j)+e1)*F1 for e in {0,1}^2, mask m>=0. Each: position c*sqrt(m)*(cos,sin of alpha(m)), distance. Keep min with its m and local vector. Outputs: distance, rnd(hash m), scaled index (m/maxN, gradient from centre), or a local frame for scale shapes (u along radial).

[FibonacciCellular, lit-recent] Params: PointCount N (int), Jitter (float 0..1), Output enum {F1, F2minusF1, CellValue, CellIndex}, Distance enum.
3D (direction cells): n = normalise(p) (radius ignored, or used as a seed slice via hash(floor(|p|)) for 'layered shells'). Spherical Fibonacci point i: z_i = 1 - (2i+1)/N, phi_i = 2pi * frac(i*PHI). Inverse mapping (Keinert): k = max(2, floor(log(N*pi*sqrt5*(1-n.z^2)) / log(PHI^2))); Fk = round(PHI^k/sqrt5), Fk1 = round(Fk*PHI); build the 2x2 basis B from (Fk, Fk1): B = [[2pi*frac((Fk+1)*PHI-1) - 2pi*(PHI-1), same for Fk1],[-2Fk/N, -2Fk1/N]]; c = round(B^-1 * (phi_n, n.z - (1-1/N))); the 4 candidates i = Fk*(c.x+s.x) + Fk1*(c.y+s.y) for s in {0,1}^2; reconstruct each candidate point, jitter it by Jitter * tangent rnd(hash(seed,i)) (keep within half the inter-point spacing ~ sqrt(4pi/N)/2), pick the nearest (F1) and second nearest (F2) by angular/chord distance.
2D (planar spiral cells): Vogel point i: r_i = sqrt(i/N)*Rmax... use r_i = c*sqrt(i), theta_i = 2pi*i*(PHI-1); inverse: with k from log of (pi*r^2), same Fibonacci-basis trick in (theta, r^2) space (the planar spiral is the sphere mapping with z replaced by r^2), 4 candidates, pick nearest. Points are capped: beyond the max index the domain tiles with an ordinary jittered grid (Select) so far coords stay cheap.
F1 normalised by the mean nearest spacing; CellValue = rnd11(hash(seed,i)).
ideas.look:
Look-tested (m=13): dense spiral parastichies with characteristic moire arms. 2D distance output is immediately sunflower or cactus. Combined with TileSplit Interior or CellularLookup style instancing, you get fields of rosettes, succulents, or pinecone scales using the local frame with FlowShingle-like profiles.
[PhyllotaxisCellular, lattice-kernels] The sunflower tessellation: cells arranged along interlocking clockwise and counter-clockwise spirals, cell size constant over the disc (equal-area), with F1 giving dimples, F2-F1 giving the scale/bract network and Index giving a radial age gradient. 3D: nested shells of near-hexagonal cells (pollen grains, pangolin, pineapple skins, golf balls) in a volume.
ideas.why_new: Nothing on the sheet has rotational order or spirals. The usual approach searches a large index range; here the 2x2 solve gives 4 candidates, verified against a 4000 candidate brute force with only 0.004% of pixels differing. Spirals are normally thought of as unreachable from a hash lattice.
ideas.simd_plan: 1 atan poly, 1 log (or use float exponent extraction for k), 4 candidates each with sin, cos and sqrt. Int multiply gives exact angle. Measured 1.7x Perlin scalar (float32 m is enough). No hash at all except for output value. 3D: pinecone mode, z scales the spacing (conical stack) or spherical Fibonacci inverse for shells (from memory: Keinert et al. 2015, same local-basis trick on the sphere). 4D: w as extra spacing modulation, so a real function exists but torus tiling is not meaningful.
ideas.continuity: C0 for F1 distance if candidates contain the true nearest (measured c0ratio about 36, smooth). Value and local frame outputs are discontinuous at Voronoi walls as with any cell value. A very rare miss creates tiny discontinuities (0.004% differ, max image difference 70/255).
ideas.params: Spacing (hybrid would move all points, so better fixed), Output enum (Distance, Value, Index), Max Radius with fade, Angle Offset. Mainly per-node floats; Seed changes rotation only.
ideas.risks:
Non-stationary: a single centre at origin, needs DomainOffset or TileSplit Interior to instance. Not stationary coherent noise, so it may feel niche. Dimension story for 3D and 4D is the weakest of the list. Candidate misses increase near k switches. Small n near centre needs mask care. Index beyond 2^31 is out of scope, which is far beyond practical radius.
[FibonacciCellular, lit-recent] float32 precision of k and the Fibonacci basis for N > ~1e5 (paper discusses GPU precision fixes); 2D far-from-origin behaviour needs the fallback lattice; F2 is only approximately exact from 4 candidates.
sources: B. Keinert, M. Innmann, M. Saenger, M. Stamminger, 'Spherical Fibonacci Mapping', SIGGRAPH Asia 2015 (inverse mapping; from memory, not fetched)
H. Vogel, 'A better way to construct the sunflower head', 1979 (from memory, not fetched)
ideas.variant_notes: Verified against brute force: 0.004% of pixels differ. 3D uses the spherical Fibonacci inverse (Keinert), giving even, pole-free planet cells with an exact count.
ideas.cost_note: Measured 1.7x Perlin scalar (float32 m is enough).

ideas.name: PlateDrift
ideas.one_liner: Voronoi plates that each shrink, slide and rotate as rigid polygons (via the per-cell polygonal gauge evaluated in the plate's own frame), producing ice floes, shattered glass, drying-mud curls and cobbles with variable sand gaps where the gap width and plate rotation are real, not painted.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Drift (hybrid, cell units <= 0.3), Rotation (hybrid, radians), Gap (hybrid, 0..1 shrink), Bevel, Priority enum {Random, Nearest}, Mode {Margin, Lookup, PlateValue, TiltedHeight}, Source, Jitter.

Window 3^d around the sample. For every cell j precompute site c_j (jittered), rigid transform: translation t_j = Drift*rnd01*rndDir(h_j), rotation R_j (2D: angle = Rotation*rnd11(h_j), one sin/cos per candidate or a cheap normalised (1, eps*rnd11) direction; 3D: rotation about a hashed axis by a small angle, or z-only), shrink s_j = 1 - Gap*(0.5 + 0.5 rnd01), priority pr_j = rnd01.
For each candidate plate i: p_i = R_i^T (p - c_i - t_i) + c_i (bring the sample into plate i's undeformed frame). Polygonal gauge of plate i at p_i: g_i = max over j != i of 2 (p_i - c_i).(c_j - c_i) / |c_j - c_i|^2 (0 at the site, 1 on every Voronoi wall of cell i; this is rel_gauge's PolyGauge). Inside_i = g_i < s_i; signed margin m_i = s_i - g_i.
Outputs: Margin = max_i m_i (positive inside a plate, negative in gaps; clamp(m/Bevel) gives bevelled plates with gaps). Winner w = argmax over inside_i of pr_i (dead leaves where drifted plates overlap) or of m_i (Nearest, no visible overlap). Lookup = Source.Gen(seed ^ h_w, p_w - c_w [, z]) so the texture rides with the plate; PlateValue = rnd11(h_w); TiltedHeight = per-plate plane in plate coordinates. Gap value = constant or distance via Margin.
Why the gauge is enough: the walls that decide whether plate i covers p are the ones between c_i and p, formed by sites near that segment, all inside the 3^d window around p; sites at the window edge only have inaccurate far walls which cannot reach p under the Drift/Jitter bounds (proto audits against brute force like dcc_edgecheck did for edge distance).
ideas.look: A field of convex polygonal plates each slightly rotated and shifted, with wedge-shaped gaps that open and close, some edges touching, some overlapping (dead leaves), like river ice breaking up, a dropped plate, tempered glass, kintsugi gaps, or curling mud. With Drift as a hybrid noise, gaps open in bands (rift zones) and close elsewhere. The sheet has no cells with real variable gaps or rotated plate outlines.
ideas.why_new: CellPatchDomain rotates the texture inside a cell but the cell outline stays put; F2-F1 cannot open wedge gaps or rotate outlines; stamps/dead leaves cannot make the shards fit each other. Displacing the actual polygon pointwise needs the gauge-in-plate-frame trick.
ideas.simd_plan: Standard 3^d window, nested loop candidates x neighbours of dot products only (no sqrt in the inner loop): 2D 9x8=72 FMA-dots plus 9 cheap rotations, roughly 10-14 ns (3x CellularDistance 2D). 3D Full: 27x26 dots (~60-90 ns) with sites recomputed from hashes inside the inner loop to avoid spilling 81 registers; default 3D/4D is Extruded (plates in xy, z/w passed to the Source), which keeps GenTileable2D usable via an explicit Period rather than the 4D torus.
ideas.continuity: Margin mode is C0: each m_i is continuous in p, and a candidate entering or leaving the window at a cell boundary has margin far below the max under the Drift bound. Lookup, PlateValue and TiltedHeight are discontinuous at plate edges by design.
ideas.params: Drift (hybrid), Rotation (hybrid), Gap (hybrid), Bevel, Priority enum, Mode enum, Source, Jitter, 3D mode enum {Extruded, Full}.
ideas.risks: Needs the brute-force audit of window reach versus Drift/Jitter; expensive in true 3D; dead-leaves overlaps can expose the far (inaccurate) walls of window-edge plates if Drift is pushed past the bound, so clamp Drift in the setter.
ideas.cost_note: Standard 3^d window, nested loop candidates x neighbours of dot products only (no sqrt in the inner loop): 2D 9x8=72 FMA-dots plus 9 cheap rotations, roughly 10-14 ns (3x CellularDistance 2D).

ideas.name: PolarCells
ideas.one_liner: Cellular feature field where each feature has its own polar frame and a periodic angular noise, so radially structured landforms (volcanoes with flank gullies and calderas, star-rimmed sinkholes, ribbed karst towers, star dunes, rayed craters) emerge from a single node.
ideas.algorithm: Jittered lattice, 3x3 window (3x3x3 in 3D). Per cell: point c, radius R = Radius*(1 - RJit*rnd), hash h. dx,dy = p - c, r = |d|, angle in turns a = atan2(dy,dx)/(2*pi) (polynomial). Periodic angular noise: ringnoise(a, n, h) = quintic-lerp of rnd11(mix(h, k mod n)) over n lattice points on the circle (periodic by index wrap), plus a 3n harmonic at 0.25 amplitude. Star radius: R_eff = R*(1 + Gully*ang); rr = r/R_eff. Profiles (enum Kind): Volcano: cone = smoothstep(1-rr) minus 0.6*sat(1 - r/(Caldera*R))^2; Bowl (doline/cockpit): -(1-t^2)^2 with t = sat(rr); Tower: (1-t)^2; Fan: profile only inside a sector (see FanField); Crater: bowl + raised rim exp(-(rr-1)^2/s) + rays via a second angular noise with amplitude growing with r. Combine (enum): Max (hills), Min (depressions), Sum, Youngest (per-feature age hash, the newest covering feature overwrites: needs an edge feather of width Feather to stay C0). In 3D the angular noise lives on a sphere: use the two angles (atan2(dy,dx), asin(dz/r)) on a lat-long lattice, or cheaper, use 3D value noise of the unit direction scaled by n.
ideas.look: Clusters of volcanic cones with radial spurs and gullies and a summit pit; fields of star-shaped sinkholes separated by sharp residual hills (cockpit karst); conical ribbed towers; with Youngest combine, overlapping craters where new ones cut old rims. Prototyped: Volcano / Cockpit / TowerKarst / YoungestWins (the last one is discontinuous as implemented, by design of the hard overwrite; a feather fixes it). Scalar cost 7.3x Perlin.
ideas.why_new: CellularDistance has no notion of 'around the feature point': every radial variation an artist wants (gullies down a cone, rays from a crater, distributaries on a fan) is impossible because the only per-cell quantities are distance and one value. Adding a per-feature periodic angular noise, with amplitude that vanishes at the apex, is the small primitive that unlocks all of these.
ideas.simd_plan: 9 cells x (1 Sqrt, 1 polynomial atan2, 2 periodic lerps with 4 hashes, profile ~10 ops, Select by Kind resolved at compile/dispatch time or by masks): ~5-7x Perlin in 2D; 27 cells in 3D ~20x Perlin; 4D 81 cells ~60x, feasible. Angular noise lattice index via Convert of a*n and masked wrap (n power of two preferred: wrap is an AND).
ideas.continuity: C0 for Max/Min/Sum (measured 7.6-7.7): the angular term is multiplied by r implicitly through rr, so the apex singularity is harmless. Youngest combine is C0 only with Feather > 0 (smoothstep between the overwriting feature's edge and its interior).
ideas.params: Feature Scale, Jitter, Radius, Radius Jitter, Kind enum, Combine enum, Spokes (int n), Gully (angular amplitude), Harmonic, Caldera Fraction, Rim Height (crater), Ray Length, Feather (Youngest), Density (hybrid: feature is skipped when rnd > density, so a mask thins volcanoes regionally).
ideas.risks: Features larger than one cell leak out of the 3x3 window (seams): clamp Radius*(1+Gully) to 1 cell. Polynomial atan2 accuracy near the +-x axis must be C0 across the branch cut (handle with the standard octant-folding form). Density thinning changes which cells participate, fine for Max/Min, slightly jumpy for Sum (feather the density too).
ideas.cost_note: 9 cells x (1 Sqrt, 1 polynomial atan2, 2 periodic lerps with 4 hashes, profile ~10 ops, Select by Kind resolved at compile/dispatch time or by masks): ~5-7x Perlin in 2D; 27 cells in 3D ~20x Perlin; 4D 81 cells ~60x, feasible.

ideas.name: PolyGauge
ideas.one_liner: Voronoi cells turned into exact flat-faceted pyramids: 0 at the feature point, 1 on every wall, using the bisector with each neighbour.
ideas.algorithm:
Pass 1: normal F1 over the 3^D window, storing all p_j and keeping p_i of the winner with Select. Pass 2: g = max over j != i of 2*dot(x-p_i, p_j-p_i) / max(|p_j-p_i|^2, dmin^2). g is the polygon's gauge (Minkowski) function: g=0 at p_i, g=1 exactly on the wall with j, and linear along any ray from p_i. Outputs: (a) 1-2g, pyramid with planar facets; (b) (1-g)*v_i, per-cell apex height with walls still at a shared base; (c) tri(g*k), rings that are perfectly scaled copies of the cell polygon; (d) facet id: hash(h_i ^ h_j) of the winning j, which gives a kite mosaic where each Delaunay edge owns one kite (symmetric, so both halves match).

[CellCoverage, distribution-topology] Pass 1: find nearest site s1 and its lattice cell c1, as CellularDistance does. Pass 2: over neighbours j of c1 (window centred on c1 per lane, not on the sample, so the facet set is a pure function of the cell and cannot seam): rho = max_j 2*dot(p - s1, s_j - s1) / |s_j - s1|^2. Then rho = 0 at the site and 1 on every wall, and level sets {rho < c} are exact homothetic copies of the cell, covering exactly c^D of it. U = rho^D is exactly uniform per cell. Outputs: Uniform = 2U - 1. Halftone = smoothstep(-w, w, Level - U) with Level from a hybrid sampled at s1 (extra source eval, as CellularLookup does), so each polygon's inked area fraction equals the source value at its site.
ideas.look:
Cut-gem or low-poly rock cells with straight creases from the feature point to each Voronoi vertex. Rings are nested polygons rather than F1 circles. The kite mosaic looks like shattered tile and is not a Voronoi mosaic. Good for crystal ground, cobbles, stylised rock, armour plates, normal-map masks. Prototyped: rel_gauge, grid mode=0,1,2,3.
[CellCoverage, distribution-topology] Faceted pyramids with polygon contours. Halftone: stipple of shrinking and growing polygons with even blue-ish spacing whose local mean reproduces the source gray level. Good for cracked tiles, mosaics, stippled masks, exact scatter density and rubble. Measured per-cell coverage at a level targeting 30 percent over 441 cells: U mean 0.3000 std 0.0016 (pixel quantisation scale); (F1/F2)^2 std 0.039; F1^2 std 0.063.
ideas.why_new:
F1 gives round cones and F2-F1 gives uneven ridge height and width; neither has planar facets or a constant wall value. It needs the F1 point's relation to every neighbour, so no graph of existing nodes can produce it. The per-wall kite mosaic has no equivalent at all.
[CellCoverage, distribution-topology] F1 and F1/F2 level sets cover a different fraction per cell, so large cells fill differently from small ones. Here thresholding has an exact area meaning cell by cell, and Halftone preserves local mean without any neighbour pass. Another lab lens prototyped this gauge (rel_gauge) for its facets; the additions here are the rho^D exact-uniform output, the coverage guarantee, and area-exact halftoning.
ideas.simd_plan: Fixed-size stack arrays for the window points. Pass 2 uses a masked reciprocal (den floor handles j==i by giving a value below 1 once masked out). No branches. 3^D window, the same hashes as CellularDistance plus one dot and one reciprocal per cell. Estimate: about 1.4x CellularDistance (2D 5-6 ns, 3D 17 ns, 4D 60 ns). Measured scalar with 3x3: 0.8x worley2. Generic GenT works since nothing is dimension-specific. 3D prototyped through the same template.
ideas.continuity: C0: every wall has g=1 from both sides. check gives c0ratio 8.00 in 2D with win=1 and win=2, and z-continuity is fine in 3D. Facet-id mode is intentionally discontinuous.
ideas.params: Grid Jitter (hybrid), Min Spacing dmin (float), Output enum (Facets, ApexHeight, Rings, FacetId), Ring Count (hybrid), VariableRange.
ideas.risks:
Two very close feature points make steep needle creases (max slope about 30 without dmin). The dmin floor stays C0 because both sides of a wall use the same den. A 3x3 pass 2 can miss a neighbour outside the window at high jitter, though check showed no jumps at the FastNoise jitter radius of 0.437.
[CellCoverage, distribution-topology] Exact homothety needs Euclidean bisectors, so other distance functions do not apply. 4D is expensive. Reduced 3^D windows need the jitter limit or facets will be missed and contours bend. Halftone Level sampled at the site makes spot size stepwise per cell, which is correct but visible at low density.
ideas.variant_notes: The polygonal gauge, with rho^D making output exactly uniform per cell (CellCoverage), so a threshold covers exactly X percent of every cell (measured std 0.0016 vs 0.063 for F1^2). Halftone and kite-facet outputs included.
ideas.cost_note: Estimate: about 1.4x CellularDistance (2D 5-6 ns, 3D 17 ns, 4D 60 ns). Measured scalar with 3x3: 0.8x worley2.

ideas.name: RecursiveCutNoise
ideas.one_liner: Stateless recursive hyperplane cuts: a fixed loop that gives shattered-glass, Mondrian and crack patterns with real T-junctions, at a cost independent of dimension.
ideas.algorithm:
id=seed; f=F0; d=inf.
for level l in 0..Levels-1:
  h=mix(id,l)
  keep = rnd(h) >= Skip  (mask)
  w = direction from h: table of unit vectors, or one axis in AxisAligned mode
  t = dot(w,x)*f + phi(h)
  fl=Floor(t); fr=t-fl
  dl=min(fr,1-fr)/f
  d=Select(keep, min(d,dl), d)
  id=Select(keep, mix(id ^ int(fl)*PrimeX, l), id)
  f*=Ratio  (1.41 halves cell area per level)
The next level's lines depend on the parent cell id, so a line stops at its parent's border: T-junctions, which Worley cells cannot make.
Output enum: Crack = saturate(d/Width)*2-1. CellValue = rnd(mix(id)). Value x crack. Plane tilt = dot(hashdir,x-local) per cell.
Optional root: id0 from nearest Voronoi site (one Cellular search) so level-0 lines are not global.
ideas.look: Prototype cl_cut sheet (levels 7, Ratio 1.41, Skip .3): stained glass, smashed window, angular shards; the 3D XZ slice works directly. AxisAligned: Mondrian panels, city blocks, circuit boards, glitch rects. Crack output for dried mud, crazed glaze, fault lines. FFT is a star of streaks, utterly unlike the rest of the sheet.
ideas.why_new: All existing cell nodes are Voronoi: convex cells, Y-junctions, no hierarchy. Hyperplane recursion gives long straight lines, T-junctions and wide cell size variety. It is also the only cell pattern whose cost does not rise with dimension. Guehl et al. list iterative cell subdivision imitating STIT tessellations as a new cellular noise; this version needs no precomputed wave table.
ideas.simd_plan: Per level: hash, direction lookup, dot, Floor, 2 Selects, ~25-30 ops, ~.35 ns. Levels=7: ~2.5 ns in 2D (2.3x Perlin) and about the same in 4D (0.7x Perlin, 16x cheaper than CellularDistance 4D). Pure GenT<P...>; id is per lane int32v, so no masks beyond keep. Scalar 4x perlin2 at L=6, using trig the port replaces with a table.
ideas.continuity: Crack output C0, c0ratio 7.2-7.8: d is 0 on both sides of a crossed line, and inside a convex cell it is the min of plane distances. CellValue is discontinuous by design (Output Min/Max range still holds).
ideas.params: Int: Levels. Float: F0, Ratio. Hybrid: Skip, Width. Enum: Direction (Random, AxisAligned, K-fold), Output. Optional Width taper per level.
ideas.risks: Level-0 lines are global and parallel for a given seed, a visible bias at wide views unless the Voronoi root option is used. Deep levels make slivers and dust if Ratio is above about 1.5 (seen at 1.5/1.6). Line spacing per family is regular, so a jittered 1D line version with 3 Selects may be needed. Hard edges alias. Thresholds need Width taper tuning.
ideas.cost_note: Levels=7: ~2.5 ns in 2D (2.3x Perlin) and about the same in 4D (0.7x Perlin, 16x cheaper than CellularDistance 4D).

ideas.name: RosetteCells
ideas.one_liner: Leopard and jaguar coats: each cell holds a broken wobbly ring, a darker interior and sometimes a centre dot, shaped by one polar evaluation at the nearest seed.
ideas.algorithm: Find F1, F2, nearest vector v and hash in the 3^D window. dir=v/|v|. n=3+floor(4*r3); wobble=1+0.18*cos2(dir,phi)+0.1*cos3(dir,phi), using Chebyshev forms; rr=R*(0.75+0.5*r5). ring=smoothstep(w,0.5w,|F1-rr*wobble|); lobes=smoothstep(-0.25,0.15,cosn(dir,phi)); inner=smoothstep(rr,0.7rr,F1)*0.35; dot=(r6<0.3)*smoothstep(0.07,0.04,F1); edge=smoothstep(0,0.12,F2-F1); out=max(ring*lobes,inner,dot)*edge. cos(n*theta+phi) comes from rotating dir by phi with a table or by recurrence, so atan is not needed. In 3D: shell(F1) with lobes from a product of cos along hash axes.
ideas.look: Clusters of 3-6 dark blobs around a slightly darker centre: recognisable as leopard rosettes. Lobe count, ring radius and dot probability span spots to rosettes to jaguar. Also applicable to lichen or coral polyps with altered profiles.
ideas.why_new: Reaction-diffusion gets rosettes by simulation, with tissue growth, which is not pointwise. Graphs can threshold F1 into rings but cannot break each ring with its own angular lobes.
ideas.simd_plan: Cellular pass plus one polar evaluation: about 5.5 ns in 2D (1.4x CellularDistance), 14 ns in 3D, 43 ns in 4D. n varies per lane, so use a Select between precomputed recurrence terms up to T6, or fix n per node for lower cost.
ideas.continuity: C0: a seam at the F1 switch is removed by edge (F2-F1), which zeroes the field at the cell boundary. Dense scanlines: 0 jumps. Random-pair ratio 9.9.
ideas.params: Ring Radius, Ring Width (hybrid), Lobes Min/Max, Lobe Sharpness, Inner Tone, Dot Probability, Wobble, Grid Jitter (hybrid).
ideas.risks: Stylised and specialised, so less of a general building block. The prototype used atan2; the Chebyshev port is untested but mathematically equal. Cell-confined rings are clipped by edge when the seed is close to a neighbour. The Malheiros preprint PDF was unreadable through the fetch tool, so biological staging is not drawn from it.
ideas.cost_note: Cellular pass plus one polar evaluation: about 5.5 ns in 2D (1.4x CellularDistance), 14 ns in 3D, 43 ns in 4D. n varies per lane, so use a Select between precomputed recurrence terms up to T6, or fix n per node for lower cost.

ideas.name: ShatterBSP
ideas.one_liner: Each Voronoi cell recursively cut by a few random planes, giving T-junction fractures with an exact C0 distance to the cracks and no extra window.
ideas.algorithm:
F1 + pass 2 gives owner p_i and wall = min_j (d_j^2-d_i^2)/(2|p_j-p_i|). Then for k=0..L-1 (constant loop): h=mix(h,k); n=unit vector from h; s=dot(x-c,n); if hash says active: crack=max(crack, depth_k*profile(|s|/w_k)); c += sign(s)*n*step_k; h=mix(h, s>0). Start c=p_i; step_k=0.42*0.62^k keeps the next cut inside the child; w_k and depth_k decay geometrically. Leaf id = final h. Because a leaf is convex and every bounding half-space is on the path, min(wall,|s_k|) is the true distance to the leaf boundary. Outputs: crack depth, leaf value, distance to boundary, per-leaf tilted plane.

[ShatterBSP, lattice-kernels] Base cell options: (a) Voronoi: F1 site, then d = min over window of the bisector distance dot(mid-x, n); (b) brick or hex with zero window, d = distance to base edges. Then local u = x - site, c = 0, r = 0.5, id = base hash. for l in 0..Depth-1 (constant): h = mix(id, l); gate = h01 < CutProb; n = gradient table[h bits]; off = rnd11*0.4*r; s = dot(u-c, n) - off; d = Select(gate, min(d,|s|), d); side = sign(s); c += gate*n*(off + side*r/2); r *= gate ? 0.72 : 1; id = mix(h, side bit). Output modes: EdgeDistance = 1-2*sat(d/Cap), CellValue = rnd11(id), or the product of the two. The distance is exact because for a point inside a convex polygon the distance to the boundary equals the min distance to its supporting lines, and redundant cuts are only further away.
ideas.look:
Dried mud, cracked glaze, broken glass, slate, ice sheets. Thick primary cracks with thinner secondary cracks that stop dead at their parent (T junctions), which Voronoi cannot do because it only makes Y junctions. Leaf-value mode is a sharp shard mosaic; the tilted mode is rubble. Prototyped: rel_bsp, modes 0-4.
[ShatterBSP, lattice-kernels] Broken glass, shattered ice, drying mud with long cracks, faceted rock, tectonic plate maps. Prototyped with Voronoi base: strongly glass-like, no visible lattice. Brick base works but shows axis lines at base scale.
ideas.why_new: F2-F1 has only Y junctions, a single scale and tapering walls. Layering two cellular nodes gives lines that cross instead of stopping. Hierarchical stopping needs the path-dependent state here, and no node exposes it.
ideas.simd_plan: All masks, Depth is constant. Each level: 1 hash mix, 1 table lookup, 1 dot, 2 Selects. Depth 5 costs about one Perlin in 2D, and is dimension independent apart from dot size. Voronoi base: about 2x CellularDistance (F1 pass plus bisector pass), so 8-10 ns 2D, 28 ns 3D. Brick base: 2 ns 2D, 3 ns 3D, 5 ns 4D. GenT generic is straightforward. Measured scalar with 5x5 Voronoi base: 6x perlin2.
ideas.continuity: Crack and distance outputs are C0 provided depth_k decreases with k: at a level-k cut both sides share all ancestors and value depth_k dominates deeper ones. Verified c0ratio 8.00 in 2D and smooth z in 3D. Leaf value and tilted plane are discontinuous by design.
ideas.params: Levels (int), Cut Probability (hybrid), Crack Width (hybrid), Width Decay, Depth Decay, Step, Grid Jitter (hybrid), Output enum.
ideas.risks:
Cuts are unbalanced, so slivers appear (visible but they read as natural fracture). A hybrid Crack Width varying fast may break depth ordering. Without the Voronoi top level the lattice shows as straight grid lines, so the F1 cost cannot be dropped.
[ShatterBSP, lattice-kernels] With a 3x3 bisector window a missing distant neighbour could overestimate d near far corners; capping d (Cap < 0.5 cell) hides it, needs measuring. Tree tends to many thin triangles at high Depth: shrinking off range or biasing the cut normal to the longest axis would need tracking cell extents.
[StitCrystalCellular, lit-recent] Split planes chosen through the base cell may produce cells with the base-grid square outline visible (jitter the base grid by a hashed per-cell offset or make the first split cut the grid cell at a random position to hide it). Exact EdgeDistance only counts planes in the ancestry, which is exact for the cell's own boundary but ignores planes of neighbouring cells that stop at a T-junction (harmless: those are not boundaries of this cell).
ideas.variant_notes: One random plane per node descended pointwise. Voronoi root hides the lattice but costs 2x CellularDistance; brick or STIT grid root is much cheaper and dimension-free but shows axis lines.
ideas.cost_note: Voronoi base: about 2x CellularDistance (F1 pass plus bisector pass), so 8-10 ns 2D, 28 ns 3D.
