ideas.name: SignCodeRegions
ideas.one_liner: Regions keyed by the sign bits of several noises, hashed to a value: curved mosaics with X-junctions instead of Voronoi Y-junctions.
ideas.algorithm:
code=0; f=1. For i in 0..Bits-1: code=code*2 + (S(seed+i, p*f) > Threshold); f*=Lacunarity.
Out=rndNeg1To1(hash(code, seed)).
Optional modes: Parity (xor of all bits, two-colour map with soft variant product of Clamp(beta*n_i)); Weighted (sum 2^-i * sign, ordered plateaus, soft variant with Clamp(beta*n)).
ideas.look: Tested. Same-frequency bits look like overlapping translucent curved shapes, as in layered tissue-paper collage. Lacunarity 1.4 gives multi-scale curved camouflage. Curves cross straight through each other. Uses: biome and territory IDs with curved borders, geological cross-cutting veins, camouflage, stained glass that is not Voronoi.
ideas.why_new: Every region node on the sheet is Voronoi, with convex-ish cells, Y-junctions and uniform size. This yields non-convex regions of wildly varied size with X-junctions, and a stable per-region value, with no window at all. It cannot be expressed in the graph, since there is no sign or hash-of-int node.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch free. Bits constant loop: Bits x source (Bits=5, Perlin: about 5.5 / 11 / 21 ns for 2D / 3D / 4D). Integer code in lanes, standard hash finish. Identical code for all dimensions. No window.
ideas.continuity: Discontinuous by design at region borders (ID mode). The soft Parity and Weighted modes are C0.
ideas.params: Int: Bits. Float: Lacunarity. Hybrid: Threshold (per bit via offset), Softness. Source required.
ideas.risks: Many tiny slivers occur when curves nearly coincide or lacunarity is high. With few bits the 2^Bits values collide and repeat across the map by construction, so non-adjacent regions with the same code share a value; that is a feature for biomes but not for unique IDs. A soft ParityFractal mode looked noisy in the prototype, so keep it optional.
ideas.cost_note: Bits constant loop: Bits x source (Bits=5, Perlin: about 5.5 / 11 / 21 ns for 2D / 3D / 4D).

ideas.name: SpanningTunnels
ideas.one_liner: Exact signed distance to a lattice spanning forest of capsules: every cell owns a tunnel to a hashed negative-axis neighbour (plus optional loop links and chambers), so every passage belongs to an infinite connected network and the field is a true SDF.
ideas.algorithm:
c = Floor(p). For each cell k in the 3x3x3 window (3x3 in 2D):
  h = Hash(k); q_k = k + 0.5 + Jitter*rnd3(h)   // Jitter <= 0.25
  axis a = pick from h (compute the 3 candidate parents k-ex, k-ey, k-ez and Select by mask), parent = k - e_a
  q_par = parent + 0.5 + Jitter*rnd3(Hash(parent))   // 27 extra hashes
  dSeg = capsuleDistance(p, q_k, q_par): t = Clamp(((p-q_k).(q_par-q_k)) / |q_par-q_k|^2, 0, 1); d = |p - q_k - t (q_par-q_k)|
  r_k = Radius * (1 + RadiusJitter * rnd11(h >> 20))
  sdf = Min(sdf, dSeg - r_k)
  optional LoopChance L: mask = ((h>>8)&255) < L*255; second link to parent2 = k - e_b (b = another axis from bits) evaluated unconditionally, folded in with Select(mask, d2 - r, BIG)
  optional Chamber: sdf = Min(sdf, |p - q_k| - ChamberRadius * rnd01(h >> 12))
Output: Signed = sdf scaled (ScaleOutput over [-Radius, ~0.7]); Solid = Clamp(1 - sdf/Radius). Seam proof: a segment of an out-of-window cell lies in the bounding box of two cell centres each within Jitter of its cell centre, hence >= 0.5 - Jitter from the sample's cell faces, so results are exact for Radius + RadiusJitter*Radius <= 0.5 - Jitter (clamp params to that). 4D: keep the 3D lattice and let w drive jitter phase: q_k += WobbleAmp * (sin(w+phi1), sin(w+phi2), sin(w+phi3)) with phi from h (table), i.e. tunnels breathe and loop in w at 3D cost (continuous in all four coords, so GenTileable2D still tiles).
ideas.look:
3D iso at 0: a Manhattan-ish but jittered network of straight-ish tunnel segments meeting at nodes, like mine workings, ant nests, root burrows or circuit-board vias; with Chamber > 0 the nodes become rooms joined by corridors; with LoopChance the forest gains cycles. DomainWarp (or DomainWarpCurl) turns it into organic burrows. 2D: a classic random labyrinth of corridors (every corridor reaches the edge, dead ends exist). Vertical cave layers: DomainAxisScale on y gives flattened stacked labyrinths.
[DirectedForestMaze, distribution-topology] At Jitter 0: a crisp perfect maze (right-angle corridors, no loops, no rooms). With jitter 0.5 and Bias 0.5: a dendritic drainage network with random tilts, like river basins or lightning; Bias toward one axis makes parallel streams joining a trunk; Diagonal gives braided 45-degree channels. Hillshaded SDF: carved channels of constant width and depth; the band mode around level w gives a single winding ribbon that fills the plane. 3D: a loop-free cave/root/vessel network (every tunnel leads out, nothing is sealed), 4D version tiles.
ideas.why_new: Nothing in the graph produces 1D connected networks or exact SDFs to segments. Every tunnel connects to an infinite component (no sealed pockets), the field is Lipschitz-1 (sphere tracing, uniform wall offsets), chambers/corridors in one node, 2D doubles as a maze generator.
ideas.simd_plan: Cellular.inl window loop; per cell: 2 hashes, one capsule distance (~20 ops), optional second capsule and sphere; all Select-based. 3D: 27-54 capsules ~ 1.5-2.5x CellularDistance 3D (20-30 ns). 2D: 9-18 capsules ~ 1.5x CellularDistance 2D. 4D: 3D lattice + w-phase jitter (1 Sin/Cos per lane plus a phase table) ~ same as 3D; a true 3^4 window would be ~3x Cellular 4D and is not recommended.
ideas.continuity: C0 (min of exact capsule SDFs), gradient magnitude <= 1 everywhere.
ideas.params: Radius (hybrid), RadiusJitter, Jitter (<=0.25), LoopChance (0-1), ChamberRadius, Up/Down bias (prob of choosing the vertical axis as parent), WobbleAmp (4D), Feature Scale, Seed, Output enum.
ideas.risks:
Directed-forest topology is anisotropic (all links go toward -x/-y/-z) and reads as 'grid-like' without a warp; many leaf dead ends in the forest (no isolated pockets, but dead ends are common). Radius is capped at 0.25 cells for exactness, so wide tunnels need Feature Scale, not Radius.
[DirectedForestMaze, distribution-topology] The 'single tree' property is almost-sure and asymptotic: inside any finite view several trees that merge far away are visible, so 'all corridors in view are mutually reachable' is not guaranteed, only 'no loops, no pockets, every corridor exits the view'. Hybrid Bias changing across a cell can flip that cell's parent between samples (discontinuity) unless treated as above. Right-angled graph structure shows through even with jitter; the Diagonal option and smooth-min joins help.
ideas.variant_notes: DirectedForestMaze is the same forest in 2D and states the topology honestly: acyclic and pocket-free, with almost-sure coalescence only asymptotically.
ideas.cost_note: 3D: 27-54 capsules ~ 1.5-2.5x CellularDistance 3D (20-30 ns). 2D: 9-18 capsules ~ 1.5x CellularDistance 2D.

ideas.name: SplatKernel
ideas.one_liner: Sparse-convolution noise with a shaped per-feature kernel (crater, bump, cone, ring, Gabor scratch, Wyvill blob) and per-point size/amplitude/orientation jitter, combined by Sum / Max / Nearest-on-top: craters, boulders, metaballs, scratches, spots (Lewis 1989 sparse convolution; PPTBF windowed-Gabor kernels, Guehl 2020).
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Kernel enum {Cone, Gaussian, Wyvill, Crater, Ring, GaborScratch, Dome}, Combine enum {Sum, Max, Min, NearestOnTop}, Radius (hybrid, <=0.5 cell for a 3x3 window... use 3^dim window with Radius<=1.0 cell), RadiusJitter, AmpJitter (float), Density (hybrid 0..1: probability a cell has a feature), Profile params (CraterDepth, RimWidth, ScratchFreq, ScratchLength).
Gen(p): ic = floor(p), fp = p - ic; acc = identity for Combine; for each offset o in [-1..1]^dim (fixed): c = ic+o; h = hash(seed,c); present = rnd01(h) < Density; centre = o + rnd(h) (jitter in [0,1)^dim); R = Radius * (1 + RadiusJitter*(rnd-0.5)); A = 1 + AmpJitter*(rnd-0.5); d = |fp - centre| / R (0 at centre, 1 at rim); k = kernel(d, dirs from h): Cone: 1-d; Gaussian: exp(-4d^2); Wyvill: (1-d^2)^3; Dome: sqrt(max(0,1-d^2)); Crater: -CraterDepth*(1-d^2)^2 + rimHeight*exp(-((d-1)/RimWidth)^2) (bowl plus raised rim, then clamp to d<1+2RimWidth); Ring: exp(-((d-0.7)/0.1)^2); GaborScratch: exp(-4 d^2 * aspect) * cos(2pi ScratchFreq * dot(fp-centre, dir_h)) with an elongated Gaussian along dir_h (PPTBF-style window x Gabor). All masked to 0 where d>=1 (or 1+rim) and where !present.
Combine: Sum: acc += A*k; Max: acc = max(acc, A*k); NearestOnTop: keep the k of the cell whose rnd 'height' is largest among overlapping kernels (Select by a per-cell priority) -> crater overlap order like real impact sequences. Normalise: Sum by sqrt(expected count) (measured constant), others already in [-1,1].
3D: 27-cell window, spherical kernels (craters in 3D = cavities in a density field); 4D: 81 cells (justified only for tiling).

[SparseImpulse (Craters, Boulders), lattice-kernels] For window points: gate = smoothstep(0, Softness, Density(x) - rnd01(h)). Density is sampled at the sample position, so features fade in and out rather than pop, keeping C0 with a per-lane hybrid. Radius R = lerp(Rmin, Rmax, rnd^k), heavy tailed. t = |v|/R. Profile enum: Crater = (t<1 ? t^2-1 : 0) + RimH*exp(-(t-1)^2*RimS) with outer fade; Bump = (1-t^2)^3; Ring = bump((t-1)/w); Dipole = (g.v/R)*(1-t^2)^3. Sum = sum(gate * R^AmpExp * profile(t)). Clamp or normalise by a measured constant.
ideas.look: Lunar/planetary crater fields with raised rims and overlap ordering, boulder/cobble fields (Dome+Max), metaball slime (Wyvill+Sum), scratches and brushed hairline marks (GaborScratch), polka/spot stains, pebble beaches. Shape-driven features rather than distance fields, visibly different from CellularDistance's smooth bowls.
ideas.why_new: CellularDistance only gives distances; shaping it with Remap/Terrace cannot produce overlapping summed features, raised rims, elongated scratches, or density thinning. This is the general sparse-convolution node FastNoise lacks (and the PPTBF paper shows a windowed Gabor kernel covers cells/cracks/grains/scratches/spots/stains/waves).
ideas.simd_plan: Same lattice window and loop structure as CellularDistance (3^dim fixed loop), per cell one hash + kernel (<= 1 Exp + 1 Cos). 2D ~ CellularDistance2D x 1.3; 3D ~ 27 kernels ~ 1.5x CellularDistance3D. Kernel/Combine enums resolved outside the loop (template or per-node switch), branch-free inside.
ideas.continuity: C1 for Bump and Crater (t^2 factor at the boundary), C0 for Cone, discontinuous for Disc. Max combine is C0. Measured c0ratio 8.0 for Crater.
ideas.params: Kernel (enum), Combine (enum), Radius (hybrid), RadiusJitter, AmpJitter, Density (hybrid), CraterDepth, RimWidth, ScratchFreq, ScratchAspect, Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks:
Radius must stay within the window (clamp to 1 cell, else seams). Sum normalisation depends on Density/Radius (compute expected variance analytically from the kernel or scale at param-set time). GaborScratch at high frequency aliases like any oscillatory kernel.
[Splatter, terrain-tools-engines] Extent <= 1 cell bounds the largest shape to about half the point spacing (use fractal octaves or a coarser cell with K>1 for big+small mixes); Source kernel cost; variance normalisation in Sum mode depends on Density and SizeBias (measure).
ideas.variant_notes: Sparse convolution with analytic kernels. SparseImpulse contributes the smooth density gate that keeps a hybrid Density continuous; Splatter adds K>1 kernels per cell and a Source kernel mode that overlaps StampScatter.
ideas.cost_note: 2D ~ CellularDistance2D x 1.3; 3D ~ 27 kernels ~ 1.5x CellularDistance3D.

ideas.name: SubstitutionTiling
ideas.one_liner: Pointwise descent through a substitution tiling (pinwheel 1:2 right triangles with irrational rotations, or quad/octree), with hashed per-tile stop depth, outputting tile value, edge distance, orientation, or a Source stamped into each tile's local frame.
ideas.algorithm:
Canonical tile T: right angle at O(0,0), long leg to X(2,0), short leg to Y(0,1). Top level: lattice of 2x1 rectangles of size S; cell (ix,iy) with local (u,v)=(frac*2, frac): lower-left triangle if u/2+v<1 -> (x,y)=(u,v) else (x,y)=(2-u,1-v); h = HashPrimes(ix,iy) ^ diagonal bit. Then for d in 1..MaxDepth (uniform loop):
  // pinwheel split: altitude foot H=(0.4,0.8); 1 small tile OHY + big triangle OHX split into 4 medial tiles
  small = (y > 2x)
  tile0: x0 = 2 - x - 2y ;  y0 = y - 2x                     // scale sqrt5, reflected
  big  : xb = x - 0.5y ;    yb = 1 - 0.5x - y                // scale sqrt5/2
  B = xb > 1 ; C = yb > 0.5 ; A = (xb + 2yb < 1) ; D = otherwise
  (xA,yA)=(2xb,2yb) (xB,yB)=(2xb-2,2yb) (xC,yC)=(2xb,2yb-1) (xD,yD)=(2-2xb,1-2yb)
  idx = Select chain 0..4 ; (x,y) = Select chain ; hNew = Hash(h, idx)
  stop = (d >= MinDepth) & (rnd01(hNew) < StopProb)  ; frozen |= stop (per-lane mask)
  (x,y,h,scale) = Select(frozen, old, new); scale *= sqrt5 where !frozen
  (also push a unit vector e=(1,0) through the same linear maps for the orientation output)
Outputs (enum): TileValue = rnd11(h);  EdgeDistance = S/scale * min(y, x, (2 - x - 2y)/sqrt5);  Orientation = e.x (cosine of tile angle, dense in [-1,1] for pinwheel);  Stamp = Source(x*StampScale + hashOffset, y*StampScale) i.e. the Source rendered in each tile's own congruent frame; Mortar = smoothstep(EdgeDistance/Width) * TileValue.
Quad/Oct mode: same loop with 4/8 children (x,y[,z]) = 2*frac - floor, trivially 3D. Pinwheel 3D: evaluate in xy with the z slab index folded into the top-level hash (extrusion); honest fallback, not isotropic.
ideas.look:
A crisp tiling of congruent triangles at mixed sizes (adaptive stop), where tile orientation is irrationally distributed so no two regions line up, yet every edge is shared exactly (T-junctions, no cracks, unlike Voronoi subdivision). Stamp mode gives a 'quilt' of a pattern repeated in randomly rotated, exactly congruent patches at several scales (parquet, shattered glass, aperiodic mosaics, roof tiles, circuit die). Quad mode gives a clean hashed quadtree (Mondrian, pixel-sorting, city blocks) with 3D octree support. Nothing on the sheet has exact congruent tiles with dense rotations.
[PinwheelCells, lattice-kernels] Radiating fans of triangles, stained glass, crystalline facets; hillshade reads as cut gems. Prototyped at depth 4, 5, 7: at depth 7 base rectangle is invisible and no axis direction stands out. Important detail found during prototyping: the naive midpoint split yields all five children mirrored, so orientations cancel on even depth and look axis aligned. The H-M3 diagonal split is required.
ideas.why_new:
Only known family of tilings with congruent tiles and uniformly distributed orientations. Isotropy comes from geometry, not jitter. Fans of up to many triangles around a vertex are not reachable by Voronoi, BSP or warps. Cost is independent of any window.
[SubstitutionTiling, hierarchy-multiscale] Voronoi-based patch nodes (CellularLookup, shatter/BSP variants) have irregular cells and cracks or hard borders; this gives exact hierarchical subdivision with irrational orientations, pointwise, with a user Source stamped in tile frames. Quadtree/octree with hashed stop is the 'adaptive subdivision by hash' primitive in its simplest exact form.
ideas.simd_plan: Depth loop with constant count, 5-way child select via masks then 6 table values per lane (Select chain or permute table). Scalar at depth 4: 1.9x perlin2, 0.9x worley2 with branches. Port estimate 2-3 ns 2D at depth 5. 3D: Conway-Radin quaquaversal prism dissection (8 children, ratio 1/2) with dense rotation group, needs a table derived and verified. 4D: product form min(d(x,y), d(z,w)) with hashed combined id, enough for GenTileable2D seamlessness.
ideas.continuity: EdgeDistance C0 (measured c0ratio 7.98). CellValue discontinuous.
ideas.params: Tiling enum {Pinwheel, Quad}, MaxDepth int, MinDepth int, StopProb hybrid (0 = uniform depth), Output enum, Edge Width, Stamp Scale, Source (optional), Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks:
Pinwheel top level is a visibly axis-aligned rectangle lattice until depth>=3; apply a fixed irrational rotation of the top lattice. Reflections are part of the pinwheel; Stamp of a chiral pattern will show mirrored copies (could be a toggle). Cumulative float error at depth>8 at far coordinates; clamp depth to 8.
[PinwheelCells, lattice-kernels] Without the stochastic variant geometry repeats every sqrt5^Depth*2 units and does not change with seed; base seams become visible at low depth. Depth above about 8 loses float precision in far coords (remap multiplies by sqrt5 each level). 3D dissection not yet verified. The 3D form may be weaker than 2D.
ideas.variant_notes: Pinwheel needs the H-M3 split: the naive midpoint split makes all five children mirrored and looks axis aligned (found in the PinwheelCells prototype).
ideas.cost_note: Scalar at depth 4: 1.9x perlin2, 0.9x worley2 with branches. Port estimate 2-3 ns 2D at depth 5.

ideas.name: ThinSpots
ideas.one_liner: Per-spot thresholding against a coverage hybrid read once at the sample, so whole spots shrink away individually instead of being cut by a mask: pits, freckles, rust pores, lichen, stipple.
ideas.algorithm: C=Coverage(p), one hybrid eval per lane. For each cell in 3x3: centre c(h), threshold t=rnd(h), size s=R*(.5+.5*rnd). on=smoothstep(t,t+Soft,C*(1+Soft)). r=s*on. d2=|p-c|^2/(r^2+eps). Spot profile Dome (sqrt(1-d2)), Pit (negative), Ring (rim) or Cone, masked when d2<1. Output Max (or Min for pits). Since C is read at the lane, a spot's radius near its threshold varies gently over its own disc. Reach fits window if R<=1-jit/2.
ideas.look: Look-tested (m=1). Clusters of full round spots fade to a dithered edge of ever smaller spots following the low-frequency field, unlike Multiply where spots are sliced. Reads as rust pitting edge, leopard fade, gravel patches, pores on leather. Coverage can be a StrataBands output for ring-porous wood pores.
ideas.why_new: CellularDistance cannot change density across space, and Multiply or Remap with a mask truncates features. The hard thing it makes easy is spatially varying feature density with intact features, for just one coverage eval, where CellularLookup style sampling would need 9.
ideas.simd_plan: 9 candidates, 1 hash plus mix bit fields, 1 optional sqrt deferred until the max (track max of 1-d2): about CellularDistance 2D cost, 3.5x Perlin. Coverage is 1 eval. Scalar proto 6x Perlin with a 3-octave fbm coverage. 3D 27 candidates, about CellularDistance 3D. 4D 81, about CellularDistance 4D, so real tiling works.
ideas.continuity: C0 everywhere with Coverage continuous, since r goes to 0 smoothly and profile is 0 at the rim. Measured c0ratio 3.3 because Dome has a vertical tangent at the rim; Cone or a (1-d2)^2 profile gives C1 and measured smoothness.
ideas.params: Coverage (hybrid), Radius (hybrid), Softness, Size Jitter, Grid Jitter, Profile enum, Combine enum (Max, Min), plus Value mode to output a per-spot value.
ideas.risks: Fast-varying Coverage distorts spot shape (they become egg-shaped), which is usually fine. High coverage saturates at a fixed density, so a second layer is needed for dense packing. R above window budget produces seams, so clamp it.
ideas.cost_note: 9 candidates, 1 hash plus mix bit fields, 1 optional sqrt deferred until the max (track max of 1-d2): about CellularDistance 2D cost, 3.5x Perlin.

ideas.name: TileSplit
ideas.one_liner: Window-free tile node: base bond (grid, running bond, basket, herringbone) plus recursive per-tile KD splits, with exact edge distance and a per-tile source frame for parquet, ashlar and planks.
ideas.algorithm:
Base bond: row jr=floor(y), tx=x+Bond*(jr odd), ir=floor(tx/BrickW), bounds [x0,x1]x[y0,y1], h=hash(ir,jr). Herringbone and basket use a small mod 4 table for bounds and id. Loop L levels (constant): h=mix(h,l); stop mask if rnd<Stop (frozen via Select); split axis by comparing size*rnd per axis (longer axis favoured, RowBias); cut m=lo+size*(Bal+(1-2Bal)*rnd). Select lower or upper side, update bound and h. After loop: e=Min over axes of (p-lo, hi-p), exact distance to own rectangle, T-junctions automatically correct. Local frame l=p-centre. Outputs by Mode: tone(h); bevel smoothstep(0,Bevel,e)*tone; Interior: eval source once at R90(h)*l + offset(h), times bevel. Parquet = TileSplit(Interior=Strata(GrowthAge)).

[MondrianTree, hierarchy-multiscale] Root box=floor(p/RootSize) cell; val=k*min distance to box faces; id=hash(cell). For L=1..Depth: h=mix(id,L). Split mask: rnd(h)<SplitProb(L), or Density.Gen at the box centre remapped to a probability. Split axis = longest box side (Select across axes). t=0.3+0.4*rnd(h>>8); c=lerp(bmin[a],bmax[a],t); d=p[a]-c. Update bmin/bmax by Select. val=min(val, Age*L+k*|d|). id=mix(id,d>0). Output: Crack, Leaf=rnd(id), Plate=rnd(id)*smoothstep(0,w,val), Bump=Leaf window times Source sampled in leaf coordinates (detail always vanishes at leaf edges, so per-leaf changes cannot seam).
ideas.look:
Look-tested (m=11). Rich ashlar or city-block tiling and a very convincing parquet where each plank has its own wood slice and rotation. Axis-aligned, nothing like the Voronoi family. Warps make hand-laid stone, and fractal stacks make circuit-board or greeble maps.
[MondrianTree, hierarchy-multiscale] Rectilinear rooms and streets with multi-size tiles, greeble panels, PCB layouts, floorplans. Very unlike everything on the contact sheet except Checkerboard.
ideas.why_new: Per-tile source frames do not exist anywhere: CellularLookup gives a constant per cell, and domain ops cannot jump per-tile. No search, so cost is independent of dimension: 4D costs barely more than 2D, unlike every cell node. Exact edge distance gives clean bevels.
ideas.simd_plan: L levels each with one mix, a few Selects and compares, no sqrt. Scalar 2.3x Perlin at L=3 including the mode hash; AVX2 about 1-2x Perlin in 2D. Dimension agnostic: GenT over pack with axis choice via argmax of size*rnd and Select per axis. 3D and 4D about 1.3x and 1.6x of 2D, making this far cheaper than Perlin 4D. Interior adds exactly one source eval.
ideas.continuity: Crack is C0, measured at c0ratio 8.00 with max slope 12. Leaf is discontinuous by design. Plate and Bump are C0.
ideas.params: Bond enum, Brick Width, Bond Offset, Levels (int), Stop, Balance, Row Bias, Bevel, Mode enum, Interior (generator), Interior Rotation enum, Interior Offset. Hybrid: Stop, Balance, Bevel (splits may vary across space, which moves walls, so document it).
ideas.risks:
Another lens has also explored BSP-style splitting (rel_bsp), so the new parts here are the bond table and Interior frame. Hybrid Balance shifts cut lines smoothly, but crossing a stop threshold creates a jump. Torus tiling works numerically but rectangles become curved.
[MondrianTree, hierarchy-multiscale] The root grid is visible in the proto as lines of constant period. Mitigate with large root cells and small Age at level 0, or suggest a domain warp input. Axis alignment is the feature, but the FFT will show a strong cross. A Density hybrid sampled at the pixel would jump, so it must be evaluated at the box centre.
ideas.variant_notes: Axis-aligned KD descent with no window, so cost barely rises to 4D. MondrianTree adds source-driven split density evaluated at the box centre, not the lane.
ideas.cost_note: Scalar 2.3x Perlin at L=3 including the mode hash; AVX2 about 1-2x Perlin in 2D. 3D and 4D about 1.3x and 1.6x of 2D, making this far cheaper than Perlin 4D.
