ideas.name: TruchetNoise
ideas.one_liner: Random Truchet tiles (quarter-circle arcs on a square or hex grid, tube triples on a cube) evaluated as a distance field: endless connected winding paths, mazes and 3D tunnel networks.
ideas.algorithm:
2D square: c = floor(p), f = p - c, h = hash(c). flip = h & 1 -> f.x = Select(flip, 1 - f.x, f.x). Arcs of radius 0.5 centred on corners (0,0) and (1,1): d = min(| |f| - 0.5 |, | |f - (1,1)| - 0.5 |). Arcs meet neighbours at edge midpoints, so d is continuous across cells for any random choice.
Output enum: PathDistance d; Stripe profile cos(d*Stripes*TwoPi) (multi-lane paths); Side = sign of the arc's signed distance (two-colour interlocking regions, Smith tiles: continuous regions only if the sign is chosen so colours match across edges: use the cell parity (c.x+c.y)&1 to flip the sign); Weave (Shane's over/under: 1 at |d|<w scaled by which arc is on top from bit 2).
2D hex (Shane/Fabrice): hex cell id via axial rounding (branch-free compare/select), three arcs of radius sqrt(3)/2 centred on alternating hex corners; 2 random rotations per cell (h%3) selected via Select.
3D cube (Shane's 3D Truchet): the six face centres are paired into 3 tubes; 15 pairings stored in a tiny table indexed by hash%15 (same for all lanes? no: per lane gather from a 15-entry constant table via Select chain or a 4-bit LUT). For a pair of adjacent faces the tube is a quarter torus of major radius 0.5 around the shared cube edge: d = | sqrt( (|f.a - ea|)^2... ) | i.e. d = | |(f - edgeCorner).(perp plane)| - 0.5 |; for an opposite pair it is a straight cylinder along that axis: d = |f.perp|. Take the min of 3 tube distances. Tubes exit through face centres so they connect across cells.
4D: use (x,y,z) with w selecting the hash (discontinuous in w) and document, or 4D tile with 4 tubes among 8 face centres (105 pairings table) - optional.

[TruchetNoise, lit-recent] Params: Tile enum {SmithArcs, Diagonals, Hex3Arcs, MultiScale}, LineWidth (hybrid), Depth D (int, MultiScale only), SubdivideProb (hybrid), Output enum {Distance, Mask2Colour, Stripe}.
SmithArcs 2D: c = floor(p), f = p - c, bit = hash(seed,c)&1; if bit: f.x = 1 - f.x (mirror the tile). The two arcs: circle radius 0.5 centred at (0,0) and at (1,1): d = min(| |f| - 0.5 |, | |f-(1,1)| - 0.5 |). Distance output = 1 - d/0.5 ... map to [-1,1]. Stripe: sin(2pi d/LineWidth). Mask2Colour: the Smith tile is two-colourable: colour = parity(c.x+c.y) XOR inside(arc regions) where inside = (|f|<0.5) | (|f-(1,1)|<0.5) -> gives closed blobs/regions, meandering 'maze' walls when thresholded.
Hex3Arcs: hex cell lookup (axial coords), hashed rotation among 2 states, arcs of radius 0.5 between adjacent edge midpoints.
MultiScale (Carlson): for l in 0..D-1 (fixed loop): cell at level l size 2^-l; sub = rnd01(hash(seed,l,cell)) < SubdivideProb; if !sub stop (mask 'done'); else descend. Final tile at level l*: arcs connect side points at 1/3 and 2/3 (two concentric quarter arcs radius 1/3 and 2/3 at a hashed corner, plus the 'frown/T/+' motif family chosen by hash); parity colour = (l* & 1) XOR arc-side; winged overlap handled by evaluating the 4 neighbouring tiles' arcs at the final level and taking min distance (Carlson's 'wings' = arcs extend 1/6 beyond the tile).
3D: cube cell, hash picks one of the pipe-tile orientations: quarter-torus arcs (major radius 0.5) joining 3 pairs of face centres; d = min over 3 arcs of distance to torus centreline; this is the classic 3D Truchet 'pipes' field, exact and pointwise. 4D: drop w.

[FaceTubes, texture-materials] Cell i=floor(p), f=fract(p). Hash picks a signed axis permutation applied to f (reflections and permutes via Select). In transformed cell: 2D has 2 quarter arcs at corners (0,0) and (1,1) connecting edge midpoints; 3D has 3 disjoint quarter tori along 3 mutually skew edges (standard 3D Truchet); 4D has 4 quarter arcs pairing the 8 faces. For an arc in plane (a,b) with corner c: rho=|(f_a-c_a,f_b-c_b)|, d=sqrt((rho-.5)^2+Sum others (f_o-.5)^2). Face radius: R_face=lerp(Rmin,Rmax,rnd(hash(face index, axis))), same from both cells that share the face since it is hashed by lattice coords. Arc param t=|f_b-c_b|/(|f_a-c_a|+|f_b-c_b|) (no atan). r=lerp(Ra,Rb,hermite(t)). Tube profile q=1-d/r, height sqrt(q(2-q))*r/Rmax. Output Max over arcs, or signed d-r for cave thresholds.
ideas.look:
Labyrinths, celtic-knot-like weaves, pipes; in 3D a fully connected random tunnel network (caves!) whose every tunnel joins another, something no distance-threshold of noise gives. Distinct from everything on the sheet.
[FaceTubes, texture-materials] Look-tested in 2D (m=12). Winding pipes with visible swelling and narrowing, continuous through cell borders, no dead ends. Warping makes intestine or worm-trail; 3D thresholded gives guaranteed connected tunnels. Connectedness is the main value for caves.
ideas.why_new: Connected curved paths with guaranteed continuity across tiles are a topological property; no amount of warping/thresholding existing noise yields closed, loop-free-or-not, connected networks. Caves via 3D Truchet are a cheap alternative to simulated tunnel systems.
ideas.simd_plan:
One hash per sample, no neighbour window; a handful of abs/sqrt/min and Selects. Cost ~ 0.5-1x Perlin 2D (~1 ns), 3D ~2 ns. The 15-entry pairing table becomes a sequence of Select on hash bits (or FS::Gather if available). Cube version generic over axes via 3 code paths unrolled.
[FaceTubes, texture-materials] Single cell, no window. 2D: 1 cell hash, 4 face hashes, 2 sqrt: measured 0.94x Perlin scalar. 3D: 1+6 hashes, 3 sqrt plus permutation Selects, about 1.5x Perlin 3D. 4D: 1+8 hashes, 4 arcs, about 1.5x Perlin 4D, an order of magnitude cheaper than cellular 4D. Reflection and permutation through Select on coordinate vectors works in generic GenT.
ideas.continuity: C0 given tube radius below about 0.35: on a face both cells measure distance to the face centre. check: c0ratio 8.00 in 2D, z-continuity fine in 3D.
ideas.params: Feature Scale, Variant enum {Square, Hex, Cube}, Output enum {Distance, Stripes, Side, Weave}, Stripes (int), Path Width (hybrid), Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks:
Visibly regular under-the-hood grid (paths always cross edges at midpoints); combine with a DomainWarp for organic look. Hex cell id needs a careful branch-free axial rounding. 4D story is weak.
[TruchetNoise, lit-recent] MultiScale 'loose ends' are only resolved by Carlson's winged overlap; a pointwise version needs the neighbour-tile evaluation to reproduce it, and the resulting multi-level mask parity logic needs care. Hex tiles need a hex lattice helper not present in FastNoise.
[FaceTubes, texture-materials] Pattern shows lattice in straight runs (axis peaks in spectrum); needs domain warp to hide it. Rmax must stay under 0.5 minus clearance for arcs to remain separated. 3D orientation table should be checked against the 2D proto: only 2D was look-tested. Another lens has a rel_truchet, so overlap is possible; radius hashing on faces is the contribution.
sources: Truchet tiling / C. S. Smith 1987 and shader-community 'Truchet' and '3D Truchet pipes' variants (recalled, not fetched)
ideas.variant_notes: Options merged: multi-scale Carlson tiles, 3D pipes via face pairing (PairedFaceTubes), and tube radius hashed on shared faces, so pipes swell and narrow with no seams (FaceTubes). Needs a warp to hide the grid.
ideas.cost_note: Cost ~ 0.5-1x Perlin 2D (~1 ns), 3D ~2 ns.

queue.name: TruchetNoise
queue.reason: Under 1 ns, continuous by construction, and 3D tiles give a fully connected tunnel network (J1 top pick). Find the warp recipe that hides the grid at edge midpoints.

ideas.name: WanderingColumns
ideas.one_liner: A 2D cellular field whose feature points wander independently along the third axis on closed sinusoidal paths: bundles of bending columns and twisting honeycomb cracks at Cellular-2D cost in 3D, phase-animated by w.
ideas.algorithm:
Axis = Y (enum). Window 3x3 in (x,z). Per cell k: h = Hash(k); base c = k + 0.5 + Jitter*rnd2(h); phases phi1, phi2 from bits (table); S,C = Sin/Cos(Kappa*y + Phase*w) once per lane;
 c(y) = c + WanderAmp * (S*cphi1 + C*sphi1, S*cphi2 + C*sphi2)   // each column follows its own ellipse as y changes
 optional second harmonic from more bits for less regular paths; optional per-column radius modulation rho(y) = 1 + Taper*(S*cphi3 + C*sphi3) applied as d / rho (columns swell and pinch)
 d = |(x,z) - c(y)| (Euclid; or the Cellular distance enum)
 keep F1, F2, winner hash. Outputs: F1, F2-F1 (cracks between columns), Value (column id), F1 with SizeJitter.
Validity: Jitter + WanderAmp <= 1 (same bound class as Cellular jitter). 2D Gen: a 1D window of 3 cells in x with centres wandering along y: wavy vertical bands. 4D: w adds phase (loops with period 2pi/Phase), tiles via GenTileable2D because continuous in all four coords.
ideas.look: 3D: a forest of vertical columns that lean, bend and squeeze past each other (basalt columns with curvature, organ pipes, kelp, cable bundles, vertical cave shafts); F2-F1 iso-surface: a honeycomb of crack walls that twist with height; Taper makes beaded or budding columns. Horizontal 2D slice: an ordinary Voronoi that morphs as you move up (cells change neighbours); vertical slice: wavy curtains / wood-grain bands.
ideas.why_new: AddDimension(Cellular 2D) gives straight prisms; DomainWarp bends all columns coherently with the same field, never past each other and never changing cell adjacency. Independent per-column motion changes the topology and costs ~1/3 of Cellular 3D.
ideas.simd_plan: Cellular.inl 2D window loop plus one Sin/Cos per lane and 2-4 FMAs per cell for the phase-table recombination. 3D ~1.3x CellularDistance 2D (~5 ns), 2D ~2 ns (3-cell window), 4D same as 3D.
ideas.continuity: F1/F2-F1: C0 like Cellular; the column paths are C-infinity in y and w.
ideas.params: Axis enum, WanderAmp, Kappa (bend frequency along the axis), Jitter, Taper, Phase (w rate), Distance enum, Output enum (F1 / F2-F1 / Value), Feature Scale, Seed.
ideas.risks: With one harmonic the bending is visibly sinusoidal; add a second harmonic or a hybrid WanderAmp. Columns are strictly non-branching (that is also the feature).
ideas.cost_note: 3D ~1.3x CellularDistance 2D (~5 ns), 2D ~2 ns (3-cell window), 4D same as 3D.

ideas.name: FractalDerivative
ideas.one_liner: Fractal with an internal derivative-capable basis and per-octave derivative feedback: No Man's Sky Uber noise (sharpness, slope erosion, altitude erosion, perturb), de Carpentier's Swiss and Jordan turbulence, and IQ's derivative fbm in one node.
ideas.algorithm: Internal basis enum {Simplex (OpenSimplex2 with analytic gradient), Perlin (quintic, gradient via de Carpentier's dn formulas), Value (IQ noised)} returning (n, dn). Common loop, fixed Octaves: sum=0, amp=1, freq=1, dsum=0(vec), dwarp=0(vec). Octave o: pos = p*freq + Warp*dwarp (Swiss: (p + warp*dsum)*freq); (n,dn) = basis(seed+o, pos); Sharpness s in [-1,1]: billow = 2|n|-1, ridge = 1-2|n|; n' = lerp(n, billow, max(s,0)); n' = lerp(n', ridge, max(-s,0)); dn' uses n*dn in place of sign(n)*dn (de Carpentier's artifact-free substitute). Altitude erosion: a_o = amp * lerp(1, clamp(sum,0,1), AltitudeErosion). Slope erosion: a_o *= 1/(1 + SlopeErosion*dot(dsum,dsum)) (IQ 1/(1+d.d)). sum += a_o*n'; dsum += a_o*dn'; dwarp += Perturb*n*dn (Jordan's warp accumulator); freq*=Lacunarity; amp*=Gain; optional per-octave rotation of p (2D 2x2 matrix [0.8,-0.6;0.6,0.8], 3D fixed rotation). Mode presets: Swiss = {ridge, dsum += amp*dn*(-n), amp *= gain*clamp(sum,0,1), pos=(p+warp*dsum)*freq, defaults gain 0.6 warp 0.15}; Jordan = {n2 = n*n, sum += damped*n2, dwarp += warp*n*dn, ddamp += damp*n*dn, damped = amp*(1 - dampScale/(1+dot(ddamp,ddamp))), defaults gain1 0.8 gain 0.5 warp0 0.4 warp 0.35 damp0 1 damp 0.8}; IQ = {raw n, a_o = amp/(1+dot(dsum,dsum))}. Output ScaleOutput by analytic amplitude bound (VariableRange).
ideas.look:
Prototype cl_flowfrac: Damp .15 on ridged gives clean thin connected ridge networks; on FBm gives smooth slopes with detail only on flats, like eroded or wind-scoured land. Swirl at .03-.1 pulls fine octaves along coarse contours: flowing streaks and crumpled silk; Swirl .25+ gives topographic hair lines. Advect darkens creases like wrinkled skin.
[FractalUber, terrain-tools-engines] Eroded-looking mountains with sharp ridges and smooth sediment-filled valleys (slope erosion flattens where accumulated gradient is high), billowy Jordan hills with gully-like warps, Swiss sharp crests. Visibly different from FBm/Ridged: valleys are flat, ridges are knife-like, detail is where slopes are.
ideas.why_new: Nodes output one float, so octave-to-octave gradient feedback cannot be built in a graph; finite-difference emulation would cost 3-5 evals per octave and still cannot warp by the accumulated gradient. This is the single most cited 'how do AAA terrain look good' trick (NMS GDC 2017, de Carpentier, Elevated).
ideas.simd_plan:
Constant octave loop, all formulas branch free. Fork's measurements, AVX2, Simplex, 5 octaves, 4096 points: FBm 38.5 / 76.7 / 105 us; analytic damped 56.2 / 107.4 / 214.8 us; forward differences 120 / 267.9 / 470.9 us (2D/3D/4D). So about 1.4 to 2x FBm with analytic gradients. Swiss and Jordan add only a position add per octave.
[FractalGradientFeedback, lit-classic] Fixed loop: Octaves x (d+1) Source evals with FD = 3x/4x/5x FractalFBm cost. 2D 6 octaves of Simplex ~20 ns; analytic gradient drops it to ~1.3x FBm (see notes on a Gradient virtual). Scalar 8.9x perlin2 at 6 octaves using analytic derivatives. Same GenT structure as FractalFBm, members are hybrids sampled once per Gen.
ideas.continuity: C0 in theory. Prototype c0ratio 7.5 at 2 octaves, falling to 2.85 at 6 octaves because domain feedback compounds slope (slope effect, not a jump). The ridged+damp case with sign-based gradient measured 1.18, a true jump, so the -n*g form is mandatory.
ideas.params: Basis enum, Octaves (int), Lacunarity, Gain (hybrid), Sharpness -1..1 (hybrid), Slope Erosion (hybrid), Altitude Erosion (hybrid), Perturb/Warp (hybrid), Damping (Jordan), Octave Rotation (bool), Mode enum {Uber, Swiss, Jordan, IQ}, Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks:
Many knobs; amplitude normalisation is data dependent (slope erosion reduces amplitude unpredictably) so Output Min/Max will be approximate; derivative accumulation in 4D doubles register pressure.
[FractalDerivative, repo-demand] GenGradient touches every coherent generator's kernel and dispatch. Overlaps upstream plans, so coordinate with existing fork design. Fork reported an unexplained 32-bit MSVC AVX512 build failure. Fractal range is unbounded (#212 complaints) and damping complicates normalising further.
[FractalGradientFeedback, lit-classic] Advect or Swirl above small values alias quickly, since feedback amplifies per octave; recommended range is narrow, perhaps scale by 1/f. Output needs clamp. FD on non-smooth Sources gives noisy directions. Swirl 3D form untested.
ideas.variant_notes: Unified loop covering IQ slope damping, Swiss, Jordan, Uber (sharpness, altitude erosion, perturb) and flow-noise advection. The Swiss -n*g form is mandatory: a sign(n)*g form measured a real jump. A fork has already merged the damped mode with analytic gradients, with AVX2 numbers in simd_plan.
ideas.cost_note: So about 1.4 to 2x FBm with analytic gradients.

queue.name: FractalDerivative
queue.reason: Uber, Swiss and iq derivative fBm: the most demanded terrain fractal, 1.4-2x FBm measured on a fork (J1, J2, J4 top pick). Its gradient basis is plumbing for ~15 other ideas, so build it first and diet the knobs.

ideas.name: FractalMultifractal
ideas.one_liner: Musgrave-style multiplicative, hybrid and heterogeneous multifractals plus a lognormal multiplicative cascade (Kolmogorov intermittency): octaves modulate each other instead of adding, giving smooth lowlands with rugged peaks or intermittent spiky fields.
ideas.algorithm:
Common: s_i = Source(seed+i, x*Lacunarity^i), gain_i = Gain^i (or Lacunarity^(-H*i)).
Mode Multiplicative (Musgrave 'multifractal'): v = Prod_i (Offset + s_i*gain_i) ; output remapped by measured range.
Mode Hybrid (Musgrave hybrid multifractal): v = (s_0+Offset)*1; w = v; for i>=1: w = Min(w,1); sig = (s_i+Offset)*gain_i; v += w*sig; w *= sig.
Mode Heterogeneous (Musgrave hetero terrain): v = s_0 + Offset; for i>=1: inc = (s_i+Offset)*gain_i*v; v += inc   (roughness proportional to current height).
Mode Cascade (lognormal multiplicative cascade): L = Sum_i gain_i*s_i*Sigma; v = Exp(L - Sigma^2*Sum gain_i^2/2) (unit mean lognormal); output via Log1p/ScaleOutput or raw with VariableRange.
Mode RidgedMulti (Musgrave ridged multifractal, differs from FractalRidged by weight = clamp(signal*Gain)): sig = (Offset - |s_i|)^2 * w ; w = clamp(sig*Gain,0,1); v += sig*gain_i.
Fixed Octaves loop; all per-octave scalars precomputed when params change (like the existing fractals).

[FractalMusgrave, dcc-tools] pw=lac^-H. Multifractal: v=1; for o: v*=1+amp*S_o(p*f); amp*=pw. Hetero: v=Offset+S_0; for o>=1: v+=(S_o(p*f)+Offset)*amp*v; amp*=pw. Erosion: s=0,n=0; for o: m=sat(0.5+0.75*s/n); a=Exp(-Log(f)*((3-2D)+E*(1-2m))); s+=a*S_o(p*f); n+=a. Formulas for Multifractal and Hetero follow the Musgrave forms from memory; docs consulted describe behaviour only. Erosion is my reading of the PxrFractal description (crossover scale, sign picks which end smooths), not Pixar's code.
ideas.look: Heterogeneous terrain: flat plains and valleys that stay smooth while mountains gain detail (Hybrid/Heterogeneous); Multiplicative: sparse spiky clusters on a calm background (intermittent); Cascade: turbulent dissipation / cloud density with heavy-tailed bright filaments and large voids; RidgedMulti: Musgrave's classic sharp alpine ridges with varying ruggedness.
ideas.why_new: FractalFBm's Weighted Strength only damps an octave by the previous octave's value; it cannot do height-dependent roughness, products of octaves or lognormal intermittency. These are the standard terrain tools in Texturing & Modeling and in most terrain engines but absent from FastNoise.
ideas.simd_plan: Octaves x Source plus a few FMAs/Min per octave, one Exp for Cascade; same structure as FractalFBm (GenT, any dimension). Cost = octaves x source (+ <5%).
ideas.continuity: Same as Source: C0 if the source is. Measured c0ratio 7.85 Hetero, 7.93 Multifractal.
ideas.params: Source, Octaves (int), Lacunarity, Gain / H, Offset (hybrid: spatially varying roughness onset), Sigma (Cascade), Mode enum {Multiplicative, Hybrid, Heterogeneous, Cascade, RidgedMulti}, Output Min/Max (VariableRange).
ideas.risks:
Analytic output ranges do not exist for products; needs measured normalisation per octave count (or expose VariableRange and document); Cascade has heavy tails (clamp).
[FractalMusgrave, dcc-tools] Difference from Weighted is visible but not dramatic. Range is awkward: Multifractal's analytic bound (product of 1+amp) is far wider than typical output, so use a measured constant and accept occasional overshoot. Hetero with low Offset can go negative and flip sign.
ideas.variant_notes: FractalMusgrave contributes PxrFractal-style Erosion, which changes the spectral exponent locally.
ideas.cost_note: Octaves x Source plus a few FMAs/Min per octave, one Exp for Cascade; same structure as FractalFBm (GenT, any dimension). Cost = octaves x source (+ <5%).

queue.name: FractalMultifractal
queue.reason: Musgrave hybrid, hetero and multiplicative: plains with rough peaks at FBm cost, which the graph cannot make (J1 top pick). Main work is a measured range table. Cascade mode absorbs multiplicative-cascade.

ideas.name: FractalShearCascade
ideas.one_liner: Each octave's zero isoline acts as a strike-slip fault: everything finer is displaced along the isoline tangent in opposite directions on the two sides, giving nested fault networks that offset layers and detail at every scale.
ideas.algorithm:
F=0; off=0; amp=1; freq=1
  for i in 0..Octaves-1:
    (v, dv) = gradSimplex((p+off)*freq, seed+i)
    F += amp*v
    t = perp(dv) * InvSqrt(dot(dv,dv)+eps)      // 2D isoline tangent, unit; 3D: t = normalize(dv x e_i) with e_i a per-octave hashed constant direction; 4D: t = normalize(dv x e_i x f_i) or drop to 2 planar perps
    sgn = Min(Max(v / FaultWidth, -1), 1)         // soft sign, C0 (optionally smoothstep for C1)
    off += Slip * amp * sgn * t / freq            // slip proportional to fault size
    amp*=Gain; freq*=Lacunarity
  // optional final 'Strata' stage: out = Source((p+off)*freq_final) with the user's own Source (stripes, cellular, ...) so the faults offset a chosen pattern; mode 'Self' returns F.
  out = F / sum(amp)  (or Source value)
ideas.look: Faulted terrain/texture: coherent slip lines where the pattern is sheared, with bigger faults offsetting smaller ones (coarse to fine order, like old faults cutting young layers). With a striped Source (SineWave) you get textbook displaced strata; with FBm you get torn, en-echelon ridge offsets. Clearly different from any warp on the sheet: displacement is tangential and sign-flipping, so it preserves local structure and only breaks continuity visually along the lines.
ideas.why_new: Sign-flipping tangential displacement across an octave's own isoline cannot be built from existing warps (no gradients, no per-octave sign gating). Geologists' 'strike-slip' look at multiple scales is missing in every noise library I know.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch-free, reuses gradient kernel. Window: none beyond kernels. Cost ~1.7x Simplex per octave 2D, ~2x in 3D (cross product + normalise). 5 octaves ~10 ns/sample 2D AVX2 estimate. Per-octave e_i directions precomputed when seed/params set (small table).
ideas.continuity: C0 with the clamp soft-sign (jump in derivative across the fault zone of width FaultWidth); C1 if FaultWidth>0 and smoothstep is used. Never discontinuous in value; a FaultWidth near 0 looks discontinuous but samples still vary continuously, so no NaN or seam problems.
ideas.params: Octaves int, Gain hybrid, Lacunarity, Slip hybrid (slip distance in units of the octave's feature size), FaultWidth hybrid, Mode enum {Self, Source}, Source (GeneratorSource for Source mode), Seed Offset.
ideas.risks: Fault lines are the zero sets of each octave, so they are closed loops at coarse scale, not infinite fault traces; a Ridged-style |v| variant turns them into open ridge faults. 4D form needs a decision on the slip direction.
ideas.cost_note: Cost ~1.7x Simplex per octave 2D, ~2x in 3D (cross product + normalise). 5 octaves ~10 ns/sample 2D AVX2 estimate.

queue.name: FractalShearCascade
queue.reason: Octave zero sets as strike-slip faults give nested offsets at every scale, a new multi-scale operation (J3 top pick). Risk to judge: closed-loop faults may read less tectonic.

ideas.name: FractalSlopeAligned
ideas.one_liner: FBm where each finer octave is sampled in an anisotropic frame built from the accumulated gradient of the coarser octaves, so detail becomes gullies running downhill or strata lines running along contours.
ideas.algorithm:
Needs value+gradient per octave: use an internal gradient-returning Simplex/Perlin (iq 'noised' style; the existing gradient kernels already have the dot products, derivative adds ~50%). Pseudo (dimension agnostic, vectors are D-vectors):
  F=0; G=0 (D-vec); amp=1; freq=1
  for i in 0..Octaves-1 (uniform loop):
    g = G * Sensitivity                       // accumulated slope so far
    m2 = dot(g,g); n = g * InvSqrt(m2 + 1)    // |n|<1, ->0 on flats (regularised, no branch)
    s = 1 + Aniso * Sqrt(m2/(m2+1))           // stretch factor, 1 on flats
    // Gullies: elongate features along the slope direction -> M = I + (s-1)(|n|^2 I - n n^T)
    // Strata : elongate features along contours        -> M = I + (s-1) n n^T
    q = p*freq + Drift * G                    // optional downhill(+)/uphill(-) drift of the lattice (iq)
    q' = M * q                                 // 2D: 4 FMAs; 3D: 9
    (v, dv) = noised(q', seed+i)
    damp = 1 / (1 + Damp * dot(G,G))          // optional iq erosion damping
    F += amp*damp*v
    G += amp*damp*freq * (M^T dv)             // chain rule, frame derivative ignored (look only)
    amp*=Gain; freq*=Lacunarity
  out = F / sum(amp_i)
Enum Mode {Gullies, Strata}. Drift, Damp, Aniso, Sensitivity are the knobs; Aniso 0 and Drift 0 and Damp 0 degenerate to plain FBm.
ideas.look: Terrain whose fine detail is organised by the big shapes: parallel rills/gullies that run down the flanks of coarse hills (Gullies), or layered ledges that wrap around hills like contour lines (Strata). On flats it relaxes to isotropic noise. Nothing on the contact sheet has orientation that follows the landform; FBm detail is isotropic everywhere. Good for DEM-like terrain, dunes (features perpendicular to a wind direction derived from the coarse field), lichen/bark growth along gradients, and as a heightmap whose hillshade reads as eroded.
ideas.why_new: A graph cannot access gradients of a node (scalar outputs only), so no graph can orient one octave by another. DomainWarp stretches detail but with no relation to slope; this is the first node where the frame of octave i+1 is a function of d/dp of octaves <= i.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch-free by construction (regularised normalisation, Select-free). Needs a GradSimplex/GradPerlin internal kernel for 2D, 3D, 4D (iq noised generalises; in 4D the M matrix is 16 FMAs). No lattice window beyond the kernel's own. Cost per octave ~1.6x Simplex (gradient) + 10-25 FMAs for the frame => 5 octaves roughly 12-14 ns/sample 2D on AVX2 vs 5.5 for FBm Simplex 5; about 2x an equivalent FBm. A generic-source variant using finite differences costs (D+1) source evals per octave; offer it only as 'any source' fallback.
ideas.continuity: C1 when the internal noise is C2 (Simplex/quintic Perlin): the frame depends on the gradient (C1) and composition keeps C1. Drift and Damp are smooth functions of G. No discontinuities anywhere.
ideas.params: Source kernel enum (GradSimplex/GradPerlin), Octaves int, Gain hybrid, Lacunarity float, Mode enum, Aniso hybrid (0..4, spatially variable is useful), Sensitivity float, Drift hybrid (signed), Damp hybrid, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks: Large Aniso with high Lacunarity can alias (features compressed below sample spacing); clamp s*freq. Ignoring the frame derivative in the gradient update is an approximation; it only affects how later octaves are oriented, not continuity. 4D version is expensive (mainly for tiling).
ideas.cost_note: Cost per octave ~1.6x Simplex (gradient) + 10-25 FMAs for the frame => 5 octaves roughly 12-14 ns/sample 2D on AVX2 vs 5.5 for FBm Simplex 5; about 2x an equivalent FBm.

queue.name: FractalSlopeAligned
queue.reason: Downhill gullies inside the octave loop at ~2x FBm (J4 top pick). Direct cheap competitor to erosion-filter, so compare them. Clamp stretch; may end up a fractal-derivative mode.

ideas.name: FractalSpectrum
ideas.one_liner: Fractal driven like an equaliser: hybrid Center, Width and Tilt in octave units, at constant variance everywhere, with optional Cantor or two-band spectra.
ideas.algorithm:
For i in 0..Octaves-1: x=(i-Center(p))/Width(p). w_i=Bell(x)*2^(-Tilt(p)*i)*Pattern[i]. Bell is exp(-x^2/2) or the cheaper compact (1-x^2/9)^3 clamped. Pattern is a constant table from an enum: All, Odd only, Cantor (digits 0,2 in base 3), or Two Bands. sum+=w_i*Source(seed+i, R^i*p*Lac^i), with R a fixed golden-angle rotation (2D) or fixed rotation matrix per octave. Output=sum/sqrt(sum w_i^2+eps), so local variance is constant regardless of how many bands are active.

[FractalSpectrum, hierarchy-multiscale] Precompute when params change (small tables, MaxOctaves <= 16): for octave i: a_i from log-linear interpolation of (Coarse, Mid, Fine) at i = 0, N/2, N multiplied by Gain^i; freq_i = prod_{j<i} Lacunarity * 2^(rnd11(seed,j)*LacJitter); R_i = rotation by i*RotationStep (2D angle; 3D: rotation about a hashed axis per octave; 4D: two plane rotations) composed, stored as matrices.
  Gen: det = Detail(p) (hybrid, 0..MaxOctaves); F=0; n2=0
  for i in 0..MaxOctaves-1 (uniform):
     w_i = a_i * Min(Max(det - i, 0), 1)      // last partial octave fades in linearly (or smoothstep)
     F += w_i * noise(R_i * p * freq_i, seed+i)
     n2 += w_i * w_i
  out = F * InvSqrt(n2 + eps) * NormGain       // variance-preserving: amplitude independent of how many octaves are on
Optional: Weighted Strength and Ridged variants reuse the same weights.
ideas.look:
Smooth patches running into gritty ones with no change in contrast. Sweeping Center is a zoom through scale without changing the pattern's seeds. Narrow Width gives clean band-pass labyrinth patterns. Two-band spectra give large soft forms with fine grit and nothing in between, which FBm can never do.
[FractalSpectrum, hierarchy-multiscale] Same family as FBm but (a) detail amount varies across space without any seam or popping (LOD by camera distance, roughness maps, 'fine detail only in valleys'), (b) spectra that are not power laws: peaked mid-band (sand ripples over smooth dunes), hollowed mid-band (big shapes + grain only), rising-to-fine (blue-ish grain), and (c) no octave lattice alignment (RotationStep ~ golden angle) so the sheet's faint grid-like crossings in multi-octave Perlin/Value disappear.
ideas.why_new: Hybrid Gain on FBm can only tilt from the top scale and changes contrast. Width and Center are the parameters artists actually think about (feature size and how many sizes), and bimodal or gapped spectra are not reachable by any Gain or Lacunarity setting. Per-lane normalisation is impossible in a graph without many extra nodes.
ideas.simd_plan: Same as FBm: Octaves evals of the source regardless of weight (no skip possible), plus about 8 ops per octave for weight. Golden-angle rotation is a per-octave constant. Cost: octaves x source + 3 hybrid evals. Exp can be replaced with the polynomial.
ideas.continuity: C1 if source and hybrids are C1. Measured c0ratio 5.05 only because high octaves are steep; no jumps seen.
ideas.params: Source, Octaves (int), Lacunarity, Center (hybrid), Width (hybrid), Tilt (hybrid), Pattern enum, Octave Rotation.
ideas.risks:
Output is not bounded by construction: measured about +/-1.46. Needs measured scaling or soft clamp. All octaves cost even when weighted zero. Cantor and Odd patterns may look only subtly different from FBm; only Bell with varying Center and Width was prototyped.
[FractalSpectral, signal-phase] Weight renormalisation per lane changes the variance where few octaves are active (RMS mode fixes). All octaves are always paid for even where the band excludes them (inherent to data-parallel). Name clash risk with 'band-pass' expectations: it is a band in octave index, not a spatial filter.
[FractalSpectrum, hierarchy-multiscale] Low novelty by design; its value is usability. Variance normalisation changes the look relative to FBm when Detail is low (single octave at full amplitude).
ideas.variant_notes: Per-lane octave weights with variance normalisation. Includes hybrid band Center/Width/Tilt, gapped spectra (Cantor, two-band), a fractional Detail cut-off, and per-octave rotation and lacunarity jitter.
ideas.cost_note: Cost: octaves x source + 3 hybrid evals.

queue.name: FractalSpectrum
queue.reason: Hybrid per-octave weights at constant variance: a strong graph control that is still FBm visually. Only normalisation needs testing.

ideas.name: IsoFocusFractal
ideas.one_liner: Octaves that exist only near a chosen level set: fractal coastlines and surfaces with smooth interiors, at FBm cost.
ideas.algorithm: rem=sum of amplitudes. h=a0*Source0. For i=1..Octaves-1: rem-=a_(i-1); gate=1-smoothstep(0, Focus*0.7*rem, |h-Level(p)|); h+=a_i*Source_i(p)*gate. The gate radius tracks how much the remaining octaves could still move the value, so with Focus>=1 almost any point able to change sides of the level still gets all its detail. Points that could never reach the level stay smooth.
ideas.look: Soft hills and basins with an intricately crinkled shore. In 3D, smooth cave-field interiors with a detailed surface, closer to a distance field. A threshold looks like FBm but the height field does not.
ideas.why_new: Weighted Strength and hetero-terrain tie detail to high or low values, not to a specific level, and detail shows everywhere else. This aims detail exactly at the set you threshold, which keeps the look of FBm's coastline but a calm heightfield for shading, slopes and gradient-based uses. A graph would need a Fade plus Remap per octave.
ideas.simd_plan: Same as FBm plus about 6 ops per octave. Fixed loop on Octaves. No early out; gated octaves are still evaluated. Cost about 1.05 x FBm.
ideas.continuity: C1 if source is C1: smoothstep of |d| has zero slope at d=0, so the abs kink vanishes. Measured c0ratio 3.58, driven by steep high octaves, no jumps seen.
ideas.params: Source, Octaves, Gain (should be hybrid), Lacunarity, Level (hybrid), Focus Width.
ideas.risks: Visual change is subtle at low Gain; it needs Gain above 0.5 to show. Periodic-level variant (many contours) looked close to plain FBm and was dropped. Claimed coastline equivalence with FBm at Focus>=1 is reasoned, not tested. Output range is not exactly FBm's; measured +/-0.76 with proto scaling.
ideas.cost_note: Cost about 1.05 x FBm.

ideas.name: KIFSFractal
ideas.one_liner: Kaleidoscopic IFS / escape fold fractals as a texture: Kali inversion, Mandelbox box+sphere fold, Menger and Sierpinski folds iterated a fixed count with orbit-trap, distance-estimate and smooth-escape outputs; hybrid fold constant for spatially varying Julia sets.
ideas.algorithm:
p = x*Scale (optionally Tiled: p = frac(x)-0.5 with the fold constant C hashed per cell, giving a quilt of different fractal tiles). dr = 1; trapMin = inf; trapAvg = 0
for it in 0..Iterations-1 (fixed):
  Kali:       r2 = dot(p,p)+eps ; dr *= 1/r2 ; p = Abs(p)/r2 - C
  Mandelbox:  p = Clamp(p,-1,1)*2 - p                                       // box fold
              r2 = dot(p,p); m2 = MinRadius^2; f2 = FixedRadius^2
              k = Select(r2<m2, f2/m2, Select(r2<f2, f2/r2, 1))             // sphere fold
              p *= k; dr *= k; p = S*p + C; dr = dr*|S| + 1
  Menger:     p = Abs(p); sort components descending (2-3 compare/Select swaps); p = S*p - C*(S-1); dr *= S
  Sierpinski: fold across the 3 planes x+y, x+z, y+z (p.xy = (p.x+p.y<0)? -p.yx : p.xy etc. via Select); p = S*p - C*(S-1); dr *= S
  trapMin = Min(trapMin, dot(p,p)); trapAvg += Exp(-TrapScale*dot(p,p))
Outputs: OrbitTrapMin = 1 - 2*Sqrt(trapMin)/range ; OrbitTrapAvg = trapAvg/Iterations*2-1 ; DistanceEstimate = Sqrt(dot(p,p))/dr (Mandelbox: 0.5*log(r)*r/dr) clamped and remapped ; LastLength = tanh(|p|).
Seed: perturbs C by Seed*0.001 and picks a per-iteration rotation angle from a hash (optional 'Twist' param, 1 sincos per iteration).

[InversionLace, dynamics-iteration] Warp: q=p+W*(n1(p*0.5), n2(p*0.5)). Fold: rotate by a small fixed angle, then a=tri(q,period). c=c0+Ca*(n3(p*0.35), n4(p*0.35)). Repeat N (8..12): a=|a|/Max(a.a,1e-3)-c; L=|a|; acc+=|L-last|; last=L. Output 0.7*log(acc/N+0.01). Direct folding works in any dimension. Prototype: dyn_lens mode=39,N=8 and without warp mode=14,N=10 for comparison.
ideas.look:
Self-similar structure at every scale from only ~8-12 iterations: Kali gives electric filaments, organic cathedral veins and exponential peaks/holes when used as displacement; Mandelbox orbit traps give crystalline boxes-in-boxes circuitry; Menger gives sponge slices; Sierpinski gives gasket lattices. In Tiled mode: a quilt of distinct fractal medallions.
[InversionLace, dynamics-iteration] Verified in prototype. With warp: bubble clusters, soap foam and lace rims with fine detail of varying scale, small dark cracks between; without warp a clear periodic ornament grid. Good for alien organic detail, cellular foam, tooled metal or ornament, procedural filigree.
ideas.why_new: FBm is only statistically self-similar; these are geometrically self-similar with sharp hierarchical detail (sci-fi hull plating, circuitry, mineral veins, alien ornament) and are cheap. Hybrid C lets a slow noise morph the fractal across space, which is unique to a node implementation.
ideas.simd_plan: Fixed Iterations loop; per iteration Abs/Clamp/Min/Select and one Reciprocal; no lattice. Est. AVX2 10 iterations: ~2-4x Perlin in 2D, dimension agnostic (GenT; Sierpinski/Menger folds generalise to d planes). 4D works (Kali is any-dimensional). Guard dot(p,p) with eps, clamp DE.
ideas.continuity: Fold maps (Abs, Clamp, sphere inversion, plane folds) are continuous, so OrbitTrapMin/Avg and LastLength are C0 with fractal-dense gradient creases; DistanceEstimate is continuous outside the set and ill-defined inside (clamped); none are differentiable in a useful sense.
ideas.params: Fold enum {Kali, Mandelbox, Menger, Sierpinski}, Iterations (int 2-20), Scale S (hybrid), Fold Constant C X/Y/Z/W (hybrid per axis), Min Radius, Fixed Radius, Trap Scale, Output enum {OrbitTrapMin, OrbitTrapAvg, DistanceEstimate, LastLength}, Tiled (bool), Seed.
ideas.risks:
Not stationary: the pattern is anchored at the origin and changes with distance from it; untiled mode cannot tile and breaks the 'same look everywhere' expectation (document as texture, not noise). Tiled mode has hard cell seams. Output ranges must be measured per fold.
[InversionLace, dynamics-iteration] Parameter space is touchy: most c values are dull and only some give lace, so presets are needed. Faint periodicity remains without enough warp. Aliasing at N>10. Range needs a measured constant.
[KaliFoldFractal, shader-community] Not stationary: the pattern's character drifts with distance from the fold axes; large coordinates converge quickly to boring regions (|p| large -> |p|/|p|^2 -> 0 -> -c fixed point). Output range is parameter-dependent; needs VariableRange. Aliasing: infinite detail means it must be used at modest Iterations or with mip-aware scales.
ideas.variant_notes: Generator form with orbit traps. InversionLace shows a noise warp plus noise-driven constant turns the periodic ornament into foam and lace; good c values are rare, so presets are needed.
ideas.cost_note: About 2-4x Perlin in 2D at 10 iterations, and dimension agnostic.

ideas.name: MorseLockFBm
ideas.one_liner: fBm whose octaves cannot create new extrema or islands: coastlines get fractal detail but keep the topology of the base octave.
ideas.algorithm: F = S0(p), g = grad S0(p). For octave k = 1..N-1: f = lac^k, a = gain^k, evaluate n = Sk(p*f) and its gradient gn (forward differences, step ~0.02/f). glen = |g|. Limit lim = glen / (MaxSlope*f), where MaxSlope is the source's max gradient per unit frequency (2.2 for unit Perlin). k_ = lim / (a*Lock). amp = a * k_^2 / (1 + k_^2). F += amp*n; g += amp*f*gn. Rationale: if the amplitude of octave k keeps its slope below |g|, the sum's gradient cannot vanish there, so no new critical point can appear. Detail fades at hilltops, valley floors and saddles, and is full strength on flanks. Normalise by sqrt(sum a^2).
ideas.look: Hillshade has smooth lake floors and rounded summits with wrinkled flanks. Thresholded, it gives one clean wiggly coast with no dust islands or pinholes. Useful for terrain, continents, coastlines and masks that must stay clean at every threshold. Measured at 6 octaves, window 8, threshold at median: classic fBm 96 islands / 97 lakes / 12573 extrema; Lock=1 gives 10 / 9 / 186; the base Perlin octave alone gives 10 / 9 / 75, so the island and lake counts match the base exactly on that seed. A second seed gave 88 / 90 / 12242 classic and 6 / 10 / 203 locked. Lock=0.5 gives 22 / 21 / 3907.
ideas.why_new: FBm and Weighted Strength gate on value, so neither removes dust. Domain-specific remedies need a global pass; this one is pointwise. It is the inverse of derivative-damped fBm, which suppresses detail on slopes. Here detail lives on slopes and dies at critical points, with a stated topological reason. The graph cannot do it because amplitude depends on the accumulated gradient of earlier octaves.
ideas.simd_plan: Fixed octave loop, branch-free. Each octave costs (1+D) source evals with forward differences: 2D 3, 3D 4, 4D 5, so 6 octaves of Perlin is about 18 / 24 / 30 Perlin evals. A dedicated analytic-gradient Perlin path measured 8x perlin2 scalar for 6 octaves, against 6x for plain fBm. The gate is one Sqrt-free ratio using g2 directly: k^2 = g2 / (MaxSlope*f*a*Lock)^2. All dimensions and tiling come through the source.
ideas.continuity: C1 when the source is C1. amp is a smooth rational function of g2 and is 0 where g = 0, so it does not introduce a crease. Measured c0ratio 7.8.
ideas.params: Lock (hybrid, 0 = classic fBm, 1 = full lock), Gain, Lacunarity, Octaves, Max Slope (float, per source type), Source.
ideas.risks: The gate ignores the gradient of amp itself, so extrema drop about 60x but do not reach the base count (186 vs 75). Lock=1 removes a lot of roughness (std 0.288 vs 0.313 and a less craggy look), so 0.5 may be the practical default. Max Slope must suit the source, and FD cost is high for expensive sources. Tested only in 2D.
ideas.cost_note: A dedicated analytic-gradient Perlin path measured 8x perlin2 scalar for 6 octaves, against 6x for plain fBm.

ideas.name: MultiplicativeCascade
ideas.one_liner: Mandelbrot/Schertzer-Lovejoy multiplicative cascade as a node: the field is a running product of per-level weights that can hit zero, producing intermittent clumps and hard voids nested at all scales, optionally used as a spatially varying gain for FBm (multifractal terrain).
ideas.algorithm:
R=1; freq=1; F=0; amp=1
  for i in 0..Levels-1:
    w = noise(p*freq, seed+i)                          // Value (cell-shaped voids) or Simplex (round voids), enum
    W = Select(Model==PModel, Max(0, 1 + Intermittency*w),   // can be exactly 0 -> hard voids
                               Exp(Sigma*w - 0.5*Sigma*Sigma)) // lognormal, never zero
    R *= W
    // Multifractal mode: also accumulate a signal octave gated by the cascade so far
    F += amp * R * noise(p*freq, seed+i+1000)
    amp*=Gain; freq*=Lacunarity
  Density mode: out = ScaleOutput( R / (R + Knee) , 0, 1 )  // Knee ~ 1 maps the heavy tail into [0,1); or out = Log(R+eps) remapped (enum)
  Multifractal mode: out = F / sum(amp)
ideas.look: Density mode: sparse bright clumps separated by large empty regions, with voids of all sizes carved out of clumps (Intermittency>1 gives true zero floors, so the void set is the union over scales). Reads as rain cells, galaxy filaments, lichen colonies, ore veins, population density. Multifractal mode: terrain where roughness itself is patchy and inherited hierarchically (smooth basins next to very rough massifs, rough patches containing rougher sub-patches), unlike FBm's uniform roughness.
ideas.why_new: exp(FBm) alone is a trivial graph (PowFloat of FBm) and is NOT this: the p-model with max(0,...) kills regions at each level, so voids are not expressible as a function of the FBm sum. Weighted Strength in FractalFBm is a cousin (gain modulated by the previous octave's own value), but it cannot zero out, uses the signal octave as the weight, and has no lognormal/intermittency control. One loop replaces N Multiply+Remap+noise nodes.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch-free (Max, Exp, Select). No window beyond the inner noise. Density mode ~Levels x noise; Multifractal mode 2x that. 6 levels of Simplex 2D ~7-8 ns/sample AVX2 estimate; 2D/3D/4D free via GenT since it is just noise calls.
ideas.continuity: Same as the inner noise (C2 Simplex) except at the p-model zero floor where Max(0,.) is C0; the product stays continuous.
ideas.params: Levels int, Lacunarity, Model enum {PModel, Lognormal}, Intermittency hybrid (p-model, 0..3), Sigma hybrid (lognormal), Inner noise enum {Value, Simplex}, Output enum {Density, Log, Multifractal}, Gain hybrid (multifractal), Knee float, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks: Heavy-tailed range: normalisation must be by knee/log remap, not by measured max. With Value inner noise and Lacunarity exactly 2 the voids align to a quadtree (desirable for a Cantor look, but visibly axis aligned).
ideas.cost_note: 6 levels of Simplex 2D ~7-8 ns/sample AVX2 estimate; 2D/3D/4D free via GenT since it is just noise calls.

ideas.name: OrderStatFractal
ideas.one_liner: Fractal that combines octaves by order statistic instead of sum: Max, Min, Median or any fractional rank of the scaled octaves via a fixed sorting network, bounded in [-1,1] for any octave count, giving blobs-within-troughs and karst-like nesting.
ideas.algorithm:
v_i = gain^i * S(x * lacunarity^i, seed + i), i = 0..N-1 (N = Octaves, int member, same for all lanes; N <= 8).
Sort the N lanes-parallel values with a fixed compare-exchange network (odd-even merge; N=5: 9 CEs, N=8: 19 CEs; CE(a,b) = (Min(a,b), Max(a,b))).
Rank r = Rank parameter in [0, N-1] (float): out = lerp(v_(floor r), v_(floor r + 1), frac r) (Mode Max = r = N-1, Min = r = 0, Median = r = (N-1)/2). Fractional rank gives a continuous blend between order statistics.
Range: each v_i is in [-gain^i, gain^i] subset of [-1,1] so every order statistic is in [-1,1] without renormalisation; subtract a per-(N, gain, rank) measured median constant to centre (Centre option), VariableRange for the rest.
Weighted Strength as in FBm (amplitude of octave i scaled by the previous octave's value) applies before sorting.
ideas.look: Max: the base octave shapes dominate where they are high, and in its troughs the finer octaves poke through, so there are blobs at every scale nested inside each other (cumulus cauliflower, piles of stones, lichen on lichen); the superlevel set at any threshold is the union of the per-octave superlevel sets, so small islands are guaranteed to exist between big ones. Min: pits inside pits, sponge or karst. Median: a smooth, scale-balanced field with fewer extremes than FBm and a distinct 'plateau and gully' texture. Fractional rank morphs continuously between these.
ideas.why_new: Expressible only as a chain of ~3N nodes for Max and not at all for the median; the sorting network makes rank selection as cheap as FBm's sum. Statistically, the output range does not shrink with octave count (FBm's 1/sum(gain^i) normalisation changes variance and therefore coverage whenever Octaves changes), and the max-union topology of level sets is a property no additive fractal has.
ideas.simd_plan: Fractal.inl octave loop writing to a small fixed array of float32v (N <= 8), followed by the compile-time sorting network for the current N (switch on N outside the lane loop, 5 networks). Cost = N x source + ~2N log^2 N Min/Max ops (negligible): same as FBm.
ideas.continuity: C0 (min/max of smooth functions have kinks along the loci where two octaves tie); fractional rank is C0 too.
ideas.params: Source; Octaves (int); Lacunarity; Gain; Weighted Strength; Rank (float, hybrid possible); Mode enum (Max, Min, Median, Rank); Centre (bool).
ideas.risks: Kinks everywhere where octaves cross (fine for terrain, visible in hillshade as creases). Max mode is strongly biased positive; needs the centring constant. A hybrid Rank makes the per-lane lerp index vary, requiring a Select chain over the N sorted values (still branch-free, N Selects).
ideas.cost_note: Cost = N x source + ~2N log^2 N Min/Max ops (negligible): same as FBm.

ideas.name: PercolationFractal
ideas.one_liner: Mandelbrot percolation with soft coherent masks: gaps at every scale, from Swiss-cheese dust to archipelagos on flat sea.
ideas.algorithm: M=1,h=0,a=1,f=base. For i in octaves: n=Source(seed+i,p*f). m=smoothstep(T(p),T(p)+Soft,n). Island mode: e=sat((n-T)/(1-T)); h+=a*M*e. M*=m; a*=Gain; f*=Lac. Output: Mask=M*2-1 (lacunar dust), Islands=h/norm*2-1 (each octave grows only on land that survived all coarser octaves). Survival fraction after N octaves is P(n>T)^N, so a Coverage parameter can solve for T from a measured source histogram.
ideas.look: Mask: big empty voids surrounded by ever finer Swiss-cheese specks, like lichen, spray, corrosion, star clouds. Islands: rough land patches on an exactly flat sea. Real gaps survive at all scales, which additive FBm never has.
ideas.why_new: FBm's support fills the plane; gaps cannot appear. Graph equivalent is Remap, Multiply and DomainScale per octave and needs manual seeds. A dedicated node gives per-octave Coverage control and the correct nesting.
ideas.simd_plan: Octaves x one source eval (mask and detail reuse one value) plus about 8 ops. Dimension agnostic. Cost equal to FBm.
ideas.continuity: C1 for C1 sources. Mask world-space edges tighten at high octaves: measured c0ratio 2.04 with max slope 982 at Soft 0.2 and 5 octaves. No sign of jumps in the formula, but this should be confirmed; expect aliasing at far zoom-out.
ideas.params: Source, Octaves, Lacunarity, Gain, Threshold or Coverage (hybrid), Softness, Output enum.
ideas.risks: Coverage is very sensitive: tau -0.35 left almost nothing, -0.6 to -0.75 worked, so Coverage must be the exposed control. Mask is close to binary, so high frequency aliases. Island normaliser overshoots (measured 1.24), needs correcting.
ideas.cost_note: Octaves x one source eval (mask and detail reuse one value) plus about 8 ops.

queue.name: PercolationFractal
queue.reason: Mandelbrot percolation masks at FBm cost give archipelagos on flat sea. Coverage must be the exposed knob, solved from the histogram.

ideas.name: PuffyCaps
ideas.one_liner: A fractal sum of spherical-cap layers that gives cauliflower and cumulus tops: convex lobes on lobes, where FBm and billow give creases and blobs.
ideas.algorithm: H=0; a=1; f=f0. For octave o: X=Rot_o*x*f+offset_o; best=0; for each jittered cell in the 3^D window: r2=|X-p_i|^2; best=max(best,R_i^2-r2) with R_i=0.55+0.45*r3. H+=a*sqrt(best)/f; a*=gain; f*=lacunarity. Taking max of (R^2-r^2) and a single sqrt per octave is exactly the max of caps, with no per-cell sqrt.
ideas.look: Hillshade looks like broccoli, cumulus tops or botryoidal mineral: every lobe is convex at every scale. The contact sheet has nothing like it.
ideas.why_new: Abs(noise) billow gives long sinuous creases and irregular domes; a sum of circular caps has convex, round lobes. A graph could approximate it only by a separate CellularDistance chain per octave, with Sqrt and Add nodes, and it would pay extra per-cell InvSqrt and F-slot work.
ideas.simd_plan: No per-cell sqrt or distance sort. Estimated 3 ns per octave in 2D, so 5 octaves are about 15 ns (3x FBm of Perlin); 48 ns in 3D (4x FBm); 160 ns in 4D. Own-cell and 2^D shortcuts failed: 2^D corners showed lattice blocks, jittered corners showed fine cross-hatch, and own-cell showed a grid of balls at the coarse octave. A mix may work (3x3 for coarse octaves, own-cell or corners for fine ones), but my one mix test still showed cross-hatch.
ideas.continuity: C0: caps meet at creases where the max switches, and the outer edge has infinite slope only where the coverage gaps reach 0. Jittered windows with R up to 1.0 cover the plane well, though a cap can reach beyond the 3x3 window at high jitter (not measured).
ideas.params: Octaves (int), Gain, Lacunarity, Radius Min/Max, Radius Jitter (hybrid).
ideas.risks: Cost is several times FBm in 3D and 4D, and the cheap paths were rejected visually. Output range needs a measured constant. A related SDF form (clipped smooth union of spheres, so bumps exist only near a base surface) gave cloud-like silhouettes but looked less striking as a height field; it may suit 3D iso-surfaces and was not rendered in 3D. The fBm-of-SDF idea is from my memory of Quilez's writing, as the article URL returned 404.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated 3 ns per octave in 2D, so 5 octaves are about 15 ns (3x FBm of Perlin); 48 ns in 3D (4x FBm); 160 ns in 4D.

queue.name: PuffyCaps
queue.reason: Max of spherical caps per octave: convex lobes on lobes that FBm cannot make, for clouds and rock. 3-4x FBm, and cheaper paths were rejected by eye.

ideas.name: RegionSpectrumFractal
ideas.one_liner: One fractal whose per-octave amplitudes are hashed per Voronoi region of a coarse cellular lattice, so adjacent regions have different spectra (smooth plain, grainy plateau, mid-band hills), blended across region borders with an F2-F1 fade.
ideas.algorithm:
coarse cellular 3x3 search at RegionScale -> nearest two points, hashes h1,h2, distances F1,F2
  for region r in {h1,h2}: per-octave weights a_r[i] = Base^i * Select(bit_i(h_r) ...)  more usefully a_r[i] = Base^i * Lerp(1, rnd01(Hash(h_r, i)), Variation)  (so Variation 0 = plain FBm everywhere) ; n2_r = sum a_r[i]^2
  evaluate octaves ONCE: v_i = noise(p*freq_i, seed+i) for i < Octaves  (uniform loop, store in registers/stack array of MaxOctaves)
  F_r = sum a_r[i] v_i / Sqrt(n2_r)   for r = 1,2
  m = smoothstep(0, Fade, F2 - F1)   -> out = Lerp(F_2, F_1, 0.5 + 0.5*m)  (Fade in region-space units)
  Optional per-region hashed overall gain and a per-region 'roughness exponent' instead of independent weights (Variation controls spread). Optional sharpening of the region mask with Terrace-like hashed region 'height' offset so regions also differ in base elevation (biome plateaus).
ideas.look: Patchwork landscapes: each cell-shaped region has its own character (one is smooth rolling hills, its neighbour is all fine grain, another is mid-frequency bumps), with soft borders. Reads as geological provinces / biome tiles, the thing FBm never gives because its roughness is spatially stationary. Compared with multiplying by a cellular mask this changes the *spectrum* per region, not just amplitude.
ideas.why_new: A graph would need one fractal per region type plus a region-selection blend (N fractals evaluated); here octaves are evaluated once and reweighted twice, so N 'biomes' cost one FBm plus a small cellular search. Not aware of any library offering per-region spectral coefficients inside one fractal.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch-free: cellular window for F1/F2 (existing code), octave loop with values kept in a fixed-size array indexed by compile-time unrolled loop (MaxOctaves template or 8 slots), two weighted sums. Cost ~ FBm(Octaves) + CellularDistance(coarse, 2D 3.9 ns) + 2*Octaves FMAs; 3D/4D via the cellular window costs (41 ns in 4D), acceptable since region search is at coarse scale.
ideas.continuity: Same as the source inside regions; C1 across borders via smoothstep fade (the two blended fields share the same octave values, so the blend is a smooth reweighting rather than a crossfade of unrelated fields, which keeps features aligned across the border).
ideas.params: Source, Octaves int, Gain, Lacunarity, Region Scale, Variation hybrid, Fade, Region Height Variation, Jitter, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks: Needs MaxOctaves slots (fixed 8 or 12); with 3 or more near-equidistant regions at a Voronoi vertex only two are blended (tiny kink at vertices, same as other F1/F2 blends).
ideas.cost_note: Cost ~ FBm(Octaves) + CellularDistance(coarse, 2D 3.9 ns) + 2*Octaves FMAs; 3D/4D via the cellular window costs (41 ns in 4D), acceptable since region search is at coarse scale.

queue.name: RegionSpectrumFractal
queue.reason: Octaves evaluated once and reweighted per Voronoi region: cheap biome spectra at FBm plus one coarse Cellular. Check the kink at Voronoi vertices.

ideas.name: RootVein
ideas.one_liner: A three-tier line fractal: distance-normalised zero sets of rough noise with constant-width lines, where finer branches exist only near their parent and taper as they leave it. Marble veins, lightning, roots.
ideas.algorithm: Tier k field: sum=Sum_i amp_i*n(p*f_k*2.1^i), gradient g from only the two lowest octaves; d_k=|sum|/(|g|+Floor)/f_k. Rough sum but smooth denominator keeps width constant and jagged. Tier 0: l0=1-smoothstep(0,W,d0). Gate g1=1-smoothstep(0,Reach,d0). Tier 1: f1=BranchFreq, width W*Bw*g1, l1=g1*(1-smoothstep(0,W*Bw*g1,d1)). Gate g2=g1*(1-smoothstep(0,Reach/2,d1)). Tier 2: f2=BranchFreq^2, same using g2. Output Max(l0,l1,l2). Amplitude scales with the gate, so branches fade rather than ending as hairlines. Variant with parameter Roughness=0 gives smooth lines with hair roots.
ideas.look: Look-tested (m=15 and m=0, at zoom: window 2.5-3.5, width=.02, reach=.2, gain=.4). Thin, crisp, jagged primary veins with fine branchlets clinging only near them: very close to marble veining or lightning. Mostly black background, so it composes well with Max over cloud fields. Note: only works at low base frequency; at 1 feature per unit it degenerates into hairy noise.
ideas.why_new: Ridged FBm gives a dense uniform web whose line width depends on gradient, with no hierarchy. Weighted Strength attenuates amplitude but does not localise lines to parents. Distance normalisation and proximity gating give sparse, tree-like structure which is otherwise only possible with simulation.
ideas.simd_plan: Needs gradients: Perlin or Simplex with analytic derivative inline, about 1.3x cost each. 3 tiers x 3 octaves = 9 evals, 12x Perlin; measured 13x scalar. Worth a building block of its own, but heavy. Reduced form: octaves 2 per tier (6 evals), 8x Perlin. A Source-driven variant by finite differences needs 3 (2D), 4 (3D), 5 (4D) evals per tier, so it is more flexible but far more expensive. No window issues. 2D, 3D and 4D all follow from the noise, and 4D lines tile.
ideas.continuity: C0 with amplitude gating (measured c0ratio 1.43 from very steep thin lines; without the amplitude gate the m=0 variant measured 1.00, jump-like hairlines). Zero-set crossing is continuous; |g| floor prevents blowups at critical points.
ideas.params: Tiers (fixed at 3 or int), Octaves, Roughness Gain, Line Width, Reach, Branch Width Ratio, Branch Frequency, Gradient Floor. Hybrid: Line Width, Reach.
ideas.risks: Very sensitive to scale; a poor default looks like static, so feature-scale defaults must be set carefully. Thin lines alias without supersampling. Gate cuts branch ends softly rather than truly joining the parent, and branches cross parents rather than sprout from them. High cost per sample.
ideas.cost_note: Needs gradients: Perlin or Simplex with analytic derivative inline, about 1.3x cost each. 3 tiers x 3 octaves = 9 evals, 12x Perlin; measured 13x scalar.

ideas.name: SparseOctaves
ideas.one_liner: A soft winner-take-all between octaves: at each point one scale dominates, which gives clean smooth regions broken by patches of rough detail.
ideas.algorithm: For i: v_i=a_i*Source(seed+i,p*Lac^i). w_i=v_i^2 squared Sharp times by repeated multiply (Sharp=3 gives v^16). Output=sum(w_i*v_i)/(sum(w_i)+eps). Sharp 0 is a mild magnitude-weighted average; a large Sharp tends to the single largest |v_i|. Branch free, no Exp. Output is bounded by max |v_i|, so it stays in range for a_0=1.
ideas.look: Crisp blobs with sudden pockets of grit, heavier-tailed and more natural-image-like than FBm, where every scale is active everywhere. Reads like weathered stone or lumpy plaster.
ideas.why_new: Every octave in a Gaussian-style sum is active everywhere; real textures are sparse across scales. This couples all octaves per point, which no chain of two-input blends can do with low node count. It is not Weighted Strength, which only feeds forward and only in amplitude.
ideas.simd_plan: FBm plus Sharp+2 multiplies per octave and one divide total. Fixed octave loop. Dimension agnostic. Cost about 1.15 x FBm.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity for smooth sources thanks to eps, measured c0ratio 4.44, driven by steep values and no jumps seen. Higher Sharp makes switching regions steep.
ideas.params: Source, Octaves, Gain, Lacunarity, Sharpness (int; 2-4 useful).
ideas.risks: An exp-based version overflowed to NaN at high beta, so keep the power form. Sharp at 3-4 with Gain below 0.6 leaves the top octave always winning, so it needs Gain 0.75-0.9. Close to plain FBm at low Sharp. Denormal risk when all v are near 0; eps covers it.
ideas.cost_note: Cost about 1.15 x FBm.

ideas.name: SphereFractal
ideas.one_liner: Fractal of real spheres in distance space: carve mode gives multi-scale pumice and swiss-cheese voids, union mode grows cauliflower cumulus or rubble on any base field.
ideas.algorithm: Base d (source treated as SDF units, or constant for carve). s=S0. Loop Octaves: q = grid(R_o p / s)*s, where grid is min over the 2^dim corners of floor(p): corner sphere radius r = Rmin + (Rmax-Rmin)*rnd01(hash), distance |f - corner| - r. Union mode (cumulus): q = smax(q, d - Clip*s, Ka*s); d = smin(q, d, Kb*s). Clipping makes detail appear only in a shell around the current surface, so puffs stack on puffs (after iq's SDF fBm). Carve mode (pumice): d = smax(d, -q, Kb*s). Per octave use fixed rotation R (table) and lacunarity ~2. Each sphere must satisfy r + jitter <= corner reach. Optional RadiusBias: r scales with exp(-d/s) so puffs shrink away from surface. Sphere-sized distribution from rnd01 sets pore-size power law.
ideas.look: Prototyped. Carve: golf-ball and pumice crust with craters at several scales, strong at 3 octaves. Union: crumbly cauliflower or rubble clumps around a Perlin base; with these parameters it looks gravelly, and needs larger S0, 2 to 3 octaves and bigger smin to read as cumulus. 2D slice: discs on discs (bubbly edge) or Apollonian-like holes. For clouds, rocks, moss, sponges, bread, coral.
ideas.why_new: FBm adds values, so it can never make round overhanging lobes; here lobes are real spheres and output keeps a distance-like bounded gradient, so sphere tracing and meshing behave. A graph equivalent needs 3 nodes per octave with parameters scaled by hand and shares no rotation. Not visually near anything on the sheet, particularly in 3D.
ideas.simd_plan: Constant octave loop; 2^dim hash+sqrt per octave, plus smin/smax. 3D: about 2.5 ns per octave, so 4 octaves about 10 ns plus source. 2D 1 ns per octave; 4D 16 corners, about 5 ns per octave. Hash per corner uses the current octave's seed.
ideas.continuity: C0 at least; C1 mostly due to smin and smax, except at grid transitions where radii must fit reach. Grid reach limited so no seams when r <= reach.
ideas.params: Source (base), Mode enum, Octaves (int), S0 (float), Lacunarity, Clip (hybrid), Ka, Kb, Rmin, Rmax, RadiusBias.
ideas.risks: Parameter sensitivity: clip plus dense spheres dilates surface, and earlier test filled the whole box until tuned (base amplitude and clip must relate). Base must be roughly unit-gradient, so pair with LevelSetDistance or bound its range. The union mode is near iq's known technique; hierarchy and carve with distribution are the variation. Fine-scale octaves alias.
ideas.cost_note: 3D: about 2.5 ns per octave, so 4 octaves about 10 ns plus source. 2D 1 ns per octave; 4D 16 corners, about 5 ns per octave.

queue.name: SphereFractal
queue.reason: SDF fBm of spheres in union and carve: pumice, swiss cheese and cumulus on any base. Per-octave rotation must hide 2^D lattice blocks, and clip and base amplitude couple touchily.

ideas.name: DomainWarpCurl
ideas.one_liner: Divergence-free warp family: swirling folds with no pinches or bubbles, with a Potential enum covering lattice curl noise, sparse vortices, and curl of any source.
ideas.algorithm:
v=A*grad(psi) with A antisymmetric, so div v=0 because the Hessian is symmetric.
2D: v=(d_y psi,-d_x psi).
3D: v=grad(phi) x grad(psi) from two potentials sharing lattice corners (cheaper than Bridson's 3 potential curl).
4D: single potential v=(d_y,-d_x,d_w,-d_z)psi, which keeps GenTileable2D working.
Potential enum:
- Simplex: analytic gradient from the simplex corners.
- SparseVortex: window of jittered sites, v=sum_i G_i*A_i*d_i*s(r_i), s=(1-r^2/R^2)^3. A_i=J in 2D, cross with hash axis in 3D, hash-chosen skew plane in 4D. This is exactly divergence free since d^T A d=0 and tr A=0. Site kept when rnd<Density; G from hash with sign.
- Source: any generator via tetrahedral FD.
Constraint (Bridson boundary): psi'=psi*ramp(g(x)), so v=ramp*A*grad psi+psi*ramp'*A*grad g, tangent to g=0 contours, via FD on g. Warp() adds amp*v to the positions, so the Fractal warp nodes work unchanged.
ideas.look: Prototype cl_vortex: curl warp of stripes folds and streaks like marble with even line density; gradient warp of the same source pinches into bubble rings. SparseVortex at A=2-4 winds stripes into agate eyes and Jupiter eddies, separated by calm zones when Density <1. Marbling, smoke, gas giants, rivers that avoid a mask.
ideas.why_new: Existing warps use independent vector noise, so they are compressible and pinch. Curl warp preserves area to first order, so thresholded area of a mask stays stable. Constraint-aware flow and localized eddies are impossible with a plain Warp Amplitude hybrid because scaling the velocity by a mask breaks the divergence-free property.
ideas.simd_plan:
Simplex: ~1.2x simplex with gradient, about 2/3.5/5 ns (3D shares hash fields for 2 gradient sets; 4D single potential). SparseVortex 3^d: polys only, no sqrt, no trig, ~.8x Cellular cost = ~3/10/33 ns; R<=1.2 with jitter +-.3 is seam free. Optional 2^d window with lower jitter and R<=.9: 4/8/16 sites for ~1.8/3.6/8 ns. Source: (d+1) x Source per Warp. Fixed count all modes; plugs into the existing Warp virtual functions.
[DomainWarpCurl, volumetric-3d4d] DomainWarpSimplex.inl pattern, Perlin lattice; value+gradient per potential ~2x Perlin FMAs; 3D with 3 potentials ~3x Perlin 3D (~7 ns per warp), 2D ~2x Perlin 2D, 4D 6 potentials ~4x Perlin 4D (~17 ns). Branch-free.
ideas.continuity: C1 for Simplex potential at least (source of warp C2+), c0ratio 7.99 in the vortex prototype. No seams when R fits the window.
ideas.params: Enum: Potential. Hybrid: Warp Amplitude, Density, Constraint source. Float: Vortex Radius R. Standard DomainWarp frequency, axis scale and seed offset.
ideas.risks:
Divergence-free holds for the velocity, not the finite displacement: large amplitude still folds, so a multi-step option or the Progressive fractal may be needed. 3D form is not a true curl of one vector potential, but is still solenoidal. Tangent-only flow does not enforce no-slip. Only 2D was prototyped.
[DomainWarpCurl, volumetric-3d4d] A finite displacement along a divergence-free field is only volume-preserving to first order; large Amplitude should go through Progressive fractal steps. 4D version costs 6 potentials; a cheaper 'warp xyz only, w passthrough' mode breaks nothing for animation but is not a 4D divergence-free field.
sources: from memory, not consulted: Bridson, Hourihan, Nordenstam 2007 'Curl-Noise for Procedural Fluid Flow'
ideas.variant_notes: Seven proposals agreeing on a Warp()-family node. Implementation options to weigh: analytic Simplex/Perlin potential from one lattice visit (cheapest), 3D bitangent cross of two gradients vs three-potential curl, 4D paired planes vs six-component 2-form, Bridson boundary mask. Only 2D was prototyped.
ideas.cost_note: SparseVortex 3^d: polys only, no sqrt, no trig, ~.8x Cellular cost = ~3/10/33 ns; R<=1.2 with jitter +-.3 is seam free.

ideas.name: DomainWarpFlow
ideas.one_liner: Advect the sample point through N steps along the rotated gradient of any potential node: curl gives ink marbling, gradient gives watershed cells, path modes give slope blur and LIC.
ideas.algorithm: q = p. For i in 0..Steps-1: psi0 = Potential(q); g = forward-difference gradient of Potential at q; v = cos(A)*g + sin(A)*J*g, where J is antisymmetric (2D J(x,y) = (-y,x); 3D J = cross(axis, .); 4D pairs xy and zw). If Normalize: v /= sqrt(|g|^2 + eps). q += v * Length / Steps. If PathMode != End: acc = Combine(acc, Source(q)). Result: PathMode == End ? Source(q) : acc (Average, Min, Max). A = 90 degrees: v is divergence free in every dimension and psi is conserved along the exact flow because g.J.g = 0, so the warp cannot pinch. A = 0: hill climbing; every point falls toward a basin peak of psi, so Source is sampled near the peak, giving a segmentation into catchments with curved organic borders. A = 0 with Average/Min/Max is Substance-style Slope Blur; A = 90 with Average is a line integral convolution.
ideas.look:
Look-tested (modes 25, 26). 6 curl steps: vortices, folded ink marbling. A=0 L=1: leathery glossy plate cells, not Voronoi, with basins and curved seams. Slope blur on a hard mask: crumbled, eroded coastlines. Single-step curl alone looked ordinary, so the multi-step is what matters.
[SpiralSinkWarp, dynamics-iteration] Verified in prototype. Dense field of hooks, whorls and spiral arms, one per basin, in both rotation senses around maxima and minima; like Van Gogh swirl, hurricane fields, or ammonite ribs. Hillshade reads as wind-carved scrolls. Good for storms, gas giants, stylised ornament, fur whorls.
ideas.why_new: Existing warps take one evaluation of a built-in noise and pinch. Here the vector field comes from any graph (terrain, cellular, masks) and is iterated. Watershed segmentation in particular is a shape family absent from the sheet. A graph cannot express this because it requires per-lane gradient of a subtree at moved positions, repeatedly.
ideas.simd_plan: Constant Steps, no per-lane loop exit. Steps*(dim+1) Potential evals + 1 Source (or Steps Source evals in path modes). At 6 steps on Perlin potential: 18/24/30 evals = 20/53/129 ns. J is fixed per node so no branching. Implement as Warp() so the DomainWarpFractal family can wrap it. 4D is a pure function of the torus coordinates, so tiling survives. Justify cost by look; 2D use is affordable, 3D medium, 4D expensive.
ideas.continuity: C0 for finite steps with a C1 potential and Normalize off: measured c0ratio 6.5 (curl) and 7.6 (A=0). Normalize on makes the field discontinuous at critical points. Path modes on a discontinuous source stay discontinuous.
ideas.params: Source, Potential (generators), Steps (int), Length (hybrid), Angle (hybrid), Normalize (bool), Path Mode enum, Axis (3D), Gradient Step h.
ideas.risks:
Euler overshoot at high speed gives fine tangled filaments that alias (maxSlope 241 in the test), so a midpoint option may be needed. Needs a C1 potential; F1 potentials misbehave. A=0 collapses Source detail. Path modes show the discrete step count as bands on hard masks. LIC with gradient-noise input looked weak with visible lattice grid in my test (white-ish input would be needed), so LocalFrame rotate is the better streak tool.
[SpiralSinkWarp, dynamics-iteration] The source needs to be 3..6x higher frequency than the flow or arms do not show. Unit-speed steps cause small limit cycles at the sink centres, visible as a tiny knot; decay the step. In 3D the look is less iconic.
ideas.variant_notes: Angle sets the regime: 0 is a pure gradient flow, 90 is curl, in between is a spiral sink (SpiralSinkWarp, whorls and hurricane arms, with both senses around maxima and minima).
ideas.cost_note: At 6 steps on Perlin potential: 18/24/30 evals = 20/53/129 ns.

ideas.name: DomainWarpSine
ideas.one_liner: Iterated rotated sine shears: an exactly area-preserving, lattice-free fluid warp at a fraction of simplex warp cost.
ideas.algorithm: freq = 1/Scale. For i in 0..Octaves-1: phase = freq*dot(p, n_i) + phi_i(seed); p += Amp * d_i * sin(phase) / freq; freq *= Lacunarity (default 1.4). Then Source(p). n_i and d_i are orthonormal pairs from a constant table: 2D rotates by (0.6, 0.8) each octave; 3D and 4D use precomputed irrational axes. phi_i from seed hash bits plus i. Each step is a shear, so Jacobian det = 1 + g'*(d.n) = 1 exactly: pointwise area-preserving in any dimension, no pinch, and the Source histogram is preserved.
ideas.look: Smooth folded ribbons, ink in water, flowing marble when applied to a stripe source. No lattice imprint. Look-tested (mode 15): strong fluid-like folds, clearly different from Warp Gradient and Warp Simplex on the sheet, which show pinched highlights.
ideas.why_new: Existing warps cost a noise evaluation per axis or per octave and have lattice signature plus pinch-related contrast change. This one is orders of magnitude simpler per octave, has no hash per lattice corner and leaves range and histogram unchanged, which makes it safe to insert into any graph. Not reachable by a graph because each iteration depends on the previous position.
ideas.simd_plan: Constant-octave loop with one FS::Sin + one dot per octave and no branches. Estimated about 3 ns AVX2 for 8 octaves + Source in any dimension (scalar prototype inflated by std::sin at 5.5x Perlin including 1 Perlin). Dim-agnostic via table of pairs. Seed via a single hash per call then bit-shifted per octave. 4D is automatically tile-safe.
ideas.continuity: The map is C-infinity, so output has the continuity of Source. Measured c0ratio 8.0.
ideas.params: Source, Octaves (int), Warp Amplitude (hybrid), Feature Scale, Lacunarity, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks:
Quasi-periodic at low octave counts (visible plaid). Direction table is constant so seeds change only phases, and different seeds can look related at large scale. High amplitude gives thin filaments that alias. A hybrid amplitude loses exact area preservation (d*g becomes spatially modulated). SIMD Sin accuracy at far coordinates needs checking; scalar check at 4e4 was fine.
[DomainWarpSine, shader-community] Large amplitudes fold the domain (overlaps), as with any warp; visible 1D-wave structure at Layers<3. Sine phase precision far from origin (use range-reduced Sin, same as SineWave).
ideas.variant_notes: The Xor-style form displaces each axis by a sine of another rotated axis; the shear form here is what gives exact area preservation.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated about 3 ns AVX2 for 8 octaves + Source in any dimension (scalar prototype inflated by std::sin at 5.5x Perlin including 1 Perlin).

ideas.name: DomainWarpSource
ideas.one_liner: A DomainWarp-family node whose warp vector is the finite-difference gradient or curl of ANY source node (Cellular, Ridged FBm, Terrace, another warp), so curl-noise advection and 'warp by cellular' become one node and compose with DomainWarpFractalProgressive/Independent.
ideas.algorithm:
Implements the DomainWarp Warp() interface (vector output allowed only in this family). Params: Potential (GeneratorSource), Warp Amplitude (hybrid), Epsilon, Mode enum {Gradient, Curl, Independent}.
Gradient: w_i = (P(pos + e e_i) - P(pos - e e_i)) / (2e); pos += A * w
Curl 2D: w = (dP/dy, -dP/dx) from the same 4 taps (divergence free)
Curl 3D (Bridson): three potentials P_a = P(seed+a) for a in {0,1,2}; w = (dPz/dy - dPy/dz, dPx/dz - dPz/dx, dPy/dx - dPx/dy); each potential needs only 4 of its 6 axis taps -> 12 taps
Independent: w_i = P(seed + i, pos) (one tap per axis, like DomainWarpGradient but with an arbitrary source)
4D: Gradient and Independent are dimension agnostic; Curl 4D is defined via the 4D cross product of three potentials' gradients (expensive, 3 x 8 taps) or falls back to Gradient on w.
Then the normal DomainWarp machinery applies: Warp() is used by the fractal warp nodes for iterated/progressive warps.
ideas.look: Curl warp of a Cellular F2-F1 by a Simplex FBm potential (proto sheetB m9) gives incompressible swirls: the cells are bent and stretched into vortex filaments with no pinching or tearing, whereas gradient warps (m9_gradwarp, and the existing Warp Simplex) crumple and fold the texture. Gradient warp by a Cellular F1 potential pushes everything away from cell centres (bubble-wrap domains); gradient warp by Ridged FBm creases the source along the ridges. Through DomainWarpFractalProgressive, N curl-warp iterations approximate fluid advection: marble, smoke, cirrus.
ideas.why_new: Today the warp field can only be the built-in gradient noises; the Warp() vector is never exposed to the graph and no node can produce one from an arbitrary scalar source. Curl (divergence-free) warps are what make advection-like swirls without the folds that gradient warps create, and 'warp by whatever node you like' opens Cellular/Ridged/Terrace/warped potentials with zero new math per potential type.
ideas.simd_plan: Warp() overloads per dimension inside DispatchClass<DomainWarpSource>: Gradient 2D taps (4/6/8), Curl 4 taps in 2D, 12 in 3D; Independent D taps. Cost = taps x potential: Simplex potential 2D ~5 ns per warp, 3D curl ~26 ns per warp, i.e. 2-4x the existing DomainWarpSimplex, affordable even inside a 3-octave progressive warp. Branch-free; no lattice window of its own.
ideas.continuity: C0 whenever the potential is C0 (the warp vector is a finite difference) and the warped source is C0. Curl warps are additionally area preserving to first order so they never fold for small amplitudes, which keeps the warped texture's density uniform.
ideas.params: Potential (node); Warp Amplitude (hybrid, as in the other warps); Epsilon; Mode; Seed Offset per potential for Curl 3D. Inherits the Warp family's behaviour so it slots into DomainWarpFractalProgressive (Octaves, Lacunarity, Gain) for iterate-N warps.
ideas.risks: Finite-difference warps of a Cellular potential are discontinuous across cell edges only if the potential is (F1 is C0, so fine; CellularValue is not). Epsilon interacts with the potential's frequency; default to 0.01 of a feature. Curl 4D is heavy; a documented fallback is acceptable since tiling (GenTileable2D) only needs the result to depend on w, which the Gradient/Independent modes satisfy.
sources: Bridson, Hourahine, Nordenstam, Curl-Noise for Procedural Fluid Flow, SIGGRAPH 2007 (recalled, not fetched)
ideas.cost_note: Taps x potential: Simplex potential about 5 ns per warp in 2D, about 26 ns for 3D curl, so 2-4x DomainWarpSimplex.
