ideas.name: FeistelWarp
ideas.one_liner: Domain warp built from coordinate shears: exactly area/volume preserving and invertible at any amplitude, so warping never folds, never changes coverage and never changes topology.
ideas.algorithm: For r in Rounds: for each axis i: pos[i] += Amp * S_r,i(pos with coordinate i replaced by a per-round constant). Then apply a fixed rotation (golden angle in 2D, fixed orthonormal matrix in 3D/4D). Each shear has Jacobian determinant exactly 1 and an exact inverse (subtract in reverse order), for any source S and any Amp, which is the Feistel network construction. Rotations also have determinant 1. Evaluate the warped source at the final position.
ideas.look: Warped checkerboard: organic jigsaw cells of exactly equal area. Warped fBm at high Amp: long marbled lamellae with no pinched or inflated zones. Good for marble, fluid mixing, equal-area biome cells, and warping any mask without changing its coverage. Measured unit-cell area after warp: Feistel Amp 0.8 mean 1.000 std 0.001 max 1.005; Amp 1.6 mean 1.000 std 0.001 max 1.004. Additive vector warp: Amp 0.8 mean 1.149 std 0.452 max 3.58; Amp 1.6 mean 1.206 std 0.773 max 6.10 (upper two thirds of cells by area).
ideas.why_new: Existing warps add a vector, which folds when the gradient of the warp exceeds 1, and they change local area, so a warped threshold no longer has the source's coverage. Curl-noise warps approximate incompressibility and need integration and gradients. Shears are exact with no gradient, and exact in 2D, 3D and 4D alike. A warped CellularValue or Checkerboard gives equal-area organic cells, which is otherwise a hard global problem.
ideas.simd_plan: Rounds*D source evals: R=3 gives 6 / 9 / 12. One source call per axis with coordinate i set to a constant, no lane-dependent flow. Using Simplex or Perlin as the shear source is about 6-12x Perlin; measured 12x perlin2 scalar including a 3-octave fBm source evaluation. Rotations are constant-matrix FMulAdd. Fits the DomainWarp Warp() interface or a modifier over a source. 4D tiling is preserved because shears are periodic functions of periodic inputs.
ideas.continuity: As smooth as the shear source: C1 or better with Perlin, and C1 in the composite. The downstream source's own discontinuities are preserved.
ideas.params: Amp (hybrid), Rounds (int), Shear Source (GeneratorSource, or built-in Simplex with Frequency), Source. Hybrid Amp breaks exactness only if Amp depends on the sheared coordinate, so document that it should be a constant or low-frequency.
ideas.risks: Axis-aligned shears show through at few rounds, which the rotation mitigates. At high Amp, thin lamellae alias on coarse grids. Exactness holds for measure, not for local shape, which can stretch hard. If the source ignores a fixed coordinate there is no problem, but a hybrid Amp varying along the sheared axis breaks exactness. Only 2D was run.
ideas.cost_note: Using Simplex or Perlin as the shear source is about 6-12x Perlin; measured 12x perlin2 scalar including a 3-octave fBm source evaluation.

ideas.name: FlowWatershed
ideas.one_liner: Gradient-descent the sample position N steps down a smooth source and read something at the landing point: lake-filled basins, slope-length, catchment ids.
ideas.algorithm:
Inputs: Field F (GeneratorSource, smooth), Steps N (int, 4..12), StepLen h (hybrid, sampled once at p0), Direction (enum Descend/Ascend), Normalise (bool), Output (enum BasinValue / Travel / BasinId / BasinSource), CellScale (float, BasinId only), Basin B (GeneratorSource, BasinSource only).

  p = p0
  for k in 0..N-1:                       // same N for all lanes
      g = grad F(p)                      // central differences: 2d extra F evals at p +- eps*e_i (eps ~ 0.02 feature), or forward diffs d+1 evals; or analytic if F is the built-in gradient Perlin/Simplex
      if Normalise: g *= InvSqrt(dot(g,g) + 1e-6)    // constant-speed descent, branch-free
      p = p - dir * h * g
  Travel  : out = |p - p0| / (N*h)  (or path length sum of |h*g|)
  BasinValue: out = F(p)              // every point takes the value N steps downhill
  BasinId : out = rnd11(hash(floor(p*CellScale)))   // piecewise-constant catchment mosaic
  BasinSource: out = B(p)             // any node evaluated at the landing point
As a DomainWarp-family node (DomainWarpFlow) the vector p - p0 is simply added to the positions, so any downstream graph is 'gathered' into the pits.

[SlopeSlide, graph-meta-filters] Simplex stencil v_i (triangle in 2D, tetrahedron in 3D, 5-cell in 4D), with sum v_i = 0. q = p. Repeat N times (int member, 1 to 6): g = D/((D+1)h) * sum S(q + h v_i) v_i; q -= a * g / sqrt(1 + c*|g|^2). Output Target(q), where Target defaults to S. a is the step and c softens the step on steep ground. Regimes seen in the prototype with single-octave Perlin: a=0.05-0.12 gives bright ridge network around dark rounded basins; a=0.25-0.5 overshoots the minimum, so plate interiors fill with parallel ripple bands; a<0 gives fat pillow plates with thin dark seams and ripple rings. N=3-4 at a=0.1-0.2 gives flat basin floors with crisp watershed lines. Extra outputs: HeightAboveDrain = S(p) - S(q_down), and LocalPosition = (S(p) - S(q_down)) / (S(q_up) - S(q_down) + e), which equalises every hill to 0..1.
ideas.look:
Organic polygonal plates whose borders are the actual ridge lines of the source: varied cell size, curved walls, each floor at its own depth, optional agate-like ripple interiors. Looks like dried mud, giraffe patches, cloisonne or basin terrain. With 2-3 octave sources it gives plates carrying inner detail. Good for terrain basins, cracked ground, biome regions and masks.
[Catchment, dynamics-iteration] Verified in prototype. Flat-coloured patches with curved borders and a wide natural size distribution, no convexity and no grid. Multi-octave sources give fractal or irregular borders. Distance gives pitted bowls with curved walls. Rings gives agate, orbicular lichen or target nests, each bounded by a watershed. Edge gives branching crack networks with fractal tufts. Good for biomes, plates, drainage basins, stone, lichen, tectonic provinces.
ideas.why_new: No node can move a position along a field's own gradient for several steps; a one-shot DomainWarp by a single gradient has no convergence so cannot produce catchments or lake floors. The output is the flow map of the field, which a graph cannot express (it needs the gradient at each successive position). Shares one 'FlowEngine' with StirAdvect, StretchFTLE and StreamlineLIC.
ideas.simd_plan:
Dimension-agnostic GenT<P...> over a pack: fixed loop of N, inside it d+1 (forward) or 2d (central) source evaluations and FMA updates; no per-lane branching at all. If a built-in gradient-aware Perlin/Simplex is added internally (PerlinD, ~1.6x Perlin), use it when Field is left empty. Costs (AVX2 est.): 2D N=6 forward diffs, Perlin field: 18 Perlin = ~20 ns (18x Perlin); 3D: 24 Perlin3D = ~53 ns; 4D: 30 Perlin4D = ~130 ns. With FBm-5 Simplex field multiply by 5. 4D works and tiling via GenTileable2D is preserved because the moved position stays a function of the 4D input point. Far-coordinate safety: clamp per-step |h*g| to 1 feature with FS::Min.
[SlopeSlide, graph-meta-filters] No lattice of its own and no branches. Taps: N*(D+1)+1, so 4/5/6 at N=1 and 10/13/16 at N=3 for 2D/3D/4D. On Perlin at N=1 about 4.4/11/26 ns (scalar prototype measured 4.4x perlin2), comparable to CellularDistance in 2D and cheaper in 3D and 4D. Dimension agnostic via a GenT stencil table.
ideas.continuity: Mathematically C0 (composition of continuous steps), numerically a step at watersheds: measured c0ratio 1.0..1.2, max slope about 2400 per unit. Inside a basin it is smooth.
ideas.params: Field (GeneratorSource); Steps int; StepLen hybrid (sampled at p0 only, so spatially varying descent length is free); Epsilon float for finite differences; Direction enum; Normalise bool; Output enum; CellScale float; Basin GeneratorSource (optional). Seeded + ScalableGenerator mixins.
ideas.risks:
Cost scales with N x field cost; FBm fields get expensive (use GeneratorCache-style thinking, or let the field be a cheaper noise than the terrain). Large h overshoots pits and oscillates (Normalise + h <= 0.25 feature avoids it). BasinId has lattice edges where flow has not converged.
[Catchment, dynamics-iteration] Unconverged areas near flat maxima or saddles show hatched grain (fixed-step limit cycle); decaying step fixes most of it, and it worsens beyond 3 octaves. Basins are not guaranteed to reach the minimum in N steps on big features, so Step*N should match the source's feature scale. Border aliasing is unavoidable at the output level.
[BasinFlow, distribution-topology] Comb-shaped artifacts and rippled patches appear where trajectories bounce along narrow ridges and do not converge in N steps, visible even at N=14. Plateau values retain faint rings. Cell ID by rounding fails unless convergence is good. Expensive; smooth 1-octave sources only. The histogram is spiky by nature. This is the riskiest idea on the list.
ideas.variant_notes: Fixed-count gradient descent then read something at the landing point. Regimes: N=1 small step gives ridge-network plates, overshoot gives ripple interiors, N=3-4 gives flat basins, decaying N=12 gives true watershed cells. Outputs merged from Catchment, SlopeSlide, BasinFlow, FlowDescentBasin and DomainWarpGradientDescent: value, distance, rings, height-above-drain, label, path min, or a Warp() displacement.
ideas.cost_note: Costs (AVX2 est.): 2D N=6 forward diffs, Perlin field: 18 Perlin = ~20 ns (18x Perlin); 3D: 24 Perlin3D = ~53 ns; 4D: 30 Perlin4D = ~130 ns.

ideas.name: ImplicitWarp
ideas.one_liner: Domain warp by damped fixed point q = p + A*V(q) rather than one forward step, which produces crumpled-foil creases and folded sheets instead of the smeared look of forward warps.
ideas.algorithm: q=p; repeat N (6..10): V=(n1(q), n2(q)[, n3(q)[, n4(q)]]); q=lerp(q, p+A*V, Damp). Return Source(q) as a generator, or implement Warp() so q-p is the warp displacement. Below A*Lipschitz<1 this is the exact inverse of a forward warp; above it, the iterates oscillate and period-double, which is where the creases appear. Prototype: dyn_lens mode=20,N=6,A=1.3,damp=0.6,of=1.2 and N=10,A=2,damp=0.4.
ideas.look: Verified in prototype. A=1: triangular crumpled paper facets with crisp creases. A=1.3: folded satin or foil with sharp ridges and swirl pockets. A=2: chaotic torn foil with fine detail in small regions and smooth elsewhere. Good for crumpled materials, rock folds, cloth and metal textures, alien terrain.
ideas.why_new: Forward warps stretch into streaks; the inverse compresses where forward stretches, so the visual vocabulary is flipped into creases and facets. Known nested warps f(p+fbm(p+fbm(p))) use a few undamped levels and do not reach this crease regime; Damp is the key control, and it goes from a smooth inverse through to period-doubling folds.
ideas.simd_plan: N x D noise evals + source. 2D 12 evals about 14 ns; 3D 18 evals about 40 ns; 4D 24 evals about 100 ns. Fits the DomainWarp base class and Warp() interface, so it composes with DomainWarpFractal. Reuse one noise with offset coordinates rather than separate nodes.
ideas.continuity: C0 always (continuous composition). Slope up to (1+A*L)^N in the chaotic regime; measured c0ratio 5 at A=1.3, max slope about 320 per unit. Not a smooth function along creases.
ideas.params: Warp Amplitude (hybrid), Damp float, Iterations int, Warp frequency, Source.
ideas.risks: Regime change is abrupt in A; above about 2 it becomes grainy in patches. Low Iterations combined with low Damp just looks like a weak warp.
ideas.cost_note: 2D 12 evals about 14 ns; 3D 18 evals about 40 ns; 4D 24 evals about 100 ns.

ideas.name: ImpulseWarp
ideas.one_liner: Domain warp built from sparse discrete eddies: exact local rotations about lattice points, so spiral arms remain coherent even at many radians of twist.
ideas.algorithm: For window points with rnd < Density: v = x-c; w = max(0, 1 - r^2/R^2)^2; th = Amp*rnd11*w. Plane rotation form, valid in any dimension with orthonormal pair (g,h): a = g.v, b = h.v; dx += (cos(th)-1)*(a*g + b*h) + sin(th)*(a*h - b*g). 2D: g,h = basis, simply R(th)v - v. Mode Lens: dx += Amp*rnd11*w*v (pinch and bubble). Warp() adds dx to the positions as all warps do. Fades smooth-gated by Density so a hybrid density does not pop.
ideas.look: Marble eddies, Jupiter bands, oil film, whirlpools, Van Gogh swirls; calm areas next to tight knots. Prototyped: a stripe source becomes tight knotted loops, and fractal source becomes marbled swirl. Very unlike DomainWarpSimplex, which shears without closed spirals.
ideas.why_new: Displacements from gradient noise are not rotation preserving: amplitude yields folding, not spirals. Rotation about centres keeps radii, so 10+ radians still give clean arms. Sparsity gives quiet areas, which domain-warp nodes today cannot.
ideas.simd_plan: Each point: 2 dots, Sin+Cos. 2D 9 points: about 8 ns, 3D 2^3 corners with R<=1-jitter: 8-10 ns, 27 points: 30 ns, 4D 2^4: 15 ns. Fits the Warp interface, costs as simplex warp-class. Proto 6.9x perlin2 with 19 points including a source.
ideas.continuity: C1 when kernels overlap, since the weights are C1 (measured c0ratio 7.66 with high slope due to tight twist).
ideas.params: Amplitude (hybrid), Radius, Density (hybrid via smooth gate), Mode enum (Vortex, Lens), Grid Jitter.
ideas.risks: Overlapping rotations are added, not composed, so strong overlap slightly folds; bounded at reasonable density. Tight spirals alias at Amp>10, especially at low feature scale. Sampling the source once per warp is fine.
ideas.cost_note: 2D 9 points: about 8 ns, 3D 2^3 corners with R<=1-jitter: 8-10 ns, 27 points: 30 ns, 4D 2^4: 15 ns.

ideas.name: ScatterWarp
ideas.one_liner: A domain warp built from scattered vector stamps (vortices, sources/sinks, directional pushes, shear ribbons) summed over the lattice window, giving discrete eddies and whirlpools instead of smooth noise warps.
ideas.algorithm:
Implements the DomainWarp Warp() interface (adds to the positions). For each cell in the 2^d window: centre, h, s, strength a = Amplitude*(1 + Jitter*rnd11(h)), optional sign from a hash bit. d = (p - centre)/s; r2 = dot(d,d); env = (1 - r2)^2 for r2<1 (C1 at the edge).
Kernel enum:
- Vortex: 2D v = a*env*(-d.y, d.x); 3D v = a*env*(axis x d) with axis a random unit vector (or fixed Up); 4D: rotation in a random 2-plane (bivector) represented by two orthonormal random vectors e1,e2: v = a*env*(dot(d,e2)*e1 - dot(d,e1)*e2).
- Source/Sink: v = a*env*d (sign bit chooses).
- Push: v = a*env*u with random unit u (per stamp direction).
- Shear ribbon: v = a*env*u*dot(d, perp(u)) (a local rotation-free shear).
- Dipole: v = a*env*(u - 2 d dot(d,u)) ... (optional).
Sum v over cells, scale by Feature Scale, add to positions. Octaves as in Scatter (coarse eddies plus fine ones = a cheap 'turbulence cascade').
Because vortex and shear fields are divergence free inside the envelope (up to the envelope gradient term), area is nearly preserved: textures swirl rather than stretch.
ideas.look:
Swirled bands: gas-giant stripes with embedded storms when the source is horizontal Bands (A about 1.6, Density 0.5). Curly eddies on FBm. Strong amplitude tears into marble. Through DomainWarpFractalProgressive, eddies at multiple scales. Prototype: dcc_lens mode=9.
[ScatterWarp, stamp-scatter] Visible whirlpools, eddies, cyclone bands, fingerprint-like curls, galaxy arms, spiral marbling, and 'stirred paint' when applied to stripes or Checkerboard; sink kernels pinch the texture into dimples, push kernels create slip bands. Current warps (Gradient, Simplex, Fractal) produce smooth, uniform marbling; there is no way today to get localised rotation with a clean eye.
ideas.why_new: DomainWarp nodes read a scalar noise's gradient; they cannot produce a rotation centre or a sink. Building a vortex field from existing nodes would need vector output, which only the Warp family has. This reuses the Scatter lattice but emits vectors, so it belongs in the DomainWarp family and chains with DomainWarpFractalProgressive for free.
ideas.simd_plan: Per cell: hash, centre, envelope (~25 ops), kernel (~10-20 ops), accumulate d components. No source eval, no trig (random unit vectors via normalised rnd11 pairs/triples). 2D 4 cells ~2.5 ns, 3D 8 cells ~7 ns, 4D 16 cells ~20 ns, i.e. in the same band as DomainWarpGradient to Simplex. Dimension agnostic except the kernel's rotation construction.
ideas.continuity: C1 displacement (t^3 at the boundary), so warped output is as continuous as its source. Measured c0ratio 7.47 on a high-frequency banded source, which is steep rather than broken.
ideas.params: Kernel enum, Feature Scale, Amplitude (Warp Amplitude, hybrid like the other warps), Size, Size Jitter, Jitter, Strength Jitter, Signed bool (random handedness), Axis enum for 3D (Random/Up), Octaves, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks:
Large amplitudes fold the domain and create overlaps (true of all warps). 4D plane rotation needs an orthonormal pair per stamp (Gram-Schmidt, ~20 ops). Prior art exists in fluid-like texture synthesis (vortex particles, curl noise), but not as a lattice-window warp node.
[DomainWarpVortex, dcc-tools] At high amplitude the tangent push moves points far outside the rotation arc and folds occur; iterating with less amplitude is better. Far fewer swirl features than cells unless Density is near 1. 3D axis table visible if too small.
ideas.variant_notes: Summed tangential or radial kernels, first-order in amplitude. For many-radian swirls see ImpulseWarp and VortexCells.
ideas.cost_note: 2D 4 cells ~2.5 ns, 3D 8 cells ~7 ns, 4D 16 cells ~20 ns, i.e. in the same band as DomainWarpGradient to Simplex.

queue.name: ScatterWarp
queue.reason: 2^d-window vector stamps (vortex, sink, push, shear) in Warp form give local art control. Most general of the eddy trio; try impulse-warp spirals as a kernel.

ideas.name: ShearFlow
ideas.one_liner: A chain of 1D-noise shears: an exactly area-preserving warp at about 1/3 Perlin per step that behaves like fluid mixing (marbling), and in periodic mode gives KAM islands inside a chaotic sea.
ideas.algorithm: Table of unit directions u_k with perpendicular t_k (Golden mode: angle k*2.39996; Periodic mode: k mod 3 x 60 degrees). For k in 0..N-1: s=dot(p,t_k); p+=u_k*A*gradnoise1(s*F, seed+salt_k). Since the displacement along u depends only on the perpendicular coordinate, every step has det J = 1. Output options: Warp() displacement; Source(p); Birkhoff average sum w_k*Source(p_k)/sum w_k with w(t)=exp(-1/(t(1-t))), whose super-convergence separates islands (smooth) from chaotic sea (grainy). In 3D/4D, s can be a 2D perpendicular noise for richer sheets. Prototypes: dyn_lens mode=6,N=10; mode=7,N=30,A=0.8.
ideas.look: Verified in prototype. Final sampling: pulled ink filaments, fine marbling folds without any pinched blobs. Periodic A=0.5: smooth contour-following streams. A=0.8: marble with lens-shaped smooth islands wrapped in fine layered filaments. A=1.2: smooth islands in a grainy sea with zig-zag strata. Good for marble, agate, ink, gas giants, mixed fluids, wood.
ideas.why_new: Existing warps compress and pinch, and fold features with visible stretching blur; this preserves area exactly, so sampled densities stay statistically unchanged (no range or contrast collapse) and scalar sources keep their distribution. Very cheap per step, which allows N=12..30 where nested Simplex warps cannot afford it. Islands plus chaos in one field is a phase-space structure that single-pass noise never gives.
ideas.simd_plan: 1D gradient noise plus dot and add: about 0.3..0.5 ns per step. N=12: about 5 ns plus source. Birkhoff with a source sample every period (N/3 samples): 8..12 Perlin total. Direction table per node (computed once). Dimension-agnostic: use a D-dim direction list, ideally a low-discrepancy set. 4D cost barely grows, excellent for tiling. Warp() fits the existing interface.
ideas.continuity: C1 or C2 for the map (quintic 1D noise); composition keeps smoothness, with Lipschitz growing exponentially at high A. Birkhoff output is continuous but grainy in the chaotic regime.
ideas.params: Amplitude (hybrid), Shear Frequency, Steps, Direction Mode enum (Golden, Periodic 3), Output enum (Warp, Sample, Birkhoff), Source.
ideas.risks: 1D noise has lines of constant s, so low N shows straight-ish shear artefacts; N>=8 hides them. Periodic mode with 3 dirs shows faint zig-zag axis structure in the chaotic sea. Birkhoff is costly at N=30.
ideas.cost_note: 1D gradient noise plus dot and add: about 0.3..0.5 ns per step. N=12: about 5 ns plus source.

queue.name: ShearFlow
queue.reason: 1D-noise shear chain with det exactly 1, ~6 ns at N=12, flat across dimensions (J4 top pick). Also the base lyapunov-stretch needs, which earns it a slot beside domain-warp-sine.

disp.how: the node

ideas.name: StirAdvect
ideas.one_liner: Advect the sample backward N small steps along a divergence-free (stream-function) field so textures stretch into laminated marbling filaments instead of blotchy warps.
ideas.algorithm:
Field: 2D V = (-d psi/dy, d psi/dx) from one potential psi; dimension-agnostic rule: for each axis pair (i,j) in the cycle (x,y),(y,z),(z,w),(w,x) use a seeded potential psi_ij and add its in-plane rotated gradient to components i and j. 2D: 1 potential, 3D: 3 (= curl), 4D: 4. Every such term is divergence free, so the composite flow preserves volume.

  p = p0
  for k in 0..N-1:
      v  = V(p)                                   // analytic gradients (internal gradient Perlin) or forward-difference d+1 evals per potential
      pm = p - 0.5*h*v                            // RK2 midpoint (optional, 2 field evals/step; Euler with small h is acceptable)
      p  = p - h*V(pm)
  DomainWarpFlow: Warp() adds (p - p0) to positions; or Generator form: out = B(p) with B a GeneratorSource (stripes, checkerboard, Perlin, cellular...).
Total 'stir time' T = N*h controls mixing: small T = gentle wobble, T >> 1/|grad V| = exponentially stretched laminae.

[DomainWarpFlow, volumetric-3d4d] Wrapper over a DomainWarp source (same Warp interface). Warp(p): with step h = Amount/N; repeat N: v = Inner.displacement(p); p = p + h*v. If h*Lip(v) < 1 the map is injective and homeomorphic to identity, so any connected tunnel stays connected and any tube stays a tube: use with BondTunnels and LevelSetDistance. Curl-based inner flow makes it nearly volume preserving (for tube width near constant). Amount as hybrid or via w gives true advection: source pattern is carried along streamlines rather than boiling. Two-phase flow-map trick for looping: F = lerp(S(flow(p, t mod 1)), S(flow(p, (t+.5) mod 1)), triangle(t)) with sqrt-normalised weights, 2 source evals.
ideas.look: Paper-marbling / Suminagashi: long, thin, parallel laminations that fold on themselves without tearing or smearing; a SineWave or Checkerboard source becomes classic marbled stripes, Perlin becomes fluid-mixed swirls, Cellular becomes stretched cells with intact edges. Clearly different from Warp Fractal Progressive, which (being a single large-amplitude non-area-preserving displacement) folds and blotches. Good for marble, agate, fluid, wood figure, cloud shear.
ideas.why_new: Existing warps are one-shot, position-only displacements; large amplitude gives folds and overlaps. Iterating many small steps along a divergence-free field yields the flow map of an incompressible fluid, which stretches material lines exponentially while preserving area, and that is exactly what makes marbling look like marbling. A graph cannot chain N warps that each depend on the already-moved position with one shared field.
ideas.simd_plan: Same engine as FlowWatershed: fixed N loop, each step d potentials x (d+1 or analytic) evals, rotated-gradient assembly is pure FMAs, no masks. Cost (AVX2 est.): 2D Euler N=8 with internal gradient Perlin: 8 x 1.6 = ~13x Perlin (~14 ns); forward-difference arbitrary potential: 24 evals (~26 ns). 3D: 3 potentials: analytic 8x3x1.6x2.2 = ~85 ns; FD 96 Perlin3D (~210 ns). 4D: 4 potentials ~ 8x4x1.6x4.3 = ~220 ns. Expensive in 3D/4D, acceptable for a look node; RK2 doubles. Tiling preserved (position stays a function of the 4D point).
ideas.continuity: Continuous and smooth: flow map of a smooth field; C1 with analytic gradients, C0 with finite differences on a C0 potential. No seams.
ideas.params: Potential (GeneratorSource, optional; default internal gradient Perlin), Steps int, StepLen hybrid, Strength hybrid (scales V), Integrator enum (Euler/RK2), Epsilon float (finite diff), as DomainWarp-family: Warp Amplitude mixin; Generator form adds Source B.
ideas.risks:
3D/4D cost; too large h makes Euler non-area-preserving (use RK2 or h <= 0.1 feature); visually requires N*h >= ~2 features to look marbled, i.e. 10-20 steps; without a gradient-capable noise inside the library every step pays finite-difference evaluations.
[DomainWarpFlow, volumetric-3d4d] Untested. Cost multiplier. Euler errors at low N can still fold where hybrid amplitude is large, so injectivity requires h*Lip(v)<1, which is only checkable numerically. Long stretches create very high local frequencies in Source, aliasing at large Amount. Hybrid Amount varying across space adds extra deformation and loses the volume property. Overlap with chained warp graphs is a real argument against, so value must show up in usability and guaranteed topology.
ideas.variant_notes: Small-step flow-map integration. The DomainWarpFlow (volumetric) wrapper form integrates any existing warp and adds the guarantee that a homeomorphic warp cannot change topology, for caves, plus a two-phase looping mode.
ideas.cost_note: Cost (AVX2 est.): 2D Euler N=8 with internal gradient Perlin: 8 x 1.6 = ~13x Perlin (~14 ns); forward-difference arbitrary potential: 24 evals (~26 ns).

ideas.name: VortexCells
ideas.one_liner: Exact finite rotation inside hashed discs, in Warp family form: real spiral eddies with zero pinch at about 2 ns per layer.
ideas.algorithm:
For each layer l: rotate and offset lattice. cell = floor(u). h = hash. R in [.25,.5], c = cell + .5 + (.5-R)*(h2,h3) (inside cell, 1x1 window). d2 = |u-c|^2/R^2. If d2<1: ang = Turns*2*pi*rnd11(h4)*(1-d2)^2, u = c + Rot(ang)*(u-c). Compose sequentially over 2-3 layers with different rotation offsets. Every disc is a shear flow mapped exactly: rigid circles rotate, so area and local isotropy on each circle are preserved and no pinching occurs. Warp returns displacement; can also be an ordinary domain node.

[WhirlFold, stamp-scatter] For rep in Layers, for each colour c in 3^dim: recompute floor(p) from the current, already-moved p (essential), get the unique colour cell g = 3*floor((floor(p)+1-c)/3)+c. Feature f, radius r<=1 (same-colour stamps are 3 cells apart with centres at least 2 apart, so same-colour discs never overlap and each colour is one well-defined global map). t = |p-f|/r, angle a = Amount*rnd11(h)*(1-t^2)^3 for t<1 else 0. Rotate p about f by a: this preserves radius, so it is invertible with exact inverse (run colours in reverse with -a). 3D: rotate about a random unit axis from hash via Rodrigues; 4D: rotate in one or two hash-chosen planes. Warp() returns p_out - p_in. Pinch mode: scale the radial coordinate by a monotonic function of t (stays bijective while dr'/dr > 0).
ideas.look:
Gas-giant bands with cyclones, ocean eddies, marble curls, Van Gogh swirl, smoke. With strata the prototype instantly reads as Jupiter. Uses: planet textures, water, stylised clouds, wood knots. Prototyped: mode=8.
[WhirlFold, stamp-scatter] Prototype with FBm or stripes behind it: marbled eddies, curls and hooks at a controlled size, like Jupiter bands, Suminagashi ink, or wood-grain knots on a Gradient source. Clearly different from the Warp thumbnails on the sheet, which are ropey and lack discrete vortices.
ideas.why_new: DomainWarp nodes create smooth folds with stretching, not discrete eyes with many wraps. Summed vortex velocity kernels (see cl_vortex prototype in the lab) only approximate a small-time flow; this form allows many whole turns at no distortion cost.
ideas.simd_plan:
Per layer: floor, 1 hash, compare, sin+cos: about 2 ns (estimate). 2 layers total about 4 ns in any dim. 3D: rotate about hashed axis with Rodrigues, or about sphere normal for planets. 4D: rotate in a hash-chosen plane or two planes. Fits Warp() interface so it composes into DomainWarpFractal chains.
[WhirlFold, stamp-scatter] Fits the DomainWarp interface. Per colour: floor, one hash, sqrt, polynomial, sin+cos of the angle (or a cheaper rational rotation). 9 or 27 or 81 per layer. Estimate 2D ~10-15 ns per layer, 3D ~40 ns per layer, 4D ~130 ns per layer. Cost is 2-3x CellularDistance and includes no source eval except the warped one downstream; a single-layer lookup avoids the second pass.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity-ish away from the mask edge and C1 at it because of the cubed falloff. Verified scalar: c0ratio 7.86 at Amount 1.5 and 7.24 at Amount 3 with one layer. At Amount 6 with two layers the reading fell to 1.81, with max slope 584: composed stretching makes extremely steep gradients; I attribute this to compounding because the lower-amount runs are clean and the geometry cannot seam, but I did not separately prove it at that amplitude.
ideas.params: Cell Size, Turns (hybrid), Layers (int), Radius Min/Max, Spin Bias (signed, for one-way cyclones), Warp Amplitude maps to Turns.
ideas.risks:
Discs are visibly circular at low Turns. Overlap with another lens's VortexWarp, so choose one or keep both as variants. High Turns with fractal source aliases at the shear ring.
[WhirlFold, stamp-scatter] High amount yields aliasing in the warped source, not a real tear, but it looks like noise at low resolution. Hybrid Amount must stay spatially smooth or lose bijectivity. Since this needs recomputed floors, the proto's first version with a fixed window gave seams; that detail is easy to get wrong. Non-periodic colour pattern is not an issue here because the order is invisible except in overlap.
ideas.variant_notes: Sequentially composed exact rotations, hence a true bijection. Two orderings: one disc inside its own cell per layer (VortexCells, 1x1 window), or colour-ordered 3^d cells with radius up to 1 (WhirlFold). Floors must be recomputed from the moved position or seams appear.
ideas.cost_note: Per layer: floor, 1 hash, compare, sin+cos: about 2 ns (estimate). 2 layers total about 4 ns in any dim.

queue.name: VortexCells
queue.reason: Exact disc rotations in a 1x1 window at ~2 ns per layer: Jupiter bands with no pinch. Cheapest of the eddy trio; discs show at low Turns.

ideas.name: AnchoredFrameDetail
ideas.one_liner: Gradient-aligned detail that actually works pointwise: a detail source is evaluated in local frames rotated to the gradient of a control source at 2^D lattice anchors and blended with variance-preserving weights, giving gullies that run downhill or strata that run along contours.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Control (GeneratorSource, e.g. the terrain), Detail (GeneratorSource, e.g. an anisotropic Simplex via DomainAxisScale), Cell Size c, Epsilon, Along/Across enum, Mix (hybrid) if the node also adds the base.
GenT(pos): X = pos / c; i0 = floor(X); t = X - i0 (quintic/hermite weights).
For each of the 2^D anchors a = (i0 + corner) * c:
  g = central-difference gradient of Control at a        // 2D taps per anchor, NOT at pos
  frame: 2D u = g/|g|, v = perp(u); 3D: u = g/|g|, v = normalize(up - (up.u)u) with Select to a second up vector when |up.u| > 0.9, w = u x v
  o = pos - a ; local = (o.u, o.v[, o.w]) + hash(a) * 100   // per-anchor decorrelation offset
  d_a = Detail(local)
  w_a = prod_axes (corner ? h(t) : 1 - h(t))
return sum w_a d_a / sqrt(sum w_a^2)                        // variance preserving, no contrast loss in the overlaps
The trick: the naive version (rotate the global coordinates by the gradient at pos) fails because a direction change dTheta moves the sample by |pos| dTheta, which the proto shows as white noise (sheetD m7). Anchoring the frame origin at the lattice point bounds the lever arm to one cell, so the detail is coherent inside each cell and crossfades between cells.
ideas.look: Brush-stroke / fur-like hatching whose stroke direction follows the control field's gradient everywhere (proto sheetD m12): with Across it reads as erosion gullies pointing downhill, with Along as terracettes/strata following the contours; the hatching reorganises around every peak and saddle. On the contact sheet nothing is direction-coherent with a second field. Uses: slope-aligned erosion detail on terrains, wood grain following a shape, flow-combed fur/grass, anisotropic rock strata.
ideas.why_new: The existing graph cannot rotate a domain by a spatially varying angle at all (DomainRotate is constant), and the one spatially varying rotation that is pointwise-correct requires the anchor-blend trick plus a gradient per anchor, which no composition of existing nodes expresses. It makes the standard 'erosion stripes aligned to slope' look available as one node on any heightfield.
ideas.simd_plan: GenT with 2^D anchors unrolled: each anchor costs 2D Control taps (gradient) + 1 Detail eval. 2D: 4 x (4 + 1) = 20 evals, 3D: 8 x (6 + 1) = 56, 4D: 16 x 9 = 144 (offer Forward differences to cut to 4x4 / 8x5 / 16x6, or treat w as pass-through in 4D). With Simplex control and detail, 2D ~26 ns AVX2, 3D ~150 ns: heavy but a one-shot detail layer, comparable to a 4D CellularDistance. Frame construction is branch-free (InvSqrt, Select for the up-vector fallback). Scalar proto: 59x perlin2, consistent with 20 evals.
ideas.continuity: C0 (proto c0ratio 8.0): the anchor frames are constants per anchor, the blend weights are C1 hermite, and the per-anchor detail is a C0 function of pos. Frames flip discontinuously between anchors where the control gradient rotates by ~180 degrees, but the crossfade hides it; it appears as crossing strokes (the hatching look).
ideas.params: Control, Detail (nodes); Cell Size (should be >= the detail's correlation length along the stroke; proto used 0.7-1.0 units with 6x anisotropy); Epsilon; Orientation {Across gradient, Along contour}; Up vector (3D); optional Base Mix hybrid so the node outputs Control*(1-m) + Detail*m in one go.
ideas.risks: Cell size versus detail anisotropy is a real tuning knob: too small a cell shows the anchor lattice as a patchwork, too large loses direction fidelity; the proto's default looks like cross-hatching rather than clean parallel gullies, which may or may not be wanted. Critical points of Control (|g| ~ 0) give arbitrary frames; the InvSqrt epsilon floor keeps it finite. 3D frames need an up vector fallback; 4D is a cost problem.
ideas.cost_note: With Simplex control and detail, 2D ~26 ns AVX2, 3D ~150 ns: heavy but a one-shot detail layer, comparable to a 4D CellularDistance.

ideas.name: BubbleInvert
ideas.one_liner: Random non-overlapping circles or spheres where the domain is circle-inverted, so each bubble holds a mirrored, shrunken copy of the whole outside world, seamless at its rim.
ideas.algorithm: Loop Iterations times: cell = floor(p). h = hash(cell). R = lerp(Rmin,Rmax,h1) with Rmax <= .5. c = cell + .5 + (.5-R)*(h2,h3), so the circle stays inside its cell and needs a 1x1 window. d2 = |p-c|^2. mask = d2 < R^2. p = Select(mask, c + (p-c)*R^2/max(d2, eps*R^2), p). Inversion is the identity on the circle, so no seam. After inversion the point is outside, and may land in another bubble on later iterations, nesting (Schottky/Kleinian group behaviour). eps caps magnification at 1/eps. Output S(p). Optional Density hash bit disables some bubbles.
ideas.look: Chrome-ball inclusions: rosettes and butterfly pairs set in otherwise untouched source. With stripes every bubble turns into a butterfly dipole; with a checker it shows nested fractal Apollonian-like dust; with fbm it reads as speckled star-shaped patches or geodes. Outside bubbles the source is unchanged, so it is a local embellishment for terrain, coral, geodes, alien ground, 3D foam voids. Prototyped: mode=2.
ideas.why_new: Conformal, exact pointwise, isolated features with fractal interior at Value-noise cost. Domain warps cannot produce an interior that swaps inside and outside, and no existing node has this structure.
ideas.simd_plan: Per iteration: floor, 1 hash, 3 bit-field floats, compare, Select. About 1 ns per iteration (estimate), no window search, same in every dimension. Generic GenT over the pack, so 2D, 3D, 4D are all the same code.
ideas.continuity: C0 at rims, C-infinity inside; crease at rim. c0ratio 7.99 at iter=1 eps=.2. Steeper at iter=3 (4.03) from multiplied minification, not a jump.
ideas.params: Cell Size, Radius Min/Max (hybrid), Iterations (int 1-4), Eps (magnification cap), Density, Source.
ideas.risks: High minification means aliasing near the centre (bubble core looks like white noise at eps<.05). Keep eps >= .1 for building-block use. Lattice is visible if radii are large and density is high; pre-warp or a rotated second layer hides it. Source frequency also matters: a low-frequency source gives the clearest result.
ideas.cost_note: About 1 ns per iteration (estimate), no window search, same in every dimension.

queue.name: BubbleInvert
queue.reason: Wild card. Own-cell circle inversion nests whole worlds in bubbles at ~1 ns per iteration. A look nobody has, with no clear terrain use and aliasing cores.

ideas.name: BurgersSteepen
ideas.one_liner: Solves v = Source(p - t*v*d) per sample, so any noise steepens like a breaking wave into sharp one-sided shock fronts, dunes and shingles for about 5 source evals.
ideas.algorithm: This is the implicit characteristic solution of inviscid Burgers u_t + (u.d)u_grad = 0. Solve the scalar root of f(v) = Source(p - t*v*d) - v. For |Source|<=B, f(-B)>=0 and f(B)<=0, so a bracket always exists and bisection never diverges. lo=-B, hi=B, flo=B, fhi=-B; repeat N (4..6): v=(lo+hi)/2; f=Source(p - t*v*d) - v; m=f>0; lo=Select(m,v,lo); flo=Select(m,f,flo); hi=Select(m,hi,v); fhi=Select(m,fhi,f). Final false-position step with no extra eval: return lo + (hi-lo)*flo/Max(flo-fhi,1e-6). d is a unit vector from Angle (2D) or a normalised direction member (3D/4D). Prototype: dyn_lens mode=26,N=5,t=1.5,polish=1.
ideas.look: Verified in prototype. Smooth windward ramps ending in razor-sharp leeward cliffs; asymmetric sawtooth skyline. t=0.5 gives skewed noise, t=1.5 gives dunes and fault scarps, t=3 on 2 octaves gives shattered shards with flat tops. Spatially varying Angle gives feather or petal flakes. Good for dunes, wave crests, rock strata, shingled scales, wood-burl faults, wind-sculpted terrain. Feeding it SineWave gives asymmetric ripple marks.
ideas.why_new: Nothing on the contact sheet is directionally asymmetric. Warps move features but never make slopes one-sided. No graph of existing nodes can do it because the warp amount depends on the node's own output (a true feedback fixed point).
ideas.simd_plan: Fixed N, all Select, no per-lane exit. Dimension-agnostic GenT over the pack. Cost N x Source: 5 evals, about 5x the source (Perlin 2D about 6 ns, 3D about 11 ns, 4D about 22 ns). A wrapper over a GeneratorSource, so it composes with FBm. 3D form prototyped with perlin3: the XZ slice shows the same shock structure. N=4 with false position already has no visible banding; N=5..7 plain bisection shows stair stripes in hillshade.
ideas.continuity: C1-ish below breaking time t < 1/max(-dn/ds). Above it, deliberately discontinuous at shock fronts (Select branch in the bisection, measured c0ratio 1.0). Range stays inside the source range.
ideas.params: Time t (hybrid: 0 returns the source untouched, so a mask can localise steepening), Angle (hybrid in 2D, varying it gives flakes), Iterations int, GeneratorSource Source.
ideas.risks: Bisection picks a consistent but not entropy-correct root, so shock positions are not physically exact and small pinholes appear at very large t. Source must be roughly within the bracket B. Hybrid angle at high variation can look messy. In GenTileable2D the constant 4D direction projects to a varying direction across the image, though it still tiles because the result is a pure function of 4D position.
ideas.cost_note: Cost N x Source: 5 evals, about 5x the source (Perlin 2D about 6 ns, 3D about 11 ns, 4D about 22 ns).

queue.reason: One-sided shock fronts from any noise by bracketed bisection, 5 evals; clean earlier proto (J2, J3 top pick). Check pinholes and the contraction bound on high-octave FBm.

ideas.name: CellLens
ideas.one_liner: Continuous CellularLookup: pulls the domain toward each cell centre, from flat bevelled plates through bead lenses to anti-lenses, single source eval.
ideas.algorithm:
Find F1, F2 and nearest centre c (Voronoi) or analytic cell (Square, Hex, Brick). edge = (F2-F1)/2 (for square/hex: analytic distance to cell edge). t = smoothstep(0, Bevel, edge) * Pull. q = lerp(p, c, t). Output S(q). At edges t=0 so q=p from both sides, and c swaps only there. Use F2-F1 rather than true bisector distance to the F2 cell: the first prototype used bisector distance to F2 and jumped where F2 swaps with F3 (c0ratio 1.0); F2-F1 is continuous (c0ratio 7.74). Pull=1 with small Bevel: flat plates at S(c) with walls where the whole source between c and p is squeezed into a rim, showing radial streaks. Pull 0.5-0.9: magnifying droplet. Pull<0: minified crumple toward centre.

[DomainSnap, domain-geometry] Params: Lattice enum {Square, Hex (2D) / BCC (3D) / D4 (4D), Cubic}, Cell Size L, Hardness h (hybrid, 0..1), Jitter j, Random Flip (bool).

  c = nearest lattice point to p (Square/Cubic: Round(p/L)*L; Hex: axial coords + cube rounding with 2 Selects; BCC: round on both cubic sublattices (Round(p/L), Round(p/L - 0.5)+0.5) and keep the closer with one Select set; D4: same idea with the checkerboard sublattice)
  f = p - c                                             // offset inside the Voronoi cell of the lattice
  n = cellNorm(f) / halfWidth                           // = 1 exactly on the cell boundary: Square: Max(|fx|,|fy|)/(L/2); Hex: Max_i |Dot(f, e_i)| / apothem over the 3 edge normals; BCC: Max(Max|f_i|, (|fx|+|fy|+|fz|)/1.5)/(L/2)
  m = h / (1 - h + eps)                                 // exponent: 0 => identity, large => flat plateau
  g = Pow(n + eps, m)                                   // radial profile: 1 on the boundary for every h, ~0 deep inside for large m
  q = c + f * g                                         // soft snap: the cell interior collapses toward c, the boundary stays put => continuous across cells
  if Jitter: q += j * L * rnd11(Hash(seed, c))          // per-cell content shift (texture-bombing-lite)
  if RandomFlip: q = c + Select(bits(Hash), -(q-c), q-c) per axis   // per-cell mirror; only continuous at h=1
  return Source.Gen(seed, q)

h = 1 (m -> infinity) is handled as g = 0 with a Select (hard pixelate / voxelise). Dimension agnostic apart from the lattice rounding and the cell norm.

[DomainQuantize, graph-meta-filters] Params: Source; Cell Size (hybrid); Lattice enum {Square, Hex (2D) / BCC (3D), Voronoi (jitter param, 3^D window)}; Keep enum; Rotation Steps (0 = free angle, 4 = quarter turns); Inset (hybrid).
GenT: find the cell centre c for pos (Square: floor + 0.5; Hex: axial rounding; Voronoi: the F1 point from a CellularDistance-style window, as CellularLookup does).
  o = pos - c
  Keep=Centre : q = c                                 // == CellularLookup for Voronoi, pixelate for Square
  Keep=Offset : q = c + o * Inset                     // Inset<1 shrinks the fragment content (grout)
  Keep=Rotated: theta = hash(c) -> angle (quantised to Rotation Steps if > 0); q = c + R(theta) o (3D: random axis-angle from the hash)
  Keep=Mirrored: q = c + o * sign bits from hash(c) per axis
  return Source(q)
Note: for Keep=Offset with Inset=1 and Square lattice the node is the identity; the interesting cases are rotations/mirrors, which make the fragment boundaries visible as discontinuities while the interiors stay coherent.
ideas.look:
Basalt columns, mesas, cracked-mud plates, stained-glass with bevelled lead, rain droplets on glass, compound-eye lenses. Hex and Square lattices give pixel/hex/voxel mosaic with continuous bevel, covering quantise, pixelate, hex-snap, voxelise in one node. Prototyped Voronoi: mode=5.
[DomainSnap, domain-geometry] Pixel-art / hex-pixel versions of any noise (hex-pixelated FBm is a ready hex-grid strategy map; voxelised 3D noise is a blocky cave field), and at intermediate hardness a 'bathroom glass' / lens-array look where each cell shows a slowed-down, magnified patch of the source with fast transitions at the borders. With Jitter + hard: random block sampling.
[DomainQuantize, graph-meta-filters] Proto sheetB m10: a Voronoi mosaic of rotated fragments of one FBm: every shard carries a coherent piece of the field at its own orientation, like shattered glass or crazy paving, with hard cracks at cell edges. Square + Centre is pixel art of any node; Hex + Centre is hex pixels (no existing node can produce a hex lattice look); Square + Mirrored gives kaleidoscopic tiles. Uses: stylised maps, tile-based art, broken ice/rock plates, cracked paint, puzzle textures.
ideas.why_new: Fade(CellularLookup, Source, F2-F1) lerps values and costs 2 source evals plus 2 searches. This warps the domain, so the rim shows compressed real source rather than a crossfade, costs one eval, and is not discontinuous like CellularLookup or DomainSnap.
ideas.simd_plan: Reuse Cellular search (F1,F2, offset to nearest). 3.9/12/41 ns plus one source for Voronoi; analytic Square or Hex about 0.5-1 ns. Generic GenT works for all dims. Hybrid Pull and Bevel sampled at p.
ideas.continuity: C0; C1 at the edge if Bevel smoothstep starts flat. Measured c0ratio 7.74-7.82. Bevel=0 gives hard snap (discontinuous, deliberately).
ideas.params: Lattice enum (Voronoi, Square, Hex, Brick), Cell Size, Grid Jitter, Pull (hybrid, may be negative), Bevel (hybrid), Source.
ideas.risks:
Rims contain very compressed source and can alias if the source is high frequency and Bevel small. F2-F1 is not true edge distance, so bevel width varies along an edge with centre spacing (narrow near vertices), though in the prototype this reads as natural.
[DomainSnap, domain-geometry] Pow per sample (cheap but present); Hex cell norm must use the same orientation as the rounding; at mid hardness the profile is C0 at the cell centre (kink) which can read as a dot in hillshade; feature interplay between the cell size and the source scale needs presets.
ideas.variant_notes: Continuous pull toward cell centres, on Voronoi or analytic lattices. Hard limit is plain pixelate; hex and BCC snapping are not otherwise reachable. DomainQuantize's rotated and mirrored Keep modes overlap CellularPatchwork.
ideas.cost_note: 3.9/12/41 ns plus one source for Voronoi; analytic Square or Hex about 0.5-1 ns.

ideas.name: ChiralWallpaper
ideas.one_liner: One-eval wallpaper-group domain: a Coxeter mirror fold plus an equivariant pre-warp reaches all 17 groups with no seams, including rotation-only pinwheels that plain folds cannot do.
ideas.algorithm:
Problem: only 4 groups are pure mirror groups (pmm *2222, p4m *442, p3m1 *333, p6m *632). A fold into their triangle is C0 for any source. The other 13 have glued non-mirror edges, so folding them seams. Trick: F(p) = S( fold_K( p + a*v(p) ) ), where K is a Coxeter supergroup of the target group G and v is a G-equivariant, K-breaking vector field. If v(gp) = g v(p) for g in G then F(gp) = S(fold_K(g(p + a v(p)))) = F(p), since g is in K. F is continuous because fold_K and v are.
Building v: v_G(p) = sum over g in G/T of g^-1 v0(g p), for any T-periodic trig field v0 (Reynolds average). Store it as 2-6 sin/cos terms in a table computed when the enum is set. Shortcut: if psi is K-invariant, J*grad(psi) (J = rot90) is equivariant under rotations and anti-equivariant under mirrors, so it kills exactly the mirrors. p4 from p4m, mirrors at integers: psi = cos(pi x) + cos(pi y), v = (sin(pi y), -sin(pi x)). p6 from p6m with k in {(0,2/sqrt3),(1,1/sqrt3),(1,-1/sqrt3)}: grad = sum k_i sin(2 pi p.k_i), v = J grad. p3 from p3m1 with k in {(2/3,0),(1/3,1/sqrt3),(1/3,-1/sqrt3)}. pm from pmm: v = (0, cos(pi x)). pg uses a 2x1 sublattice with v_y = cos(pi x), v_x = cos(2 pi y). A psi that is anti-invariant under chosen mirrors keeps those mirrors instead, which gives p4g, p31m, cmm and so on.
Folds: pmm x=tri(x), y=tri(y). p4m adds (x,y)=(max,min). p3m1 and p6m: reduce by hex lattice, then 3-4 rounds of masked reflect across the 3 triangle lines (the prototype uses 12 rounds as a safe bound; a closed-form fold also works). Optional soft fold abs(x) -> sqrt(x^2+e^2) removes creases.
ideas.look: Crisp tilings of any source. a=0 gives kaleidoscope mandalas. a>0 gives swirling pinwheels with no mirror lines (the p6 prototype looks like interlocking blades, Escher-like). Good for tiles, fabrics, parquet, sci-fi panels, alien terrain, masks. Prototyped: mode=0.
ideas.why_new: No symmetry node exists at all. A graph cannot reach this because reduction to the triangle needs masked reflections, and the chiral groups normally need seam hacks or several blended evals. This gets the whole 17-group enum with one source eval.
ideas.simd_plan: Enum picks a small coefficient table plus one of 4 fold routines, all floor/abs/min/max/Select. Cost is source + about 1 ns (p4m) to 3 ns (p6m), estimated. 3D: cubic C3~ fold (tri plus sort axes), chirality from an ABC-flow field (A sin z + C cos y, B sin x + A cos z, C sin y + B cos x). 4D: product of two 2D folds on (x,y) and (z,w), which keeps GenTileable working because it is a pure function of all 4 inputs.
ideas.continuity: C0 by construction, with creases along K mirrors; measured c0ratio 7.94 on p6 chi=.12. C1 with soft fold.
ideas.params: Group enum (17), Cell Size, Chirality (hybrid), Crease Softness, Source (GeneratorSource).
ideas.risks: Large Chirality makes the warp non-invertible: still continuous and still symmetric, but extra folds appear. Hybrid Chirality breaks exact symmetry (often desirable). Only p4, p6, p3 and p4m/p6m were looked at; the rest of the table is derived on paper. Rectangular groups need a DomainAxisScale for non-1:1 aspect. Closest related work is Farris's wallpaper functions from averaged waves.
ideas.cost_note: Cost is source + about 1 ns (p4m) to 3 ns (p6m), estimated.

ideas.name: ClosestPointTransport
ideas.one_liner: Newton-project each point onto a contour of S, then read a detail node there, which holds detail constant along gradient lines.
ideas.algorithm: q = p. Repeat N (1-2): st = (S(q) - L)/(|g(q)|^2 + e), D = st*g, soft clamp D *= maxs/max(|D|, maxs), q -= D. Output Target(q). L is the iso level. Because every point on a gradient line lands on the same contour point, Target is smeared perpendicular to the contours and stays sharp along them. Fans form around each extremum.
ideas.look: Petal, pinwheel and mica-like shards: radial fins fanning out of every peak and basin, meeting along sharp seams at the medial axis. At high target frequency it looks like cracked glass or crystal druse. Low frequency with N=1 and L=0.2 gives strong flower-like rosettes. In 3D it should give fibres growing perpendicular to an isosurface (stalactite or geode growth), not verified here.
ideas.why_new: Directional structure locked perpendicular to level sets of any field, with crisp seams at the medial axis, which warps cannot produce because they never collapse a whole line to one point. Uses the closest point method idea from PDE work, which I have not seen used as a noise node.
ideas.simd_plan: N*(D+2)+1 taps: 2D 5 or 9, 3D 6 or 11, 4D 7 or 13. Perlin-based 2D about 6-10 ns. Clamp is Max and Min only, no branch. Dimension agnostic.
ideas.continuity: Discontinuous by design along medial seams and around critical points. Measured c0ratio 1.16. Larger e softens fans near extrema but seams remain. The look depends on the jumps.
ideas.params: Level L (hybrid), Max Step (hybrid), Steps N, Regularisation e, Target source, Sample Distance h.
ideas.risks: Discontinuous output is a poor heightfield unless Target amplitude is small. Very high frequency target aliases at seams. Newton overshoot at low |g| is controlled only by the clamp, which sets the fan size.
ideas.cost_note: Perlin-based 2D about 6-10 ns.

ideas.name: ColeHopfDunes
ideas.one_liner: An exact viscous Burgers solution along a wind direction, evaluated pointwise from K taps, giving long windward ramps and crisp slip faces.
ideas.algorithm: Treat source S as potential Phi. Wind unit vector d, time t, viscosity nu, reach R. Taps s_k = R(2k/(K-1)-1), E_k = S(p - s_k d) + s_k^2/(2t), Emin = min E_k. Integrate exp(-E/nu) exactly over the piecewise-linear E between neighbouring taps, which removes banding: a=(E_k-Emin)/nu, b=(E_{k+1}-Emin)/nu, D=b-a, I0=(e^-a - e^-b)/D, I1=(e^-a - e^-b*(1+D))/D^2, with a Taylor fallback I0=e^-a, I1=e^-a/2 selected by mask for small |D|. W += I0, U += s_k*I0 + (s_{k+1}-s_k)*I1. Output u = U/(W*R)*gain. This is the Cole-Hopf solution of u_t + u u_x = nu u_xx: u is the Boltzmann mean displacement along the wind.
ideas.look: Transverse dune fields: wavy crest lines roughly across the wind, smooth backs and sharp one-sided drops, with barchan-like horns where crests break up. With fBm sources it reads as wind-carved rock or sastrugi. nu slides from soft swell to knife-edged slip face. Clearly asymmetric, unlike anything on the contact sheet.
ideas.why_new: Nothing in FastNoise makes a consistently one-sided profile. Ridged, PingPong and Abs are all symmetric, and warps smear rather than form shocks. The shock position, merging and crest spacing come from real conservation-law behaviour, and the node works on any input graph. The exact segment integral was the key finding: K=7 with exact segments looked cleaner than K=13 with plain taps.
ideas.simd_plan: A 1D search, so K is the same in every dimension. K=7-9 taps plus K FS::Exp calls and one masked Select per segment. On Perlin at K=7 roughly 13/20/35 ns for 2D/3D/4D (scalar prototype 8.5x perlin2). No lattice. Dimension agnostic because only the wind vector changes.
ideas.continuity: C1 for nu>0 with a smooth source: the output is a ratio of smooth positive integrals, so shocks are steep ramps and not jumps. Measured c0ratio 7.92 with max slope about 30 per unit at nu=0.03. Becoming discontinuous only as nu goes to 0.
ideas.params: Wind X/Y/Z/W (hybrid for bending wind per lane), Time t (hybrid; dunes sharpen and migrate), Viscosity nu (hybrid), Reach R (float), K (int). Hybrids are read once at p. R should cover t*max|grad S|, or shocks are clipped.
ideas.risks: Tileable 4D has no uniform wind plane, so the wind direction varies around the torus and the look needs checking. High octave sources need K=13 or more, because tap spacing must resolve the source. Exp in FS has its own cost and range, and subtracting Emin keeps values safe.
ideas.cost_note: On Perlin at K=7 roughly 13/20/35 ns for 2D/3D/4D (scalar prototype 8.5x perlin2).

disp.how: Root Viscous: the only continuous form of the one-sided profile (c0 7.97-7.99)

ideas.name: DomainHilbertRibbon
ideas.one_liner: Parametrise the plane as a ribbon along a Hilbert curve (t along the curve, n across it, quarter-circle arcs in turn cells) and sample the source at (t, n): any noise flows through a labyrinth.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Order N (int, 2^N x 2^N cells, pattern repeats with that period), Cell Size L, Along Scale, Across Scale (hybrid ok), Edge Fade e (0 = off), Corner mode {Arc, Sharp}.

  q = p / L; cell = Floor(q); f = q - cell (in [0,1)^2); ix,iy = int(cell) & (2^N - 1)
  // Hilbert decode, N uniform iterations of the standard xy->d loop (rx = (ix & s) > 0, ry = (iy & s) > 0, d += s*s*((3*rx) ^ ry), rotate quadrant), all with int32v masks and Selects.
  // Alongside d, track the accumulated frame as a signed permutation (3 bits: swap, flipX, flipY). At the last level the quadrant index (0..3) and the frame give the cell's entry and exit sides (one of N/E/S/W each) through a constant 4 x 8 table => 12 possible (entry, exit) pairs.
  // Local coordinates:
  straight (exit opposite entry):  tl = coordinate of f along the travel direction (0..1); n = signed lateral offset of f from the cell's centre line (-0.5..0.5), sign = left of travel
  turn (exit adjacent to entry):   pivot = the cell corner shared by the entry and exit edges; g = f - pivot; r = |g|
       Arc: the curve is the quarter circle of radius 0.5 about pivot; tl = angle fraction 0..1 from the entry edge toward the exit edge = (2/pi)*atan(min/max of |g.x|,|g.y|) with a one-quadrant polynomial atan (and a Select for the ordering); n = (0.5 - r) with sign chosen so left-of-travel is positive
       Sharp: nearest point on the L-shaped polyline (cheaper, but tl jumps on the inner bisector: use only with Edge Fade)
  All 12 cases are computed as a few Selects on (f.x, f.y, 1-f.x, 1-f.y) chosen by the entry/exit bits; no branches.
  t = (float(d) + tl) * AlongScale          // d up to 4^N: keep N <= 11 for float precision, or use double-free trick: t = (d mod M + tl) with a hash-based M period
  val = Source.Gen(seed, t, n * AcrossScale)
  return (e > 0) ? val * Max(0, 1 - Pow(2*Abs(n), e)) : val   // fade to 0 at the ribbon edges so cells that are not curve-adjacent meet continuously

3D: 3D Hilbert curve (same decode scheme with 3 bits per level) and tube coordinates: straight cells (t, n1, n2) from the two lateral axes; turn cells pivot on the cell EDGE shared by the entry and exit faces: t from the angle about that edge, n1 = 0.5 - distance to the edge, n2 = coordinate along the edge. Source sampled in 3D at (t, n1, n2). 4D: fallback (drop w).
ideas.look: Labyrinths, circuit-board traces, intestine / brain-coral folds (smooth source + edge fade), serpentine river canyons (as a heightmap: the ribbon is the valley, the fade is the ridge), maze terrain with recursive quadrant structure, 'flow through a maze' textures. Unlike any field on the sheet, the coherence runs along a one-dimensional path.
ideas.why_new: A space-filling-curve parametrisation gives a 1D-coherent field that is still a pure pointwise function. It is impossible to build from existing nodes (no node produces a curve-following frame), and it yields a maze/labyrinth family that cellular and gradient noises never produce.
ideas.simd_plan: N x ~12 int ops (And, Compare, Xor, Select, Add) for the decode (N=8 is ~100 ops), a short polynomial atan, ~20 Selects for the 12 cases, 1 Pow, one source eval: about 2-3x Perlin 2D plus the source. Window: the single cell. All loops are uniform (N is an int member).
ideas.continuity: C0 along the ribbon (t and n are continuous across curve-crossing edges and inside arc cells). Without Edge Fade the field jumps across cell edges the curve does not cross; with Edge Fade > 0 the output goes to 0 on every ribbon edge from both sides, so it is C0 everywhere. Sharp corners add jumps on the inner bisector.
ideas.params: Order int, Cell Size float, Along Scale float, Across Scale hybrid, Edge Fade float, Corner enum.
ideas.risks: Visible 2^N quadrant hierarchy (by design, choose N large); arc cells have curve length pi/4 vs 1 so features stretch ~27% in turns unless t is rescaled (pointwise unknown prefix counts make an exact fix impossible: accept); the outer corner of arc cells (r > 1) is a dead zone that the fade must cover; d precision for N > 11; the 3D variant is a real project.
ideas.cost_note: N x ~12 int ops (And, Compare, Xor, Select, Add) for the decode (N=8 is ~100 ops), a short polynomial atan, ~20 Selects for the 12 cases, 1 Pow, one source eval: about 2-3x Perlin 2D plus the source.

ideas.name: DomainHyperbolicTiling
ideas.one_liner: Poincare-disk {P,Q} kaleidoscope: fold any point into the fundamental Schwarz triangle with N conditional reflections and circle inversions, then sample the source there; Escher Circle Limit with noise content.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: P, Q ints (1/P + 1/Q < 1/2, clamp to nearest valid), Iterations N (int, default 12), Disk Radius Rd, Source Scale, Outside enum {Invert, Clamp}, Rim Fade f.
Precompute when P/Q change (derived from the (P,Q,2) Schwarz triangle: a geodesic circle of centre c on the x axis, orthogonal to the unit circle, meeting the line at angle pi/P under angle pi/Q):
  c = cos(pi/Q) / sqrt(cos^2(pi/Q) - sin^2(pi/P)); rho2 = c*c - 1; nP = (-sin(pi/P), cos(pi/P))

  z = p / Rd
  r2 = Dot(z,z)
  if Outside == Invert: z = Select(r2 > 1, z / r2, z)          // reflect the exterior into the disk: continuous at the rim
  for i in 0..N-1:                                             // uniform count
     z.y = Abs(z.y)                                            // mirror in the x axis
     d = Dot(z, nP); z -= 2*Max(d, 0)*nP                       // mirror in the line at angle pi/P if beyond it (iterating converges to the sector)
     dx = z.x - c; d2 = dx*dx + z.y*z.y
     k = Select(d2 < rho2, rho2 / d2, 1)                       // inside the geodesic => invert across it
     z = (c + dx*k, z.y*k)
  v = Source.Gen(seed, z * SourceScale)
  return (f > 0) ? v * Pow(Max(1 - r2, 0), f) : v              // optional fade of the sub-pixel rim

All three mirror operations are hyperbolic isometries, so the N copies of the source are isometric in the hyperbolic metric and shrink Euclideanly toward the rim. Points very near the rim need more than N steps; they remain continuous (every step is continuous), just not fully folded, and are sub-pixel at any sane zoom.
3D: Poincare ball with a Coxeter tetrahedron (e.g. {4,3,5} or {5,3,4}): the Oh or Ih sector fold from DomainKaleidoscope plus one sphere orthogonal to the unit sphere (centre distance solved numerically from the dihedral-angle condition when params change); same loop with a sphere inversion. 4D: fold on xy, pass z,w (hyperbolic cylinder). General (P,Q,R) triangles are a second circle; straightforward extension.
ideas.look:
Infinitely many shrinking copies of the source toward the disk edge, arranged on a {7,3} heptagonal, {4,5}, {3,7}, {5,4}... hyperbolic tiling. Cellular source: hyperbolic stained glass / Circle Limit fish; Perlin: symmetric clouds that densify to the rim; Checkerboard: the classic hyperbolic chessboard. Masks for portals, ornaments, iris textures, 'infinite' floors.
[HyperbolicFold, domain-geometry] Circle Limit tilings: rosettes shrinking to fractal dust at the disc rim, {7,3} star-chains, {5,4} petals with strata. Highly distinct from anything on the sheet. Use for portals, mandalas, sigils, magic circles, alien artifacts, or the half-plane variant for edge-of-world bands. Prototyped: mode=7 with {7,3} and {5,4}.
ideas.why_new: Non-Euclidean geometry cannot be composed from affine domain nodes; this gives true hyperbolic symmetry with one source evaluation and a fixed op count. Unlike the half-plane (x/y, log y) idea (sheared, not isometric; a dead end) the fold is exact.
ideas.simd_plan: N x ~14 ops (Abs, Dot, Max, FMA, Select, Reciprocal) = ~170 ops at N=12 => roughly 2-3x Perlin 2D plus the source; 3D ~N x 20 ops. No lattice window, no per-lane early out needed since all lanes run N steps.
ideas.continuity: C0: mirror and inversion folds are continuous and fix their mirror sets; creases along mirror lines and geodesic circles (the look). Fade keeps the rim continuous.
ideas.params: P int, Q int, Iterations int, Disk Radius float, Source Scale float, Outside enum, Rim Fade float, Rotation float.
ideas.risks:
Rim aliasing is inherent (infinite frequency); fade or clamp zoom. Invalid P/Q combos must be clamped. Fixed N cost even for the easy interior. 3D centre-distance derivation needs care; prototype in 2D first.
[HyperbolicFold, domain-geometry] Rim aliases to noise: fade it using an extra output or accept. Disc is a singular hero object. Source appears only within one small triangle, so scale must fit. Every tile is identical (cannot reseed per tile without seams). Need to verify interior continuity separately from the rim in a real check.
ideas.variant_notes: Prototype c0ratio 1.14 is rim aliasing rather than a confirmed interior jump, not separately verified. Half-plane variant gives an edge-of-world band.
ideas.cost_note: N x ~14 ops (Abs, Dot, Max, FMA, Select, Reciprocal) = ~170 ops at N=12 => roughly 2-3x Perlin 2D plus the source; 3D ~N x 20 ops.

ideas.name: DomainKaleidoscope
ideas.one_liner: Table-driven Coxeter fold: wallpaper kaleidoscopes (pm, pmm, p4m, p3m1, p6m) in 2D, polyhedral (Td, Oh, Ih) and cubic honeycomb folds in 3D, hyperoctahedral in 4D, one source eval.
ideas.algorithm:
Group enum. 2D: Strip(pm), Rect(pmm), Square(p4m), Tri(p3m1), HexTri(p6m), finite sectors D2/D4/D8. 3D: Box(abs only), Cubic(Pm-3m, 48 copies per cell), Tetra(Td), Octa(Oh), Icosa(Ih). 4D: HyperBox, HyperCubic. Params: CellSize L, Centre (per dim), Rotation.

Step A (affine groups only), reduce by the translation lattice to the Wigner-Seitz cell:
  square/rect/cubic: q = p - Round(p/L)*L                      // q in [-L/2, L/2)^n
  hex (Tri, HexTri): axial coords (a,b) = (2x/3, -x/3 + y/sqrt3)/L; cube-round (ra,rb,rc) with the usual 'fix the largest error' done as 2 Selects; q = p - centre(ra,rb)
Step B, point-group fold = fixed sequence of conditional reflections from a per-group constant table of unit normals n_i (count <= 6, same for all lanes):
  for n_i in table: d = Dot(q, n_i); q -= 2*Min(d, 0)*n_i           // reflect only if on the negative side; axis normals reduce to q.x = Abs(q.x)
  Rect: {x, y}. Square: {x, y, (1,-1)/sqrt2} (abs + one conditional swap). HexTri (D6, sector [0,30deg]):
     q.x=|q.x|; n=(-1/2, sqrt3/2): q -= 2*Min(q.n,0)*n; q.x=|q.x|; n=(-sqrt3/2, 1/2): q -= 2*Min(q.n,0)*n   (exact in 4 steps)
  Tri (D3): q.y=|q.y|; n=(-sqrt3/2,1/2) twice interleaved with abs (3-4 steps).
  Oh: q = Abs(q); sort components descending with 3 conditional swaps (x=y, y=z, x=y planes). Td: Abs + one swap. Ih: Abs; reflect in n1=(phi,1,0)/|.|; Abs; reflect in n2=(1,0,phi)/|.| and n3=(0,phi,1)/|.|; Abs (Knighty-style icosahedral fold, 6-8 steps).
  4D: Abs + 5-compare sorting network (hyperoctahedral B4).
Step C: return Source.Gen(seed, q + Centre).
The finite groups (Td/Oh/Ih/D_k) act on the direction and preserve |p|, so a sphere shell (via DomainWrap) gets exact polyhedral symmetry.
ideas.look: Ornamental wallpaper made from any noise: damask (p4m + Perlin), honeycomb crystal (p6m + Cellular), stained glass (p3m1 + CellularValue), snowflake fields. In 3D: planets/shells/gems with exact octahedral or icosahedral symmetry (virus capsids, radiolaria, geodesic domes, cut gemstones with Cellular). The derivative flips at the mirrors, which gives a crisp, faceted 'kaleidoscope' character that no stationary noise on the sheet has.
ideas.why_new: Symmetry is unreachable with the existing affine domain nodes. A fold costs a handful of Abs/FMA/Min ops and one source evaluation, and because it is driven by a per-group table one Gen body covers 2D/3D/4D. Honest limitation: only the reflection-generated groups fold continuously for an arbitrary source (pm, pmm, p4m, p3m1, p6m in 2D; the other 12 wallpaper groups need a symmetric source, see DomainSymmetrize + DomainWrap recipe).
ideas.simd_plan: 6-20 ops (Round, Abs, FMA, Min, Select), no lattice window, same structure in every dimension; ~0.2-0.5x Perlin + source. Tables are constexpr per group; the fold count is a compile-time or per-node constant so the loop is uniform.
ideas.continuity: C0: every conditional reflection is continuous and fixes the mirror, so q is continuous; the gradient reverses across mirrors (creases), which is the intended look.
ideas.params: Group enum, Cell Size float (not hybrid: the lattice must be coherent), Centre per-dimension float (which patch of the source becomes the motif), Rotation float (pre-rotates the lattice).
ideas.risks:
Lattice reduction and fold table must match exactly (hex orientation, p31m vs p3m1) or seams appear; prototype each group with the continuity check. Mirror creases can look mechanical; pair with DomainSymmetrize for soft symmetry.
[DomainKaleidoscope, math-physics] Dihedral, hyperbolic and Kleinian are not translation invariant (centred), so they are decals, not noise, and not tileable; hyperbolic needs float care near the rim (fold count insufficient -> unfolded garbage at |p|>0.995); the p6m lattice reduction must be exact or seams appear.
ideas.variant_notes: Reflection groups only fold continuously for any source; ChiralWallpaper covers the remaining groups.
ideas.cost_note: 6-20 ops (Round, Abs, FMA, Min, Select), no lattice window, same structure in every dimension; ~0.2-0.5x Perlin + source.

queue.name: DomainKaleidoscope
queue.reason: Table-driven Coxeter folds in 6-20 ops at any dimension, with one source eval. Needs per-group continuity tests; base for chiral-wallpaper.

ideas.name: DomainKIFS
ideas.one_liner: Kaleidoscopic IFS as a domain remap: N iterations of fold / rotate / scale-about-point, then sample the source; the detail is arranged self-similarly instead of summed like fBm.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Iterations N (int 1..12), Scale s (>1), Offset o (per dim, hybrid ok), Angle (2D) or Yaw/Pitch (3D), Fold enum {Orthant, Diagonal, Hex, Icosa (3D), BoxSphere}, Normalise bool, CellSize.

  q = p / CellSize
  for i in 0..N-1:                               // uniform count
     q = Fold(q)
        Orthant:  q = Abs(q)
        Diagonal: q = Abs(q); conditional swaps so q.x >= q.y (>= q.z)
        Hex:      the 4-step D6 fold from DomainKaleidoscope
        Icosa:    the icosahedral reflection sequence (3D)
        BoxSphere (Mandelbox): q = Clamp(q,-1,1)*2 - q; r2 = Dot(q,q); q *= Select(r2 < 0.25, 4, Select(r2 < 1, 1/r2, 1))
     q = Rot(q)                                  // constant matrix from Angle/Yaw/Pitch
     q = q*s - o*(s-1)                           // scale about the fixed point o
  if Normalise: q *= s^-N                        // deepest-level features match CellSize
  return Source.Gen(seed, q)

Presets: Orthant, s=2, o=(1,1) => Sierpinski triangle partition; Diagonal, s=3, o=(1,1) => Sierpinski carpet / Menger in 3D; Icosa, s=2.0-2.6 => dodecahedral fractal shells; BoxSphere s=2-3 => Mandelbox cavities. Dimension agnostic (GenT over the pack).

[DomainFold, libs-modifiers] If TilePeriod > 0: p = T * abs(fract(p/T + 0.5)*2 - 1) (mirror tile, C0 and infinite). For i in 0..Iterations-1 by FoldType: Mirror: p = abs(p) - Offset. Polar (in a plane): r = |p.xy|; a = atan2poly(p.y, p.x); w = 2*pi/Sectors; a = mod(a, w); a = min(a, w - a); p.xy = r*(cos a, sin a) - Offset. Box: p = clamp(p, -L, L)*2 - p. Sphere: p *= 1 / clamp(|p|^2, Rmin^2, 1). Then p = Scale * R * p, with R a constant rotation. Log Radial option for Polar: (x,y) = (log r * K, a * K). Return Source(p).
ideas.look:
A fractal kaleidoscope: every triangle / square / tetrahedron of a self-similar subdivision contains an isometric copy of the source at its own scale. Terrain: nested plateaus and crystalline 'alien architecture'; caves (3D, Cellular or Perlin source inside a Mandelbox fold); textures: Sierpinski lace, Menger sponge tiles. Clearly different from FBm/Ridged, which spread detail uniformly.
[DomainFold, libs-modifiers] Look-tested (modes 9, 19). Mirror + rotate: lozenge carpet with soft quasi-tile symmetry. Sphere fold: dense ornate lace. Polar with 6 sectors: mandala. Log radial: recursive zoom into the centre. All unlike anything on the sheet, mostly for textures and stylised art rather than terrain.
ideas.why_new: The fractal nodes add detail everywhere; this one places detail with exact self-similar symmetry at a cost of roughly one Perlin per 6 iterations plus one source evaluation. There is no way to get hierarchical symmetric partitions from the current graph.
ideas.simd_plan: Per iteration <= 12 ops (Abs, FMA, Min/Max, Select, Reciprocal for BoxSphere); N=6 is ~70 ops (about one Perlin 2D); one source eval; no lattice; identical code 2D/3D/4D with a per-dimension Fold specialisation.
ideas.continuity: C0: Abs and conditional swaps are continuous; the BoxSphere piecewise scale is continuous at r2=0.25 (4 = 1/0.25) and r2=1 (1 = 1). Creases at every fold plane at every level.
ideas.params: Iterations int, Scale float, Offset per-dim hybrid (noise-driven offset gives a 'warped KIFS' that stays continuous), Angle / Yaw / Pitch float, Fold enum, Normalise bool, Cell Size float.
ideas.risks:
Strong 'CG fractal' signature can dominate; high N shrinks features past pixel size (aliasing). A noisy hybrid Offset is amplified by s per iteration, so document that. Offsets near 0 collapse to a plain kaleidoscope.
[DomainFold, libs-modifiers] Non-stationary unless Tile Period is set: far from origin Mirror folds act as a plain translation, and there is a visible centre. Magnifying folds alias fast. Effective source frequency shifts, so Feature Scale feels different. Polynomial atan2 accuracy at the sector seam matters. Low use for terrain, so priority depends on whether stylised textures matter.
ideas.variant_notes: DomainFold adds tile folding (infinite, stationary), polar sectors and a log-radial Droste option.
ideas.cost_note: Per iteration <= 12 ops (Abs, FMA, Min/Max, Select, Reciprocal for BoxSphere); N=6 is ~70 ops (about one Perlin 2D); one source eval; no lattice; identical code 2D/3D/4D with a per-dimension Fold specialisation.

ideas.name: DomainMap
ideas.one_liner: Per-node cylinder / torus / lat-long sphere / cube-sphere mapping: 2D input sampled on an embedded 3D or 4D surface, so seamless tiles and planets become composable inside the graph.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Mode {CylinderX, Torus, SphereLatLong, CubeSphere, SphereShell3D}, Period X, Period Y (world units), Radius (3D), Face Layout {Strip 6x1, Atlas 3x2}.

  CylinderX:     R = PeriodX/(2pi); a = x / R; return Source.Gen(seed, R*Cos(a), R*Sin(a), y)                           // 2D -> 3D, seamless in x
  Torus:         R1 = PeriodX/(2pi), R2 = PeriodY/(2pi); return Source.Gen(seed, R1*Cos(x/R1), R1*Sin(x/R1), R2*Cos(y/R2), R2*Sin(y/R2))   // 2D -> 4D: GenTileable2D as a node
  SphereLatLong: u = 2pi*x/PeriodX, v = pi*y/PeriodY (v in [-pi/2, pi/2]); cv = Cos(v); return Source.Gen(seed, R*cv*Cos(u), R*cv*Sin(u), R*Sin(v))  // equirectangular planet, poles converge correctly
  CubeSphere:    face = Floor(x/PeriodX) (Strip) or (Floor(x/Px), Floor(y/Py)) (Atlas); s,t = face-local in [-1,1]; optional equal-angle warp s = Tan(s*pi/4) via Sin/Cos; build the cube point from face with 6-way Select on sign/axis; normalise with InvSqrt; scale by R; return Source.Gen(seed, point)
  3D input:      CylinderX -> 4D (x wraps, y,z pass); SphereShell3D: (u, v, h) -> dir(u,v) * (R + h) (3D source: altitude-aware planet shells). Torus in 3D needs 5D: unsupported (document). 4D: identity.

[ManifoldLift, domain-geometry] Enum of pure maps with dim raise. Torus(Px,Py): 2D input to S4(Px/2pi*cos(2pi x/Px), Px/2pi*sin(2pi x/Px), Py/2pi*cos(2pi y/Py), Py/2pi*sin(2pi y/Py)), flat and no stretching. Cylinder(Px): to S3(cos,sin,y), or 3D input to S4. LatLong: lon=x*2pi/W, lat=(y/H-.5)*pi, to R*(cos lat cos lon, cos lat sin lon, sin lat) in S3, seamless at wrap and poles. CubeFace(face): gnomonic plus tan-adjust (u=tan(pi/4*x) with polynomial tan) to unit sphere in S3. Stereographic: (2x,2y,|p|^2-1)/(|p|^2+1), infinite plane to finite sphere. 3D to S^3: same in 4D for bounded-coordinates worlds. OctaFold (reverse direction): 3D direction n = p/|p|_1, feed S2(nx, ny) (lower hemisphere mirrors onto upper). This has creases on the equator but no seams, so any 2D-only source wraps a planet.
ideas.look: No new look by itself; it makes hard things easy: seamless strips and tiles per sub-graph (tile the base noise but not the Terrace after it, or tile two branches with different periods), equirectangular planet heightmaps without pole pinching, cube-map faces that match across edges, and shells with altitude. Combined with DomainKaleidoscope Icosa or DomainSymmetrize it also gives symmetric planets.
ideas.why_new: Asked repeatedly: FastNoiseLite #53 (torus), #86 (tile plus 'evolution looping' with UI video), gamedev links in #86 about world maps, Unity thread about planets, Reddit Burst erosion port added cubemap sampling for spherical terrain. FN2 can only hypertorus the entire output with GenTileable2D, and users cannot express this in graphs at all: no cos/sin domain, AddDimension only adds a constant or field. It also lets the editor preview planets, which GenPositionArray callers cannot.
ideas.simd_plan: 2-4 Sin/Cos (or one Sin+Cos pair reused) + source at +1/+2 dimensions: Perlin 2D 1.1 ns becomes Perlin 3D 2.2 / 4D 4.3 ns plus ~0.5 ns. CubeSphere: 6-way Select chain (~20 ops) + InvSqrt. No lattice window.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity (smooth embeddings) for all modes; CubeSphere is C0 across face edges (the sphere point is continuous, the direction derivative kinks), fine for sampling.
ideas.params: Mode enum, Period X/Y float, Radius float, Face Layout enum. All constant (not hybrid): a varying period breaks the seam.
ideas.risks:
Costs a dimension (4D sources for Torus); a user can already tile with GenTileable2D so the value is composability, not novelty; 3D Torus impossible.
[DomainMap, repo-demand] 4D source required for Torus and TimeLoop; node has to reject or fall back when input dim + added dims exceeds 4. Feature scale relationships are confusing: fractals stay seamless, since scaling happens below the map, but scale should be explained in world units. Not prototyped; simple enough.
ideas.variant_notes: Per-subtree tiling, wrap and planet projection. OctaFold direction mode (ManifoldLift) lets 2D-only sources wrap a planet, with mirror creases.
ideas.cost_note: 2-4 Sin/Cos (or one Sin+Cos pair reused) + source at +1/+2 dimensions: Perlin 2D 1.1 ns becomes Perlin 3D 2.2 / 4D 4.3 ns plus ~0.5 ns.

queue.name: DomainMap
queue.reason: Cylinder, torus and sphere embedding per sub-graph, so you tile the base rather than the Terrace. Plumbing with very high utility; costs one dimension.

ideas.name: DomainMobius
ideas.one_liner: Conformal remaps (sphere inversion, complex Mobius, z^k, exp, radial power/fisheye): curvature and scale gradients that keep isotropic noise locally isotropic.
ideas.algorithm:
Map enum: Inversion (n-D), Mobius (2D complex), Power (2D, int k), Exp (2D), RadialPower (n-D, fisheye). Centre C, Radius R.

  Inversion:   d = p - C; r2 = Dot(d,d) + eps; return Source.Gen(seed, C + d * (R*R / r2))          // works in 2D/3D/4D (inversions are conformal in all dims)
  Mobius:      z = x + i y; num = a*z + b; den = c*z + d (complex FMAs); w = num * conj(den) * Reciprocal(|den|^2 + eps)
               Presets enum: Identity, Loxodromic (fixed points +-1, multiplier m*e^{i theta}: conjugate z -> m e^{i theta} z by g(z) = (z-1)/(z+1)), Elliptic (|m|=1), Hyperbolic (theta=0)
  Power:       w = z^k by k-1 complex multiplies (k int member); k<0 via inversion first
  Exp:         w = (Exp(Min(x, xmax)) * Cos(y), Exp(..) * Sin(y))   // inverse of DomainPolar Log mode: a y-periodic source (period 2 pi s) becomes rings; rotate input by alpha first for log spirals
  RadialPower: d = p - C; r = |d|; w = C + d * Pow(r/R + eps, gamma - 1)                            // gamma<1 barrel/fisheye, gamma>1 pincushion
  3D/4D: Inversion and RadialPower are dimension agnostic; Mobius/Power/Exp act on xy and pass z,w.
ideas.look: Inversion of Checkerboard or Cellular yields circle packings and curved tilings (Apollonian look); noise that implodes toward a pole.
