Loxodromic Mobius: paired vortices / Droste double spirals. Power k: exact k-fold rotational symmetry with features shrinking outward (sunflower, vortex). Exp: rings and log spirals from any horizontally periodic source. RadialPower: lens bulge. All stay locally isotropic (no shear), unlike DomainWarp.
ideas.why_new: 5-20 ops for a family of smooth maps whose Jacobian is a similarity everywhere: curvature and feature-size gradients without the smearing of warps. Inverting lattice-based sources is a very large visual jump for the cost. Complements DomainPolar (Exp is its inverse) and DomainPerspective (projective vs conformal).
ideas.simd_plan: Branch-free: a few FMAs, one Reciprocal (or Pow / Exp+Sin+Cos for RadialPower / Exp), one source eval at the same dimension; ~0.1-0.3x Perlin + source. GenT for Inversion/RadialPower; 2D-specific for the complex maps.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity away from poles (inversion centre, Mobius pole -d/c, Power origin for k<0); poles are point singularities with infinitely fine detail.
ideas.params: Map enum, Centre per-dim float, Radius float, k int, Gamma float, Preset enum plus a,b,c,d complex (8 floats) for raw Mobius, Rotation float.
ideas.risks: Raw Mobius coefficients are unfriendly (presets mitigate); detail near poles aliases; Exp overflows for large x (clamp). Several modes overlap with DomainPolar; keep the node small if DomainPolar ships.
ideas.cost_note: Branch-free: a few FMAs, one Reciprocal (or Pow / Exp+Sin+Cos for RadialPower / Exp), one source eval at the same dimension; ~0.1-0.3x Perlin + source.

ideas.name: DomainPerspective
ideas.one_liner: Projective remap (homography): screen coordinates become ground-plane coordinates with a horizon; 'mode-7' depth for any source in one node.
ideas.algorithm:
Mode {GroundPlane, Matrix}. GroundPlane params: Height h (hybrid ok), Pitch, Focal f, Sky enum {Mirror, Clamp}, Far Fade F. Matrix mode: 9 floats (2D) / 16 (3D).

GroundPlane 2D (screen x right, y up; precompute cp=cos(Pitch), sp=sin(Pitch)):
  // view ray for screen point: d = (x, y*cp - f*sp, y*sp + f*cp)  (rotation of (x,y,f) about x by Pitch)
  dy = y*cp - f*sp; dz = y*sp + f*cp
  W  = Select(Sky==Mirror, Abs(dy), Max(-dy, eps))     // ground is where the ray goes down (dy<0); Mirror reflects the sky onto the ground
  t  = h / (W + eps)
  u  = t*x; v = t*dz                                   // ground hit point
  val = Source.Gen(seed, u, v)
  return (F>0) ? val / (1 + (t/F)^2) : val             // fade distant (aliasing) samples toward 0
Matrix 2D: (X,Y,Wn) = H*(x,y,1); return Source.Gen(seed, X/Wn, Y/Wn) with the same |Wn|+eps guard.
3D input: GroundPlane maps (x,y) to (u,v) and passes z as a third coordinate (animation / layering) -> Source(u,v,z); Matrix mode uses a 4x4 homography on (x,y,z,1) -> 3D source (perspective box). 4D: (u,v,z,w).
ideas.look: Any source turned into a receding textured plane: Tron grids (Checkerboard), lava seas, deserts, perspective cobblestones (Cellular), with a mirrored 'reflection' sky. Raw matrix mode gives vanishing-point distortion for parallax layers and fake depth. Every entry on the sheet is stationary; this has a horizon.
ideas.why_new: DomainScale/Rotate/AxisScale are affine; projective maps are the missing classical family (straight lines preserved, scale varies with depth). Replaces per-app shader code for 2D background art and makes depth gradients of feature size available to any graph for ~15 ops.
ideas.simd_plan: ~15 ops + 1 Reciprocal + source at the same dimension; ~0.2x Perlin + source. Fully branch-free; the sky handling is one Select.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity except on the horizon line W=0 (singular: feature size -> 0); with Mirror sky and Far Fade > 0 both sides converge to 0 so the node is continuous across the horizon.
ideas.params: Mode enum, Height hybrid (rolling ground), Pitch float, Focal float, Sky enum, Far Fade float, Matrix floats.
ideas.risks: Horizon aliasing is unavoidable without fading or a max depth; mostly a 2D/2.5D art node, less useful for terrain; a 16-float matrix UI is clunky (keep GroundPlane as the default).
ideas.cost_note: ~15 ops + 1 Reciprocal + source at the same dimension; ~0.2x Perlin + source.

ideas.name: DomainPolar
ideas.one_liner: Seam-free log-polar / spiral / mandala remap: 2D input becomes a 3D source sample (unit-circle embedding + log radius), no atan2, no theta=pi seam.
ideas.algorithm:
2D input, 3D source. Params: RadialMode {Log, Linear}, RadialScale a, AngularRadius R, Twist k (hybrid), Symmetry m (int >= 1), Mirror (bool), MinRadius rmin.

  r2 = x*x + y*y; r = Max(Sqrt(r2), rmin); inv = 1/r
  ux = x*inv; uy = y*inv                       // unit direction = (cos th, sin th) without atan2
  rho = (Log) ? Log(r)*a : r*a                 // Log => features scale with r (scale invariant zoom)
  phi = k*rho                                  // twist angle grows with rho: log spiral (Log) / Archimedean (Linear)
  c = Cos(phi); s = Sin(phi)
  (ux,uy) = (ux*c - uy*s, ux*s + uy*c)         // rotate the direction by phi
  // m-fold symmetry by de Moivre: (ux + i uy)^m, m-1 complex multiplies (m is an int member => uniform loop)
  (vx,vy) = (ux,uy); repeat m-1: (vx,vy) = (vx*ux - vy*uy, vx*uy + vy*ux)
  if Mirror: vy = Abs(vy)                      // dihedral symmetry; folding the circle onto a half circle is continuous
  return Source.Gen(seed, vx*R, vy*R, rho)     // circle of circumference 2*pi*R in source space, rho along the third axis

3D input: Cylindrical mode = same on (x,y), z passed through -> Source.Gen(seed, vx*R, vy*R, rho, z) (4D source). Spherical mode: d = p/|p| (3 comps), rho = Log(|p|)*a -> Source.Gen(seed, dx*R, dy*R, dz*R, rho); m-fold about z applies de Moivre to (dx,dy)/h with h = sqrt(dx^2+dy^2) and rescales by h, so poles stay continuous.
4D input: cylindrical on xy with z passed and w dropped (documented), or spherical on xyz.
No lattice; range unchanged (passes the source's range through).

[DrosteLift, domain-geometry] r2 = |p-c|^2 + e^2. r = sqrt(r2). L = .5*log(r2). Unit vector u = (p-c)/r needs no atan. Spiral: rotate u by Twist*L via sin, cos. Cylinder form: S3(K*L, K*ux, K*uy): locally conformal, features scale with r, seam-free because the angle is a circle in the source space. Droste form with log-period T: a = 2*pi*L/T, S4( (T/2pi)*K*cos a, (T/2pi)*K*sin a, K*ux, K*uy ), exactly repeating at each scale factor e^T when Twist*T = 2*pi*m, otherwise self-similar with rotation. N-fold: replace u by u^N through repeated complex multiply (fixed int count). 3D input: S4(K*L, K*nx, K*ny, K*nz) with n = unit direction; 3D Droste would need 5D, so drop it there.
ideas.look: Whirlpools, spiral galaxies, snail shells (Twist), tree rings and ripples (small R so angular variation vanishes), mandalas and snowflakes (m=6 + Mirror), infinite-zoom detail converging to the centre (Log mode). With Cellular source: radial crystal facets; with Checkerboard: log-polar grid (Escher-like zoom tiles). Good for ornaments, vortex masks, planetary storms, radial terrain features (calderas, impact basins) and any 'around a point' structure.
ideas.why_new: Nothing in the graph can produce radial, spiral or scale-invariant structure; DomainWarp only bends locally. The classic obstacle (polar mapping has a seam at theta = pi unless the source is periodic) disappears by sampling the source on an embedded circle instead of an angle, the same trick GenTileable2D uses, and the m-fold symmetry comes from complex powers so arbitrary m is exact and continuous. One source evaluation.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch-free: Sqrt/Reciprocal, Log, one Sin+Cos, m-1 complex multiplies (uniform int loop), one Abs/Select. ~25-30 ops + the source at one dimension higher. 2D cost ~0.3x Perlin + Perlin3D (2.2 ns) => ~2.5 ns; 3D ~0.4 ns + Perlin4D (4.3 ns). GenT works for the shared part; per-dimension overloads choose cylindrical vs spherical.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity wherever the source is, except the single centre point (log diverges, direction undefined; MinRadius clamps it). Mirror adds C0 creases along the m mirror lines by design.
ideas.params: RadialMode enum, RadialScale float, AngularRadius float, Twist hybrid (spatially varying twist gives swirls that stay seam-free), Symmetry int, Mirror bool, MinRadius float, Mode3D {Cylindrical, Spherical}. Centre via DomainOffset upstream.
ideas.risks:
Log mode aliases near the centre (features below pixel size): clamp with MinRadius or fade. Large m compresses angular features; users must raise R. 4D input cannot be made tileable in all four axes.
[DrosteLift, domain-geometry] Hero object, not stationary. Features at the core shrink below pixel size: control by e. Requires a higher dimension source and 3D Droste plus 4D input are not supported, so GenTileable falls back to dropping dims or reduces to the cylinder form. Far coords collapse to nearly constant (expected, log compression).
[DomainLogPolar, signal-phase] Needs a D+1-dimensional source (a 2D image needs a 3D-capable source: fine for all lattice noises, not for user 2D-only sources). The seamless Twist constraint is subtle. Centre-dependent, so not stationary: it is a design tool, not a terrain base.
ideas.variant_notes: Circle embedding removes the seam without atan2. Options merged: complex-power p-fold symmetry and mirror, Twist spirals, exact Droste by a torus lift, axis chirps, and an Unwrap mode with true angle so lattice sources wrap as arches and fans.
ideas.cost_note: 2D cost ~0.3x Perlin + Perlin3D (2.2 ns) => ~2.5 ns; 3D ~0.4 ns + Perlin4D (4.3 ns).

queue.name: DomainPolar
queue.reason: Log-polar through a unit-circle embedding into a 3D source, so no atan2 seam. Needs a minimum radius; 4D input drops out.

ideas.name: DomainQuasicrystal
ideas.one_liner: Cut-and-project: 2D position becomes a 4D source sample along 4 symmetric directions, so any lattice-based 4D source (Value, Perlin, Cellular, Checkerboard, SineWave) shows 8-, 10- or 12-fold aperiodic quasicrystal order.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Symmetry enum {Octagonal(8), Decagonal(10/5), Dodecagonal(12)}, Scale, Phase (4 floats, hybrid ok), Rotation.
Precompute 4 unit directions e_j (2D): Octagonal: angles j*pi/4, j=0..3; Decagonal: 2*pi*j/5, j=1..4 (Euler totient phi(5)=phi(8)=phi(12)=4, so Z^4 suffices for all three); Dodecagonal: j*pi/6, j=0..3.

  (x,y) rotated by Rotation, scaled: q = p / Scale
  X_j = Dot(q, e_j) + Phase_j         for j = 0..3          // 8 FMAs
  return Source.Gen(seed, X_0, X_1, X_2, X_3)               // 4D source

Why it works: the image plane is a totally irrational 2-plane of Z^4 that is invariant under the k-fold rotation acting as a signed coordinate permutation (e.g. octagonal: rotating by 45 deg maps (a,b,c,d) -> (-d,a,b,c)). The cell walls x_j = integer of any cubic-lattice source project to 4 families of parallel lines at the symmetric angles, i.e. de Bruijn's multigrid, whose dual is the Ammann-Beenker (8), Penrose (5/10) or Socolar (12) tiling. Cellular/Value in 4D therefore produce aperiodic rhombus-like cells; SineWave 4D gives the textbook quasicrystal interference pattern.
3D input: X_j = Dot(q.xy, e_j) + z * e_perp_j (z slides the cut through the lattice => phason flips: the pattern locally rearranges continuously), so animating z morphs between valid quasicrystals; 4D: w adds a second phason axis. (True icosahedral 3D needs 6D: not available.)
ideas.look: Penrose / Ammann-Beenker / dodecagonal aperiodic patterns: local 8/10/12-fold rosettes that never repeat, Islamic girih vibes with Checkerboard or Value sources, aperiodic Voronoi-like cells with Cellular, interference quasicrystals with SineWave. Nothing on the sheet has rotational order above 4-fold, and nothing is aperiodic with long-range order.
ideas.why_new: Lattice sources are inherently 4-fold (square) or 6-fold (simplex) periodic; this one-node change turns them into quasi-periodic structures with forbidden symmetries, at the cost of one 4D evaluation and 8 FMAs. Not expressible by any combination of existing nodes (AddDimension cannot make the irrational 2-plane).
ideas.simd_plan: 8 FMAs + a 4D source eval; cost dominated by the source (Perlin 4D 4.3 ns, Value 4D cheaper, Cellular 4D 41 ns). No lattice window of its own. Uses the existing 4D Gen path of every source, so it also pressures 4D performance work.
ideas.continuity: As the source (the map is linear).
ideas.params: Symmetry enum, Scale float, Phase 4 floats (hybrid: a noise-driven phase gives slow phason wobble), Rotation float.
ideas.risks: Generic smooth sources (Perlin/Simplex) look only subtly quasi-symmetric; the effect shines with lattice-aligned sources, so ship presets. Cellular 4D is expensive. Features along different e_j directions have equal scale only if the source is isotropic across its 4 axes.
ideas.cost_note: 8 FMAs + a 4D source eval; cost dominated by the source (Perlin 4D 4.3 ns, Value 4D cheaper, Cellular 4D 41 ns).

queue.name: DomainQuasicrystal
queue.reason: Cut-and-project to a 4D source in 8 FMAs turns any lattice source quasi-periodic. Strong on Value and Cellular, subtle on smooth sources; Cellular 4D costs ~41 ns.

ideas.name: DomainSymmetrize
ideas.one_liner: Average (or max/min/RMS) the source over the k rotations / 2k dihedral images of the position: exact k-fold symmetry with no mirror creases, and the missing rotational wallpaper groups via a torus-embedded source.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Group {Cyclic Ck, Dihedral Dk (2D); Ck about Z, Tetrahedral rotations (12) (3D)}, k int (2..8), Combine {Average, Max, Min, RMS}, Contrast Preserve bool, Centre.
Precompute cos/sin of 2pi*i/k, i=0..k-1 when k changes.

  d = p - Centre
  acc = 0 (or -inf / +inf for Max/Min); acc2 = 0
  for i in 0..k-1 (uniform):                                     // Dk: also the mirrored point (dx, -dy) rotated => 2k evals
     r = (d.x*c_i - d.y*s_i, d.x*s_i + d.y*c_i)
     v = Source.Gen(seed, Centre + r [, z])
     acc = combine(acc, v)
  Average: out = acc / k; if ContrastPreserve: out *= Sqrt(k) (sum of k far-apart samples has variance k * var, so the mean scaled by sqrt(k) keeps the source variance where the samples are independent)
  RMS: Sqrt(acc2 / k); Max/Min: acc.
3D: Ck about the z axis (rotate xy), or the 12 rotations of the tetrahedral group as a constant quaternion table (12 evals, heavy; expose as an opt-in). 4D: Ck in the xy plane, zw passed.
Wallpaper recipe: Symmetrize(C4 about the cell centre) -> DomainWrap(Torus, square cell) -> source gives the p4 wallpaper group continuously; C3/C6 with a hex-compatible torus period gives p3/p6; combine with DomainKaleidoscope for the remaining groups that contain glides only approximately.
ideas.look: Soft mandalas, snowflakes and rosettes with smooth (creaseless) symmetry, symmetric clouds, flower-like masks; Max combine yields a 'k-fold symmetric cellular' look (sharp ridges where images cross); with Perspective or Polar upstream it produces symmetric ornaments that still read as noise rather than folded tiles.
ideas.why_new: Folding (DomainKaleidoscope) gives symmetry with creases and cannot realise the rotation-only groups; averaging gives C-infinity symmetry for any source and unlocks p3/p4/p6 wallpaper via the torus embedding. Not expressible as a small graph (a Rotate+Add tree per k is possible but clumsy, and the variance normalisation and dihedral option make a dedicated node worthwhile).
ideas.simd_plan: k source evals + ~4 ops each; no lattice; cost = k x source (cap k at 8, 2k for Dk). The cos/sin table is per-node, no transcendental at Gen time.
ideas.continuity: As smooth as the source (sum of smooth functions), including through the centre.
ideas.params: Group enum, k int, Combine enum, Contrast Preserve bool, Centre per-dim float.
ideas.risks: k x cost. Near the centre the k samples coincide, so Contrast Preserve over-amplifies the centre (bright/dark dot) -- fade the sqrt(k) factor toward 1 inside a radius of about one feature. Tetrahedral 12 evals is expensive; probably 2D-first.
ideas.cost_note: k source evals + ~4 ops each; no lattice; cost = k x source (cap k at 8, 2k for Dk).

ideas.name: DomainTile
ideas.one_liner: Makes any subgraph tile at any period in any dimension by wrapping and crossfading, including warps, fractals and 3D volumes.
ideas.algorithm: Per axis with period P and blend fraction B: u = x - P*floor(x/P) in [0,P). x0 = u; x1 = u - P. w = smoothstep(P*(1-B), P, u). For each of 2^n combinations (n tiled axes) evaluate Source at the combination; weight = product of (1-w) or w. out = sum(weight*S) / sqrt(sum(weight^2)), with variance flatten relative to a Mean member (0 for noise). At u=P: w=1, value S(P-P) = S(0) which equals u=0's value, so the seam closes. Positions are bounded to about [-P,P).
ideas.look: Same character as the input with a slightly blended band near the tile edge. Gives tiled warped marble, tiled FBm clouds, tiled 3D volumes for any graph.
ideas.why_new: #12 needs 3D tile which the library says would need 6D. PR #72 ('Repeat version of Tileable2D accepting custom repeat interval') and #20 ask for custom period, and FastNoiseLite #86 asks for tiling. GenTileable2D works only for full output in 2D and through 4D. This tiles a subtree only, for example just the mask, not the detail, and avoids the 41 ns 4D cost for Cellular (4 x 3.9 = 16 ns). Side benefit: bounded coordinates avoid far coordinate precision loss, as in #83 and FastNoiseLite #176.
ideas.simd_plan: Fixed 2^n source calls: 4 in 2D, 8 in 3D, 16 in 4D. Weights via Floor, Select, polynomial. Whole-batch skip when no lane is in the band on that axis is legal for coherent grids, not assumed. Worst cost 4x / 8x / 16x source.
ideas.continuity: C1 if Source is C1: smoothstep has zero slope at both band ends, so derivative at the seam equals S'(0) on both sides.
ideas.params: Source, Period X/Y/Z/W (0 off, world units), Blend Fraction, Mean, Flatten toggle.
ideas.risks: Blend band shows ghosting on sharp features (cellular walls, ridges show double images). Variance flatten is only right for zero-mean roughly independent values; Gaussian assumption fails for heavily skewed sources. Worst-case cost grows quickly with dimension. PeriodicFBm is better when the source is lattice-only. Not prototyped; formula checked by hand only.
ideas.cost_note: Worst cost 4x / 8x / 16x source.

queue.name: DomainTile
queue.reason: Wrap and crossfade for any graph including 3D. Check ghosting in the band and the 16x worst case in 4D.

ideas.name: DomainTwist
ideas.one_liner: Rotate the plane perpendicular to an axis by an angle that grows along the axis (twist), decays with radius (swirl/vortex column) or grows with w (continuous spin, exact loop): helical caves, tornado funnels, barber poles, spinning fields.
ideas.algorithm:
Axis enum (X/Y/Z/W). Let s = coordinate along the axis, (u,v) the perpendicular pair (for Axis=W rotate (x,y) or a chosen plane), r2 = u^2 + v^2.
 falloff = (Radius > 0) ? Exp(-r2 / Radius^2) : 1
 theta = Rate * s * falloff + Swirl * falloff + Angle(p)   // Angle hybrid, Rate per unit along axis, Swirl constant vortex term
 (u', v') = (u cos theta - v sin theta, u sin theta + v cos theta)
Pass s and remaining coords through. 2D: Axis is implicitly the out-of-plane axis, so only the Swirl/Angle terms act (vortex around origin, or around per-lane Center X/Y hybrids). Axis=W in 4D: theta = Rate*w gives a field spinning about the axis, looping exactly with period 2pi/Rate.
ideas.look: Twist a TubeNoise or TPMSNoise about Y: helical tunnels and screw-shaped sponge; twist CrystalGrainNoise: twisted columnar crystals; with Radius: a tornado/whirlpool funnel where only the core rotates; Axis=W: slowly rotating cloud banks that loop. 2D: vortex-swirled noise around a point.
ideas.why_new: DomainRotate and DomainRotatePlane take constant angles; an angle varying with position cannot be built from existing nodes (hybrid angles would rotate about the origin unboundedly, which the falloff and the axis-relative formulation here avoid). Cost is negligible.
ideas.simd_plan: One Sin/Cos (+ one Exp with falloff) and 6 FMAs; DomainModifiers pattern with per-dimension Gen. Negligible cost (~0.3 ns).
ideas.continuity: C-infinity in the warp (so output as smooth as the source).
ideas.params: Axis enum, Rate, Swirl, Radius (0 = none), Angle hybrid, Center X/Y/Z hybrids.
ideas.risks: Twist without falloff makes displacement grow with radius from the axis, so far-off-axis features shear into streaks (that is what twist is; document Radius). Modest novelty compared with the other proposals; cheap enough to justify.
ideas.cost_note: Negligible cost (~0.3 ns).

queue.name: DomainTwist
queue.reason: Axis twist with falloff at ~0.3 ns for helical caves and vortex columns. Trivial and missing from the graph.

ideas.name: FaultLines
ideas.one_liner: Sequential families of long straight fault planes, each slab slipped by a hash, so later faults cross-cut and offset earlier ones like real geology.
ideas.algorithm: For l in 0..Faults-1: n = dir(l) (golden-angle table), t = perpendicular to n (3D: strike or dip vector in plane). d = dot(p,n)*s_l + o_l. i = floor(d). slip = rnd11(hash(i,l)). Zone option, f = d-i: slip = s_i + (s_(i+1)-s_i)*.5*smoothstep(1-z,1,f) + (s_(i-1)-s_i)*.5*smoothstep(z,0,f). p += t*slip*Slip/s_l. Output S(p). Because p is updated in the loop, later faults displace earlier ones, giving true cross-cutting relationships. z=0: hard scarps. z>0: drag folds in shear zones, C1.
ideas.look: Tectonic block faults with offset strata, shifted glass, broken marble and terrain with long linear scarps; with Zone it gives big sheared drag folds. Prototype with strata source reads as a geological cross-section. Prototyped: mode=9.
ideas.why_new: Voronoi-based cells have no long straight lines across the map, and no cross-cutting offsets. Warps cannot produce slip discontinuities with undisturbed blocks between them. Hard thing made easy for geology and strata.
ideas.simd_plan: Each family: dot, floor, 1 hash (3 with Zone), about 0.5-1 ns (estimate). 4 faults about 3 ns. Dimension agnostic through a table of n, t per dimension. Bounded displacement regardless of far coords.
ideas.continuity: z=0: discontinuous on purpose (c0ratio 1.02). z>0: C1 (5.07 at z=.15, steep, no jump).
ideas.params: Fault Count (int), Spacing (hybrid per node), Slip (hybrid), Zone Width, Direction Seed, Source.
ideas.risks: Fault spacing has lattice regularity per family: use jittered per-family scale (prototype uses 1 + l*.31) and pre-warp. Isotropic sources show faults only weakly; needs strata or high-gradient sources. Tilted 3D variants need checking. Slip should be well below spacing to preserve slab identity.
ideas.cost_note: Each family: dot, floor, 1 hash (3 with Zone), about 0.5-1 ns (estimate). 4 faults about 3 ns.

queue.name: FaultLines
queue.reason: Sequential slipped slabs with drag zones: true cross-cutting offsets at ~1 ns per family (J2 top pick). Needs a strata source to show; check regular family spacing.

disp.how: the node

ideas.name: GradientSmear
ideas.one_liner: Streamline-like streaks at about 10 taps: one gradient at p sets a direction, then a short weighted line integral of detail runs along it.
ideas.algorithm: g from stencil of guide S at p. t = R90(g)/sqrt(|g|^2+e) (contour mode) or g/sqrt(|g|^2+e) (along mode). Output sum_{k=-M..M} w_k Detail(p + k a t) / sum w_k, with w_k = (1-|k|/(M+1))^2, then multiply by a measured gain to restore variance. 3D contour mode: t = cross(grad A, grad B)/(norm+e) using two guides, which has no hairy-ball seam and fades where the two are parallel. 4D: along mode only, or a generalised cross of three gradients. The direction is not re-evaluated along the segment, which is what keeps the cost flat.
ideas.look: Swirling closed flow lines, hair, wood grain, fingerprint whorls, marbled smoke, with vortices at extrema and saddles of the guide. Along mode gives radial streak bursts between basins. Good for fur, wood, wind streaks, fluid-like textures.
ideas.why_new: True directional low-pass filtering. Warps stretch features but keep them sharp across the flow, while this removes energy along the flow only, which yields actual line structure. It was a surprise that this straight-segment version looks better than true curved LIC at the same budget: curved LIC at N=3 showed beads, and needed 49 taps at N=6.
ideas.simd_plan: Taps 2D 3+7=10 (M=3), 3D 8+7=15, 4D 5+7=12 along only. Perlin detail about 11/33/52 ns (scalar 2D prototype 12.4x perlin2 using fbm wrapper overhead). Direction is computed once for all lanes, then a fixed loop.
ideas.continuity: C0, C1 with a C2 guide, thanks to e in the normalisation. Measured c0ratio 7.76 with max slope about 103 per unit at detail frequency 8.
ideas.params: Guide, Detail, Step a (hybrid; length of streak, 0 fades to no smear), M (int), Mode enum, Sample Distance h. Keep a below half the detail feature size or beads appear.
ideas.risks: Contrast drop requires a measured gain per M and a. Detail sampling along a straight segment wrongly crosses tight curvature near vortices, though it looks acceptable. 3D requires a second guide and has more cost. Known cousin: line integral convolution, not seen as a noise node.
ideas.cost_note: Perlin detail about 11/33/52 ns (scalar 2D prototype 12.4x perlin2 using fbm wrapper overhead).

ideas.name: KaleidoStamp
ideas.one_liner: Scatter rosettes of any node: N-fold symmetry by O(log N) mirror folds in stamp-local coordinates, with no trig or atan2.
ideas.algorithm: Choose top K stamps as in StampScatter (rank-subtract fade). For each winner, local l = (p-c)/r rotated by hash angle. Fold: th = pi; for q in 0..Folds (constant): th /= 2; n = (-sin th, cos th) from a precomputed table; dn = min(0, dot(l,n)); l -= 2*dn*n. Reflection is continuous (it maps across its own mirror exactly), so fold seams cannot jump. This gives 2^(Folds+1)-fold mirrored rosettes. v_k = Source.Gen(h_k, l*Zoom). Output sum(w_k v_k). 3D: fold across chosen octahedral or icosahedral mirror sets (constant table of 3-6 planes), for crystal-symmetric solids. Also useful as K=1 Scatter-free node: DomainKaleido around a single origin or hybrid-free lattice.
ideas.look: Prototype: each stamp becomes a symmetric mandala, snowflake, or insect-face-like Rorschach blot from plain Perlin. With R around 1.3, the field densely covers with overlapping symmetric motifs. Instantly reads as designed instead of random; ornament, flowers, snowflakes, crystal cross-sections.
ideas.why_new: No node has mirror folding, and DomainAxisScale or abs of coordinates only offers a single global axis fold. Local per-instance mirror groups with per-stamp seeds provide endless non-repeating motifs from any existing graph.
ideas.simd_plan: Scan as StampScatter (5 ns in 2D, 15 ns in 3D, 50 ns in 4D), plus K*(Folds dot-and-subtract + Source). Folds table computed at param set. 3D mirror table cost ~ number of planes. K=2 Folds=3 in 2D: about 8 ns + 2 Source.
ideas.continuity: C0 verified: c0ratio 8.17 at K=2, Folds=2. Reflection folding is C0 with mirror kinks in the source's image, visible as creases when Source has gradient across a mirror (which is the look).
ideas.params: Folds (int), Source, K, Size, Zoom, Rotation (per stamp), Density, Mirror Set enum in 3D
ideas.risks: Reads as ornamental, so its niche is decorative textures and props rather than terrain. Pareidolia (faces) with low octave sources. Fold count per-lane is impossible; it is a member. Could overlap with a generic Kaleidoscope domain modifier from another lens, but per-stamp local fold is the distinct part.
ideas.cost_note: Scan as StampScatter (5 ns in 2D, 15 ns in 3D, 50 ns in 4D), plus K*(Folds dot-and-subtract + Source).

ideas.name: KnotField
ideas.one_liner: Stereographic lift of 3D space to S3, then Hopf or Milnor map to a low-dimensional source: fields whose level sets are linked rings or literal torus knots.
ideas.algorithm: X = p*s, r2 = |X|^2, n = (2X, r2-1)/(r2+1) on S3, with u = n0+i*n1, v = n2+i*n3. Hopf mode: h = (2 Re(u conj v), 2 Im(u conj v), |u|^2-|v|^2) on S2, output S3(k*h): constant along linked Villarceau circles, so every isosurface is a linked set of tori. Milnor mode with integers (P,Q): f = u^P + v^Q in C, output S2(k Re f, k Im f), or Tube: 1-2*smoothstep(0,Tube,|f|). The zero set of u^2+v^3 on S3 is a trefoil, so Tube carves a literal knotted tube in a volume. Polys only, no atan. For a stationary field pre-apply pmm fold (tri on each axis), giving a lattice of knots with continuous joins.
ideas.look: 3D volumes with impossible structure: interlocked ring clouds, magnetic-field-like plasma, trefoil caves and lattice of chained cells. In 2D slices it looks only like smooth low-frequency warp and is dull (prototype confirmed this), so this is a 3D or volumetric node. Good for hero caves, magic plasma, strange attractor clouds. Prototyped 2D slice only: mode=11.
ideas.why_new: Topology cannot be made by warping noise, as warps are homeomorphisms of the plain source and cannot generate linking or knots on demand. Very cheap, with no lattice.
ideas.simd_plan: About 15 multiplies and 1 divide, under 1 ns (estimate), plus a 3D (Hopf) or 2D (Milnor) source. P,Q small ints with constant multiply loops. Input 2D: slice at constant z. Input 4D: skip stereographic, normalise p onto S3 directly (bounded and elegant, and GenTileable torus input lands exactly on a Clifford torus of S3, worth testing).
ideas.continuity: C-infinity as rational functions, except for optional fold creases. Field tends to constant at infinity since all far points map near the pole.
ideas.params: Mode enum (Hopf, Milnor, Tube), Scale s, P, Q, Source Scale k, Tube Radius, Lattice Fold flag, Source.
ideas.risks: Niche and hero-object unless lattice folded. Isosurface knot look has not been rendered in 3D, only derived, so it needs a raymarch or marching-cube look test before any node work. Knot tube thickness varies strongly with distance from origin since stereographic is non-uniform.
ideas.cost_note: About 15 multiplies and 1 divide, under 1 ns (estimate), plus a 3D (Hopf) or 2D (Milnor) source.

queue.name: KnotField
queue.reason: Wild card. Hopf and Milnor lifts give linked and knotted isosurfaces for ~15 mults. Top distinct score, but never rendered, so the prototype must prove the 3D look.

ideas.name: LocalFrame
ideas.one_liner: Spatially varying scale and rotation without swirl artifacts: quantise the control into bins, evaluate the source at the two adjacent frames, and contrast-preserving blend them.
ideas.algorithm:
VariableScale: s = Scale(p) (log2 units); k = floor(s/Step)*Step; t = quintic((s-k)/Step); A = Source(p * 2^k); B = Source(p * 2^(k+Step)). VariableRotate: th = Angle(p); dl = pi/Bins; k = floor(th/dl); t = hermite(th/dl - k); A = Source(R(k*dl)*p); B = Source(R((k+1)*dl)*p). Both: out = lerp(A, B, t) / sqrt(t^2 + (1-t)^2). k needs no wrap for a continuous scalar control. Combining both controls would need 4 evals (bilinear), so ship as two nodes or a mode switch. Anisotropy comes from the source, e.g. DomainAxisScale(X=0.25, Y=3, Perlin).

[ScaleField, signal-phase] L=Range*(ScaleSource(p)*0.5+0.5), the log2 of the frequency.
ra=2*Round(L/2) is the even slot; rb=2*Round((L-1)/2)+1 is the odd slot.
wa=1-|L-ra|; wb=1-wa; optionally smoothstep wa.
fa=Exp(ra*ln r), fb=Exp(rb*ln r).
Out=(wa*S(seed+ra, p*fa)+wb*S(seed+rb, p*fb))/Sqrt(wa*wa+wb*wb).
Each slot jumps only at the L where its weight is zero, so there are no seams. The source gets per-lane positions and seeds, which the execution model already allows because lanes may be spatially unrelated. Sibling mode Rotate: the same two-slot scheme on rotation angle, which gives oriented anisotropic sources (DomainAxisScale noise, SineWave) a spatial orientation field.
ideas.look:
Scale: noise whose feature size changes smoothly across space with stable statistics. Rotate with an anisotropic source: fur, wind-swept grass, wood-like streaks flowing along an angle field. Look-tested (modes 4, 5): naive p*2^s shows large moire swirls and naive R(th)p shows tight moire loops, while both quantised versions are clean. The rotate result is one of the most striking looks from this lens.
[ScaleField, signal-phase] Tested. Noise goes smoothly from fine grain to broad blobs across the image, with the same isotropic character at each scale. The naive noise(f(p)*p) on the same field gives violent swirls and shear (rendered side by side). Uses: terrain roughness zones, gravel to sand transitions, detail focused near a mask, biome-dependent roughness.
ideas.why_new: A hybrid DomainScale or DomainRotate would have shear proportional to |p|*|grad control|, so artifacts grow with distance from the origin, which is why people avoid it. Quantisation removes the origin dependence with exactly 2 source evals regardless of range or bin count. Feature size or orientation as a spatial input is otherwise unavailable, and DomainScale's Scaling is a constant float today.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch-free, always 2 source evals + 1 control. Floor, Convert. 2^k by writing the float exponent bits (integer steps) or FS::Pow (fractional Step). Per-lane cos/sin of two angles (4 FS::Sin/Cos), or a small permute table when Bins is a power of two. About 2x source + ~1 ns in all dimensions. 3D rotates in a plane or about a constant axis (R built by the same Sin/Cos); 4D rotates xy and zw planes.
ideas.continuity: C0: at a bin change t reaches 0 or 1, so only one frame has weight. Measured c0ratio 8.0 for both.
ideas.params: Source, Scale (hybrid, log2), Step (float), Angle (hybrid, radians), Bins (int), Axis enum, Contrast Preserve (bool).
ideas.risks:
Ghosting in the blend band (two unrelated patterns as a double exposure), especially when the control changes slowly or the source is strongly anisotropic. Mid-blend amplitude can reach sqrt2 x source on correlated values, so clamp if range matters. An angle from atan2 of a direction field wraps and would jump, so use a continuous scalar (or map the wrap via multiples). Large scale ranges lose float precision at far coordinates.
[ScaleField, signal-phase] The mid-blend zone shows two scales overlaid, which is mild for r=2 and worse for larger ratios. Sources must honour per-lane seed and positions; GeneratorCache would miss heavily. GPU-style lane coherence assumptions in sources would break. Rotate mode has only been reasoned through via the SteeredStripes test, and with stripes it gives herringbone (see that entry).
sources: Flow-map two-phase blending (Vlachos, Valve, from memory, not consulted)
ideas.variant_notes: Six proposals: vary scale or rotation by quantising per lane and blending exactly two evals. The odd/even slot form (ScaleField) keeps a single source pair for any range. Rotate mode with stripes gives herringbone at low bin counts.
ideas.cost_note: About 2x source + ~1 ns in all dimensions.

queue.name: LocalFrame
queue.reason: Binned scale and rotation crossfade removes origin shear when scale varies by mask, 2x source. Earlier proto beats naive scaling; watch the ghosting band.

ideas.name: LogPolarVortex
ideas.one_liner: Each Voronoi cell becomes a self-similar zoom into its centre: the Source is evaluated in (log radius, unit direction) coordinates with optional spiral twist, giving whirlpools/galaxies/rosettes whose detail density grows toward the centre, packed seamlessly by a cell-edge fade.
ideas.algorithm:
cellular 3x3 search -> nearest point c (hash h), F1, F2 (reuse Cellular code)
  d = p - c ; r = Max(|d|, MinRadius) ; u = (d / r)               // unit direction, no atan2
  L = Log(r) * ZoomRate + rnd01(h)*Period                           // log-radius coordinate
  twist: (cs, sn) = (Cos(Twist*L), Sin(Twist*L)); u' = rotate(u, cs, sn)   // spiral arms; 3D: rotate u about a hashed per-cell axis
  2D node: v = Source3D(u'.x * Angular, u'.y * Angular, L)          // Source sampled one dimension up (as AddDimension does)
  3D node: v = Source4D(u'.x*Angular, u'.y*Angular, u'.z*Angular, L)
  m = smoothstep(0, Fade, F2 - F1)                                   // cell-edge fade so neighbouring vortices meet without a crack
  out = Lerp(Source(p) * Background, v, m)   or  v*m
Because the direction lives on the unit circle/sphere the angular coordinate is automatically periodic (no seam at 2pi); the radial coordinate is logarithmic so each factor of e in radius maps to a fixed noise distance: structure repeats statistically under zoom (Droste effect) down to MinRadius.
ideas.look: Fields of whirlpools, galaxies, rosettes, tree rings with ever-finer rings toward the centre, drain/vortex surfaces; with Twist the Source's features become logarithmic spiral arms. Nothing on the sheet is scale-covariant around points. Good for magical/alien terrain, shells, eyes, fluid vortices, spiral galaxies in space skyboxes, and as a warp when used inside a DomainWarp graph on its output.
ideas.why_new: Requires evaluating a Source in a log-polar frame per cell with a dimension lift; a graph has no log, no per-cell centre, no unit-direction coordinates. Combines multi-scale self-similarity (literal) with cellular packing.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch-free: Cellular F1/F2 window + Log, InvSqrt, Sin/Cos + one Source call one dimension higher (+ optional second Source call for background). Cost ~CellularDistance + Source(D+1) + 20 ops. 2D and 3D exact; 4D requires a 5D Source (not available): 4D falls back to using (u.xyz, L) and dropping the 4th direction component (tiling then imperfect; acceptable, document it).
ideas.continuity: C1 inside a cell where the Source is C1 (log and normalisation are smooth for r>0; MinRadius caps the singularity, leaving a flat disc); across cell edges continuity comes from the Fade (C1 with smoothstep).
ideas.params: Source (required), Zoom Rate, Angular Scale, Twist hybrid, Min Radius, Fade, Background, Jitter, Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks: Near the centre the Source is sampled at extreme frequency in angle terms; aliasing inside MinRadius is avoided by the cap but the ring at MinRadius is a visible disc; blend to Source(c) there. 4D story is weak.
ideas.cost_note: Cost ~CellularDistance + Source(D+1) + 20 ops.

ideas.name: QuasiFold
ideas.one_liner: Average of N triangle-wave pleats at N-fold angles: an aperiodic quasicrystal mirror-facet domain at about the cost of one Perlin.
ideas.algorithm: q = (2/N) * sum_{i<N} T( dot(p*s, n_i) + o_i ) * n_i, where n_i is at angle pi*i/N, T is a slope +-1 triangle wave with range [-1,1], and o_i is a fixed irrational offset per i. If T(x)=x this is the identity, so T only introduces creases along N line families. Output S(q/s + drift*p). The Jacobian is (2/N) sum +-n_i n_i^T, piecewise constant, so every facet is a linear image of the source, with scale varying per facet. For N not in {1,2,3,4,6} the result is quasi-periodic and has no translational period. Drift (about 0.05-0.1) stops q being confined to a bounded disc.
ideas.look: Stained-glass polygons and cut-gem facets with straight creases in an aperiodic pattern with 5, 7 or 9-fold local order. With a stripe source it becomes bold polygon contour bands like a topographic map of a crystal. Very different from anything on the contact sheet. Good for crystalline terrain, rock faces, sci-fi plating, masks. Prototyped: mode=1 with N=5, 7.
ideas.why_new: Hard straight-edged facets with mixed scales and no lattice. Warps only give smooth folds and Cellular only gives convex cells of value. Requires tri-wave fold not expressible in current graph.
ideas.simd_plan: Loop of constant N: dot, floor, abs, FMulAdd. No hash. About 0.2 ns per direction, so N=5 is about +1 ns in 2D (estimate) plus the source. 3D: 6 icosahedral axes (6D cut-and-project analogue) or 4 cube diagonals. 4D: table of 8-10 directions. Pure function of all inputs, so tileable through the 4D torus with some distortion.
ideas.continuity: C0 with creases (Lipschitz); measured c0ratio 7.95. C1 option by rounding T near its peaks.
ideas.params: Directions N (int), Cell Size, Drift (hybrid), Offset Seed (derive o_i from Seed), Source.
ideas.risks: Zero Jacobian regions stretch source (large blurry facets) at some sign combinations. That is part of the look at low N but can read as out-of-focus patches; fbm sources look less crisp than stripe or ridged sources. Offsets are fixed per seed, so results are a function of seed only through o_i and the source.
ideas.cost_note: About 0.2 ns per direction, so N=5 is about +1 ns in 2D (estimate) plus the source.

ideas.name: SteeredBank
ideas.one_liner: Orient detail along a sampled gradient by crossfading a small bank of fixed-direction stretched noises, so there is no rotation and no far-from-origin shear.
ideas.algorithm: K axes a_k mod 180 degrees (2D K=4-6; 3D 6 icosahedron diagonals; 4D 12). Stretch without frames: q_k = p + (1/ani - 1)(p.a_k)a_k + offset_k, n_k = Detail(q_k). Orientation weight from the guide's gradient, with no atan: o_k = ((g.a_k)^2/(|g|^2+e) - 1/D) scaled by |g|^2/(|g|^2+e2). w_k = (0.5 + 0.5 o_k)^P via integer power. Output sum(w_k n_k)/sqrt(sum w_k^2), which preserves variance. Enum selects streaks along contours or along the slope by flipping the sign of o_k.
ideas.look: K=6 and sharpening P=6 give feather and leaf-like fans, with sector boundaries that resemble plumage or shell ridges. Multi-octave detail with larger K looks like brushed, Van Gogh-style flow. K=4 and low P looks woven or herringbone. Good for feathers, foliage masses, brushed metal, strata following terrain, fabrics.
ideas.why_new: Hybrid rotation of a domain shears without bound far from the origin, so spatially varying anisotropy is not achievable today. The bank is a linear blend of linear domains, so shear cannot grow with distance and the node stays correct at any coordinate. A graph would need K+D+1 hand-wired nodes, and it could not get the double-angle weights.
ideas.simd_plan: Taps (D+1) guide + K detail: 2D 3+6=9, 3D 4+6=10, 4D 5+12=17. On Perlin-based detail about 10/22/73 ns. A guide may be a cheap low-frequency single octave. Could skip detail evaluation when all lanes have w_k=0, which does not alter results.
ideas.continuity: C0 and generally C1 when the guide is C2 with the fade at |g|=0. Measured c0ratio 7.32 with the fade, 1.9 without it, so the fade term is essential.
ideas.params: Guide source, Detail source, Anisotropy ani (float), K (enum), Sharpness P (int), Orientation enum, Sample Distance h (hybrid). Sharpness could be hybrid at the cost of Pow.
ideas.risks: Crossfade between two directions shows crosshatching in between unless P is large, and large P makes sector seams (which is the feather look but may not be wanted). The stretch and K are compile-style choices for the axis tables. Related to Goldberg et al. anisotropic noise, which uses a precomputed texture bank; this is the pointwise form.
ideas.cost_note: On Perlin-based detail about 10/22/73 ns.

ideas.name: TileDomain
ideas.one_liner: Closed-form structured tilings (running bond, herringbone, basket, hex, chevron, random-course ashlar, fan cobbles) that hand the Source per-tile local coordinates, a per-tile seed and an exact edge distance, so bricks, parquet, roof tiles, stone walls and honeycombs with per-tile variation become one node plus whatever Source you like.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Pattern enum, TileW/TileH, N (brick length in units of width, Herringbone/Basket), RowOffset (hybrid; RunningBond), LengthJitter/HeightJitter (RandomCourses), Mortar (hybrid, world units), Bevel, Rotation enum {None, Quarter, Random(+-A)}, LookupScale, Output enum {Lookup, EdgeDistance, TileValue, TiltedHeight, LocalU, LocalV}, Source (GeneratorSource), MortarValue (hybrid).

Every pattern yields: integer tile id (i,j,extra), local (u,v) in [-0.5,0.5]^2 (normalised by the tile's own extents), edge distance e in world units. Then common post-processing.

Grid: i=floor(x/W), j=floor(y/H), u=x/W-i-0.5, v=y/H-j-0.5, e=min((0.5-|u|)W,(0.5-|v|)H).
RunningBond: j=floor(y/H); xs = x - RowOffset(j)*W with RowOffset(j)=off*j (0.5 = stretcher bond) or rnd01(j) (random bond); i=floor(xs/W); rest as Grid.
Basket: square s=(floor(x/(N W)), floor(y/(N W))); horizontal planks if (sx+sy)&1; plank index = floor(frac across * N); local coords with N:1 aspect; e from plank edges.
Hex: axial coords q=(2/3)x/R, r=(-1/3)x/R+(sqrt3/3)y/R, cube-round (3 rounds + 1 fix via masks) -> centre; e = R - max(|dy|, |dx| sqrt3/2 + |dy|/2) style hex SDF; (u,v) = offset/R.
Chevron: band b=floor(x/(N W)); sign = (b&1)? -1:+1; d=(sign*x+y)/sqrt2; strip k=floor(d/W); u along strip, v across; e = min(across distance, distance to band boundary).
Herringbone (1xN bricks): fundamental L = H brick [0,N)x[0,1) union V brick [N,N+1)x[0,N); lattice basis A=(-1,1), B=(N+1,N-1) (det = 2N = area, verified). (a,b) = M^-1 p; a0=floor(a), b0=floor(b); for (da,db) in {-1,0,1}^2: o=(a0+da)A+(b0+db)B, q=p-o; inH = 0<=q.x<N & 0<=q.y<1; inV = N<=q.x<N+1 & 0<=q.y<N; exactly one candidate hits; Select id, (u,v) (for H: (q.x/N-0.5, q.y-0.5); for V: (q.y/N-0.5, q.x-N-0.5)), e = min distance to the 4 brick edges. Proto should prune the 9 candidates to the 4 that can actually hit.
RandomCourses (ashlar / stacked stone / log pile / bookshelf): rows are a 1D jittered lattice on y: boundaries B_j=(j+HeightJitter*(rnd01(j)-0.5))*H, j found with the 4-boundary select (compute B_{k-1..k+2}, k=floor(y/H), row = k+1-[y<B_{k+1}]-[y<B_k]); within row j stones are a 1D jittered lattice on x seeded by j with per-row phase: C_i=(i+rnd01(j)+LengthJitter*(rnd01(i,j)-0.5))*W; stone = same select on x; (u,v) normalised by the actual stone width/height; e = min distance to its 4 boundaries. 8 hashes total; vertical joints never align across courses.
Fan (European fan cobbles): staggered fan cells (RunningBond with off 0.5, pitch P); in each fan, polar coords about the fan's bottom-centre: rho=|q|, theta via polynomial atan2 (seam at +-pi lies on the clipped fan base); ring k=floor(rho/ring), cobbles per ring m_k=round(pi(k+0.5)ring/cobble), cobble index floor(theta/pi*m_k) -> cobble centre -> dome or edge distance; fans overlap, higher row wins where rho<=P (2 rows x 2 columns candidates).

Common post: H=hash(i,j,extra,seed); e' = e - Mortar; inside = e'>0; TileValue = rnd11(H); Rotation: Quarter rotates (u,v) by (H&3)*90deg via swaps/negations, Random rotates by A*rnd11(H) (one sin/cos per lane); Lookup = Source.Gen(seed ^ H, (u*W+offX(H))*LookupScale, (v*H+offY(H))*LookupScale [, z, w]) selected with MortarValue outside, times smoothstep(0,Bevel,e') if Bevel>0; EdgeDistance = ScaleOutput(e'); TiltedHeight = HeightJitter*rnd11(H) + u*tx(H) + v*ty(H) (sunk / tilted tiles).
Nesting works because Lookup passes tile-local coordinates: TileDomain(Hex, Source=TileDomain(Grid,...)) = mosaic within tiles; TileDomain(Herringbone, Quarter, Source=wood rings) = parquet.
ideas.look: Crisp regular masonry with controllable irregularity: stretcher-bond brick with per-brick colour and sunken bricks, herringbone/basket parquet with grain rotated per plank, hex honeycomb with bevelled walls, random-course stone walls where every stone has its own length and height but courses stay level, fan-pattern cobbles. In 3D the pattern is extruded along z with the tile seed, so per-column strata on z gives basalt columns and brick walls with thickness. Nothing on the contact sheet is structured and periodic with per-tile randomness.
ideas.why_new: Checkerboard is the only structured lattice node. A graph cannot find the tile containing a point for bond/herringbone/hex/ashlar, cannot give the Source tile-local coordinates with a per-tile seed, and cannot produce an exact tile edge distance for mortar and bevels. Random courses in particular (rows of random-length elements) are a top texture-artist request with no graph equivalent.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch-free: floors, a few hashes, mask selects; Herringbone is 9 (prunable to 4) candidate parallelogram tests with integer/compare ops; Hex is cube-rounding with masks; RandomCourses is 8 hashes and two 4-way selects. No window search except Fan (4 candidates). 2D/3D/4D: the pattern lives in (x,y) and extra axes pass through to the Source with a per-tile offset (rotate the plane upstream with DomainRotate); GenTileable2D is not needed because the pattern is periodic by construction with an integer Period. Cost: Grid/Bond/Hex about 0.5-1 ns + Source, Herringbone/RandomCourses about 1.5 ns + Source, Fan 4-6 ns (Worley-like).
ideas.continuity: EdgeDistance mode C0 (min of distances). Lookup/TileValue/TiltedHeight are discontinuous at tile edges by design (it is a tiling); Bevel>0 makes Lookup C0 by forcing it to MortarValue at the edge.
ideas.params: Pattern enum, TileW/TileH, N int, RowOffset (hybrid), LengthJitter/HeightJitter, Mortar (hybrid, lets a noise erode the grout), Bevel, Rotation enum + Angle, LookupScale, Output enum, Source, MortarValue (hybrid), optional integer Period for hash wrap (explicit tiling).
ideas.risks:
Herringbone candidate pruning and the exact hex SDF need a proto check. Fan needs an atan2 polynomial (allowed) and its seam must stay on the clipped base. Many enum branches mean a long but shallow .inl; keep each pattern a small inlined function returning (id, u, v, e). Mortar as a hybrid can create tiny islands where e'<0 everywhere (fine).
[TilePattern, stamp-scatter] Herringbone and basketweave index math is fiddly; prototype in the scalar lab first. Aspect ratios other than 2:1 for herringbone need generalising. Per-tile seed discontinuities are the point, but the continuity check will WARN.
ideas.variant_notes: TilePattern overlaps fully and adds a Random Flip option and true 3D brick bond and hex prisms.
ideas.cost_note: Cost: Grid/Bond/Hex about 0.5-1 ns + Source, Herringbone/RandomCourses about 1.5 ns + Source, Fan 4-6 ns (Worley-like).

queue.name: TileDomain
queue.reason: Bricks, herringbone, hex and ashlar with per-tile frame and edge distance, a perennial material ask (J1, J2 top pick). Many enum branches, so test each for continuity.

disp.how: the node

ideas.name: TruchetFlow
ideas.one_liner: Feeds the source arc-ribbon coordinates (along-path, across-path) of a random Truchet tiling, so any noise flows along closed meanders with one eval.
ideas.algorithm: cell = floor(p*s). (u,v) = frac; if hash bit, u = 1-u. Pick nearest arc corner: r1 = |(u,v)|, r2 = |(1-u,1-v)|, (dx,dy) = nearer corner offset, r = min(r1,r2). th = atan(min(dx,dy)/max(dx,dy)) by polynomial on [0,1], in [0,pi/4]. U = th*r, V = abs(r-.5). Output S( ku*U/s + drift*x, kv*V/s + drift*y ). Continuity proof: on every tile edge th=0 so U=0, and V = |edge offset - .5| matches both sides for either flip; on the anti-diagonal r1=r2 and the min/max form makes th equal from both corners; at corners r=0 so U=0 (the first prototype used th*.5 and had a jump there, th*r fixes it). Fold means source is mirrored at each tile edge and arc midpoint; drift adds slow variation to break repetition.
ideas.look: Brain-coral and labyrinth meanders: bands of source follow closed curves and rings around tile corners. With strata it looks like agate worm tracks, wet fingerprint loops, river meanders or Maori koru. Prototyped: mode=3, src=1 gives the clearest result.
ideas.why_new: Puts texture along a path network rather than just drawing the network. No cell or warp node can route a source along curved channels, and a graph cannot since it needs local arc coordinates.
ideas.simd_plan: 1 hash, 2 sqrt (or 1, comparing squares first), atan poly, Select. About 1.5-2 ns (estimate) plus source. Lattice 1x1, no neighbours. 3D: pass z through as S(U,V,z), or true tube form using a hash-picked set of 3 quarter tori in a cube with V = tube radius, U = arc angle*r (needs its own seam proof). 4D: S(U,V,z,w).
ideas.continuity: C0 with creases along edge and mid lines; measured c0ratio 8.07 after the fix.
ideas.params: Cell Size, Along Scale ku, Across Scale kv, Drift (hybrid), Source.
ideas.risks: With no drift the tile content repeats and looks stamped. Very anisotropic stripe sources show star-shaped mirror junctions at corners (seen with ku=.3,kv=1.2 on a sine source), so anisotropy needs limits. True 3D tubes were not prototyped. The square lattice remains faintly visible; pre-warping helps.
ideas.cost_note: About 1.5-2 ns (estimate) plus source.

ideas.name: BiomeBlend
ideas.one_liner: Pointwise form of KdotJPG's scattered biome blending: N sources blended by normalised sparse convolution over jittered points, giving constant-width, non-square transitions.
ideas.algorithm: For cells c in the 3x3 window of floor(p/Cell): q = c + 0.5 + Jit*(rnd11, rnd11) with |Jit| <= 0.25. k = max(0, R^2 - |p/Cell - q|^2)^2 with R in [1.07, 1.25], so at least one point always contributes and none outside the window can. Then b = clamp(floor(Control(q*Cell)*N)), W[b] += k, tot += k. out = sum_b (W[b]/tot)*S_b(p). Same kernel max(0,r^2-d^2)^2 and dynamic normalisation as the source article, but per point rather than per chunk, with the window bound derived to fit FastNoise's lattice rule: p is at most (0.5+0.25)*sqrt2 = 1.06 from a point; points outside the window are at least 1.25 away.
ideas.look: Look-tested (mode 18, 4 sources): the hard version shows jagged cell biomes and the blended version gives smooth organic boundaries with each biome's own texture intact and no axis squareness.
ideas.why_new:
Common worldgen need. FastNoiseLite #91: three commenters say they had to write their own cell noise to place biomes per cell. The FastNoise2 wiki tells people to use CellularLookup/CellularValue for biome-like regions, which gives hard edges only. FastNoise2 #163 and discussion #162 are about blending many big trees. KdotJPG's write-up documents that grid interpolation shows squareness and full blur is slow, measuring 196 ns per coordinate for scattered at r=24 cells of 8. No graph can accumulate kernel weights by per-cell id: Fade is 2-way and CellularLookup returns only the nearest cell.
[BiomeScatter, libs-modifiers] Fade on a control node has transition width proportional to 1/|grad control|, so borders vary from razor sharp to continent-wide, and N biomes need a chain of N-1 Fades. KdotJPG's method assumes chunks and a linked list of weights; the pointwise window form obeys the handbook. Constant world-space blend width is a real authoring gain for worldgen.
ideas.simd_plan: Window*Control evals (9 in 2D) + cells*N MaskedAdd + active sources. A source is skipped when its W is zero for every lane (FS::AnyMask batch skip, output identical). 2D with 2-octave Perlin control: about 20 ns + active sources. 3D: use a plane mode (lattice in x,z, sources get full 3D), since biomes are columnar anyway, at the same 9 evals. Full 3D is 27 evals; 4D tiling needs a 2^4 window with R near 1 and small jitter, accepting weaker coverage, or is unsupported.
ideas.continuity:
C0: kernel reaches zero at R and is normalised by a strictly positive total. Measured c0ratio 8.0.
[BiomeBlend, repo-demand] C1 wherever total>0: w has zero slope at R and the quotient is smooth. Measured coverage holes (total=0) in the prototype at R=1 over a 256 cell window: about 0.05% of samples at jitter 1, about 0.01% or less at 0.8, none seen at 0.6. Default jitter 0.7, or add a small weight that follows the nearest cell, to remove the rare C0 break. Overall c0ratio 2.9 in the prototype but that includes the Worley and ridged test biomes.
ideas.params: Control (generator), Sources 0..7 (hybrid), Source Count (int), Cell Size, Radius R (clamped to safe range), Jitter (clamped), Plane enum, Contrast Preserve (bool).
ideas.risks:
Control runs 9x, so it needs to be cheap. Control detail below Cell size is lost, as with CellularLookup. R range is narrow, so blend width is tied to Cell. Fixed source slots make for a large node UI. Batch-skip gains shrink for incoherent lanes and when borders fill the batch.
[BiomeBlend, repo-demand] Member list is long and the editor needs variable pin count, since metadata has no variable sources. Borders wobble at the cell scale (author notes the same tradeoff). All N sources run for every batch that touches them. 4D tile cost is high. 3D coverage worst case is worse than 2D, so check jitter limits.
ideas.variant_notes: Two window bounds are in play: R up to 1 with Jitter 0.7 and rare holes (BiomeBlend measured 0.05% holes at jitter 1), or R in [1.07,1.25] with |Jitter|<=0.25 which guarantees coverage (BiomeScatter).
ideas.cost_note: 2D with 2-octave Perlin control: about 20 ns + active sources.

queue.name: BiomeBlend
queue.reason: Scattered-point blending with constant-width transitions, a core world-gen problem, and the earlier proto works (J2 top pick). All sources run every batch plus 9 control evals, so measure.

ideas.name: BlendMode
ideas.one_liner: Photoshop and W3C separable blend modes in a normalised space: Overlay, SoftLight, HardLight, Screen, ColorDodge, ColorBurn, Vivid, Linear and Pin Light, Exclusion, with an opacity hybrid.
ideas.algorithm: b = 0.5 + 0.5*Base; s = 0.5 + 0.5*Blend (W3C naming: Cb = backdrop, Cs = source). HardLight: s <= 0.5 ? b*2s : b + (2s-1) - b*(2s-1). Overlay = HardLight(s, b). Screen: b + s - b*s. SoftLight: s <= 0.5 ? b - (1-2s)*b*(1-b) : b + (2s-1)*(D(b) - b), with D(b) = b <= 0.25 ? ((16b-12)b+4)b : sqrt(b). ColorDodge: min(1, b / max(1-s, eps)). ColorBurn: 1 - min(1, (1-b)/max(s, eps)). Exclusion: b + s - 2bs. LinearLight: sat(b + 2s - 1). VividLight: s <= 0.5 ? Burn(2s) : Dodge(2s-1). PinLight: s <= 0.5 ? min(b, 2s) : max(b, 2s-1). out = lerp(b, B(b,s), Opacity) * 2 - 1.
ideas.look: Overlay: large-scale FBm modulates the contrast of detail while keeping range and mean. Look-tested (mode 20): Multiply of two [-1,1] fields is flat grey with sign flips, while Overlay/SoftLight stay contrasty. Dodge and VividLight with cellular produce blown-out bubbly plates; Burn gives isolated bright blobs on black.
ideas.why_new: Multiply in [-1,1] is a sign-flipping operation, whereas the common intent (modulate) needs Remap + Multiply + Remap. Overlay and SoftLight additionally need a per-lane compare with no graph form except duplicating sources. These modes are what texture artists reach for first, so authoring gets far faster from Substance and Photoshop habits.
ideas.simd_plan: Two source evals; enum selects code path once per Gen; per-lane Select on compares; guarded division. About sum of sources + under 1 ns. No lattice, dimension agnostic.
ideas.continuity: C0 for Screen, Overlay, HardLight, SoftLight, Exclusion, Linear, Pin. Dodge, Burn and Vivid have a corner discontinuity at (s=1, b->0) softened by eps; measured c0ratio 7.7 on Dodge with cellular.
ideas.params: Base, Blend (generators), Mode enum, Opacity (hybrid), Input Min, Input Max (default -1, 1).
ideas.risks: Mathematically not novel, so value is entirely in convenience and frequency of use. Assumes normalised inputs; out-of-range inputs clip. Dodge and Burn saturate large areas (test panel mostly white). Enum count may be trimmed to Overlay, SoftLight, HardLight, Screen, Dodge, Burn, Linear Light.
ideas.cost_note: About sum of sources + under 1 ns.

ideas.name: CombineOps
ideas.one_liner: hg_sdf distance-field combiners for two noise fields: chamfer, round fillet, stairs, columns, groove, tongue, engrave, pipe.
ideas.algorithm: With a, b and min convention. Chamfer: min(a, b, (a+b-r)/sqrt2). Round: max(r, min(a,b)) - length(max(r-a,0), max(r-b,0)). Soft: e = max(r-|a-b|, 0); min(a,b) - e^2/(4r). Stairs: s = r/n; u = b - r; min(a, b, 0.5*(u + a + |mod(u-a+s, 2s) - s|)). Columns: if a<r and b<r place n-1 circular columns of radius r*sqrt2/(2(n-1)+sqrt2) along the diagonal, else min(a,b). Pipe: sqrt(a^2+b^2) - r. Engrave: max(a, (a+r-|b|)/sqrt2). Groove: max(a, min(a+ra, rb-|b|)). Tongue: min(a, max(a-ra, |b|-rb)). Max-family by negation of inputs and output; Difference by max(a,-b) form. Use mod floored (hg_sdf uses GLSL mod).
ideas.look: Look-tested (mode 10). Stairs: rippled terraces in the crease where fields meet. Chamfer: flat planar facets. Round: clean fillet that keeps sharp elsewhere. Tongue and Engrave: raised or cut line following one field's zero set across the other, like roads with embankments or ditched rivers. In 3D, these give bevelled cave junctions.
ideas.why_new: MinSmooth and MaxSmooth have a single fillet shape. Crease shaping with steps, chamfer or inlaid lines is unavailable, and a graph version needs repeats of a and b, each an expensive subtree evaluated several times.
ideas.simd_plan: 2 source evals + few Min/Max/Sqrt/FS::Modulus ops, under 1 ns extra, one enum dispatch per Gen. Columns uses Select instead of a branch. Generic GenT, all dimensions.
ideas.continuity: C0: measured c0ratio 8.0 for Stairs and Tongue; hg_sdf operators are piecewise smooth with continuous joins. Columns may have a slope break at the column boundary.
ideas.params: A, B (generators), Operation enum, Radius (hybrid), Step Count (int), Tongue Radius (hybrid), Side enum (Union, Intersection, Difference).
ideas.risks: Operators are built for true distance fields, and on raw noise the fillet width depends on local slope, so pairing with IsoDistance gives better results. FS::Modulus must match floored mod semantic or stairs break for negatives; check against Blends.inl. Niche compared with BlendMode and HeightBlend, and Columns and Soft may not earn enum slots (Soft is close to MinSmooth).
ideas.cost_note: 2 source evals + few Min/Max/Sqrt/FS::Modulus ops, under 1 ns extra, one enum dispatch per Gen.

queue.name: CombineOps
queue.reason: Chamfer, stairs and groove combiners under 1 ns. Fillet radii are only true on distance-like inputs, so pair with iso-distance.

ideas.name: ContrastFade
ideas.one_liner: Variance-preserving crossfade: ((1-t)A + tB) / sqrt((1-t)^2 + t^2 + 2 rho t(1-t)) with hybrid t, so the transition zone between two noises keeps full contrast instead of the washed-out band that Fade/lerp produces; exact histogram preservation when inputs are Gaussianised.
ideas.algorithm:
a = A(x), b = B(x), t = clamp(Fade(x), 0, 1) (hybrid), rho = Correlation (float, 0 for independent sources, measured for correlated ones).
wa = 1 - t, wb = t (optionally t = smoothstep(t) first).
norm = InvSqrt( wa^2 + wb^2 + 2 rho wa wb )
out = (wa a + wb b) * norm
Mean handling: if Mean != 0, subtract Mean from a and b, blend, add back (keeps the mean fixed and the std fixed).
N-way variant via chaining: StatBlend(StatBlend(A,B,t1), C, t2) is still variance preserving when the sources are independent.
With A, B passed through ExactGaussianNoise/CdfRemap (Gaussian) first and CdfRemap (target) after, the blend preserves the full histogram, not just variance (the Heitz-Neyret operator applied to procedural noise).
ideas.look: Same two sources, but the transition band keeps peaks and valleys rather than turning into low-contrast mush. Look-tested (mode 7): hillshade across the fade retains full relief while plain lerp visibly flattens in the middle.
ideas.why_new: Plain lerp of two uncorrelated zero-mean fields has std/sqrt2 at t=0.5, and this is visible around every biome boundary and in all crossfade animation. The fix needs a per-lane sqrt of the fade value, which cannot be done on Fade's internal value from a graph. It is an obvious quality win that I did not see offered in other noise libraries consulted here. Small change, large benefit, so a dedicated option is worthwhile.
ideas.simd_plan: Inside Fade after interpolation: one InvSqrt and a multiply, under 0.2 ns, no extra source evals. Dimension agnostic because it only touches outputs.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity in t, because W stays at or above 1/sqrt2. Output continuity equals sources.
ideas.params: A, B (GeneratorSource); Fade (hybrid 0..1); Correlation rho (float, -1..1, default 0); Mean (float); Smooth Fade (bool).
ideas.risks:
Variance preservation assumes both inputs have the same variance (scale them first or use CdfRemap to Gaussian); with very different inputs the normalisation slightly over-boosts the transition. Only the second moment is preserved unless the Gaussianise/de-Gaussianise sandwich is used; the full pipeline is 3 nodes.
[ContrastFade, libs-modifiers] Statistically right only for uncorrelated sources of similar variance. Correlated A and B overshoot up to 1.41x, so output can leave [-1,1] (Burley uses a soft-clip for that). Not meaningful when A and B have very different means (flat plain vs mountain), where a Mean per source would be needed. Ghosting persists, only contrast is corrected.
sources: Heitz & Neyret, 'High-Performance By-Example Noise using a Histogram-Preserving Blending Operator', HPG 2018 (variance-preserving blend of Gaussianised textures; cited from memory, not fetched in this task)
ideas.variant_notes: Could be an enum on Fade. Full histogram preservation needs the Gaussianise and de-Gaussianise sandwich via CdfRemap.
ideas.cost_note: Inside Fade after interpolation: one InvSqrt and a multiply, under 0.2 ns, no extra source evals.

queue.name: ContrastFade
queue.reason: Variance-preserving lerp with one InvSqrt that fixes washed-out fades. Likely a Fade option rather than a new node.

ideas.name: HeightBlend
ideas.one_liner: Terrain-splat style blend where the higher material wins inside a depth band, so one layer interlocks with the other instead of fogging over it.
ideas.algorithm: t = sat((Control - FadeMin) / (FadeMax - FadeMin)). a = HeightA(p) + (1 - t); b = HeightB(p) + t. T = max(a, b) - Depth. wa = max(a - T, 0); wb = max(b - T, 0). out = (A(p)*wa + B(p)*wb) / (wa + wb). The taller layer always has weight Depth, so the denominator is positive for Depth > 0. Heights default to the (remapped) A and B outputs.
ideas.look: Pebbles poke through sand; grass overtakes rock at its tips first; scree invades snow along cracks. Look-tested (mode 8): sheet Fade produces a foggy grey ramp, while HeightBlend gives a crisp interlocking cell-shaped boundary with full contrast on either side.
ideas.why_new: Fade is transparency, which is the main reason procedural biome borders look like mush. HeightBlend is the standard engine and tool answer (Unreal HeightLerp, splat shaders), but as a graph it needs two to four source copies, several Add/Max nodes and a Divide. As a node, it is a hard thing made trivial and likely among the most-used nodes for biome work.
ideas.simd_plan: Generic GenT, two Max and one division. Costs the sum of inputs and adds under 1 ns in any dimension. Reuse A and B values when heights are not separately connected to avoid double evaluation. Can apply batch-skip when all lanes have wa = 0 or wb = 0 (FS::AnyMask, as Terrace does).
ideas.continuity: C0 for Depth > 0 (measured c0ratio 5.8). Depth to 0 becomes a hard switch. Output stays within the range spanned by A and B because it is a convex combination.
ideas.params: A, B (generators), Control (hybrid), Fade Min, Fade Max (hybrid), Height A, Height B (hybrid), Depth (hybrid), Height Scale.
ideas.risks: Heights must share a scale with the fade range or one layer always wins. Depth too small gives aliasing. Skipping evaluation must stay exact for feature-set parity. Heights with very smooth content reduce to a plain threshold.
ideas.cost_note: Costs the sum of inputs and adds under 1 ns in any dimension.

queue.name: HeightBlend
queue.reason: Splat-style height-interlocking blend under 1 ns, what every material graph wants from Fade (J1 top pick). Low look risk; the must-have of the blend category.

disp.how: own node; the critic said a Fade mode, but the terrain lens asks for its own node, the maintainer lens lists it as one, and it leaves Fade alone

ideas.name: LevelSetWeave
ideas.one_liner: Over-under textile weave driven by two arbitrary fields: threads are level-set bands of A and B, and parity decides which lies on top.
ideas.algorithm:
u=A(p)*k; v=B(p)*k; iu=Floor(u); iv=Floor(v); fu=u-iu; fv=v-iv.
par=1-2*((iu+iv)&1).
prof(t)=Cos(pi*Clamp((t-0.5)/gap,-0.5,0.5)).
ha=prof(fu)*(0.5+0.5*par*Cos(pi*(fv-0.5)));
hb=prof(fv)*(0.5-0.5*par*Cos(pi*(fu-0.5)));
Out=Max(ha,hb), remapped to [-1,1].
Optional thread colour: Select(ha>hb, hash(iu), hash(iv)) gives plaid. A=x+warp and B=y+warp gives warped cloth; two low-frequency noises give flowing bark-like weave.
ideas.look: Tested with a hillshade. With warped axes it reads clearly as woven basket or cloth with visible over-under, puckered threads. With two noises it gives flowing, stacked strands like bark, muscle fibre or woven kelp. Unlike anything on the sheet. Uses: fabric, wicker, chainmail bases, stylised terrain folds, roots.
ideas.why_new: Checkerboard plus warp gives colour cells, never a height relief with threads that cross over and under. Doing this as a graph would need floor, parity and select nodes, none of which exist. Any two node graphs can drive it, not just axes.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch free, integer parity bit test. 2 source evals + 4 Cos, replaceable by even polynomials. Estimated under 2x the source cost + 1 ns. 3D: A,B level sets become sheets, which give a ribbon structure; optional C source and a max of 3 terms for a triaxial weave. 4D is the same formula via sources.
ideas.continuity: C0, verified numerically (ratio 8.0), with creases along Max(ha,hb) where threads meet. Not C1, as with real thread crossings.
ideas.params: A, B sources (hybrid so constant offsets work). Hybrid: Threads k, Gap. Enum: Height, Plaid Id.
ideas.risks: Thread width scales inversely with |grad A| because the bands are not distance-normalised, so low-gradient regions show fat threads (visible in the two-noise plate). Piping sources through IsoBands distance would fix that at extra cost. The 3D look is unverified. Requires large noise amplitude on A,B to get many threads.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated under 2x the source cost + 1 ns.

queue.name: LevelSetWeave
queue.reason: Over-under weave from the level sets of any two fields at ~1 ns over the sources. Thread width follows the gradient, so try iso-distance inputs.

disp.how: optional A and B coordinate sources

ideas.name: SlopeProjectedDetail
ideas.one_liner: Triplanar-style cliff texturing for heightfield graphs: on flats the detail is sampled in the plane, on steep flanks it is sampled as a function of (along-contour position, height), so sedimentary strata appear exactly along the contours of steep faces and fade out on flats.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Height (GeneratorSource), Detail (GeneratorSource, 2D-ish texture), Height Scale kH, Detail Scale, Slope Min/Max (hybrids), Epsilon.
2D node: h = H(pos); g = central gradient of H (4 taps);  s = |g|; steep = smoothstep(SlopeMin, SlopeMax, s)
  wx = |g_x| / (s + eps), wy = |g_y| / (s + eps)
  top   = Detail(x * ds, y * ds)
  sideX = Detail(y * ds * 0.5, h * kH)   // face normal mostly +-x: vary along y and with height
  sideY = Detail(x * ds * 0.5, h * kH)
  side  = (wx * sideX + wy * sideY) / (wx + wy + eps)
  out   = Lerp(top, side, steep)  (optionally Add to h with a Mix hybrid)
3D node (volume): planes are the three axis planes of the position, weights |n_i|^k from the gradient of H, which is the classic triplanar blend; the 'height' coordinate is the third axis of each plane.
4D: dimension-agnostic version with D planes; or fall back to the 3D blend on xyz and pass w into the detail.
ideas.look: Proto sheetA m5: blobby detail in the valleys and flats, switching to thin banded layers on steep slopes whose bands follow the iso-height lines (cliff strata), with the transition following the slope mask. Different from anything on the sheet: band orientation is dictated by the terrain rather than by a global axis. Uses: canyon walls, sedimentary cliffs, basalt columns (use a Cellular detail), snow lines (bands at fixed heights).
ideas.why_new: The graph can almost do it: DomainOffset/AddDimension chains could feed h into a detail's second axis, but the slope-dependent per-axis blend needs the gradient components, three detail evaluations and a normalised blend, i.e. 15+ nodes with a SourceGradient. The node bundles the technique engines use for cliff texturing, which is what people actually want from 'detail where the terrain is steep'.
ideas.simd_plan: 2D: 1 + 4 taps of Height plus 3 Detail evals; 3D: 1 + 6 + 3; 4D: 1 + 8 + 4. With FBm Simplex x3 height and Simplex detail: 2D ~ 5x4 + 3x1.3 ~ 24 ns, 3D ~ 7x8 + 3x2.6 ~ 64 ns. All Select/FMA, no lattice window.
ideas.continuity: C0 (proto c0ratio 7.7): smooth weights, continuous taps. The axis-weight normalisation needs the eps floor at |g| = 0 where 'side' is undefined but also unused (steep = 0).
ideas.params: Height, Detail (nodes); Height Scale kH; Detail Scale; Slope Min / Max (hybrids, so a biome mask can decide where strata appear); Blend Sharpness k for the axis weights; Mix hybrid to add onto the height.
ideas.risks: Strata density depends on kH times the local slope, so very steep faces get aliased bands; a SuperSample wrap or a kH clamp by 1/s helps. The height coordinate makes strata horizontal in world terms, which is right for sediment but wrong for tilted bedding (add a Tilt param that mixes a world axis into the height coordinate). In 3D the volume version is just triplanar and less novel.
ideas.cost_note: With FBm Simplex x3 height and Simplex detail: 2D ~ 5x4 + 3x1.3 ~ 24 ns, 3D ~ 7x8 + 3x2.6 ~ 64 ns.

ideas.name: CdfRemap
ideas.one_liner: Monotone histogram transform: pushes a source through its (assumed or auto-measured) CDF to a uniform, then through a chosen inverse CDF (Gaussian, Beta(a,b), bimodal hypsometric), so threshold X covers X percent and the height histogram is designed.
ideas.algorithm:
Stage A (to uniform) by InputDist:
  Gaussian: u = 0.5(1+erf(v/(sigma sqrt2)))  (Sigma float, e.g. measured once for Perlin/Simplex/FBm presets)
  Range:    u = clamp((v - lo)/(hi - lo), 0, 1)
  Measured: table q[0..64] of source quantiles computed when Source (or Calibrate Seed/Extent) is set: evaluate the source on 65536 fixed pseudo-random positions in a box of side CalibrateExtent, sort, q[k] = value at rank k/64. At Gen, gather-free piecewise-linear CDF:
     u = (1/64) * sum_{k=0..63} clamp( (v - q[k]) / (q[k+1] - q[k]), 0, 1 )   // 64 FMA + clamp, all lanes same table
Stage B (uniform to target) by TargetDist:
  Uniform: out = 2u - 1
  Gaussian: out = PhiInv(u)/3 (Acklam rational approx, 1 Log + 1 Sqrt in the tails, or central polynomial)
  Beta(Alpha,Beta) / Bimodal(SeaFraction, Separation) / any preset: inverse-CDF table T[0..64] built at param-set time by numeric integration, then gather-free: out = T[0] + sum_k (T[k+1]-T[k]) * clamp(64u - k, 0, 1)
Strength (hybrid): out = lerp(v, out, Strength(x)).
Topology note: the map is monotone, so every level set of the source is a level set of the output; only the value attached to each level set changes.

[Equalize, libs-modifiers] q = 1.702*(Source(p) - Mean) / Sigma; out = 2/(1 + exp(-q)) - 1 (logistic approximation of the Gaussian CDF; same form as ANL's sigmoid node with centre and ramp, but parameterised by distribution). With a flat output, threshold T selects area (1-T)/2. Optional Calibrate() helper outside Gen: evaluate the source at a fixed 4096-point pseudo-random pattern with a fixed seed, and set Mean and Sigma, or fill a 16-knot empirical CDF table for skewed sources (ANL AutoCorrect idea, but producing stored parameters so Gen stays pure).
ideas.look:
Same shapes as the source, redistributed tones. Uniform target: flat histogram, every threshold meaningful (coverage = threshold). Beta(0.5,0.5) target: U-shaped histogram, terrain splits into plateaus and basins with steep connecting slopes (two-level look without Terrace's steps). Bimodal hypsometric: Earth-like, most area near two heights (abyssal plain, continental shelf) and little in between: continents with well-defined coasts from any noise. Gaussian target: normalises any weird source (cellular, warped) to a Perlin-like tone distribution.
[Equalize, libs-modifiers] Flat histogram, full contrast regardless of octave count. Look-tested numerically (mode 28, 64-unit window, 3-octave Perlin FBm): source std 0.198-0.202 across seeds; with Sigma 0.207, threshold 0.2 gave mean -0.200 (expected -0.200) and threshold 0.6 gave -0.585 (expected -0.6), so coverage error is about 1% area at the tails.
ideas.why_new: Users ask for this constantly: gamedev.stackexchange biome-selection answers suggest histogram equalisation, and a Minetest forum thread asks what thresholds divide a world into 3 biomes equally. FN2 #57 asks to normalise to a guaranteed range; #121 and #212 ask about predictable ranges; Godot proposal #11001 asks to expose min and max. No graph has the erf-shaped map; Remap is linear. Could be a preset on SplineRemap if that lands, so judge it after that node exists.
ideas.simd_plan: Source eval + two 64-segment piecewise-linear evaluations done as sums of clamps (no gathers, tables are node members broadcast per segment): roughly 2 x 64 x 3 ops ~ 1-1.5x Perlin per stage; analytic Gaussian stages are 1 Exp or 1 Log + poly (~0.5x Perlin). Dimension agnostic (GenT). Calibration runs on the scalar/SIMD path once at SetSource time with a fixed seed and positions (deterministic).
ideas.continuity: Monotone C0 map (piecewise linear tables, C1 for the analytic erf/PhiInv stages); preserves the source's continuity class up to the table knots.
ideas.params: Source; InputDist enum (Gaussian, Range, Measured); Sigma, Range Min/Max; Calibrate Extent, Calibrate Seed; TargetDist enum (Uniform, Gaussian, Beta, Bimodal); Alpha, Beta / Sea Fraction, Separation; Strength (hybrid).
ideas.risks:
Measured mode holds state derived from the source subtree: if the user edits a child node after calibration the table is stale (fine in the NodeEditor where the tree is rebuilt, a footgun in the C++ API; needs a Recalibrate trigger or calibrating lazily on first Gen behind a flag). Calibration cost ~65k source evaluations at setup. 64 knots make the output slightly piecewise linear (visible as faint banding in hillshade of smooth sources; use 128 knots or C1 monotone cubic segments if it shows).
[CoverageRemap, distribution-topology] Not automatically updated when the upstream graph changes, so the table can go stale; an editor warning would help. Coverage is exact only for the calibrated law, and finite sampling gives about 1 percent error. Metadata would have 9 extra floats on a small node. Not prototyped since it is a straightforward table; numbers above are design estimates. Hybrid-varying source params shift the law.
ideas.variant_notes: Thresholds as area percent. Calibration must stay off the Gen path, stored as plain members, and goes stale if the subtree changes, so it needs tooling. Measured about 1% area error at tails for the logistic approximation.
ideas.cost_note: One source eval plus two table stages at about 1-1.5x Perlin each, or about 0.5x Perlin per analytic Gaussian stage.

queue.name: CdfRemap
queue.reason: Threshold X means X percent coverage. Start with the analytic Gaussian stage, since Measured mode holds stale state across subtree edits.

ideas.name: ContourScarp
ideas.one_liner: Uses the first-order distance to a source's level set to apply a cliff, talus and plateau profile in world units, regardless of source slope. The f/|grad f| approximation is known from SDF rendering; the terrain node is the variation.
ideas.algorithm: h=S(p); grad by forward differences (dim extra evals). L=Level+EdgeNoise(p). d=(h-L)/max(|grad|,eps), clamped to the profile range. Mesa profile: for d>=0, Z=Cap (+CapDetail*small amp). For -Wc<=d<0, Z=Cap-Hc*(-d/Wc)^p (cliff). For the next Wt, a concave talus curve drops by Ht. out=SmoothMax(Base(h), Z), so below the talus the source's own lowlands return. Multi-band option: repeat Levels at fixed spacing, with band index by floor((h-L0)/spacing), to get stacked cliff bands of constant width.
