Use with fractal EdgeNoise to get crenulated rims and side embayments while the cross-section stays physically constant.
ideas.look: Mesas, buttes, table mountains and escarpments with constant-width vertical walls and aprons of scree. Plateau tops are flat, and the rim is fractal in plan view. Also useful for beaches and shore shelves of constant width.
ideas.why_new: Terrace and Remap operate on height, so cliff width varies inversely with source slope: smeared on gentle slopes and hairline on steep ones. Graphs have no gradient access, so world-space profiles are not possible today. This separates plan-form fractal detail from cross-section, which answers how detail stays plausible.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch free: 1+dim source evals plus EdgeNoise, then Select and Min/Max. 2D 3x, 3D 4x, 4D 5x source cost. GenT works for every dimension and keeps tiling. Cheap relative to what it provides.
ideas.continuity: C0 with the eps floor and clamp if the source is continuous; forward differences at a finite step stay continuous even on C0 sources.
ideas.params: Source, Level (hybrid), Edge Noise (hybrid), Cliff Width and Height, Talus Width and Height, Cap Detail (hybrid), Band Spacing (float, 0 = single), Gradient Step (float), Eps (float).
ideas.risks: Not tested. First-order distance is wrong near saddles and maxima, where the gradient vanishes, so cliffs may widen or vanish there. Gradient Step must exceed the finest source wavelength or the distance becomes noisy, so feed low octaves and add detail afterward.
ideas.cost_note: 2D 3x, 3D 4x, 4D 5x source cost.

queue.name: ContourScarp
queue.reason: World-unit cliffs and talus regardless of source slope, the control Terrace lacks. Untested and saddles break the distance. May end up an output of iso-distance.

ideas.name: ContourSnapLandforms
ideas.one_liner: Stamps whose apexes snap onto a chosen contour of the terrain, then use Max with a cone for alluvial fans or Min with a paraboloid for cirques, so the terrain itself cuts the landform's outline.
ideas.algorithm:
For each lattice cell in the 3x3 window: start at jittered a; evaluate placement source P and its gradient; one or two Newton steps a'=a-(P(a)-L)*gradP/|gradP|^2, displacement clamped to 0.5 cell. Validity v=smoothstep on |P(a)-L|/|gradP| vs max displacement; cells with no nearby contour fade out.
Aggrade mode (fans, talus cones): cone_i(p)=L+e-s*r_i, minus radial distributary grooves, minus a large v-based sink. out=SmoothMax(h(p), max_i cone_i). Uphill the cone lies below the terrain and disappears; in the valley it buries the floor, so the fan's outline follows topography without any angular mask or flow calculation.
Excavate mode (cirques, sinkholes): bowl_i(p)=L+a*r_i^2 (or a superellipse), plus sink for invalid. out=SmoothMin(h(p), min_i bowl_i). Adjacent bowls intersect in sharp curves, which produce aretes and pyramidal horns automatically.
ideas.look: Aggrade: fans spilling from a mountain front into a valley, merging as bajadas. Excavate: alpine amphitheatres with knife-edge aretes and horn peaks above an elevation line, or sinkholes on a limestone bench.
ideas.why_new: Stamps usually ignore terrain. Here placement comes from any source and the shape is resolved by min/max against it, turning a simulation-looking landform into a few lines of math. A graph cannot place features on a level set.
ideas.simd_plan: 9 candidates x (dim+1) x Newton steps of Placement evals, plus 1 Source eval. 2D with one Newton step is 27+1 evals. Estimate at a 1-2 octave Perlin placement: 40-80 ns. In 3D and 4D keep the lattice in the XY plane (9 candidates, 4 or 5 evals each) because 27 or 81 candidates is too costly; a full 3D option can place on iso-surfaces at 108 evals. 4D tiling therefore does not hold unless the search goes 4D.
ideas.continuity: C0 via validity fade, radius cutoff smoothing and SmoothMin/Max. Newton displacement must be continuous across p, which it is since each candidate is fixed per cell.
ideas.params: Source, Placement Source (often a low-octave version of Source), Level (float), Mode (enum), Slope s or Bowl a (hybrid), Radius (float, must fit window), Groove Amount, Newton Steps (int), Jitter.
ideas.risks: Not tested. An apex's fade-out may show as pop-in-like shapes when the contour leaves the cell. Max cone radius limited to about 1 cell, so big fans require coarse lattice and sparse density. Mismatch between Placement and full Source can float apexes above or below the visible terrain.
ideas.cost_note: Estimate at a 1-2 octave Perlin placement: 40-80 ns.

ideas.name: FeigenbaumRemap
ideas.one_liner: Modifier that iterates the logistic map with growth rate from the source: flat calm where it converges, period-doubling contour rings at the transition, and lacy chaos at peaks, all for a few multiplies.
ideas.algorithm: r=Min(4, Rmin + (0.5+0.5*Source(p)*Gain)*Rspan); v=0.5 (or Source2-perturbed start: 0.5+0.2*Source2(p)); repeat N (6..12): v=r*v*(1-v). Output v*2-1, range guaranteed because r<=4 and v in [0,1]. Prototype: dyn_lens mode=33,N=8; mode=33,N=12,v0=1,rr=1; mode=33,N=8,oct=4,rr=1.
ideas.look: Verified in prototype. Plateau-like calm gray areas (fixed point), abruptly hugged by nested ring contours around high regions (period 2,4,8), with white-speckled lace in the cores (chaos). With a perturbed start the lace gets coherent 2D grain. With FBm source: lichen or corroded metal patches with crisp outlines. Good for corrosion, lichen, foam edges, alien coasts, detail masks that only fire at high values.
ideas.why_new: PingPong and Terrace are regular across the value range; this has three distinct behaviours partitioned by value, from one cheap node. Detail is added selectively where the source is high, with hierarchical contour doubling that no single remap of Remap, Terrace or PingPong gives.
ideas.simd_plan: Source + N x 2 mul-adds, under 1 ns extra. GenT over pack, all dimensions, trivially tileable. Optional Source2 hybrid. Much cheaper than a fractal for detail creation.
ideas.continuity: C0 and piecewise polynomial; slope grows like up to 4^N in chaos; N<=12 stays numerically sane. Measured c0ratio 7.7 at N=8 and max slope about 125 per unit, i.e. Lipschitz.
ideas.params: Rmin, Rspan (hybrid), Gain, Iterations int, Start hybrid (constant 0.5 or second source), Source.
ideas.risks: High N in chaos is sample-rate dependent aliasing, effectively white in the core. Needs clamp at r=4 or it diverges (hit in test with FBm source, fixed with Min). Its behaviour is a 1D function of value, so it can also be a LUT, but the Start hybrid breaks that and is the better look.
ideas.cost_note: Source + N x 2 mul-adds, under 1 ns extra.

ideas.name: GlacialTroughs
ideas.one_liner: Carves U-shaped troughs of constant world width along a source's zero contours, with raised floors per tier so hanging valleys and truncated spurs emerge from a simple Min.
ideas.algorithm: For tier t in 0..T-1: n=ValleySource(p*scale_t, seed+t), grad by forward differences, d=|n|/max(|grad|,eps). Trough surface U_t=Floor(p)+Hang*t+Dt*min((d/W_t)^q,1) with q about 2-4 and W_t=W*r^t. Ice gate: e=smoothstep(ELA-b,ELA+b,h(p)), so only high ground is glaciated: h'=lerp(h, min(h,U_t), e_t), applied sequentially. Since Min simply cuts through spurs, spurs truncate into straight faces. A smaller tier with a higher floor ends abruptly on a parent's wall as a hanging valley, and waterfalls are implied there.
ideas.look: Yosemite and fjord-like valleys: flat floors, near-vertical walls, cut spurs, side valleys that end in mid-wall. Setting Floor below sea level makes winding fjord systems with islands.
ideas.why_new: Ridged and Abs-based valleys are V-shaped, widening with low slope. Constant-width U and tiered floors require gradient normalisation unavailable to graphs. Hanging valleys normally suggest simulation, but here they arise from a Min of independent surfaces.
ideas.simd_plan: T x (dim+1) Valley evals + h + hybrids; 3 tiers in 2D with single Perlin valleys is 9 Perlin evals plus source, about 10-15 ns plus h. GenT works for 2D, 3D and 4D and preserves tiling when sources tile.
ideas.continuity: C0: min and lerp of continuous fields; d uses the eps floor.
ideas.params: Source, Valley Source, Tiers (int), Width and Width Ratio r, Hang (float), Depth, Sharpness q, Floor (hybrid), ELA, ELA Blend, Tier Scale.
ideas.risks: Not tested. Zero contours of noise form closed loops rather than trees, so the pattern might look like lakes or moats unless warped or stretched. Near-zero gradient on contour is rare but gives wide troughs. Overlaps some ContourScarp machinery; could share a helper.
ideas.cost_note: T x (dim+1) Valley evals + h + hybrids; 3 tiers in 2D with single Perlin valleys is 9 Perlin evals plus source, about 10-15 ns plus h.

queue.name: GlacialTroughs
queue.reason: U-troughs with hanging tiers along zero contours; canyon-style earlier proto looks strong. Closed loops read as moats unless warped.

ideas.name: HopfLaxEnvelope
ideas.one_liner: Moreau envelope of a noise: min over y of h(y)+|x-y|^2/(2t), which rounds valleys into parabolic bowls and leaves sharp creases on true ridgelines; the negated form gives pillow cobbles with sharp valleys.
ideas.algorithm: Viscosity solution of Hamilton-Jacobi via polished multi-start. For K (5 in 2D) starts y_i = p + r*dir_i plus p itself: repeat M (4..6): g=grad h(y); y -= Step*(g + (y-p)/t). E_i=h(y)+|y-p|^2/(2t). Output Min over i of E_i (erode), or Sign*Min over negated h (dilate). Prototype: dyn_lens mode=8,t=0.3,oct=3,gain=0.4,st=0.08,M=6,r=0.4 and mode=8,t=0.3,sgn=-1,st=0.1,M=6,r=0.4.
ideas.look: Verified in prototype, at lower distinctness than the others. Erode t=0.6: crater bowls with sharp crest web between them; t=0.3 with 3 octaves: pits with rough rims. Dilate t=0.3: organically sized cobbles or pillows with creased joints. Small t returns the source. Good for craters, pebbles, cobbles, cushions, semi-eroded terrain.
ideas.why_new: Billow via Abs creases at zero crossings; this creases on the true ridge or valley lines of the source (independent of the value level). Cell structure comes from source minima, not a lattice. Morphological erosion normally needs a neighbourhood pass.
ideas.simd_plan: K*(M+1) gradients: 2D about 25..35 gradients, about 40 ns with analytic Perlin. 3D K=7 about 110 ns. 4D too heavy: reduce to K=4 axis-free starts with a warning. A plain unpolished stencil (K=8..16 source evals with quadratic penalty) is a cheaper quality option at about 10..16 evals.
ideas.continuity: C0 (Min of continuous functions), with deliberate creases. Each trajectory stays continuous with fixed M.
ideas.params: Time t (hybrid: amount), Start Radius, Starts int, Polish Iterations, Sign enum (Erode, Dilate), Source.
ideas.risks: Expensive relative to its look; instability if Step*(1/t + curvature) exceeds about 1 (seen as wrinkles until Step was lowered). Finite K misses far minima at large t, making a slightly lumpy envelope.
ideas.cost_note: K*(M+1) gradients: 2D about 25..35 gradients, about 40 ns with analytic Perlin. 3D K=7 about 110 ns.

ideas.name: LocalRank
ideas.one_liner: Soft rank of the centre value among K fixed-offset probes of the source: a pointwise local histogram equalisation that removes trends, equalises contrast everywhere, and doubles as a scale-selective local-extremum mask.
ideas.algorithm:
Probe offsets o_k, k=1..K: a fixed deterministic set on the unit disc/ball (2D golden-angle spiral radii sqrt(k/K), 3D Fibonacci sphere x 2 shells, 4D 16 fixed points), scaled by Radius R (world units). K = 8 or 16 (compile-time constant or int param).
v0 = S(x); v_k = S(x + R o_k).
u = (1/K) * sum_k smoothstep( (v0 - v_k) / Softness + 0.5 )     // soft empirical CDF of the neighbourhood evaluated at v0
Modes: Rank: out = 2u - 1.  PeakMask: out = smoothstep((u - Threshold)/Edge) (u~1 means x is a local max at scale R).  Contrast: out = (v0 - mean_k v_k) / (std_k v_k + eps) (local z-score, same probes).
ideas.look: On fBm: the large-scale tone is flattened and every region, including formerly dull low-contrast areas, shows full-range detail, like CLAHE on a photo; the output histogram is nearly flat. PeakMask gives a sparse, evenly spaced set of blobs at the local maxima of any source (spacing set by R), a blue-noise-like scatter derived from the terrain itself (trees on local tops, cities on local highs). Contrast mode gives a 'normalised detail' layer that never saturates.
ideas.why_new: No node can see a neighbourhood; local extremum detection, detrending and adaptive contrast are not expressible (DomainOffset+Subtract gives one difference, not a rank). The rank is monotone-local, so it preserves the topology of level sets within a radius while fixing the global statistics; the peak mask gives feature placement that follows the terrain, unlike CellularDistance which ignores it.
ideas.simd_plan: Modifier evaluating the source K+1 times at fixed offsets (same offsets for all lanes), K smoothsteps and adds; cost = (K+1) x source (K=8 on Perlin 2D ~10 ns). Int K from an enum {8,16} to keep loops lane-uniform. Dimension agnostic apart from the offset tables (one table per dimension).
ideas.continuity: Same class as the source (smoothstep is C1), continuous because the probe set is fixed per node, not per lane.
ideas.params: Source; Radius (world units); Softness (source units); Probes enum (8, 16); Mode enum (Rank, PeakMask, Contrast); Threshold, Edge.
ideas.risks: Expensive (9-17 source evals). The rank marginal is only approximately uniform because the centre is correlated with its probes (not exchangeable). A fixed probe pattern can imprint faint directional bias at scale R; 16 probes in a spiral reduce it. Do not stack on expensive fractals without GeneratorCache-style care.
ideas.cost_note: Modifier evaluating the source K+1 times at fixed offsets (same offsets for all lanes), K smoothsteps and adds; cost = (K+1) x source (K=8 on Perlin 2D ~10 ns).

ideas.name: Oscillator
ideas.one_liner: Missing sine-of-noise modifier, with pulse-width modulation for engraving hatches, skew for dune profiles, trig-free Chebyshev mode and a local Nyquist guard.
ideas.algorithm:
phi=Freq*S(p)+Phase. Waves: Sine: Sin(phi). Triangle: from fract. Skew: Sin(phi+Skew*Sin(phi)), a one-step Kepler solution that morphs sine toward saw with steep lee and gentle stoss slopes. Pulse: Clamp((Sin(phi)+Duty(p))/Edge,-1,1), so Duty is a hybrid and any node becomes line width: halftone engraving. Chebyshev: T_k(clamp(S)) by recurrence T_{n+1}=2x*T_n-T_{n-1}, with exactly k zero crossings in [-1,1], no trig, and bounded by 1.
Optional Band Guard: forward-difference S, local freq=Freq*|g|, multiply output by Exp(-(freq/limit)^2) to fade instead of alias.

[Oscillator, signal-phase] x = Frequency*src(p) + PhaseOffset(hybrid). t = x - floor(x). Waveform enum: Sine -> sin(2pi t) via FS::Sin or a 5th-order poly on t; Triangle -> 1-4|t-0.5|; Saw -> 2t-1 softened by s = smoothstep(1-Edge,1,t): out = lerp(2t-1, -1, s) (C0 for Edge>0); Pulse -> 2*smoothstep(Duty-Soft, Duty+Soft, t)-1 with Hybrid Duty (PWM: stripe width from another noise) and the symmetric drop at t=1 handled by min(smoothstep up, 1-smoothstep(1-Soft...)); Harmonics -> clamp(src,-1,1)=u, out = a1*u + a2*(2u^2-1) + a3*(4u^3-3u) (Chebyshev T2,T3: adds 2nd/3rd harmonics to any noise without extra evals, sharpening ridges or flattening plateaus). Optional 'Steps' int quantises t before the waveform (quantised phase bands).
ideas.look:
Tested. PWM hatch on warped carrier gives banknote or woodcut line engraving where line width encodes a second noise, and is unlike anything on the sheet. Skew gives asymmetric dune or ripple relief in the hillshade. Sine and Chebyshev give the classic sine-of-noise contour family (Chebyshev T12 is visually near sine-of-noise, its value is cost and exact bounds).
[Oscillator, signal-phase] Oscillator(Add(axis ramp, k*fbm)) = marble; Oscillator(fbm, F=10) = topographic contour hatching; Oscillator(DistanceToPoint) = rings; Pulse with Duty = CellularValue gives per-cell stripe widths; Harmonics on Simplex gives sharper, more 'volcanic' bumps. Also the standard way to render any Phase output as stripes.
ideas.why_new: Confirmed in sources: FS::Sin appears only in SineWave (position-only) and the tiling map; no node applies a wave to a source. So this family is currently unreachable other than PingPong's fractal fold. A dedicated node is justified by that gap, and by Duty and Band Guard, which a graph cannot do.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch free. 1 source + 1-2 Sin: about 1x source + 1-2 ns estimated. Chebyshev k=12 is 24 mul-adds. Band Guard adds D source evals and Exp. All dimensions.
ideas.continuity: C-infinity on smooth sources for Sine and Skew when |Skew|<1; C0 for Triangle and Pulse with Edge>0; a hard square is discontinuous.
ideas.params: Wave enum. Hybrid: Frequency, Phase, Duty, Skew. Float: Edge, Guard Limit. Int: Chebyshev Order.
ideas.risks:
Close to a one-liner in its base form, so the argument for it rests on opening the whole family. Stripe width is uneven in base mode (use IsoBands for constant width). Chebyshev bands crowd near +-1 and clip when the source exceeds its range, so the source must be well normalised.
[Bands, dcc-tools] Close to a one-liner for Sine; the case for a dedicated node is the missing primitive plus Strata. High Frequency on steep sources aliases; no constant-width guarantee, which needs a gradient.
ideas.variant_notes: Enabler for the sin-of-noise family: FS::Sin is otherwise only in SineWave and the tiling map. Bands (dcc) contributes the recipe view: Marble, Wood, Agate.
ideas.cost_note: 1 source + 1-2 Sin: about 1x source + 1-2 ns estimated.

queue.name: Oscillator
queue.reason: Sine-of-noise with PWM, skew and Chebyshev modes: the common missing modifier at one source plus 1-2 Sin. PWM hatching is the new bit.

ideas.name: SplineRemap
ideas.one_liner: Arbitrary cubic Hermite curve over a source, with knot values that can themselves be subgraphs: Minecraft-style nested terrain shaping and N-way fade.
ideas.algorithm:
Knots i in 0..N-1 (N<=8): Location (float, sorted), Value (hybrid), Slope (float). x = Coordinate(p). Fixed loop over segments, picking per lane with Select: mask_i = x >= loc_i. For the chosen segment: dx = x1-x0, t = (x-x0)*rcp(dx) (reciprocal precomputed at set), dy = y1-y0, a = m0*dx - dy, b = -m1*dx + dy, out = lerp(y0,y1,t) + t*(1-t)*lerp(a,b,t). Outside the range: linear extrapolation with end slopes, or clamp. Nested: Value input can be another SplineRemap with a different Coordinate, giving a multi-parameter table like continentalness x erosion x weirdness.

[SplineBlend, libs-modifiers] c = Coordinate(p). Knots k[0..N-1] are constant floats (sorted when set) and V[i] hybrid. i from masks: for j in 1..N-2: m = c >= k[j]; lo = Select(m, k[j], lo); hi = Select(m, k[j+1], hi), and similarly for values. t = sat((c - lo) / (hi - lo)). Interp: Linear, Smooth (quintic with zero tangents, so plateaus and libnoise Select style falloff are just repeated values), MonotoneCubic (Fritsch-Carlson tangents precomputed when all V are constants; no overshoot, unlike libnoise Curve) or limited Catmull-Rom for hybrid V. out = interpolation of V[i], V[i+1]. Before evaluating a hybrid V[j], test whether any lane uses a segment touching j with FS::AnyMask; if not, skip it. A nested SplineBlend as V[j] gives multi-parameter terrain shaping, e.g. continentalness, then erosion, then ridges.
ideas.look: Any transfer curve: coast shelf, mesa plateau, plains-to-mountain profile, tiers. As a mixer: smooth interpolation across N biome sources by one control. Not prototyped as it is standard math.
ideas.why_new: Remap is linear, Terrace is uniform steps, Fade is one lerp; an arbitrary curve needs many chained nodes and still cannot do Hermite tangents. Minecraft's whole overworld shaper (offset/factor/jaggedness) is nested splines over 3 noises; with hybrid y_i this node reproduces it directly (coordinate = continents, each point's value = a spline over erosion, etc.).
ideas.simd_plan: Under 8 knots: N compares + Selects, about 1-2 ns constant-value case. Per-batch rather than per-lane skipping, so it honours the data-parallel rule and output is bit-identical to no skip. Up to 2 hybrids per lane matter, but a batch straddling segments evaluates each used hybrid once. GenT dimension agnostic.
ideas.continuity: C1 across knots by construction when knot values are constant. With hybrid values, smoothness inherits them, still C0 minimum. Loc spacing near zero is guarded at set time.
ideas.params: Coordinate (source), Knot Count, Knot N Location, Knot N Value (hybrid), Knot N Slope, Extrapolate enum.
ideas.risks:
Metadata has no dynamic arrays, so 8 fixed slots clutter the node UI. Skip saves nothing on incoherent lanes (GenPositionArray) or lanes straddling knots. Catmull-Rom with hybrid values needs up to 4 values per segment, which reduces the skip gain. Overlaps Remap, Fade and Terrace semantically, so naming should explain why it exists. Knot positions as constants (not hybrid) are needed for tangent precompute and skipping.
[SplineCurve, terrain-tools-engines] Node-editor UI for arrays of points; sorted-x invariant; 16 hybrid sources is a lot of metadata; Extrapolation choice matters because noise outputs exceed [-1,1] after fractals.
ideas.variant_notes: Knot values may be hybrids, enabling Minecraft-style nested splines and N-way mix. Batch-level skipping of unused hybrids keeps output bit-identical.
ideas.cost_note: Under 8 knots: N compares + Selects, about 1-2 ns constant-value case.

queue.name: SplineRemap
queue.reason: Minecraft-style Hermite shaper with hybrid knots (J1 top pick), very high demand. Hybrid knots always run for all lanes, so cost must be documented.

ideas.name: StencilIterate
ideas.one_liner: Apply a local rule (Laplacian, mean, erode, dilate, sharpen, talus, majority) over a fixed stencil of source samples, iterated 1-2 times via the evaluation tree, to filter noise pointwise.
ideas.algorithm:
Stencil T: 2d axis points at +-r (plus centre), or 3^d cube at +-r, chosen by enum; Depth D in {1,2}. Define u_0 = source; u_D(p) = Rule( u_{D-1}(p + t) for t in T ) evaluated recursively with fixed nested loops (|T|^D source evaluations, no state).
  Rules:
    Laplacian : (sum_neigh u - 2d*u_c) / r^2 * gain
    Mean      : average over T
    Erode/Dilate: min / max over T
    Sharpen   : u_c + gain*(u_c - mean)
    Talus     : u_c - k*max(0, (u_c - min_neigh) - talus)        // one thermal-erosion step
    Majority  : tanh(gain*(mean - bias))
  out remapped.
ideas.look: Laplacian of fBm: one-line-wide ridge/valley crease map (negative on crests, positive in troughs), a line-art terrain skeleton. Dilate of CellularDistance: rounded plateaus/pebbles; Erode then Dilate (Depth 2, two rules) removes thin features; Talus on steep fBm: cliffs collapse into angle-of-repose scree slopes; Majority: coarsened two-phase domains with rounded walls. These are classic image filters but applied to resolution-free noise.
ideas.why_new: A depth-1 stencil needs 2d+1 offset evaluations plus min/max/sum chains (5-9 nodes per filter in-graph, more with Depth 2), and talus/majority rules need per-lane maths on the stencil values. The node is a general 'local CA step' primitive: any synchronous local update can be run D steps pointwise at |T|^D cost.
ideas.simd_plan: Nested fixed loops over a precomputed offset table (rebuilt when Stencil/Radius set), each source eval followed by Min/Max/FMA; Majority uses a tanh polynomial. Cost = |T|^D x source: 2D axis depth 1 = 5 evals, depth 2 = 25; 3D 7/49; 4D 9/81. Cube stencil 9/81, 27/729 (3D depth 2 disallowed). Dimension-agnostic; tiles.
ideas.continuity: Mean/Sharpen/Laplacian: source class minus nothing (Laplacian of C2 Perlin is C0); Erode/Dilate/Talus: C0; Majority: continuous (tanh) but near-step.
ideas.params: Source, Rule enum, Stencil enum (Axis/Cube), Radius hybrid (sampled at p), Depth int (1..2), Gain/Bias/Talus floats, VariableRange.
ideas.risks: Depth 2 cost with fractal sources; axis stencil is anisotropic (slight axis bias visible in Laplacian; cube stencil fixes it at higher cost); Talus one step is a cue, not erosion.
ideas.cost_note: Cost = |T|^D x source: 2D axis depth 1 = 5 evals, depth 2 = 25; 3D 7/49; 4D 9/81.

ideas.name: StrataBands
ideas.one_liner: Remaps any field through a jittered 1D band lattice with an asymmetric ring profile and an independent source slice per band: tree rings, agate, sediment, onion layers.
ideas.algorithm:
s=Source(p)*Bands. i=floor(s). Band boundaries b(k)=k+Jit*(rnd(hash1(k))-.5). Evaluate b(i), b(i+1), and via masks b(i-1) or b(i+2) to find band k with b(k)<=s<b(k+1) (3 hashes, 2 Selects). u=(s-b(k))/(b(k+1)-b(k)). Envelope v=u^e*(1-smoothstep(1-Drop,1,u)): slow earlywood rise, sharp latewood drop. Per band: amp a(k)=.4+.6*rnd; lateral eval L=Lateral(p + Offset(k)) once, at a domain offset hashed from k. Output a*v*(1+Lat*L). Because v is 0 at both band ends, the jump in k and in L is invisible, so one lateral eval suffices with no blend. Output clamped and scaled.

[StrataBands, signal-phase] t=Freq*S(p)+Offset. For o in 0..Octaves-1: x=t*2^o; i=Floor(x); u=smoothstep(x-i); a=hash1(i,seed+o); b=hash1(i+1,seed+o); sum+=g^o*lerp(a,b,u).
Out=normalised sum to [-1,1].
Variants: Sharpness applied to u; band width jitter by warping t with a first-octave value; hard sync: per-band integer ratio n=1+hash(floor(t))%R and an inner Tri of n*fract(t), which gives sub-bands that change per band (needs a window to stay continuous).
ideas.look:
Look-tested (m=2 and m=3). Agate-like banding over warped fields, and with a GrowthAge source very believable plain-sawn wood: thick and thin rings, each ring with its own mottling. Sediment cliffs over a Gradient. Very different from Terrace and PingPong, both of which are uniform.
[Strata, libs-modifiers] Look-tested (mode 12). Monotone: subtly uneven sedimentary terraces. Agate: dramatic black/white banding following contours, with thin dark seams, like polished agate or oil film; clearly different from Terrace and PingPong on the sheet. On a Gradient + warp source in 3D it should give rock strata (not rendered).
ideas.why_new: Terrace and PingPong apply a uniform periodic function, and rings never differ from each other. There is no way in the graph to hash on the value of a field. The per-band source slice, with a zero-envelope seam trick, gives independently mottled layers for the cost of one extra eval.
ideas.simd_plan: Cheap: 3 1D hashes, Select, one Pow (or fixed u^2/u^3 polynomial if e is an enum), one Source eval, one Lateral eval: about 1x Perlin over source cost. Dimension agnostic since Source and Lateral do the dimension work: GenT pack with offset added on all axes. 4D automatically works and tiles.
ideas.continuity: C0 everywhere the source is continuous, because the envelope vanishes at band ends. Kink at the drop. Measured c0ratio 2.46 only because of steep drops at high band counts; slope scales with Bands*|grad Source|/Drop.
ideas.params: Source (generator), Lateral (generator, optional), Bands (hybrid), Band Jitter, Profile Power, Drop, Lateral Amount, Amp Jitter, Lateral Offset. Hybrid: Lateral Amount, Drop, Bands if the caller accepts ring shifts where it varies.
ideas.risks:
Source with near-zero gradient gives wide flat bands. Hybrid Bands shifts all rings far from zero, so it causes fast movement. Measured range 1.41 before normalisation, needs a clamp or a constant divide. Pow can be expensive per lane, so prefer the polynomial.
[Strata, libs-modifiers] Monotone differs only mildly from Terrace unless Jitter is high, so the Agate mode carries the visual novelty. Agate removes height meaning, so it is for masks and textures. Output of Monotone can exceed [-1,1] slightly by Jitter/2K. Sharpness 0 limit produces a hard step, as with Terrace.
[ValueStrata, hierarchy-multiscale] Bands alias on steep sources because frequency scales with source gradient. Output std is low (about 0.2-0.3), so it needs a measured scale. Feedback barely changed the look in the proto.
ideas.variant_notes: Hash on the value itself. Options: monotone terraces and agate per-band gray (Strata), per-band lateral source with a zero-envelope seam trick (StrataBands, texture), fractal column with Drift and Feedback (ValueStrata).
ideas.cost_note: Cheap: 3 1D hashes, Select, one Pow (or fixed u^2/u^3 polynomial if e is an enum), one Source eval, one Lateral eval: about 1x Perlin over source cost.

queue.name: StrataBands
queue.reason: Jittered 1D band lattice with asymmetric profile and per-band lateral slice: wood and agate from any field at ~1 Perlin overhead. Pairs with growth-age.

ideas.name: StrataTerrace
ideas.one_liner: Terrace the source in a tilted, foldable strata coordinate with per-layer hashed thickness and hardness, and a cliff/talus riser whose talus width is measured horizontally: mesas, buttes, cuestas, hogbacks and cliff bands from any height field.
ideas.algorithm:
Inputs: height source E(p), dip vector (Dip X, Dip Y, hybrid), optional Fold source F(p). Strata coordinate s = E(p) - dot(dip, p) - F(p). Layer boundaries: u = s/T; k = floor(u); jittered boundaries lo_k = k + 0.5*J*rnd11(hash(k)), hi_k = lo_{k+1}; fix k by one compare each way so lo <= u < hi. f = (u-lo)/(hi-lo). Per-layer hardness hard_k = rnd01(hash(k, salt)): riser fraction c = clamp(Cliff*(0.5+hard), 0.05, 0.95) (hard layers = wide bench, short cliff). Horizontal talus: estimate |grad E| by forward differences (dim extra source evals, eps param); talusV = min(Talus*|grad E|/((hi-lo)*T), 0.9) converts a horizontal talus width into a fraction of the layer's value span; tf = clamp(talusV/c, 0, 0.85). rise(f) = 0 for f < 1-c, else r=(f-(1-c))/c, rise = r<tf ? 0.35*r/tf : 0.35 + 0.65*(r-tf)/(1-tf). Output = (lo + rise*(hi-lo))*T + dot(dip,p) + F(p). Variant 'LithologyRetreat' (prototyped, mode 2 of terr_lens2): instead of analytic layers, sample a 3D hardness source K(x, y, E(p)) and displace the sample position downhill by Retreat*softness*gradE/(|gradE|+c) in K steps before re-evaluating E; general but prone to fold-over, so keep the analytic version as the node and mention the other as a DomainWarp variant.

[TiltedStrata, terrain-landforms] c=h(p)+Dip*dot(p,n)+FoldAmp*Fold(p)+Throw(p); t=c/Th; layer boundaries b_i=i+0.4*(rnd(i)-0.5) from a 1D hash; compare t to b_floor(t) to Select the layer i; w=(t-b_i)/(b_(i+1)-b_i). Hardness H_i=hash(i). T(w)=H_i*smoothstep(1-cw,1,w)+(1-H_i)*w, monotone with T(0)=0 and T(1)=1. out=h+Th*(b_(i+1)-b_i)*(T(w)-w)*Strength. Because the bench offset is a function of c, not h, benches climb and descend across terrain with dip. Hard layers form cliffs and benches, soft layers form slopes. 3D density mode: density=(h-y)+OffsetTable(c) where c includes y, giving real overhanging ledges. Output modes: Height, Layer Value for rock colouring.
ideas.look:
Contour-following benches and cliff bands whose spacing follows a tilted plane instead of the horizontal: on a plateau noise it gives mesas and buttes with caprock ledges and talus aprons, with large dip the benches become asymmetric ridges (cuestas/hogbacks), with a Fold source the bands wave like folded sediments. Layers differ in thickness and in bench/cliff proportion, which is what makes it read as rock rather than paddy terraces. Prototyped: Strata/StrataFold.
[StrataFaults, nature-phenomena] Section output reads as a real rock outcrop: bands with varying thickness and tone, with vertical offset blocks at faults. Terrace output gives ledged cliffs with irregular, not equally spaced, benches when applied to a terrain height.
ideas.why_new: Terrace steps in value space only: horizontal strata, equal layers, risers that are vertical wherever the source is steep and benches that vanish on slopes. A graph cannot tilt the stepping plane or make the talus width independent of slope because it has no access to the source gradient.
ideas.simd_plan: 1 + dim source evaluations (forward differences), two integer hashes for the layer boundaries and one for hardness, a handful of Selects for the k fix-up and the piecewise riser. No window. Dimension-agnostic GenT over the pack: dip is per-dimension; 4D works (tileable). Cost ~ (1+dim) x source + ~30 ops: with a Perlin source ~3-5x Perlin in 2D.
ideas.continuity: C0 whenever rise(0)=0 and rise(1)=1 (adjacent layers meet at hi*T); the cliff is intentionally steep with a user-bounded minimum horizontal width. The probe reports c0ratio 3.6 only because the cliff is narrower than its step h; the construction has no jumps. C1 breaks at bench/riser corners by design.
ideas.params: Source, Layer Thickness, Thickness Jitter, Hardness Jitter, Cliff Fraction, Talus Width (horizontal units), Dip X/Dip Y (hybrid, so a node can rotate strata regionally), Fold Source (optional GeneratorSource, 0 = none), Gradient Epsilon.
ideas.risks:
The talus conversion uses a first-order gradient estimate and clamps at 90% of the riser; near saddles of E the estimate is poor but only affects talus width. Per-layer hashing means the layer sequence is global (same stratigraphy everywhere), which is geologically correct but a 2D 'layer id offset' source could vary it. The LithologyRetreat variant overshoots and tears unless Retreat is well under a feature length (measured c0ratio 1.27 at retreat 0.25 with a 4-octave source).
[TiltedStrata, terrain-landforms] Not tested. Partly graph-reachable in simple form, so its value rests on the table and the layer output. Linear Dip grows without bound with distance and float precision on c falls at far coordinates, so wrap c using a large period.
[StrataFaults, nature-phenomena] Discontinuous Section output can alias. Fault cells look like stretched Voronoi, not like true planar faults over large ranges. The value needs per-bed hash on a floor index, which loses float precision at far coordinates.
ideas.variant_notes: Terrace in a tilted, folded, faulted coordinate with per-layer hardness. 3D density form gives real overhanging ledges (TiltedStrata). Linear dip is not periodic on the 4D torus.
ideas.cost_note: Cost ~ (1+dim) x source + ~30 ops: with a Perlin source ~3-5x Perlin in 2D.

queue.name: StrataTerrace
queue.reason: Tilted foldable strata with hashed hardness and world-unit talus: mesas and cuestas Terrace cannot do (J2 top pick). Looks modest until tuned, so find good defaults.

ideas.name: StreamlineGullies
ideas.one_liner: Line integral convolution of a detail noise along the gradient flow of a terrain source, so added detail runs downslope and converges on its own. LIC is known from flow visualisation and slope-aligned gullies from recent erosion filters (both from memory); this form as a node is the variation.
ideas.algorithm: Inputs: Flow source F (low octaves), Detail source D (high frequency). v(p)=gradF/(|gradF|+g0), which decelerates near critical points. Trace x+=sgn*step*v(x) for k steps uphill and k steps downhill. Sum D at every step plus D(p), then divide by sqrt(2k+1) to preserve variance. out=F(p)+Amp*LIC*min(|gradF|/g0,1), which leaves flats free of streaks. Choose total trace length near 4-8x the detail wavelength. For plausible multi-scale detail, nest nodes: each stage uses the previous output as Flow, with shorter step and higher-frequency Detail, so finer rills follow slopes created by coarser gullies.
ideas.look: Streaked flanks radiating from peaks and pits, with cusps where opposing streak fields meet along ridges and valleys. It looks strikingly unlike the isotropic pitted result of adding the same detail directly, which I rendered side by side. Good for mountain flanks, rills, scree chutes and snow streaks.
ideas.why_new: Fractal octaves ignore the underlying slope. Here direction comes from any source graph, with no cell kernel or phase blending, and flow convergence comes from the trajectories themselves. No current node can read a source along a computed path.
ideas.simd_plan: Dimension agnostic GenT with a fixed k loop and no per-lane branching. Flow evals: 2k*(dim+1); detail evals: 2k+1. For k=7 in 2D that is 42 Flow plus 15 Detail. Estimate with 3-octave Perlin Flow: about 150 ns, about 135x Perlin; k=4 about halves it. Keep Flow cheap. 3D and 4D work directly, and tiling is preserved if the sources tile in 4D.
ideas.continuity: C0 where Flow is continuous, because deceleration keeps v continuous through critical points. Very steep cusps occur at separatrices.
ideas.params: Flow Source and Detail Source (GeneratorSource), Steps k (int), Step Length (float), Decel g0 (float), Amplitude (hybrid), Gradient Epsilon (float).
ideas.risks: TESTED in numpy with spectral noise. First try with unit-length steps and endpoint sampling failed: concentric rings from orbiting maxima, flat per-basin cells. Deceleration, short traces and two-way summation fixed it. Remaining issue: star patterns at every extremum look too regular on simple sources, and the test amplitude was too strong. Cost is the main barrier to using this as a building block.
ideas.cost_note: Estimate with 3-octave Perlin Flow: about 150 ns, about 135x Perlin; k=4 about halves it.

ideas.name: CausticWeb
ideas.one_liner: Inverts the gradient map y = x + a*grad(h) with a few damped steps and outputs log(1/|det J|), giving a soft-bright caustic network (cracked mud, pool light, cosmic web) from one smooth noise.
ideas.algorithm: Zel'dovich or lens map: rays start at q and land at y = q + a*grad h(q). Intensity at y is 1/|det(I + a*Hess h(q))| at the preimage q. Pointwise: q=p; repeat M (3..6): g=grad h(q); q=lerp(q, p - a*g, 0.5). Then compute grad h at q and at q+eps*e_i (D+1 gradients), J = I + a*(g_i - g_0)/eps, det J by closed form (2x2, 3x3, 4x4 cofactor). Output Scale*log(1/(|det|+Floor)). Prototype: dyn_lens mode=29,A=0.2,M=3.
ideas.look: Verified in prototype. Closed polygonal net of bright soft filaments, each cell a dark gradient bowl with internal fainter folds, like pool caustics or dried-mud cracks with depth. Hillshade reads as cobbles or plated hide. Two octaves with a=0.12 gives a finer double-scale net. Good for water caustic textures, cracked ground, cell walls, foam, cosmic-web density.
ideas.why_new: Unlike CellularDistance F2-F1 it has no lattice-cell convexity: the net bends, has unequal cell sizes, cusps and internal secondary folds, and line brightness varies continuously. Single-pass ridged noise has lines at zero crossings, not at fold catastrophes. Cannot be built from existing nodes because they have no Hessian or fixed-point preimage.
ideas.simd_plan: M + D + 1 gradients. Best with an internal analytic-gradient Simplex or Perlin (2D about 6 gradients, about 9 ns; 3D 7 gradients, about 25 ns; 4D 8 gradients, about 60 ns). With a GeneratorSource and finite differences multiply by D+1. 3D form prototyped with perlin3: the slice is a clean web. All straight-line maths.
ideas.continuity: C0: compositions of continuous maps with Abs. Kink along det=0, softened by Floor. Measured c0ratio 3.6 and max slope 305 per unit in 2D at a=0.2.
ideas.params: Strength a (hybrid; acts as water depth, must stay low enough for fixed point convergence, about a*max|Hess|<1.5), Floor (line sharpness), Iterations, Source or internal noise frequency.
ideas.risks:
Above the convergence limit (a=0.35 on 2 octaves in test) it turns to grainy chaos, so a needs clamping or an auto scale. Single-start inverse sees one preimage only, so brightness is not a true caustic sum where 3 preimages exist. It looks right anyway. Output is skewed; range normalised by measured constant.
[CausticFilter, nature-phenomena] Single back-map is approximate: it does not sum over all folded sheets, so cusps are not physically exact. FD step must be tied to source Feature Scale, or the result shows noise or aliasing. Range is heavy-tailed. In a 4D tile, full-D det includes curvature normal to the image surface, so it may not match the 2D look (untested). The prototype used central differences (11 evals), so the 9-eval form is unverified.
ideas.variant_notes: CausticFilter is the M=1 back-map form of this and adds a Plane mode that differentiates x,y only, so an animated 3D source costs 9 evals rather than 14.
ideas.cost_note: With analytic gradients about 9 / 25 / 60 ns for 2D / 3D / 4D (M+D+1 gradients); finite differences over a source multiply that by D+1.

queue.reason: Earlier proto is one of the best images in the catalogue: pool-light webs, stable in 2D and 3D slices (J2 top pick). Needs an amplitude clamp and a Hessian kernel. Decides the caustic family.

ideas.name: CrestLines
ideas.one_liner: Uniform-width ridge and valley lines of any field by a Newton projection on the Hessian. Open branching drainage networks with no simulation.
ideas.algorithm: Hessian H by minimal stencil: 2D 6 taps (9 for symmetric), 3D 10, 4D 15. Crest: take the most negative eigenvalue l with eigenvector e, other eigenvalue m. Across-crest Newton distance d = |g.e| / (|l| + c). Line = (1 - smoothstep(0,w,d)) * smoothstep(a,b, -l - |m|). Valley uses the largest eigenvalue with the sign flipped. Eigenvector 2D closed form: e proportional to (H_xy, l-H_xx) or (l-H_yy, H_xy), selected by the larger norm. 3D/4D: 2-3 steps of power iteration on (sI - H), starting from g. The mask -l-|m| reaches 0 at umbilics, which hides the eigenvector ambiguity there.
ideas.look: Thin, even-width branching, meandering lines with free ends, like river maps, leaf veins or mountain spines. Interleaved crest and valley networks in one output look like a drainage map. Very different from FractalRidged and F2-F1, whose lines are closed loops. Uses: rivers, roads along valleys, ridge masks, cracks, veins.
ideas.why_new: Gives the true topographic ridge and valley skeleton, with dangling ends and tree-like branching, which level-set based lines cannot have. Pointwise river-like lines that actually lie in the valleys of the terrain they were computed from are hard to get today. Width is in world units and independent of steepness.
ideas.simd_plan: Taps 6-9 / 10 / 15. On Perlin about 7-10 / 22 / 65 ns (scalar 9-tap version 8.3x perlin2). Eigen solve is closed form in 2D; fixed power iteration in 3D and 4D, with Sqrt and masks only. Fractal sources multiply cost; compute the Hessian on the lower octaves only by giving the node a low-octave source.
ideas.continuity: C0 by construction with the umbilic mask. Measured c0ratio rises with width (1.4 at w=0.08, 6.2 at w=0.3 on one octave), consistent with thin steep lines, not jumps. Should be verified with fnlab. Line ends fade via the strength mask.
ideas.params: Line Width w (hybrid), Strength thresholds a,b, Mode enum (Crest, Valley, Both signed), Sample Distance h (hybrid). h should be about 1/20 of the source's finest feature.
ideas.risks: Second differences amplify lattice artifacts and float error: Perlin axis bias appears as occasional right-angle segments, and far coordinates need larger h. Not a real hierarchical river network: no guaranteed connectivity or flow-order widening. In 3D the lines become sheets, and whether that is useful is unproven.
ideas.cost_note: On Perlin about 7-10 / 22 / 65 ns (scalar 9-tap version 8.3x perlin2).

ideas.name: EikonalStripes
ideas.one_liner: Project each sample onto a source's zero set with a fixed number of Newton steps, then turn the travelled distance into constant-wavelength stripes: a Turing or fingerprint labyrinth from plain Perlin.
ideas.algorithm: q = p; n0 = S(p). Repeat It times (3): g = grad S(q) by FD; step = S(q)*g / (|g|^2 + Eps^2); clamp |step| to MaxStep (0.5); q -= step. d = |q - p| * sign(n0). Output tri(d / Wavelength)*2 - 1, or d clamped when used as an approximate signed distance. Eps = 0.3 damps the chaos near source critical points. Iso offset: use S - Iso.
ideas.look:
Parallel, equal-spacing bands that follow every coastline of the source, forming a coral / brain / fingerprint / topographic-ripple labyrinth. The FFT shows a clean isotropic ring, which no existing node does, and the histogram is nearly flat. Thresholding gives an even-width labyrinth, usable for reaction-diffusion looks, fingerprints, zebra, dune ripples, wave lines around islands and shells in 3D.
[IsoPhase, dynamics-iteration] Verified in prototype. Coral or brain-coral labyrinth, fingerprint whorls, zebra stripes of near-uniform width, parallel bands wrapping every contour with Y-defects along the medial axis. FFT shows a real ring, so it is narrow-band like reaction-diffusion. Raw mode gives a rounded distance-to-coast terrain with creases on the medial axis. Good for zebra or coral masks, topographic contour art, shoreline bands, sdf-based terracing, geology stripes.
ideas.why_new: PingPong and Terrace make band width depend on slope, so they squeeze and blow out. Here spacing is fixed in world units whatever the source slope. A pointwise fixed-iteration projection gets the reaction-diffusion look without simulation and works over any source graph.
ideas.simd_plan: Fixed It, no per-lane branching (clamp via Min on a scale factor). Forward differences: (It+1)*(1+D) source evals, so 2D 12, 3D 16, 4D 20. Tetrahedral differences reduce 3D to 12. With a dedicated analytic Perlin gradient it measured 6.3x perlin2 scalar (It=3). Sampling must use per-lane displaced positions, which Gen permits. Dimension-agnostic code via a GenT pack.
ideas.continuity:
Discontinuous at sparse points. Measured c0ratio about 1, because Newton basins do not exactly follow the medial axis. Most of the area is smooth and bands are C0 at tri peaks.
[IsoPhase, dynamics-iteration] Mathematically C0 (continuous composition, sign flips only where d=0). Numerically very steep at medial axes and near-critical points: measured c0ratio 1.0, max slope about 2000 per unit at Frequency 15.
ideas.params: Wavelength (hybrid), Iterations (int), Eps (float), Max Step (float), Iso (hybrid), Source, Output (Stripes or Distance).
ideas.risks:
Small speckled knots remain near source critical points. They are much reduced at Eps 0.3 / It 3, but visible at Eps 0.01 and worsen with more octaves in the source (oct=2 was clearly noisier), so it suits smooth 1-octave sources best. Hillshade through it is harsh. Only the 2D form was run; 3D shells are the same formula, untested.
[IsoPhase, dynamics-iteration] Works best on 1-octave sources; 2+ octaves break into noisy dislocations. Distance is capped at N*MaxStep, so low-gradient regions need the cap to cover half a feature. Small speckle at saddles.
ideas.variant_notes: Newton projection to the zero set, then sine of the distance: clean FFT ring, equal spacing, single-octave sources work best.
ideas.cost_note: With a dedicated analytic Perlin gradient it measured 6.3x perlin2 scalar (It=3).

ideas.name: ErosionFilter
ideas.one_liner: Modifier that adds branching drainage gullies to any height source, pointwise: stripes aligned to the slope in octaves, each octave steered by the previous one.
ideas.algorithm: Inputs: Source (height), Octaves, Gully Scale s0 (cells), Strength, Lacunarity, Gain, Branching, Detail, Slope Reference, Epsilon, Differences enum {Forward (d+1 evals), Central (2d+1)}. Step 1: h = Source(p); g = finite-difference gradient (2D: 2 or 4 extra evals). mask m = ease_out(|g|/SlopeRef) with ease_out(t) = 1-(1-sat(t))^2 (Runevision replaces sqrt to avoid discontinuity). G = g (working gradient), M = m (combined mask). Step 2, per octave o (fixed count): s = s0/lac^o, a = Strength*gain^o. Stripe normal n = perp(G)/max(|G|,eps) in 2D (gullies run along G, cross-section varies along n); 3D: n = normalize(G x Up) with Select fallback when parallel. Phacelle-style cell loop over 3x3 (or 4x4) cells of size s: pivot q_c = (c + rnd01^d(hash(seed,o,c)))*s; w_c = max(0, 1-|p-q_c|^2/(cut*s)^2)^2; phi_c = 2*pi*((p-q_c).n)/s; C += w_c cos(phi_c); S += w_c sin(phi_c). Normalise: L = sqrt(C^2+S^2); f = min(2L,1)/max(L,eps); C*=f; S*=f (only magnitudes > 0.5 are normalised, avoids spikes where waves cancel). Height delta: dh = a*M*C. Gully slope: slopeVec = -a*(2*pi/s)*sign(S)*n (sign gives straight triangle-wave gullies). Feedback: G += Branching*slopeVec (finer gullies tilt into coarser ones -> tributaries); newMask = sat(|S|) (zero at creases/ridges); M = (1-(1-M)^Detail)*newMask; h += dh. Output enum {Height = h, Delta = h - Source, Mask = M, RidgeMap (last octave faded toward 0)}.
ideas.look: Prototype cl_misc node 5: plain fbm becomes eroded mountains with dendritic gullies running off ridges into smooth valleys, by far the most convincing terrain from any prototype here. Good for mountain heightfields, detail maps, ridge maps.
ideas.why_new: Needs the source gradient and an orientation-driven noise, neither of which the graph can express (no derivative node, no anisotropic noise). Makes a hard thing (erosion without simulation) a one-node drop-in on any height graph, and it stays pointwise so it works with GenPositionArray and chunked generation.
ideas.simd_plan: Source evals dim+1 once. Inner cost octaves*window^d iterations of hash + weight + sin + cos; octave count is constant so the loop is legal. Estimated 30-40 ns/sample AVX2 in 2D at 4 octaves (about 30x Perlin; scalar sketch measured 31x Perlin with a 3-octave FBm base). Reductions: 3x3 window with R up to 1.25 and small jitter, polynomial cos. 3D: run the 2D lattice on a chosen plane and pass the third axis to Source, same cost. 4D tiling: 2^4 cells, R about 1, near-zero jitter (t = J*g with pairs xy, zw). Cost is justified only by the result, so it is a finishing node, not a building block.
ideas.continuity: Delta field is C1 away from stripe cancellation points (handled by the k=2 clamp) and from |G|->0 (masked to zero by M). Simple per-lane direction gives visible direction discontinuities where G turns fast (Runevision accepts this because the mask hides them). Overall continuity = min(source, C0).
ideas.params: Source (GeneratorSource), Octaves (int, ~5), Lacunarity (2), Gain (0.5), Strength (hybrid), SlopeStrength (~3), BranchStrength (~3), Cell Scale (erosion feature size), Stripe Frequency, Step (gradient epsilon, hybrid), WaterLevel / ValleyAlt / PeakAlt (hybrid), Detail, GullyWeight, StraightGullies (bool), Output enum.
ideas.risks:
LICENSE: the gist says its erosion function derives from Gavoronoise under CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, while FastNoise2 is MIT; reimplement from the mathematical description in Johansen's blog and check provenance before shipping. Cost. A fractal base's gradient is noisy at fine scale and scrambles stripes, so low octave bases work best. True 4D or tileable form is unproven.
[ErosionFilter, libs-modifiers] High cost. Distortion when the gradient changes sharply within a cell. Altitude-based fade target fails where a valley sits above a peak. Gullies do not form true connected drainage. It is a heightfield idea, so 3D is plane-based. My prototype is a sketch rather than the author's code, so the real look depends on a port; check the licence of his code before porting (one port is reported as MPL-2.0 with his permission).
[ErosionFilter, nature-phenomena] The Bevy port warns against finite-differenced gradients, since they break consistency between height and gradient, and FastNoise has no analytic gradients. This is the main technical risk. My crude reimplementation with FD did not reproduce branching gullies with either stripe form, but it omitted some masks and tuning, so it says nothing about the real filter. Substituting 4-corner stripes looked the same as 16-kernel stripes in that crude test, which needs retesting once the base look works. Shader code is on Shadertoy under MPL-2.0 per the search summary, so confirm the licence before porting.
[ErosionFilter, repo-demand] Shader code is MPL-2.0, so derive from the article or ask. Needs source range knowledge for the fade target (connects to #121). Gradient by stencil multiplies source cost. The article does not cover 3D, so the 3D form here is my extension. Altitude-based fade misbehaves where valleys are higher than distant peaks (author notes this).
ideas.variant_notes: Seven independent proposals of the Fewes/clayjohn/Johansen technique. One crude reimplementation (nature-phenomena) did not reproduce branching gullies, and the Bevy port warns against finite-differenced gradients: treat the look as unconfirmed until a port matches the author's. Licences differ by source (CC BY-NC-SA, MPL-2.0, MIT): implement from the description only.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated 30-40 ns/sample AVX2 in 2D at 4 octaves (about 30x Perlin; scalar sketch measured 31x Perlin with a 3-octave FBm base).

ideas.name: FoldCaustic
ideas.one_liner: Jacobian determinant of a displacement field: bright one-line-wide caustic filaments with cusps where the warp folds, forming an organic cell network, at ~3x Perlin.
ideas.algorithm:
W(p) = A * (n_1(p), ..., n_d(p)), d seeded internal gradient noises (Perlin with analytic derivative). G = [d n_i / d x_j]. Optional Symmetrise: G = (G + G^T)/2 (mimics the Hessian of a height field, i.e. refractive pool caustics).
  J = I + A*G ; det = det(J)   (2x2 closed form; 3x3 rule of Sarrus; 4x4 cofactors)
  Output enum:
    Density : out = exp(-det^2 / sigma^2)   (smooth, peaks on fold lines det = 0)
    Inverse : out = min(1, k / (|det| + eps))
    Signed  : out = det remapped
    Flipped : out = smoothstep(-s, s, -det)   (mask of folded-over regions)
  Iterations M > 1 (self-warp feedback): q = p; J = I; repeat M times: q = p + W(q); J = I + A*G(q)*J; then det as above.
FiniteDifference mode: accept any DomainWarp node as Source and build J from d+1 Warp() calls (forward differences).
ideas.look:
Water-caustic / crumpled-foil networks: thin bright curves with cusps and swallowtails enclosing smooth dark cells; Flipped gives cusped organic blobs; with iterations the fold curves acquire nested sub-folds. Signed det alone is a smooth noise with unusual, 'sheared' statistics. Suited to water caustics, cracked glaze, cell membranes, lightning-ish filaments, and as a mask for where a warp over-folds.
[WarpStrain, graph-meta-filters] Proto sheetC m6: for a strong gradient warp, large organic blobs mark the regions where the warp has folded over itself (det < 0), surrounded by a continuous compression field; the warped texture inside the folds is the inverted, crowded part that gives 'Warped Cellular' its cut look. Det-1 is a smooth signed field (stretch positive, squeeze negative) that is itself a usable noise with strong spatial correlation to the warp. Uses: masks to hide or stylise warp folds, 'ink pooling' in the compressed zones of marble, density compensation for scattered features placed after a warp, FTLE-like stretch maps for stylised fluid textures.
ideas.why_new: Nothing in the graph can see how much a warp compresses area; det J is a first-derivative quantity of a vector field, unreachable from scalar nodes. It is cheap (d gradient noises) and gives caustic cusp geometry, which is absent from all existing nodes. Also valuable as a diagnostic filter on existing DomainWarp nodes (FD mode).
ideas.simd_plan:
d gradient-noise evaluations (~1.6x Perlin each), small determinant, exp. 2D ~3.5 ns (~3x Perlin), 3D ~11 ns, 4D ~28 ns (4x4 det ~100 flops, negligible). Iterations multiply by M plus d x d matrix products. FD mode: (d+1) x warp cost. Fully dimension-agnostic, tiles in 4D. Requires an internal gradient-returning Perlin (not a public node): the same utility the FlowEngine ideas need.
[WarpStrain, graph-meta-filters] 2D Warp() evaluations per output (4 / 6 / 8 calls in 2D/3D/4D), each a vector-returning call on the child warp (DomainWarpSimplex 2D ~2-3 ns), so ~12 / 40 / 100 ns before the child's own fractal octaves. Determinants are fixed FMAs; 2D stretch needs one Sqrt. Branch-free. Works in 4D because Warp() exists in 4D.
ideas.continuity: det is C1 for quintic Perlin (C2 noise); Density/Flipped smooth; Inverse C0 at the abs kink. Iterated version stays continuous (compositions of smooth maps).
ideas.params: Amplitude A (hybrid), Output enum, Sigma / Epsilon floats, Symmetrise bool, Iterations int (1..4), Source DomainWarp (optional FD mode), Seeded, ScalableGenerator, VariableRange.
ideas.risks:
Needs analytic-gradient noise plumbing; Inverse output has an unbounded peak and must be clamped/normalised by a measured constant; Symmetrised G is not a true Hessian (caustics look right but are not physically exact).
[WarpStrain, graph-meta-filters] Needs a DispatchClass that can call Warp() on a child DomainWarp; the typed GeneratorSourceT<DomainWarp> already exists for the fractal warps, so this is plumbing, not new infrastructure. The proto's Det output saturates at modest amplitudes because second derivatives of Simplex are large; LogDet or a Strength divisor is the better default. Niche compared with the other ideas, but very cheap.
ideas.variant_notes: WarpStrain is the any-DomainWarp form of the same Jacobian, adding Stretch, LogDet and Compression outputs, usable to mask or density-compensate warp folds.
ideas.cost_note: d gradient-noise evaluations (~1.6x Perlin each), small determinant, exp. 2D ~3.5 ns (~3x Perlin), 3D ~11 ns, 4D ~28 ns (4x4 det ~100 flops, negligible).

queue.name: FoldCaustic
queue.reason: det(I+A*G) of D gradient noises at 3.5/11/28 ns, the cheapest caustic (J4 top pick). Third leg of the caustic comparison; J2 expects smooth curves rather than cusps.

disp.how: Field Free: back-mapped silk filaments, with the single-sheet as-written form dropped

ideas.name: HorizonShadow
ideas.one_liner: Fixed-count ray march of a source treated as a heightfield (2D) or density (3D) along a light direction: cast shadows (horizon test), horizon-based ambient occlusion over M directions, or Beer-Lambert transmittance for clouds.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Source; Steps N (int, same for all lanes); Step Size s0 (hybrid); Step Growth g (geometric spacing); Direction X/Y[/Z] and Elevation (hybrids); Height Scale a; Softness; Mode {Shadow, Lit (Shadow x Lambert), AO, Transmittance}; Directions M (AO).
Shadow (2D): h0 = a*S(pos); best = -inf; t = s0; repeat N: h = a*S(pos + t*L); best = max(best, h - h0 - t*tanEl); t *= g.  shadow = sat(best / Softness). out = 1 - shadow (or Lit = out * sat(0.5 + 0.5 * dot(grad, L)) using 2D extra taps).
AO: for m in 0..M-1 with directions at angle 2 pi m / M (+ fixed phase): horizon_m = max over N steps of (h - h0)/t ; occ += horizon / sqrt(1 + horizon^2); out = 1 - occ / M.
Transmittance (3D): T = exp(-k * sum_n max(0, S(pos + t_n L)) * dt_n); out = 2T - 1. In 3D the Shadow mode is the same march with max replaced by the sum, so all modes share one loop.
4D: L has a w component of 0; the march is in xyz, so tileable 2D works.
ideas.look:
Shadow (proto sheetA m3): hard-edged dark regions trailing every hill in the light direction, length set by elevation; Lit adds the Lambert term and reads like a lit relief map with cast shadows. AO (m4, also with only 4 directions x 5 steps): valleys and the base of slopes darken, crests stay bright: a 'wetness / sediment' mask that is not a slope mask. Transmittance on a 3D FBm gives self-shadowed cloud densities. Nothing on the sheet is non-local in a direction; hillshade is purely local.
[HorizonShelter, graph-meta-filters] Asymmetric masks: flat fully exposed plateaus on one side of each hill and ramped, elongated lee shadows on the other. Used for snow drifts, moss on sheltered sides, tree-line bias, directional weathering, baked hillshade. SkyView gives a soft crevice and hollow mask.
ideas.why_new: A shadow is a max over many samples displaced along a line; as a graph that is N DomainOffsets + N Subtract + N Max chains per direction and it still would not expose a per-lane direction. Cast shadows and AO are the two masks terrain artists most often bake offline; here they are pointwise, seed-stable and infinite, and the hybrid light direction makes them animatable.
ideas.simd_plan:
Loop count N (and M) is a member int, so the loop is uniform across lanes; body is 1 source eval + a few FMAs and a Max. Cost = (1 + N*M) x source (+ 2D taps for Lit). Shadow N=8 with FBm Simplex x5: 2D ~ 9 x 6.5 ~ 60 ns, 3D ~ 120 ns. AO 4x5 = 21 taps: 2D ~140 ns, 3D ~280 ns. Geometric step growth (g = 1.5) lets 8 steps cover 25 step sizes so long shadows are affordable. 4D is the 3D march with w fixed.
[HorizonShelter, graph-meta-filters] M+1 taps: 9 at M=8, in any dimension: Perlin 10/20/39 ns. SkyView 19 taps in 2D, only sensible in 2D. Fixed march, max and min only, no per-lane early out.
ideas.continuity: C0 (proto c0ratio 7.95 shadow, 8.0 AO): max of continuous functions plus a soft clamp; the horizon arg-max switching between steps gives mild C1 kinks that read as shadow terminators. Sparse geometric steps can let a thin ridge slip between samples, producing small gaps in long shadows (a classic sparse-march artefact).
ideas.params: Source; Steps N; Step Size (hybrid: distance LOD); Growth; Light Dir X/Y/Z + Elevation (hybrids: a time-driven direction sweeps shadows); Height Scale; Softness; Mode; Directions M; VariableRange.
ideas.risks:
Cost scales with N x M x octaves and users will set N=32; expose a sane max and show cost in the editor. Softness is in height units, so it needs retuning when Height Scale changes (derive Softness from Height Scale x Step Size internally). Shadows from features outside the march range are missing, which is fine for texture work.
[HorizonShelter, graph-meta-filters] Narrow peaks fall between taps at large R, so M should scale with R times source frequency. Output heavily saturates unless gain is matched to the source. It is more of a mask than a shape generator. Tileable direction issue as with other directional nodes.
sources: Max, N. Horizon mapping: shadows for bump-mapped surfaces, The Visual Computer 1988 (recalled, not fetched)
ideas.variant_notes: Shadow, AO, sky view, and Sx wind shelter, all a horizon march. Geometric step growth reaches far cheaply at the price of possible gaps behind thin ridges.
ideas.cost_note: Cost = (1 + N*M) x source (+ 2D taps for Lit). Shadow N=8 with FBm Simplex x5: 2D ~ 9 x 6.5 ~ 60 ns, 3D ~ 120 ns.

ideas.name: IsoDistance
ideas.one_liner: Divides any smooth source by its gradient length to get an approximate world-unit distance to an iso-level, giving constant-width lines, rivers, bevels and terraces.
ideas.algorithm:
h = Epsilon. f0 = S(x) - Level(x) (Level hybrid). g = central differences (2d evals), n = max(|g|, GradFloor).
If Period P > 0: r = f0 - P * round(f0 / P)   // signed offset to the nearest contour of the family Level + kP, in [-P/2, P/2]
else r = f0.
d = r / n.
Newton refinement (Iterations = 0..2, same count for all lanes): x1 = x - d * g / |g|; f1 = wrap(S(x1) - Level); d = d + f1 / n (optionally recompute g at x1 for a second-order correction).
Out = clamp(d, -MaxDist, MaxDist) (world units; VariableRange maps to +-1 with MaxDist). Band use: Abs(out) < w is a band of true width 2w around the iso-level.

[IsoDistance, libs-modifiers] f0 = Source(p) - Level; for each axis g_i = (Source(p + h*e_i) - Level - f0) / h; L2 = sum(g_i^2); d = f0 / sqrt(L2 + eps). Modes: Signed: out = clamp(d / MaxDist, -1, 1). Band: out = clamp(|d| / Width, 0, 1) * 2 - 1. IsoLines(N): t = f0*N; e = (t - round(t)) / N; d = e / sqrt(L2 + eps), then Band. ContourTerrace(N, Riser): t = f0*N; r = floor(t); fr = t - r - 0.5; a = sign(fr) * max(|fr| / (N * sqrt(L2 + eps) * Riser), 2*|fr|); a = clamp(a, -1, 1); out = (r + hermite(a*0.5 + 0.5)) / N. The 2*|fr| term forces the riser to saturate at band edges, which keeps it C0 where contours crowd. Optional Newton refinement: st = f0 / (L2 + eps), limited to MaxStep; p1 = p - st*g; d = sign(f0)*|st|*|g| + f(p1) / |grad f(p1)| (doubles the cost).
ideas.look:
Even-width contour lines, rivers and roads along the zero set of a low-frequency noise. Plateaus get constant-width cliffs, like bevelled masks or rice-paddy terraces. Rescaling source amplitude does not change the output. Look-tested (lm_lens modes 1 and 3): naive |f| shows blobs at saddles and hairlines on slopes, while IsoDistance stays nearly uniform with faint smudges at f~0, grad~0. The Newton version is sharper but adds specks, so first order is the recommended default.
[LevelSetDistance, terrain-landforms] One continuous meandering incision of uniform width through any terrain, with flat floor, vertical or terraced walls, no pinch-outs where the source is steep and no bloat where it is flat. Prototyped: Canyon (terraced walls) and Slot (narrow). Also coastline cliffs (Level = sea level of a continent noise), mesa rims (Level = caprock elevation), rivers for texture masks.
ideas.why_new: abs(noise) < w has width proportional to 1/|grad f|, so a river cannot be asked for in world units today. Width becomes a real length, independent of source amplitude and octave count. It also gives Terrace a riser width that does not collapse on steep ground. No existing node exposes a gradient, and the graph version needs dim+1 source copies plus a dozen operators.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch-free, generic GenT over the position pack, no lattice. Source evaluated dim+1 times: 3/4/5 evals in 2D/3D/4D, so 3.3/8.8/21.5 ns on Perlin (3x/4x/5x Perlin). InvSqrt or Sqrt once. Fractal sources multiply accordingly. 4D output inherits GenTileable2D periodicity because it is a pure function of the 4D coordinates.
ideas.continuity: C0 wherever the source is C1, since the sqrt(L2+eps) denominator is smooth and positive. Measured c0ratio 6.8 (band) and 7.9 (terrace). C1 is lost at the band clamp and along |d|.
ideas.params: Source; Level (hybrid); Period (float, 0 = single level); Epsilon; Gradient Floor; Iterations (int 0..2); Max Dist; Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks:
Estimate is only valid near the level set, so keep MaxDist under the source feature size. Smudges at critical points. Needs C1 sources (not CellularValue or White). h must suit the source scale and survive far coordinates. Sources with kinks (Abs, F1) give a usable but biased estimate.
[IsoDistance, distribution-topology] Far from the level set the value is only a distance estimate (clamp it); near saddles/plateaus of the source the estimate overshoots. Epsilon must be below the finest source detail. Cost multiplies the source cost by 5-7.
sources: Inigo Quilez distance estimation of implicit functions (from memory, not consulted)
Taubin 1994, Distance approximations for rasterizing implicit curves (the |f|/|grad f| estimate)
from memory, not consulted: Taubin 1994 'Distance approximations for rasterizing implicit curves'
ideas.variant_notes: f/|grad f| with band, canyon, shell, contour-period and terrace outputs. Tests: first order is the recommended default, as Newton is sharper but adds specks. Tetrahedral stencil from TaubinDistance is the cheapest gradient.
ideas.cost_note: Source evaluated dim+1 times: 3/4/5 evals in 2D/3D/4D, so 3.3/8.8/21.5 ns on Perlin (3x/4x/5x Perlin).

queue.reason: S/|grad S| with optional Newton: constant-width rivers, bevels and contours, the primitive for world-unit widths (J2, J4 top pick). Use the simplex D+1 stencil. Try a Period output to cover eikonal-stripes.
