ideas.name: KuwaharaField
ideas.one_liner: Edge-preserving smoothing by sector variance, which steepens flanks and flattens tops. Mesas at independent heights with no global terrace levels.
ideas.algorithm: Shared taps: centre, ring of N at radius r, ring of N at r/2. For each of N overlapping sectors, take its taps (centre, three consecutive outer, one inner), with mean m_s and variance v_s. Weights w_s = ((vmin+e)/(v_s+e))^q with vmin = min v_s, so values stay in [0,1] with no overflow; q=8 is three squarings. Output sum w_s m_s / sum w_s. Sectors in 3D are defined by directions from a 12-point icosahedral ring.
ideas.look: Flat-topped patches with organic ragged borders and cliffs, each patch at its own height: mesas, paint-dabs, posterised camouflage, flood-basalt steps. Thresholds are local, so it differs from Terrace, whose levels are global and contour-shaped, and from CellularLookup, whose borders are straight polygon edges.
ideas.why_new: Local adaptive posterising from any field, with no chosen levels and no cells. Also an oil-paint filter for textures. Not expressible with any existing node since it requires variance comparison across sets of taps.
ideas.simd_plan: 2D 13 taps (N=6) to 17 (N=8), 3D about 25, 4D about 25 with a sparser stencil. On Perlin about 14-19 / 55 / 108 ns. Sectors share taps, so it is one batch of taps plus fixed sums. Min for vmin; no branches.
ideas.continuity: C0 for finite q, since it is a smooth weighted average of continuous quantities. Measured c0ratio 7.68. Hard Kuwahara (q large) approaches jumps.
ideas.params: Radius r (hybrid, about feature size/3), Sharpness q (int power of two), Sample stencil enum, Epsilon e. Hybrid r lets areas morph between original and mesa.
ideas.risks: Stencil imprint: at larger r and q, borders show a stair or polygon look from the fixed tap directions. 3D and 4D stencils are untested, and sparse stencils may imprint more. Expensive on fractal sources.
ideas.cost_note: On Perlin about 14-19 / 55 / 108 ns.

ideas.name: LineIntegralNoise
ideas.one_liner: Pointwise line-integral convolution: average a high-frequency source along K fixed Euler steps of a direction field (angle source, or the contour/gradient of a scalar source) to get long flow-aligned streaks: brushed metal, wind-combed sand, wood grain around knots, fur.
ideas.algorithm:
Inputs: Source (texture), DirectionMode enum: FixedAngle; AngleSource (hybrid angle, 3D: Yaw+Pitch hybrids); GradientOf(scalar GeneratorSource) with sub-enum Downhill (d = -grad/|grad|) or Contour (2D: rotate grad 90 deg; 3D: normalize(cross(grad, Up))). Steps K (int), StepLength L. acc = w0*src(p); q = p; for k in 1..K: d = dir(q); q += L*d; acc += w_k*src(q). Reset q = p; for k in 1..K: d = dir(q); q -= L*d; acc += w_k*src(q). Weights w_k = 1 - k/(K+1) (triangle). out = acc / sum w. Gradient directions by central differences (1+2D evals per step) with |grad| clamped by eps so d never NaNs. Because every lane integrates its own path with a fixed step count the node is pure and stateless.

[StreamlineLIC, dynamics-iteration] Field V = gradient of source A (or curl, or user DomainWarp), unit-normalised softly: u = V * InvSqrt(dot(V,V) + delta^2).
Texture B must be piecewise constant on a lattice (cell-white: rnd11(hash(floor(p*freq)))) with cell size >= 2h so neighbouring samples on one streamline hit the same cells; a continuous White noise would average to mush.
  acc = w0*B(p0); wsum = w0; pf = pb = p0
  for k in 1..N:                                   // forward and backward legs, fixed N each
      pf = pf + h*u(pf); pb = pb - h*u(pb)
      w = hann(k/N)
      acc += w*(B(pf) + B(pb)); wsum += 2w
  out = acc / wsum  (Output Min/Max remap; also 'Contrast' pass: (out - mean)*gain)
Optional Bias direction (constant vector added to V) for combed grain.
ideas.look:
Prototype cl_misc node 1, K=8-12: Source at scale 2-3 along Perlin contours gives closed eddies, agate rings and thin dark separatrix lines; longer L gives combed fibres crossing at saddles. Different from warp since values are integrated rather than displaced. Fur and wind masks, geology bands, painterly strokes, dune streaks.
[FlowFIR, signal-phase] Tested. Box with 8 taps each side gives flowing streaks: silk, feathers, fur tufts, wind-blown sand, with sharp cusps at flow convergence. Very distinct from the warp nodes: warp bends features, whereas this anisotropically smears them along curves while retaining fine cross-flow detail.
ideas.why_new: van Wijk built spot noise for vector field visualization, and LIC is the pointwise successor. Warp nodes move a sample, they do not smear along a path. A graph would have to nest K warps per side per step, with sharing issues.
ideas.simd_plan:
Branch-free: 2K iterations of (direction eval + source eval + FMA), all lanes same K. Cost = 2K x (dir + src): K=8, Value source, Perlin angle: ~16 x 1.7 ns ~ 27 ns in 2D (about 7x Perlin, comparable to CellularDistance 3D); gradient-of-scalar mode triples the direction cost. 3D/4D: generic vectors; 4D contour mode undefined, use Downhill or AngleSource. Offer K up to 16.
[StreakFilter, volumetric-3d4d] Modifiers.inl pattern; fixed-count loop of source Gen calls on offset positions (the sources are evaluated at other positions, allowed). Cost N x Source (+ N x direction in Curved mode): with Perlin 3D and N=6 about 15 ns.
ideas.continuity: Unnormalised velocity: C0, c0ratio 7.94. Normalised velocity (the usual LIC): c0ratio 1.42, real discontinuities along separatrices. So no normalisation, stream length scales with speed, and stagnation zones get less smear.
ideas.params: Source; DirectionMode; Angle / Angle Sources (hybrid); Scalar Source; Steps K (int); Step Length; Weighting enum (Box/Triangle); Seed Offset.
ideas.risks:
Expensive; streak length is limited to K*L; Euler drift on curved fields (acceptable visually); users will chain it with fractals and pay octaves x 2K.
[StreamlineSmear, lit-classic] Expensive. If Source frequency is above 1/h, you get beading (seen at fs=6, K=8), so the step must track Source scale. Weak stats with the Potential at high amplitude. Grows with Potential cost. Tileability unverified. Only 2D prototyped.
[StreamlineLIC, dynamics-iteration] The coherence trick fails if StepLen > half a texture cell; near critical points of V streaks degenerate to dots (delta softening); cost grows with N.
sources: Cabral & Leedom, 'Imaging Vector Fields Using Line Integral Convolution', SIGGRAPH 1993 (recalled, not fetched)
from memory, not consulted: Cabral & Leedom 1993 Line Integral Convolution
Cabral and Leedom 1993, Imaging vector fields using line integral convolution (from memory, not consulted)
ideas.variant_notes: Seven proposals of fixed-step LIC. Key findings: unnormalised velocity is needed for C0 (normalised measured c0ratio 1.42); the source feature must exceed the step or it beads; a cell-white texture with cell >= 2 steps gives crisp hairlines; contrast needs a measured gain.
ideas.cost_note: Cost = 2K x (dir + src): K=8, Value source, Perlin angle: ~16 x 1.7 ns ~ 27 ns in 2D (about 7x Perlin, comparable to CellularDistance 3D); gradient-of-scalar mode triples the direction cost.

ideas.name: LocalPhase
ideas.one_liner: Demodulate a narrowband noise into local amplitude and phase from its value and gradient, then rebuild it with any wave shape or harmonic.
ideas.algorithm:
Treat S locally as A cos(phi) with carrier Omega: A = sqrt(S^2 + |g|^2/Omega^2), x = cos(phi) = S/(A+e). g comes from the simplex stencil, and the Teager-Kaiser form sqrt(|g|^2 - S lap S) can estimate A*Omega from the same taps. Outputs: Envelope (A), Equalised (x, all peaks equal height), Harmonic m = T_m(x) via Chebyshev recurrence t2 = 2x*t1 - t0 (no atan needed), Triangle or Saw (polynomial acos of x, then a wave shape). Multiply by A/(A+e2) to fade phase vortices. Optional second source: amplitude of B with phase of A (AM/FM).

[MonogenicFilter, signal-phase] Evaluate source at p and p +- h*e_i (1+2D evals; h float param). g_i = (s+ - s-)/(2h); lap = sum(s+ + s- - 2s)/h^2; G = |g|. Mode enum: GradMag = G; Laplacian = lap; Slope = dot(g, dir) with dir from fixed angle or Hybrid angle (lighting-like shading baked as a value); NewtonDistance = clamp(s / max(G, Gmin), -Dmax, Dmax) (first-order signed distance to the source's zero level set; stripes from Oscillator on it have constant width because |grad| ~ 1 near the zero set); MonoAmplitude = sqrt(s^2 + G^2/k0^2) with k0 = 2pi/CarrierWavelength (envelope of a narrowband source: the Riesz/monogenic magnitude); MonoPhase = atan2approx(G/k0, s) mapped [0,pi] -> [-1,1], or cos(m*phase) with int Harmonics m (each bump of the source is split into m nested rings of equal PHASE spacing, so ring width stays constant for a narrowband source); Orientation = atan2approx(g_y, g_x)/pi (2D; 3D returns azimuth, feeds PhasorNoise direction); Teager = max(0, G^2 - s*lap) (AM-FM energy, works on broadband sources); Hessian det (2D) via 4 extra diagonal taps as an optional Curvature mode (ridge/valley line detector).
ideas.look:
Harmonic output gives fingerprint or brain-coral stripes with a fixed number of bands between every crest and trough, everywhere, regardless of local amplitude. Equalised gives a contrast-flattened Turing-like labyrinth. Envelope gives a smooth slowly varying blob field. Good for agate, wood ring bands, topographic line art, coral, and contrast-normalised masks.
[LocalPhase, distribution-topology] Flat: inflated Perlin in which all peaks have equal height, and every peak and trough is reachable at a high threshold. Multiplied m=5: equal-amplitude nested contours, closer to fingerprint than PingPong. A much cheaper relative of EikonalStripes. Good for equal-height dune or wave fields and cheap contour stripes.
[MonogenicFilter, signal-phase] GradMag of Perlin: cell-like web of bright creases; NewtonDistance + Oscillator: contour hatching with equal spacing and fingerprint-like convergence at saddles; MonoAmplitude: soft positive blobs where the noise is 'loud', zero where it is flat; MonoPhase cos(m.): nested ring sets inside each bump (tree-ring blobs, lichen); Teager: etched, embossed texture energy; Slope: directional hillshade that can be used as a mask (windward/lee). Uses: erosion masks from curvature, hatching, SDF-ish blending of noises, orientation fields for stripe nodes.
ideas.why_new: Sin or PingPong of a value gives a ring count proportional to local amplitude, with spacing bunched on slopes and dead zones where the amplitude is low. Here band count and contrast are locked by phase, and the spacing tracks the carrier and not the slope. A graph cannot do this because it needs the gradient. It also extracts an amplitude envelope from a single noise, which no existing node does.
ideas.simd_plan: D+2 taps (4/5/6), or D+1 when h is small and the stencil mean stands in for S. About 4.4/11/26 ns on Perlin (scalar prototype 4.7x perlin2 including atan2, which the Chebyshev port removes). m Chebyshev steps with int m are a fixed loop. Dimension agnostic because only |g| matters.
ideas.continuity: C0 away from isolated vortices where S and g vanish together; there phase is undefined and the amplitude fade makes it continuous. Harmonic bands are steep at high m (measured c0ratio 2.0-2.8, slope about 400 per unit), which I read as narrow bands plus the vortex points. Needs confirming in fnlab.
ideas.params: Carrier Period (hybrid; constant per source type, Omega^2 about 9 per feature unit for Perlin), Mode enum, Harmonic m (int for Chebyshev; a hybrid float would need the acos path and costs a little more), Sample Distance h. Epsilon e.
ideas.risks:
Assumes a narrowband source. Single-octave Simplex or Perlin is ideal, and three-octave fBm still worked with a higher Omega but looked noisier. A wrong Omega skews band spacing without breaking anything. Lattice directionality of Perlin may show more clearly once amplitude is equalised.
[LocalPhase, distribution-topology] Assumes a narrowband source; broadband fBm gives rough output. Cusps show in hillshade as small pinch points at extrema. Band spacing is equal in phase, not in world units, so EikonalStripes is the one to choose when spacing must be constant. Only tested at 1 octave in 2D.
[MonogenicFilter, signal-phase] Central differences on a fractal source are noisy for small h (h must be ~1/4 of the finest feature). Monogenic amplitude/phase are only meaningful for narrowband sources (single octave or Phasor); document. Multiple source evaluations multiply cost: GeneratorCache does not help because positions differ.
sources: Felsberg & Sommer, 'The Monogenic Signal', IEEE TSP 2001 (recalled, not fetched)
Maragos, Kaiser, Quatieri, Teager-Kaiser energy operator, IEEE TSP 1993 (recalled, not fetched)
ideas.variant_notes: Monogenic demodulation of narrowband sources. Chebyshev harmonics avoid atan. MonogenicFilter adds Teager energy and orientation outputs.
ideas.cost_note: About 4.4/11/26 ns on Perlin (scalar prototype 4.7x perlin2 including atan2, which the Chebyshev port removes). m Chebyshev steps with int m are a fixed loop.

ideas.name: LyapunovStretch
ideas.one_liner: Propagates the analytic Jacobian through a shear chain and outputs log stretch (finite-time Lyapunov exponent), drawing the invisible veins of a mixing flow as thin filament networks at very low cost.
ideas.algorithm: J=I. For each shear k of ShearFlow: compute d=A*n(s), ds=A*F*n'(s) analytically; p+=u*d; J=(I + ds*u*t^T)*J. Output Scale*log(||J||_F^2) - Offset. Cheaper option: propagate one tangent vector v=(I+ds*u*t^T)v only and output log(v.v), with no Frobenius matrix; after a few steps it aligns with the max stretch direction. Prototype: dyn_lens mode=25,N=12,A=0.6,per=1,k=0.3,o=0.5.
ideas.look: Verified in prototype. Dark background with bright thin curling filaments and fibre bundles, like Lagrangian coherent structures in ocean currents, fine marble veins or hair flow. N=10 Golden is broader and streakier; periodic N=21..30 gives cleaner thread-like veins. Hillshade reads as combed fur or wind streaks. Good for veins, cirrus, flow fields, fur masks, wood grain detail.
ideas.why_new: Ridged and warped noises make lines at contour levels of a warped field; here lines are places of maximum strain in the map and are thin because of exponential growth, not due to thresholding. Gradient-flow FTLE was tried and is grainy; the shear chain's exact analytic Jacobian is what makes it clean and cheap.
ideas.simd_plan: Each step: 1D noise with derivative plus 2x2 matrix update (or 2 mul-adds for tangent form): about 0.7 ns. N=12: about 8 ns, N=21: about 15 ns. 3D/4D: single tangent vector form keeps it near-linear in D. No source evals at all, a pure generator.
ideas.continuity: C0 and smooth since log(||J||^2) is smooth with ||J||>=1 for area-preserving maps. Measured c0ratio 3.3 and max slope about 460 per unit at N=12.
ideas.params: Amplitude (hybrid), Shear Frequency, Steps, Direction Mode, Output Scale. Mixins: Feature Scale, VariableRange.
ideas.risks: Output is positive-skewed; normalisation by a measured constant varies with N and A. Periodic mode is not fully isotropic. Very thin veins alias at low sample rate.
ideas.cost_note: Each step: 1D noise with derivative plus 2x2 matrix update (or 2 mul-adds for tangent form): about 0.7 ns.

queue.name: LyapunovStretch
queue.reason: Analytic Jacobian through a shear chain gives filament veins at ~0.7 ns per step (J4 top pick). Exists only as a shear-flow output; replaces stretch-ftle at a fraction of the cost.

disp.how: the node; own class since it takes no Source

ideas.name: RankTaps
ideas.one_liner: Rank filter via a sorting network over taps, with a hybrid rank morphing smoothly from erode through median to dilate.
ideas.algorithm: Fixed K=9 stencil: centre plus 4 at r plus 4 at 0.55r rotated by 45 degrees (3D: centre + 12 icosahedral directions). Sort with a min/max network: 25 exchanges for 9 inputs, or Paeth's 19 for median only. q = rank*(K-1); output lerp(v[floor q], v[floor q + 1], frac q), done per lane by sum of masked terms or 8 Selects. Median on a thresholded field approximates curvature motion of the level set (Merriman-Bence-Osher).
ideas.look: On CellularValue: rounded-corner pebble mosaics with plates eating into each other per rank. On FBm: rounded peaks or narrowed crests. On hard masks: corners round and specks vanish, without the blur a soft filter would bring.
ideas.why_new: The only continuous morph between dilate and erode, painted by a hybrid. The only filter here that handles discontinuous sources gracefully, since its output is always one of the actual values, so cell values stay crisp. Plain Min and Max of taps are the two end ranks.
ideas.simd_plan: K taps + sorting network of min/max pairs, which is ideal for SIMD. 2D about 10 ns + 6 ns network on Perlin, more on Cellular (9 x 3.9 = 35 ns for rounded cells). 3D 13 taps about 29 ns + 10 ns network. Branch-free and identical across dimensions except for the table.
ideas.continuity: Inherits the source's class: C0 for continuous sources, since order statistics of continuous functions are continuous, with kinks. On discontinuous sources, jumps move and round but remain.
ideas.params: Rank (hybrid, 0 to 1), Radius r (hybrid), K enum, Source.
ideas.risks: Stair or polygon imprint on hard edges with only 9 taps, visible in the prototype. Weak visual effect on smooth single-octave sources. Radii past about half a feature start showing ghost copies at end ranks.
ideas.cost_note: 2D about 10 ns + 6 ns network on Perlin, more on Cellular (9 x 3.9 = 35 ns for rounded cells).

ideas.name: ReposeMorph
ideas.one_liner: Grey-scale morphology by a cone on a fixed stencil of source samples: enforces an angle of repose, builds talus and fills valleys, for any source. Morphology is standard in image processing; as a slope-parameterised terrain node it is the variation.
ideas.algorithm: Stencil: 2 rings of 8 offsets, the outer ring rotated by 22.5 degrees, with radii r1 and r2. Dilate: out=max(h(p), max_i(h(p+o_i)-S*|o_i|)), so peaks grow into cones of fixed slope S. Erode: out=min(h(p), min_i(h(p+o_i)+S*|o_i|)), so pits widen into V-cones and ridges narrow. Fill (closing approximation): erode a dilated result by nesting two nodes, or use a built-in 8x8 form. Paraboloid structure function option: S*|o|^2 for rounded hillslope results. Flat structure option (S=0) gives flat plateaus and flat valley floors. Put detail octaves after this node rather than before.
ideas.look: Fixed-angle talus aprons around peaks, sharpened inverted cones in pits, flat alluvial lowlands when closed, broad plateaus from opening. The surface looks weathered, with sharp creases where slope limits meet.
ideas.why_new: All existing modifiers are per-value, so none can use neighbours. A node that compares samples at other positions can enforce a world-space slope, which Remap, Terrace or blends cannot do.
ideas.simd_plan: Fixed 17 evals with Min/Max, no branches; 2D, 3D or 4D offsets (plane stencil or a 14-direction 3D stencil at higher cost). Closing with an 8-point stencil is 64+ evals. Estimated 17x source cost single-op. Tiling is preserved only if offsets are applied in native position space, and in 4D torus mode they do not correspond to plane offsets, so verify.
ideas.continuity: C0: Min and Max of continuous fields.
ideas.params: Source, Op (enum Dilate, Erode, Open, Close), Slope S (hybrid), Radius r1, r2, Structure (enum Cone, Paraboloid, Flat).
ideas.risks: Not tested. Sparse stencils give octagonal cones and miss features smaller than the stencil spacing, so only low-octave input is reliable. Fixed-position sampling gives visible stencil patterns on high-frequency sources. Costly when nested.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated 17x source cost single-op.

ideas.name: SlopeBlur
ideas.one_liner: Substance's Slope Blur made pointwise: walk N fixed steps along a flow map's gradient or contour and accumulate a source, giving smeared leaks, chipped facets, or silky line-integral swirls.
ideas.algorithm: q=p; acc=0; mn=+inf; mx=-inf. for i in 0..Samples-1 (constant): m=Flow(q); g_a=(Flow(q+e*axis_a)-m)/e; g=g/Sqrt(dot(g,g)+Eps); if Contour: 2D g=perp(g) (3D: cross with a fixed member axis); v=Source(q); acc+=v; mn=Min(mn,v); mx=Max(mx,v); q+=g*Length/Samples. Output by Mode: Mean acc/Samples, Min mn, Max mx.
ideas.look: Short length: rust and dirt smears following a surface. Long along-gradient: paths converge on extrema, so catchment basins go flat and give leaf-like faceted plates with crisp borders (a pointwise watershed look). Contour mode on fine noise: silky hair and wood flow (LIC). Prototype: dcc_lens mode=13.
ideas.why_new: Substance users rely on this for worn edges; nothing here integrates along a field. Domain warp moves a sample once; this averages along a streamline. The basin-partition look, organic cells whose borders follow valleys of a noise, is not reachable another way.
ideas.simd_plan: Samples x ((dim+1) x Flow + Source). Samples=8 with Perlin flow and Perlin source: about 35 / 88 / 190 ns (30x+ Perlin). Justified only as an effect node. Keep Flow cheap; analytic Perlin-derivative path cuts a lot. Everything is per-lane position math, so no masks needed.
ideas.continuity: Effectively discontinuous across ridges of the flow map since paths diverge exponentially. Measured c0ratio 1.09-1.5 even with soft normalisation, and unnormalised stepping (remove the /Sqrt) keeps it Lipschitz at some loss of reach. Treat as a stylised filter, not a displacement source, without smoothing.
ideas.params: Source, Flow (GeneratorSource), Samples (int), Length (hybrid), Mode enum, Direction enum (Gradient, Contour), Eps (float), Epsilon step (float).
ideas.risks: Expensive and not C0. Substance's docs warn the slope input must be smooth. FD precision at far coords. A sibling lens has a flow-blur variant, so may overlap; the basin look is the part to keep.
ideas.cost_note: Samples=8 with Perlin flow and Perlin source: about 35 / 88 / 190 ns (30x+ Perlin).

ideas.name: SpillLevel
ideas.one_liner: Pointwise depression filling: the lake level at p is the min over a fan of rays of the max of the source along each ray, so basins fill to their spill point and output either flooded terrain, lake depth or a flat-floor mask.
ideas.algorithm: h = S(p). For D fixed directions (D=8..16 on the unit circle in 2D; in 3D the 26 neighbour directions or a 2-ring icosahedral set) and N samples per ray at distances t_k = R*k/N: m_d = max_k S(p + t_k*dir_d) (start m_d = h). L = min_d m_d (or a smooth-min with temperature param to hide fan faceting). Outputs: Flooded = max(h, L); Depth = L - h (water depth / sediment thickness mask); Fill Fraction = smoothstep(0, Blend, L - h). Interpretation: a point is under water if every escape route within radius R must climb above its height; it is exact for depressions narrower than R with a spill pass in a sampled direction, and conservative otherwise. Cheaper lattice variant (not prototyped): per coarse cell, spill = min over the 8 neighbour-boundary midpoints of S, blended across cells with a partition of unity; fills only cell-sized basins but costs 9 evals.
ideas.look: Smooth terrain with flat water surfaces / playas / alluvial floors in every closed depression, each at its own correct spill height; the Depth output is a clean lake mask. Prototyped: SpillSmooth / SpillSmoothMask (12 dirs x 6 samples on a 1-octave base). With a multi-octave source the ray fan undersamples and prints directional ridges inside lakes (terrain_round2 Spill8/Spill16), so the intended use is a low-frequency basin source plus detail added afterwards, or more samples.
ideas.why_new: Depression filling (Priority-Flood) is the textbook global operation nobody can do in a pointwise graph; Min/Max/Remap cannot know where the spill point is. A radius-limited ray estimate turns it into a fixed-cost, stateless node. Flat-floored basins at varying heights are a dominant landform cue (lakes, salt flats, valley fill, glacial tarns) and are absent from the contact sheet.
ideas.simd_plan: D*N + 1 source evaluations with constant loop counts, running Max/Min per lane, direction table precomputed when params are set; smooth-min via Exp if enabled. 2D at 12x6 = 73 evals -> ~75x source (about 80 ns with Perlin); 3D with 26 directions x 4 samples = 105 evals; 4D: 80 directions x 3 is the ceiling. Honest cost tier: 'use on a cheap basin source'.
ideas.continuity: C0: max and min over a fixed set of continuous functions. Measured c0ratio 7.99-8.00. Per-lane random fan rotation (tried) breaks it and must not be used; rotate the fan by a low-frequency continuous angle instead if faceting matters.
ideas.params: Source, Radius (hybrid), Directions (int enum 8/12/16), Samples per ray (int), Output enum {Flooded, Depth, Fill Fraction}, Smooth Min temperature, Blend.
ideas.risks: Angular and radial aliasing: polygonal lake outlines and faint ridges inside lakes when the source has detail finer than the sample spacing. Basins wider than Radius are only partially filled (leaves a ring of water, which can look like a lakeshore terrace, sometimes acceptable). Expensive; a lattice-based single-level variant is the fallback.
ideas.cost_note: 2D at 12x6 = 73 evals -> ~75x source (about 80 ns with Perlin); 3D with 26 directions x 4 samples = 105 evals; 4D: 80 directions x 3 is the ceiling.

ideas.name: StencilFilter
ideas.one_liner: K-tap ring/star stencil over any source with modes Mean (blur), HighPass, Sharpen, Dilate, Erode, Range (morphological gradient), PeakMargin / PitMargin (extract local maxima/minima as blue-noise dots), Roughness (variance) and LocalNormalize (local AGC).
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Source; Radius r (hybrid); Taps enum {Star 2D taps on the axes, Corners 2^D, Ring8 (2D) / Cuboctahedron12 (3D)}; Rotation (hybrid, 2D angle; 3D: rotate about a fixed axis) to de-lattice the stencil continuously; Mode; Amount; Width.
GenT: v0 = S(pos); for k in 0..K-1: v_k = S(pos + r * R(theta) u_k) where u_k are compile-time unit offsets and R is the per-lane rotation built from (cos,sin) of the hybrid angle.
  Mean      = (v0 + sum v_k) / (K+1)
  HighPass  = v0 - Mean ; Sharpen = v0 + Amount * (v0 - Mean)
  Dilate    = max(v0, max_k v_k) ; Erode = min(...) ; Range = Dilate - Erode
  PeakMargin= (v0 - max_k v_k) / Width, clamp [-1,1]  // > 0 only within ~r/2 of a local maximum of S
  PitMargin = (min_k v_k - v0) / Width
  Roughness = sqrt(mean((v - Mean)^2)) -> VariableRange
  LocalNormalize = (v0 - Mean) / (Roughness + eps) * 0.5
max/min run as FS::Max/Min over the unrolled taps; no per-lane loop count differences.

[NeighbourhoodFilter, terrain-landforms] Stencil: centre plus 2*dim axis points at +-eps (Slope, Laplacian), optionally a ring of S points at Radius (S=8 in 2D, 12-26 in 3D) for Mean/Min/Max/TPI. Slope = |(S(p+eps e_i) - S(p-eps e_i))/(2eps)| over i; Laplacian = sum_i (S+ + S- - 2S0)/eps^2 (negative = convex ridge, positive = concave hollow); TPI = S0 - mean(ring); Range = max(ring) - min(ring); Relative Height = (S0 - min)/(Range) in [0,1]. Output scaled by a user Gain and clamped to [-1,1]. Typical terrain uses: Fade(detail, 0, smoothstep(curvature)) deposits fine 'sediment' noise only in hollows; Multiply(rock texture, slope mask); Remap relative height to carve only upper slopes (free-face/talus split).
ideas.look:
PeakMargin on a one-octave Simplex gives scattered convex blobs centred on the noise maxima (proto sheetC m2): a Poisson-disk-like scatter mask whose spacing is set by the source frequency and whose blob size by r, with no lattice (local maxima of band-limited noise repel). On FBm it gives summit caps (snow caps, hilltop vegetation); on -CellularDistance it marks cell centres. Range is an edge detector that turns any field into outlines; Mean of Checkerboard/CellularValue is a proper box blur; LocalNormalize flattens the amplitude of a warped or fractal field so its busy-ness is uniform (sheetB m8). Dilate/Erode fatten or thin any mask by r.
[LocalStatistics, signal-phase] Mean of White at R: soft grainy cloud (a true isotropic low-pass of white noise, different in character from any lattice noise); Max of CellularDistance: rounded pebble tops; Min of thresholded fbm: eroded archipelagos with margins; Range of Perlin: crease web; RMS of PhasorNoise: the stripe envelope (blotches where stripes are strong). Band-split: src - Mean(src) isolates the fine band of any graph.
ideas.why_new: Min/max over shifted copies is possible with Max/Min + DomainOffset nodes (8 DomainOffset + 7 Max for one ring), but nobody will build it; the dedicated node is 1 node with a hybrid radius, and the PeakMargin / LocalNormalize modes need the whole tap set at once (variance, max and centre share taps). PeakMargin in particular is a cheap blue-noise scatter generator that needs no point lattice and inherits the correlation structure of whatever source you give it, which no existing node offers.
ideas.simd_plan: Taps are compile-time constant offset tables per dimension (Star: 2D entries, Corners: 2^D, Ring8/Cubocta12); the rotation is applied with 4 FMAs per tap in 2D. Cost = (1+K) x source: Star 2D/3D/4D = 5/7/9 taps, Corners 5/9/17, Ring 9/13/-. Perlin+Ring 2D ~10 ns, 3D Cubocta ~29 ns; FBm Simplex x5 2D ~60 ns. 4D works with Star/Corners sets. Dilate/Erode of a hard mask at radius r needs at least the Ring set or it looks square.
ideas.continuity: Mean/HighPass/Sharpen/LocalNormalize: C0 for C0 sources. Dilate/Erode/Range/Margins: C0 (min/max of continuous functions) but C1 breaks where the arg-max tap switches. A rotation hybrid that is itself C0 keeps everything C0; a hashed per-cell rotation would not (so it is not offered).
ideas.params: Source; Radius (hybrid: distance-dependent blur, or a mask that only dilates in one biome); Rotation (hybrid: feed a low-frequency noise to randomise stencil orientation continuously); Taps; Mode; Amount (Sharpen); Width (margins); Eps (LocalNormalize); VariableRange.
ideas.risks:
Sparse-tap blur of a high-frequency source aliases (K taps cannot integrate a field with features smaller than the tap spacing); document 'Radius <= 2 x source feature size' or combine with SuperSample. Blur is not Gaussian; an N-fold blur is not affordable (taps^N). LocalNormalize can amplify float noise in flat regions, hence the eps.
[StencilFilter, lit-recent] Cost multiplies the source; Radius must match the feature scale and the intended octave of detail; finite differences on discontinuous sources (Cellular value) give spikes.
sources: World Machine / Gaea / Houdini HeightField Mask by Feature (slope, curvature, TPI style masks; general knowledge, no URL consulted)
ideas.variant_notes: Fixed-tap neighbourhood statistics: blur, sharpen, erode, dilate, range, RMS envelope, TPI, plus PeakMargin, which extracts local maxima as a blue-noise-like scatter mask with no lattice.
ideas.cost_note: Cost = (1+K) x source: Star 2D/3D/4D = 5/7/9 taps, Corners 5/9/17, Ring 9/13/-. Perlin+Ring 2D ~10 ns, 3D Cubocta ~29 ns; FBm Simplex x5 2D ~60 ns.

queue.name: StencilFilter
queue.reason: K-tap blur, sharpen, erode, dilate and peak mask with rotated taps. PeakMargin is the valuable mode; absorbs rank-taps and local-rank.

ideas.name: StreakSmear
ideas.one_liner: One-sided decaying multi-tap of a Source along a direction (mean, max or min), the pointwise equivalent of 'directional blur / streaks': rust runs below bolts, water stains, drips, wind-blown snow and brushed smears from any blotchy noise.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Direction per axis (floats; 'down' = (0,-1)), Length L (hybrid, world units), Taps K (int, 2..16), Decay w (0..1), Mode {Mean, Max, Min, Accumulate}, Threshold T (Accumulate), Source.
h = L/K; for k = 0..K-1: s_k = Source(p - k*h*dir) (samples taken upstream along the direction, so a spot at position c influences points downstream of it). Mean: sum w^k s_k / sum w^k (soft smear). Max: max_k (s_k - k*Fall) (a bright spot carries a fading streak below it: drips). Min: symmetric for dark stains. Accumulate: sum_k w^k max(0, s_k - T) normalised (streak intensity from the amount of 'dirt source' above). Output through ScaleOutput.
Use with Direction derived from gravity in texture space; for a terrain, use (0,0,-1) in 3D to streak down slopes of a volumetric field, or feed Direction from DomainRotate upstream. Combining Max mode on CellularDensity Coverage (rivet pits) gives rust streaks whose length is per-spot random when Length is a hybrid CellularValue.
ideas.look: Vertical rusty tails under spots, drip trails that fade, rain-stain streaks on walls, snow or sand drifted onto one side of bumps, motion-blurred noise. The sheet has only isotropic patterns; nothing has one-sided directional structure.
ideas.why_new: DomainWarp and DomainAxisScale stretch a field symmetrically; a graph cannot sample a Source at a fixed set of offset positions and combine them. The symmetric ring stencil already prototyped (dcc_lens mode 18) blurs/dilates isotropically; the one-sided decaying kernel is what makes gravity effects.
ideas.simd_plan: Fixed loop of K Source evaluations at offset positions (positions computed by FMA), accumulate with mask-free arithmetic; GenT over the pack. Cost K x Source (K=8 on Perlin 2D: ~9 ns). 2D/3D/4D trivially; tiling is preserved if the offsets are applied before the torus mapping (they are, since it is a Source position offset).
ideas.continuity: C0 whenever the Source is C0 (finite sum/max of continuous functions).
ideas.params: Direction (per-axis floats), Length (hybrid), Taps (int), Decay, Fall, Threshold, Mode enum, Source.
ideas.risks: Visible banding with few taps and long Length (K must grow with L/feature size); Max mode with Fall = 0 produces hard-edged drips (sometimes wanted). Overlaps conceptually with the ring stencil idea; could be merged as a 'Directional' kernel enum on that node.
ideas.cost_note: Cost K x Source (K=8 on Perlin 2D: ~9 ns).

queue.name: StreakSmear
queue.reason: One-sided decaying taps for rust runs and drips, K x source along a straight direction. Only banding at long lengths needs a look.

ideas.name: StretchFTLE
ideas.one_liner: Finite-time Lyapunov exponent of the N-step flow map: thin sharp filaments (Lagrangian coherent structures) for curl fields, dendritic watershed divides for gradient fields.
ideas.algorithm:
Trace d+1 twin trajectories through the same flow as FlowWatershed/StirAdvect: q_0 = Phi(p0), q_i = Phi(p0 + eps*e_i), i=1..d, all with the same fixed N steps.
  J[:,i] = (q_i - q_0)/eps                       // Jacobian of the flow map by finite differences (no Hessian needed)
  2D: S = ||J||_F^2, D = det J, sigma_max^2 = (S + sqrt(S^2 - 4 D^2)) / 2
  3D/4D: use ||J||_F^2 / d as the stretch proxy, or two power-iteration steps of J^T J on a hashed start vector
  out = log(sigma_max) / (N*h), remapped by a measured constant; Direction enum: Forward (repelling structures) / Backward (attracting, negate field).
For gradient-descent fields the repelling set is the watershed divide; for curl fields it is the stretching skeleton of the stirring.
ideas.look:
Curl field: braided, sharply defined ribbons and filaments wrapping around vortex cores, like dye visualisations of 2D turbulence; the ridges are one line wide while interiors are smooth, which no fractal gives. Gradient field: a continuous dendritic network of divide lines (the ridgelines of fBm as thin crisp curves, branching tree-like), i.e. a true ridge/divide detector, far cleaner than FractalRidged, and usable as a mask for ridges, crack lines, lightning, root systems.
[FlowSeparatrix, terrain-landforms] Thin bright closed-cell network tracing the source's valley floors and separating each peak's basin, with occasional dangling arms. Carving it produces sharp incised lines. Good for crack-like valleys, river masks that agree with terrain, and watershed-cell partitioning.
ideas.why_new: Measures sensitivity of the flow map, which needs the flow map evaluated at d+1 nearby points: inexpressible in a graph. It extracts topological structure (divides, stretching manifolds) that single-pass noise never has. Shares the FlowEngine; could be an Output enum of the flow node rather than a separate class.
ideas.simd_plan: (d+1) full trajectories each with the flow's per-step evals; closed-form 2x2 singular value or Frobenius norm; log via FS::Log; no masks. Cost ~ (d+1) x flow cost: 2D N=8 analytic-gradient engine ~3 x 13 = ~40x Perlin (~45 ns); 3D ~4 x 85 = ~340 ns; 4D ~5 x 220 = ~1.1 us. Heavy in 4D; recommend 2D/3D use, but it is dimension-agnostic and correct. When a user DomainWarp node is the field, call its Warp() d+1 times per step.
ideas.continuity: Continuous (log of a smooth positive quantity, finite-difference Jacobian of a smooth map), C1 with analytic gradients; very steep at the ridges by design.
ideas.params: Same as the flow node (Field/Potential, Steps, StepLen, FieldType enum Gradient/Curl/WarpSource) plus Epsilon float (1e-3..1e-2 feature), Direction enum, Measure enum (SigmaMax / Frobenius), Output Min/Max.
ideas.risks:
Cost; ridge contrast depends on N*h (too short: blurry, too long: everything saturates); eps must stay > floating error of far coordinates (use 1e-2 feature at large world coords).
[FlowSeparatrix, terrain-landforms] TESTED in numpy. It produces closed cells, NOT dendritic trees, so it does not by itself solve river networks. Unit-length stepping produced contour-like ring artifacts; deceleration removed them. Fine lines need antialiasing or a larger dx, and the carve looks scratched when thin. Applying it to many-octave sources was not tested.
ideas.variant_notes: FlowSeparatrix tested the gradient-flow case and found closed cells, not dendritic trees, so it does not by itself solve river networks.
ideas.cost_note: Cost ~ (d+1) x flow cost: 2D N=8 analytic-gradient engine ~3 x 13 = ~40x Perlin (~45 ns); 3D ~4 x 85 = ~340 ns; 4D ~5 x 220 = ~1.1 us.

ideas.name: SurfaceProbe
ideas.one_liner: The sampled-derivative building block: value, gradient, Laplacian, Hessian and iso-distance from one node at the cheapest possible stencil.
ideas.algorithm:
Stencil choice by Output enum. Jet stencil: simplex v_i at step h, with sum v_i = 0 and sum v_i v_i^T = (D+1)/D I. g = D/((D+1)h) sum f_i v_i. Laplacian = 2D/h^2 (mean f_i - f_0). Outputs needing it: Slope |g|*FeatureRef, Slope Angle (polynomial atan), Directional Derivative g.u, Relief (normalised sun term), Normal component g_x/sqrt(1+|g|^2), Laplacian, Unsharp S - k*lap, Double-angle Aspect (gx^2-gy^2)/|g|^2, IsoDistance S/sqrt(|g|^2+e^2) (uniform width bands). Hessian stencil adds ShapeSign tr(H)/(sqrt(D)||H||_F), Mean Curvature, det(H) for passes. Blur stencils: Vogel disc or rotated-grid taps with box or Gaussian weights, with hybrid radius (spatially varying blur).

[GradientFilter, distribution-topology] h = Epsilon (world units, e.g. 0.05 x feature size). Stencil evals of the source S:
  f0 = S(x); f+a = S(x + h e_a), f-a = S(x - h e_a) for each axis (2d evals); for Hessian modes also f(+-h e_a +-h e_b) for a<b (2d(d-1) evals).
  g_a = (f+a - f-a)/(2h); H_aa = (f+a + f-a - 2 f0)/h^2; H_ab = (f++ - f+- - f-+ + f--)/(4h^2)
Modes:
  Slope: |g|            Directional: dot(g, L) with L = (Light X,Y,Z,W) normalised at param-set
  Laplacian: sum_a H_aa
  Ridge / Valley (2D): m = (H_xx+H_yy)/2, r = sqrt(((H_xx-H_yy)/2)^2 + H_xy^2); lambda_max = m + r, lambda_min = m - r; Ridge = max(0, -lambda_min) * (optional) exp(-|g|^2/s^2) to keep only crest lines; Valley symmetric. 3D: second derivative across the gradient, n = g/|g|, kappa_n = n^T H n, and the transverse Laplacian L_t = trace(H) - kappa_n as a cheap ridge measure (no eigen solve), or 2 power-iteration steps for lambda_max.
  ContourCurvature (2D): kappa = (H_xx g_y^2 - 2 H_xy g_x g_y + H_yy g_x^2) / max(|g|^3, eps) (curvature of the level set through x; sign = concave vs convex side). 3D: mean curvature of the level set = (trace(H) - n^T H n)/|g|.
Out scaled by Output Min/Max; Slope optionally through 1 - exp(-k slope) to bound it.
ideas.look:
Slope: bright ridges and cliff bands, dark flats - the mask everyone uses for rock-vs-grass; Laplacian: thin bright ridgelines and dark valley lines (a pointwise 'ridge detector'); Hillshade: an instantly readable relief render usable as a texture mask (sun-facing snow, shadowed moss).
[SourceCurvature, graph-meta-filters] Ridge strength on a Simplex FBm gives a smooth, organic vein / crack network that follows the crests of the source (proto sheetC m1): thin bright filaments with Y-junctions, nothing like Cellular F2-F1 (which is polygonal) or Ridged FBm (which is a different field). Valley strength is the dual network. Laplacian is an isotropic band-pass of any source (a Mexican-hat of Cellular gives rims). LensDensity at k ~ 1/f^2 gives an underwater-caustic net (proto sheetA m0; on Simplex base it needs a larger k than Perlin). Uses: crack/vein textures that are coherent with a terrain, river/ridge masks for an existing heightfield, rims around cells, detail placement by convexity (rock on convex, sediment on concave), caustic textures.
ideas.why_new: Every graph that wants slope logic is impossible today: there is no multi-sample node, and Fade and Remap only see values. This is the piece that unlocks slope-weighted detail, slope-driven biome mixing, uniform-width lines. It also defines the shared internal helper used by most other nodes on this list. A dedicated node is justified since finite differences cannot be wired with existing nodes except by hand with DomainOffset, at twice the taps and with no scale compensation.
ideas.simd_plan: Cost in source evaluations, 2D/3D/4D. Gradient only: 3/4/5 (central differences would be 4/6/8). Jet, value+gradient+Laplacian: 4/5/6. Full Hessian: 6/10/15 with first-order mixed terms, 9/19/33 symmetric. Blur: K taps, independent of D but quality falls. On Perlin, jet = 4.4/11/26 ns; on 5-octave FBm multiply by 5. Hybrids add one evaluation each at p only, not per tap. Nesting multiplies, so a Slope of a Slope is (D+2)^2; for a cheap second derivative use the Hessian stencil instead. Taps compose fine with lanes unrelated in space. GeneratorCache gives no savings since taps differ in position.
ideas.continuity: One order lower than the source: C1 source gives C0 slope. Slope has a cone-shaped kink at extrema unless regularised, sqrt(|g|^2+e^2) smooths it. On Cellular F1 sources, gradient outputs jump at cell walls but stay finite since h is finite.
ideas.params: Output enum, Sample Distance h (hybrid; clamp to a positive floor), Direction X/Y/Z/W (hybrid for directional), Slope Reference (world units per feature so that output stays scale invariant), e (regularise), Source.
ideas.risks:
Float error: differencing at far coordinates loses bits; with h = 0.05 feature at x=1e5 and small feature scale, error is noticeable, so h needs a floor in ulps. Slope range depends on the source, so outputs need a stated reference or measured normalise. ShapeSign on single-octave Perlin clearly revealed the lattice, so it is better on Simplex or SuperSimplex. Forward stencils leak h^2 bias from the Laplacian into the gradient; symmetric stencils are an enum away.
[SourceCurvature, graph-meta-filters] Second differences amplify float error by 1/e^2: with e=0.03 and far coordinates (|pos|>1e4) precision collapses; needs a documented minimum Epsilon or an internal clamp relative to |pos|. 3D eigenvalues via Jacobi add ~60 ops; invariants-only (Laplacian/det/Frobenius) may be enough for most looks. Expensive on fractal sources; recommend GeneratorCache is irrelevant (different positions) so cost is real.
ideas.variant_notes: Nine proposals of derivative analysis of a source; shared helper for many other nodes on this list. Outputs: DX..DW, slope, normal, hillshade, aspect, Laplacian, ridge/valley via Hessian eigenvalues, Gaussian/mean curvature, NormalRGBA8. The same graph needs about 12 nodes and there is no plain Sqrt node.
ideas.cost_note: On Perlin, jet = 4.4/11/26 ns; on 5-octave FBm multiply by 5.

ideas.name: TubeNoise
ideas.one_liner: Turns 1, 2 or 3 source fields into a first-order true distance to their common zero set, so spaghetti caves get uniform tube radius and cheese walls uniform thickness.
ideas.algorithm:
Sources f (and g, h). Gradients by forward differences at Epsilon, or analytically in a built-in Perlin variant. Gauss-Newton distance with Levenberg damping, 1 source: d = |f| / sqrt(|grad f|^2 + L). 2 sources: a = grad f . grad f, b = grad f . grad g, c = grad g . grad g, det = (a+L)(c+L) - b^2, d^2 = ((c+L) f^2 - 2 b f g + (a+L) g^2) / det. 3 sources: the same with the 3x3 inverse by cofactors. Output ScaleOutput(min(d, Dmax), 0, Dmax), optionally minus Radius (hybrid). Damping is the key detail: with a det+eps form, d goes to 0 at critical points and creates false tunnels, while with G+L*I, d^2 goes to |f|^2/L, which is large, so rock stays rock. Codimension 2 in 3D gives curves, in 2D isolated points, in 4D surfaces.

[TubeNoise, volumetric-3d4d] One Perlin lattice visit (8 corners in 3D, 16 in 4D). Per corner hash h: two independent gradients g1 = Grad[h & 15], g2 = Grad[(h >> 4) & 15]. Compute n1, n2 by quintic-interpolated gradient dots AND their analytic gradients G1 = grad n1, G2 = grad n2 (standard Perlin-with-derivatives: value = a + u(b-a) + v(c-a) + w(e-a) + ... ; derivative = lerped corner gradients + du*(corner differences), du = 30 f^2 (f-1)^2). In 4D take only the x,y,z partials (w is time).
 a = G1.G1, c = G2.G2, b = G1.G2
 d2 = (c*n1*n1 - 2*b*n1*n2 + a*n2*n2) / max(a*c - b*b, eps)   // n^T (J J^T)^-1 n, first-order distance to the codim-2 set
 d  = Min( Sqrt(d2), MaxDist )
Outputs (enum): Tunnel = 1 - 2*Min(d/Radius, 1) (inside = +1), Distance = signed (d - Radius), Phase = n1 * InvSqrt(n1^2+n2^2+eps) (angle-like coordinate around the tube, for stripes/ribs along tunnels). Codim param (int 1..3, default 2): codim 1 uses only n1 -> d = |n1|/|G1| (constant-thickness sheets / rivers in 2D), codim 3 adds n3 -> isolated blobs. 2D with codim 2 gives dots (the curve pierces the plane); 2D default should be codim 1 (wandering rivers/cracks).
ideas.look:
Prototyped against the plain sqrt(f^2+g^2) Minecraft form using an isosurface render, and the difference is large: the plain form bulges into webs and sheet-like blobs where gradients are weak, while this one gives clean worm tubes of near constant radius tangled through the volume. 2D: small near-round dots at zero crossings. 3D slice: ellipses and elongated dashes. Also gives constant-thickness sponge walls from 1 source, and a cheap Lipschitz-normalised field for sphere tracing.
[TubeNoise, volumetric-3d4d] 3D iso-surface: a tangle of smooth near-constant-diameter worm tunnels that bend, pass over and under each other and branch at saddle points, with no dead ends (level-set intersections are closed 1-manifolds). With FBm-warped input the tubes wriggle. 2D slice: round discs of similar diameter, a few elongated where a tube grazes the plane; with w the discs drift, merge and split as tubes sweep through. Codim-1 mode: uniform-width sheets (cheese/sheet caves) or 2D river networks.
ideas.why_new: The known spaghetti recipe has pinches and blowouts because thickness depends on local noise gradient, and no graph can cure that (no gradient node exists; a hand-built graph would have dozens of duplicated nodes). Works with any source, including warped fractals, and output is in world units so Radius is meaningful. Makes a hard thing easy rather than adding a new texture.
ideas.simd_plan:
Perlin.inl-style per-dimension Gen, second gradient set from spare hash bits, derivative accumulation alongside the value (about 2x the FMAs). All branch-free; one Sqrt, one Reciprocal. Est. 2.5-3x Perlin: ~3 ns 2D, ~6 ns 3D, ~13 ns 4D (vs 12/41 for Cellular). 4D is exact (true 4D lattice), so GenTileable2D works.
[LevelSetDistance, volumetric-3d4d] No loop or window. Sources evaluated (1+dim) times each: 3D with 2 sources is 8 evals, 8 x 2.2 = 18 ns for Perlin, plus about 1 ns algebra. An analytic Perlin3 pair built in costs about 7 ns. 4D: 10 evals, 43 ns with Perlin. Tetrahedral gradient has no benefit here. Branch free.
ideas.continuity: Inherits the source's smoothness (C1 to C2 for Perlin) apart from the first-order min with Dmax, which is C0 and only far from the tube. d itself has a cone point at the centre line only, matching a true distance.
ideas.params: Codimension via 1 to 3 GeneratorSource inputs, Epsilon (float), Damping L (float), Dmax (float), Radius (hybrid). Variant enum for built-in Perlin pair with analytic gradients.
ideas.risks:
Estimate is only trustworthy near the zero set: at 0.6 units the 2D dots turn into teardrops, so keep Dmax near 2 to 3 radii. Cost 8x Perlin if generic. Epsilon must scale with source Feature Scale, or use a world-unit default. Near-tangent crossings of f and g produce short dashes rather than round tubes.
[TubeDistance, libs-modifiers] All gradient noises are zero at their own lattice points, so two same-lattice sources make a regular grid of fake dots (observed before adding kOffset; seen clearly in the wide view). Thin specks remain where gradients are nearly parallel. In 2D the output is only dots, so the value is mostly 3D. The real SIMD eps value needs tuning for source scale.
sources: from memory, not consulted: Minecraft 1.18 'spaghetti caves' (|n1|<t && |n2|<t); Taubin 1994 first-order distance estimate
ideas.variant_notes: Levenberg damping is the key detail: det+eps creates false tunnels at critical points. Same-lattice sources make a grid of fake dots unless offset by a non-lattice constant. The analytic built-in form is much cheaper and offers phase around the tube.
ideas.cost_note: Perlin.inl-style per-dimension Gen, second gradient set from spare hash bits, derivative accumulation alongside the value (about 2x the FMAs). 2.5-3x Perlin: ~3 ns 2D, ~6 ns 3D, ~13 ns 4D (vs 12/41 for Cellular).

ideas.name: AdhesionWeb
ideas.one_liner: Full-dimensional Hopf-Lax over a disc of taps with Boltzmann weights, which gives shock webs and pebbled transport from any field.
ideas.algorithm: Tap set e_k: Vogel disc, K=19 in 2D, Fibonacci ball K about 33 in 3D. E_k = S(p+e_k) + |e_k|^2/(2t). w_k = exp(-(E_k-Emin)/nu). W = sum w_k, mean e = sum w_k e_k / W. Outputs: ShockWeb = (sum w_k |e_k|^2/W - |mean e|^2)/R^2 (Boltzmann variance, peaks where two distant minima tie); Potential = Emin - nu log W (soft Moreau envelope with smooth hollows and sharp creases); Displacement = |mean e|; Transport = sum w_k T(p+e_k)/W (each point reads a second field near the minimum it collapses onto).
ideas.look: ShockWeb: thin bright curved network with very varied cell sizes, like the cosmic web in the adhesion model. Potential: rounded valleys with creased crests, ridged but with a different topology from FractalRidged. Transport: pebbled, scaly clumps. Displacement: camouflage-like plates caused by tap discretisation.
ideas.why_new: Unlike SlopeSlide it is a global-in-window search, so it can jump across a small hill and report real competition between basins, which gives actual shock lines. Gets a variable-size cell network out of a noise, with transport of a second field across cells, which no combination of existing nodes can do.
ideas.simd_plan: K taps + K Exp, K=19/33/about 50: Perlin about 35/100/300 ns; 2D and possibly 3D only as a practical choice, and 4D is expensive. 4D falls back to fewer taps with more artifacts. Fixed tap tables, one Min pass, one weighted sum.
ideas.continuity: C1 for nu>0 with a smooth source, though the web lines are steep. Tap discretisation creates plates when nu is small against tap spacing.
ideas.params: Time t (hybrid), Reach R (hybrid), Viscosity nu (hybrid), K enum, Output enum, Transport Target.
ideas.risks: Stencil imprint is real and blotchy line brightness is visible in the prototype. The 2D look is promising but may need K of 30+ for clean lines. SlopeSlide gets many of the same looks at a fifth of the cost, so ship this only if the Transport and Web outputs prove their worth.
ideas.cost_note: K taps + K Exp, K=19/33/about 50: Perlin about 35/100/300 ns; 2D and possibly 3D only as a practical choice, and 4D is expensive.

ideas.name: BlueNoiseScatter
ideas.one_liner: Scatter whose candidate stamps are thinned pointwise into a Poisson-disk-like set: a candidate survives only if no higher-priority candidate in its own neighbourhood lies within the spacing radius, computed from hashes alone, so stamps never overlap and spacing looks even.
ideas.algorithm:
For each candidate cell c in the sample's 2^d window: f(c), priority pr(c) = rnd01(hash(c)). Survival test: for each neighbour n of c in c + {-1,0,1}^d, n != c (fixed loop): dead |= (pr(n) > pr(c)) & (|f(n) - f(c)| < Spacing) & present(n). This is Matérn type II hard-core thinning on a jittered grid, evaluated independently per candidate, so it is stateless: the same c always gets the same answer from any sample point. Then the surviving candidates are stamped exactly as in Scatter (local frame, per-stamp seed, source eval or analytic stamp, combine). Spacing <= 1 - Jitter guarantees that checking only the 3^d neighbourhood is complete.
Optional Soft Spacing: instead of killing, shrink: s *= smoothstep(0, Spacing, nearest higher-priority distance), so stamps shrink rather than vanish near a dominant neighbour (no popping, denser fill).
The unique cells touched are the union of candidates' neighbourhoods: 4^d (2D 16, 3D 64, 4D 256) hashes + feature points; hashing is cheap compared with source evals, and only the 2^d survivors are stamped.

[PoissonScatter, repo-demand] One candidate per cell: position x (uniform in the cell) and priority a from hash. Survival rule, one round of Luby-style independent set: keep candidate i iff a_i < Density(x_i) (density reject) and no other candidate j with priority a_j > a_i lies within Rmin of x_i. Rmin<=1 cell means the neighbours fit a 3x3 around each candidate. Sample evaluation: 3x3 candidates around p, each tested against its own 3x3, so 5x5 unique hashes in 2D. Output: Profile(F1/Radius) as a compact smoothstep, or F1 distance, or hash-value per point.
ideas.look:
Isolated dots with even spacing and no clumps (prototype 'thin' vs 'raw' clearly different: raw jitter has near-touching pairs and holes). Density field varies count smoothly and dots stay whole. Sparse star fields, tree masks, ore seeds, crater centres.
[BlueNoiseScatter, stamp-scatter] Evenly spaced, non-overlapping stamps: polka dots, leopard rosettes, pebbles in a creek bed, trees seen from above, acne/pore patterns, bubbles, lily pads, with the characteristic blue-noise regularity of nature instead of the clumpy jittered-grid look (plain Scatter has frequent near-collisions and bare patches). Soft Spacing gives graded sizes that fill the plane like a packed pebble bed.
ideas.why_new: godot-proposals #9690 asks for point placement inside FastNoiseLite for rocks, twigs, ores and trees, with fixed positions across runs; a maintainer suggests Poisson. Current workaround is noise threshold, hard to tune, clumped, and can cut features in half. Voxel Tools describes rehashing neighbour blocks by hand to place trees. CellularDistance can't drop points or guarantee spacing. Only a small hash window is needed: this makes a global-looking algorithm local.
ideas.simd_plan:
2D: 25 hashes into arrays, 9x8 distance compares (pairs could share), masks ANDed, then F1 over survivors with Select. Estimated AVX2: 15 to 20 ns, about 4x CellularDistance; scalar not benchmarked. Density hybrid at candidates: 9 evaluations if blockers skip density check (blockers then always block, slightly lower density, no flicker) or 25 for exact. 3D: 125 hashes, 27x26 compares, about 60 to 90 ns; cut to 6 face neighbours if needed. 4D impractical: thinning disabled, jitter only.
[BlueNoiseScatter, stamp-scatter] Hash + feature point for 4^d cells (2D 16 x ~15 ops), 2^d x (3^d - 1) distance tests (2D 4 x 8 = 32 tests x ~8 ops), then the normal Scatter stamping of 2^d candidates with the dead mask folded into presence. 2D ~+2 ns over Scatter, 3D +~10 ns (64 hashes, 8 x 26 tests), 4D +~60 ns (256 hashes, 16 x 80 tests), so 4D should offer an 'axis neighbours only' reduced test. Fully branch free; loop counts fixed.
ideas.continuity: Continuous: survival is a property of the candidate alone (density read at the candidate, not the sample), so no flicker across space. Profile output C1 with compact support. Distance C0 like F1.
ideas.params: Everything in Scatter plus Spacing (0..1-Jitter), Soft Spacing bool, Density hybrid (still at stamp centre; density thinning composes with hard-core thinning).
ideas.risks:
Matérn II thinning loses ~30-40% of candidates at Spacing near 1, so maximum achievable density is lower than Scatter's; expose that. 4D cost. The 3^d neighbourhood completeness proof depends on the Spacing clamp, which must be enforced in the setter.
[PoissonScatter, repo-demand] One round leaves gaps compared to maximal Poisson disk, though prototype looks good. 3D and 4D costs high. Radius has to stay in the 3x3 window. Hybrid density evaluated at other positions multiplies cost.
ideas.variant_notes: Matern II thinning from hashes alone. PoissonScatter gives the demand evidence (rocks, trees, ore; godot-proposals 9690) and its density-at-candidate rule avoids flicker.
ideas.cost_note: Estimated AVX2: 15 to 20 ns, about 4x CellularDistance; scalar not benchmarked. 3D: 125 hashes, 27x26 compares, about 60 to 90 ns; cut to 6 face neighbours if needed.

ideas.name: BoulderField3D
ideas.one_liner: A volumetric Scatter specialised to signed distance stamps: randomly rotated superellipsoid boulders (and their 2D/4D analogues) combined with a polynomial smooth-min into an approximate SDF, so a threshold gives rubble, scree, debris in caves, asteroid interiors and rock walls with individual stones.
ideas.algorithm:
Scatter lattice in 3D (2^3 = 8 cells, rAllow rule). Per stamp: centre, Shoemake quaternion rotation from 3 hash uniforms, axis radii (a,b,c) = s * (1 + Aspect*rnd11) each, superellipse exponent e per node (2..8), per-stamp low-harmonic bumps: rEff = r*(1 + Bump*(rnd11*cos2 + rnd11*cos3 + rnd11*sin2)) using cosines of the local azimuth from (x/r, y/r) via the Chebyshev recurrence, plus a polar term from z/r (Legendre P2) for 3D lumpiness.
SDF per stamp: d_i = (|x/a|^e + |y/b|^e + |z/c|^e)^(1/e) - 1 scaled back by s (approximate distance, exact for e=2 after the usual sphere correction), minus the bump term.
Combine: smooth min with polynomial k: h = clamp(0.5 + 0.5*(d2 - d1)/k, 0, 1); d = lerp(d2, d1, h) - k*h*(1-h), folded over the 8 stamps; Background = Scatter's empty value is +rAllow (far). Output modes: SDF (raw signed distance, clamped to [-1,1] via ScaleOutput of [-s, rAllow]), Inside (smoothstep(-Edge, Edge, -d) = a density mask), Height2D (in 2D, the SDF interpreted as a height: boulders from above with correct silhouettes).
2D: superellipses; 4D: superellipsoid with 4 radii and two-plane rotation (so tiling works); the smooth-min is dimension free.
Optional ground coupling when used as terrain: because the output is a distance, Max(terrain, -d*height) places boulders on a terrain built elsewhere; the Scatter density hybrid (evaluated at the stamp centre, e.g. a slope mask of the terrain) controls where stones appear.
ideas.look: Individual stones with flat-ish faces (high e) or rounded pebbles (e=2), embedded or piled, each rotated differently; in 3D slices, discrete blobs of varying ellipticity; thresholded 3D: caves with rubble floors, boulder fields on asteroids, conglomerate rock cross sections, cobbled beds. SDF output also drives distance-based effects (moss in the crevices via Remap of d). The contact sheet has only smooth noises and cells; there are no bodies with silhouettes in 3D.
ideas.why_new: The generic Scatter node could compose this from Stamp(Boulder) with Min, but the specialised version is worth it: it keeps SDF semantics correct (smooth-min with a distance, not a value), builds the 3D rotation and harmonic bumps once per stamp, and avoids a virtual call per cell. SDF output is also a new kind of signal for FastNoise (usable for ray marching / voxel placement), which no node currently provides.
ideas.simd_plan: 3D: 8 cells x (2 hashes, quaternion build ~25 ops, rotate ~20, superellipse with Pow ~40, bumps ~20, smooth-min ~12) ~ 140 ops per cell, ~15-18 ns on AVX2 (close to Cellular 3D). 2D ~5 ns, 4D 16 cells ~45 ns. e=2 fast path avoids Pow. All branch free; Octaves give graded rubble sizes with the D^-2 law.
ideas.continuity: C1 (smooth-min of C1 distances except on the superellipsoid ridges where it is C0 for e>2); the rAllow clamp keeps it seamless.
ideas.params: Feature Scale, Size, Size Jitter, Aspect, Exponent, Bump, Smoothness k, Jitter, Density hybrid (at centre), Octaves, Output enum SDF/Inside/Height, Edge, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks: Approximate SDF (superellipsoid distance is not exact for e != 2), fine for thresholds, slightly off for ray marching. Pow cost; e fixed per node so can precompute 1/e. Overlaps with Scatter+Stamp functionally; justify by cost and SDF correctness or fold into Stamp(Boulder) + Scatter(Min) if the generic path proves fast enough.
ideas.cost_note: 3D: 8 cells x (2 hashes, quaternion build ~25 ops, rotate ~20, superellipse with Pow ~40, bumps ~20, smooth-min ~12) ~ 140 ops per cell, ~15-18 ns on AVX2 (close to Cellular 3D).

ideas.name: CellFrame
ideas.one_liner: Runs any source graph in a different frame per Voronoi grain (rotation, stretch, scale, seed) with a seam-free two-sample blend; a guide source turns the grains into flow-aligned texture without integration.
ideas.algorithm: Search window for F1,F2,F3 (d0<=d1<=d2) and hashes/seed positions. Blend: t=(d2-d1)/((d2-d0)+(d2-d1)+eps), which is exactly 0.5 when d0=d1 and exactly 0 when d1=d2, so the second sample fades out before its identity can change. w=0.5*sat((t-(0.5-Width))/Width). Frame per grain from hash: unit axis n, scale f; q=(p+(Aniso-1)*n*dot(n,p))*f. Output=(1-w)*Source(seed^h0,q0)+w*Source(seed^h1,q1). Guided mode: n=normalized gradient of Guide by finite difference at the grain's seed position, optionally with a small angle jitter from hash; high frequency across the gradient makes streaks run along Guide's contours. Frame comes from one point per grain and is constant within it, so nothing shears, however wild the guide.
ideas.look: Random mode: fibre bundles, woven patches, metal grains, feathers, brushed-metal tiles. Guided mode: fur, wind streaks, wood grain and hair flowing around the contours of another noise, a line integral convolution look at a fixed cost.
ideas.why_new: CellularLookup samples at the cell centre but cannot transform a graph's domain per cell. A per-pixel rotation or stretch shears far from the origin; picking the frame per grain avoids that entirely. It gives Source graphs orientation fields, which FastNoise has no way to express now.
ideas.simd_plan: One window pass extended to F3 (about 15% over CellularDistance), then 2 Source evals with per-lane position and seed. The axis stretch is dimension agnostic. With Source=FBm 3 octaves: about 11 / 30 / 75 ns in 2D/3D/4D. Guided adds 2*(D+1) guide evals, so a cheap guide is required, about +15 ns in 2D with a 2-octave guide.
ideas.continuity: C0 everywhere except for a bounded singular point at exact triple junctions where the weight is undefined, invisible on the sheets. Measured c0ratio 2.0-2.3, but the sources are highly stretched and steep, so that metric does not separate seam from slope here; run a dedicated seam test before trusting it. No visible seams on the sheets.
ideas.params: Source (generator), Guide (optional generator), Cell Scale, Aniso, Scale Jitter, Angle Jitter, Blend Width, Grid Jitter.
ideas.risks: The proto used a 5x5 window; at 3x3 an incorrect F3 at full jitter could cause small jumps, so limit Jitter to about 0.7. Guided mode has sign flips of n harmlessly, since stretch is even in n. At guide critical points the gradient is near 0 and direction is arbitrary. Cross-fades lose contrast slightly in borders.
ideas.cost_note: Guided adds 2*(D+1) guide evals, so a cheap guide is required, about +15 ns in 2D with a 2-octave guide.

ideas.name: CellularFacet
ideas.one_liner: First-order CellularLookup: each cell becomes the tangent plane of the source at its centre, turning any field into low-poly chipped rock.
ideas.algorithm: Closest site c in the 3^dim window, d=p-c. v0=Source(c); g_a=(Source(c+e*axis_a)-v0)/e. out=v0+Slope*dot(g,d). Slope 0 equals CellularLookup. Slope 1 is a tangent facet. Slope>1 exaggerates into chips. Sources are evaluated only at the selected site per lane, so count is dim+1 regardless of window.
ideas.look: Faceted crystal or chipped stone over any terrain, low-poly stylised landscape. FBm with cell scale 2-3.5x feature gives rock chip fields. Matches Substance Crystal's angular character and C4D Displaced Voronoi's chipped feel by description. Prototype: dcc_lens mode=19.
ideas.why_new: Sheet's CellularLookup is piecewise constant and terraced; this is piecewise linear, so shading varies inside each cell. Not expressible: graph cannot evaluate a source at a cell centre and its neighbours and then form a plane. Low-poly on an arbitrary source is otherwise a mesh operation.
ideas.simd_plan: Cellular window plus D+2 taps at the site, where sites differ per lane, which is fine since positions are per lane. 2D 3.9+4.4 = about 8 ns, 3D 12+11 = about 23 ns, 4D 41+26 = about 67 ns on Perlin. Scalar prototype 6.2x perlin2 with the harness's 5x5 search. C0 variant roughly adds D+2 taps.
ideas.continuity: Discontinuous at cell borders, measured c0ratio 1.00; jump size scales with curvature*cell^2, and looks like hard chips rather than noise. Interior is C-infinity (plane).
ideas.params: Lookup (GeneratorSource), Feature Scale, Grid Jitter (hybrid), Slope (hybrid), Distance Function, Epsilon (float), Lookup Frequency.
ideas.risks:
Not continuous, so displacement has cracks; small jump when cells are small relative to source features. Far coordinate FD precision. Slope>1 amplifies out of range.
[CellularTangentHold, graph-meta-filters] Steep source with big cells gives large jumps and output beyond the source range, so clamp or Remap. Needs a site position output from the cellular search, which is in hand in Cellular.inl.
ideas.variant_notes: Same tangent-plane hold; second-order Curve term and a C0 blend band come from CellularTangentHold.
ideas.cost_note: 2D 3.9+4.4 = about 8 ns, 3D 12+11 = about 23 ns, 4D 41+26 = about 67 ns on Perlin. Scalar prototype 6.2x perlin2 with the harness's 5x5 search.

ideas.name: CellularPatchwork
ideas.one_liner: Each Voronoi cell gets its own rotated, offset and reseeded copy of the source, with a K-nearest partition of unity that is provably continuous for fixed K evals.
ideas.algorithm:
Search window for sorted F1..F(K+1) with cell centres and hashes. For i<=K: w_i = (F(K+1)-F_i)^Sharpness. value = sum w_i * S( R(h_i)*(p-c_i) + off(h_i), seed^h_i ) / sum w_i. Continuity: swapping cells among the top K is symmetric, and swapping K with K+1 happens where w_K = 0. Denominator vanishes only if F1..F(K+1) are all equal, a codimension-K set: K=3 in 2D never hits it generically, K=2 only at isolated Voronoi vertices where the value stays bounded. K=1 is the hard-edged mode (1 eval, intentional jump). Per-cell params: rotation (random or quantised to N), mirror bit, scale jitter, offset.

[CellularPatchwork, lit-classic] Run the 3^d F1 search, keep per-lane best site vector d1, hash h1 (and d2,h2, F3 for seams).
u=Rot(rnd(h1)*Rotation)*(x-site1)*Scale(h1)+Offset*rnd2(h1).
Result=Source(seed+SeedStep*h1,u).
Seam>0: evaluate the 3 nearest sites, w_i=saturate(1-(F_i-F1)/Seam)^2, normalise, blend. Source=SineWave: per-cell stripes. Source=Gradient: per-cell tilted plane (facets). Source=FBm with axis scale: oriented grain.
ideas.look:
Polycrystal or foliated metamorphic rock: patches of strata or grain at different angles meeting at sharp (K=1) or soft (K=2,3) grain boundaries. Also metal grain, wood parquet, cracked ice, camouflage, kaleidoscope cells if each cell folds. Prototyped: mode=4, K=1 and K=3.
[CellularPatchwork, lit-classic] Prototype cl_cell modes 2-4: rotated stripes per polygon like plywood or metallographic grains or farmland; stretched fbm with seams gives hair or fur patches; facets look like shattered tinted glass with crisp creases under hillshade. Biome plates, flagstones where each stone has its own texture, tectonic masks.
[CellularGrain, math-physics] Etched polycrystal metallography (pearlite lamellae, each grain with its own stripe direction), mica schist, crystalline ice, wood knots mosaics, Voronoi stained-glass with hatching; 3D slices show planar lamellae inside each grain, like real lamellar colonies.
ideas.why_new: CellularLookup samples the source at the site, so each cell is flat. No graph can feed a per-cell rotation into a subtree's coordinates. Worley's flagstone-like tiled areas and PPTBF's per-cell feature functions both want this, and SIMD suits it because the Source call count is fixed regardless of which cell each lane is in.
ideas.simd_plan: CellularDistance-style window with a small sorting network to F(K+1), storing centre and hash for top K, then K source evals with per-lane seed (seed is int32v, so reseeding per lane is free). About 6 ns plus K*source in 2D, 15 ns plus K*source in 3D, 45 ns plus K*source in 4D (estimates). Rotation: sin/cos of hash or a small table of unit pairs. 3D: 24 cube rotations table, or Rodrigues about hash axis. 4D: two plane rotations.
ideas.continuity: K>=2: C0 (measured c0ratio 7.96 at K=3), Sharpness>=2 gives smooth weights except at top-K swaps. K=1: discontinuous on purpose (c0ratio 1.2).
ideas.params: Blend Count K (1-3), Sharpness (hybrid), Rotation Amount, Rotation Steps, Offset Amount, Reseed flag, Grid Jitter, Cell Size, Source.
ideas.risks:
Prototype searched 5x5. In a 3x3 port F4 is exact only for jitter up to about 0.3, and F3 up to about 0.4; beyond that tiny seams can appear. Blending lowers contrast near boundaries; K=3 with Sharpness 2 looks fairly soft, so raise Sharpness. Cost is K times source, so wrap around a cheap source or keep K=2.
[CellPatchDomain, cell-relations] Soft blends reduce contrast like any cross-fade. Seeding per cell multiplies effective source variety, which may surprise users with GeneratorCache sources. Isotropic sources show little beyond faint seams.
ideas.variant_notes: Nine proposals: source evaluated in the nearest Voronoi cell's rotated, offset, reseeded frame. Continuity options: K=1 hard, K=2 or 3 by rank-subtract partition of unity, or F2-F1 fade. CellularGrain is the built-in-stripes preset (per-grain lamellae, twin bands), cheaper than a general source call.
ideas.cost_note: About 6 ns plus K*source in 2D, 15 ns plus K*source in 3D, 45 ns plus K*source in 4D (estimates).

ideas.name: ExchangeFoam
ideas.one_liner: Evaluate K seeds of any source and take argmax: each label gets exactly 1/K of the area with no calibration, and the interfaces form an organic lattice-free cell foam.
ideas.algorithm: s_k = Source(seed + k*prime, p), k = 0..K-1. Identically distributed fields are exchangeable, so P(argmax = k) = 1/K for any source and any histogram, and rank(s_0) is exactly uniform on 0..K-1. Track m1 and m2 (largest and second largest) and the label with Select. Outputs: Label = k/(K-1) mapped to [-1,1] or a hash of k; Margin = clamp((m1 - m2)*Gain); Rank = sum_{k>=1} smoothstep(-eps, eps, s_0 - s_k). Weighted shares (theory, not run): for sources with exactly uniform marginals, transform each to Gumbel with -log(-log(u)) and add log(w_k); the Gumbel-max property then gives exact shares w_k / sum w.
ideas.look: Label: camouflage-like blobby mosaics with triple junctions where any label can touch any other, unlike a thresholded single noise where only value-adjacent bands touch. Margin: organic crackle foam, with non-convex cells and no lattice or point sites. Rank: stacked plateaus with soft steps. Good for biome maps, camouflage, cracked mud and multi-material masks. Measured area per label for K=5: 0.199 to 0.201 on oct 1 and oct 5 sources and two seeds.
ideas.why_new: Biome coverage normally comes from tuning thresholds per source. This gives exact equal shares regardless of source, including warped and fractal graphs, with no measurement. Max can get the top value but no node exposes the winner index or margin. It gives a cellular look without feature points.
ideas.simd_plan: Fixed K, K source evals. Masked update of m1, m2 and label, no per-lane branching. Cost K x source; K=5 Perlin measured 7.5x perlin2 scalar. Dimension and tiling come from the source. Uses seed offsets, so the source graph must respond to seed.
ideas.continuity: Label is discontinuous by design, like CellularValue. Margin is C0 with a kink at interfaces. Rank is C1 with eps > 0.
ideas.params: Phases K (int), Output (Label, Margin, Rank), Margin Gain (hybrid), Softness (float), Seed Stride (int), Source. Up to 4 float weights if the Gumbel mode is added.
ideas.risks: Exactness is about the field's stationary law, so a source with a spatial trend or a fixed-seed sub-node shared between phases loses it. Cost scales with K. Soft rank at large K blurs towards the mean. Gumbel shares need exactly uniform inputs (PhaseVortex) or a good CoverageRemap, and are untested. Margin has no fixed relation to distance, so cell wall widths vary.
ideas.cost_note: Cost K x source; K=5 Perlin measured 7.5x perlin2 scalar.

queue.name: ExchangeFoam
queue.reason: argmax over K seeded sources gives exact 1/K shares: lattice-free biome labels, trivially SIMD. Judges split on wow, so the Label mode needs a look.

ideas.name: GroundedScatter
ideas.one_liner: 3D stamps that sit on a heightfield source: rocks, hoodoos and stumps placed on terrain inside a density graph, pointwise, with no decoration pass.
ideas.algorithm: 3D sample (x,y,z), Up axis y. Column lattice in XZ only: window 3x3 (9 cells), not 27. For each column cell: hash h, centre (cx,cz) with jitter; ground height g = Height.Gen(seed, cx, cz), one eval per cell, at the feature rather than the sample. Stamp centre c = (cx, g + Sink*r, cz). Local d = p-c, optionally squashed in y. Tilt option: 2 extra Height evals per cell for a finite-difference normal, 27 evals in total, then rotate d into the slope frame so stones lie flush. Shape: analytic sphere or superellipsoid SDF, or capsule from (cx,g-Depth,cz) to (cx,g+Tall,cz) for pillars, or top-K Source in local coords for detailed rocks. Combine by Max SDF, or K=1 for the nearest. Union with the terrain density as usual: Output = max(terrainDensity, stampDensity) or Output only the stamps. Slope and altitude rules: alive = rnd<Density and g in [Min,Max], decided per feature with the same g, so nothing pops. 2D: side-view 1D column lattice with height from 1D line of Source. 4D: column lattice in x,z,w, 27 cells.
ideas.look: Boulders, hoodoos, dolmen fields and tree-trunk stumps that are actually attached to the terrain's surface and follow it in 3D volumes, with undercut overhangs. Not prototyped: the look is inferred, and should be tested first.
ideas.why_new: Voxel engines do this with a post-generation decoration pass that needs world state and chunk-border handling, which FastNoise's stateless model cannot do. Using column lattice and feature-centre height eval lets a density graph do it pointwise, with no seams at chunk borders. A hard thing made easy, and a very common request.
ideas.simd_plan: 9 column hashes + 9 Height evals (9x height source; with a 5-octave FBm Perlin ~50 ns, tilt triples this) + 9 SDF. Using column lattice is 3x cheaper than a 3D window; no Y search needed because each column holds exactly one stamp (a Stack Count constant gives more). Add GeneratorCache-like reuse is not possible across cells. Cost estimate 3D: ~5 ns + 9*Height + SDFs. 2D ~ 3 Height evals. Tiling with 4D is costly: 27*Height.
ideas.continuity: C0 for SDF or bump output that reaches zero at stamp reach and only depends on feature values. Height needs to be pure and non-sample-dependent, which it is at the column centre. A tall reach above 1 cell in y is fine because the column window is XZ only.
ideas.params: Height (GeneratorSource), Up Axis enum, Density (hybrid at feature), Size, Size Jitter, Sink, Squash, Shape enum, Tilt (bool, 3x evals), Min/Max Altitude, Stack Count, Source (optional detail)
ideas.risks: Unverified by prototype. 9 Height evals may be heavy for deep graphs, so an artist should feed a low-octave version to placement. Height must match the terrain the density graph really uses, or stones float; expose a shared Source. Only heightfield-like; cave walls need 27+ evals per Newton step, so left out.
ideas.cost_note: 9 column hashes + 9 Height evals (9x height source; with a 5-octave FBm Perlin ~50 ns, tilt triples this) + 9 SDF.
