ideas.name: QuadStamp
ideas.one_liner: Stamps with sizes spanning orders of magnitude and no window at all: hash-driven quadtree descent to a leaf, then 1 stamp inside the leaf, linear in depth and same cost in 4D.
ideas.algorithm: scale = 1, alive = all lanes. For d in 0..Depth-1 (constant count): i = floor(p*scale); h = hash(i, level d); leaf coords (for alive lanes) = p*scale - i - 0.5, saved via Select with leaf hash and leaf scale. alive &= rnd(h) < SplitProbability(d); scale = Select(alive, scale*2, scale). The result is one leaf per lane with lx in [-0.5,0.5]^dim. Stamp lies strictly inside the leaf: mask m = (1-t^2)^3 with t = |l-j|/(0.4*R), j = jitter bounded so that j+0.4R < 0.5. Output = m * Source.Gen(seed=h, Rot(h)*l*Zoom)/sqrt(scale)^Roughness, or analytic dome; also output leaf size as a mask. Hybrid SplitProbability sampled at the leaf's centre gives density-driven refinement: fine stamps where the source says.
ideas.look: Prototype: large spots surrounded by clusters of small ones with a visible quadtree order; reads like tech greeble, circuit boards, mitotic cells, city blocks and starfields. Axis-aligned parent grouping is visible and is a signature; not an organic look unless warped or rotated.
ideas.why_new: Sizes spanning 1:32 in a window-based scatter would need a separate lattice per size and a window for each. Here it costs Depth hashes plus 1 Source eval, regardless of dimension. Fractal octaves stack everywhere and cannot drop large features where small ones go; this partitions space by level.
ideas.simd_plan: Loop of Depth iterations with floor, hash and masks: Depth=5 is ~5 hashes (~3 ns) + 1 stamp, in every dimension. 2D, 3D and 4D all ~4-6 ns + Source, the cheapest node here and the only scatter with no exponential window cost. Tiling via 4D is free of penalty. Rotation per stamp local.
ideas.continuity: C0: c0ratio 7.90 at depth 1 and 6.13 at depth 3, falling to 3.23 at depth 5 because tiny stamps have very steep slopes, not jumps. Requires mask reaching zero inside the leaf, enforced by bounding jitter + radius.
ideas.params: Depth (int), Split Probability (hybrid), Split Falloff per depth, Stamp Radius, Jitter, Rotation, Roughness (amplitude vs size), Source (optional), Output enum (stamp, leaf size, leaf hash)
ideas.risks: Axis-aligned hierarchy is visible, and DomainRotate only hides the absolute axis, not the squareness of the arrangement. Layer two rotated instances with Max to help. Stamps cannot cross leaf borders, so never overlap and coverage has a visible gridded gap structure. Hybrid split with a lane-position sample would seam: must sample at the leaf centre, adding Depth Source evals.
ideas.cost_note: 2D, 3D and 4D all ~4-6 ns + Source, the cheapest node here and the only scatter with no exponential window cost.

queue.reason: Hash quadtree descent to one leaf stamp: 1:32 size range, no window, 4-6 ns at any dimension. Square hierarchy shows, so try two rotated layers.

ideas.name: RayMarch
ideas.one_liner: Fixed-count march of a source along a direction (or along an added dimension): projected density, Beer-Lambert transmittance, or soft first-hit depth giving the heightfield of a 3D isosurface (cliffs and mesas).
ideas.algorithm:
Source S; Axis enum: Direction (in-plane vector, same dimension) or Extra (march along an added coordinate: a d-dim node evaluates S in d+1 dims, exactly AddDimension semantics; not available for 4D nodes).
  T = 1; acc = 0; depth = 0
  for k in 0..N-1:
      s = S(q_k) where q_k = p + (Start + k*h)*dir  (Extra: (p, Start + k*h))
      Mean          : acc += s
      Transmittance : acc += max(0, s - Thresh)
      FirstHit      : a = smoothstep(Thresh - soft, Thresh + soft, s); depth += T*(k*h); T *= (1 - a)   // expected depth of first crossing
  Mean: acc/N ; Transmittance: exp(-Density*h*acc) ; FirstHit: depth + T*(N*h)  (remapped)
Step lengths may grow geometrically (h*g^k) to reach far cheaply.
ideas.look:
Mean along an in-plane direction: directional smear / motion-blur streaks. Mean/Transmittance along the extra axis: 2D map of the thickness of a 3D cloud volume, with the characteristic smoother-yet-holey cloud layer look and Beer-law contrast. FirstHit along the extra axis with a 3D fBm: the top surface of a 3D isosurface seen from above: flat-topped mesas, vertical cliffs, arches hidden, canyon mazes; a heightfield that 2D noise can never produce because its walls are vertical and organic (Terrace walls are value-aligned, not shape-aligned).
[FirstHitHeight, dynamics-iteration] Verified in prototype. Smooth rolling surfaces cut by vertical drop edges along overhang silhouettes, flat-topped plateaus and floating-island outlines with sharp contour-like cliffs. Low Bias gives more 3D holes, high Bias gets close to plain noise. Good for cliffs and mesas in a 2D heightmap, canyon lands, layered strata with bias stacking, and masks for overhang placement.
ideas.why_new: N offset evaluations with running products/maxima cannot be built in-graph except by N chained DomainOffset/Add/Multiply nodes. FirstHit in particular turns FastNoise's strong 3D noises into a new class of 2D terrains. One node, three modes, dimension-agnostic in Direction mode.
ideas.simd_plan: Fixed N loop, one source eval per step plus a few FMAs; FirstHit uses only multiplies (no masks). Cost = N x source: N=16 with Simplex3D as the extra-axis source: ~35 ns for a 2D node; with FBm-4 Simplex ~140 ns; Direction mode 2D Perlin N=8: ~9 ns. Extra mode: implement 2D->3D and 3D->4D overloads; 4D node falls back to Direction mode (document it). Tiling: Direction mode preserves GenTileable2D; Extra mode cannot tile (needs 5D).
ideas.continuity: Mean/Transmittance: same class as the source (C0+). FirstHit: continuous for finite Softness (product of smooth factors), tending to jump discontinuities at vertical walls as Softness -> 0, which is the intended cliff look.
ideas.params: Source (GeneratorSource), Mode enum (Mean/Transmittance/FirstHit), Axis enum (Direction/Extra), Direction X/Y/Z/W hybrids, Steps int, StepLen float, StepGrowth float, Start float, Threshold hybrid, Softness float, Density float, VariableRange.
ideas.risks:
Cost for fractal sources; FirstHit needs enough steps to resolve small features (aliasing of thin walls); Extra mode breaks the 4D/tiling story.
[FirstHitHeight, dynamics-iteration] Pinholes at low Steps; the 3D form needs a 4D source so is costly; a true 4D form changes the semantics. Volumetric lit-cloud output was tested as an alternative and was not visibly worth its N*M cost, so stick to height.
ideas.variant_notes: FirstHit along an added axis is the distinctive mode: 3D isosurface top as a heightfield with organic vertical cliffs. Cannot tile, because the extra axis needs a 5th dimension in the 4D path.
ideas.cost_note: Cost = N x source: N=16 with Simplex3D as the extra-axis source: ~35 ns for a 2D node; with FBm-4 Simplex ~140 ns; Direction mode 2D Perlin N=8: ~9 ns.

ideas.name: SplatBurst
ideas.one_liner: Stamps with radius driven by a direction-sampled source: ink splats, spiky shards and, in 3D, solid lumpy asteroids, all without atan2.
ideas.algorithm: Window 3^dim, K top stamps as in StampScatter, or analytic source. For each stamp: d = p-c, r=|d|, unit u=d/r. Sample the angular function by evaluating on the unit circle or sphere, seamless by construction: n = Angular.Gen(seed=h, u.x*F, u.y*F, hashOffset(h)). For 3D use 3D Angular at u*F; offset by seed. Shape: n' = n>0 ? (n^1.5)*Spike : n*Dent. Radius rad = R0(h)*(1+Amp*n'); clamp to <=1 cell. Output m = 1 - smoothstep(rad-Sharp, rad, r), or SDF-like value (rad-r) for 3D density. Analytic fast mode: Chebyshev: n' = cos(N*theta) = Re((u.x+i u.y)^N) computed via integer-count complex power with constant N, for stars and flowers (no Source eval at all). Mask out r<epsilon: r near 0 is always inside rad so direction singularity is hidden.
ideas.look: Prototype: jagged ink blots, spiky splats, blood or paint splatter, lichens, burst shapes. With 3D density: rocks and asteroids with star-shaped solid shape, closed surface, no floating fragments. Analytic N mode gives flowers and stars.
ideas.why_new: Threshold of noise never gives a star-shaped single-connected object with a defined centre; radial spikes do not come from isotropic noise. Sampling on the unit sphere means no polar coordinate seam and no atan2.
ideas.simd_plan: Scan cost plus K (1-3) Angular source evals, or analytic Chebyshev in constant N with 3^dim cells. 2D at K=2: 5 ns scan + 2 Perlin3 ~10 ns. 3D at K=2: 15 ns + 2*Perlin3 ~20 ns. 4D: u is 4D, Angular 4D, K=2, ~55 ns. Using max across K with rank-subtract as in StampScatter.
ideas.continuity: C0 with Sharp>0: c0ratio 2.85 at Sharp 0.05 (steep) and 6.36 at Sharp 0.15, with max slope 265 from narrow spike walls. In 3D density output, slope is bounded when returning rad-r.
ideas.params: Angular Source or Star Count N (enum), Amp, Spike Exponent, Dent, Base Radius (hybrid), Sharp, K, Output enum (mask, radial SDF)
ideas.risks: Spike tips are clamped by the 1-cell reach, so they flatten at high Amp, unless Base Radius is reduced. Near-centre angular gradient is singular but hidden only if rad is always positive, so require Amp*Dent < 1. Fast-mode N must be a member, not per-lane.
ideas.cost_note: 2D at K=2: 5 ns scan + 2 Perlin3 ~10 ns. 3D at K=2: 15 ns + 2*Perlin3 ~20 ns.

ideas.name: StampScatter
ideas.one_liner: Use any node as a stamp: scan the window cheaply, then evaluate Source only K times per lane, with a rank-subtract fade so swapping candidates cannot pop.
ideas.algorithm:
Lattice = unit cells, window 3^dim. For each window cell: hash h, centre c = cell + 0.5 + Jitter*(rnd-0.5), radius r = Size*lerp(SizeMin,1,rnd) (clamp so reach <= 1 cell), d = p - c, mask m = (1 - sat(|d|^2/r^2))^3, multiplied by alive = rnd < Density. Per-lane partial selection (the same insertion-with-Select used by Cellular for F1..F4) keeps the K+1 largest masks with their d, r and h in K+1 register slots. Then wK = max(0, m_k - m_(K+1)): each kept stamp fades to exactly zero at the moment it would lose its slot, so the result stays C0 whatever K is. For k in 0..K-1 (constant loop): rotate d by the hash angle (2D: rational or table cos/sin; 3D: unit quaternion from hash bits), l = R*d/r, v_k = Source.Gen(seed = h_k, l...). Note that the seed and position differ per lane, which Gen already supports. Combine: Sum = sum(w_k v_k); Variance-preserving = sum(w v)/sqrt(sum w^2); PNorm max = (sum (w v)^4)^(1/4) via two sqrts. Polynomial MinSmooth/MaxSmooth is not associative, so it is order dependent and seams when the slot order changes; p-norm and sum are order independent and contribute exactly 0 at w=0. Density has two modes: AtCentre (Density source evaluated at c for each window cell, gives whole stamps, costs 3^dim evals) or AtSample (one eval at p, r *= density(p), stamps erode smoothly, 1 eval). Optional Source B/C/D with a hash-picked bank: every bank member is evaluated at each K slot and Selected.

[StampField, lit-classic] For layer l (scale Ratio^l), cell c in 3^d window: h=hash; site=c+.5+.7*(rnd-.5); radius Rr=lerp(Rmin,Rmax,rnd); r2=|x_l-site|^2/Rr^2; if r2<1 candidate.
u=Rot(rnd*Rotation)*(x_l-site)/Rr.
Sum: v+=G_i*(1-r2)^2*Source(seed^h,u).
Max: v=max(v,(1-r2)^2*(Source+offset)).
Over: keep per-lane best priority among covering stamps (prio=Layers-l+rnd); after the whole window call Source(seed^h_best,u_best) ONCE for each lane. Soft variant: top-2 and blend by r2.
Density source and Size source may be sampled at stamp centre (one extra eval per candidate) for stable shapes; sampling at x is cheaper.
ideas.look:
Scattered independent copies of any graph: rocks, lichen patches, moss clumps, islands of detail on a flat background, with random rotation and a per-copy seed. Clumped by a density source. Look test with 2-octave Perlin as the stamp reads as separate patches of texture, nothing like FBm.
[StampField, lit-classic] Prototype cl_stamp: hemispheres as a pile of pebbles or balls (dead leaves); Perlin discs as cloud puffs or lichen; stripes as rotated Gabor patches in Sum (classic spot noise) and fish-scale patchwork in Over; ring profiles as bubbles or craters. Layers 3+ close all gaps. Scales, rock litter, foliage clusters, craters, polka dots with jitter 0, and cyclostationary weaves.
ideas.why_new: CellularLookup samples at the site only, so stamps are flat. There is no way to place, rotate or occlude copies of a generator in a graph. Occlusion gives hard-edged, non-Gaussian structure the survey lists as an open direction. Worley's paper names bombing as the pre-basis-function approach; this makes it a pointwise node with any kernel.
ideas.simd_plan: Scan cost is about CellularDistance (9/27/81 cells) plus K+1 register slots of Select; rotation and Source evals happen only for the K winners. Estimate: 2D scan ~5 ns + K*Source; 3D ~15 ns + K*Source; 4D ~50 ns + K*Source. K is a constant int member. Dimension agnostic via GenT pack; 4D keeps GenTileable2D working, though 4D rotation should be reduced to two plane rotations. Stamps larger than a cell: use Feature Scale and accept lower density, because reach is capped at the window.
ideas.continuity: C0 verified in scalar proto: c0ratio 1.00 without the fade and 8.15 with rank-subtract at K=2, same seed. C1 is not guaranteed because of the kink at slot swaps.
ideas.params: Source (GeneratorSource), K (int 1..4), Size (hybrid, AtSample only), SizeMin, Density (hybrid, enum AtCentre/AtSample), Jitter, Rotation amount (hybrid), Mask profile enum, Combine enum, Sample Scale R (stamp zoom), Background constant
ideas.risks:
Low K with many overlaps thins the field, since all weights are reduced by m_(K+1) where stamps are dense. Density AtCentre in 3D is 27 evals of the density source. Range depends on combine mode, so normalise analytically for Sum and accept clamp for others. A source with strong DC offset produces visible discs; a Remove Mean option or an offset would help.
[Scatter, stamp-scatter] Cost multiplies with source cost and dimension (4D Wide = 81 source evals: must warn in the metadata). Hybrids evaluated at the stamp centre is a new convention for hybrids (CellularLookup sets precedent). Hash bits: two hashes per cell needed. Artists will ask for stamps bigger than rAllow; the clamp silently shrinks them, so expose rAllow in the description and suggest Octaves. Sum mode range depends on overlap count; normalise by measured constant per Window.
[StampScatter, repo-demand] Cost explodes for heavy sources (FBm source with 5 octaves: 9x5 octaves). AlphaOver in fixed order needs care to be seed-stable. Not prototyped directly; CellularDomain's look-test covers the transform part.
ideas.variant_notes: Any node as a stamp. Three cost strategies to compare: scan then K top-mask source evals with rank-subtract fade (cheapest C0), Over mode with one eval per lane, and full window x Source for true Sum. Source seed must respond per lane.
ideas.cost_note: Estimate: 2D scan ~5 ns + K*Source; 3D ~15 ns + K*Source; 4D ~50 ns + K*Source.

ideas.name: StochasticPatch
ideas.one_liner: Any node evaluated exactly dim+1 times per lane, in simplex-vertex local frames with variance-preserving or height-based blending: the cheapest way to scatter and to break repetition.
ideas.algorithm:
skew p onto the simplex lattice (same skew constants as Simplex); find the simplex containing p and its D+1 vertices v_j with barycentric weights w_j (linear, sum 1)
  for j in 0..D: h = HashPrimes(v_j)
     off_j = rnd vector in [-OffsetRange, OffsetRange]^D
     R_j  = rotation from hash (2D: (c,s) = rndDir2(h); 3D: hashed unit quaternion; 4D: two hashed plane rotations), scaled by Rotation in [0,1] via slerp toward identity (precompute formula: angle*Rotation)
     sc_j = 2^(rnd11 * ScaleJitter)
     q_j = R_j * (p - v_j) * sc_j + v_j + off_j     // rotate/scale about the vertex so the patch stays near its lattice site
     X_j = Source(q_j)
  W = Sqrt(sum w_j^2)
  out = Mean + sum_j w_j (X_j - Mean) / W        // variance preserving (Heitz-Neyret), Mean param default 0
  optional Sharpen: out = Lerp(out, sign(out)*|out|^Sharpen, s) to restore contrast for non-Gaussian sources

[StochasticPatch, stamp-scatter] Simplex-skew lattice as in Simplex noise: find containing simplex, giving dim+1 vertices, each with weight a = max(0, 0.5-|d|^2)^2 and hash h. For each vertex: frame rotation R(h) and offset O(h); v_i = Source.Gen(seed or h_i, R(h)*p + O(h)). Note that the frame is global at that vertex, not stamp-local: copies are continuous rotated patches of a globally defined pattern. Weights w_i = a_i^Sharpness / sum. Blend Variance mode: sum(w v)/sqrt(sum w^2) (Heitz-Neyret histogram-preserving form). Height mode: w_i = a_i*(1+H*v_i); w_i = max(0, w_i - 0.75*max w); renormalise, so patches interlock along their own contours. Loop count is dim+1 constant; weights are never zero-branch-dependent.
ideas.look:
SineWave becomes a bent, tangled zebra of rotated stripe patches; a plank pattern becomes herringbone chaos; crackle in Height mode becomes interlocked shard mosaics. Prototype with sine, plank and crackle each looked unlike the input and unlike anything on the sheet. Also the standard fix to a visibly periodic or strongly directional source.
[PatchTuft, texture-materials] Look-tested (m=9, Source = stretched fbm). Crisscrossing clumps of straw or brushed patches, tangle of grain direction. Strongly different from the sheet and stays contrasty because the blend does not wash out. Anisotropic Source sets the material: fibres, wood, wave ripples, sand ripple patches; AngleRange small gives subtle hair-flow variation.
ideas.why_new: It is the standard real-time anti-repetition technique for textures, but applied to the procedural graph itself: it needs lattice-driven random frames and d+1 source evaluations with barycentric weights, impossible from existing nodes. Also gives 'Sampled Phacelle'-style per-tile orientation for free when the source is PhasorNoise.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch-free: simplex traversal exactly as in Simplex noise (compare masks, Select), then D+1 Source evaluations with hashed transforms. Cost = (D+1) x Source + ~Simplex overhead: with FBm Simplex 4 as Source, 2D ~3x that source. Dimension-agnostic via the simplex lattice (2D/3D/4D all exact; tiling works).
ideas.continuity: C1 (measured c0ratio 7.99, the cleanest of the batch) if the kernel falls to zero at its support boundary and Source is continuous. Normalisation denominator cannot reach 0 since at least one kernel is nonzero everywhere.
ideas.params: Source, Rotation amount (hybrid), Offset amount, Sharpness, Blend enum (Variance/Height), Height Influence, Per-vertex seed toggle, Scale jitter
ideas.risks:
Known technique in texture synthesis, though unknown as a graph node. Simplex 3D/4D kernels at radius 0.5 and 0.6 need care so a weight is zero at simplex boundaries (handbook notes small jumps in Simplex at 0.6). Rotation breaks the Source's axis-dependent meaning (e.g. terrain slope), which is the point, but needs a Max Angle param. Low-frequency sources show less.
[StochasticPatchBlend, hierarchy-multiscale] Binary/high-contrast sources blur in blend zones (Heitz solves with a Gaussianising histogram transform, which we cannot do on a black-box node; Sharpen is the pragmatic fix). Rotation of anisotropic lattices (Perlin) can expose the Source's own grid at some angles; fine for Simplex sources.
[SimplexTileBlend, terrain-tools-engines] Variance-preserving blend assumes roughly Gaussian source statistics (binary sources like Checkerboard get overshoot: clamp); 3x source cost in 2D, 4x in 3D; large OffsetRange with far coordinates eats float precision (keep offsets modest and let the source's own hash decorrelate).
ideas.variant_notes: Heitz-Neyret blending of d+1 transformed source evals on the simplex lattice. Best in tests with anisotropic sources (PatchTuft straw, stripes as tangled zebra). Height-based blending interlocks patches. Binary sources blur in blend zones.
ideas.cost_note: Cost = (D+1) x Source + ~Simplex overhead: with FBm Simplex 4 as Source, 2D ~3x that source.

queue.name: StochasticPatch
queue.reason: Simplex-vertex local frames with a variance-preserving blend: D+1 evals, the cheapest repetition breaker. Known technique, so a quick port is enough.

ideas.name: StreakScatter
ideas.one_liner: Long, randomly oriented ribbons that are several cells long without breaking the window rule: K orientation layers, each with its own anisotropic (stretched) lattice aligned to that layer's direction, each cell holding one elongated stamp that fits its long cell.
ideas.algorithm:
Layers k = 0..K-1 (K is an int param, fixed loop), direction angle a_k = pi*k/K + LayerJitter(seed,k) (constant per layer, computed when params are set or from a hash of k). For each layer: rotate p into the layer frame (u along a_k, v across), scale u by 1/Length so the lattice cell is Length x 1 in world units. Run the Scatter 2^2 window in (u,v). Each stamp is a capsule/ribbon: local coords q = (u', v'/Width) with per-stamp small angle jitter (+/- pi/(2K)) applied before the lattice lookup, per-stamp length fraction in [0.5,1], per-stamp seed. Stamp profile: gaussian across the ribbon, smooth taper along it (optionally a Source node evaluated in the ribbon frame, e.g. a 1D-ish Perlin along u for bristle wobble), optional along-ribbon sine for scratches. Combine stamps within a layer and across layers by Max/Sum/SmoothMax.
3D: directions on the sphere via a fixed set of K unit vectors (Fibonacci sphere, table), lattice stretched along each; stamps are capsules in 3D (hairs, roots, needles). 4D: use the 3D directions and treat w as a 4th unstretched lattice axis (tiling works).
Why it is seamless: in the layer frame every stamp is confined to a 1 x 1 lattice cell exactly as in Scatter; the stretch happens in the domain, not in the stamp.

[ScratchLayers, stamp-scatter] For layer l in Layers (constant): table rotation a_l chosen at param set. u = (cos a x - sin a y)/Spacing + o_u, v = (sin a x + cos a y)/(Spacing*A) + o_v. Cell (iu,iv), window 3x3. Each cell: alive if rnd<Prob; centre cu = iu + 0.25 + 0.5*rnd, cv = iv + rnd; slope s in +-0.3 and bend b in +-0.15 cells over the unit v, chosen so lateral excursion stays below 1 cell (essential for seamlessness). Curve line: u0(v) = cu + s*(v-cv) + b*(v-cv)^2; half length hl in [0.25,0.95] of a long cell; tv = (v-cv)/hl. Width w = Thick*(power-law random)*sat(1-tv^2). dist = |u-u0|. Profile = sat(1-dist/(w+soft))*sat(1-tv^2). Combine by max across all. 3D: lattice 1x1xA (27 cells per layer), distance sqrt(du^2+dw^2) gives rods, fibers, needles.
ideas.look:
Prototype at 6 layers: crossed hairline scratches, tapered, varying brightness, like brushed metal, sword wear, straw, pine needles, rain, cross-hatching. Long continuous structures of a kind no isotropic node makes, and the staple missing mask for material work.
[StreakScatter, stamp-scatter] Brush strokes, scratches on metal, wood splinters, grass blades, hatching, rain streaks on glass, needle beds, fibre mats, frost feathers; K=1 gives a combed/hair look, K=4 gives criss-cross scratches, K=8 looks isotropic. Elongated features with random orientation and visible ends are absent from the contact sheet (DomainAxisScale gives stretched noise but every feature is parallel and endless).
ideas.why_new: A long oriented feature cannot fit a square lattice window, so plain Scatter cannot do it, and DomainAxisScale on a noise makes all features parallel. Quantising orientation into K layers and stretching each layer's lattice is the trick that keeps it pointwise. Gabor noise does something related with a Poisson process but produces sine blobs, not shaped strokes with ends.
ideas.simd_plan: K x (2D: 4 cells) with ~50 ops per cell; K=4 in 2D ~5 ns, K=8 ~10 ns. 3D K x 8 cells, K=6 ~30 ns. Layer frames are precomputed when params are set (rotation matrices in a small table). Branch free; K is a fixed loop count. Per-stamp angle jitter is a small rotation inside the cell, kept within the cell by reducing the stamp length fraction accordingly.
ideas.continuity: C0 verified: c0ratio 7.87 after limiting lateral excursion; first version with excursion above the window gave real seams (c0ratio 1.04), confirming the constraint.
ideas.params: Layers int K, Length (cells), Width, Angle Jitter, Length Jitter, Taper, Profile enum (Gaussian/Flat/Sine scratch/Source), Source (optional), Combine enum, Density hybrid (sampled at stamp centre), Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks:
K orientation classes are visible at small K (hatching look) — fine for most uses, add LayerJitter so angles are not exactly uniform. Cost scales with K; cap at 8. 3D direction set of K vectors must be chosen well to avoid obvious preferred axes.
[ScratchLayers, stamp-scatter] Thin features alias at coarse sampling, like any line. Width smaller than a pixel means Feature Scale and output sample rate need thought. Fixed-angle layers give a limited orientation set when Layers is small, which is visible; Slope helps. Value of 4D modest.
ideas.variant_notes: Rotated anisotropic lattices per layer. A 1:A lattice keeps long strokes inside a 3x3 window; lateral excursion must stay below 1 cell or real seams appear (measured c0ratio 1.04 before that fix).
ideas.cost_note: K x (2D: 4 cells) with ~50 ops per cell; K=4 in 2D ~5 ns, K=8 ~10 ns. 3D K x 8 cells, K=6 ~30 ns.

ideas.name: SuperSample
ideas.one_liner: Footprint integration of any source over a pixel-sized area with a fixed rotated-grid pattern (Mean) or a threshold-coverage mode that gives antialiased, uniform-width edges independent of source slope.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Source; Footprint (hybrid; world-space size of the area to integrate, e.g. the pixel size); Pattern enum {RGSS4 (2D) / 8 points (3D: BCC-like corners), Grid 2^D, Star 2D taps}; Mode {Mean, Coverage}; Threshold (hybrid, Coverage only).
GenT: offsets o_k = Footprint * q_k where q_k is the fixed pattern in [-0.5,0.5]^D (RGSS: (1/8,3/8),(3/8,-1/8),(-1/8,-3/8),(-3/8,1/8)).
  Mean     = (1/K) sum S(pos + o_k)
  Coverage = (1/K) sum Select(S(pos + o_k) > T, 1, 0) * 2 - 1
No centre tap needed for Mean. With Footprint equal to the output pixel size this is the band-limited (minified) version of the source.
ideas.look: Mean turns hard-edged nodes (Checkerboard, CellularValue, Terrace, Fade with Step, ConvertRGBA8 inputs) into antialiased ones at any zoom and removes the shimmering of minified FBm; visually identical to the source at 1:1 and progressively smoother when minified. Coverage gives a soft band of constant world width around any iso-contour of any source (proto sheetB m11): unlike smoothstep on the value (band width ~ 1/|grad|), the band is as wide on steep flanks as on flat ones. Uses: texture baking, minimaps, LOD, uniform-width coastlines/biome borders, dithering-free masks.
ideas.why_new: Nothing in the graph can be told the pixel footprint; GenUniformGrid samples point values, so every hard node aliases when the grid is coarse. Coverage is a sampling-based 'IsoDistance' that needs no gradient normalisation and therefore has no singularities at critical points. As a graph it would be K DomainOffsets + K Fades + Adds; here it is one node whose cost is exactly the same K source evals.
ideas.simd_plan: GenT with a compile-time pattern table per D (RGSS 4 taps in 2D, 8 in 3D as the two interleaved tetrahedra of a cube scaled by 0.5, 8 axis taps in 4D). Cost = K x source: 4x in 2D, 8x in 3D/4D. CellularValue 2D at 3.9 ns becomes ~16 ns; cheaper than most alternatives. Branch-free: Coverage is a mask-to-float conversion.
ideas.continuity: Mean: C0 when the source is C0 and still C0 for piecewise-constant sources only in the integral sense: with 4 taps the output is piecewise constant with 4x finer steps, i.e. a sparse approximation; true continuity needs the footprint to be the pixel size so steps fall below one output level. Coverage is a step function with K+1 levels (discontinuous) by construction; at pixel footprint that is exactly what antialiasing wants.
ideas.params: Source; Footprint (hybrid: pass a constant from the caller or a DistanceToPoint-based function for perspective-correct LOD); Pattern; Mode; Threshold (hybrid: a noise threshold gives a dithered-looking but still antialiased border).
ideas.risks: Fixed K=4/8 patterns are visible as 4-level staircases on hard edges when the footprint is larger than a pixel; offer K=16 (two rotated RGSS sets) as an expensive option. Not a substitute for a true band-limiting filter of fractals (only removes the worst aliasing). Users must supply the footprint; document the GenUniformGrid relation (footprint = frequency step).
ideas.cost_note: Cost = K x source: 4x in 2D, 8x in 3D/4D. CellularValue 2D at 3.9 ns becomes ~16 ns; cheaper than most alternatives.

ideas.name: BondTunnels
ideas.one_liner: A cave network with a one-cell window: bond percolation on lattice faces, with hub and stub arms inside each cell, giving tubes that are connected by construction.
ideas.algorithm: c=floor(p), f=p-c. Each cell face has a hash keyed by its lower cell and axis, so the two cells sharing it agree: open = rnd01(h) < BondP; port = face centre + J*rnd11 on the tangent axes. Cell hash gives hub = 0.5 + Jh*rnd11. For each of the 2*dim faces, if open: segments port -> inner (port moved Stub along the inward normal) and inner -> hub, distance d_arm = min of two segment distances; closed face: Select to Dmax. d = polynomial smin across arms. Output ScaleOutput(min(d, Dmax), 0, Dmax), and isosurface at Radius. Seamless because at a face only the shared perpendicular stub lies within Dmax of it, so Dmax <= Stub and J + Radius < 0.5. Percolation: cubic-lattice bond threshold is 0.2488, so BondP 0.5 to 0.6 gives a giant connected component with almost no orphans. Strict mode: each cell picks one parent among its 3 negative faces; low face open if the cell picked it, high face open if the neighbour across picked it (4 hashes). In 3D transverse walks are 2D and recurrent, so all paths coalesce into one tree, like the Scheidegger drainage model, with a provable connected network and no flood fill. Hybrid BondP: arm radius scales by sat((BondP(x)-rnd)/width), so bonds shrink instead of popping.
ideas.look: Prototyped in 2D and 3D. 3D isosurface: dense uniform pipe network with junctions. 2D: blocky maze with branching corridors and dead ends. 3D slice: clean round dots plus occasional stub traces. Needs DomainRotate and warp to look like caves rather than plumbing; with FlowWarp the topology stays guaranteed. Also pipes, roots, circuit, mycelium, mine levels.
ideas.why_new: Connectivity guarantee is impossible with thresholded noise, and usually takes a flood fill. The trick of putting all information on faces reduces a segment network from 27 lattice cells and two hashes each to 1 cell and 7 hashes, so it is cheaper than a window search, with exact control of tube radius.
ideas.simd_plan: Fixed loop over 2*dim faces, Select by open mask, no window. Compare squared distances, take sqrt once if no smin. 3D: 7 hashes and 12 point-segment distances, estimate 7 to 10 ns, about 4x Perlin and well below CellularDistance. 2D about 2 ns; scalar prototype 1.66x perlin2. 4D: 9 hashes, 16 segments, about 15 ns versus 41 for CellularDistance, and a true 4D field for tiling; 4D tree mode gives a forest, not a tree, since transverse walks are transient there.
ideas.continuity: C0 everywhere (c0ratio 8.0, max slope 10 in the 2D sheet); C1 inside tubes when smin is used. Flat at Dmax in rock. Only near-surface values are distance-like, which is what caves use.
ideas.params: BondP (hybrid), Radius applied downstream or built in (hybrid), PortJitter, HubJitter, Stub, Dmax, Smooth, Mode enum: Percolation or Tree.
ideas.risks: Lattice signature is strong: axis-aligned stubs and grid dots in the FFT, axis ratio 64. It needs warp or rotation to look organic, and that is the main look risk. Tree mode has a global diagonal bias towards the negative corner. Very faint traces appear in slices when Dmax equals Stub, so use Dmax slightly below Stub.
ideas.cost_note: 3D: 7 hashes and 12 point-segment distances, estimate 7 to 10 ns, about 4x Perlin and well below CellularDistance.

queue.name: BondTunnels
queue.reason: Caves connected by construction from face-hash bond percolation in a 1-cell window, 4-8 ns in 3D (J4 top pick). Find how much warp hides the lattice signature.

ideas.name: FlowStrokes
ideas.one_liner: Painterly strokes following a direction field from a single per-lane Source eval, composited in priority order: fur, feathers, impasto, grass.
ideas.algorithm: Evaluate Direction source once per lane: th0 = Direction(p)*AngleRange. Window 3^dim of stroke features; for each cell: th = th0 + small hash offset. Frame: u = cos(th)*dx + sin(th)*dy, v = -sin(th)*dx + cos(th)*dy. Bend v -= b(h)*((u/L)^2 - 0.3). Taper t = sat(1-(u/L)^2). Absolute edge m = 1 - smoothstep(-E,0,|v| - W*sqrt(t) + (t>0?0:1)). Stroke surface: q = clamp(v/W, -1, 1); value = hash value*0.25 + 0.55*sqrt(1-q^2) + 0.15*sin(18*q + phase(h)) (bristle grooves). Priority per feature from hash; composite front to back as CollageStack (vis, col). Because th0 is the sample's angle, not the feature's, every stroke deforms into the field locally: the iso-orientation locus {p: p-c parallel to theta(p)} forms a curve through c. Alternative CentreAngle mode: Direction evaluated at each c, straight strokes, 9 evals.
ideas.look: Prototype: calligraphic tapered petals, flames and feathers that sweep together. Lane mode curves strokes like Van Gogh swirls; centre mode looks like straight scattered brush dabs. Bristle grooves show in hillshade. Very different from the contact sheet, closer to an illustration than to noise.
ideas.why_new: Warped cellular or stretched noise has no discrete object edges, and no node has occlusion plus orientation. Single eval per lane gives a field-following look with only 1 Source eval, where LIC would need many integration steps and centre orientation needs one per cell.
ideas.simd_plan: 1 Direction eval + cos/sin once (shared across all cells: the rotation is per lane and can be reused, cheap), then 9 cells of frame arithmetic + selection ~10 ns in 2D. 3D is a real open question: direction needs a unit vector, three Direction sources or a Curl-like derived tangent; rods and elliptic flakes in 27 cells ~35 ns + 3 evals. 4D fallback: drop to 3D-direction plane, 81 cells.
ideas.continuity: C0 with absolute edge softness: proto c0ratio improved from 1.10 to 3.04 with max slope 563; remaining steepness comes from bristle grooves and stroke tips. I did not isolate whether a small residual jump remains at tips, so treat as C0 unverified until bristle-free run.
ideas.params: Direction (hybrid), Angle Range, Length, Width, Bend, Bristle Strength and Frequency, Edge, Angle Jitter, Mode enum (Lane/Centre), Background
ideas.risks: High field gradient makes strokes shear into odd flames (seen at high field frequency), which may or may not be wanted. Stroke length is limited by window: 1 cell without anisotropic lattice. Coverage varies with width, leaving background. 3D form unproven: flagged for prototype.
ideas.cost_note: 1 Direction eval + cos/sin once (shared across all cells: the rotation is per lane and can be reused, cheap), then 9 cells of frame arithmetic + selection ~10 ns in 2D.

disp.how: Shape Stroke with Bristle and random Priority Jitter; the researcher lens wants it to headline the node

ideas.name: HilbertCurveNoise
ideas.one_liner: Pointwise Hilbert space-filling curve: exact distance to the curve polyline (maze/circuit corridors with width), position-along-curve value, and hashed adaptive depth for mixed corridor widths; 3D via Skilling's algorithm.
ideas.algorithm:
Scale p so the top cell is [0,2^n). Per lane integers X=floor(x), Y=floor(y) clamped by tiling the top cell with a hashed per-top-cell flip/rotation to avoid a visible period.
  xy2d (Wikipedia form, branch-free): d=0; for s=2^(n-1) down to 1: rx=(X&s)>0; ry=(Y&s)>0; d += s*s*((3*rx)^ry); rot(s,X,Y,rx,ry) using Select (if ry==0: if rx==1 {X=s-1-X; Y=s-1-Y}; swap X,Y).
  d2xy similarly for dPrev=d-1 and dNext=d+1 (clamped) giving the centres cPrev, cNext of the neighbouring leaves (they are 4-adjacent, distance exactly 1 cell).
  Inside the current leaf the curve is the polyline  mid(c,cPrev) -> c -> mid(c,cNext). dist = min(segDist(p, mid1, c), segDist(p, c, mid2)) in cell units.
  Outputs: Corridor = 1 - 2*smoothstep(0, Width, dist); Distance = dist; Along = valueNoise1D(d * AlongFreq / 4^n) (smooth value that varies along the path, exposes the maze as a gradient); Index = d / 4^n.
  Adaptive depth: n_lane = Select(frozen_at_level_k ...) implemented by computing d at the full depth and masking lower bits (d >> 2*(n-k) << 2*(n-k)) plus centre at that coarser cell; neighbours at the coarse depth. Joints between depths are offset by a quarter cell (dead-end look).
  3D: AxesToTranspose/TransposeToAxes (Skilling 2004) on 3 coordinates, same polyline construction with 6-adjacent neighbours.
ideas.look: A dense labyrinth of corridors that never cross, filling space at one scale, or with adaptive depth a circuit-board/Greek-key texture mixing wide and narrow corridors and dead ends. Along mode gives a continuous path value, turning it into 'a single river that visits every cell'. Distinct from everything on the sheet (nothing produces non-crossing connected corridors). Uses: mazes, circuitry, ornaments, sci-fi panelling, wall masks for dungeon generators, 3D 'pipes' volumes.
ideas.why_new: Space-filling corridors are impossible from any graph of existing nodes; the exact pointwise distance construction (neighbouring leaves via d2xy) makes it a real generator, not a lookup. Hashed depth makes it a multi-scale structure.
ideas.simd_plan: Three integer traversals of n levels (xy2d + 2x d2xy), each level ~12 int ops with Selects, all lane-uniform loops; n<=12 in 2D, n<=10 in 3D (fits int32). Then 2 segment distances. Estimated 2D n=8: ~3-4x Perlin; 3D Skilling ~2x that. 4D: Skilling generalises to any dimension (loop over 4 axes), fine for tiling.
ideas.continuity: Distance/Corridor are C0 (true distance field to a polyline). Along and Index are piecewise constant per leaf (discontinuous), as intended.
ideas.params: Depth int, Width hybrid, Output enum {Corridor, Distance, Along, Index}, Adaptive StopProb hybrid, MinDepth, Along Frequency, Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
ideas.risks: Top-level period of 2^n cells; hide with per-top-cell hashed symmetry (8 dihedral variants) at the cost of corridors not connecting across top cells (acceptable: a dead end). Integer precision limits depth. Adaptive joints are offset by design.
ideas.cost_note: Three integer traversals of n levels (xy2d + 2x d2xy), each level ~12 int ops with Selects, all lane-uniform loops; n<=12 in 2D, n<=10 in 3D (fits int32). Estimated 2D n=8: ~3-4x Perlin; 3D Skilling ~2x that.

ideas.name: LowDiscrepancyDither
ideas.one_liner: Pointwise low-discrepancy grids: Interleaved Gradient Noise (Jimenez 2014) and the R2/R3 plastic-constant grids (Roberts 2018) as a dither/threshold generator whose values are evenly spread within every small neighbourhood, unlike White noise (Wolfe 2022 analysis).
ideas.algorithm:
Params: Mode enum {IGN, R2, Bayer-like via R2 rounding}, CellSize (Feature Scale; positions are floored to integer cells), Frame/Phase (hybrid, animates by offsetting), Threshold Source (optional hybrid: output a binary mask Source > dither).
IGN (2D): i = floor(p); v = frac(52.9829189 * frac(0.06711056*i.x + 0.00583715*i.y)); animated: i += 5.588238 * (frame mod 64).
R2 (2D): v = frac(0.5 + 0.7548776662*i.x + 0.5698402910*i.y) (plastic constant g=1.32471795724: a1=1/g, a2=1/g^2). R3 (3D): a = (0.8191725134, 0.6710436067, 0.5497004779) from the 'plastic-3' root of x^4 = x+1. R4: 4 constants from x^5 = x+1. Output 2v-1.
ThresholdMode: out = Select(ThresholdSource(p) > v, 1, -1): a binary scatter/stipple mask whose local density equals the source value exactly (within every 3x3 block the 9 dither values are ~k/9).
Optional 'xor-shuffle' of i by a hash of floor(i/64) to de-periodise the R2 grid at large scales (R2 is exactly periodic only in the limit; IGN is quasi-periodic).
ideas.look: Fine, extremely even 'ordered-but-random' grain; thresholded against a smooth field it yields stipple/halftone-like scatter masks (vegetation placement, pebble sprinkle, decal density, stochastic transparency, dithered terracing) with no clumps or voids. White noise thresholded shows clusters; this does not.
ideas.why_new: White is the only stochastic point-pattern source in FastNoise and it clumps; a blue-ish low-discrepancy grid gives visually uniform coverage for placement masks and dithering at ~20 ops with no tables (true blue-noise tables are not allowed by the rules). The threshold mode makes 'density field -> uniform scatter' a one-node operation.
ideas.simd_plan: Trivial: floor, 2-4 FMAs, 2 frac; < 0.3x Perlin in any dimension. Branch-free.
ideas.continuity: Discontinuous by design (piecewise constant per integer cell), like White/Checkerboard.
ideas.params: Mode (enum), CellSize (Feature Scale), Phase (hybrid), Threshold (hybrid source), Dimension constants chosen per Gen dim.
ideas.risks: IGN/R2 have visible diagonal micro-structure when viewed as an image; fine for masks, not as a texture. Precision of frac for huge coordinates (use integer cells and a periodic wrap of 2^16).
ideas.cost_note: Trivial: floor, 2-4 FMAs, 2 frac; < 0.3x Perlin in any dimension.

ideas.name: QuasiTile
ideas.one_liner: Penrose rhombs (5-fold), Ammann-Beenker (8-fold) and other quasicrystal tilings evaluated pointwise through de Bruijn's multigrid dual with a bounded candidate search, so aperiodic floor tiles, girih-like ornament and quasicrystal etch patterns become a FastNoise node with edge distance, tile type and per-tile Source lookup.
ideas.algorithm:
Params: N (4..7, 5 = Penrose P3), Scale, Offsets gamma_k from the seed (generic values, no sum constraint needed: generalised Penrose tilings), Mortar, Output {EdgeDistance, TileType, TileValue, Lookup, VertexDistance}, Source.
Multigrid: unit vectors e_k = (cos 2 pi k/N, sin 2 pi k/N). Multigrid lines: q.e_k + gamma_k = integer. The dual vertex of the multigrid cell with index vector n (n_k = ceil(q.e_k + gamma_k)) is V(n) = sum_k n_k e_k. Each intersection X of lines (j,a) and (k,b) becomes the rhomb with vertices V(n(X)), +e_j, +e_k, +e_j+e_k where n(X) uses the indices of the cell just below X and n_j=a, n_k=b (convention fixed in the proto).
Pointwise location of the rhomb containing P (tiling space): estimate q' = (2/N)(P - sum_k gamma_k e_k) (frame identity sum_k e_k (e_k.q) = (N/2) q). Bound: |V(n(q)) - (N/2) q - sum gamma_k e_k| <= 1.618 for N=5 (max norm of a sum of unit vectors with weights in [0,1)), rhomb diameter < 1.9, so the intersection whose rhomb contains P satisfies |X - q'| < 1.41, i.e. its two line indices are within +-1 of round(q'.e_j + gamma_j) and round(q'.e_k + gamma_k). Candidates: all pairs j<k (10 for N=5) x 9 index offsets = 90. For each: X from a precomputed per-pair 2x2 inverse; n(X) by N ceils (with the j,k entries forced to a,b); V0 = sum n_m e_m (int->float, 2N FMAs); local (alpha,beta) = per-pair precomputed inverse of [e_j e_k] applied to (P - V0); hit = 0<=alpha<1 & 0<=beta<1. Exactly one hit (the dual is a proper tiling for generic gamma). Select outputs by mask.
Outputs: TileType = thick/thin from (k-j) mod N (as -1/+1); TileValue = rnd11(hash(j,k,a,b)); EdgeDistance = parallelogram SDF from (alpha,beta) and the rhomb angle, minus Mortar; Lookup = Source(seed^hash, alpha-0.5, beta-0.5 [, z, w]); VertexDistance = min over the 4 corners (Penrose star/sun motifs).
3D/4D: pattern in (x,y), other axes pass through to the Source.
ideas.look: The unmistakable Penrose rhomb floor: five-fold stars and decagons, never repeating, every tile the same two shapes; with N=4 the octagonal square/rhomb Ammann-Beenker pattern, with N=7 denser quasi-lattices. Edge distance gives grouted tiles; Lookup gives marble per tile. Absolutely nothing on the contact sheet or in the lab is aperiodic and structured.
ideas.why_new: No combination of existing nodes can produce a tiling with long-range order and no period; even the sum-of-five-cosines quasicrystal interference pattern (a 5-node graph) gives blobs, not tiles. It also makes a hard thing (Penrose textures) a one-node job.
ideas.simd_plan: Fixed loops: pairs (N(N-1)/2) x 9 candidates x (2x2 solve, N ceils, 2N FMAs, 2x2 solve, compares) all branch-free with mask selects; per-pair constants are small tables computed when N changes. Estimated 3600 flops for N=5: about 20-30 ns per 2D sample on AVX2 (5-7x CellularDistance 2D), 12-18 ns for N=4. Cost does not grow with dimension since z/w pass through.
ideas.continuity: EdgeDistance and VertexDistance are C0. TileType/TileValue/Lookup are piecewise by design.
ideas.params: N int, Scale, Seed (drives gamma), Mortar (hybrid), Output enum, Source, LookupScale.
ideas.risks: The candidate bound (+-1 after rounding, margin 1.41 vs 1.5) and the n(X) convention must be validated by brute force in the proto; non-generic gamma (triple intersections) must be avoided by deriving gamma from the seed with a guard. Cost is high for a building block but fine for a texture; a cheap alternative is Robinson-triangle substitution descent (about 2x Perlin) seeded by a periodic lattice of thick rhombs, which however leaves rare seams of broken tiles along the top-level lattice lines, so I do not recommend it as the primary method.
sources: N.G. de Bruijn, 'Algebraic theory of Penrose's non-periodic tilings of the plane', Indagationes Mathematicae 43 (1981) (cited from memory, not fetched)
ideas.cost_note: Estimated 3600 flops for N=5: about 20-30 ns per 2D sample on AVX2 (5-7x CellularDistance 2D), 12-18 ns for N=4.

queue.name: QuasiTile
queue.reason: Wild card. True Penrose and Ammann-Beenker tiles via the multigrid dual (J3 top pick). ~3600 flops and 20-30 ns; brute-force validate the candidate bound and compare with the multigrid-noise mosaic.

ideas.name: SpanningMaze
ideas.one_liner: Pointwise perfect maze from a hashed quadtree of spanning trees: corridors and walls are both trees, and the zero level set is one uninterrupted curve with no enclosed pieces.
ideas.algorithm: For edge between lattice cells a and a+1 along an axis: l = highest differing bit of a ^ (a+1). If l >= L, use a top-level binary-tree rule: each 2^L block links to its N or E neighbour by a hash bit at a hashed gate. Otherwise take the block of size 2^(l+1), hash it, omit one of the 4 joins between its children (leaving a spanning tree of the 4-cycle), and open only the hashed gate cell along each retained join. All tests are O(1) in the sample's window. Field: dPath = min distance to open edges between cell centres, dWall = min distance to closed wall segments, in a 3^D window. f = clamp((dWall - dPath)*k). Primal and dual trees interlock, so {f = 0} is a single curve. Wrap in a warp, since any homeomorphic warp preserves the topology.
ideas.look: Coral or brain-like labyrinth with wide even corridors and T-branches, rectilinear unless warped. Useful for guaranteed-reachable caves, dungeons, circuit patterns and reachable road or river masks. Measured over window 96, 3 seeds, 1500 px: both phases had 0 enclosed pieces unwarped. With warp 0.3 there are 0 enclosed pieces above 6 px, and 0 to 3 tiny pixel-scale pieces from 4-connected rasterisation at pinches.
ideas.why_new: Connectivity is guaranteed, not just likely, without flood fill, and no threshold of any existing node can guarantee it. Truchet gives loops, while Voronoi edges give a network with cycles and enclosed cells. Recursive-division mazes are global generators; the pointwise evaluation with infinite extent is the new part.
ideas.simd_plan: Highest differing bit: fixed loop over L (same for all lanes), or read the exponent of Convert(a^(a+1)) to float. In 2D about 12 edge tests x 1-2 hashes, plus segment distances; measured 5x perlin2 / 2.3x worley2 scalar. 3D: 54 edges in a 3^3 window, about 2x CellularDistance if restricted to the sample cell's neighbours; spanning tree of the cube's 8 children built by recursive halving: join two half-cubes by one hashed bridge per axis level. 4D by the same recursion, expensive at about 200+ edge tests.
ideas.continuity: C0, with kinks at the medial axis of distance fields. Measured c0ratio 8.
ideas.params: Levels L (int), Output (Signed Curve, Corridor Distance), Gain (float). Warp via upstream DomainWarp. Corridor width comes from thresholding.
ideas.risks: Long straight hierarchical walls and faint block lines at 2^L spacing are visible in the wide view; warp and larger L reduce them. Top-level binary-tree rule is directionally biased at the largest scale. 3D and 4D are unproven in code. Hard guarantee is lost if the user thresholds far from 0 (corridors can pinch only if threshold exceeds half-corridor width).
ideas.cost_note: In 2D about 12 edge tests x 1-2 hashes, plus segment distances; measured 5x perlin2 / 2.3x worley2 scalar.

queue.name: SpanningMaze
queue.reason: Perfect maze from hashed quadtree spanning trees, pointwise with guaranteed connectivity (J3 top pick). Block lines at 2^L need a warp; 3D is unexplored.

ideas.name: Stamp
ideas.one_liner: An origin-centred analytic shape generator (crater, ring, ripple, cone, dome, gaussian, superellipse/boulder, star/polygon, dune, capsule/ribbon, torus) with seed-driven per-instance variation, designed to be the Source of Scatter but usable alone.
ideas.algorithm:
Input p in local coords, radius 1 = stamp edge. r2 = dot(p,p) in d dims, r = sqrt(r2). Per-instance variation: h = HashPrimes(seed, 0): depth' = Depth*(1 + Variation*rnd11(h)), etc. (the seed differs per instance when driven from Scatter).
Profiles (enum), all defined for any d because they use r only unless noted:
- Crater: bowl = -depth'*(1 - r2/rimR^2) for r<rimR; rim = rimH*exp(-((r-1)/rimW)^2); ejecta = ejH*exp(-(r-1)*ejK) for r>1 (clipped by Scatter envelope); value = Select(r<rimR, bowl, 0) + rim + ejecta. Optional rays: angular term rayA*max(0,cos(n*theta))^8 using cos(n theta) via Chebyshev recurrence from ct = p.x/r, st = p.y/r (no atan2): c1=ct, c2=2ct^2-1, c_{k+1}=2ct c_k - c_{k-1}, n fixed small int; 3D uses the xz or xy plane for theta.
- Ring: exp(-((r-r0)/w)^2). Ripple: cos(2*pi*f*r + phase(h)) * (1-r2)^2. Cone: 1-r. Dome: sqrt(max(0,1-r2)). Gaussian: exp(-k r2).
- Boulder: superellipsoid |x/a|^e + |y/b|^e (+|z/c|^e) via Pow with e in [2,6], then perturb radius by low harmonics: rEff = r*(1 + A*(rnd11 * c2 + rnd11 * c3)) using the same cos recurrence; value = 1 - rEff (an approximate SDF, negative outside). Axis ratios a,b,c from the hash (per instance).
- Polygon/Star (2D plane in any d): regular n-gon SDF: fold angle without atan2 is hard, so use 'cos(n theta) modulated radius' instead: rStar = 1 + Spike*cos(n theta) (star) or the Minkowski-like polygon approximation max_k dot(p, dir_k) over n fixed directions (n <= 8, fixed loop) which is exact and needs no trig at Gen time (dir table built at param set).
- Dune: asymmetric along local x: windward = smoothstep(-1,0,x)-ish slope, slip face = 1 - smoothstep(0,SlipLen,x); multiply by a Gaussian across y (and z).
- Capsule/Ribbon: segment from (-L,0) to (L,0), d = distance to segment, value = 1 - d/w (clamped), or gaussian across. L*s must respect Scatter's rAllow (Scatter can read nothing from its source, so document, or add a 'Max Local Radius' float the artist sets on Scatter).
- Torus (3D/4D): sqrt((rxy - R)^2 + z^2) < w.
Output in [-1,1] by analytic range per profile.
ideas.look: A single crater/ring/boulder/star at the origin; through Scatter these become lunar surfaces with rims and ejecta, raindrop ripple fields, boulder scatters, starfish/sea-urchin patterns, dune fields, broken-rock rubble. The Chebyshev angular term gives spoked craters and n-fold stars without atan2.
ideas.why_new: DistanceToPoint gives only a radial distance; everything with a rim, an asymmetric profile, an anisotropic body or an angular lobe needs ~6 nodes of Remap/Abs/Multiply per shape and still has no per-instance variation. A shape library with seed-driven variation is what turns Scatter from 'tiled Perlin blobs' into a crater/rock tool. Standalone it is also the natural 'single feature' node (one volcano, one island) that currently does not exist.
ideas.simd_plan: Pure arithmetic on p, no lattice, no window: ~20-60 ops depending on profile (Pow/Exp for superellipse and rims). All profiles are enum-switched at the node level (one Gen per profile via a template parameter or a static dispatch when the enum is set) so Gen is branch free. 3D and 4D trivially share the radial code; angular profiles pick a fixed plane. Cost ~0.3-1x Perlin. Combined with Scatter Fast window in 2D: ~4 + 4x0.5 ns.
ideas.continuity: Profile dependent: Crater/Ring/Ripple/Gaussian/Dome C1 (Dome C0 at the edge), Cone C0 at the apex, Boulder SDF C0 along the superellipse ridge, Polygon via max of dots is C0 at vertices. Variation is per seed so it never changes within one instance.
ideas.params: Profile enum, Depth, Rim Height, Rim Width, Ejecta Height/Decay, Ring Radius/Width, Frequency (ripple), Exponent (superellipse), Lobes int (star/polygon/rays), Spike, Aspect X/Y/Z, Length (capsule), Slip Length (dune), Variation (0..1, fraction of each parameter randomised by seed). Few should be hybrid: Depth and Lobes could be, the rest are per-stamp constants.
ideas.risks: Large enum surface; keep each profile's parameter set small or split into 2-3 nodes (StampRadial, StampBoulder, StampAngular). Pow for superellipse is expensive; e=2 and e=4 fast paths. The capsule length and ejecta decay can poke outside Scatter's radius budget: Scatter's envelope clips them (slight truncation), acceptable.
ideas.cost_note: Cost ~0.3-1x Perlin. Combined with Scatter Fast window in 2D: ~4 + 4x0.5 ns.

queue.reason: Origin-centred analytic profiles, so stamp-scatter and quad-stamp work with no source graph. Dull alone; keep the enum small or split it.

ideas.name: StrataCaverns
ideas.one_liner: Karst-style cavern layers: per-slab 2D cave plans with flat floors and domed ceilings, separated by rock and linked by hashed vertical shafts.
ideas.algorithm: Slab coordinate y' = y/H + Dip*Tilt(x,z) from an optional hybrid. j = floor(y'), t = y' - j. Slab hash gives lateral offset (ox,oz). Plan value n = Source(x+ox, j*137.0, z+oz) evaluated at a snapped y so it is constant through the slab. Openness a = sat(n*g + Coverage). Floor tf = Base + small hash shift. Ceiling tc = tf + Height * sqrt(a) (domed, vertical at walls). dv = max(tf - t, t - tc) * H (positive = rock, a = 0 gives tc=tf, so rock). Shafts: for boundary indices j and j+1, macro-cell (floor(x/S), floor(z/S)) hash gives centre, r, presence; ds = max(cylinder distance, span distance around boundary). d = smin(dv, ds). Output ScaleOutput(min(d, Dmax)). Continuity at slab boundaries needs Base*H >= Dmax and (1 - Base - Height)*H >= Dmax. Connectivity within a slab: in 2D a symmetric field's level set percolates exactly when coverage exceeds 50% (Zallen-Scher, proven for Gaussian fields), so Coverage just above 0 gives one giant horizontal cavern with pillars, by a known theorem, not by luck. Dense shafts link slabs.
ideas.look: Not prototyped. Vertical (XY) slice: stacked flat-bottomed lens voids in rows like limestone bedding planes. Horizontal (XZ) slice: island-and-pillar plans (room-and-pillar). 3D iso: horizontal galleries with level floors, walkable, joined by vertical pits. Different from all blob caves, which have no flat floors. For game levels, limestone, salt mines.
ideas.why_new: Every noise cave is isotropic blobby and not walkable. Flat floors and horizontal layering need a floor(y) snapped source position, not available in a graph (no quantise-domain node). Terrace only remaps values. Controlled by designer-level parameters like layer height and coverage.
ideas.simd_plan: 1 source eval, 1 slab hash, 2 shaft hashes, then a few mins and one sqrt; no window. 3D: Source cost + 1.5 ns; 2D (x,y) uses 1D plan. 4D: extra axis to source (morphing plan over w). Slab offset is converted to int via bit field; Select-free except for presence mask. Far cheaper than a volumetric fractal.
ideas.continuity: C0, by the boundary rule above; rock is flat at Dmax beyond the band. Sqrt dome has infinite ceiling slope at a=0 which makes vertical walls; regularise by sqrt(a+e)-sqrt(e).
ideas.params: Source (plan), Layer Height H, Base, Height, Coverage (hybrid), Gain g, Shaft Spacing S, Shaft Radius (hybrid), Dip (hybrid optional), Dmax.
ideas.risks: Untested. y is privileged. Shaft may not land in a cavern; density must be high, or use shaft mask by plan value at centre (one extra source eval per shaft). 50% percolation holds for symmetric fields; Perlin is close but not exact and near threshold connections are thin. Walkable look depends on height vs feature scale.
ideas.cost_note: 3D: Source cost + 1.5 ns; 2D (x,y) uses 1D plan.

queue.reason: Slab-wise cave plans with flat floors and shafts: walkable karst at source + 1.5 ns. Untested, y is privileged, and shafts can miss caverns.

ideas.name: Textile
ideas.one_liner: One closed-form cloth node: woven threads with a linear over-under rule, or real interlocking knit loops solved from the textile stitch curve, with per-thread variation from 1D hashes.
ideas.algorithm: Structure=Weave: i=floor(x), j=floor(y), f=fract, phase ph=mod(i*Step+j, N). Warp is over when ph<K; weft is over otherwise. (N,K,Step) gives plain (2,1,1), twill (4,2,1), satin (5,1,2). Warp crown coordinate cw=(ph+fy)/K when over, (ph-K+fy)/(N-K) when under, and z_warp=+/-sin(pi*cw). Weft uses fx the same way with the opposite sign. Per-thread hashes hi=hash(i), hj=hash(j) set width w=W*(1+WJ*rnd(h)) and wobble u=fx-.5+Wob*noise1D(y,hi). Height of each thread = 0.5*z + 0.5*sqrt(1-(u/w)^2) + Fibre*sin(F*(u+Twist*y)); output Max(warp,weft). Structure=Knit: stitch curve x(t)=t+a*sin(2t), y(t)=h*cos(t), z(t)=d*cos(2t). X=pi*x folded to |X-2pi*round(X/2pi)|. For each row j in a fixed window: start t0=acos(clamp((y-j)/h)), try branches t0 and 2pi-t0, run 2 Newton closest-point steps t+=clamp(dot(P-C,C')/dot(C',C'),-.7,.7) using sin 2t=2sc and cos 2t=1-2s^2. Then d^2=|P-C|^2, tube q=1-d^2/w^2, height=z(t)+0.55*sqrt(q), Max over rows and branches. Row hash gives yarn width and tone.
ideas.look: Look-tested (mat_inv m=6 and m=14). Weave gives convincing plain, twill and satin with twisted thread shading. Knit reads immediately as interlocking stockinette loops; thinner yarn becomes chainmail. Good for fabric, wicker, chainmail, wire mesh, and as a bump layer under fractals. Warps turn it into draped cloth.
ideas.why_new: Nothing on the contact sheet has periodic structure with real over-under occlusion, and a graph cannot express the phase rule or the per-thread hashes. The knit curve has overhang, so it cannot be a height function of x. The closest-point solve is what makes it work pointwise.
ideas.simd_plan: Weave: one cell, 2 hashes, integer modulus for ph, Select for over/under, 2 sin plus one or two sqrt: scalar proto 4.4x Perlin including two 1D wobble evals, about 2x Perlin expected in AVX2. Knit: rows x 2 branches x 3 sincos pairs is 17x Perlin scalar with a 6 row window. Shrink to 3-4 rows (h<=0.8) and replace Newton with a small per-node polyline table of the folded half stitch (4-5 segments, built when params are set), target 6-8x Perlin. 3D: Z selects a ply (floor(z*Plies) hash shifts the phase and lateral offset) with a shell profile. 4D: W is a second ply index, so it is a real function but the torus map bends the pattern.
ideas.continuity: Discontinuous by design at occlusion edges (measured c0ratio 1.04 for weave), since one thread really passes over another. Inside each thread C1. A Softness param using MaxSmooth gives C0 at some cost in crispness.
ideas.params: Structure enum, N, K, Step (ints, per node), Thread Width, Width Jitter, Wobble, Fibre Amount, Fibre Frequency, Twist, Stitch a/h/d. Hybrid: Thread Width, Wobble, Fibre Amount. Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output range.
ideas.risks: Lattice-locked pattern looks distorted through GenTileable2D's 4D torus; an integer Repeat param on (i,j) would give true tiling. Newton can land on the wrong branch if a or h are extreme, so clamp the param ranges. Output range measured slightly above 1 (1.08): normalise by a constant.
ideas.cost_note: Weave: one cell, 2 hashes, integer modulus for ph, Select for over/under, 2 sin plus one or two sqrt: scalar proto 4.4x Perlin including two 1D wobble evals, about 2x Perlin expected in AVX2.

ideas.name: TriaxialWeave
ideas.one_liner: Three families of strands at 60 degrees with a provably consistent cyclic over-under rule and no trig per strand, giving the hexagonal-hole kagome basket, rattan cane webbing and closed 'mad weave' looks that a two-family weave cannot.
ideas.algorithm:
Three unit normals 120 degrees apart: n0=(0,1), n1=(-sqrt3/2,-1/2), n2=(sqrt3/2,-1/2) so n0+n1+n2=0 and s0+s1+s2=0 for s_a = p.n_a. Strands of family a are centred on half-integer s_a with pitch 1. For each a: k_a=floor(s_a), f_a=s_a-k_a-0.5 (across coordinate, |f|<=0.5), per-strand hash h_a=hash(a,k_a), half-width hw_a = HW*(1+WidthJitter*rnd11(h_a)) with HW<=0.5 (HW<1/6 keeps the small triangles open, HW=0.5 closes the hexagons into mad weave), crown_a = sqrt(max(0, 1-(f_a/hw_a)^2)) * Thickness.
Interlace (cyclic rule 0 over 1, 1 over 2, 2 over 0): because s0+s1+s2=0, where strand centres of families a and a+1 cross (both half-integers) s_{a+2} is an integer, i.e. the third family passes exactly between its strands: no triple points, and along any strand the crossings alternate between the other two families, so the cyclic rule is automatically alternating over/under and pairwise consistent (checked: at an a/(a+1) crossing a says over, a+1 says under its a-1=a). Lift without any crossing bookkeeping: lift_a = Amp*(cos(2 pi s_{a+2}) - cos(2 pi s_{a+1}))/2, which evaluates to +Amp at crossings with a+1 and -Amp at crossings with a+2 and interpolates smoothly between (3 cosines total, shared by all three families).
height_a = crown_a + lift_a where crown_a>0 else -1 (hole). Output Height = max_a height_a (ScaleOutput). Modes: Height; Lookup = Source(seed^h_top, t_a, f_a/hw_a) with t_a = p.d_a along the top strand (ribbon texture, Strata on k_a gives coloured cane); TopFamily (0,1,2 as -1,0,1 for three-colour patterns); Wobble: f_a += W*n1d(t_a, k_a) (1D value noise along the strand, 2 hashes) for hand-woven irregularity.
3D: Height - z gives a solid woven sheet (iso-surface), or z selects layers; 4D passes through. Explicit integer Period on the hashes makes it tile.
ideas.look: A regular lattice of hexagonal holes bordered by six-pointed star overlaps, every strand clearly passing over then under its neighbours, chair cane webbing, kagome baskets, rattan, and at full width the dense three-way 'mad weave' with its tumbling-block illusion. Visibly different from the two-family plain/twill weaves already prototyped and from any hex cellular pattern.
ideas.why_new: A two-family weave node cannot produce three-directional interlacing; the existing hex nodes give cells, not strands with over-under. The identity s0+s1+s2=0 is what makes the interlace rule and lift closed-form, so the node is as cheap as a plain weave.
ideas.simd_plan: Branch-free: 3 dot products, 3 floors, 3 hashes, 3 sqrt, 3 cos, a few selects, max of three. Roughly 2-3x Perlin in 2D; 3D/4D cost identical plus passthrough. GenT over the pack works since only (x,y) are used for the pattern.
ideas.continuity: Height is C0 (max of continuous terms; crown goes to 0 at strand edges and the hole level -1 is below any strand). Lookup and TopFamily are discontinuous at strand edges and crossings by design.
ideas.params: HalfWidth (hybrid), Thickness, LiftAmp (hybrid), WidthJitter, Wobble, Mode enum, Source, Period, optional Chirality flip (swap the cyclic rule) and per-strand presence (rnd01<Density, broken cane).
ideas.risks: The cyclic rule yields one chirality; the physical kagome exists in both, so expose a flip. Lift amplitude versus crown height must be tuned so an under-strand is never visible through an over-strand at the crossing centre (Amp >= Thickness*(1-cos(pi*hw)) roughly; proto to confirm). Verify the no-triple-point claim numerically for the chosen normals.
ideas.cost_note: Roughly 2-3x Perlin in 2D; 3D/4D cost identical plus passthrough.
